A novel method of categorizing images using unsupervised Bayesian techniques is proposed in this paper. The method is based on the asymmetric Gaussian mixture (AGM) model, which has been shown to perform better than the symmetric Gaussian mixture model (GMM) in previous research. The estimation of mixture parameters is achieved through a sampling-based reversible jump Markov chain Monte Carlo (RJMCMC) method. The introduction of RJMCMC allows for model transfer throughout the parameter learning process, resulting in automatic convergence to the optimal number of categories. 

To generate image representative data, scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT), bag-of-visual-words (BOVW), and probabilistic latent semantic analysis (pLSA) techniques are adopted. Feature selection is applied to filter out irrelevant and unneeded information. To evaluate the performance of this method, a comparison is made with other popular classifiers and the merits of AGM are demonstrated. Future work may focus on expanding the application of this technique to other datasets and improving its accuracy further.

Association rule mining (ARM) has been paid more attention of both data mining users and database researchers in the last decade. Generation of various association rules from large distributed databases is the crucial task due to its intrinsic distribution of data sources. Identifying these type of distributed data sources requires a deep knowledge on data mining and planning for deployment in distributed environment. In this paper, a survey of the distributed framework for ARM is presented. It is observed that the parallelized nature of Apriori, Hadoop, MapReduce and Spark proves to be very efficient in Distributed association rule mining (DARM) environment. We expect that, the comprehensive review, references cited will convey foremost hypothetical issues and a guideline to the researcher in interesting research direction.

In order to obtain high classification accuracy and reduce time consumption for large-scale polarimetric synthetic-aperture radar (PolSAR) data. In this letter, we propose a fast semisupervised classification algorithm using histogram-based density estimation (called FSHDE). First, a noniterative collaborative training using our proposed Wishart-clustering selection strategy is designed to expand the labeled sample set from unlabeled samples. Second, a fast feature mapping based on histogram density estimation is employed to reliably capture the interaction of nonlinear features. Third, submodular optimization is used to select optimal subspace features to reduce feature correlation. Experimental results on synthetic and real PolSAR data indicate that FSHDE greatly reduces the time consumption and improves the accuracy for terrain classification compared with the state-of-the-art methods.

The proliferation of cyberattacks highlights the urgent need for the development of sophisticated detection tools. One promising approach is to draw inspiration from the Human Immune System (HIS) and develop algorithms based on it. One such method is the Dendritic Cell Algorithm (DCA) that is based on the Danger model. This study focuses on the analysis of two types of DCA algorithms, deterministic and classical DCA, with the objective of detecting DoS attacks. Furthermore, the paper discusses the potential of enhancing the DCA algorithm to detect malicious TCP port scanning. The evaluation and results of different use-cases demonstrate the effectiveness of the DCA algorithm in detecting port scanning.

Currently, mobile applications such as interactive gaming, virtual reality, and natural language processing are becoming more computationally intensive, but the computing capacity of mobile devices is limited. An effective solution to this problem is offloading the tasks to nearby cloudlets, which are small mobile data centers deployed in wireless metropolitan area networks (WMANs). However, cloudlets consume a large amount of energy, which leads to negative effects such as increased carbon dioxide emissions and aggravating the greenhouse effect.

To address this challenge, we propose an energy-aware virtual machine (VM) scheduling method for cloudlets in WMANs. We have designed an optimization model that formalizes our problem. Using VM Live Migration Technology, we have developed an energy-saving VM scheduling method, abbreviated as MFEA, to determine which VMs should be migrated and where they should be migrated. 

Experimental data demonstrates that the proposed method is effective in reducing energy consumption while still maintaining the overall performance of the system. By scheduling VMs in a smarter and more energy-efficient manner, we can reduce the negative impacts of excessive energy consumption associated with cloudlets in WMANs.

In this paper, we present our methodology for designing a smart doorbell system for homes. While many big companies offer home voice assistants that integrate various services, privacy concerns and a desire for independence from a single service provider have created demand for more freedom in choosing "smart objects." Our doorbell system uses both iris and voice recognition to identify the user at the door, and we have taken special care in handling the biometric data involved. Specifically, our system avoids storing or sending biometric data to the cloud, and utilizes machine-learning algorithms to perform local computations. Edge-Computing analytics are used to determine the user's identity by combining voice and iris biometrics, and reconfigurable hardware is employed for optimal performance and power consumption. Our tests yield impressive results, demonstrating a performance increase of 5x the sequential case and a 7x reduction in energy consumption.

As mobile data traffic continues to grow rapidly, content delivery has become a major concern for the internet. To address this issue, information-centric networking has been proposed as a potential solution, particularly for wireless networks. Unfortunately, the impact of edge caches and decision schemes on content delivery performance has been largely overlooked in existing research.

To improve network performance in information-centric wireless networks, our team has developed an edge cache-based intelligent content delivery solution. Our approach involves a smart router that uses advanced analytics to analyze the popularity of content, user mobility patterns, and social relationships. Based on this information, the router makes intelligent caching decisions that help to optimize the delivery of content.

As the router makes caching decisions, its connected access points are kept up-to-date about the status of network content. This allows for dynamic optimization of content delivery based on changing use patterns and content popularity. With our edge cache-based intelligent content delivery solution, we believe that significant improvements in network performance are possible.

Many Internet of Things (IoT) services nowadays are accessible through smartphone applications, making it more convenient for users to use IoT systems. However, this accessibility also brings potential security issues, such as remote intrusion or privacy attacks. Cyber attackers are now targeting not only personal computers and the internet but also mobile devices. This paper aims to reduce these risks by extracting network traffic features during internet connections and using these features to implement the Information Gain algorithm in selecting relevant classification features, creating a classifier through the Bayesian model updating technique. Compared to other machine learning classifiers, such as k-nearest neighbor, support vector machine and J48, our improved algorithm showed a higher level of validity, accuracy, efficiency, and practicality making it an effective measure to protect IoT systems from potential security breaches.

The integration of wearable wireless devices and cloud computing in e-health systems has significantly improved their effectiveness and availability. Patients can upload their personal health information (PHI) files to the cloud, from where the health service providers (HSPs) can obtain appropriate information to determine the health state. This system not only reduces the costs associated to healthcare but also provides timely diagnosis to save lives. However, a number of privacy concerns arise while sharing sensitive information. In this paper, we propose a novel privacy-preserving patient health information sharing scheme, which allows HSPs to access and search PHI files in a secure yet efficient manner. We make use of the searchable encryption technique with keyword range search and multikeyword search. The proposed privacy-preserving equality test protocol allows different types of numeric comparison searches on encrypted data. We also use a variant of bloom filter and message authentication code to classify PHI files, filter false data, and check integrity of search results. The simulations on real-world and synthetic data show the feasibility and efficiency of the system, and security analysis proves the privacy-preservation properties.

Vehicular Ad Hoc Networking (VANET) is an emerging technology defined with main motive of avoiding on road accidents and provide safety and life critical applications to users in a well-organized manner. We present current challenges in designing VANET protocols through extensive survey from the perspective of decentralized congestion control (DCC) strategies. The challenges in routing and security applications are also outlined briefly. Internet of things (IoT) will be the future networking system in which all things will be connected to interact. In the near future, VANETs will be the main part of IoT networks because of its safety and infotainment applications. A lot of work is done in this area, still, the industry thrusts for more efficient and robust design. This paper highlights various research challenges, which will help other researchers who wish to work in this area.

It is essential to develop proper energy management strategies (EMSs) with broad adaptability for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). This paper utilizes deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to develop EMSs for a series HEV due to DRL's advantages of requiring no future driving information in derivation and good generalization in solving energy management problem formulated as a Markov decision process. History cumulative trip information is also integrated for effective state of charge guidance in DRL-based EMSs. The proposed method is systematically introduced from offline training to online applications; its learning ability, optimality, and generalization are validated by comparisons with fuel economy benchmark optimized by dynamic programming, and real-time EMSs based on model predictive control (MPC). Simulation results indicate that without a priori knowledge of future trip, original DRL-based EMS achieves an average 3.5% gap from benchmark, superior to MPC-based EMS with accurate prediction; after further applying output frequency adjustment, a mean gap of 8.7%, which is comparable with MPC-based EMS with mean prediction error of 1 m/s, is maintained with concurrently noteworthy improvement in reducing engine start times. Besides, its impressive computation speed of about 0.001 s per simulation step proves its practical application potential, and this method is independent of powertrain topology such that it is applicative for any type of HEVs even when future driving information is unavailable.

These studies demonstrate a combination of tested methods to separate lung and heart sound signals' (LS-HS) principal components recorded using a digital dual stethoscope. Initially, when these raw signals are acquired, their principal components intertwine in the characteristics of the frequency and time domains. Applying Independent Component Analysis (ICA) combined with Empirical Mode Decomposition allows separation of their origin. Further, Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) were utilized to determine to which specific class of components they belong. Each set of recorded signals was evaluated and the outcomes were compared against the verified reference group. As cardiopulmonary diseases represent a major global health concern, this can be helpful in an early screening for distinct cardiopulmonary problems manifested by peculiar acoustic indicators.

In a geological study, an important step is to determine the type of sedimentary rock or its grain size. Such a determination requires accurate analysis in the field or in a laboratory. As the size of the study area grows, this activity can be time consuming and error prone because the number of specialists working under rigid criteria also increases. This paper proposes a novel methodology to classify grain size using unique wavelength reflectance data and artificial neural networks. The results indicate that the proposed method can be reliably used in the field.

High-speed robotics often involves complex movements that require precise control and accurate models. However, accurately modeling dynamic trajectories with large accelerations can be challenging. This is where kinematic optimization using compact representations can be useful. It can lead to an efficient online computation of these dynamic movements, but successful execution requires accurate models or aggressive tracking with high-gain feedback. 

For situations where accurate models are not available, learning to track references in a safe and reliable way is an open problem. One issue with model-based learning approaches is that stability issues in the iteration domain can prevent successful implementation. To address this, the authors propose a new adaptive and cautious iterative learning control (ILC) algorithm in this paper. In this algorithm, the stability of the control updates is analyzed probabilistically. The adapted local linear models are used to increase the probability of update monotonicity, exercising caution during learning. 

The resulting learning controller can be implemented efficiently using a recursive approach. It is evaluated extensively in simulations as well as in the authors' robot table tennis setup for tracking dynamic hitting movements. Testing with two seven-degree-of-freedom anthropomorphic robot arms, the authors show improved and more stable tracking performance over high-gain proportional and derivative (PD) control, model-free ILC (simple PD feedback type), and model-based ILC without cautious adaptation.

Currently, the market for Korean language education is valued at over 4 trillion won in Korea, 20 trillion yen in Japan, and 50 trillion in China. Traditional methods of language learning, such as offline academies and textbooks, often result in poor learning efficiency and create pressure on learners. This is especially true for English, which has become more of a test subject than a means of communication.

To truly acquire a language as a tool for communication, an immersive environment needs to be created. Virtual reality technology has the potential to provide such an environment. There are already language learning programs available in the virtual reality space, such as `Learn Languages VR by Mondly' and `House of Language VR'. However, these programs have limitations. In the case of `Learn Languages VR by Mondly', the degree of speech freedom is limited. In the case of `House of Language VR', the program lacks realism due to its reliance on animation.

To truly excel in a language, it is essential to practice speaking with native speakers in real-life situations. With this in mind, we intend to create a learning program using VR devices and interactions with native speakers. By immersing learners in an environment where they can practice speaking with native speakers, we aim to provide an effective and realistic language-learning experience.

This paper considers the transceiver design for uplink massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems with channel sparsity in the angular domain. Recent progress has shown that sparsity-learning-based blind signal detection is able to retrieve the channel and data by using massage-passing-based sparse matrix factorization methods. Short pilot sequences are inserted into user packets to eliminate the so-called phase and permutation ambiguities inherent in sparse matrix factorization. In this paper, to exploit the knowledge of these short pilot sequences more efficiently, we propose a semi-blind channel-and-signal estimation (SCSE) scheme in which the knowledge of the pilot sequences are integrated into the message passing algorithm for sparse matrix factorization. The SCSE algorithm involves enumeration over all possible user permutations, and so is time-consuming when the number of users is relatively large. To reduce complexity, we further develop the simplified SCSE (S-SCSE) to accommodate systems with a large number of users. The numerical results show that our semi-blind signal detection scheme substantially outperforms the state-of-the-art blind detection and training-based schemes in the short-pilot regime.

Lung nodules that overlap with ribs and clavicles in chest radiographs can be difficult to be detected by radiologists as well as by computer-aided detection systems. Removing bony structures would result in better visualization of undetectable lesions. Our purpose in this study was to develop a deep-learning scheme to separate ribs and clavicles from soft tissue in chest radiographs. To achieve this, we developed a mixture of anatomy-specific, orientation-frequency-specific (ASOFS) deep neural network convolution (NNC) experts. Anatomy-specific (AS) architecture was designed to separate bony structures from soft tissue in different lung segments. The orientation-frequency-specific (OFS) was designed to decompose bone and soft-tissue structures into specific orientation-frequency components of different scales using a multi-resolution decomposition technique. For evaluation, we used a database of 118 chest radiographs with pulmonary nodules. Quantitative and qualitative evaluation showed that our ASOFS NNC was superior to a state-of-the-art bone-suppression technique. Particularly, our NNC scheme separated ribs and clavicles from soft tissue, while it was better able to maintain the conspicuity of lung nodules and vessels, comparing to the reference technique. Therefore, our deep-learning scheme can be useful for radiologists as well as CAD systems in detection of lung nodules in chest radiographs.

Lung nodules are a prevalent issue in our society, particularly among those who are exposed to risk factors such as smoking and pollution. However, current techniques for segmenting lung nodules from CT images have several drawbacks. For instance, most segmentation algorithms use Local Fitting Models that require re-initialization for the sign distance function. In addition, the inhomogeneity of CT images can cause algorithms to settle at local minima, resulting in incorrect segmentation. Re-initialization also increases the amount of time it takes to implement the algorithm, making it slower.

A solution to these issues is to incorporate the Global Convex Segmentation (GCS) and Split Bregman techniques into a region-based active contour model such as the Chan-Vese (CV) with Region-Scalable Fitting (RSF) scheme. This approach is powerful and flexible, able to segment both synthetic and real images, and has been shown to effectively segment the lung nodule region.

To extract tumor features from the segmentations, Local Binary Pattern descriptors (LBP) are utilized. The extracted features are then fed into a Support Vector Machine (SVM) to classify the nodules as either tumor or non-tumor. The accuracy of this classification is enhanced when compared to other existing methods.

Experimental results with Lung CT images demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach. By using these techniques, we can improve the accuracy and efficiency of lung nodule segmentation and classification, potentially leading to more effective and timely treatments for patients.

In this paper, we propose an algorithm that can prove the objectivity of the image reading that depends on personal / subjective judgment in the clinic and can prove it by the scientific method. We analyze the characteristics of liver cancer in ultrasound images by using the deep - run algorithm, and propose an algorithm that can diagnose lesions using extracted features.

In today's social media landscape, Twitter has become a crucial platform, with the power to make or break one's public image. The platform is rife with opinions and statements, some of which can be downright hateful, leading to the widespread phenomenon of hate speech. Such speech is regulated under Article 28 of the ITE Law, and many individuals, both intentionally and unintentionally, have voiced their opposition to social media platforms that promote or tolerate hate speech.

However, despite such concerns, social media platforms often lack the capability to aggregate information and draw conclusions from existing conversations. To address this issue, this paper proposes the use of text mining to classify text as either containing or not containing elements of hate speech. By developing a deep learning-based Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) algorithm, the authors aim to train a computer to recognize and classify hate speech.

Tests conducted on the program showed an average precision of 91%, recall of 90%, and accuracy of 91%. The results offer a potentially powerful tool for identifying and addressing hate speech on social media, which has become increasingly important in today's age of heightened awareness of online harassment and discrimination.

In conclusion, the proposed approach offers a promising avenue for addressing the issue of hate speech on social media, highlighting the potential of machine learning-based techniques to help regulate harmful online behavior.

In this study, we obtain life log data from visibility information using smart glass which is a wearable device. In the proposed system, it consists of a text data collection part by cooperation between smart glass and image recognition API and activity recognition part. The activity recognition part incorporates multidimensional scaling analysis method and correspondence analysis for classifying data. As a result of utilizing the development system in real life, it was able to detect similarities and events for behavior from the difference of the object caught on sight.

In this paper, we propose a robust fault estimation approach for multi-input and multioutput nonlinear dynamic systems. This approach is based on back propagation neural networks and integrates various techniques such as the augmented system approach, input-to-state stability theory, linear matrix inequality optimization, and neural network training/learning.

By combining these techniques, we are able to achieve a robust simultaneous estimate of system states and actuator faults. Our approach has been successfully applied to a 4.8 MW wind turbine benchmark system and the effectiveness of the approach has been well demonstrated.

Overall, our proposed approach is a promising solution for robust fault estimation in multi-input and multioutput nonlinear dynamic systems.

The study intends to improve walkability in the walkways by providing better illuminance levels. Firstly, the study has defined the existing typology of walkways in the campus then selected the worse type-with less protection from the sun-for further improvement. The methodological tools used in the study were: a field survey, illuminance meter, and an Integrated Environmental Solution Virtual Environment (IESVE) software packages. The questionnaire was used to understand the right feedback on the existing walkways. The lowest ranked satisfactions received from the respondents were from excessive brightness and temperature in the walkways. Thus, this paper proposes a successful envelope layout solution that provides better lighting levels and glare-free spaces. The Islamic style pattern used in the campus design was considered for the proposed simulations. Light meter was used to measure the existing illuminance levels in the corridors. Accordingly, four cases with several parameters such as the integration of shading elements: fully or partially, and vertically or horizontally in addition to the flooring materials were conducted in the simulation. Lastly, the study could provide a design layout as a proposal that provides glare-free walkways.

Predicting stock market movements is an extremely challenging task due to the complex and dynamic nature of this system. The stock market is a chaotic system, which means it is highly sensitive to even the smallest initial conditions, causing errors to compound over time, making future predictions even more challenging.

Recently, machine learning algorithms have been used to try and forecast stock prices. In this study, we test the effectiveness of a type of Recurrent Neural Network, known as a Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network, in implementing technical analysis to predict AAPL ticker prices on the NASDAQ exchange.

The performance of the model is tested with three popular output activation layers - linear, sigmoid and tanh - and trained using Adam optimizer as the back-propagation algorithm. The performance is compared using Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSE).

Our results showed that the LSTM model had an average RMSE value of 12.483 for the linear output activation layer scaled between 0 and 1. For the same activation layer scaled between -1 and 1, the average RMSE was 3.258. When using the sigmoid activation function scaled to a range of 0 and 1, the average RMSE was 21.769. The tanh activation function scaled to a range of -1 and 1 produced an average RMSE of 21.738.

In conclusion, using LSTM networks with technical analysis can be an effective method for predicting stock prices. However, the choice of activation function and scaling method can significantly impact the accuracy of predictions. Therefore, further research is needed to optimize the model and improve its accuracy.

Enabling high-speed connectivity for a vast number of IoT devices over the unlicensed spectrum poses significant challenges, such as identifying a large number of narrowband channels in a wideband spectrum, and reusing these channels to support the high density of IoT objects. This paper puts forth a novel sensing-based architecture that leverages spectral and spatial resources at a fine resolution to address these challenges.

The proposed approach involves two steps. First, a sensing assignment scheduler assigns a subset of the spectrum to each base station to sense at a high resolution. Then, a distributed sensing algorithm is employed to locally process and share sensing reports among base stations, enabling each station to obtain occupancy information for the wideband spectrum at its location. Once the bandwidth is partitioned into spatio-spectral resource blocks, a distributed resource allocation algorithm is used to maximize spatial reuse of spectral opportunities while minimizing intra-network and inter-network interference.

Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed architecture effectively identifies more spatio-spectral resources, with lower misdetection of incumbents. Consequently, more IoT devices can be connected with limited interference into incumbents. The proposed distributed algorithms are more effective compared to centralized and non-cooperative schemes providing excellent performance on this challenging problem.

In the field of disease identification and diagnosis, it is crucial to pay attention to the patterns of diseases. For cotton plants, diseases tend to manifest on their leaves, flowers, and fruits. Thus, the focus of this research is on identifying and diagnosing diseases that affect cotton leaves.

To achieve this goal, a prototype android mobile application using template matching techniques has been developed. The images required for the application are sourced from various cotton farms located in the Vidharbha region. With the aid of smartphones connected to the internet, farmers are now able to easily identify diseases affecting their cotton crops.

The proposed system is designed to detect disease patterns at an early stage, making it easier for farmers to take necessary action to prevent further spreading of the disease. This innovative solution has the potential to significantly reduce the time and effort farmers spend on disease diagnosis, as well as enhance their yield in the long run.

This paper presents a practical procedure regarding inertia estimation and speed loop auto-tuning for sensorless interior permanent-magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) drives. In many applications, well-tuned speed controller is essential to enable dynamic and stable drive operations. However, high-performance speed controller design requires system parameters such as inertia which are unknown at the beginning of drive commissioning. Manual trial-and-error tuning is unattractive due to its blind, lengthy, non-optimal, and potentially unsafe nature. On the other hand, model-based tuning through inertia estimation has unique challenges at this step of self-commissioning. Determining the test torque for a safe and reasonably short test in inertia estimation is a real practical problem because the total inertia can be in wide range in different mechanical systems. Furthermore, feedback controllers are not usable to automatically determine the test torque due to unknown motor parameters. As a solution, this paper proposes an automated test torque selection procedure. Then it identifies the inertia and lastly tunes the speed controller using the identified parameter. Overall, a fully automated speed-loop auto-tuning method is proposed which aims minimal operator involvement. The findings are experimentally verified on an IPMSM drive. In addition, the proposed method can easily be extended to different motor types and sensored or sensorless vector control strategies.

In this paper, we explore the use of deep learning (DL) to solve a generic constrained optimization problem in wireless networks. The problem involves nonconvex objective and constraint functions, which are tackled by replacing the computation process of the solution with deep neural networks (DNNs). Our approach involves transforming the original problem into a training task for the DNNs, while subjecting them to nonconvex constraints. However, existing DL libraries are not suitable for constrained training, and thus, we propose a novel constrained training strategy based on the primal-dual method from optimization techniques. We apply this DL approach to solve transmit power allocation problems across different network configurations. Through simulation results, we demonstrate the potential of our DL method as a viable alternative to traditional optimization algorithms.

The security of IoT edge/sensor nodes is crucial as they are vulnerable to numerous attacks in the wireless sensor network domain. To ensure the trust of the IoT local area network (LAN), it is essential to authenticate edge nodes before allowing them to join the network, especially after being in sleep mode. However, this authentication process presents a non-trivial problem due to the limited resources and computational constraints of IoT nodes. Additionally, IoT devices are often placed in uncontrolled environments, making them easily accessible to potential attackers who can clone devices or steal secret keys.

To address these concerns, this paper proposes an extremely lightweight authentication scheme for constrained end-devices that are part of a given IoT LAN. Authentication occurs between the end-device and the gateway acting as an edge computing device. The proposed scheme underwent both formal and informal security verification, and its overall impact on the system was measured through voltage drop, current, and power measurements. The testing results indicate that the scheme has minimal impact on the resources, making it an efficient and secure authentication method for IoT edge/sensor nodes.

Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) refers to a group of sensors used for monitoring and recording the physical conditions of the environment and organizing the collected data at a central location. WSN has no mechanism that can organize or check the broadcast of information through the nodes. Nodes themselves are able to transmit the sensed information towards the Base Station, causing greater vulnerability of data being gathered and fiddled with. Amongst many such attacks, Rushing Attack specially is a frequently adapted strategy in On-demand protocol. The counter measure available for such kind of attack is not effective enough as most of the approaches have their own limitations. This work focuses on ill effects of Rushing Attack under different conditions with an intend to find out such limitations of each of the earlier adopted counter measures.

Security assurance in a computer system can be viewed as distinguishing between self and non-self. Artificial Immune Systems (AIS) are a class of machine learning (ML) techniques inspired by the behavior of innate biological immune systems, which have evolved to accurately classify self-behavior from non-self-behavior. This work aims to leverage AIS-based ML techniques for identifying certain behavioral traits in high level hardware descriptions, including unsafe or undesirable behaviors, whether such behavior exists due to human error during development, or due to intentional, malicious circuit modifications, known as hardware Trojans, without the need for a golden reference model. We explore the use of Negative Selection and Clonal Selection, which have historically been applied to malware detection on software binaries, to detect potentially unsafe or malicious behavior in hardware. We present a software tool which analyzes Trojan-inserted benchmarks, extracts their control and data-flow graphs (CDFGs), and uses this to train an AIS behavior model, against which new hardware descriptions may be tested. The proposed model is capable of detecting the specified (Trojan or Trojan-like) behavior with an accuracy of ~85% and an average false negative rate of 12.6% for Negative Selection and 12.8% for Clonal Selection.

The concept of qualitative simulation is central to qualitative reasoning, so it is worth considering its properties in more detail. Some of these properties have been extensively worked out and proven formally to apply to any theory of qualitative dynamics. Others are based more on experience with qualitative simulation techniques applied to a variety of problems and domains. We begin by summarizing the basic ideas, bringing together concepts introduced in chapters 5, 6, and 7. Then we discuss how existence and continuity interact with reasoning about change. Finally, we discuss some formal properties of qualitative simulation, ending with an open question.

In this paper, we propose an observer-based super-twisting sliding mode control with fuzzy variable gains (OST-FVG) for general second-order nonlinear systems. First, the super-twisting observer with fuzzy variable gains is designed for state estimation, for which we show finite-time convergence of the estimation error to zero under the bounded disturbance. Then, together with the proposed observer, the sliding mode control with fuzzy variable gains is designed to ensure precise tracking control performance and to alleviate the chattering phenomenon. We apply the OSTFVG to the overactuated quadrotor modeled by the second-order nonlinear system within the quaternion framework, which resolves underactuation and singularity problems appeared in standard quadrotors. In simulation results of attitude and position control, the fuzzy mechanism implemented in the OSTFVG guarantees faster convergence of the quadrotor to the desired position and more precision tracking performance compared to the standard observer-based super-twisting sliding mode control.

To address the need for continuous and localized brain electrical activity recordings, implantable neurosensing systems are often used. However, current systems involve highly invasive procedures that can interrupt day-to-day activities. In this paper, we present an approach for developing a device that can obtain neural data during normal activity without hindering the quality of life. For the first time, we introduce the design and application of improved neural probes for a fully-passive wireless brain implant. The integration of these neural probes to the neurosensing system results in enhanced impedance matching capable of sensing neural signals as low as 15 μVpp and improves the RF sensitivity to approximately -135 dBm, allowing for recording of all neural activity.

Feature extraction is to transform a text document from any format into a list of features that can be easily processed by text classification techniques. Feature extraction is one of significant preprocessing techniques in data mining and text classification that computes features value in documents. Hence, efficient feature extraction techniques like the BM25 and term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) techniques are normally utilized in term weighting. Nevertheless, BM25 is not a single function that is utilized to exceedingly correct very long documents. This problem cannot denote the helpfulness or importance of confident features, and decreases the efficiency of classification. This paper presents a comparative study of feature extraction techniques. Two techniques were evaluated BM25 and TF-IDF to weight the terms on Twitter. In this paper, TF-IDF feature extraction technique is presented to compare between the two techniques. The experiments show that TF-IDF improves the performance evaluation of feature extraction according to the maximum value of F1-measure is 89.77 for TF-IDF and 89.16 for BM25.

Existing forensic techniques for image manipulation localization crucially assume that probe pixels belong to one of exactly two classes, genuine or manipulated. This letter argues that this convention fuels mis-labeling particularly in unsupervised settings, where singular but genuine content or the presence of multiple distinct manipulations may easily induce non-optimal partitions of the feature space. We propose to relax constraints via a greedy n-ary clustering approach, which we instantiate exemplarily in the popular pixel descriptor space of residual co-occurrences. Experimental results on widely used public benchmark datasets highlight the benefits of our approach.

In recent years, healthcare administrations have been transitioning to digital systems, leading to an increase in networked medical devices and medical telemetry. The digitization of medical devices has revolutionized the medical industry, providing new areas of therapeutic and diagnostic treatments and improving the accessibility and quality of healthcare. These state-of-the-art medical devices are now portable, networked, and capable enough to facilitate human lives, offering a promising future for healthcare facilities.

Despite its advantages, the healthcare sector is also facing security breaches due to security flaws in medical devices. As these devices are network-connected, their attack surface has significantly increased. Unfortunately, these devices were not designed with security as a significant design constraint, and as such, flaws are present. Researchers from industry and academia have studied and demonstrated security vulnerabilities in more than a hundred devices. To mitigate the risks, this survey studied state-of-the-art solutions and countermeasures along with applicable regulations in literature.

Given that medical devices are life-critical and can cause deaths, this survey is significant in identifying the loopholes in medical devices and countermeasures available to researchers. The conclusion highlights open research areas that need consideration to secure these life-critical medical devices.

Agriculture plays a crucial role in India, and the application of modern technologies can significantly improve the situation for farmers and decision makers in this field. Python serves as a front-end tool for analyzing agricultural datasets, while Jupyter Notebook is used for data mining to predict crop production. The dataset incorporates essential parameters such as precipitation, temperature, reference crop, evapotranspiration, area, production, and yield for the season from January to December for the years 2000 to 2018. High levels of accuracy can be realized through the application of data mining techniques such as K-Means Clustering, KNN, SVM, and Bayesian network algorithm.

The Naive Bayes Classifier is a widely used and effective method, especially for document classification and large datasets. It works by assigning instances a class label based on the maximum posterior probability, under the assumption that instance features are independent. However, when a class is composed of many different components, the many-to-one assumption can be applied. An important issue is how to construct these components for each class.

To address this issue, we propose a heuristic solution of using a hierarchical tree to assign components to classes. Our evaluation experiments show that this approach outperforms the conventional one when the training data size is sufficiently large. We also discuss other challenges in implementing the many-to-one assumption.

Overall, our proposed solution offers a simple and effective approach for constructing class components in the many-to-one assumption, which can further improve the accuracy of the Naive Bayes Classifier.

The issue of mobile malware is becoming increasingly prevalent and affects users on a global scale. Malicious individuals and organizations have been able to mask their harmful payloads within seemingly benign applications, subsequently distributing them through major app stores such as Google Play Store. Despite efforts to combat the escalation of these malicious applications, app stores are struggling to keep up. Signature-based methods of detection, such as those utilized in antivirus software, are proving to be limited, prompting the development and exploration of new machine learning-based approaches to bolster mobile malware detection methods. These new approaches utilize both static and dynamic characteristics of the application, analyzing behavior in addition to the static components. This paper provides an overview of current machine learning-based mobile malware detection approaches utilizing a combination of static, dynamic, and hybrid analysis. Advantages, limitations, and comparisons are also presented.

To detect the position of moving vehicles, a wireless power and data transfer (WPDT) system is required to supply power to the wireless passive sensor placed in the direction of travel. However, in cases where the vehicle is high-speed and the sensor environment is compact, such as on railways or roadways, the sensor's operation is hindered by charging time and range limitations due to its small size. To improve the working zone of the compact sensor, this paper presents a longitudinally misalignment-insensitive dual-band WPDT system with an extended working zone.

The proposed system utilizes dual transmitting and receiving coils operating at different frequencies to achieve high isolation between the power and data links. The system comprises a distributed antenna array with a gap between antenna elements for wireless power transfer at 27.1 MHz and an extended rectangular loop for data communications at 4.23 MHz. With this system, an extended working zone of approximately 112% at 0.25 m distance is achievable in comparison with a traditional system with dual square coils. Moreover, the proposed system achieves uniform received signals within a misalignment of up to 0.53 m.

In summary, the proposed longitudinally misalignment-insensitive dual-band WPDT system with an extended working zone enhances the detection of moving vehicles in compact sensor environments, such as on railways or roadways. The system achieves high isolation between the power and data links and an extended working zone.

A new recursive identification algorithm with output weighted cosine basis functions (WCS) is investigated for the time-varying systems. After introducing a weight factor to the output of a time-varying process within the current time window, the weighted time-varying parameters, which are expanded into the virtual even periodic functions, are explicitly approximated by the cosine series. Following the orthogonality of the trigonometric functions, the parameter estimation problem becomes to the estimation problem of the series coefficients with respect to each degree of the cosine harmonic term in recursive manner. It is demonstrated that weight factor decreases the degree of cosine series and suppress the series approximation error so that the proposed algorithm has better tracking performance for rapid-variation than the conventional basis functions based identification algorithms and the existing standard methods such as RLS, LMS/NLMS, AP/BOP.

In computer numerical control machine tools, using machining simulation to prevent collision have become more popular due to higher machining speed. The 3D reconstruction of objects is one of the main goals for 3D machine vision is presented in this paper. In the stereo vision, a 2D edge feature detection algorithm designed by integration of vision base image processing which can generate a new straight line on the edges of the object. The matching comparison process is solved with the Normalized Cross Correlation (NCC) to obtain the results of a new straight line matching to find disparity from distance between feature points on plane. The disparity can be obtained from two cameras by overlapped two objects that show the different positions of two objects in horizontal using the principles of geometry of two cameras. The different position results can find the coordinates of 3D (x, y, z) to be generating the straight lines on edge of the 3D objects. This method is simply and easier in the computing process for the reconstruction of the object. The results obtain are presented with an effective and accurate model and can take results input into the 3D recognition process.

Ad-hoc Mobile Cloud (AMC) was developed as a solution to the connectivity challenges faced in Mobile Cloud computing (MCC). In AMC, mobile devices form groups to share their resources, including Web Services, Storage, and Computing resources. However, potential participants in AMC are concerned about losing control over their personal and confidential data during resource sharing. To address this issue, a trust management system is needed to safeguard the interests of the participating mobile devices. 

This study proposes a Multi-Criteria Trust Management system (MCTM) architecture for AMC that identifies trustworthy mobile devices and alerts participants of any malicious acts. An evaluation procedure was conducted, which showed that the proposed architecture achieved a high level of precision compared to other existing research. 

The MCTM system provides mobile users with the confidence to participate in the AMC system, knowing that their personal and confidential data is protected. By implementing this trust management system, AMC can increase its appeal to users who wish to share resources through mobile devices.

Speech separation is a technique used to separate individual voices from an audio mixture of multiple simultaneous talkers. However, audio-only approaches tend to perform poorly when the speakers are of the same gender or share similar voice characteristics. This is due to difficulties in learning appropriate feature representations to separate voices in single frames and streaming voices across time. To address this challenge, the proposed audio-visual deep clustering model (AVDC) integrates visual signals of speech, such as lip movements to learn better feature representations for Time-Frequency (T-F) bin clustering.

The AVDC model employs a two-stage audio-visual fusion strategy where speaker-wise audio-visual T-F embeddings are first computed after the first-stage fusion to model the audio-visual correspondence for each speaker. In the second-stage fusion, audio-visual embeddings of all speakers and audio embeddings calculated by deep clustering from the audio mixture are concatenated to form the final T-F embedding for clustering. The proposed AVDC model outperformed audio-only deep clustering and utterance-level permutation invariant training baselines and three other state-of-the-art audio-visual approaches. Furthermore, the AVDC model learned better T-F embeddings for managing the source permutation problem across frames, and it can generalize across different numbers of speakers between training and testing and shows some robustness when visual information is partially missing.

With the rapid advancements in natural language processing technologies, there has been an increasing number of text steganographic methods based on automatic text generation technology in recent years. These methods utilize the self-learning and feature extraction abilities of neural networks to learn the feature expression of vast amounts of normal text. Consequently, the models can generate dense steganographic texts that follow statistical distribution based on the learned statistical patterns. In this letter, we have observed that the conditional probability distribution of each word in the automatically generated steganographic texts gets distorted once embedded with hidden information. Thus, we have employed recurrent neural networks to extract these feature distribution changes and classify them into cover text and stego text categories. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model can achieve high detection accuracy. Moreover, our proposed model can effectively estimate the amount of hidden information embedded in the generated steganographic text by leveraging the subtle differences in the feature distribution of texts.

Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging plays a crucial role in the topographic and tomographic imaging of planetary surfaces and sub-surfaces. However, SAR imaging has also been utilized in the exploration of the interior of comets. The application of time-domain back-projection and a straightforward ray-bending solution has allowed for the imaging of the icy interior of comets, taking into consideration the bulk dielectric property of such areas. 

In conclusion, SAR imaging has proven to be an essential tool in understanding various astronomical bodies, including comets, and continues to enhance our understanding of the universe as a whole.

This work evaluates strategies to reduce the computational cost of Gabriel graph-based classifiers, in order to make them more suitable for hardware implementation. An analysis of the impact of the bit precision provides insights on the model's robustness for lower precision arithmetic. Additionally, a parallelization technique is proposed in order to improve the efficiency of the support edges computation. The results show that the lower bit precision models are statistically equivalent to the reference double-precision ones. Also, the implementation of the proposed parallel algorithm provides a significant reduction in the running time when applied in large datasets, while maintaining its accuracy.

Relationship between the delay and Doppler shift with the radar return is nonlinear in nature. Therefore, a nonlinear estimator based on sparse kernel least mean square algorithm is proposed. Further, an adaptive kernel width optimization technique is proposed to lower the computational complexity and for simple implementation. An expression for the Cramer-Rao lower bound is derived and validated for the proposed estimator over linear frequency modulated, and orthogonal frequency division multiplexed radar systems.

Enhancing the contrast of target and clutter is a crucial issue in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image target detection. In this paper, we define a novel subspace, called minimal clutter-to-signal ratio (MCSR) subspace, which can minimize the clutter-to-signal ratio (CSR) by projecting the feature vector to the subspace. Based on MCSR, a novel polarimetric contrast enhancement method is proposed. The MCSR subspace is learned based on the commonly used polarimetric feature vectors extracted from the labeled training SAR image pixels. The feature vectors extracted form candidate SAR image pixels are projected to the MCSR subspace. By calculating the square norm of each transformed feature vector, an enhanced image can be obtained. It is demonstrated that the existing optimization of polarimetric contrast enhancement (OPCE) is a special case of the proposed method to some extent. Experimental results show that our method outperforms the traditional OPCE method on the RadarSat-2 SAR data.

Web engineering is a subtopic of software engineering that focuses on the development of software applications for the web. While software engineering covers various sub-processes for different systems, the packaging and delivery sub-process for web applications has not been given enough attention. This paper aims to address this issue by presenting two research topics. Firstly, a systematic mapping review was conducted to gather current contributions on packaging and delivery for sub-processes. Secondly, an elicitation process was carried out in a real setting to refine the map of activities involved in the packaging and delivery sub-process. This research aims to contribute to improving the packaging and delivery sub-process for web applications.

The extreme learning machine (ELM) is an algorithm used for training feedforward neural networks. It has been widely accepted as suitable for both multiclass classification and multivariate regression problems. However, recent research has shown that the closed-form ELM solution is not optimal for multivariate regression problems since it overlooks correlations between the different target variables. In light of this, we propose an improved algorithm called canonical ELM, which takes into account the correlations between the target variables while adhering to the ELM principle of learning without iteratively updating the weights in the network.

We conducted experiments using both synthetic and real-world datasets, and our results demonstrate that the proposed canonical ELM algorithm achieves higher prediction accuracy than the ELM algorithm. Additionally, the canonical ELM algorithm is shown to be more stable.

In conclusion, this paper highlights a new approach for improving the ELM algorithm's accuracy in multivariate regression problems by accounting for correlations between the target variables. Our proposed canonical ELM algorithm shows promising results and presents a viable alternative for improving the ELM algorithm in this context.

Most current face recognition systems utilize Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) for their functionality. These types of networks are trained using huge numbers of face images with the aim of capturing identity information in a compact form. Recognition is then carried out by assessing the similarity or distance between these captured descriptors. Nevertheless, in reality, these descriptors contain intra-class variability such as pose and expressions. To tackle this issue, loss-functions or metric learning modules must be implemented to ensure that the learned descriptors maximize the inter-class differences and minimize the intra-class variance in the feature space. Instead, we approach this issue by noticing that the descriptors affiliated with images of the same subject share similar patterns in the highest activation units on average. We demonstrate our assumption by proving that accuracy can be boosted in a template-based recognition situation by keeping descriptor bins with the average highest activation and setting all other bins to zero. These activation patterns also serve to construct identity-representative binary masks used in place of descriptors for matching templates. Through experimentation performed on the IJB-A dataset, we show that this strategy significantly increases recognition accuracy.

We present MCF3D, a Multi-stage Complementary Fusion Three-Dimensional (3D) object detection network designed for various applications including autonomous driving, robot navigation, and virtual reality. This end-to-end learnable architecture takes both LIDAR point clouds and RGB images as inputs and employs a 3D region proposal subnet and second stage detector(s) subnet to generate precise 3D bounding box prediction in an oriented manner. By exploiting the strength of multimodal information, we have designed a series of fine and targeted fusion methods grounded on the attention mechanism and prior knowledge including “pre-fusion,” “anchor-fusion,” and “proposal-fusion”. We have also introduced an RGB-Intensity form that incorporates reflection intensity into the input image to boost representational power, and a proposal-element attention module that allows the network to focus more on essential information with minimal overheads. Furthermore, we have proposed a cascade-enhanced detector that is more selective against near false positives. Our MCF3D method’s robustness has been demonstrated via experiments conducted on the demanding KITTI benchmark, producing state-of-the-art results and running in near real-time with low memory footprint.

Measures of node centrality that describe the importance of a node within a network are crucial for understanding the behavior of social networks and graphs. In this paper, we address the problem of distributed node centrality identification. In particular, we focus our attention on alpha-centrality, which can be seen as a generalization of eigenvector centrality, particularly suitable for graphs with asymmetric interactions. In this setting, our contribution is twofold: first we derive a distributed protocol where agents can locally compute their alpha-centrality index by means of local interactions; then we propose a novel consensus-algorithm running in parallel to the alpha-centrality estimator, which converges towards a weighted average of the initial conditions, where the weights are dictated by the alpha-centrality vector. The proposed algorithm finds application in social networks, where agreement protocols typically place more value on experts and influencers than on the rest of users. Simulations results are provided to corroborate the theoretical findings.

Alfa-Beta method has extensively used since its formulation by Akagi in 1983 [1] and become the classical wide spread solution for shunt active power filtering.For majority of situations this has a good efficiency and simplicity both for analogical and digital implementation. The development of vector 3D method gives o more rigorous approach, with the price of a more complex and expensive implementation, sometimes unjustified. However, for some special cases its utility is revealed.The purpose of the paper is to derive a comparative analysis of these methods, in a unitary way, based on geometrical representation and vector variables which enable a good evaluation from qualitative and quantitative point of view of characteristics and specific problems. Thus, may be revealed the steps and connections where problems occur with corresponding effects.The tools implied are 2D and 3D simulations for the parameter evolution when the algorithms are suited. The Mathcad mathematical interpreter enables a natural representation of vector operations, easy to be verified formally.

The aim of this short paper or extended abstract is develop an intelligent lifelong learning cancer care framework that will be adapted by the King Hussein Cancer Center in Jordan. Cancer Care is defined as "Comprehensive care for the cancer patient as a whole including all their needs - not just the medical and physical ones - using the services of many professionals working together" [3] . Lifelong learning is about continuous development throughout a life time. Our lives, as humans, span many decades in which the environment we grew up in is in a continuous state of change. Therefore, we need to be empowered to deal with emerging challenges and thrive in a continuously changing environment. Clearly, there are multiple interactions that take place between an individual human and the surrounding environment. The Oxford dictionary defines "interaction" as "Communication or direct involvement with someone or something". Another definition: "A particular way in which matter, fields, and atomic and subatomic particles affect one another, e.g., through gravitation or electromagnetism" [4] . Therefore, communication though interactions takes place and in certain times for precious causes and purposes. On the one hand, such communication is didactic with complex interactions between an individual and the environment, and on the other hand between an individual and other members of the community - who themselves are continuously changing.

JavaScript plays an important role in web applications and services, which is used by millions of web pages in optimizing interface design, embedding dynamic texts, reading and writing HTML elements, validating form data, responding to browser events, controlling cookies and much more. However, since JavaScript is cross-platform and can be executed dynamically, it has been a major vehicle for web-based attacks. Existing solutions work by performing static analysis or monitoring program execution dynamically. However, since the heavy use of obfuscation techniques, many methods no longer apply to malicious JavaScript code detection, and it has been a huge challenge to de-obfuscate obfuscated malicious JavaScript code accurately. In this paper, we propose a hybrid analysis method combining static and dynamic analysis for detecting malicious JavaScript code that works by first conducting syntax analysis and dynamic instrumentation to extract internal features that are related to malicious code and then performing classification-based detection to distinguish attacks. In addition, based on code instrumentation, we propose a new method which can deobfuscate part of obfuscated malicious JavaScript code accurately. Ultimately, we implement a browser plug-in called MJDetector and perform evaluation on 450 real web pages. Evaluation results show that our method can detect malicious JavaScript code and de-obfuscate obfucation effectively and efficiently. Specifically, MJDetector can detect JavaScipt attacks in current web pages with high accuracy 94.76% and de-obfuscate obfuscate code of specific types with accuracy 100% whereas the base line method can only detect with accuracy 81.16% and has no capacity of de-obfuscation.

Electricity is an essential source of power for gadgets, machinery, and other electronic goods at both the household and industrial levels. However, the majority of the world's electric grids operate on fossil fuels that are becoming scarcer each day. As a result, the best solution available is to implement a Smart Grid, which integrates information sensing, transmission, and processing to achieve the extensive use of sustainable energy sources. Today, the Internet of Things (IoT) technology plays a significant role in the construction of power grids. This paper aims to review the ways in which IoT has been integrated into Smart Grids.

Although IoT-integrated Smart Grid systems are already deployed, the full capabilities of instant knowledge and sustainable large-scale data processing have yet to be fully realized. There are two main architectures of IoT integrated Smart Grids: the four-layered architecture and web-enabled Smart Grid. To process and manage the Big Data in Smart Grids, the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system is used, which can be further enhanced with cloud computing.

The Smart Grid is the future of electric grids, solving problems related to information flows, rising energy consumption, energy waste, reliability, and security in conventional power grids. By integrating IoT technology and sustainable energy sources, the Smart Grid system not only meets the energy requirements of the present but also ensures that future generations can continue to derive benefits from it.

Color retinal images have been widely used in diagnosis and screening of ophthalmic diseases. Macula detection and fovea location in retinal images are important steps in grading and diagnosis of ophthalmic diseases. However, due to the weaker reflection of the macula, it is difficult to determine the fovea accurately by the lack of clear border in the macula. An efficient method for detecting and locating macula based on morphological features fitting is proposed. The macula area is detected by its low brightness and round shape features. And then the K-means clustering and circle fitting is applied to achieve accurate position of macular center. A series of tests show good performance in the public retinal images database. Thus the proposed method based on morphological features fitting is proved to be efficient and useful for computer-aided diagnosis of ocular diseases.

This paper presents a co-dynamic simulation of a wind turbine with a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) that has been implemented on a field programmable gate array (FPGA) board. The wind energy conversion system (WECS) includes various components such as the wind turbine model, pitch angle and maximum power point tracking (MPPT) controllers, generator model, and the control schemes of power converters for the machine and grid sides.

By utilizing an FPGA board for computational purposes, this study confirms that the simulation speed is notably higher in comparison to traditional computing methods. This is especially true for parallelized operations. Overall, the results of this simulation study demonstrate a feasible approach for implementing PMSG-based wind turbines in real-time applications.

In conclusion, the use of FPGA boards allows for a faster and more efficient simulation process of wind turbines when compared to traditional computing methods. By implementing this technology, it becomes possible to perform simulations in real-time and provide feasible solutions for the future of wind turbine research and development.

Sequential far infrared (FIR) image mosaic is a challenging task due to repeated patterns, low contrast, image blurring, illumination change, and sparse structure. In this paper, a novel matching approach is proposed for the sequential FIR image registration, which is based on coarse-to-fine strategy and grid-based motion statistics (GMS). In the coarse matching step, a transitive relation is deduced to obtain the coordinate relations of the current registering image and its adjacent images to ensure enough number of feature points and guarantee the accuracy of the preregistration results. In the fine matching step, a principle for fine-tuning registration and a strategy for changing the distribution of the feature points are developed for finding most appropriate feature points. Based on the point pairs, the position of the current registering image can be accurately located. Besides, an effective post-processing, such as gray-scale non-uniformity correction and mosaic seam elimination, is also utilized to refine the fine-tuning results to achieve the promising mosaic effect. A comparative study and quantitative evaluation with commercial software or representative image mosaic algorithm demonstrate that better quality results can be obtained by using the proposed method.

Cloud computing is an Internet-based service which provides shared virtual resource and data to accomplish certain computation. In order for the servers to have sufficient resources when the request arrives, as well as save server resources as much as possible, we propose a prediction-based server capacity planning and dynamic scheduling algorithm. There are mainly three steps in our capacity planning algorithm. The first step characterizes the given data on several indices and then present an effective model in order to predict the oncoming demands in the near future. The second step generates the workload of servers combined with the predicted demands and then make capacity planning based on this workload. Thus it's obvious that the effectiveness of capacity planning depends on the accuracy of prediction to a great extent. Finally, a demand prediction based strategy on workload allocation is brought out. A dynamic resource allocation strategy is given to ensure the quality of service at any moment in future meanwhile taking energy consumption into consideration. The results of the experiment show that the required server number decreases by 33% after the prediction-based capacity planning applying on server scheduling.

In this modern era research in mechanical ventilator model designing has increased a lot. Mathematical model of lungs is used to distinguish the pulmonary diseases. In this work bond graph model of breathing mechanism i.e. inspiration and expiration of lungs is developed. Hydraulic analogies are allocated to lungs using cylinders and accumulators. From nostrils to trachea single cylinder is considered having resistance and compliance effect associated with it. Trachea to lower lung section comprised of 23 generations of airways. In this study, 2 generations are considered with resistance, compliance and inertial effect, whereas resistance and compliance effect, of 3rd to 17th generations are lumped. These generations are modelled with cylinders with decreasing sizes. 17 to 23 are modelled as accumulators with resistance and compliance. Model parameters were estimated using grey box estimation.20 sim is used to make the bond graph model and determine the relationship of pressure and volume curves. Model can be used for screening of lungs diseases. Model can be used for clinical trials with any existing mechanical ventilator.

In conventional point cloud delivery, a sender uses octree-based digital video compression to stream three-dimensional (3D) points and the corresponding color attributes over band-limited links, e.g., wireless channels, for 3D scene reconstructions. However, the digital-based delivery schemes have an issue called cliff effect, where the 3D reconstruction quality is a step function in terms of wireless channel quality. We propose a novel scheme of point cloud delivery, called HoloCast, to gracefully improve the reconstruction quality with the improvement of wireless channel quality. HoloCast regards the 3D points and color components as graph signals and directly transmits linear-transformed signals based on graph Fourier transform (GFT), without digital quantization and entropy coding operations. One of main contributions in HoloCast is that the use of GFT can deal with non-ordered and non-uniformly distributed multidimensional signals such as holographic data unlike conventional delivery schemes. Performance results with point cloud data show that HoloCast yields better 3D reconstruction quality compared to digital-based methods in noisy wireless environment.

This paper presents the design and implementation of long-range self-powered wireless IoT devices that utilize nRF52840 and energy-harvesting technologies. The devices are tested in both star and multi-hop configurations, using optimized custom protocols to achieve improved performance. In both configurations, the nodes consume less power than what they harvest from an indoor light environment, using a small 0.36W monocrystalline solar panel. The average power by which the battery was charged during the test was measured at 941.94μW. Each node can operate for 12 months with a fully charged 120mAh rated rechargeable coin cell battery with a 55s transmission interval. The devices are capable of transmitting coded data over a line of sight range of up to 1.8km. Additional sensors (temperature, relative humidity, and visible light) are integrated into the nodes, making them versatile and suitable for various IoT applications.

The Weapon-Target Assignment (WTA) problem is a critical aspect of air defense command and control, and thus it is imperative to find an efficient solution. This paper proposes an improved Artificial Fish Swarm Algorithm (AFSA) for this purpose. The AFSA is enhanced by incorporating Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to modify individual vision and a genetic operator to avoid the local extremum trap. The proposed algorithm is validated with cooperative air defense examples, and simulation results show an improved computational accuracy and rate of convergence in solving the WTA problem.

In this paper, the angle-of-arrival (AOA) measurements are adapted to locate a target using the UAV swarms equipped with passive receivers. The measurement noise is considered to be target-to-receiver distance dependent. The Cramer-Rao low bound (CRLB) of the AOA localization is calculated, and the optimal deployments are explored through changing angular separations and distances. Then, a distributed collaborative autonomous generation (DCAG) method is proposed based on the deep neural network (NN). The off-line training and on-line application rules are applied to generate the optimal heading angles for the UAV swarms in the AOA localization. The simulation results show that through the DCAG method, the generated heading angles for UAV swarms enhance the localization accuracy and stability.

Fuzzy co-clustering induced by multinomial mixture model (FCCMM) is one of the effective methods for analyzing cooccurrence information data. In FCCMM, we have to determine the number of clusters in advance. Furthermore, we have to select the best solution from a lot of trials with various patterns of the number of clusters and random initial values. In Gaussian mixture models, a robust EM clustering algorithm, which is robust to initial values and can automatically estimate the optimal number of clusters, have been proposed in order to resolve such problems. It introduces an entropy-based penalty term with respect to cluster volumes to the objective function of the standard EM algorithm and obtains the optimal number of clusters by continually eliminating clusters with low competitiveness in volumes. In this paper, we propose a method which automatically estimates the optimal number of clusters without being influenced by the initial values by introducing the entropy-based penalty term with respect to cluster volumes to the objective function of FCCMM in a similar manner to the robust EM algorithm and demonstrate its estimation performance through numerical experiments.

Common security tools produce vast amounts of data that can be further analyzed. Unfortunately, the raw data can be too complex, leading to an overwhelming number of records and the loss of crucial information. In response, we introduce a system to visualize data originating from a DNS firewall and elaborate on the process of highlighting important data points for incident handlers. Our prototype proves that visualizations are viable, striking a balance between data volume and granularity.

In recent literature, there has been a significant amount of emphasis placed on the estimation of the side-slip angle, as this information is pivotal in controlling vehicle systems. In this study, we propose an innovative Kalman filter observer for side-slip angle that relies on the Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy modeling of vehicle non-linear lateral dynamics. With the estimated side-slip angle, we then propose a fuzzy logic direct yaw moment controller to enhance vehicle performance. We present simulation results to validate the effectiveness of both the estimator and the controller.

Camera-based lane detection and vehicle tracking algorithms are critical for the success of many autonomous systems. The navigation of these systems is heavily dependent on the output of detection algorithms. However, lane detection algorithms require substantial pre-processing time and computational effort, and they are susceptible to environmental conditions and require regular updates. This paper proposes the use of machine learning techniques and computer vision algorithms for lane and vehicle tracking in an autonomous vehicle control scenario. The proposed system can handle complex image problems, allowing for the vehicle to autonomously track lanes, follow other vehicles, and stop when necessary. To achieve this, data augmentation is utilized to create diversity in the dataset, and a Convolutional Neural Network architecture based on NVIDIA's PilotNet is preferred for lane tracking. The system is also trained on the faster region-based convolutional neural network (Faster R-CNN) for object and vehicle detection, using Haar Cascade Classifier for identifying traffic lights and stop signs. All learning models are trained on the NVIDIA GTX 1070 Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) to minimize training time. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system is capable of autonomously controlling vehicles for lane and vehicle tracking purposes by vision, providing favorable results.

In this paper, we introduce a novel and robust approach to quantized matrix completion. First, we propose a rank minimization problem with constraints induced by quantization bounds. Next, we form an unconstrained optimization problem by regularizing the rank function with Huber loss. Huber loss is leveraged to control the violation from quantization bounds due to two properties: first, it is differentiable; and second, it is less sensitive to outliers than the quadratic loss. A smooth rank approximation is utilized to endorse lower rank on the genuine data matrix. Thus, an unconstrained optimization problem with differentiable objective function is obtained allowing us to advantage from gradient descent technique. Novel and firm theoretical analysis of the problem model and convergence of our algorithm to the global solution are provided. Another contribution of this letter is that our method does not require projections or initial rank estimation, unlike the state-of-the-art. In the Numerical Experiments section, the noticeable outperformance of our proposed method in learning accuracy and computational complexity compared to those of the state-of-the-art literature methods is illustrated as the main contribution.

The safe operation of transmission overhead lines is often threatened by the fast growing and tall trees that grow under the line corridor. The limited height of transmission network results in insufficient safe distance between the line and the trees, leading to tree-related faults and tripping. To prevent damage to overhead lines caused by the growth of extra tall trees, it is necessary to understand the growth rule of these trees and predict their growth height. 

This study employs the deep learning algorithm to investigate the growth rule of extra tall trees under overhead transmission lines. Various deep learning and artificial neural network algorithms, including Deep Belief Network, Auto-Encoder, and Long-Short-Term-Memory Algorithm, are used to predict tree height.
