These algorithms have been verified, and the accuracy of the combined algorithm is found to be higher than that of the single multilayer perceptron and mathematical statistical model. By using these methods, we can effectively prevent tree-related faults and ensure the safe operation of transmission overhead lines.

Lexical semantics is a subfield of linguistics that deals with the meaning of words and their variations. This chapter delves into the various forms of extending lexical meaning, the paradigmatic relations between words, and the major theories concerning lexical semantics. There are different ways in which lexical items can be used figuratively, and these are explored in detail in the chapter. Many natural language processing applications rely on structured lexical resources in their treatment processes, typically in the form of a database that provides information on the morphology and semantics of words. To represent knowledge, formalisms have been developed to establish ontologies. The key distinction between knowledge and ontology is that an ontology is language-independent, generic, and digitally available, making it easy to manipulate with a computer.

This paper investigates a grant-free non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system where massive number of users wake up and send data right away without performing a grant-based initial access procedure. Since no scheduling grant is used in this system, the base station (BS) does not know which user is transmitting on each resource. Also, due to the lack of an uplink (UL) timing control process, multiple user's signals are asynchronously received at the BS. This causes asynchronous interference, or multiuser inter-carrier and inter-symbol interference. We propose two ideas to address these two problems. We first propose an auxiliary preamble structure to successfully detect the user activity, even in the presence of a massive number of users. We, then, propose a modification to the interleave-division multiple access (IDMA) receiver to mitigate asynchronous interference. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme significantly improves the preamble detection performance and BER performance compared to the conventional schemes. Furthermore, we show that the proposed grant-free NOMA system can achieve much better performance than the grant-based NOMA system in terms of transmission time and signaling overhead.

Traditional steganography methods have a limitation in terms of their embedding capacity as they often rely on creating a mapping relationship between secret data and a cover image. A new image steganography scheme is proposed in this paper, which is based on the concept of deep learning and utilizes a U-Net structure. The deep neural network is trained in a paired manner and consists of a hiding network and an extraction network. The hiding network is used by the sender to embed the secret image into a full-size image without any changes, and the resultant image is sent to the receiver. The extraction network helps the receiver to correctly reconstruct the original cover image and the secret image. The proposed scheme overcomes the issue of visual cues and offers a higher embedding capacity by compressing and distributing the information of the secret image across all available bits in the cover image.

In this study, we utilized two machine learning algorithms, linear support vector machine (SVM) and convolutional neural network (CNN), to classify EEG data obtained from the BCI competition IV-2a 2-class MI (motor imagery) data set. The dataset consisted of signals recorded from three electrodes (C3, Cz, and C4) with a sampling rate of 250Hz, taken from 9 subjects. The training data included 400 trials from the first 3 sessions, and the evaluation data included 320 trials from the last 2 sessions. Each trial began with a 3-second fixation period followed by a one-second visual cue indicating either left or right motor imagery for 4 seconds. Features were extracted from the signals between 0.5 and 2.5 seconds after the visual cue. The signals were then bandpass filtered into delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma frequency bands and used as training data for the SVM. Additionally, we generated a 2 by 500 matrix from each training trial to train the CNN. Our CNN architecture included two convolutional layers, two fully connected layers, a batch normalization layer before the activation layer, and a dropout layer with a 50% probability after the activation layer. The classification accuracies evaluated by the averaged kappa values showed that the deep learning CNN method outperformed the classical linear SVM, with accuracies of 0.5 and 0.621, respectively.

To enhance the efficiency of life-saving equipment training and ensure the safety of trainees, this paper presents an analysis of the functional requirements of the ship lifesaving training system, followed by the design of an overall structure for the same. Through the implementation of two modes of collaborative working, the paper proposes a method of multi-role collaborative training, allowing for flexible multi-user training. The system has built a virtual database of scenes and utilizes a regular data acquisition and sending method to overcome issues faced during collaborative simulation. To fully simulate realistic situations, three-dimensional modeling software and Unity3D engine have been utilized to create scenes of varying aquatic scenarios, such as fire, stormy waves, wrecks, and men overboard. A full range of life-saving processes have been simulated, culminating in the development of a virtual training system for free-fall lifeboat. Following extensive testing, the system has proven to be stable with outstanding results for training.

Virtualization technologies have become common-place both in software development as well as engineering in a more general sense. Using virtualization offers other benefits than simulation and testing as a virtual environment can often be more liberally configured than the corresponding physical environment. This, in turn, introduces new possibilities for education and training, including both for humans and artificial intelligence (AI). To this end, we are developing a simulation platform AILiveSim. The platform is built on top of the Unreal Engine (www.unrealengine.com) game development system, and it is dedicated to training and testing autonomous systems, their sensors and their algorithms in a simulated environment. In this paper, we describe the elements that we have built on top of the engine to realize a Virtual Environment (VE) useful for the design, implementation, application and analysis of autonomous systems. We present the architecture that we have put in place to transform our simulation platform from automotive specific to be domain agnostic and support two new domains of applications: autonomous ships and autonomous mining machines. We describe the important specificity of each domain in regard to simulation.In addition, we also report the challenges encountered when simulating those applications, and the decisions taken to overcome these challenges.

This paper discusses transceiver design for uplink massive MIMO systems with channel sparsity in the angular domain. It has been discovered that sparsity-learning-based blind signal detection can retrieve data and channels using massage-passing-based sparse matrix factorization techniques. Inserting short pilot sequences in user packets can eliminate the inherent phase and permutation ambiguities in sparse matrix factorization. To efficiently utilize pilot sequences, the semi-blind channel-and-signal estimation (SCSE) scheme is proposed as it integrates the pilot sequence knowledge into the message passing algorithm for sparse matrix factorization. However, the SCSE scheme can be time-consuming when the number of users is relatively large. Thus, the simplified SCSE (S-SCSE) was developed to accommodate systems with a large number of users. Numerical results indicate that the semi-blind signal detection scheme performs significantly better than the state-of-the-art blind detection and training-based schemes in the short-pilot regime.

In this paper, we aim to compare and analyze the prediction performance of various ANFIS (Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System) models. The ANFIS model is an integration of neural networks and fuzzy systems. In the study, we analyzed the prediction performance of ANFIS models using different input space partitioning techniques.

ANFIS 1 utilized Subtractive Clustering (SC) to calculate the center of the cluster by inversely proportional potential values based on the distances of different inputs. On the other hand, ANFIS 2 applied Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering to classify each data belonging to each cluster according to degree of affiliation. ANFIS 3 is a novel method that uses Context based Fuzzy C-Means (CFCM) clustering, which considers characteristics of input and output space based on FCM clustering.

To evaluate these ANFIS models, we used short term electricity price forecasting data and Boston housing data. The Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) method was utilized to measure the prediction performance. Results revealed that the prediction performance of the ANFIS model varies depending on the data's characteristics. In addition, the prediction performance of ANFIS model using CFCM clustering method remains constant. 

In summary, this study demonstrates that ANFIS models can have various prediction performances depending on the input space partitioning method used. Furthermore, CFCM clustering can provide better and constant prediction results.

Creative problems are ill-defined, and thus experimentation, evaluation, and iteration are key elements of creative problem solving. We present a computational theory of evaluation in creative design. Our technique evaluates a design concept by analogically comparing it with alternative articulations of the concept. We operationalize this theory of analogical comparison in the context of biologically inspired design that uses biological analogies for conceptual design of technological systems. Our technique of analogical comparison supports evaluation of prior technological designs, biological source cases, as well as candidate conceptual designs through analogical mapping between alternative functional models of these design concepts. Given a functional model of a design concept and an alternative functional model of the same design concept, analogical comparison leverages a novel hierarchically organized analogical mapping technique to align the two models and identify the differences between them. Our technique is implemented in an operational artificial intelligence agent called Design Evaluation through Simulation and Comparison (DESC). We evaluate DESC through computational experimentation across several models to illustrate its strengths and limits and to highlight areas for future research.

A novel approach for recognizing Chinese sign language (CSL) using multimodal fusion has been proposed. The approach, known as the LSTM2+CHMM model, employs both a dual long short-term memory (LSTM) and a couple hidden Markov model (CHMM) to merge hand and skeleton sequence data. The approach is unique in that it utilizes a hand segmentation algorithm based on power rate transforms and RGB-D image fusion, which effectively overcomes the limitations commonly encountered with complex backgrounds, inconsistent lighting, and variable skin tones. As a result, the proposed skeleton-hand fusion framework can be used to recognize sign language in non-specific environments by non-specific individuals. Additionally, the LSTM2+CHMM model uses probability theory and neural networks to offer a unified methodology for multiple-sequence fusion. Experimental results using two CSL datasets indicate that the proposed SLR framework is effective.

Ultra Dense Networks (UDN) have become one of the key technologies for 5G wireless communications, which can meet the requirements of high-traffic, high-density wireless terminal access. Compared with LTE, there are a large number of heterogeneous cells in UDN. If a failure occurs and can't be alleviated its effect in time, it will lead to a significant drop in network performance. Therefore, the cell outage compensation (COC) problem in the UDN is very important. Although deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has been applied to many scenarios related to the self-organizing network (SON), there are fewer applications for cell outage compensation. In this paper, aiming at the cell outage scenario in the UDN with the goal of maximizing the sum of the throughput of all users while meeting service quality demands of each mobile user, and present a framework based on DRL to solve it. Specifically, we first allocate compensation users to adjacent BSs by using the K-means clustering algorithm, then apply a deep neural network (DNN) to approximate action-value function. The simulation results show that the algorithm converges quickly and tends to be stable, and reach 99.53% of the maximum throughput. It verifies the efficiency of the DRL-based framework and its effectiveness in meeting the requirement of user rates and handling cell interrupt compensation.

With the growing advancements in human-computer interaction technology, understanding user emotions during natural language communication has become a crucial research topic. While previous studies have mainly focused on analyzing emotions within a single long sentence, it is important to note that in real-life interaction, people often use multi-round dialogue to convey information and emotions. Thus, in this paper, we present a new approach to identify the emotions involved in multi-round conversations between individuals in various scenarios by developing an emotional sequence. 

To achieve this, we have used several novels as analysis corpus and segmented each scene according to the chapters of the novel. We analyzed the emotional bias of each conversation between different individuals for these scenes and constructed an emotional matrix between people for each scenario. We then applied the LSTM algorithm to mine various emotional patterns and analyze the changing trends between people in comparison to machine learning algorithms. The results obtained from our experiments demonstrate that our sequential-based emotion recognition method can accurately recognize the emotions between two individuals in multi-round conversations and predict future emotional patterns.

Overall, our research introduces a better approach to analyze emotions involved in multi-round conversations between individuals to improve human-computer interaction.

Business process and requirement specification are crucial phases in the software development process. Yet, business and requirement modeling are often carried out separately by different languages and design teams, leading to misaligned models. The degree of misalignment grows continuously with their independent evolution. Thus, the potential of model-driven software development cannot be fully exploited. There is a considerable agreement among researchers about the integration technique roles to bridge the gap between heterogeneous models. Therefore, this approach is based on this technique to align the business world represented by BPMN and the software requirement world represented by the UML use case. We define an integrated meta-model that incorporates all BPMN and use case elements as well as new others to map traceable elements. Further, we define a new diagram that provides a means to visualize and combines their use within an integrated model. Our approach supplements CASE tools with additional information and relationships to maintain the global system consistency. To illustrate it, we implement an editor for designing the proposed diagram, and we apply it in a topical case study.

This research paper provides a brief description of the wireless sensor network and the protocol to be used. Through this technology, benefits are obtained that provide the sensor networks together with greater freedom when placing the sensors in the vicinity of the target. In wireless sensor networks, routing is a critical and important aspect. The work focuses on the performance of the quality of services in the wireless sensor network (WSN) under the AODV routing protocol. This document tries to characterize the AODV protocol by performing simulations in the NS3 (Network Simulator Version 3) program. In the simulations of the AODV protocol, a set of metrics that can be used for comparisons in different scenarios are shown. The main objective of this document will be to offer a suitable simulation environment to determine the operation of the protocol to be used in wireless sensor networks.

With the gradual deployment of space-based wireless networks, security risks in data communication between satellites and even the internal structure of a satellite have become increasingly significant. In this article, we focus specifically on the security threats to satellite internal communications. We begin by summarizing the crucial security requirements for space-based wireless networks. Next, we describe three common attack approaches for satellite platforms based on the MIL-STD-1553B bus. Finally, we present the results of attack simulations and propose some protective mechanisms to counter these threats.

DNA microarrays are a powerful tool for detecting genetic changes associated with cancer. This is accomplished by analyzing the expression of thousands of genes simultaneously. However, the large amount of data produced by this process makes it difficult to identify the most important genes for cancer classification. Although previous research has applied Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO) techniques to select the most relevant genes, they have not achieved high classification accuracy due to problems with local stagnation.

To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved version of the BPSO algorithm (iBPSO) to improve gene selection for cancer classification. The proposed iBPSO algorithm was tested using Naive-Bayes (NB), k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifiers with stratified 5-fold cross-validation. The results showed that the proposed iBPSO algorithm was more effective in terms of classification accuracy and the number of selected genes compared to standard BPSO on six benchmark cancer microarray datasets. Moreover, the iBPSO algorithm was able to effectively escape from local minima stagnation, which is a major obstacle in BPSO-based gene selection approaches.

Overall, the proposed iBPSO algorithm has demonstrated its potential for improving the accuracy of cancer classification by selecting the most relevant genes from a large pool of data generated by DNA microarrays. This approach has important implications for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment optimization.

There is a growing need for precise short-term travel-time prediction in urban settings in order to build an advanced intelligent transportation system (ITS). Probe data is becoming a popular data collection technology; however, the penetration rate of probe vehicles that are capable of providing probe data is currently limited. Most research on short-term travel-time prediction tends to aggregate probe data to obtain valuable samples when the penetration rate is low. While this approach can work well, it only provides a general description of travel time and may neglect changes in travel time during a short time interval. To overcome this limitation, a non-parametric model using disaggregate probe data was developed in this study based on dynamic time warping (DTW). 

In this model, data from the crossing direction are introduced to separate the data into different signal phases, rather than identifying the exact signal pattern. The proposed model was compared to a classical k-nearest neighbor (KNN) model and a naive model, and then tested in three scenarios: a computer simulation and two real cases from Nagoya, Japan. The results showed that the proposed model outperforms the other two models under different data penetration rates since it can reflect changes in travel time during a traffic signal cycle. Moreover, the proposed model has wider applicability than the KNN model and is capable of accurately predicting travel time without depending on equal time interval constraints.

This article aims to examine the strengths and weaknesses of artificial intelligence (AI) in relation to enhancing both online and offline customer experiences, as well as explore potential methods for measuring its effectiveness. The retail industry has increasingly recognized the role of AI in shaping customer experiences. By analyzing various data extraction tools, the article seeks to provide guidance on interpreting information, assisting companies in turning such insights into tangible improvements in the online and in-store retail experience. The research not only presents a snapshot of the current state of customer experiences, but it also provides predictions on how AI will become pivotal in the future. Ultimately, the aim is to improve overall customer satisfaction through the provision of AI-powered experiences.

Features of different pattern complexity and extracted from multiple context scopes all provide important information for saliency prediction. Our model considers saliency can essentially be described by a combination of relatively simple features, and the scale of features varies. For this reason, improvements for saliency prediction model in three aspects are proposed to capture multiple contexts, and in final stage saliency prediction is made in a comprehensive way. The flexibility of proposed approach makes it possible to convert many existing convolutional neural networks into saliency prediction models. Experiments on two benchmark datasets show that the proposed approach is capable of converting a VGG base model into a competitive saliency prediction model.

The effectiveness of machine learning algorithms depends on the quality of the supplied training data. Any problems embedded in the nature of data will result in obtaining incorrect classification models, especially imbalanced data distribution is among the most significant learning difficulties that can affect classifiers. As one of the classes has much more instances than the other, the learning process becomes biased towards it. Therefore, methods for alleviating the impact of skewed distributions are highly sought after. Ensemble learning has emerged as one of the leading paradigms for imbalanced data. Creation of an efficient pool of classifiers is not a trivial task and one needs to carefully select which classifiers should be combined to obtain the best predictive power. In this paper, we propose a compound ensemble pruning algorithm for imbalanced data. It aims to retain classifiers that offer the best performance on both minority and majority classes, and display a high level of diversity. Remaining learners are discarded from the pool. This is achieved by the means of a multi-criteria evolutionary algorithm. Extensive experimental study show that our proposal is able to create smaller ensembles than the state-of-the-art methods, while offering an improved robustness to imbalanced class distributions.

The modern day robots can do a variety of tasks with great efficiency, however their utility is limited due to the non-social behaviour of the robots. For the same it is important to assess the human behaviour in diverse conditions to as to eventually make robots socialistic in nature. Object & people tracking is an excellent field of computer vision in which we have tried to detect and track multiple vehicles and people at outdoor traffic environment and indoor office environment respectively. A background subtraction algorithm is applied for vehicle detection. Kalman filter is used to predict the estimated position of every vehicle in the next frame and updating of new track. Some vehicles are also detected in cluttered scenes. Every moving vehicle is counted in video frames. Multiple face detection and tracking is an also attractive field of computer vision. The faces are behaviourally very different to vehicles and indoor scenarios are also very different to outdoor scenarios. Hence a different methodology to track people is used. In this paper, we have tried to detect and track face of multiple people on two different datasets with different height of camera. Point feature is extracted and compared it in the successive frames to track face of multiple persons. Every face is bounded by rectangular shape with unique identity. We have also counted total number of faces in the frame sequences. Results on both vehicle and face datasets show promising results and the proposed methodology can accurately track the trajectories. The output of the research is a good dataset to assess human behaviour to be used in social robotic applications of the future.

The global health industry has experienced significant growth in the number of wearable health monitoring devices, which provide rapid and detailed information related to physical examinations, allowing for efficient diagnoses of sensitive heart troubles. The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is a phenomenon that connects computer networks and medical equipment through the Internet to provide real-time interaction between physicians and patients. This article presents a comprehensive view of IoMT and its related Machine Learning (ML)-based developed frameworks designed or being utilized between 2010 and 2019. These techniques are designed for monitoring limbs, controlling rural healthcare, identifying e-health applications, monitoring health through mobile apps, classifying heart sounds, detecting stress in drivers, monitoring cardiac diseases, making the decision to predict heart attacks, recognizing human activities, and classifying breast cancer. The aim is to provide a clear picture of the existing IoMT environment to pave the way for diagnosing critical disorders such as cancer, heart attack, and blood pressure. The article also presents unresolved challenges in deploying secure IoMT-based healthcare systems.

We address the issue of channel aging in massive multi-user multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems using Kalman filtering without knowledge of channel correlation statistics. Although Wiener filtering can be used to estimate the channel state information for accurate precoder and decoder construction, this method is limited when regular adaptation to channel changes is necessary. An adaptive Kalman filter is more advantageous than conventional techniques because different users exhibit different mobility conditions. We develop a general model that allows for a wide range of user mobilities in each cell. Simulations using this model reveal that the Kalman filter is effective in predicting channel coefficients for an efficient precoder. Furthermore, we analyze both the uplink and downlink scenarios and find that with poorer channel tracking, the achievable rates in massive MIMO systems decrease unless more precise channel estimates are available.

As a modern power transmission network, the smart grid connects numerous terminal devices. However, the growth of devices also brings about security threats. This is different from the previous isolated environment, where an adversary could only attack individual devices. At present, these devices can be attacked collectively, which can cause the entire power system to collapse. Therefore, ensuring the security and safety of terminal devices is critical.

To achieve this goal, it is important to detect pre-existing vulnerabilities in the device program and enhance the terminal security. In this paper, we propose a new approach to detect existing buffer-overflow vulnerabilities of terminal devices through automatic static analysis (ASA). Static analysis is used to extract device program information and build corresponding program models. By matching the program model with pre-defined vulnerability patterns, we detect vulnerabilities and report errors.

The evaluation results show that our method can effectively detect buffer-overflow vulnerabilities of smart terminals with high accuracy and low false positive rate. Increasing the security of terminal devices could protect the power system and reduce the risk of system collapse due to external attacks.

The growth of the number of vehicles in the city of Manado is very fast causing a high level of congestion. For that requires smart traffic management, especially at crossroads. Timer (time)-based traffic light settings are inefficient, because the vehicle's volume state does not change according to conditions and situations (static). If the road segment is empty, the long duration of the lamp will cause the waiting time / delay for the vehicle on the other road to occur density. As a result there is an empty road section, while the other road segments are jammed, for that it is necessary to have an intelligent traffic light control system. By using Fuzzy Logic which is an algorithm on the system control, especially for dynamic and non-linear systems can increase the time of queue delay at traffic lights with optimal accuracy in real time time settings. So that the movement of the lights can follow the conditions or situations that are needed smartly.

Open source software has gained increasing relevance in the organizational and societal world. This paper aims to identify the main research topics in the context of open source and free software. To accomplish this objective, we carried out a bibliometric study in two different digital libraries, IEEE Explore and ACM Digital Library. The methodology intent was based on clusters co-occurrence of keywords and co-authorship. The results allowed to detect the clusters and themes that are more prominent in the Free Software ecosystem. Although an almost exponential growth in publications has been identified, formed by small groups of researchers and with few links between them.

Text clustering is a powerful technique that can be used to aid crime investigation by grouping together crime-related documents. In this paper, we present the Memetic Algorithm Feature Selection (MAFS) approach as a means to improve the performance of document clustering algorithms applied to partitioning of crime reports, criminal news, and other benchmark datasets. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methodology, we selected two clustering algorithms- k-means and Spherical k-means (Spk). These methods were chosen to compare the performance of these clustering algorithms before and after applying a hybrid feature selection scheme that incorporates a Memetic Algorithm.

The MAFS method combines a Genetic Algorithm (GA) -based wrapper feature selection with the Relief-F filter. The effectiveness of the proposed MAFS method was evaluated based on the clustering outcomes before and after feature selection. Experimental results demonstrate that both k-means and Spk show improved performance after applying a Memetic Algorithm-based hybrid feature selection scheme. 

In conclusion, our proposed MAFS approach proves to be effective in improving the performance of document clustering algorithms for crime investigation purposes. The results obtained indicate that the Memetic scheme can be effectively used for feature selection in text clustering applications.

Mobile communication signal such as LTE is a good external illuminator for wireless sensing, since it is seamlessly covered and always on the air. Through channel estimation, we can find the variation of propagation channels, and then locate the moving objects passively. The basic idea of passive localization is to estimate the propagation delay of the dynamic reflection path, determine an ellipse based on the known positions of the transmitter and receiver, and finally solve the intersection point of multiple ellipses. However, the synchronization error, sampling clock drift, frequency offset and phase noise will severely impact the estimation performance. In this paper, we propose a set of methods to make the practical application of this kind of passive localization possible. A prototype system is built to test the performance in real environments, and various experiments have been done to verify its feasibility.

In this paper, the authors propose an adaptive sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) damping controller for AC/DC hybrid system with high penetration wind. The controller uses Kalman filters for online estimations and tracking of operating points caused by variable wind power output. 

To design the controller, first, a supplementary damping coordinated controller of doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) and high-voltage direct current (HVDC) is designed using multiple input multiple output (MIMO) linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Then, an adaptive method using Kalman online estimations is used to track the operating points caused by variable wind power output. 

The proposed adaptive SSR damping control method is tested using an AC/DC hybrid system integrated with wind power generation. The characteristic of variable SSR modes with wind power outputs is investigated. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method not only tracks the operating condition, but also provides robust and effective control in the case of large fluctuation of wind power output.

Machine learning is poised to play a vital role in the development of 5G wireless self-organizing networks (SONs), which promise to be much more autonomous, intelligent, adaptable, and customer-centric than current networks. This paper proposes a new routing methodology called User Specific-Optimal Capacity Shortest Path (US-OCSP), that uses machine learning to find the resource-based optimum-capacity shortest path for a user between source and destination. The methodology takes into account two primary metrics: available capacity at network nodes (eNodeBs/gNodeBs) and distance, which are essential in determining the optimal path for an end-user. An ns-3 simulation determines the capacity by measuring the availability of resources (such as Physical Resource Blocks or PRBs) at all possible serving network nodes between the source and destination, followed by the implementation of a reinforcement learning method called Q-learning. This method determines the shortest path for the user, avoiding congested network nodes, to achieve the required throughput and/or bit rate. The ability to determine the optimal-capacity shortest path route enables effective resource allocation and maximizes end-user satisfaction in a 5G SON network.

This paper analyses the impact of parametric uncertainties of a mobile robot kinematic model on velocity and pose estimation, providing models and quantifiable knowledge about them. Most works neglect how the uncertainty regarding the robot's construction aspects (such as wheels radii, the distance between them, and the robot's center of mass) affects both velocities and pose estimation. To help readers understand the influence of such parametric uncertainties, we performed experiments in a simulator and used the collected data on the proposed models. The paper also analyses how the magnitude of velocities considered by the controllers and the followed path can decrease or increase the impact of the parametric uncertainties. The proposed models and presented analysis help understanding the influence (isolated or simultaneous) of different sources of uncertainty in the robot's velocities and pose estimation. This knowledge can be applied to estimate uncertainties for localization methods based on data fusion, complementing or even avoiding the experimental procedures. Also, the development of controllers, robot simulators and new methodologies for parameters' calibration and the design and construction of new robots can also profit from the results presented in this paper.

We propose a novel machine learning strategy for studying neuroanatomical shape variation. Our model works with volumetric binary segmentation images, and requires no pre-processing such as the extraction of surface points or a mesh. The learned shape descriptor is invariant to affine transformations, including shifts, rotations and scaling. Thanks to the adopted autoencoder framework, inter-subject differences are automatically enhanced in the learned representation, while intra-subject variances are minimized. Our experimental results on a shape retrieval task showed that the proposed representation outperforms a state-of-the-art benchmark for brain structures extracted from MRI scans.

The boundaries of the Optic Disc (OD) and Optic Cup (OC) are crucial in the detection of glaucoma, yet there are few annotated datasets available for their segmentation. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown significant advances in segmentation, but the scarcity of annotated training images hinders their full potential. To overcome this issue, we propose a method to generate synthetic images to augment the training data. The proposed method employs B-spline registration and GAN to generate high-quality images with realistic vessel bending at the OC edge. In contrast, existing GAN-based methods fail to capture localized details and vasculature in the Optic Nerve Head region. The proposed method's utility is demonstrated in training deep networks for OC segmentation, resulting in an improvement in dice score from 0.85 to 0.902 by adding the synthetic images to the training set.

Improving the endurance of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) is essential for extending their operational range in space and time. However, due to hardware limitations and performance requirements, an intelligent energy management system is necessary to ensure optimal performance. This paper proposes a new model predictive control (MPC) framework that addresses the energy-optimal point-to-point motion control of AUVs. 

The MPC framework consists of two stages that address the surge motion optimization problem for AUVs. Initially, a system-level energy minimization problem is tackled by managing the balance between the energies needed to overcome positive buoyancy and surge drag force using static optimization. Then, the MPC framework handles transients and system dynamics with a unique cost function formulation. Switching logic is incorporated to handle the transition between the static and dynamic stages, reducing computational complexity. 

Simulation results demonstrate that the method proposed provides near-optimal energy consumption, while significantly reducing computational complexity. Therefore, the proposed method has significant potential for the effective energy management of AUVs, which is crucial for their smooth operation in the long run.

Currently, mobile applications, such as interactive gaming, virtual reality, and natural language processing, are becoming more computational intensive, but the computing capacity of mobile devices is limited. An effective way to solve this problem is offloading the tasks to nearby cloudlets, which are some small mobile data centers deployed in wireless metropolitan area network (WMAN). and consume a large amount of energy. Excessive energy consumption brings about some negative effects, including increased carbon dioxide emissions, aggravating the greenhouse effect, etc. In view of this challenge, we propose an energy-aware virtual machine (VM) scheduling method for cloudlets in WMAN. Technically, an optimization model is designed to formalize our problem. Then, based on VM Live Migration Technology, a corresponding energy saving VM scheduling method abbreviated as MFEA is proposed to determine which VMs should be migrated and where they should be migrated. Finally, experimental data demonstrate that the proposed method is effective.

Multi-carrier technology is an important stepping stone towards the adoption of 5G technology. Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) is a fundamental spreading technique that is used in Multi Carrier Spread Spectrum (MCSS). MCSS comes in three types: Multi Tone CDMA (MT-CDMA), Multi Carrier CDMA (MC-CDMA), and Multi Carrier Direct Sequence CDMA (MC-DS-CDMA). One of the factors that cause interference in the network is the Carrier Frequency Offset (CFO), which results in Multiple Access Interference (MAI) and Inter Carrier Interference (ICI), reducing the Spectral Efficiency (SE). However, it is interesting to note that SE will increase if the CFO among the subcarriers also increases.

In this study, we have compared two CFO distributions: truncated-Gaussian and uniform. The results indicated that there was a significant increase in the performance of MCSS with an increase in the variance of the CFO. Furthermore, SE was found to increase with an increase in the Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio (SINR) and the number of interferers. The conclusion drawn from the study is that the uniform Probability Density Function (PDF) of CFO outperformed the truncated Gaussian PDF of CFO in all three cases.

In summary, the study shows that increasing the CFO among subcarriers in MCSS increases SE, and that a uniform PDF distribution of CFO outperforms a truncated Gaussian distribution. These findings have important implications for improving network performance in multi-carrier systems.

Women are often underrepresented in the software development workforce, despite the fact that it offers well-paying jobs and career advancement opportunities. In order to gain access to technical fields, many women turn to various online communities for support. Among these communities are online programming Q&A communities, which serve as knowledge bases for self-directed informal learning and provide opportunities for individuals to showcase their expertise to potential employers. However, these communities are often male-oriented, which can create barriers for women looking to participate and build up their reputations.

To gain a better understanding of how male and female developers participate in online Q&A communities and how their participation impacts their reputations, we conducted a study using data from Stack Overflow. Our analysis revealed significant differences in behavior and outcomes between men and women in these communities. Women, for example, tended to have lower reputations on average, which was largely due to differences in their activities compared to men.

As a result of our findings, it is important for online Q&A communities to address these gender disparities by providing more opportunities and equitable access to women in their communities. By creating a more inclusive and supportive environment, these communities can help women build up their reputations and improve their chances of success in the tech industry.

In this study, we are exploring the use of deep reinforcement learning (RL) for followup clarification questions in dialogue systems. Specifically, we are looking at a nutrition domain where the system needs to narrow down the options for which foods the person has consumed based on a meal description they provided. 

Our prior work in this area focused on using novel convolutional neural network models to bypass standard feature engineering used in dialogue systems, demonstrating that our model learns semantically meaningful embedding representations of natural language. 

In this new domain, our followup questions consist of possible attributes for each food that was consumed. For example, if a user reports drinking a cup of milk, the system should ask about the percent milkfat. 

We compare our RL agent to rule-based and entropy-based methods and find that on a held-out test set, assuming the followup questions are answered correctly, deep RL significantly boosts top five food recall from 54.9% without followup to 89.0%.

We also conduct a human evaluation and find that a hybrid RL model achieves the best perceived naturalness ratings. Overall, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of using deep reinforcement learning for followup clarification questions in dialogue systems, particularly in domains such as nutrition where accurate identification of the foods consumed is crucial.

The iris is renowned for its high level of uniqueness, making it an important biometric trait. However, the accuracy of iris-based biometric applications is greatly influenced by the segmentation of the iris which can be challenged in environments such as near-infrared (NIR) and visible (VIS) ones. This paper describes two robust methods for iris segmentation based on Fully Convolutional Networks (FCNs) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). An FCN is similar to a conventional convolutional network but without fully connected layers. Instead, it employs pooling layers from different convolutional layers. In contrast, a GAN uses game theory by training two networks to compete with one another. The proposed segmentation networks performed well, surpassing previously established baseline techniques in all evaluated datasets (BioSec, CasiaI3, CasiaT4, IITD-1 for NIR images, and NICE.I, CrEye-Iris and MICHE-I for VIS images) in both cooperative and non-cooperative domains, setting a new state of the art for these datasets. Additionally, the authors manually labeled 2,431 images from CasiaT4, CrEye-Iris and MICHE-I datasets, providing access to the masks for research purposes.

Nowadays, conventional learning methods where students are often passive or forced to work show more and more their limits, especially with the advent of the Internet, tablets and smartphones… Therefore, looking for alternative methods is required. In this work, we present three new methods of teaching that seem promising for engineering students: online tutoring, playing games and interdisciplinary projects. We propose to combine them in a new inter-semestrial course for engineering students, at the middle of their curriculum, and through an example focused on the Internet of Things.

Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) is an emerging tool in power system technology, designed for monitoring, protecting and controlling power networks. It provides real-time, synchronized measurement of voltage at system buses and current phasor values of connected lines.

However, the high installation cost of PMUs has led to the need for optimal placement techniques. In this paper, various techniques are classified, discussed and compared for the optimal placement of PMUs to make power networks fully observable. The consideration of measurement redundancy is also addressed.

Ultimately, the optimal placement of PMUs plays a crucial role in optimizing the performance and stability of power systems. Therefore, it is essential to carefully evaluate and select the appropriate technique to ensure the maximum benefit is achieved.

Skeletal bone age assessment is a critical clinical practice that helps diagnose the maturity of children. To achieve accurate bone age assessment, we have developed an automatic bone age assessment method in this study that is based on deep convolution network techniques. This approach is comprised of two stages, including the mask generation network and the age assessment network. The mask generation network utilized a U-Net convolution network with pretrained VGG16 as the encoder to extract the mask of bones. In the assessment module, original images were fused with generated masks to obtain segmented normalized bone images of hands. A multiple output convolution network was then built for an accurate age assessment. Eventually, the bone age regression problem was resolved into K-1 binary classification sub-problems. For evaluating our model's performance, we tested it on the RSNA2017 Pediatric Bone Age dataset. The results showed that our model achieved a mean absolute error of 5.98 months, surpassing common methods for bone age assessment. Therefore, the proposed method presents the opportunity to develop fully automatic bone age assessment systems with increased accuracy.

Crowd counting is a crucial research topic in computer vision. While the multi-column convolution neural network (MCNN) has been widely used in this field and achieved competitive performance, it still needs improvement when dealing with uneven crowd distribution. To address this limitation, this paper proposes to incorporate crowd global density feature, which is extracted and added to the MCNN via cascaded learning method. To preserve some detailed features during the down-sampling process that may be lost in MCNN and affect the accuracy of the density map, the paper introduces an improved MCNN structure. This structure replaces max pooling with max-ave pooling to retain more detailed features, and adds deconvolutional layers to restore lost details in the down-sampling process. The experimental results in the UCF_CC_50 dataset, as well as the ShanghaiTech dataset, demonstrate that the proposed method has superior accuracy and stability compared to other approaches.

Most IoT devices are controlled remotely by mobile applications based on their sensory capabilities. However, this requires users to learn how to use the application before being able to control the devices to accomplish specific tasks. In an effort to improve user interaction capabilities with IoT devices, this paper proposes the use of Web-based Gesture Recognition and Deep Learning. This approach involves using various gestures to control different IoT devices, providing users with a more intuitive and seamless experience.

Due to the excessive number of databases, unbalanced development and behindhand sensing infrastructures, distributed network data suffers from inconsistency, data missing, large measurement error and other data quality problems, which hinder the development of smart distribution network. In order to discover more complex deep-seated rules and provide more effective decision support for power system decision-making, it is necessary to study data mining and analysis methods that are suitable for massive data under current situation. This paper studies on the method of identifying bad data for multi-temporal and multi-spatial data in distribution networks and propose a method to identify bad data using likelihood-ratio test for 3D spatio-temporal data. In order to speed up the data processing rate, a 3D-LRT method based on multi-threading and Hadoop parallelization methods is proposed.

With the increasing use of the Internet of Things (IoT), it has become essential to ensure the security of data or information exchanged between IoT devices and servers. To address this issue, a hybrid cryptosystem based on shared-key and asymmetric cryptography (also known as Public-key cryptography) has been proposed in this study. The system uses the MAC address information of the IoT device for public-key querying and exchanging, while the shared key is exchanged automatically between the IoT device and the server using asymmetric cryptography. The implementation of the system has demonstrated its feasibility in securing the data transferred between IoT devices and servers.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is rapidly advancing and making its way into various industries, including smart lighting. The rise in new IoT use cases utilizing multicast group communication has sparked the need for heightened security measures to protect multiple devices. In order to ensure the success of IoT services, providing dedicated multicast security is crucial for the constrained IoT environment.

This article surveys the current state of secure IoT group communication among devices, with a specific focus on commercial smart lighting. This industry has numerous use cases that rely heavily on secure group communication. The paper outlines the security requirements and use cases for multicast group communication, as well as the latest approaches for standardization activities.

Furthermore, the paper presents the evaluation results for the new application layer security protocol called OSCORE. This protocol has shown promising capabilities for secure IoT group communication. In conclusion, this article provides insight on open research problems to further improve the security of IoT in the future.

This paper investigates a design problem for tracking controllers in discrete-time uncertain systems. To achieve high-performance tracking with reduced chattering phenomenon, a discrete-time terminal sliding-mode tracking controller is proposed. A novel reaching-law is introduced to decrease the bandwidth of the quasi-sliding-mode domain and suppress chattering. The reaching process and tracking error bound are analyzed in detail. Comparative experimental results are also presented to demonstrate the efficacy and benefits of the proposed strategy.

The performance of sensorless induction motor (IM) drives in low-speed regenerating mode can be enhanced by improving the stability of the adaptive full-order observer (AFO) through feedback gain tuning and speed adaptive scheme modification. However, the effect on the IM operating point changes has not been sufficiently studied yet. In order to address this issue, this paper proposes an operating-point tracking method that can be used to design feedback gain and speed adaptive scheme for AFO. This method is capable of accessing lower synchronous speed during step speed and load changes in low-speed regenerating mode without the need for signal injection. 

The proposed method takes into account the operating point changes and derives the estimated flux error by adapting the projection of estimated current error with respect to speed and torque. The derivative estimated flux error with changing parameters is used as an additional variable to design feedback gain. Moreover, the speed adaptive scheme is modified by the operating-point tracking expression, allowing the proposed method to track the operating point in real time. 

Experimental results on a 2.2-kW IM experimental setup demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Thus, the proposed method provides a feasible solution for improving the stability of AFO and its performance in low-speed regenerating mode.

Authentication of human in an unobtrusive manner is important in modern technology to enrich society. Authentication of a person in an environment like smart home, car driving, etc., can lead to better man-machine conjugation. Advancement in sensor technology and machine learning makes it possible to obtain and analyze a significant amount of data. This paper explores the important aspects of human behavior daily routine in the home. Traditional approaches rely on the extraction of statistical features for machine learning algorithms. However, with an increased number of sensors, feature extraction may not be possible. Therefore, human identification in a smart home is performed using deep learning technique on the data obtained from multiple sensors placed at the various place and devices in the homes like a bed, bathroom, door. In this paper, both statistical, as well as deep neural networks, are implemented for human activity data. For humans in smart home deep learning has upper hand as compared to other machine learning techniques. Thus proposed approach can identify humans based on analysis of sensor data using various machine learning technique using unobtrusive sensory data.

In order to enhance the productivity and efficiency of China's modern agriculture sector, this proposed design incorporates Air-Kiss technology provided by the WeChat hardware platform to assist with intelligent farming. The system utilizes a two-machine communication system that is composed of ESP8266 and STC12C5A60S2 as the basic hardware platform.

The ESP8266 serves as the main control chip for the wireless data transmission module, while the STC12C5A60S2 acts as the master chip for the sensor data acquisition module. The system utilizes a serial communication protocol created via serial port, with wireless communication adopting the TCP/IP protocol.

As part of its application, the enterprise will call the ATI interface within the Air-Kiss programmer library to initiate the connection between WeChat and various device functions, thereby eliminating the need for traditional network configuration modes such as fixed IPs. Configuration of the ESP8266 network can be initiated via scanning of a 2D QR code through the user's mobile phone, providing a flexible and easy-to-use method for configuration. 

Through the implementation of Air-Kiss technology in smart agriculture, this design holds the potential to drastically improve the efficiency and productivity of the agricultural sector in China.

A specific pattern of morphological changes in the human brain is observed during the process of brain development and healthy aging. The age of subjects can be estimated from brain images by evaluating such patterns. This paper proposes an age estimation method using 3-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (3D-CNN) from brain T1-weighted images so as to fully utilize the potential of volume data. Through a set of experiments using over 1,000 T1-weighted images of healthy Japanese, we demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits better performance on age estimation than the conventional methods using handcrafted local features and 2D-CNN.

The increasing of connected tiny, low-power, embedded devices, grouped into the generic definition of "Internet of Things" (IoT), raised remarkably the amount of in-situ collected data. However, at the time of writing, IoT devices have limited storage and computation resources if compared with a cloud computing or on-premises infrastructure. IoT devices often suffer for reduced connectivity due to the place of the deployment or other technical, environmental or economic reasons. In this work, we present the DagOn* workflow engine as a part of an IoT orchestration scenario oriented to operational environmental prediction. Our novel approach is devoted to join the two worlds of workflows, in which each task runs on a dynamically allocated computational infrastructure, with tiny jobs targeted to embedded devices hosting sensors and actuators. We show our preliminary results applied to a demonstration use case. We are confident that further development of the proposed technology will affect positively production applications for massive and geographically distributed data collection.

A growing body of research has uncovered the role of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in multiple biological processes and tumorigenesis. Predicting novel interactions between diseases and lncRNAs could help decipher disease pathology and discover new drugs. However, because of a lack of data, inferring disease-lncRNA associations accurately and efficiently remains a challenge. In this paper, we present a novel network consistency projection for LncRNA-disease association prediction (NCPLDA) model by integrating the lncRNA-disease association probability matrix with the integrated disease similarity and lncRNA similarity. The lncRNA-disease association probability matrix is calculated based on known lncRNA-disease associations and disease semantic similarity. The integrated disease similarity and lncRNA similarity are computed based on disease semantic similarity, lncRNA functional similarity and Gaussian interaction profile kernel similarity. In leave-one-out cross validation experiments, NCPLDA achieved outstanding AUCs of 0.8900, 0.8996, and 0.9012 for three datasets. Furthermore, prostate cancer and ovarian cancer case studies demonstrated that the NCPLDA can effectively infer undiscovered lncRNAs.

Alignment of large-scale serial-section electron microscopy (ssEM) images is crucial for successful analysis in nano-scale connectomics. Despite various image registration algorithms proposed in the past, large-scale ssEM alignment remains challenging due to the size and complex nature of the data. Recently, the application of unsupervised machine learning in medical image registration has shown promise in efforts to replace an expensive numerical computation process with a once-deployed feed-forward neural network. However, the anisotropy in most ssEM data makes it difficult to directly adopt such learning-based methods for the registration of these images. Here, we propose a novel deformable image registration approach based on weakly supervised learning that can be applied to registering ssEM images at scale. The proposed method leverages slice interpolation to improve registration between images with sudden and large structural changes. In addition, the proposed method only requires roughly aligned data for training the interpolation network while the deformation network can be trained in an unsupervised fashion. We demonstrate the efficacy of the method on real ssEM datasets.

Many audio forensic applications would benefit from the ability to classify audio recordings, based on characteristics of the originating device, particularly in social media platforms where an enormous amount of data is posted every day. This paper utilizes passive signatures associated with the recording devices, as extracted from recorded audio itself, in the absence of any extrinsic security mechanism such as digital watermarking, to identify the source cell-phone of recorded audio. It uses device-specific information present in low as well as high-frequency regions of the recorded audio. On the only publicly available dataset in this field, MOBIPHONE, the proposed system gives a closed set accuracy of 97.2% which matches the state of art accuracy reported for this dataset. On audio recordings which have undergone double compression, as typically happens for a recording posted on social media, the proposed system outperforms the existing methods (4% improvement in average accuracy).

Previous studies have primarily utilized the nonnegative matrix factorization algorithm (NNMF) to extract muscle synergies during reaching tasks or relatively stable activities to observe muscle coordination in humans. However, tracking tasks have rarely been used due to their high complexity and unpredictability, resulting in more unstable muscle synergies that make it difficult to understand the neural mechanisms behind human motion. In this study, we applied NNMF to tracking tasks and calculated two synergy indices - the synergy stability index (SSI) and synergy coordination index (SCI). SSIW and SSIC measured the similarity between synergies and activation coefficients, respectively, while SCI indicated the size of the synergy space. Our results showed that SSIW was approximately 0.8, SSIC was around 0.3, and SCI was 0.6. These values suggest that humans tend to maintain stable synergies and flexibly control them by adjusting the activation time and amplitudes during complex and variable tasks.

A Least Squares Channel Estimation (LSCE) method is designated for a Massive MIMO system combined with Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM). The Mean Square Error (MSE) of LSCE is computed firstly in a Rayleigh fading channel. Secondly, if channel estimation was available at the receiver (Base Station), the data detection could be made by linear and nonlinear detectors i.e (ZF, MMSE) and (SNR-Based Ordering, OSIC-SINR-Based Ordering) respectively. Simulation results show that by increasing antennas number of Base Station (BS), the nonlinear detectors perform more in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER).

This paper proposes a deep learning based intelligent method for detecting and identifying radio signals considering two applications: first, cognitive radar for identifying micro unmanned aerial systems and second, an automated modulation classification scheme for cognitive radio, which can be used for aeronautical communication systems. Our proposed intelligent method is designed of a spectral correlation function based feature extractor and a low-complexity deep belief network classifier with low FPGA logic utilization.

With the continuous development of smart grids, smart meters are becoming increasingly intelligent. Apart from just recording energy consumption, smart meters now have the ability to upload data to electricity suppliers for monitoring and billing, leading to more efficient and convenient energy usage. However, the added functionalities and computation power of smart meters make them more valuable and susceptible to cyber attacks. The most common security threat for smart meters is the malicious code, which is easily accessible by adversaries due to their widespread reach. Hence, detecting malicious code in smart meters is crucial in safeguarding the security of these devices. 

To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel approach to detecting malicious code in embedded terminals, such as smart meters, using a Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network based on the power consumption of the CPU or MCU of the device. The evaluation of this method shows that it can effectively detect malicious code in smart meters, with an accuracy as high as 92%.

Plant recognition systems that developed by computer vision researchers, help botanists in faster recognition and detection of unknown plant species. Until now, multiple studies focused on the process or algorithms that maximize use of botanical datasets for plants prediction modeling, but this method depends on leaf characteristics which can be changed with botanical data and different feature extraction techniques. On the other hand, recently, due to the popularity and successful implementation of deep learning-based methods in various areas such as image classification, object detection, and speech recognition, the researchers directed from traditional feature-based methods to deep learning. In this research, one more efficient method presented that use transfer learning to recognize plant for leaf classification, which first uses a pre-trained deep neural network model for learning useful leaf characteristics directly from the input data representation. Then use a logistic regression classifier for leaf classification. It is seen that transfer learning from a large dataset to limited botanical dataset in plant recognition task is well done. The proposed method is evaluated on two well-known botanical datasets, i.e., Flavia with 32 classes and Leafsnap with 184 classes, and has succeeded in achieving an accuracy of 99.6% and 90.54%, respectively. The results show that despite the large change in the number of classes in these two datasets, the proposed method, have a good performance and show the better result than methods based on the hand-crafted feature and other methods based on the deep learning in terms of memory and precision.

Model-based controller design is a popular approach used for a variety of tasks. However, identifying accurate models of the target plants can be challenging. In this paper, we propose a unique method to design a dynamics model – specifically, an inverse dynamics model – utilizing Gaussian process.

We analyze the design process and the selection of training input patterns for inverse dynamics learning using Gaussian process. The simulation results demonstrate both the potential and limitations of the Gaussian process based inverse dynamics learning approach.

Overall, this methodology provides a promising alternative to traditional model-based controller design techniques. By leveraging the power of Gaussian process, we can develop more accurate models for a range of applications.

Information recommendation methods mainly include collaborative filtering and content-based. The collaborative filtering method is the most widely used recommendation method. It mainly uses the preferences of a group with similar interest or shared experience to recommend information of interest to users, but it will encounter serious data sparseness and cold start problems. In this paper, we propose a film recommendation model based on word vector features. The Doc2Vec model is used to extract the semantics, grammar and word order of the sentence, transform it into a fixed dimension vector, and the similarity of the vector will be calculated and applied to the collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm. Experiments show that the recommendation results are improved in both accuracy and recall.

The field of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) has recently seen a surge in the use of accurate target tracking. This paper focuses on the real-time detection and tracking of a walking pedestrian from a moving platform, amidst many interferences. To achieve this, we propose a scheme that employs CNN model (YOLO-V2) to detect pedestrian and matches the walking pedestrian with both postprocessing and feature queue, as well as Locality constrained Linear Coding algorithm. The ground station then receives and analyzes the video stream from the Parrot and sends back commands to control the motion of the UAV. At the onset of the tracking process, the UAV hovers while one pedestrian is selected as the designated target. We rely solely on visual information obtained via a front camera without assistant sensors. For the experiment, we utilized a Parrot Bebop 2, which allowed us to conduct outdoor experiments. The experimental results validate the effectiveness of our proposed solution.

Nowadays, the ability to code is becoming increasingly important in industry and is often mentioned as a crucial skill for future employment. In maker culture, the ability to program along with other technical skills often exceeds this limitation and also includes fun activities through personally fabricated projects. In this paper, we examine computational design projects that are intended to be 3D printed and could potentially introduce coding learning actions. To find computationally rich designs that are appealing to learners, we conducted data analysis on an online makerspace which exploits computational design tools for personal fabrication. We found the most liked designs of the online makerspace and examined which of them included programming features (iterations, conditional statements and functions/modules) and could foster computational thinking elements such as abstract and algorithmic thinking, pattern recognition, and decomposition. The most liked category of designs was Figures (of animals and popular animation characters among other things) which surprisingly often also included programming features. We discuss the implications of our research for technologists, academics and teachers who wish to include 3D modeling and printing in coding learning activities.

Computer vision-based real-time applications demand robust image matching approaches due to disparity in images. This can be achieved using descriptor vector with scale and rotation invariance capability. This paper presents a rotation invariant descriptor vector formation based on line point duality. The proposed descriptor uses a simple consistent method of key point detection. For obtaining the descriptor vector, line segments present in the input image are used. These line segments are located within a region of interest around obtained key points in the input image. The obtained descriptor vector is used for matching of disparate images. Experiments are carried out for four different image sets with rotation at the range of angles to validate the performance of the proposed descriptor in real-time. For comparative study, normalized match ratio is computed using multi-layered neural network with two hidden layers.

Energy Performance Contracting (EPC) is an effective measure to promote energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions in commercial facilities and operations. While EPC has been widely applied to energy-consuming facilities and equipment, there is still a lack of clear application systems for the distribution network side, which incurs significant energy losses. To address this issue, this paper proposes a power contract benefit management model for distribution transformers, which can predict the energy-saving benefits and analyze the expected benefit targets of the transformers using neural network algorithms. 

The proposed method can enable energy-saving service companies to carry out EPC business for distribution transformers by calculating the comprehensive recycling cycle. The model is highly robust and offers a feasible direction for the integrated energy service business on the distribution network side. By adopting this approach, significant progress can be made towards promoting energy efficiency and reducing carbon emissions in commercial facilities and operations.

In this work, we use a deep learning method to tackle the Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) problem in tactile material recognition by incorporating the advanced semantic information into a training model. Our main technical contribution is our proposal of an end-to-end deep learning framework for solving the tactile ZSL problem. In this framework, we use a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract the spatial features and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to extract the temporal features in dynamic tactile sequences, and develop a loss function suitable for the ZSL setting. We present the results of experimental evaluations on publicly available datasets, which show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Remote sensing image recognition has been widely used in civil and military fields. In view of plenty of interference factors in remote-sensing aircraft, such as shade, noise, the changing of perspective, etc. An improved target recognition algorithm in remote sensing image based on Faster-RCNN is proposed which uses a standard Region Proposal Network (RPN) generation and incorporates feature maps from shallower convolution feature maps. Convolution neural network is adopted to recognize aircraft target in complex environment, enhance the global context and local information to avoid information loss in the process of feature extraction, which improves recognition rate. Simulation results show that the feasibility of aircraft target recognition algorithm in remoting sensing image and the scale and posture changes of target can be overcome. Meanwhile, the proposed algorithm has higher recognition effect and stronger robustness than traditional Faster-RCNN and BP neural network and support vector machine ( SVM) methods.

We present a complete architecture for the simultaneous estimation of 2D and 3D human pose in natural images. Our approach is unique because it generates and scores multiple pose proposals per image, which enables us to predict poses for multiple individuals simultaneously. Therefore, there is no need for an approximate localization of humans prior to initialization. Our methodology, called LCR-Net, is based on a Localization-Classification-Regression architecture that is comprised of three main components. The first one is a pose proposal generator that generates candidate poses at various positions in the image. The second component is a classifier that scores the different pose proposals. Lastly, a regressor refines the 2D and 3D pose proposals. All three components use the same convolutional feature layers and are trained together. We obtain the final pose estimation by leveraging neighboring pose hypotheses, which enhances the current non-maximum suppression algorithm. Our method captures complete 2D and 3D body pose movements, and even imputes plausible body parts in the event of partial occlusion or truncation by the image boundary. Notably, our method outperforms the current state-of-the-art in 3D pose estimation on the Human3.6M dataset. More so, our approach is promising for both single and multi-person images of the MPII 2D pose benchmark, and displays satisfying 3D pose results even for multiperson images.

In wireless communication systems, it is important to have estimates of the channel in order to achieve high data rates and deliver services with the quality expected by the users. There are several channel estimation techniques used in OFDM systems, some of them based on training sequences and others on blind estimation techniques. In this paper we introduce a data aided channel estimation technique using the Vandermonde Matrix (VM)for the estimation and an interpolation through Frequency Domain Correlation (FDC). This results in a less complex method than LS or MMSE. Mean squared error (MSE)is shown for both techniques (VM and FDC)as a performance measure and it is compared to LS and MMSE. MSE performance is shown for the proposed method to be better than that of the LS and to be practically the same as the MMSE performance for low SNR values.

At present, all CNN-based fire identifications identify whether a fire is blazed with a single frame image, all of which have low accuracy under a strong interference or complex backgrounds such as flickering light or a high-brightness background. To address the issue, this paper proposes a neural network model which combines CNN with SRU. The scene content is extracted through CNN and combined with the dynamic characteristics of the flame extracted by SRU to improve the accuracy of fire alarm. There are three models proposed in the paper, including Resnet18+SRU, Resnet34+SRU and resnet18(Maxpool)+SRU. The models were validated on a test set containing intensive indoor environmental interferences and compared with CNN-based single-frame and multi-frame fire identification methods. The results show that the proposed methods are more accurate than the single-frame CNN fire recognition method by more than 25% and are more suitable for indoor environment fire alarms.

This paper presents DyCorC, an extractor and cleaner of web forums contents. Its main points are that the process is entirely automatic, language-independent and adaptable to all kinds of forum architectures. The corpus is built accordingly to user queries using expressions or item keywords as in research engines, and then DyCorC minimizes the boilerplate for further feature-based opinion mining and sentiment analysis, gathering comments and scorings. Such noiseless corpora are usually hand made with the help of crawlers and scrapers, with specific containers devised for each type of forum, entailing lots of work and skills. Our aim is to cut down this preprocessing stage. Our algorithm is compared to state of the art models (Apache Nutch, BootCat, JusText), with a gold standard corpus we released. DyCorC offers a better quality of noiseless content extraction. Its algorithm is based on DOM trees with string distances, seven of which have been compared on the reference corpus, and feature-distance has been chosen as the best fit.

This research is utilizing three different voltages for load flow forecasting to establish a short-term online forecasting. Upon completion of this research, several neural network learning algorithms will be compared that is an Adaptive Learning Recursive Prediction Error, Modified Recursive Prediction Error, Recursive Prediction Error and Back Propagation. A network entitled Hybrid Multilayered Perceptron Network is coupled to these training algorithms. By using an on-line model, it is applied to estimate the future trend. The future trend network model is train using nonlinear autoregressive moving average with an exogenous input. The projected data is collected from the utility power supplies of 33kV, 11kV and 415V at three different locations in MARA University of Teknologi, Penang, Malaysia.
