It initially forms a graph in which a pair of a position and a value on the string of a solution candidate is a vertex and directed edges are randomly made between vertexes, and then repeats the following three steps: (1) conducting random walk on the graph, (2) producing solution candidates, and (3) reconstructing the topology of the graph. The simulation results show that the proposed metaheuristic is inferior to conventional algorithms against decomposable problems, but superior to conventional ones against problems that are hard to identify their structures.

A novel policy iteration algorithm, called the continuous-time time-varying (CTTV) policy iteration algorithm, is presented in this paper to obtain the optimal control laws for infinite horizon CTTV nonlinear systems. The adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) technique is utilized to obtain the iterative control laws for the optimization of the performance index function. The properties of the CTTV policy iteration algorithm are analyzed. Monotonicity, convergence, and optimality of the iterative value function have been analyzed, and the iterative value function can be proven to monotonically converge to the optimal solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Furthermore, the iterative control law is guaranteed to be admissible to stabilize the nonlinear systems. In the implementation of the presented CTTV policy algorithm, the approximate iterative control laws and iterative value function are obtained by neural networks. Finally, the numerical results are given to verify the effectiveness of the presented method.

Increasing the operational safety of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) is necessary to fully explore their potential. Currently, AUV operations are limited by several constrains including the need to guarantee no interference with manned vessels and a safe deployment and recovery. Exclusion zones are used in many deployments to de-conflict activities but in a near-future world, populated by manned and unmanned surface and underwater vehicles, this will not be enough. In the absence of clear rules and ideal perception capabilities, one way to prevent collisions is to use acoustic communications. In this article, we propose several ways of improving the safety of AUVs and manned vehicles operations through the use of JANUS, the first standard for underwater digital communications. Other ways to communicate underwater could be explored but the usage of a standard protocol represents a landmark step to implement collision avoidance rules and to make the operations of heterogeneous AUVs safer.

Energy Harvesting Wireless Sensor Network (EH-WSN) plays an important role in the IoT paradigm. It measures and accumulates all of the physical parameters from the ambient and facilitating IoT applications to benefit from that data. Since the energy harvesting rate in EH-WSN has a random nature, the main purpose in EH-WSN is to ensure that EH-WSN nodes will not suffer from energy shortage by minimizing the energy consumption of EH-WSN as much as possible. We propose an energy efficient agglomerative hierarchical clustering approach which clusters the whole network more intelligently and efficiently. Also, we formulated an optimization problem to selects the fittest Cluster Head (CH) using Quantum Gravitational Search Algorithm (QGSA). The numerical analysis demonstrates that the proposed approach outperforms Direct Transmission and DEARER about 1.9× in the energy efficiency and 0.4× in the packet fail probability.

Calculus is usually a mandatory first semester discipline in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics). In countries where the K-12 and High School curriculum are not too flexible, as in Brazil, when the students enter the undergraduate courses is expected that they have the knowledge of basic content, that is usually more than ten years of mathematics, because students are usually introduced to mathematics since the first year of school. Mathematics is an important tool to Engineering and is used to model and understand many processes. For computational simulations in Engineering is required from the students the knowledge of mathematics to understand how the process work. But even with the need that the students have the knowledge of this discipline, most of them are not prepared to follow the content presented in Calculus discipline, and this can have a deep negative impact in their results, even in the beginning of the course. To deal with this problem, a support to the students was proposed in the first semester of Engineering course, presenting and discussing the basic knowledge necessary to students understand the concepts presented in Calculus, using explanatory presentations and computational tools.

With the expansion of the internet into the offline world, personalized recommendation algorithms have become increasingly prevalent in the traditional retail industry. This has been done in order to increase user engagement, conversion rates, and overall revenue generation. However, due to the lack of proper data segmentation, traditional recommendation algorithms have not been able to perform well in the retail industry.

In order to address this problem, we have taken into account the interest spread characteristic of retail industry behavior and have adopted the method of complex networking to construct a personalized recommendation algorithm using a segmented data set. To evaluate our algorithm, we used a real sales dataset from a large supermarket.

Our findings indicate that our algorithm has much better accuracy and recall performance than traditional algorithms. However, it does have the disadvantage of being less coverage. Overall, we believe that leveraging the segmented data sets to create personalized recommendation algorithms could significantly increase the effectiveness of recommendation systems in the retail industry.

The field of educational data mining is experiencing a transformation both domestically and internationally. The research topics have shifted from conceptual and principle levels to modeling analysis and application levels. Additionally, the focus has shifted from macro-level applications, such as statistical monitoring of educational quality and policy, to micro-level applications, including further development of school teaching and student learning.

This paper discusses the conceptual aspects of educational data mining and learning analytics, proposing a data model and system architecture while combining them with teaching practices. The methodology used in the study of education data is characterized as "Four modeling and three analysis," which leads to the construction of a "whole chessboard" analysis for data mining in the smart classroom. The analysis of data mining in the smart classroom expands across 13 specific research questions.

The paper also explores four different application modes of data mining in the smart classroom. Finally, the manuscript examines the interaction between teachers and students based on real data.

Overall, this study presents a comprehensive view of the current state of educational data mining, particularly as it relates to smart classrooms. The methodology proposed in this paper can guide future research in this area while supporting the development of more accurate and efficient educational systems that benefit students and educators.

Deep learning-based recognition systems have demonstrated outstanding performance in various tasks. However, most of these systems are based on a single modality, which is vulnerable to fraudulent inputs that may look alike. To address this issue, we propose a multi-modal deep neural network that utilizes an attention mechanism and a correspondence learning scheme. Our approach uses multiple modalities, containing distinct information about the target task, to detect fraud inputs. The attention mechanism enables the network to learn better feature representations for different modalities, while the correspondence learning scheme learns intermodal relationships to detect fraudulent inputs. 

We evaluate our proposed approach in a reverse vending machine system, where the task is to classify among three given classes (can, PET bottles, glass bottles) and reject any suspicious input. We use three different modalities: image, ultrasound, and weight. Our experiments demonstrate that our proposed model can effectively learn to detect fraudulent inputs while maintaining high accuracy for the given classification task.

Vehicular ad-hoc Network(VANET) helps various stakeholders like passengers, traffic management team, manufacturers, owners, drivers etc to access important information using a highly dynamic mobile network. Restricting unauthenticated users from free information sharing is a crucial challenge. In this paper we propose a dynamic lightweight biometric-based authentication protocol for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication networks where user after successful registration can directly login from any local mobile terminal and access his /her services/information directly from the authentication servers. We have done the security analysis of our scheme and prove that our scheme provides user anonymity, location privacy, mutual authentication to prevent spoofing attacks and resistance against forgery, modification and replay attacks. We also compare the efficiency of our scheme with other related schemes and show that our authentication scheme is more secure and performs faster than other schemes available in the literature.

Students' majors at High School (SMA) constitutes as an obligation to be carried out every year. The majors' determination at SMA, particularly at SMA in Banten, has already had its standardization. Schools that have had their standardization in majors' determination are mostly located in urban area. However, schools in such rural areas mostly have not yet conducted majors' determination for their students. It is so called as important that each school must conduct the majors for its curriculum. Commonly, the majors' determination of SMA in rural areas tends to be carried out only based on students' appetency, without considering the factors of their ability, interest, and aptitude. In our previous research, it had been conducted the comparison between Fuzzy Tsukamoto method and K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN) method. From the research result, in accordance to the comparison's result of Fuzzy Tsukamoto method, it shows that the method is a chosen method with 99.2% level of accuracy. Besides of its high level of accuracy, the choice of Fuzzy Tsukamoto method is also based on the condition in the field, where Fuzzy Tsukamoto method can be applied in schools that have good or minimal data. The researchers also design the website application to support those schools in carrying out the majors as the application can be accessed and applied everywhere. The criteria of school majors are students' skill, interest, and aptitude. This is in line with the existing criteria in DIKNAS (National Education), because the majors are not yet online facilitated by private schools in Banten. Hence, the researchers design that support system website application to assist the school in determining the appropriate majors which will be then selected by the students.

The intensity of spontaneous neuronal activity can be reflected by the fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (fALFF). Combining feature selection with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data and fALFF is a promising method for studying attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and aiding in its diagnosis. However, the limited effectiveness of feature selection has hindered ADHD research. To address this issue, a novel method for classifying ADHD individuals and neurotypicals is proposed in this study. Multiple linear regressions are used for confounding effect reduction, and fALFF is combined with principal component analysis (PCA), Shannon entropy (ShEn), and sample entropy (SampEn) to construct features. To find the most prominent features, a reliable RELIEF (R-RELIEF) algorithm is proposed. The public ADHD-200 dataset is used to evaluate this method, with the study results suggesting that fALFF is a dependable fMRI marker for the investigation of ADHD. R-RELIEF also exhibits superior performance compared to the RELIEF algorithm. The fALFF of numerous brain regions differ between individuals with ADHD and neurotypicals, supporting previous study findings.

High-dimensional and sparse (HiDS) matrices from recommender systems contain various useful patterns. A latent factor (LF) analysis is highly efficient in grasping these patterns. Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is a widely adopted algorithm to train an LF model. Can its extensions be capable of further improving an LF models' convergence rate and prediction accuracy for missing data? To answer this question, this work selects two of representative extended SGD algorithms to propose two novel LF models. Experimental results from two HiDS matrices generated by real recommender systems show that compared standard SGD, extended SGD algorithms enable an LF model to achieve a higher prediction accuracy for missing data of an HiDS matrix, a faster convergence rate, and a larger model diversity.

Considerable effort has been devoted to the design of control systems for wave energy converters (WECs) over the last twenty years. Starting from the fundamental requirement of impedance matching, different conceptual and practical algorithms have been developed, aiming to ensure maximum power transfer while taking into account various degrees of realism. Some simplifications can be adopted, such as passive or causal control, while other more sophisticated algorithms attempt to account for physical constraints, non-linear model dynamics or non-ideal power takeoff systems. However, in general, WEC control systems are evaluated in conjunction with identical simulation models, with little regard for the effect of modeling errors on controller performance. Furthermore, the WEC model typically used by the controller does not fully capture the non-linear nature of the true WEC dynamics. This paper highlights the issue of model sensitivity for various WEC control architectures and demonstrates that it can have a more significant impact than for conventional regulation/servomechanism control problems. The paper concludes by providing recommendations on the best WEC control architecture to adopt from a sensitivity/robustness perspective.

This study implements machine learning techniques to achieve a learning-based mesh generation for thermal simulation. The first phase of the study focuses on generating numerous power value sets of application processors and applying the superposition technique to obtain the temperature raw data of material blocks. From the thermal data, different mesh-size sets of material blocks are obtained for each power value set by using several defined thermal gradient ranges. Predictive regression models are then constructed and trained as a supervised learning task with seven hidden layers. In the second phase, the learning-based mesh decision engine is integrated into a developed system-level thermal simulator built by the finite difference method. The experimental results demonstrate that the temperature profiles of the handheld device calculated by the developed thermal simulator with learning-based mesh generation fit the results obtained by a commercial tool extremely well with less runtime usages. Furthermore, the learning-based mesh decision engine proves to be much more efficient than the artificial mesh decision.

In this paper, a Software Defined Network was created in Mininet using Python script. An external interface was added in the form of an OpenDaylight controller to enable communication with the network outside of Mininet. The OpenDaylight controller was hosted on the Amazon Web Services elastic computing node. This controller is used as a control plane device for the switch within Mininet. The OpenDaylight controller was able to create the flows to facilitate communication between the hosts in Mininet and the webserver in the real-life network. In order to test the network, a real life network in the form of a webserver hosted on the Emulated Virtual Environment - Next Generation (EVE-NG) software was connected to Mininet.

Enabling robots to interpret the intentions of humans, such as detecting a waving person in a restaurant or recognizing when a customer is pointing to a product in a supermarket, has the potential to revolutionize the field of human-robot interactions. However, this requires solving a highly complex and diverse problem - that of gesture recognition. 

To address this challenge, this paper proposes a method for multi-person gesture classification based on human pose features extracted from 2D images. Specifically, the method focuses on classifying five gestures and one neutral body posture. 

In order to evaluate the proposed approach, a comparison was made between supervised machine learning methods for gesture classification. The results showed that the proposed approach achieves good results on both the authors' own validation dataset as well as a public dataset, demonstrating its potential for generalized use.

This paper presents an approach to address the online identification problem of uncertain systems, which involves using a neural identification model coupled with feedback and a weight law based on Lyapunov theory. The proposed algorithm results in an arbitrarily small residual state error and is dependent on the design matrices. Moreover, it has been proven that transient can be steered by parameters uncorrelated with the residual state error, enabling the separation of the transient and steady state error. The practical implications of the algorithm have been validated through an experiment involving the identification and control of a chaotic system. The study also examined the impact of primary design parameters on algorithms' performance.

In this work, a 4 Gerbera flowers subtypes are classified according to their color components in petals and in the center. We proposed first the preprocessing of each image acquired in real scenario, the preprocessing is realized in two steps, the first is to crop each flower to create a database with the tag of each subtype, the second consist in removing the background using color space transformation to Hue and filter the image according to some specific values. With all the images a decision tree is created with the 70% of the images in each category, the first rule consists of identify the highest value in the histogram, if this value corresponds to green range or orange range the classification is done, nevertheless if the value corresponds to pink, the enclosing circles are estimated, then the color into the smallest circles defined the classification. The evaluation is performed using the last 30% of the images in each category, the classification will be positive if the correct subtype is predicted, if not the classification will be negative, nevertheless the classifier could predict no class based on any existence of the flower, or different flower, in this case if non-class is predicted over a different flower the classification will be positive, if not the classification will be negative. The results obtained in each category are showed in the next list, first is the name of each subtype, followed by the percentage of positive classifications. Gerbera Renato (95%), Gerbera Marinilla (99%), Gerbera Chiper (85%), Gerbera Rio Negro (78%), None/Different (74%).

Contribution: This article discusses how knowledge of students' Habits of Mind in a signal processing course can be used to identify factors that influence their performance. The authors provide a method for education research that applies a clustering approach to derive student cases, which is an alternative to the traditional case study method. 

Background: Habits of Mind are the modes of thinking required for students of science, mathematics, technology, and engineering to become effective problem solvers. In a signal processing course, students must learn to apply engineering knowledge to solve problems using tools and techniques previously acquired in math courses. 

Research Questions: The study aims to answer two main research questions: 1) What are the different Habits of Mind patterns exhibited by the students? 2) Are some of these patterns associated with differences in course grades? 

Methodology: The study uses a qualitative method combined with random signal modeling and machine learning. The custom-built rubric of Habits of Mind is used to manually annotate students' work. The data is then modeled and clustered to obtain statistically significant patterns of Habits of Mind corresponding to student groups. 

Findings: The study's data suggests that there is inhomogeneity in terms of Habits of Mind within the student group, and this inhomogeneity is associated with grade differences. Specifically, the course grade is found to be dependent on inhomogeneity based on at least two Habits of Mind: computation and estimation and values and attitudes. 

Overall, this article highlights the importance of Habits of Mind in signal processing courses and their correlation with student performance. The authors' proposed research method provides an alternative perspective on how to analyze and understand the factors that affect student achievement.

In this paper, an automatic math word problem solver is presented for GCE Ordinary Level set theory related problems that use Venn diagrams. In order to model all basic set relationships and operations required to solve the problems, a data representation is introduced that uses binary representations. After categorizing set problems in O/L Mathematics examinations including GCE, IGCSE, GCSE, and JCE, two types of problems are selected to solve using this representation. The solver is implemented using regular expressions and POS tag based information extraction to filter relevant data from a given problem text. Then this information is mapped into the above data representation in order to derive equations that solve the problem. On the end-to-end evaluation, an accuracy of over 90% is achieved for the selected set of math word problem types.

Imperfect observation is an indispensable but often neglected part for practical measurement. In this work, we mainly investigate its effect upon estimating quantum states by focusing on several specific examples. It is shown that the accuracy of the quantum state estimation will be greatly degraded in the presence of imperfect observation. In order to reduce its destructive influence, a cautious estimation method and the adaptive measurement strategy are attempted. However, it turns out that both of the methods cannot always overcome the performance deterioration due to the observation error. The results warn us that we have to seriously deal with the problem of imperfect observation in practical quantum information processing.

Mobile users' online traffic records are a type of data that are closely related to human activities. To explore the differences in lifestyles of Internet users, online records of base stations expressed as time series need to be classified. However, due to the circadian rhythms, such time series have the same trend and small-scale local differences. Traditional similarity measurement using original time series is difficult to adequately capture local features of time series. By mapping the time series into visibility graph, the similarity measurement in the graph domain is obtained preserving the dynamic structure and local features to the greatest extent. In this paper, a locally weighted adjustable parameter-based limited penetrable visibility graph (LWAPLPVG) is proposed to further improve the noise resistance of visibility graph and local identification of limited penetrable visibility graph. We get APLPVG by modifying the visibility criteria, which has noise resistance while preserving local features as well. Simple measurement, such as degree sequence in graph domain, is extracted and proved, which is able to amplify small-scale differences. By considering the circadian rhythms of cyclical and trend time series, APLPVG is weighted locally. We use a real dataset of usage detail records (UDRs) to verify that LWAPLPVG can better improve the identification of time series of functional regions with noise resistance.

Classifying data with disproportionate class distributions or rare events can be challenging for model groups. Kernel Logistic Regression (KLR) is a framework that tends to bias models in favor of the majority class when classes are highly imbalanced. To address this issue, a weighted form of the likelihood function has been proposed, which improves model performance on the minority class. However, this modification of the likelihood function does not take into account the possibility of incorrect training labels. 

In this paper, we propose a correction to the expression of the weighted likelihood function for KLR that is robust to the presence of noise in the training label set. Our approach allows for superior performance in both noisy and noise-free settings. We compare the performance of our modified KLR model against the original likelihood and weighted likelihood functions on several benchmark examples. The results demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of our proposed method in improving the performance of KLR for imbalanced datasets.

Reliability enhancement testing (RET) is an accelerated testing which hastens the performance degradation process to surface its inherent defects of design and manufacture. It is an important hypothesis that the degradation mechanism of the RET is the same as the one of the normal stress condition. In order to check the consistency of two mechanisms, we conduct two enhancement tests with a missile servo system as an object of the study, and preprocess two sets of test data to establish the accelerated degradation models regarding the temperature change rate that is assumed to be the main applied stress of the servo system during the natural storage. Based on the accelerated degradation models and natural storage profile of the servo system, we provide and demonstrate a procedure to check the consistency of two mechanisms by checking the correlation and difference of two sets of degradation data. The results indicate that the two degradation mechanisms are significantly consistent with each other.

In the last two decades, researchers have extensively investigated synchronization of networked systems with determined node dynamics. However, noise is inevitable in many real-life networked systems, and thus dynamical networked systems with stochastic perturbations have gained attention in theoretical research and practical applications. This paper focuses on the problem of designing novel synchronization protocols for nonlinear stochastic dynamical networked systems. We present sufficient conditions for selecting protocol parameters, and using stochastic analysis techniques and appropriate Lyapunov functions, we prove that global synchronization of nonlinear stochastic dynamical networked systems can be achieved in mean square. We also depict numerical examples to demonstrate the effectiveness of our theoretical results.

The potential of interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) heights from TanDEM-X for vegetation canopy height and aboveground biomass (AGB) estimation has long been recognized. Penetration of X-band into the canopy affects these estimations. Thus, the canopy height and AGB retrieval from InSAR are typically biased and cannot be compared directly to estimates from other data sources. The objective of this letter was to apply a penetration depth model to compensate for height biases in TanDEM-X InSAR heights. The resulting canopy height estimates are subsequently converted to AGB estimates using regression models. The uncorrected InSAR heights of the forest canopy are biased due to the penetration of the signal into the canopy and differ substantially to light detection and ranging (LiDAR) canopy height estimates. The application of the penetration depth compensation results in unbiased forest canopy height estimates and AGB regression models that are comparable between InSAR and LiDAR. These results indicate that TanDEM-X InSAR and LiDAR technologies can be used to estimate AGB in complex tropical forests suggesting a synergistic use of these fundamentally different observation concepts.

Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are becoming increasingly popular for use in wireless networks due to their ability to be deployed quickly without reliance on existing infrastructure. However, previous studies on UAV-aided communication have only explored generic scenarios, with few practical network evaluations. Therefore, a comprehensive assessment of the benefits of UAV communication in real networks is necessary. In this paper, we present a UAV-aided Wi-Fi Direct network architecture. Our proposed architecture involves deploying a UAV equipped with a Wi-Fi Direct group owner (GO), called a Soft-AP, to serve a set of Wi-Fi stations. To optimize the placement of the UAV, we propose a simpler and more efficient algorithm that dynamically assesses the network and repositions the UAV to reduce the distance between the GO and the client devices. The benefits of our scheme include improved connectivity for client devices, increased overall network throughput, and improved energy efficiency. To validate our claims, we conducted realistic simulations using the NS-3 network simulator. Our simulation results demonstrated a significant improvement in client association (23%), network throughput (54%), and energy consumption (33%) when compared to both stationary and randomly moving GO cases. Increases in the number of UAVs in the network lead to further improvements. To our knowledge, no other work has evaluated UAV-aided Wi-Fi Direct networks in this way.

As data volumes continue to grow, new approaches are needed to split big data into separate blocks that can represent the entire dataset. In this research paper, we introduce the Random Sample Partition (RSP) distributed data model, which enables big data to be represented as a collection of non-overlapping RSP blocks. Each RSP block has a probability distribution that is similar to that of the entire dataset. By using RSP blocks, it is possible to estimate the statistical features of the data and construct predictive models without having to process the entire dataset. Our study highlights the benefits of the RSP model in terms of big data sampling and introduces a new RSP-based technique for approximate big data analysis that can be adapted to various professional settings, resulting in reduced computational complexity and greater efficiency for data scientists.

The support vector machine (SVM) has become a popular tool for solving multiclass classification problems. Among the SVM methods, the multiobjective multiclass SVM (MMSVM) has received considerable attention due to its ability to accurately maximize geometric margins of pairwise classes, resulting in a high generalization ability. However, the training process of MMSVM is computationally expensive as it requires solving a nonconvex multiobjective optimization problem (MO). 

To address this issue, we propose an approximate MMSVM, which approximates the nonconvex MO using a convex one. The resulting convex problem is then solved using the reference point method, which considers the balance between geometric margins. The reference point method employs reference points and weights, which are selected based on the distances between centroids or the one-against-one margins. 

Our numerical experiments show that the proposed method can significantly reduce computational resources while achieving high generalization ability. Thus, the approximate MMSVM offers a promising solution to the challenging problem of multiclass classification.

We conducted research on the energy efficiency performance of cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. These systems have access points (APs) that are connected to a central processing unit (CPU) via limited-capacity links. In our study, we proposed using distributed maximum ratio combining (MRC) weighting at the APs, and transmitting only the quantized version of the weighted signals to the CPU. 

To account for channel estimation errors and quantization errors, we used the Bussgang theorem to model the latter. We then formulated an energy efficiency maximization problem with constraints on per-user power, backhaul capacity, and throughput requirements. As the optimization problem is non-convex, we decomposed it into two sub-problems and employed successive convex approximation (SCA) to solve it. 

Our numerical results confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed optimization scheme, which can significantly improve the energy efficiency of cell-free massive MIMO systems.

In this study, we develop a novel error detection algorithm for Lempel-Ziv-77 (LZ77) compressed data. In the proposed algorithm, additional bits are not used to detect bit errors, unlike in conventional methods such as checksum, cyclic redundancy check, Hamming code, and repetition code. We also introduce eight special features of LZ77-compressed data for detecting the presence of errors. We demonstrate the feasibility of the algorithm based on simulations and evaluate it using two publicly available databases comprising the Calgary and Canterbury corpora. The error detection rate using the proposed algorithm is below those of conventional methods, but the compression ratio is better. The application of a parity bit in the algorithm improves the error detection performance. The number of redundant bits increases owing to the insertion of the parity bit, but the code rate is still greater than or equal to 0.9, whereas conventional methods obtain code rates less than 0.9. Simulations demonstrate that the algorithm obtains significant performance improvements when a parity bit is periodically inserted. In particular, we achieve an error detection rate of 100% using the parity bit when the number of bit errors is greater than seven.

Classifying white blood cells from microscope images can be difficult due to various challenges such as non-uniform illumination, stage of maturity, scale, rotation and shifting which can create intra-class variations. In this paper, we propose a new feature extraction scheme that relies on bispectral invariant features, which are robust to these challenges. These features are extracted from the segmented white blood cell nuclei using a level set algorithm via geometric active contours. Binary support vector machines and a classification tree are used for classifying multiple classes of cells. 

To evaluate the performance of our proposed method, we used a combined dataset of 10 classes with 460 white blood cell images collected from 3 datasets and conducted 5-fold cross-validation. The proposed method achieved an average classification accuracy of 96.13%, outperforming other popular representations such as local binary pattern, histogram of oriented gradients, local directional pattern, and speeded up robust features with the same classifier over the same data. 

Furthermore, we benchmarked our classification accuracy against existing techniques for classifying white blood cells into 10 classes over the same datasets and the results showed that our method is superior to other approaches. Overall, our proposed method using bispectral invariant features and level set segmentation achieved excellent results, demonstrating its efficacy for the challenging task of white blood cell classification.

Promotions are a widely used strategy to engage consumers and as such, retailers dedicate immense effort and resources to their planning and forecasting. This paper introduces a novel interpretable machine learning method specifically tailored to the automatic prediction of promotional sales in real-market applications. Particularly, we present fully automated weighted k-nearest neighbors where the distances are calculated based on a feature selection process that focuses on the similarity of promotional sales. The method learns online, thereby avoiding the model being retrained and redeployed. It is robust and able to infer the mechanisms leading to sales as demonstrated on detailed surrogate models. Also, to validate this method, real market data provided by a worldwide retailer have been used, covering numerous categories from three different countries and several types of stores. The algorithm is benchmarked against an ensemble of regression trees and the forecast provided by the retailer and it outperforms both on a merit figure composed not only by the mean absolute error but also by the error deviations used in the retail business. The proposed method significantly improves the accuracy of the forecast in many diverse categories and geographical locations, yielding significant and operative benefits for supply chains. Additionally, we briefly discuss in the Appendix how to deploy our method as a RESTful service in a production environment.

The distinction between a traditional IT network and an industrial control network necessitates different approaches to network security assessment. As cybersecurity becomes increasingly alarming, network security assessment research faces fresh challenges.

This paper compares the construction, capabilities, and potential harms of IT networks and industrial control networks. It also looks into the present standards and critical technologies involved in IT network and industrial control network security assessments. Furthermore, the challenges of network security assessments for these two kinds of networks are analyzed, and future research possibilities are explored.

A mobile-based virtual try-on system has been developed to tackle the issues of high cost and the conflicts between computational complexity and simulation effects. The proposed system includes several modules, including automatic 3D face reconstruction based on a single image, auto-skinning, and real-time local simulations of cloth. Through experimental trials, it has been demonstrated that the virtual try-on system described in this paper achieves a better fitting effect with lower construction and computing costs. This results in a superior experience for mobile-based virtual try-on systems.

Fast and accurate harmonic extraction is essential for various applications such as power quality assessment, grid synchronization, and harmonic compensation. In this paper, we propose a multiple second-order generalized integrators (SOGIs) based comb filter (SOGIs-CF) for fast selective harmonic extraction.

Compared to the conventional multiple SOGI-quadrature signal generators (SOGI-QSGs) scheme, our proposed method removes the tedious harmonic decoupling network (HDN) without compromising the steady-state detection accuracy. As a result, the computational burden can be significantly reduced. We also provide detailed discussions on the design criteria of the parameters and digital implementation issues.

Furthermore, the experimental results show that our proposed scheme exhibits fast response and high detection accuracy. Its ability to detect harmonic magnitude signals rapidly makes it an excellent candidate for implementing flexible output capacity-limit control of multifunction inverters.

In summary, our proposed SOGIs-CF method is an effective and efficient approach for fast and accurate harmonic extraction, which can significantly improve the overall performance of power quality assessment and harmonic compensation systems.

In this article, the use of differential evolution algorithm (DEA) as an optimizer for the realizable phase weight coefficient in engineering of the linear array is discussed. It is noted that traditional phase-only weight coefficient is not implementable in actual T/R module. DEA is considered one of the best real parameter optimizers that require very few control parameters and can be easily implemented in any programming language.

The proposed adaptive DEA is demonstrated to produce a radiation pattern with minimum sidelobe level and high radiation power. Statistical analysis reveals that the results obtained using DEA are comparable to, and in some cases better than, the outcomes achieved by other state-of-the-art metaheuristics such as genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO).

Overall, this study shows that the adaptive DEA can be a valuable tool for optimizing the realizable phase weight coefficient in engineering of the linear array. The proposed algorithm can lead to improved radiation pattern and better performance compared to other existing metaheuristics.

The reweighted zero-attracting least mean square (RZA-LMS) algorithm has good performance in sparse system identification. However, the convergence performance of the RZA-LMS algorithm degrades in the impulsive noise environment. In this brief, a reweighted zero-attracting least mean M-estimate (RZA-LMM) algorithm is proposed to address the issue. The RZA-LMM algorithm employs the M-estimate cost function with a sparsity-aware penalty term and is derived by using the unconstrained minimization method. In order to further enhance the convergence speed and reduce the steady-state error of the RZA-LMM algorithm, a variable step-size reweighted zero-attracting least mean M-estimate (VSSRZA-LMM) algorithm is proposed. The variable step-size scheme, which adopts the M-estimate cost function with a sparsity-aware penalty term and a constrained term of the step-size, is obtained by using the constrained minimization method. Besides, the mean-square stability is analyzed to obtain the range of the step-size, which guarantees the stabilization of the proposed algorithms. The computer simulation results show that the proposed RZA-LMM algorithm achieves better convergence performance than the RZA-LMS algorithm, and the proposed VSSRZA-LMM algorithm exhibits better convergence performance in terms of convergence speed and steady-state normalized mean square deviation (NMSD) than the RZA-LMM algorithm for sparse system identification in the impulsive noise environment.

Many-objective optimization problems (MaOPs) present a huge challenge to the traditional Pareto-based multi-objective algorithms because the increase of the objectives results in the low-efficiency of the Pareto dominance in distinguishing the relationships between the solutions during the environmental selection. To enhance the selection pressure, in this paper, through redefining each objective function by a non-linear transformation, we first propose a new dominance method called NLAD-dominance, in which a dynamic parameter adjusting scheme is designed to dynamically adjust parameter α according to different numbers of objectives and different evolutionary states. As a result, NLAD-dominance can provide proper selection pressure for different kinds of MaOPs in different stages of evolution. Then, based on NLAD-dominance, we design a new fitness estimation strategy which takes both convergence and diversity into account, and adaptively balances them by a parameterless penalty rule. Thus, it can well evaluate the quality of each solution. At last, we conduct the experiments and compare the proposed algorithm with five state-of-the-art algorithms on 80 test instances of 16 benchmark problems with up to 20 objectives. The experimental results indicate that the proposed algorithm is highly competitive in terms of both convergence enhancement and diversity maintenance.

The article discusses the issue of information representation through the use of spatial relations in pseudo-physical logic. The goal is to analyze and structure information by formalizing human perception of information blocks, in order to improve the processing and retrieval algorithms. The chosen formalization mechanism is justified, which is then utilized in the identification and classification of objects in semi-structured information flows. Pseudo-physical logic of space is used to create formal descriptions for situational analysis and systematic organization of information. 

To achieve these objectives, a set of fuzzy quantifiers is established, along with their corresponding relations. Rules for displaying the spatial location of information are developed and formal descriptions are generated in terms that are unified with initial conditions of information search and structuring. Unification of terms allows for easier classification and identification of information while saving resources. 

Experimental studies validate the effectiveness of this approach in the problem of autonomous positioning and description of the environment of aerial vehicles. Overall, the proposed approach shows promise in improving the algorithms and methods used in the processing and retrieval of information.

MEC is an emerging computing paradigm that utilizes computing resources at the network edge to deploy heterogeneous applications and services. By offloading computation-intensive tasks to nearby computing resources, mobile users and enterprises can reduce latency and conserve energy. When making offloading decisions in the MEC system, it's essential to consider task dependency. However, the offloading problem is NP-hard, and the current solutions are mainly heuristic, making it challenging to adapt to complex and dynamic applications. 

To overcome these challenges, we propose a new deep reinforcement learning (DRL) -based offloading framework that learns the optimal offloading policy using a specially designed sequence-to-sequence neural network. The proposed DRL solution automatically discovers common patterns across various applications to infer the best offloading policy in different scenarios. 

Simulation experiments were conducted to evaluate the proposed DRL-based method's performance with different data transmission rates and task numbers. The results demonstrate that our method outperforms two heuristic baselines and achieves nearly optimal performance. 

Overall, our proposed DRL-based offloading framework offers an efficient and effective solution for addressing task dependency and adapting to dynamic scenarios in the MEC system.

This paper presents for the first time a real-time closed loop neuromorphic decoder chip-driven intra-cortical brain machine interface (iBMI) in a non-human primate (NHP) based experimental setup. Decoded results show trial success rates and mean times to target comparable to those obtained by hand-controlled joystick. Neural control trial success rates of ≈ 96% of those obtained by hand-controlled joystick have been demonstrated. Also, neural control has shown mean target reach speeds of ≈ 85% of those obtained by hand-controlled joystick. These results pave the way for fast and accurate, fully implantable neuromorphic neural decoders in iBMIs.

The black box arc model is suitable to describe the arcing process of hybrid circuit breaker, since it provides an effective way to integrate the arc model into an electrical circuit. However, it is more difficult to determine the parameters of the arc model according to the performance of circuit breaker than to solve the analytical equations of arc model. A library of arc models including Mayr, Cassie, Kema and other models has been built and verified based on MATLAB Simulink/Simscape. Heuristic optimization methods, such as Genetic Algorithm, Simulated Annealing and Particle Swarm Optimization, have been used to develop the algorithms to estimate the parameters of arc models. The results show the inverse modelling technique is effective to find the proper parameters which describe the changing of conductance of arc plasma. It is also found that the GA with well-selected parameters has the advantage over other methods.

The availability of dynamic code analysis along with the application of modeling techniques can significantly improve formal software testing activity. It quickly provides an overview of how a particular piece of code is working. In software modeling, different approaches are used to visualize the input/output behavior of a computer program. In this paper, we propose a dynamic testing approach based on Finite State Machine (FSM) modeling techniques to model the potential behavior of functions in C programs. We use dynamic code analysis technique with the help of an inference algorithm for test generation. Our approach helps not only in learning program behaviors as a finite state model but also facilitates in testing the program systematically. We have performed experiments on a range of open source C programs that has shown the effectiveness of our proposed approach, especially for anomaly detection.

This paper discusses a problem that has plagued researchers for a long time regarding the dynamic modeling of a multiple degree-of-freedom (multi-DOF) manipulator such that its manipulation exhibits a higher computational efficiency and accuracy. Unknown friction, unknown gravitational torque, an uncertain moment of inertia, and severe joint coupling are the primary disturbing factors in multi-DOF manipulator modeling. In addition, joint flexible problems caused by the integration of harmonic drives increase the modeling complexity. Hitherto, no effective method has been found to address these problems. The virtual decomposition (VD)-based method exhibits the advantages of joint dynamics decoupling and minor computation compared with the traditional Lagrangian formulation or Newton-Euler formulation. In this study, an estimation method for the deformation-related torque of harmonic drives is established based on a novel experimental model; subsequently, this method is utilized in the VD-based model for the multi-DOF manipulator. Hence, the decoupling dynamic model for the manipulator considering joint flexibility is established. The performance of this new method has been evaluated by a contrast simulation with the Newton-Euler formulation, and the multi-DOF manipulator control simulation and experiment have been conducted with a VD-based model as a feedforward compensator to verify its performance in real-time control. The results demonstrated the validity and efficiency of e proposed approach.

We present our experience with hosting scientific workloads in a private scientific cloud, where both the infrastructure as well as the workloads are heterogeneous. We support two major classes of workloads-classic virtual machines (VMs) and batch job computations. Furthermore, containerized applications and scientific portals such as Galaxy are also hosted in this infrastructure. Using our experience, we describe the system setup, the technologies used to run this heterogeneous system as well as some of the problems we have faced when managing this system throughout the years. Modern computing environments such as clouds, grids or HPC clusters are both complex and costly installations. Therefore, it has always been a major challenge to utilize them properly. Things like improper setup or bad scheduling policy may easily hamper overall performance of the whole system. We believe that our experience and observations may help other researchers and system administrators identify new research directions and/or potential weak spots. Importantly, the problems discussed in this paper are based on real-life data from the CERIT Scientific Cloud that we freely offer for further analysis and/or simulations.

Recently, modern computer vision techniques like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown significant success. However, these techniques are expensive to use in cell-level prediction problems in histopathology images due to the difficulty in providing cell-level supervision. In this study, we investigate the possibility of transferring features learned by an object detection CNN, namely Faster R-CNN, to nucleus classification in histopathology images. We utilize class-agnostic models to detect nuclei in the images, which are trained on small annotated patches. We then use the CNN representations of the detected nuclei to cluster and classify them. Our results indicate that the proposed pipeline can achieve superior nucleus classification performance with a small training dataset and generalize well to unseen stain types.

This paper focuses on a mission-critical control system comprising an unstable dynamic plant monitored by several distributed sensors, which are connected to the controller via wireless fading channels. The objective is to stabilize the dynamic plant by dynamically scheduling sensors. We present a non-convex drift-plus-penalty minimization problem that models dynamic sensor scheduling. To enhance scheduling efficacy, the proposed scheme adapts to both dynamic plant state and fading channel state. A novel transformation technique for scheduling variables and Lyapunov drift for the objective function was proposed to overcome the non-convexity of the minimization problem. Based on that, we can obtain a closed-form stability analysis via a randomized state-independent policy and a low-complexity dynamic sensor scheduling scheme. Compared to various baselines, our proposed scheme offers superior scalability performance and higher power efficiency.

Functional connectivity of the brain has become an important area of research in understanding brain function, diseases, and injuries. Statistical methods have been used to model brain functional connectivity, but they often make the assumption that connectivity patterns remain static during the recording, which is not accurate as connectivity changes over time. Therefore, a dynamical modeling of connectivity patterns is needed to characterize these variations. In this study, a simplified dynamic Bayesian modeling approach called Parallel Hidden Markov Model (PaHMM) was used to investigate temporal variations of cortical functional connectivity patterns obtained from epileptic electroencephalogram (EEG) data. 

The performance of the PaHMM was evaluated in an experimental study of epilepsy detection and classification, using multisubject epileptic EEG data from Temple University Hospital EEG Data Corpus. Results showed that the PaHMM method efficiently captured temporal variations of functional connectivity patterns, achieving an accuracy rate of 93.5% for epilepsy detection and an overall accuracy above 81% for seizure type classification. These findings suggest that the PaHMM method could be applied in clinical settings to detect epilepsy and differentiate seizure types. 

Overall, this study highlights the importance of considering temporal variations in brain functional connectivity, and presents a promising method for detecting epilepsy and categorizing seizures, which could have significant implications for clinical practice.

Edge detection is a significant problem in the field of computer vision. In this paper, we introduce a new concept for edge detection known as Structural Edge. The Structural Edges consist of occluding contours of objects as well as orientation discontinuities in surfaces that define the 3D composition of objects and their surroundings. This is in contrast to the semantic edge which only encompasses the boundary between semantic areas. While traditional edge detection methods focus on either semantic boundaries or low-level gradients, our emphasis is on the structural edge.

To achieve this, we propose a structural edge dataset in this paper along with a benchmark test. This dataset consists of 600 natural indoor and outdoor scenes, with manually labeled structural edges. Furthermore, it has been validated by eye-tracking data from ten participants, across a total of 20 trials. Subsequently, we utilize this dataset to benchmark existing edge detection methods, both learning-based and non-learning-based. Our findings suggest that current methods are inadequate for effectively detecting structural edges. We encourage future researchers to explore the proposed task.

Automated driving promises to enhance road safety and traffic efficiency significantly. Currently, host vehicle onboard sensing systems can sense the environment up to 250 meters ahead of the vehicle, while LiDARs can see about 120 meters. However, recognizing small objects, such as animals or dropped cargo, is not reliable at ranges beyond 50 meters. Collaborative sensing with connected driving, including exchange of status messages and real data, has recently garnered attention to extend the sensing range and improve efficiency. Since the uplink capacity of current cellular 3G/4G networks is limited, sharing point clouds of what vehicles see in front is not possible. Therefore, this article focuses on exploring the opportunities of 5G-based cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) collaborative sensing, based on trial results from test sites in China and Finland. The results show that the round-trip is stable (<; 60 ms) even while exchanging 1 MB/s between vehicles. Finally, this article examines the perspective of the automotive industry and identifies and prioritizes potential use case scenarios for utilizing 5G-based connected driving applications.

Numerous experiments have shown that there are similar gestures in visual-based gesture recognition. In order to solve the problem, this paper proposes a new algorithm based on Convolution neural network. According to the model test results, the confusion matrix is established. And according to the correspondence between each gesture and the predicted result, misjudgment probability matrix is established. Based on the misjudgment probability matrix, we correct the gestures that have been incorrectly identified by the Convolution neural network model. After this algorithm, the recognition rate of similar gestures is increased by 5% to 12%. The innovation of this paper lies in the secondary error correction of the wrong gesture of Convolution neural network structure.

A perennial need for safety in the community depends on country, city, and district. In some instances, feeling safe is required on a 24/7 basis. A popular and cost-effective solution based on the Raspberry Pi has the promise of being both user-friendly and costeffective. It pairs the Raspberry Pi to a camera module for face recognition. It learns to detect those with granted access to the specified area under protection. Such stored faces are the subject of system training. If during operation the system recognizes the face in the dataset, then the camera shows the matching name with a confidence level possibly granting access, but alternatively it takes a photo of the subject and sends it as an email notifications warning. The proposed system can implement face recognition even from poor quality images performing well over both known and unknown datasets. Face recognition leverages techniques from the OpenCV library and is written in the Python language.

This article presents a solution for predicting the quality of a computer network through the utilization of a widely used machine learning method - a decision tree. The approach is applied to a real-life case of quality issues in the network during the running of a web server. Through an analysis of the traffic data recorded during the network operation, a decision tree is constructed.

The constructed decision tree is then used to conduct numerical experiments in order to predict the occurrence of problems experienced by users when accessing web pages. The prediction model is assessed based on the obtained results to determine the quality of the model.

Overall, this article proposes a practical and effective approach to predicting the quality of computer networks. By utilizing a decision tree, network administrators and engineers can proactively identify and address issues that may impact the user experience, thus improving overall network performance and ensuring optimal user satisfaction.

In this paper, we present a novel pose estimation system that utilizes visual fiducial features with multi-cameras for mobile robot indoor localization experiments. The main objective of this system is to provide ground truth data at a low cost by using off-the-shelf hardware components. The system comprises an embedded vision system that employs a fiducial feature detecting algorithm to compute the pose estimation results. These results are then transmitted via pre-synchronized distributed modules to the server which retrieves the object pose by utilizing the proposed observation decision algorithm. To tackle the problems of none observation of all cameras or when the current pose data is far from the previous ones, we apply a glitch elimination method. Practical experiments on a mobile robot have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed system, achieving an impressive 6 cm accuracy.

Heart disease is the major cause of the death. Medical treatment and diagnosis of the heart disease is the major factor to improve the death rate. The main risk factors of the heart disease are obesity, tobacco, alcohol consumption and age factor etc. To reduce the death rate, the predictive system will be design so that way of treatment and diagnosis will be improve. This paper presents a big data analysis for prediction of the Coronary Artery heart disease. The analysis of huge amount of a patient by using data mining and machine learning algorithms improves a hospital administration. As a huge amount of the data in increase in every field, so it is difficult to analysis, extract, manage and store a structured and unstructured data, so that the big data technologies and tools are used.

This article introduces a data assimilation technique for social agent-based simulations that utilizes a reinforcement learning method to automatically fit real world data. The approach involves using a hidden Markov model to estimate system states during the reinforcement learning process. By incorporating new real data, this method can gradually improve simulation models without requiring total optimization. To demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed technique, it was applied to a housing market problem using real Korean housing market data.

With the advancement in sensor technology, multiple sensors have become commonly used to monitor the degradation of a single unit simultaneously. However, the challenge in multisensor degradation modeling is that the signals from these sensors are often correlated and may have incomplete or no information on the degradation status of a unit. To tackle these issues, this paper introduces a novel data fusion method that automatically selects and combines multiple sensor signals to construct a 1-D health index (HI) that can better characterize the degradation process. Specifically, this paper presents a new latent linear model that constructs the HI and selects informative sensors in an integrated manner.

Compared to existing approaches, the proposed method offers several unique advantages. Firstly, it can derive the best linear unbiased estimator of the fusion coefficients. Secondly, it provides high computational efficiency. Thirdly, it does not require the exact value of the failure threshold. Lastly, it has general applicability in practice, without imposing restrictive assumptions on the degradation process. Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness and sensitivity of the proposed method. Additionally, a case study on the degradation of aircraft gas turbine engines indicates a better prognostic performance of the proposed method than existing methods.

We consider the problem of learning graphical models where the support of the concentration matrix can be decomposed as a Kronecker product. We propose a method that uses the Bayesian hierarchical learning modeling approach. Thanks to the particular structure of the graph, we use a the number of hyperparameters which is small compared to the number of nodes in the graphical model. In this way, we avoid overfitting in the estimation of the hyperparameters. Finally, we test the effectiveness of the proposed method by a numerical example.

Fake profile detection is one of the critical problems in Online Social Networks (OSNs). So far, studies have mainly focused on profile-based, behavioral-based, network-based and content-based attributes. However, user sentiments have not been explored along this domain. In the present study, we proposed the fake profile detection model that incorporates sentiment-based attributes to differentiate real and fake OSN profiles. The study is grounded in the fact that the posts of real users reveal varied categories of emotions such asjoy, sad, angry, fear, etc. based on their life experiences. On the contrary, fake users share posts to accomplish a specific purpose, and therefore, it is highly likely that their post content will contain similar types of emotions. The experiments are conducted on the posts of Facebook users. The detection model is trained on 12 emotion-based attributes including Plutchik's eight basic emotions, positivity and negativity. Furthermore, a noise removal technique is presented to remove the outliers from the dataset. Finally, several machine learning techniques including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naive Bayes, JRip and Random Forest have been used to train the detection model.

Segmenting pulmonary lobes in computed tomography (CT) images is a crucial step in disease characterization, functional analysis, and treatment planning. The growing number and high resolution of CT scans emphasize the need for automatic and reliable lobe segmentation methods. In this study, a deep learning framework based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is proposed for efficient fissure and lobe segmentation in CT images. A novel pipeline based on a series of 3D CNNs was utilized to marginally learn lobe segmentation. The method was evaluated on a dataset of 1076 CT images from the COPDGene clinical trial, which comprised scans obtained from multiple institutions and scanners. The proposed method achieved a median Dice coefficient of 0.993 and a median average symmetric surface distance of 0.138 mm for all lobes, demonstrating robustness to various inspiratory levels, pathologies, and image quality. The results indicate that the proposed deep learning framework could be a promising approach for pulmonary lobe segmentation in routine clinical settings.

In this paper, we propose an effective technique for modeling of Lithium Ion (Li-Ion) batteries using Nonlinear Auto Regressive model with eXogenous input (NARX). The Artificial Neural Network (ANN) are trained employing the data collected from the battery testing process. The NARX network find the request battery model, where the input variables are the battery terminal voltage, SoC at the previous sample, and the current, temperature at the present sample. The proposed model is implemented on a Li-Ion battery cell. Simulation of this model in Matlab/Simulink show a good accuracy of proposed model.

Recently, the importance of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems has grown for many industries around the world. These systems are controlling many vital infrastructures such as grids of power, plants, and water treatment systems. In fact, nowadays SCADA systems cannot be isolated from the public and thus being more vulnerable and exposed to many malicious attacks. Several studies have reviewed the latest developments in cyber-security risks for SCADA systems and found that many factors are responsible for increasing the amount and the level of risks on modern control systems. Among such factors are the network architecture and the reliance on standard technologies that have known vulnerabilities. In this paper, we attempt to improve a framework of SCADA system against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks using three machine learning algorithms (i) J48; (ii) Naive Bayes; (iii) Random Forest to determine the attack patterns. These algorithms were trained and evaluated on KDDCup'99 dataset. The preprocessing phase of the dataset was conducted based on the goal of the paper and the obtained results showed that the best classification is obtained using Random Forest classifier (RF) with 99.99% accuracy rate, while Naïve Bayes classifier has the lowest accuracy rate of 97.74%.

Learning under concept drift is an emerging area of research that aims to develop learning algorithms capable of handling nonstationary data-generating processes. The majority of literature in this field focuses on learning nonstationary probabilistic frameworks, with a few studies extending to learning graphs and signals under concept drift. However, this paper stands out as the first to address the challenge of learning discrete-time Markov chains (DTMCs) under concept drift. 

Adopting a hybrid active/passive approach, this paper proposes a family of change-detection mechanisms (CDMs), which differ in their required assumptions and performance, to detect changes in DTMCs. Furthermore, an adaptive learning algorithm has been developed to deal with DTMCs under concept drift. Both the proposed CDMs and learning algorithm have been extensively tested using a combination of synthetically generated experiments and real datasets, demonstrating their effectiveness.

Multidisciplinary design optimization techniques are gaining popularity in the field of aerodynamics, thanks to the rapid advancement of high-performance computers, numerical methods, and optimization algorithms. These techniques aim to improve fluid flow solutions by coupling Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) with numerical methods and algorithms.

CFD analysis plays a crucial role in determining an airfoil's capability by generating lift and drag forces. By applying an optimization algorithm, the airfoil's shape can be enhanced to manipulate lift and drag coefficients based on desired requirements.

This study focuses on a numerical investigation using ANSYS/Fluent of two-dimensional transonic flow over a NACA 0012 airfoil at various Mach numbers, which is compared with experimental data. The compressible and turbulent flow is solved using a density-based implicit solver, which is ideal for high-speed compressible flows.

Following the analysis, a shape optimization algorithm was employed based on a Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm to obtain an improved performance control of the aerodynamic coefficients of the optimized airfoil. Overall, the use of multidisciplinary design optimization techniques proved to be a valuable method for improving aerodynamic performance in the given scenario.

ID3 algorithm and C4.5 algorithm of decision tree are commonly used in the base classifier in random forest. In order to solve the problem that the basic classifier algorithm is biased to select multi-valued attributes and contains a lot of logarithmic operations, the attribute compatibility of rough set is introduced in this paper. Rough set is a mathematical tool for dealing with uncertain information. In this paper, the expression of information gain or information gain rate in the base classifier is reconstructed with compatibility, and the attribute with the highest compatibility is selected as the segmentation attribute to segment the data set. Finally, three UCI data sets are used to verify the accuracy of the algorithm. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has a higher accuracy than the traditional random forest algorithm.

Our research provides a novel hardware/software autonomous car model that can be effectively deployed to carry out intelligent pickup and delivery missions. We develop a model of a Cooperative Autonomous Reactive Taxi System (CARTS) that contributes to solving the unsustainable urban traffic gridlock in large cities. Our model formulation is inspired by general the pickup/delivery problem (GPDP). Given dynamic stochastic variables that include a set of cars, a set of customers, a set of stations (e.g., bus stop), and a set of transport missions, devise autonomous intelligent carts capable of effectively carrying out these missions to satisfy the quality of service requirements and any associated constraints. Our model integrates novel capabilities, such as decentralized architecture, cooperative decision-making, autonomy, and intelligent navigation, as well as a transport requests logistics model. Our deployment prototype is a laboratory experimental set-up using autonomous robots and relevant infrastructure that demonstrate the feasibility of our pickup and delivery model. Analysis of collected data from the simulation and the physical implementation demonstrates the effectiveness of our model.

Disturbance that occurs on the train or at the station, such as a broken train engine, broken train line signals, and others, can cause delay on the train. The train operator at the station will reschedule the train schedule in the event of a delay. Currently, the train only reschedules when the delay occurs “on the spot”, consequently the rescheduling determination takes a long time. This can be anticipated by taking preventive action, ie rescheduling by using predictive delay. Possible conflicts that will occur when rescheduling single track are overtaking and crossing. This research will focus on the development of rescheduling considering predictive delay. The purpose of this study is to minimize the total delay time. The output of this research is a decision support tool that can generate free-conflict timetable when delay occurs.

Ever since the introduction of the domain name system (DNS), attacks on the DNS ecosystem have been a steady companion. Over time, targets and techniques have shifted, and in the recent past a new type of attack on the DNS has emerged. In this paper we report on the DNS random subdomain attack, querying floods of non-existent subdomains, intended to cause a denial-of-service on DNS servers. Based on five major attacks in 2018 obtained through backscatter measurements in a large network telescope, we show the techniques pursued by adversaries, and develop a taxonomy of strategies of this attack.

In medical imaging, the detection of biomarkers is crucial for diagnosis and treatment guidance. While supervised deep learning can accurately segment pathological areas, it requires prior knowledge of these regions, large-scale annotations, and a representative patient cohort in the training set. Anomaly detection, on the other hand, is not restricted to specific definitions of pathologies and can be trained on healthy samples without annotation. These anomalous regions can then serve as candidates for biomarker discovery.

To take advantage of the implicit information provided by normal anatomical structure for anomaly detection, we propose using Bayesian deep learning. Our approach involves training a Bayesian U-Net on a well-defined healthy environment using weak labels of healthy anatomy produced by existing methods. At test time, epistemic uncertainty estimates of our model are captured using Monte Carlo dropout. A novel post-processing technique is then applied to exploit these estimates and transfer their layered appearance to smooth blob-shaped segmentations of the anomalies.

We experimentally validated our approach on retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) images, using weak labels of retinal layers. Our method achieved a Dice index of 0.789 in an independent anomaly test set of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) cases. The resulting segmentations allowed for the separation of healthy and diseased cases with late wet AMD, dry geographic atrophy (GA), diabetic macular edema (DME) and retinal vein occlusion (RVO) with very high accuracy. Additionally, we observed that our approach can also detect other deviations in normal scans, such as cut edge artifacts.

Overall, our approach shows promise for improving biomarker detection and diagnosis in medical imaging, particularly when dealing with anomalies that have no prior definition or annotation.

This paper presents a novel method for coarse registration of RGB-D data based on mixed feature points. The proposed approach involves obtaining feature points by using mixed feature information which are then used to search for corresponding points in the target point cloud based on feature descriptors. The feature points are divided into several partitions and a rigid transformation is calculated between the corresponding point pairs in each partition. An optimal rigid transformation is chosen from the rigid transformation of each partition. To construct the mixed feature, both geometric and color information of the neighborhood points are combined. Furthermore, the feature descriptor is built using the mixed feature and normalized RGB value. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is highly effective in registering RGB-D data.

In order to ensure the stability of an electrical grid, it is crucial to efficiently detect and identify generator events (GE), which are faults that can cause cascading effects and lead to power outages. These events can arise due to a number of factors, but ultimately indicate a failure of a generator to meet the needs of the grid. In this paper, we present an algorithm that effectively identifies GE occurrences in an electrical grid, utilizing data from phasor measurement units (PMUs). Our approach involves a machine learning algorithm that analyzes PMU data to detect instances where a GE has taken place. This method allows for near real-time detection using readily available processing units. 

To further enhance our results, we have developed electrical fault maps that visually demonstrate the progress of an event as it unfolds. Our experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm can accurately identify GE occurrences, and the fault network map provides a valuable troubleshooting tool. By utilizing machine learning algorithms and utilizing PMU data, we are able to provide efficient and accurate identification of generator events, which is essential for the stability and reliability of electrical grids.

This paper presents a compression methodology using genetic algorithms and web-services to test it. The algorithm combines two well-known algorithms of fractal and neural network compressions, making some improvements in their implementation. Thus, in fractal compression we increased speed of compression by a genetic search and in neural networks we used neuroevolution approach for adaptive neural networks. This type of network uses previously processed data to increase the compression rate. In general case, our algorithm outperformed JPEG by 12%.

This paper proposes a method for evaluating the degradation stages of screw stability using data fusion technology and deep residual neural network. The method involves fusing data from multiple sensors and inputting time domain images of the signals into a deep residual neural network for training and testing. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, data sets were collected from the degradation test bench of a ball screw. These data sets comprised 3 degradation stages under 9 working conditions obtained from 3 accelerometers.
