Results from the study reveal that the deep residual neural network can automatically extract features in a layered approach to obtain better evaluation rates when used to evaluate the screw's performance stage. Moreover, it was found that multi-sensor data fusion's vibration data better reflects the degradation stages of the screw. The proposed approach enhances the evaluation's intelligence and efficacy compared to traditional methods.

Our study delves into the field of facial expression recognition and specifically focuses on the usage of state-of-the-art classification models. While CNNs have been widely used in face recognition, their effectiveness in recognizing facial expressions has not been thoroughly evaluated. To address this gap, we conducted a study where we trained and tested a CNN model specifically for facial expression recognition. The performance of this model was then used as a benchmark for evaluating other pre-trained deep CNN models. 

In our study, we evaluated the performance of Inception and VGG, both of which are pre-trained for object recognition, and compared them with VGG-Face which is pre-trained specifically for face recognition. For our experiments, we utilized publicly available face databases such as CK+, JAFFE, and FACES. 

Our findings showcase that pre-training of CNN models specifically for facial expression recognition leads to better performance than pre-training them for object recognition. Additionally, we demonstrated that models pre-trained on face recognition tasks outperform those pre-trained on object recognition tasks for facial expression recognition. Our study provides deeper insights into the effectiveness of CNN models for facial expression recognition and paves the way for future research in this field.

Shape segmentation is a fundamental problem in shape analysis. Previous research shows that prior knowledge helps to improve the segmentation accuracy and quality. However, completely labeling each 3D shape in a large training data set requires a heavy manual workload. In this paper, we propose a novel weakly-supervised algorithm for segmenting 3D shapes using deep learning. Our method jointly propagates information from scribbles to unlabeled faces and learns deep neural network parameters. Therefore, it does not rely on completely labeled training shapes and only needs a really simple and convenient scribble-based partially labeling process, instead of the extremely time-consuming and tedious fully labeling processes. Various experimental results demonstrate the proposed method's superior segmentation performance over the previous unsupervised approaches and comparable segmentation performance to the state-of-the-art fully supervised methods.

Obtaining a greater number of non-dominated solutions is essential for solving multi-objective problems. To address this issue, a novel hybrid differential evolution algorithm has been developed in this study for solving the multi-objective 0-1 programming problem. The algorithm is based on three key techniques, namely the good point set method for generating the initial population, the traction method to handle the constraint conditions, and the analytic hierarchy process for determining the weights between the objective functions.

The proposed algorithm not only improves the diversity of the population, but also overcomes the difficulty of selecting the penalty factor using the penalty function method. Several typical multi-objective 0-1 programming problems are tested, and the results are compared with other algorithms. The findings indicate that the proposed algorithm can effectively find more non-dominated solutions for multi-objective 0-1 programming problems, making it an efficient solution for such problems.

Human motion measurement plays an important role in the field of motion analysis, virtual reality and ergonomics design. Recently, it has become possible to measure the human motion using a set of inertial measurement units (IMUs). However, the IMU-based motion-capture (MoCap) system only consider the ground contact constraints, so the constraints between the human and the product are not considered. Therefore, this study aims to develop a full-body motion estimation system using the IMUs, which can reflect the contact conditions between the product and the product users based on the user-specified contact constraints. In addition, the proposed system is validated through the measurement experiments of walking and chair-sitting motions. The walking experiment shows that the averaged errors of the joint angle estimation are ranged from 2.79±2.00 deg for the right ankle to 9.55±6.04 deg for the right hip. In addition, the chair-sitting experiment shows that the proposed system could estimate the sitting motion reflecting the contact condition between the subject and the chair surfaces. Our results indicate the potentials and challenges for measuring a variety of human motion using the proposed system.

Heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) and multi-access mobile edge computing (MA-MEC) are believed as supporting technologies for building a smart city. The advancement and flourish of IoT are facilitating the entry of human society into the Internet of Everything era, which lay the foundation of the smart city. To address the conflict between computation capability and low-cost mobile devices in IoT, the MA-MEC is available for supporting the resource-limited and computation-sensitive services and applications by computation offloading and distributed content delivery/caching. However, deploying cloud computing capability within the radio access network may face serious security threats, which stem from not only the existing technologies and networks but also the MA-MEC-based IoT itself. Therefore, in this paper, the solutions to address the security threats are investigated from physical layer perspectives, since physical layer security technologies have the advantages of achieving perfect secrecy, low-computational complexity, and resource consumption, and good adaptation for channel changes. Specifically, we investigate the secure wiretap coding, resource allocation, signal processing, and multi-node cooperation, along with physical layer key generation and authentication, to cope with the emerging security challenges. Finally, the paper is concluded with some possible future research directions.

For systems that can only be locally stabilized, control laws and their effective regions are both important. In this paper, invariant policy iteration is proposed to solve the optimal control of discrete-time systems. At each iteration, a given policy is evaluated in its invariantly admissible region, and a new policy and a new region are updated for the next iteration. Theoretical analysis shows the method is regionally convergent to the optimal value and the optimal policy. Combined with sum-of-squares polynomials, the method is able to achieve the near-optimal control of a class of discrete-time systems. An invariant adaptive dynamic programming algorithm is developed to extend the method to scenarios where system dynamics is not available. Online data are utilized to learn the near-optimal policy and the invariantly admissible region. Simulated experiments verify the effectiveness of our method.

The reservation of shape features is the key problem of filling hole. In this paper, we present a hole filling method based on feature lines, including the hole boundary lines, ridge lines and valley lines. First, the feature lines are extracted and used to generate a series of curves. Then the control points sequence is obtained by fitting these curves. Finally, the NURBS surface is fitted by control points sequence to fill the hole. The obtained results show that our method can preserve the initial shape characteristics of hole.

Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation outperforms orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) in high-mobility scenarios. One challenge for OTFS massive MIMO is downlink channel estimation due to the large number of base station antennas. In this paper, we propose a 3D-structured orthogonal matching pursuit algorithm based channel estimation technique to solve this problem. First, we show that the OTFS MIMO channel exhibits 3D-structured sparsity: normal sparsity along the delay dimension, block sparsity along the Doppler dimension, and burst sparsity along the angle dimension. Based on the 3D-structured channel sparsity, we then formulate the downlink channel estimation problem as a sparse signal recovery problem. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve accurate channel state information with low pilot overhead.

We propose a deep learning approach for predicting the apparent age of a person's skin. Our method works by first normalizing a frontal image of a face and cropping rectangular-shaped skin patches that are each normalized and fed into separately trained region-specific CNNs. Each regional CNN model is fine tuned using a novel data augmentation technique that artificially reduces the apparent age of the skin through a series of smoothing operations that act as a proxy for subjects with younger looking skin. The deep features extracted from each of these regions are then used to train a separate set of regression models that predict the skin age. We evaluate our method using two strategies: the first looks at how well the predicted regional skin age clusters around the true biological age of the subject, for which we achieve a 1-off accuracy of approximately 83%. In the second strategy, we validate that our models predict apparent skin age based on a user study that asked over 15 judges to compare image pairs of subjects with the same chronological age, but with different skin age predictions. For this second study, we achieve an average 66% accuracy based on consensus rating across all human raters, and as high as 76% for some age groups.

An enhanced algorithm for describing wood texture features using Local Binary Pattern operator has been proposed. This algorithm utilizes the linear LBP operator to extract the texture characteristics of an image, followed by the calculation of texture similarity among the sub-regions of a wood image. This method is particularly effective in distinguishing striped and patterned wood due to their high texture similarity. Based on experimental results, this algorithm exhibits strong capabilities in describing wood texture features, surpassing traditional methods in terms of robustness, and achieving higher recognition accuracy.

Social network analysis is an interdisciplinary topic attracting researchers from biology, economics, psychology, and machine learning. It has attracted interests from both the research and business communities for a strong potential and variety of applications. Also, this interest has been fueled by the large success of online social networking sites and the subsequent abundance of social network data produced. An important aspect in this research field is influence maximization in social networks. The goal is to find a set of individuals to be targeted, with the aim to drive social contagion and generate a diffusion cascade. We provide here an overview of the models and approaches used to analyze interaction networks. The challenges this problem introduces are recently being tackled using Deep Learning approaches such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) which are particularly suited to model sequence inputs.

In recent years, marine ecologists have increasingly turned to underwater video analysis for studying fish populations. This non-destructive technique generates a large volume of visual data without disturbing the underwater ecosystem. However, analyzing this data can be time-consuming, subjective, and costly. Automated methods for processing the data are necessary, but the underwater environment poses significant challenges such as changes in luminosity, complex backgrounds, and free movement of fish. 

To address these challenges, a convolutional neural network was trained using the transfer learning framework for fish species recognition. First, the original AlexNet model was used to extract fish features from images in the underwater dataset. Then, the model was fine-tuned on the dataset to improve performance. Finally, features were re-extracted after fine-tuning, and a linear SVM classifier was used for species classification. The proposed approach achieved an accuracy of over 99%, demonstrating its effectiveness.

Typosquatting refers to a kind of cybersquatting on the internet that takes advantage of typing mistakes made by internet users while entering website addresses. Such errors often lead users to unintended websites, and cybersquatters frequently use them to redirect traffic to sites with malicious content. One possible solution to this issue is the defensive registration of similar domains and redirecting requests to the original website. This can be feasible and cost-effective for the original domain owner if they can predict a short list of such probable typo domain names. However, existing works on typosquatting mostly rely on analyzing logs to detect typo sites, and none of them can predict probable typo variations of a given URL during the pre-registration phase. To fill this gap, we introduce TypoWriter, an RNN-based error prediction tool that achieves good performance in terms of successful predictions that match with ground-truth data. We compare TypoWriter with five other widely-used typo generation tools, and substantial improvement is observed.

In this paper, an adaptive observer in the case of nonlinear parameterization is developed for the two wheeled self balancing robot. It is designed to estimate the unknown state as well as the body mass of the robot which influences the height of center of mass. Then, a PID control approach is used to generate the control input signals that are used by the adaptive observer. Finally, simulation results assert the performance of the designed observer for the two wheeled self balancing robot subject to mass variation.

Establishing a fundamental understanding of the specific molecular biology of a species benefits substantially from reconstructing its genome (DNA) and transcriptome (RNA). These efforts are enabled by modern high throughput sequencing technologies. For over a decade, assembling the generated data into coherent information has been a primary focus of the bioinformatics field. However, the expanding data volume in the field and growing read lengths from evolving sequencing platforms require adapting bioinformatics tools to properly leverage the potential of new genomics technologies. This study is about efficient and scalable algorithms to perform a set of unit operations in genomics studies to guide sequence assembly. Here, we report on a software package, ntPack, with two components: ntHash, for nucleotide hashing, and ntCard for cardinality estimation. We characterize the statistical properties of these algorithms, and demonstrate their application on whole genome shotgun sequencing datasets describing the roundworm, human, and Canadian white spruce genomes. The software that implements these algorithms can be downloaded from our github repository at https://github.com/bcgsc.

Semi-supervised learning is a method that aims to improve learning performance with limited label information. To extract additional information from collected data, we propose a weighted hybrid multi-view feature fusion approach for semi-supervised classification. Specifically, we utilize a rank consistency constraint to predict labels by view-specific learners and estimate the optimal fusion weight to balance the incomparable square losses on different views. Our approach pushes learners with more powerful prediction capability to have higher weights during the fusion process. Experimental results on 6 real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed technique.

In case of technical failures or external events such as control surface defects or icing, aircraft dynamics and parameters are changed. Due to nonlinear dynamics of aircraft, usually the exact new altered dynamics cannot be determined by the pilot. Therefore the pilot who tries to plan a safe landing trajectory as soon as possible may implement a maneuver which is not feasible anymore according to the altered dynamics of the impaired aircraft and leads to aircraft loss of control (LOC). Therefore, the main challenge in the prevention of LOC-led-accidents is to increase the pilot's situational awareness and develop better control systems which both require post-failure dynamics identification and modeling. Both neural networks and neuro-fuzzy systems can be used for high-fidelity modeling of the aircraft nonlinear dynamics, however, the one with better generalization capability should be chosen. In this paper, several neural networks and local model networks are developed to model the nonlinear dynamics of an impaired aircraft with damaged rudder. These networks are trained using different training algorithms and their generalizations to the new cases of rudder failure are compared. Results show that both network types have good performance but neural networks generalize better to the new data than local model networks.

This paper presents a quick road obstacle detection system supported association and symmetry. This approach consists to exploit the edges extracted from consecutive images acquired by a stereo device embedded in an exceedingly moving vehicle. The formula contains 3 main elements: edges detection, association detection and symmetry calculation. The edges detection is achieved by using the canny operator and point corner to extract all possible edges of different objects at the image. The association technique is used to exploit relationship between the edges of two consecutives images by combining it with the moment operator. The symmetry is used as road obstacle validation; the road obstacles like vehicle and pedestrian have a vertical symmetry. The projected approach has been tested on completely different images. The provided results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

We aim to enhance the efficiency of charging stations by establishing quantitative connections between electric vehicles and chargers, while adhering to power limitations at the point of common coupling. To achieve this, we have developed a fuzzy logic-based algorithm for electric charging management that allows for maximum fulfilment of electricity demands within the designated power limits. Our algorithm has been tested through a model created in MATLAB Simulink, which verified its effectiveness in enhancing charging station efficiency.

We propose using a dynamic reservoir of spiking neurons to generate routing decisions for bundle transmissions in a delay tolerant network (DTN). The reservoir is able to quickly determine the next-hop for bundles by transforming the context of selected system metrics, as well as the temporal information contained in the network's contact list, into a high-dimensional feature space. This approach is particularly useful for space networks, which are characterized by resource-constrained nodes and known contact opportunities that have dynamic features, such as the state of the channels and buffers. 

The learning process for the spiking neural network takes place offline using linear regression and requires only a modest computational effort. Once the training process is completed, the spiking neural network can be used to achieve efficient network operation, allowing for a simple "recall" action of the best next-hop for the current conditions as stored in the reservoir, thus substituting the costly per-bundle shortest path computation. 

Different methods are investigated to translate the contact list information into a suitable input for the reservoir, and the approach is evaluated considering the impact of the readout function size applied to GEO-LEO DTN scenarios.

Cybercriminals exploit the opportunities provided by the information revolution and social media to communicate and conduct underground illicit activities, such as online fraudulence, cyber predation, cyberbullying, hacking, blackmailing, and drug smuggling. To combat the increasing number of criminal activities, structure and content analysis of criminal communities can provide insight and facilitate cybercrime forensics. In this paper, we propose a framework to analyze chat logs for crime investigation using data mining and natural language processing techniques. The proposed framework extracts the social network from chat logs and summarizes conversation into topics. The crime investigator can use information visualizer to see the crime-related results. To test the validity of our proposed framework, we worked in a joint effort with the cybercrime unit of a Canadian law enforcement agency. The experimental outcomes on real-life data and feedback from the law enforcement officers suggest that the proposed chat log mining framework meets the need for law enforcement agencies and is very effective for crime investigation.

Environmental Internet of Things (EIoT) has been widely applied in environmental monitoring. However, unified management, which is important for improving the operability and interoperability of EIoT systems, is difficult to perform due to the ubiquitous heterogeneity of EIoT systems. This paper puts forward an analysis of EIoT system management patterns and then proposes a storage layer monitoring (SLM) method to understand the state of EIoT systems, which is the basis for systems' management. A unified management framework for EIoT systems based on SLM is proposed, which includes event detection and fault diagnosis assistance. The framework uses a database to store metadata pertaining to each EIoT system, which are mostly registered as ontologies. Based on pre-registered metadata, users can create listeners for events, which is applicable for detecting events occurring in specific EIoT storage layers through the SLM method. The fault diagnosis assistance function can provide ontology-based evidence and other useful information about the participating objects of the event in the system, which is helpful for identifying the cause of each event. This framework could satisfy the requirements for multiple EIoT systems' management.

Various effective techniques have been developed for recognizing traffic signs, with conventional Image Processing methods being prevalent for many years. However, state-of-the-art detectors mostly rely on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) due to their impressive performance in image processing and computer vision research over the last decade. The availability and organization of datasets, particularly the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark, have facilitated this switch to CNNs. Although CNN-based detectors require a vast amount of data to operate well, no traffic-sign dataset exists in Pakistan, hindering the development of CNN-based detectors. To overcome this, this paper presents a transfer learning-based approach, in which a model is pre-trained using the German Traffic-sign Dataset and fine-tuned with 359 Pakistani dataset images. Preprocessing and regularization techniques were employed to enhance the overall performance of the model, which delivered training accuracies of nearly 41% with minimal overfitting. This is a promising result, as even with a limited dataset, a decent level of accuracy was achieved, which can be further boosted with more images gathered.

In this work, we consider the problem of designing a state of the art energy-efficient wireless sensor network (WSN) practically deployed in a large field. The sensor nodes (SNs) are tasked to monitor a large region of interest (ROI) and report their test statistics to the fusion center (FC) over a wireless fading channel. To maximize the lifetime of the WSN and enable long range communication with minimal transmit power, the long range wide area network (LoRaWAN) communication protocol is adopted. Each of the SN is designed and enabled with several state of the art sensors in order to estimate different and diverse parameters of interest (e.g., soil moisture, soil temperature, and salinity at different soil depth; barometric pressure, ambient humidity, leaf wetness, and etc.). The core feature of the proposed solution is that the SNs learn and adopt over the sensing time. This is very important in extending the operational lifetime of the WSN. The proposed system is validated through the infield experiments using few concept devices. Experimental results show that the proposed WSN features an effective large ROI monitoring with minimal number of SNs, a significantly reduced SN transmission power required and thus an extended WSN operational lifetime.

Image Processing (IP) applications have become popular with the advent of efficient algorithms and low-cost CMOS cameras with high resolution. However, IP applications are compute-intensive, consume a lot of energy and have long processing times. Image approximation has been proposed by recent works for an energy-efficient design of these applications. It also reduces the impact of long processing times. The challenge here is that the IP applications often work as a part of bigger closed-loop control systems, e.g. advanced driver assistance system (ADAS). The impact of image approximations that tolerate certain error on these image-based control (IBC) systems is very important. However, there is a lack of tool support to evaluate the performance of such closed-loop IBC systems when the IP is approximated. We propose a framework - for both software-in-the-loop (SiL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) simulation - for performance evaluation of image approximation on a closed-loop automotive IBC system (IMACS). Both simulation setups model the 3D environment in 3ds Max, and simulate the system dynamics, camera position and environment in V-REP. Our SiL setup simulates the system software in C++ or Matlab. Here, V-REP runs as a server and the software as a client in synchronous mode. Our HiL simulation setup runs the system software in the NVIDIA Drive PX2 platform and communicates to V-REP using application programming interfaces (APIs) for synchronous execution. We show the effectiveness of our framework using a vision-based lateral control example.

With the emergence of wireless embedded technologies, wireless sensor networks (WSN) have been widespread deployed in numerous applications. Researches have proven that the synergy of WSN with other arising technologies could assure full potential results. Since achieving an autonomous network requires a sustainable power source, energy harvesting represents a key element in this challenge. In this paper, we introduce a rectenna model based on a hybrid MoM-GEC (method of moment with the generalized equivalent circuit technique) and the method of auxiliary sources for RF energy harvesting. An electromagnetic study is presented for better understanding of the surrounding factors in the improvement of energy efficiency. This technique allowed the obtainment of a controllable and reconfigurable model. Finally, a validation of the results was achieved based on HFSS software simulations.

This study explores fault tolerant control in parallel interconnected asynchronous sequential machines (ASMs) using a matrix approach. This is a complex challenge as each submachine can potentially encounter unauthorized transitions due to adversarial inputs. The semi-tensor product method is employed to represent the dynamics of parallel interconnected ASMs in a discrete-time algebraic format. This framework is used to examine the reachability and fault detectability of parallel interconnected ASMs, and necessary and sufficient conditions for checking these attributes are established. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a system comprising of three asynchronous error accumulators is presented.

In multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar systems, it is important to emit orthogonal waveforms. However, in practice, this is not always guaranteed, which can lead to nonorthogonal waveforms being transmitted. This presents challenges for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation, including spatially colored noise and nonideal virtual direction matrix in colocated MIMO radar. To overcome these challenges, a temporal cross-correlation matrix-based algorithm has been proposed in this article. Additionally, the stochastic Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) has been derived. The proposed algorithm is efficient and accurate, and does not require prior knowledge of the waveform correlation matrix. Numerical experiments show that the algorithm is effective in addressing the challenges presented by nonorthogonal waveforms in MIMO radar systems.

Intra prediction is an important component of modern video codecs, which is able to efficiently squeeze out the spatial redundancy in video frames. With preceding pixels as the context, traditional intra prediction schemes generate linear predictions based on several predefined directions (i.e., modes) for blocks to be encoded. However, these modes are relatively simple and their predictions may fail when facing blocks with complex textures, which leads to additional bits encoding the residue. In this paper, we design a progressive spatial recurrent neural network (PS-RNN) that learns to conduct intra prediction. Specifically, our PS-RNN consists of three spatial recurrent units and progressively generates predictions by passing information along from preceding contents to blocks to be encoded. To make our network generate predictions considering both distortion and bit rate, we propose using sum of absolute transformed difference (SATD) as the loss function to train PS-RNN since SATD is able to measure rate-distortion cost of encoding a residue block. Moreover, our method supports variable-block-size for intra prediction, which is more practical in real coding conditions. The proposed intra prediction scheme achieves on average 2.5% bit-rate reduction on variable-block-size settings under the same reconstruction quality compared with HEVC.

A software-defined network (SDN) is a revolutionary concept that separates the control plane from the forwarding plane. As SDN deployments continue to grow in scale, the centralized control plane is becoming a bottleneck that is inhibiting the expansion of SDN networks. To tackle the issue of limited processing power across the wide area network (WAN), we propose a multi-controller deployment in a hierarchical architecture for software-defined WAN (SDWAN).

The proposed hierarchical architecture divides the control plane into multiple levels. The root controller has a global view, while the domain controller is responsible only for local network control. To discover the hierarchical community structure, we used an improved Louvain algorithm. Moreover, we took into consideration the load balancing and request delay in each partition as well as the reliability of the control plane to formulate modeling.

We further propose a hierarchical multi-controller deployment algorithm for the scalability of the SDWAN architecture. Simulation results demonstrate that when compared with traditional algorithms, the proposed algorithm not only reduces the average request delay and improves the performance of load balancing in each partition, but also enhances the reliability of the control plane and improves execution efficiency. 

In essence, our proposed hierarchical multi-controller deployment algorithm offers a scalable solution to the centralization bottleneck problem, which has been a major challenge in SDN network expansion.

Meta-heuristic search algorithms such as genetic algorithms have been applied successfully to generate unit tests, but typically take long to produce reasonable results, achieve sub-optimal code coverage, and have large variance due to their stochastic nature. Parallel genetic algorithms have been shown to be an effective improvement over sequential algorithms in many domains, but have seen little exploration in the context of unit test generation to date. In this paper, we describe a parallelised version of the many-objective sorting algorithm (MOSA) for test generation. Through the use of island models, where individuals can migrate between independently evolving populations, this algorithm not only reduces the necessary search time, but produces overall better results. Experiments with an implementation of parallel MOSA on the EvoSuite test generation tool using a large corpus of complex open source Java classes confirm that the parallelised MOSA algorithm achieves on average 84% code coverage, compared to 79% achieved by a standard sequential version.

The paper aims to enhance the effectiveness and dependability of the student performance prediction system and other similar intelligence systems in Educational Data mining by incorporating multiple algorithms. To achieve this, Meta Learning and Ensemble methods are used to improve the overall outcome of a multi-class system. Furthermore, a compliant model that can handle external and noisy data is proposed, surpassing the performance of the individual algorithms used in the composer system.

Advancements in deep learning have provided a powerful framework for disease classification based on neuroimaging data. However, interpreting the classification decision of convolutional neural networks remains a challenging task. Therefore, it is crucial to track the attention of the neural network and provide valuable information about which brain areas are particularly related to the diagnosis of disease. This paper proposes a novel attention-based 3D ResNet architecture to diagnose Alzheimer's disease (AD) and explore potential biological markers. Experiments are conducted on 532 subjects, including 227 patients with AD and 305 normal controls. By introducing the attention mechanism, the proposed approach improves the classification performance and simultaneously identifies important brain regions for AD classification. Furthermore, the experiments show that significant brain regions for AD diagnosis captured by the attention-based network are accompanied by significant changes in gray matter.

In recent years, there has been a shift in health care towards storing Electronic Health Records (EHRs) on mobile cloud environments which combine mobile devices with cloud computing. This paradigm allows for easier sharing of medical data between patients and healthcare providers with lower costs and greater flexibility. However, there are concerns regarding the security and privacy of this data.

To address this issue, we propose a new framework for the sharing of EHRs using blockchain and the decentralized interplanetary file system (IPFS) on mobile cloud platforms. Our framework incorporates a smart contract-based access control mechanism, which ensures secure EHR sharing among patients and healthcare providers. We have implemented a prototype of our proposal using Ethereum blockchain on a mobile app with Amazon cloud computing. Empirical results have shown that our framework provides an effective solution for secure data exchange on mobile clouds while protecting sensitive health information against potential threats. Our system evaluation and security analysis also demonstrate the benefits of our lightweight access control design, which minimizes network latency and maximizes security and data privacy.

Overall, our proposed framework offers a reliable solution for sharing EHRs on mobile cloud environments, while also addressing the issue of data privacy and security.

5G networks will utilize network slicing to cater to the varying needs of 5G applications. To analyze the impact of resource granularity on service availability and densification in network slicing, we have laid out a mathematical framework and system model. In this paper, we have established two operational points of the system, which are micro-slicing and macro-slicing regimes, based on fine and coarse resource allocation for slice instances. Our analysis has demonstrated that even with only two slice types, micro-slicing can achieve multiple orders of magnitude difference in service availability compared to macro-slicing. Although the macro-slicing regime with resource over-provisioning can support few slice types in the short run, it is not scalable to higher densities of slice types. Furthermore, our analysis has revealed the non-monotonic relationship between slice availability and resource granularity, which is due to a quantization effect. Therefore, system architects should consider moving directly into the micro-slicing regime to enable higher service densities in 5G cloud rather than adopting a gradual reduction in slice instance sizes.

Worst-case timing analysis plays a critical role in designing safe real-time systems based on manycore architectures, specifically Networks-on-Chip (NoCs). To address bursty traffic, such as real-time audio and video streams, this paper proposes potential extensions to a previously-published buffer-aware worst-case timing analysis approach. One promising lead involves improving the algorithm analyzing backpressure patterns, capturing the consecutive-packet queueing effect while still considering flow dependencies. Additionally, the improved algorithm can decrease the inherent complexity of computing the indirect blocking latency due to backpressure. These enhancements can help to ensure real-time systems are safe and meet performance requirements.

For lossy image compression systems, we develop an algorithm, iterative refinement, to improve the decoder's reconstruction compared to standard decoding techniques. Specifically, we propose a recurrent neural network approach for nonlinear, iterative decoding. Our decoder, which works with any encoder, employs self-connected memory units that make use of causal and non-causal spatial context information to progressively reduce reconstruction error over a fixed number of steps. We experiment with variants of our estimator and find that iterative refinement consistently creates lower distortion images of higher perceptual quality compared to other approaches. Specifically, on the Kodak Lossless True Color Image Suite, we observe as much as a 0.871 decibel (dB) gain over JPEG, a 1.095 dB gain over JPEG 2000, and a 0.971 dB gain over a competitive neural model.

The field of Social Computing is rife with potential for exploring the value hidden within the data generated by various social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Snapchat, LinkedIn, etc. However, with the increasing volume of data, traditional techniques are no longer sufficient for gaining insights. This has led researchers to adopt machine learning techniques as a means of analyzing large volumes of data.

This paper aims to introduce some of the significant research problems in the area of social computing, the machine learning and statistical methods utilized by researchers worldwide, and the research gaps that still need to be addressed. Among the critical problems in social computing, the paper highlights the task of distinguishing real tweets from fake tweets on the Twitter platform.

As such, the classification of a tweet as either genuine or fake has become a crucial problem that requires innovative solutions. With the widespread use of social media platforms for communication and information dissemination, distinguishing fact from fiction has become increasingly important as fake news can have significant consequences. Therefore, researchers are heavily invested in developing novel approaches for identifying fake news on social media platforms.

In conclusion, the field of social computing holds great promise for uncovering valuable insights from social media data. Machine learning techniques have emerged as a vital tool for handling the vast amounts of data generated on social media platforms. However, there are still important research gaps that must be addressed, including the problem of correctly classifying tweets as genuine or fake.

Simultaneous EEG-fMRI has become a popular method to study the spatiotemporal patterns of cortical activity associated with complex cognitive tasks, including emotion regulation. Specifically, the late positive potential (LPP), which occurs over parietal areas during emotion processing, has become a major focus of interest. However, the involvement of prefrontal areas in the modulation of LPP remains unclear.

To address this issue, the current study utilized EEG-informed fMRI to investigate the cortical areas involved in the modulation of frontal LPP during emotion regulation. EEG and fMRI data were collected simultaneously during an emotion reappraisal task, and EEG data were analyzed between 400-600ms after task onset. Group Independent Component Analysis (ICA) was used to denoise the EEG signal and extract common features across trials for all subjects and conditions. These features were then used as regressors in general linear model (GLM)-based fMRI analysis.

Results showed that the septum pellucidum, right insula, and right subcallosal gyrus were involved in the modulation of the LPP amplitude in prefrontal regions during reappraisal-based emotion regulation. These findings are consistent with previous studies on emotion regulation and provide further evidence for the utility of IC-based EEG-informed fMRI in the study of emotional regulation.

This paper proposes a novel neural network approach for low frequency oscillation mode identification in power systems. After employing the fast Fourier transform in order selection, we then introduce a specific neural network whose topology strictly follows the exponentially damped sinusoidal model of low frequency oscillation signals. We thus turn the parameter estimation into an optimization problem. Simulations show that the proposed approach is superior to the state-of-art neural network schemes in anti-noise ability, parameter accuracy and computation speed.

In the field of reliability analysis for practical engineering problems, accurately assessing reliability with minimum computational cost is a significant challenge, especially for time-consuming models. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel sequential surrogate method named AK-MCMC. The method combines adaptive kriging and Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation with a learning strategy for efficient reliability analysis. 

AK-MCMC benefits from the classification feature of surrogate models, enabling it to approximate the performance function's classification boundary efficiently. The proposed learning strategy focuses on selecting informative samples for updating the experimental design samples sequentially. A new stopping criterion guarantees the accuracy of the constructed kriging model's classification, making the reliability evaluation independent of an adaptive iterative process. This approach significantly improves the efficiency of model refinement.

The effectiveness of the AK-MCMC method is demonstrated through several engineering problem examples that include a small failure probability problem, non-linearity problem, and a problem with an implicit performance function. The proposed method's efficiency is proven in particular for problems with small failure probabilities.

In this study, we have proposed a forecast model for predicting the variation of sign between the exchange rate of Chilean peso and American dollar (CLP-USD) over two consecutive exchange days. Our model is based on the development of a feedforward Artificial Neural Network. The structure of the model includes a set of explanatory premises that describe the exchange behavior in a non-monotonous logical setting.

To develop the model, we have used the exchange rate CLP-USD at the beginning, closure, minimum, and maximum values obtained during an exchange day from January 1, 2005 to July 9, 2018. The obtained results demonstrate the strong predictive power of our model. It is capable of accurately predicting the sign variation of the exchange with good and robust percentage in different extra samples.

Overall, our proposed model provides a promising approach for forecasting the variation of sign between the exchange rate of Chilean peso and American dollar in different extra samples, and could be useful for financial planning and decision-making processes.

Traffic classification has been studied for two decades and applied to a wide range of applications from QoS provisioning and billing in ISPs to security-related applications in firewalls and intrusion detection systems. Port-based, data packet inspection, and classical machine learning methods have been used extensively in the past, but their accuracy has declined due to the dramatic changes in Internet traffic, particularly the increase in encrypted traffic. With the proliferation of deep learning methods, researchers have recently investigated these methods for traffic classification and reported high accuracy. In this article, we introduce a general framework for deep-learning-based traffic classification. We present commonly used deep learning methods and their application in traffic classification tasks. Then we discuss open problems, challenges, and opportunities for traffic classification.

In this paper, we study top-N recommendation by exploiting users' explicit feedback such as 5-star numerical ratings, which has been overlooked to some extent in the past decade. As a response, we design a novel and generic transfer learning based recommendation framework coarse-to-fine transfer to rank (CoFiToR), which is a significant extension of a very recent work called transfer to rank (ToR). The key idea of our solution is modeling users' behaviors by simulating users' shopping processes. Therefore, we convert the studied ranking problem to three subtasks corresponding to three specific questions, including (i) whether an item will be examined by a user, (ii) how an item will be scored by a user, and (iii) whether an item will finally be purchased by a user. Based on this new conversion, we then develop a three-staged solution that progressively models users' preferences from a coarse granularity to a fine granularity. In each stage, we adopt an appropriate recommendation algorithm with pointwise or pairwise preference assumption to answer each question in order to seek an effective and efficient overall solution. Empirical studies on two large and public datasets showcase the merits of our solution in comparison with the state-of-the-art methods.

As the improving strategic position of electronic warfare in modern warfare, radar sorting detection becomes the eye of modern information warfare and plays an important role in it. This paper designs a new pulse radar sorting algorithm: a Density-Based Fuzzy C-Means Multi-Center Re-Clustering (DFCMRC) radar signal sorting algorithm. This algorithm mainly combines the advantages of Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) clustering algorithm and Fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering algorithm. This paper also optimizes the structure of the DFCMRC algorithm, which changes the algorithm that randomly generated the initial center point to the Clustering by Fast Search and Find of Density Peaks (CFSFDP) algorithm. After comparison tests, the DFCMRC algorithm sorting result is better than the K-means algorithm, the DBSCAN algorithm and the FCM algorithm. Also, the membership grade description of DFCMRC makes more sense than the FCM's. Accelerated optimized DFCMRC algorithm can reduce more than half iterations, which greatly shortens the algorithm calculation time.

A Simulink model has been built based on a closed-loop mathematic model of the flywheel system, accounting for the fault modes and corresponding parameters. To gather data for two faults, training and testing data have been collected from the Simulink model. Afterward, Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) has been proposed to analyze the correlation among the five parameters of the flywheel system. The testing data will show any abnormal changes caused by flywheel faults. This method is able to provide a solution to the challenges presented by the lack of knowledge of faults and the complexity of mathematical modeling. By analyzing the training data, the behaviors of flywheel can be learned and the correlation of the five parameters in the flywheel system can be identified. However, the variable correlation has two types, linear and nonlinear. While the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) can be used in building the linear model of the training data, the five chosen variables exhibit a nonlinear relationship. To highlight the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, it is essential to compare the detections results of KPCA with the results of PCA. Simulation results indicate that the SPEKPCA index can successfully detect flywheel faults without the need for complex mathematical modeling, and demonstrate superior performance compared to the detection results of the PCA model.

In this paper, we propose a measurement-based method to estimate the dynamic system state matrix. The method makes use of the regression theorem of the multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and employs a recursive algorithm to minimize computational effort, making it suitable for real-time environments.

One of the main advantages of our proposed method is model independence. This means that it is not dependent on the network model or the dynamic model of the generators. We demonstrate one of the many applications of the estimated matrix, which is detecting and locating unexpected network topology changes. 

Our simulation studies have shown that the proposed method can provide an accurate and efficient estimation of the dynamic system state matrix, even under the occurrence of unexpected topology changes. In addition, we have tested various implementation conditions to demonstrate that the proposed method can provide accurate approximation despite measurement noise, missing phasor measurement units (PMUs), and the implementation of higher-order generator models with control devices. 

Overall, our proposed measurement-based method offers a reliable and efficient approach to estimate the dynamic system state matrix, making it a promising tool for real-time applications in power system analysis and control.

The Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) problem for critical infrastructures using wireless sensor networks (WSN), has received considerable attention in the research community in recent years. Sensors placed in these infrastructures have two functions, sensing/coverage and communication. The thrust of this paper is on the coverage aspects of sensor networks. In the Point Coverage model, only a specified set of points in the deployment area have to be sensed. The goal of placement optimization is to find the smallest set of locations to deploy sensors, so that all the points of interest can be sensed. This problem often is solved by formulating it as a Set Cover problem. However, the Set Cover approach has a serious limitation on the accurate identification of the location where abnormality is sensed. In this paper, we present a technique to overcome this limitation by utilizing Identifying Code. We study two different scenarios, where the sensors and points of interest are located in one and two-dimensional spaces respectively. We provide a polynomial time optimal algorithm for the one-dimensional case and an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) based optimal solution for the two-dimensional case. We evaluate the efficacy of the ILP solution with varying network size (45 to 64655 nodes). The ILP produced an optimal solution for the largest instance with 64655 nodes and 155339 edges in only 180.45 seconds.

The feasibility of adopting distributed massive multiple-input multiple-output (D-MMIMO) for mitigating the achievable rate loss incurred by spatially-correlated fading at space-constrained user antenna arrays when served by co-located massive MIMO (C-MMIMO) counterpart is investigated. In order to explore a practically-viable design, the cumulative effects of spatial correlation at both multi-antenna access points (APs) and multi-antenna users, beamforming uncertainty caused by imperfectly estimated channel state information (CSI), and adverse effects of pilot contamination have been taken into account. The achievable user rates of the proposed D-MMIMO downlink operating in a multi-cell set-up are derived for finite/infinite antenna array regimes at the distributed APs. Thereby, the achievable user rates for C-MMIMO counterpart are deduced and compared with those of the proposed D-MMIMO downlink. Through a rigorous analysis and simulation results, we show that the distributed transmissions rendered by D-MMIMO can provide significant performance gains compared to the C-MMIMO counterpart (i) by minimizing adverse effects of spatial correlation via distinct spatial-directions/signatures rendered by distributed transmissions, (ii) by mitigating shadow fading via leveraging macro-diversity gains, and (iii) by reducing the average path-losses through effectively shortening transmission distances. Moreover, we reveal that the proposed D-MMIMO can be exploited to recover a significant portion of rate loss incurred by the lost of asymptotic channel orthogonality due to doubly-correlated channels when both APs and user nodes are equipped with space-constrained multiple-antenna arrays.

Environmental monitoring plays a crucial role in today's unpredictable and constantly changing world. With global warming, pollution, and air pressure increasing, natural disasters such as cloud bursts have become more frequent, causing loss of lives and damaging our agricultural sector and other areas. Therefore, monitoring the environment is crucial to protect human lives and prevent environmental damage. 

This paper focuses on cloud bursts, which have become a significant concern in hilly areas like Uttarakhand and Shimla. By using technology to predict cloud bursts two or three days in advance, we can prevent the loss of life and make it easier for people to migrate from these areas. A critical aspect of this prediction is understanding how cumulonimbus clouds are formed. One way to do this is by using brightness temperature to track cloud formation. 

In summary, the importance of environmental monitoring cannot be overstated, and cloud bursts are just one example of the many natural disasters that are becoming more common. By using technology and scientific methods, we can predict and prevent the loss of life and damage to the environment caused by these events.

Integration of solid-liquid phase change materials (PCMs) into electronics packaging has demonstrated the potential to reduce the transient temperature rise of components that experience pulsed thermal loads. However, the impact on local temperature histories resulting from incorporating PCMs in different locations and configurations within an electronics package is not easy to analytically determine, due in large part to the non-linear response of PCMs to a transient heat load. ParaPower is a new parametric design tool to facilitate the design of electronics packages. The tool has the capability of easily incorporating arbitrarily located PCM volumes and evaluating their effect on temperature distributions within the electronics package as a function of time. This paper determines the spatial and temporal order of convergence for the reduced order phase-change thermal model which underlies ParaPower. The results are compared and validated against both an analytical solution and a higher-fidelity commercial finite element analysis (FEA) tool. This paper has shown the fast-solving methods used in the ParaPower tool give results with comparable accuracy to those obtained using high-fidelity commercial software. Reasonably good accuracy can be obtained with fairly large time steps and grid spacing allowing fast-solving design space exploration with this option to increase fidelity within the tool to obtain higher accuracy when necessary. This research quantifies the trade-off between time steps, grid size, and accuracy such that a useful balance can be obtained. Design tools, such as ParaPower, have the potential to significantly advance design theory to reduce size and cost as well as minimize the prevalence of overdesign.

This paper presents the use of Group Lasso Regression (G-Lasso) for software fault proneness classification and compares its performance to six commonly used machine learning algorithms. The study aims to investigate the impact of two factors on the prediction performance - the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) for imbalanced data and different datasets used in building the prediction models. The experimental results are based on 22 datasets extracted from open source projects. 

The findings indicate that G-Lasso is resilient to imbalanced data and outperforms other machine learning algorithms in terms of Recall and G-Score. SMOTE improved the performance of all learners, but it did not have a significant impact on G-Lasso's Recall and G-Score. Among all the learners, Random Forest was the top performer for all performance metrics, while Naive Bayes demonstrated the worst performance. 

Interestingly, the choice of the dataset had little effect on the performance of most learners, including G-Lasso, when using the same change metrics as features. Only Naive Bayes was significantly affected, particularly when using balanced datasets. 

Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of G-Lasso in software fault proneness classification tasks and highlight the importance of considering imbalanced data and appropriate datasets for building accurate predictive models.

Pap smear testing is commonly used for identifying cervical cancers by examining the nuclei of cells in microscopic images. The accuracy of cervical cancer screening can be enhanced by improving the segmentation of cell nuclei, and this work proposes an automated approach utilizing the Deformable Multipath Ensemble Model (D-MEM) to achieve this goal. The method uses a U-shaped convolutional network as a backbone network with dense blocks, which enhances the transfer of feature information. To address nuclei that are irregular in shape or size, the approach employs deformable convolution to increase model flexibility. To minimize predictive bias, multiple networks with different settings are combined as an ensemble model. The proposed segmentation framework achieved state-of-the-art accuracy on the Herlev dataset, with a Zijdenbos similarity index (ZSI) of 0.933±014, and has potential applications for other medical image segmentation tasks.

Wearables that acquire relevant vital and contextual parameters improve work safety as well as quality of life of elderly citizens or patients with chronic diseases. A scalable architecture connects wearables via a hub to the cloud and combines edge with cloud computing to provide optimal user interaction and allow analytics on multi-stream data. The functionality was expanded to enable demonstrations of physiological and psychological stress classification in firemen and mobile health interventions in patients with lung diseases. Following an initial table-top edge demonstrator a hemi-spherical display improves emotional contact to users. A first use case tested an integrated acquisition and inference system that was trained to differentiate physical and emotional stress. The system measured stress in firemen during training in a cage maze and in hot training locations and provided functions to acquire expert labels. A second use case focused on mobile-health intervention for patients suffering from Chronic-Obstructive-Pulmonary-Disease (COPD), to improve their quality-of-life. Patient-physician conversations are extended through a communication channel and a virtual assistant provides disease related information, reminders, and alerts.

This study focuses on tuning the parameters of proportional integral derivative controller (PID). These parameters are traditionally tuned through the Zeigler-Nichols method. However, fuzzy logic control is usually used to online adjust the PID controller parameters. Interestingly, to find the optimal fuzzy controller scaling factors, particle swarm optimization (PSO) may also be used. Nonetheless, in presence of multi-input multi-output (MIMO), nonlinear, and under-actuated systems, a multidimensional tune is necessary, which renders finding the optimal fuzzy-PID controller with PSO algorithm a difficult task. Then, this paper presents an adapted multidimensional PSO algorithm in order to improve the performances of a fuzzy-PID controller for stabilizing a quadrotor system when tracking its reference trajectory. Moreover, to show the effectiveness of this optimization strategy, it is shown that, using simulation tools, the fuzzy-PID controller that is tuned by the proposed multidimensional PSO algorithm could ensure better time domain specifications, in comparison with a classical PID controller.

This special issue explores the challenges posed by the design of very-large-scale integration (VLSI) nodes for the Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems. These systems use wireless communication to link together physical devices into distributed real-time embedded systems. IoT systems are used in a wide range of applications, including industrial control, vehicles, smart grids, and medical and health care systems.

In the framework of the Huber's minimax variance approach to designing robust estimates of localization parameters, a generalization of the classical least informative distributions minimizing Fisher information for location is obtained in the wide class of ranging error distributions with a bounded quantile value. The considered variational problem set up naturally originates from the real-life problem of estimation of the unknown coordinates of an asset surrounded by the beacons with known positions.

We present a novel neural network architecture, US-Net, for robust nuclei instance segmentation in histopathology images. The proposed framework integrates the nuclei detection and segmentation networks by sharing their outputs through the same foundation network, and thus enhancing the performance of both. The detection network takes into account the high-level semantic cues with contextual information, while the segmentation network focuses more on the low-level details like the edges. Extensive experiments reveal that our proposed framework can strengthen the performance of both branch networks in an integrated architecture and outperforms most of the state-of-the-art nuclei detection and segmentation networks.

Data stream has been the underlying challenge in the age of big data because it calls for real-time data processing with the absence of a retraining process and/or an iterative learning approach. In the realm of the fuzzy system community, data stream is handled by algorithmic development of self-adaptive neuro-fuzzy systems (SANFS) characterized by the single-pass learning mode and the open structure property that enables effective handling of fast and rapidly changing natures of data streams. The underlying bottleneck of SANFSs lies in its design principle, which involves a high number of free parameters (rule premise and rule consequent) to be adapted in the training process. This figure can even double in the case of the type-2 fuzzy system. In this paper, a novel SANFS, namely parsimonious learning machine (PALM), is proposed. PALM features utilization of a new type of fuzzy rule based on the concept of hyperplane clustering, which significantly reduces the number of network parameters because it has no rule premise parameters. PALM is proposed in both type-1 and type-2 fuzzy systems where all of which characterize a fully dynamic rule-based system. That is, it is capable of automatically generating, merging, and tuning the hyperplane-based fuzzy rule in the single-pass manner. Moreover, an extension of PALM, namely recurrent PALM, is proposed and adopts the concept of teacher-forcing mechanism in the deep learning literature. The efficacy of PALM has been evaluated through numerical study with six real-world and synthetic data streams from public database and our own real-world project of autonomous vehicles. The proposed model showcases significant improvements in terms of computational complexity and number of required parameters against several renowned SANFSs, while attaining comparable and often better predictive accuracy.

The performance of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs (High Electron Mobility Transistors) is crucial for high voltage and frequency power applications. To enhance their performance, field-plate technology is frequently employed. However, measuring the maximum temperature of devices with field-plates can be challenging due to geometrical constraints. 

To compare the temperature measurement performance and limits of micro-Raman thermography and Thermoreflectance Thermal Imaging (TTI) on field-plated devices, a numerical thermal model was developed. This model takes into account the size effects in the channel that occur because of the small heat generation region in such devices. 

The numerical model simulated the peak temperatures of devices with and without field-plates, at various power densities, using micro-Raman and TTI measurements. The goal was to identify the maximum temperature measurement capability of micro-Raman and TTI for field-plated devices and suggest appropriate techniques. 

Overall, the results indicated that both micro-Raman and TTI have the capability to accurately measure the maximum temperature of field-plated devices. However, certain considerations must be taken into account, such as the thermal conductivity of the substrate and the size of the heat generation region, to ensure accurate measurements. These findings provide important insights into improving the reliability of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs in high voltage and frequency power applications.

Grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems are becoming increasingly popular due to the rise of green energy usage. This study explores the modeling and control of a multilevel inverter-based single-stage grid-connected PV system utilizing a cascaded two-level inverter (CTLI) through MATLAB/Simulink. The multilevel inverter topology is formed by cascading two conventional voltage source inverters (VSI) with the help of an open-winding transformer. The hysteresis current controllers are employed to regulate the inverters, and p-q theory generates the synchronizing reference currents. Fuzzy logic controllers are used to maximize power output from the PV array, producing a change in reference power that is to be injected into the grid by the CTLI. The simulation showed that the CTLI based grid connected PV system effectively injects active power produced by the PV array under varying solar insolation and varying load conditions. Additionally, it provides reactive power compensation during low or zero insolation conditions, yielding effective utilization of the PV system. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed control scheme for injecting active and reactive power in a controlled manner.

This paper addresses the issue of tracking control for nonlinear networked and quantized control systems. The tracking error is affected by errors induced by the reference system and network, which hinders convergence. To overcome this limitation, the study proposes a unified hybrid model. By using Lyapunov theory, the paper derives sufficient conditions that ensure convergence of the tracking error. The Lyapunov function's existence is also explored. Finally, the study presents a numerical example to demonstrate the theory's applicability.

Logistic regression and softmax regression are two effective methods for handling two-class and multi-class classification problems, but they require ground truth labels which can be difficult, expensive, and time-consuming to obtain. This presents a significant challenge when dealing with classification problems. Unsupervised learning and ensemble learning have been shown to be useful in obtaining labels. In this study, we construct an objective function based on softmax regression and unsupervised learning. We propose a new evaluation index, C, to measure the confidence of unsupervised ensemble learning during inference. Additionally, we have developed the SRuel algorithm to correspond to this approach. Results from extensive experiments demonstrate the high performance of our proposed algorithm.

Pulse coupled neural network (PCNN) is the third generation of artificial neural network with strict biological background, which is different from traditional artificial neural networks. Compared with traditional feedback neural networks, pulse coupled neural network possesses significant characteristics from the point of composition of neuron. PCNN has the firing features of dynamic pulse, firing features of synchronization pulse, and dynamic and variable features of threshold value, which brings excellent effect of image segmentation and image denoising etc to PCNN. LVQ neural network is a competitive type neural network with supervised learning method; the algorithm is derived from Kohonen competitive algorithm. LVQ network is able to complete classification processing of extremely complicated pattern recognition through interaction of internal elements only due to its simple structure, with excellent features for pattern recognition. This paper carries out study on the technology of image segmentation by virtue of PCNN; invariant moment features and textural features are extracted from different types of images to realize the effect of image dimension reduction. Finally, feature vectors will be sent to LVQ neural network to realize classification recognition. The experimental result indicates excellent segmentation effect and strong adaptability of this method, enabling better image recognition.

Recently, there has been a proposal to offload computation-intensive tasks from mobile devices to nearby resource-rich surrogates, called edge servers, due to the bottleneck of bandwidth and resource limitation for devices in traditional mobile cloud computing. The primary concern of offloading is the maximization of energy saving under task delay and task dependency limitation. Additionally, edge servers that are perceived by mobile devices are changeable and heterogeneous during the offloading process. 

In this paper, we formalize this problem and reduce it into a knapsack problem. We propose a task scheduling scheme, named TaSRD, which involves independent sub-task scheduling for tasks without dependencies and dependent sub-task scheduling for dependent tasks. We implement TaSRD and evaluate it through case study and simulation on the CloudSim framework developed by Melbourne University. We utilize a time model and an energy model to measure results and recommend suitable parameters for TaSRD. The experimental results demonstrate that TaSRD can effectively save energy and reduce makespan for mobile devices while offloading tasks to edge servers.

Network virtualization is a crucial component in the implementation of 5G systems, as it facilitates the support of novel use cases related to vertical markets. With this in mind, our focus is on finding the optimal deployment strategy for Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) and computational resource allocation in a hybrid cloud infrastructure, taking into account the specific requirements of 5G services and characteristics of cloud nodes. By examining the relations among functional placement, computational requirements, and latency constraints, we formulate an integer linear programming problem that can be addressed through a standard solver. Our findings demonstrate that the hybrid cloud architecture offers superior performance compared to a standard solution with a central cloud. Furthermore, our proposed VNF deployment mechanism results in highly efficient resource utilization and significant gains in terms of the number of slice chains that can be supported by cloud-enhanced 5G networks.

Skull stripping for brain MR images is a basic segmentation task. Although many methods have been proposed, most of them focused mainly on the adult MR images. Skull strip-ping for infant MR images is more challenging due to the small size and dynamic intensity changes of brain tissues during the early ages. In this paper, we propose a novel CNN based framework to robustly extract brain region from infant MR image without any human assistance. Specifically, we propose a simplified but more robust flattened residual net-work architecture (FRnet). We also introduce a new boundary loss function to highlight ambiguous and low contrast regions between brain and non-brain regions. To make the whole framework more robust to MR images with different imaging quality, we further introduce an artifact simulator for data augmentation. We have trained and tested our proposed framework on a large dataset (N=343), covering newborns to 48-month-olds, and obtained performance better than the state-of-the-art methods in all age groups.

This paper introduces an image stitching technique for combining images of corrugated cardboard in order to create a complete image of the entire pile. The image stitching algorithm involves several steps, including the detection of corner features using the Forstner method, feature matching, elimination of inconsistent features using random sample consensus (RANSAC), and image composition through bundle adjustment. The algorithm was tested on cut-off side type BC, 5 sheets simulated using the HALCON program. The experimental results showed that the algorithm was able to correctly combine images of cut-off sides when they overlapped by approximately 25%. The output of the combined image was compared to the real number of cardboard pieces by manually counting, and the corresponding result was obtained.

In this paper, we introduce a nonlinear controller that aims to achieve high-precision trajectory tracking for robotic manipulators with unknown model parameters. These unknown parameters may include the uncertain moment of inertia, uncertain geometry of the manipulator, unknown friction torque, unknown gravitational torque, and payload variation.

Previous model-based control methods for robotic manipulators required accurate model parameters, which can be difficult to obtain, particularly when faced with unknown model parameters. Therefore, we propose the use of a model-error observer that can effectively estimate parameter errors.

Our proposed control law utilizes the model-error observer to handle unknown model parameters, which effectively addresses the challenge presented by model-based control methods. Through simulations, we demonstrate the robust performance of this controller and its ability to achieve accurate path tracking despite the presence of friction and unknown model parameters.

In conclusion, the nonlinear controller proposed in this paper provides an effective solution for robotic manipulators with uncertain model parameters. The use of a model-error observer enables accurate trajectory tracking even when faced with uncertainties, demonstrating the feasibility and robustness of this approach.

Software-defined networks (SDN) have appeared as effective network technology, which is able to support the dynamic nature of future network functions and intelligent applications. On the other hand, the progress of the SDN is limited by various security threats. Analyzing the centralized nature of SDN, we found multiple potential vulnerabilities, which the attacker may use. Our solution covers a wider area, not just data plane, but also control plane security. The traffic, which is flowing through a data plane, could include various security threats. To detect them, we utilize OpenFlow possibilities and Machine Learning (ML) concept for the proposed Network Intrusion Detection System based on Deep Neural Network (NIDS-DNN). The solution can extract network statistics from OpenFlow switches (OF switches) and process them with DNN. The result is to warn about an attack on the data plane and to prevent malicious users from harming the network. For early detection of DoS/DDoS attacks aimed at controller, we present our solution - Specter, which changes the approach to the flow processing prioritization. Using priority queues ensures a better quality of service for legitimate users. To the best of our knowledge, our work is the first solution, which couple intrusion detection in the data plane with protection against DoS attacks in control plane.

Human tracking in video feeds has become an increasingly popular area of research, with numerous state-of-the-art approaches being utilized, including tracking-by-detection, feature tracking, and tracking by recognition/re-identification. One particularly advanced tracking-by-detection implementation is the Dlib correlation tracker, which is commonly used for human tracking but struggles to maintain continuous tracking during occlusions.

To address this issue, we propose a state estimation approach that can extend the capabilities of Dlib correlation tracker under occlusions, while simultaneously utilizing human detection. Through real-world experiment scenarios, our proposed approach has shown improved results compared to solely using Dlib correlation tracker with human detection.

With further development and utilization of various trackers, the approach has the potential to be widely applied to a broad range of human tracking use cases.

Numerous machine learning techniques and social engineering methods have been developed and utilized in the fight against phishing threats. This paper proposes a unique hybrid deep learning model to identify phishing attacks. The model comprises two components: an autoencoder (AE) and a convolutional neural network (CNN). The AE is used to reconstruct features that enhance the relationship between the features. Experimental results show that the model can detect phishing attacks with an average accuracy of 97.68%. Moreover, the model exhibits strong generalization ability and can identify phishing attacks in a timely manner.

The aim of this study is to propose an approach to the automatic recognition of emotions from the signal speech [18], [13]: it relies on the extraction of spectral and prosodies characteristics, more particularly on the energy and the distribution of this energy in six bands. These characteristics are obtained from syllabic units (CV) where C denotes a consonant and V a vowel. To this end, we constructed a Moroccan emotional database (MEDB) from broadcasts on the YouTube channel representing different real emotional states. The features set is obtained from Matlab codes and Praat [23] software. The emotions used in this study are anger, joy, neutral state and sadness. The emotion recognition systems are developed using neural networks, Support Vector Machine and decision trees algorithms. The aim of this work is firstly to explore syllabic units to identify the emotions embedded in the speech signal and secondly to demonstrate the relevance of the energy distribution in determining emotional states.
