The paper presents an automated classification system for melanoma diagnosis. It is based on a convolutional neural network that is fed with images of skin lesions which are preprocessed in advance. The preprocess step is necessary for reducing the number of artifacts present in the images and hence, maximize the classification accuracy. The proposed solution is based on the training of the neural network with a series of preprocessed clinical images, classifying them in two categories: benign or malignant.

Novel skyrmion-magnetic tunnel junction (SK-MTJ) devices were investigated for the first time to implement the ternary neural networks (TNN). In the SK-MTJ, an extra magnetoresistance state beyond binary parallel and anti-parallel MTJ states was achieved by forming a skyrmion vortex structure in the free layer. Based on the SK-MTJ, we propose a synaptic architecture with bit-cell design of +1, 0, and -1 to replace the full precision floating point arithmetic with equivalent bit-wise multiplication operation. To explore the feasibility of the SK-MTJ-based synaptic devices for TNN application, circuitlevel simulations for image recognition task were conducted. The recognition rate can reach up to 99% with 5% device variation and an average power consumption of 29.23 μW.

Intergroup conflict induces individuals to hold negative prejudice and discriminate against others from different groups. Individual's anti-social attitudes on intergroup conflict setting are based on an individual's belief on negative outgroup stereotype. Some theories based on social identity theory have been proposed to explain the emergence of this belief but their explanatory power is limited. An agent-based model is proposed to clarify the process of negative outgroup stereotype development and to reproduce key findings. The model explains how negative outgroup stereotype belief emerges as the outcome of an intergroup conflict situation. Not only that, it also explains how an individual's position in the social network affects his/her perception of outgroup stereotype.

Indian power distribution system is highly scattered by spreading throughout the control. The present research work focuses on integration of solar PV system with the traditional power distribution system by PI and ANFIS PI system due to increasing the demand of the electrical energy, it is required to interconnect a no. of renewable PV system with the grid which not only provides the extra amount of power which is required for load point of view but also economical from its generation point of view. The current control technique must be saved and highly reliable/efficient. Again, the controller must obey the standard grid code that is applicable to Indian electricity. In this paper a comparative study of PI and ANFIS PI current control technique is presented. In order to show the robustness of the controller MATLAB Simulink environment has been adopted for designing of the proposed controllers.

This paper presents the results of data analysis from a geographically distributed network of honeypots that were deployed almost two years ago across Samara, Rostov on Don, Crimea, and the USA. The collected data was analyzed to build a model of network intrusion, which includes blacklists for attacking IP addresses for various Internet services, as well as statistics for calls to OS ports. Of particular interest are the ranked lists of basic Internet threats that are commonly used by hackers.

In a multi-tenant cloud environment, tenants are hosted using virtual machines that are deployed on physical servers to utilize physical resources better such as CPU, memory, and storage devices. The use of SSDs as an I/O cache shared among tenants for large storage systems that use HDDs as their primary storage devices is a common practice. This approach provides the benefits of both SSD and HDD, where the SSD cache can improve performance while the HDD can keep the cost low. Nevertheless, one of the challenges in using the shared cache is to ensure strong performance isolation and maintain high utilization.

Conventional SSD cache management approaches may not be effective in tackling this challenge. To address this, we propose OC-Cache, an open-channel SSD cache framework that utilizes the internal parallelism of SSD to adaptively allocate cache to tenants both for high performance isolation and SSD utilization. OC-Cache uses the miss ratio curve of a tenant to determine the amount of cache space allocation and where the allocation is (in dedicated or shared SSD channels). It also dynamically manages the cache space based on the workload characteristics.

Experimental results show that OC-Cache significantly reduces interference among tenants while maintaining high utilization of the SSD cache. The proposed framework addresses the challenge of performance isolation while ensuring efficient resource utilization in a multi-tenant cloud environment.

In spectrum-sliced elastic optical path networks (SLICE), variability of the lightpath bandwidth and optimization of the spectrum utilization through virtual topology overlay on physical topology is crucial. The typical design for SLICE networks under static traffic involves mixed integer linear programming (MILP) with the aim of minimizing spectrum utilization. However, this paper proposes a new MILP formulation for protection in SLICE networks that guarantees minimum agreed bandwidth for each source-destination pair in the surviving bandwidth through the concept of bandwidth squeezing and grooming. By using balance equations and physical layer constraints, the formulation determines the route for each demand on the physical topology, eliminating the need for pre-calculated routes while still allowing the choice of modulation format for each established lightpath. The proposed formulation jointly solves virtual topology design and physical topology design problems. Results from case studies evaluating the proposed formulation's effectiveness suggest that it can identify configurations that ensure minimum spectrum occupation even with different kinds of protection and modulation formats. A heuristic algorithm is also proposed for moderately large networks due to the NP-hard nature of the MILP formulation. Overall, this proposed formulation can greatly improve spectrum utilization optimization in SLICE networks.

In wireless sensor network (WSN) nodes relay data, which maintains consistency in the sensor network. If cut vertex nodes failed it leads to partitioning in network, which disrupts the communication. It requires an autonomous technique that finds the fail node and provides recovery to them. In this paper the proposed approach provides recovery from network partitioning in distribute WSN. The proposed approach increases the lifetime of network.

Data aggregation is a critical technique in wireless sensor networks in which the data collected from various nodes are processed and aggregated en-route by intermediate sensor nodes. Security is a significant concern in such networks, as the sensor nodes are often resource-constrained and can be compromised by malicious attackers. Previous research focused only on detecting intermediate nodes from modifying partial aggregation results, with two security challenges remaining. First, compromised sensor nodes can report arbitrary readings of their own, which is challenging to detect but is generally believed to have a limited effect on the final aggregation result. Second, compromised sensor nodes can launch repeated attacks on the aggregation process to prevent the base station from receiving correct aggregation results, leading to a special form of denial-of-service (DoS) attack. 

VMAT, a secure data aggregation scheme, was developed to deal with these security challenges. It relies on a secure MIN aggregation scheme and converts other additive aggregation functions such as SUM and COUNT to MIN aggregations. However, we present a novel enumeration attack against VMAT to highlight the security vulnerability of a sensor node reporting an arbitrary reading of its own. This enumeration attack enables a single compromised sensor node to significantly inflate the final aggregation result without being detected. To address this challenge, we also introduce an effective defense against the enumeration attack. Our theoretical analysis and simulation studies confirm the severe impact of the enumeration attack and the effectiveness of the countermeasure.

Encryption alone is not enough to protect data privacy, because access pattern leaks some sensitive information. Oblivious RAM (ORAM), the solution to this problem, is still far from practical deployment for heavy storage and communication/computation overhead. To reduce them, an insightful idea was proposed to utilize non-colluding clouds to shift client computation and client-cloud communication to the clouds. The proposed multi-cloud ORAM achieved O(1) client-cloud bandwidth cost and removed most of client computation. In this paper, we exploit “disconnected ORAMoperation” and design “two-layerencryption” to further reduce these overheads. Experiments show that our proposed scheme, NewMCOS, significantly reduces evict cache size from GB/MB to KB level with about 2-3 times lower response time and 20 percent savings in bandwidth for clouds, compared to other schemes. Theoretically speaking, we reduce evict cache size from O(√N) to O(ZK), where N is the number of real data blocks, K is the number of clouds (2 <; K <; <; √N ), and Z is the number of real blocks uploaded from the client for eviction. By employing “lazy eviction operation”, the write frequency is reduced by O(Z), the shuffling bandwidth cost is reduced by Ω(Z log Z). Meanwhile, NewMCOS is proved to be secure.

Software-defined networking (SDN) allows the smart grid to be centrally controlled and managed by decoupling the control plane from the data plane, but it also expands attack surface for attackers. Existing studies about the security of SDN-enabled smart grid (SDSG) mainly focused on static methods such as access control and identity authentication, which is vulnerable to attackers that carefully probe the system. As the attacks become more variable and complex, there is an urgent need for dynamic defense methods. In this paper, we propose a security function virtualization (SFV) based moving target defense of SDSG which makes the attack surface constantly changing. First, we design a dynamic defense mechanism by migrating virtual security function (VSF) instances as the traffic state changes. The centralized SDN controller is re-designed for global status monitoring and migration management. Moreover, we formalize the VSF instances migration problem as an integer nonlinear programming problem with multiple constraints and design a pre-migration algorithm to prevent VSF instances' resources from being exhausted. Simulation results indicate the feasibility of the proposed scheme.

This paper presents the development of an energy monitoring system that integrates IoT technology. The system utilizes a programmable logic controller (PLC) s7-1200 and a distributed power monitoring module connected through profinet interface. The PLC is an ideal solution for distributed power monitoring and is capable of IoT integration through its embedded webserver functionality. However, the PLC's data management and human to machine interface (HMI) capabilities are limited, and thus a single board computer (SBC) is utilized to enhance these functionalities, providing better database management and improved data visualization.

The paper discusses both the hardware and software aspects of the system, emphasizing the practical aspects of the design. The results obtained by the energy monitoring system are compared with those of a power quality analyzer, demonstrating the effectiveness of the IoT-integrated system.

Overall, this energy monitoring system provides an efficient and reliable solution for power monitoring and management, which integrates IoT technology for enhanced functionality. The use of the PLC and SBC together offers an optimal combination of robustness and flexibility, resulting in a system that can effectively manage power usage and quality.

Measurement of the electricity consumption of major appliances in different time segments is of crucial significance to demand-side management and energy conservation. Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) can infer the target appliances' power use information by only collecting and analyzing the aggregate power data at the single power entrance point. Inspired by the success of deep neural network in other fields, some researchers have applied it to NILM with promising results. However, existing studies require labeled real aggregate data to train the networks, while time-synchronized measurement of the target appliance for labeling is hard to achieve in practice. This paper proposes to train networks with only synthetic aggregate data. Furthermore, a training data generation method via background filtering is proposed, and the obtained training data is used to train the network for estimating electricity consumption. This generation method only needs unlabeled real aggregate data and the target appliance's operation curves, which reduces the difficulty of training data acquisition. The proposed estimation method achieves higher accuracy than current methods in tests on a public dataset which also demonstrates the effectiveness of background filtering.

With the widespread usage of smartphones, mobile applications or apps have become an integral part of our daily lives. Local apps, which are designed to provide real-world information, are beneficial not only for tourists but also for residents. While the Google Play Store has a "Travel & Local" category that houses local apps, many such apps can be found in other categories. To address this issue, we present a novel method to classify local apps based on app market data using deep neural network (DNN). 

Our approach leverages the manual labeling of each app by its developer to pre-train the DNN. Additionally, we extract features from app market data to account for the multi-modal nature of data such as app name, category, and number of installs. We evaluated our approach using a real-world dataset obtained from Google Play, and our findings show that the proposed method outperforms the baseline method by 5.5% regarding F1 score.

Structured light with spatially variant amplitude/phase/polarization has seen wide interesting applications ranging from manipulation to communications. In this invited talk, we will review recent advances in structured light communications accessing the space domain of lightwaves. Key devices, techniques and emerging applications will be introduced. Future challenges and perspectives of structured light communications will be also discussed.

Vector Matrix Multiplication (VMM) is a computationally-intensive operation that poses a challenge for digital hardware in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms. To overcome this challenge, crossbar arrays have been suggested as a viable method for achieving more efficient analog implementations. These arrays typically consist of circuits built using memristors or other custom designs, such as the Dot Product Engine and the Resistive Processing Units, both of which have been proposed as potential solutions. With either design, training time for VMM can be reduced to O(1) per layer, resulting in a significant increase in AI capabilities and a more feasible future for the technology.

Real-time battery state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is critical in many applications. The extended Kalman filter (EKF) has been successfully deployed in SOC estimation allowing real-time SOC monitoring. However, modeling inaccuracies, measurement faults, and wrong initialization can cause the estimation algorithm to diverge. The precise knowledge of statistical information about process and measurements noise is crucial for accurate system modeling and estimation. This paper presents a novel SOC estimation approach based on maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE). The process and measurements models are transformed to an error state propagation system where the innovation covariance is utilized to maximize the likelihood of the multivariate innovation distribution with respect to process and measurement covariances. The MLE formulation allows the estimation of the process and measurement noise covariance magnitudes, which are used to obtain an optimal SOC estimate. The proposed method is validated experimentally using a number of Li-ion battery cells under various testing conditions. The estimation performance is compared with that of the conventional EKF technique as well as previously published results based on autocovariance least-squares measurements noise estimation. The results indicate an enhanced performance for the new algorithm over the traditional EKF across all conducted tests.

Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) have experienced significant growth in recent years, due in large part to the availability and demand for small size sensors that can detect environmental conditions. These sensors are connected to tiny sensor nodes, which are used for communication of sensed data. WSNs typically consist of a large number of sink nodes and sensor nodes, and the multipath routing technique is crucial for ensuring reliable data transfer, reducing delay and congestion.

Multipath routing protocols play an important role in improving Quality of Service (QoS), load balancing and reliable communication in WSNs. This survey provides an introduction to multipath routing and explores the different classifications of geographic multipath routing protocols based on the routing information update mechanism, using either local or global heuristics knowledge. The protocols are compared in terms of various routing parameters for path maintenance, path discovery and traffic distribution, according to each class of geographic multipath routing protocol.

Antenatal classes are sometimes called parentcraft which help to prepare expectant mothers for their baby's birth, feeding the baby and to look after the baby. It is the best way to ensure expectant mothers stay healthy during pregnancy as well as to deliver confidence and information. This paper looks into the current state of antenatal education. It investigates the way antenatal classes are accessed by expectant mothers, the challenges they face in getting access to these classes and their attitudes towards these classes. For most women, it could be stressful and very inconvenient to attend physical antenatal classes. An online collaborative approach of interactive antenatal lecture for expectant mothers is proposed to replace these classes by providing live streaming lectures, discussion and interactive sessions between users. In order to accomplish this task, some face-to-face interviews were conducted. Questionnaires were also distributed. This paper adopted the Structured Systems Analysis and Design Method (SSADM) for the specification, development, and implementation. The web based system is implemented using PHP framework as Back-end, Front-End using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, XAMPP Server and MySQL was employed to handle the database structure. The web based system was implemented and tested using carefully thought out test cases which were successful. The proposed system offers antenatal education to expectant mothers no matter their location as well as a platform for discussion between expectant mothers, midwives, or anyone at all; sharing useful information amongst themselves and giving advice and encouragement to one another.

The growth of the first generation Internet of Things (IoT) systems for low-end devices with limited memory and infrastructure is being hindered by the lack of engineering support in terms of architecture, technology, hardware, privacy, security, and business. This paper explores the relevant system engineering issues in IoT processors and suggests that the use of rough set as an approximate computing technique could be the solution for the next generation IoT hardware. This proposed approach has the potential to address inconsistencies that arise in the layers of hardware infrastructure, particularly for IoT applications that rely heavily on cloud and fog processing. As a result, the authors propose a research direction that aims to establish IoT as an engineering discipline, with a focus on the impact of processor hardware extension.

This paper proposes a novel methodology in the area of threat intelligence by combining statistical analysis with Intrusion Detection System. The preferred threat intelligence model identifies potential malicious connections for a single node computer system utilising the IP addresses of the devices that are connected to the system. It can be inferred from the results that the proposed system performs better in terms of accuracy, True Positive Rate and False Positive Rate.

In IoT systems, WSNs and Gateways are exposed to many attacks. WSNs are usually exposed to different types of intrusions like node compromise and denial of service attacks. IoT gateways that connects WSN to the Internet are exposed to all conventional IP attacks. In this paper, we propose an anomaly detection approach using support vector machines (SVM) for WSN intrusion detection, and deep learning technique for gateway intrusion detection. We propose a detection protocol that dynamically executes the on-demand SVM classifier in a hierarchical way whenever an intrusion is suspected. We combine machine learning classification with a statistical approach for malicious node localization. This novel approach allows finding a compromise between intrusion detection efficiency and resource overhead for WSN and gateway security.

Data mining is the discovery of valuable and novel structures in datasets. Considering the number of people suffering from diet-related cardiometabolic increase, it brings into question the media's efforts in food and health communication. One of the main objectives in this study focuses on the emerging data mining methodology to understand the structure of what and how the news media discuss food, diet, and the related cardiometabolic diseases. A total of 6,625 items of coverage on food, flavor, and condiments along with cardiometabolic diseases is identified. Data mining algorithms concern food for predicting health outcomes and providing policy information. The most typical usage of a food data corpus is automatic conversion from text to health afflictions on larger cultural forces.

The use of high-performance software-defined networks (SDNs) for managing industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices is a rapidly growing trend. This next-generation technology not only provides automation, flexibility, and efficiency, but it also poses significant cybersecurity risks. One such risk is the vulnerability of SDNs to distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. In IIoT environments, attackers can send numerous requests to the SDN, causing it to interrupt services. Traditional defense systems have used honeypots for resisting DDoS attacks. However, attackers have developed new tactics to invalidate their protection. 

In this paper, we reveal a novel attack for identifying honeypots and analyze the optimal strategies of attackers to find the best time to attack. To combat these anti-honeypot attacks, we propose a pseudo-honeypot game (PHG) strategy that provides theoretical performance guarantees. We prove several groups of Bayesian-Nash Equilibrium in the PHG strategy, which can achieve optimal equilibrium between legitimate users and attackers. Our honeypot strategies can provide dynamic protection for SDNs, and malicious attacks can be effectively controlled. 

Finally, we evaluate our proposals on a testbed, and experimental results show that our proposals can effectively resist DDoS attacks with lower energy consumption compared to existing methods. Overall, our proposed PHG strategy provides a promising solution for protecting SDNs from anti-honeypot attacks in IIoT environments.

Multipath TCP (MP-TCP) has been introduced as an extension to legacy TCP to support simultaneous communication through multiple paths. Although MP-TCP has many advantages over TCP, some issues and challenges related to security robustness of this protocol remain unaddressed. The root cause of many threats specific to MP-TCP stem from the fact that user-specific credentials such as shared keys exchanged in the initial handshake are exposed. This allows an attacker to hijack an ongoing session by exploiting the authentication values of users. On the other hand, Software Defined Networking (SDN) has received much attention recently due to its many advantages, such as programmability and centralization. In this paper, a scheme for securing MP-TCP is proposed. This is achieved with the assistance of SDN, in which a new security module residing in the SDN controller acts as a third-party session-key distribution authority. After the retrieval of session keys, a lightweight information-hiding mechanism to secure the keys exchanged during the initial handshake is proposed.

The side-channel leakage is a consequence of program execution in a computer processor, and understanding relationship between code execution and information leakage is a necessary step in estimating information leakage and its capacity limits. This paper proposes a methodology to relate program execution to electromagnetic side-channel emanations and estimates side-channel information capacity created by execution of series of instructions (e.g., a function, a procedure, or a program) in a processor. To model dependence among program instructions in a code, we propose to use Markov source model, which includes the dependencies among sequence of instructions as well as dependencies among instructions as they pass through a pipeline of the processor. The emitted electromagnetic (EM) signals during instruction executions are natural choice for the inputs into the model. To obtain the channel inputs for the proposed model, we derive a mathematical relationship between the emanated instruction signal power (ESP) and total emanated signal power while running a program. Then, we derive the leakage capacity of EM side channels created by execution of series of instructions in a processor. Finally, we provide experimental results to demonstrate that leakages could be severe and that a dedicated attacker could obtain important information.

Research on the evaluation index of partitioning wireless network by jamming multiple targets, this paper analyzed the existing evaluation indexes, analysed the deficiencies of the existing indexes, and improved the network separation ratio as the evaluation index of the attack effect finally, which lay the foundation for targets selection in the process of jamming partition.

The problem of estimating rigid transformation, also known as absolute orientation, is common in the fields of robotics and computer vision. Current algorithms rely on matrix factorization techniques such as singular value decomposition or eigenvalue and eigenvector, which can be computationally expensive and unsuitable for low-end hardware when continuous absolute orientation computation is required. This paper proposes a closed-form least squares solution for the problem, focusing on three or more pairs of point vectors in 2D space. The algorithm also takes into account the scaling factor in the rigid transformation. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and numerical accuracy of the proposed method.

We present a study on the spatial modeling of polymetallic nodule parameters in the Clarion-Clipperton zone (CCZ) utilizing a semisupervised learning approach. Spatial models that incorporate factors affecting nodule formation or their proxy variables are vital for characterization of the CCZ nodule deposits and their economic potential. While some models based on neural networks exist in the literature, they have employed supervised learning and rely on hand-modeled features to incorporate the effect of topography, one of the key factors affecting nodule formation. 

In our study, we introduce an unsupervised learning approach leveraging auto-encoders or principal component analysis to efficiently capture the effect of local topography around a point being modeled in terms of a few features. We then employ these features for subsequent supervised learning-based nodule parameter modeling, making our approach semisupervised overall. Our results demonstrate that incorporating bathymetric information into these features leads to better modeling performance than using hand-modeled topographic features. 

Overall, our study presents a novel approach to spatial modeling of polymetallic nodule parameters in the CCZ. By applying unsupervised learning to efficiently capture the effect of local topography, we demonstrate improved performance compared to traditional supervised learning approaches. Our findings may have significant implications for understanding the economic potential of nodule deposits in the CCZ and elsewhere.

This paper presents a novel machine learning algorithm with an improved accuracy and a faster learning curve, for very large datasets. Previously, an algorithm using lr-partitions was designed to improve upon C4.5. However, this algorithm has a relatively high percentage of undefined combinations of attribute values in its final results, increasing the learning error. In this paper, a new type of clustering algorithm was proposed to generate output values for those undefined combinations, thus accelerating the learning curve and reducing the prediction error by several percentage points on various popular datasets from the UCI Machine Learning Database.

This chapter delves into various techniques used to estimate parameters and evaluate their accuracies. The two main types of parameter estimation - maximum likelihood (ML) and linear regression (LR) - are studied in detail, with an emphasis on their accuracy levels and their relationship to graphical analysis.

The Weibull, exponential, and normal distributions are used as examples to elaborate on the relationship between parameter estimation and graphical analysis, highlighting the general aspects of parameter estimation and the unique characteristics of estimators. The asymptotic behavior of estimated parameters and their moments is also explored in greater depth.

The chapter provides a comprehensive overview of the ML estimator for both the uncensored and censored cases, and further elaborates on the use of ranked plotting positions for LR estimation. The adjusted ranking method and the adjusted plotting position method are discussed as means for manipulating the ranked plotting positions.

Overall, this chapter provides a thorough exploration of parameter estimation techniques and their relationship to graphical analysis, emphasizing the importance of accurate parameter estimation in statistical analysis.

The frequency bands from 71-76 GHz and 81-86 GHz in the electromagnetic spectrum are highly appealing to communication system designers because of their wide bandwidth and sparse usage. The W/V-band Terrestrial Link Experiment (WTLE) was established in Albuquerque, NM, back in 2015 to study atmospheric propagation in these frequency bands. After two years of data collection, this paper presents a statistical analysis of the WTLE measurements and their comparison with seasonal variations. This study provides valuable information on W/V band propagation, which could be instrumental in designing future communication systems.

In the past two decades, there has been extensive research on automatic modulation classification (AMC) for single signals. However, the demand for multi-signal AMC is increasing, despite single-signal AMC's poor performance, and only a few methods have been proposed for multi-signal AMC. To address this issue, a new blind AMC technique for overlapped co-channel signals has been proposed, which applies capsule networks. Multiple transmitters are transmitting signals simultaneously, which are then received by a single-antenna receiver. This method processes signals at an intermediate frequency, and is capable of detecting the number of signals automatically. Our proposed method shows significant effectiveness in numerical results, with excellent generalization ability provided by the capsule network.

Analyzing the workload of a computing cluster can be done through a simulation of its operation using parallel workload models. Although we have developed several models, they all rely on the approximation of continuous random variables. In this paper, we present a simplified version of the approximation of a Hyper-gamma distribution through the method of moments, which reduces the number of parameters required.

To ensure the effectiveness of our approach, we validate our results by comparing the simulation of this approximation with the original workload from the log. Our proposed method demonstrates its characteristic features and justifies the need for selecting an appropriate approximation.

In conclusion, our work offers a simpler method for approximating the Hyper-gamma distribution and shows the importance of an appropriate approximation method when analyzing computing cluster workloads.

Speech synthesis, or text-to-speech (TTS), generates a speech waveform of the given text. To build a satisfactory TTS system, a large natural speech corpus is requested. In the traditional approach, the corpus should be accompanied with precise annotations. However, the annotation is difficult and costly. Recently, end-to-end speech synthesis methods are proposed, which eliminated the requirement of annotation. The end-to-end methods make the development of TTS system less costly and easier. We used the state-of-the-art end-to-end Tacotron model in the Mongolian TTS task. With much more unannotated speech data (about 17 hours), the new system beats the old best Mongolian TTS system, which is trained on a small amount of annotated data (about 5 hours), with a big margin. The new mean opinion score (MOS) is 3.65 vs 2.08 which is the old one. The proposed system becomes the first Mongolian TTS system can be utilized in real applications.

A cryptocurrency is a form of digital currency that employs cryptography to ensure the security of transactions, the control of the creation of new units, and the authentication of transfers. Cryptocurrencies, virtual currencies, and alternative currencies are all examples of this type of currency. Unlike traditional electronic money and central banking systems, cryptocurrencies rely on decentralized control. Each cryptocurrency's decentralized control is managed by a public transaction database known as a blockchain, which functions as a distributed ledger.

In the field of Neural Networks, there are numerous techniques for making predictions, including the prediction of future stock exchange indicator values. This paper aims to examine the use of Artificial Neural Network to predict the closing prices of cryptocurrencies and compare the difference in price changes with those of traditional stock exchanges.

Texture representation methods have traditionally focused on either pixel intensities or directionality, neglecting the importance of both factors simultaneously. To address this issue, we propose a new local descriptor called locally directional and extremal pattern (LDEP) for texture classification. LDEP combines directional local difference count pattern (DLDCP) and extremum information to effectively capture both directional and pixel intensity information of textures. Specifically, DLDCP is created by merging two patterns of DLDCP in odd and even positions, while extremum information is extracted by concatenating extremum location pattern (ELP), extremum difference pattern (EDP), and extremum compression pattern (ECP) from the sampling points, resulting in a neighbors extremum related local pattern (NERLP). Our experiments on various texture databases (Prague, Stex, UIUC, Kth-tips2-a, Brodatz, and CUReT) demonstrate that our proposed LDEP descriptor can achieve comparable classification rates with ten typical texture classification methods in different conditions, including rotation, illumination, scale variation, viewpoint variation, and noise.

This paper addresses the issue of bandwidth-constrained distributed estimation of a Gaussian vector with a linear observation model. Each sensor quantizes its observation using a multi-bit scalar quantizer and modulates it digitally before transmitting it over fading channels to a fusion center (FC) where the unknown vector is estimated. Three receiver types are considered: (i) coherent receiver; (ii) noncoherent receiver with known channel envelopes; and (iii) noncoherent receiver with known channel statistics only. The Bayesian Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) and the Weiss-Weinstein bound (WWB) are derived for each receiver type. Two optimization problems, namely maximizing the trace and log-determinant of Bayesian FIM under network transmit power constraint, are formulated and solved using FIM-max schemes. The trace of Bayesian FIM maximization problem can be implemented in a distributed fashion, whereas the log-determinant of Bayesian FIM maximization problem requires the FC to find the powers and inform the active sensors of their transmit powers. The FIM-max power allocation across sensors is numerically investigated, and system performance is evaluated in terms of mean square error (MSE) using FIM-max schemes compared to MSE-min scheme and uniform power allocation. The results illustrate that FIM-max schemes perform better than uniform power allocation, and the performance loss in terms of MSE of LMMSE estimator is not significant compared to the WWB. Furthermore, coherent receiver and noncoherent receiver with known channel statistics have the best and the worst performance, respectively.

This paper presents the development, implementation, and outcomes of an i-Semester program, which is part of the new educational model launched by Tecnologico de Monterrey to address the needs of the Mexican automotive industry. The i-Semester is an undergraduate program designed to foster disciplinary and transversal outcomes, as defined by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology, through real-life applications and industrial experiences.

The paper discusses how the i-Semester was applied to an automotive industry challenge, where students were involved in the design, analysis, and validation of components. It explains the work scheme, learning modules, and the development of the industrial challenge. The program was conducted in collaboration with Volkswagen de México, with 38 students of Automotive Design Engineering and Mechatronic Engineering immersed in 18-week periods during spring and fall 2017. Six teachers from the university and five engineers from the company served as mentors, giving feedback to solve a real-life industry problem.

The second part of the paper describes the implementation of evaluation tools in the i-Semester program. The paper concludes with comments on the implementation challenges, opportunities, advantages, and disadvantages of the new model compared to traditional education schemes.

Overall, the i-Semester program provides a valuable opportunity for students to gain practical experience and apply their knowledge to real-life industry problems. The collaboration between the university and industry partners facilitates the development of skills and competencies necessary for success in the automotive industry. While implementation challenges exist, the benefits and opportunities of this innovative education model outweigh the disadvantages.

Satellite scene images contain multiple sub-regions of different land use categories; however, traditional approaches usually classify them into a particular category only. In this paper, a new approach is proposed for automatically analyzing the semantic content of sub-regions of satellite images. At the core of the proposed approach is the recently introduced deep rule-based image classification method. The proposed approach includes a self-organizing set of transparent zero order fuzzy IF-THEN rules with human-interpretable prototypes identified from the training images and a pre-trained deep convolutional neural network as the feature descriptor. It requires a very short, nonparametric, highly parallelizable training process and can perform a highly accurate analysis on the semantic features of local areas of the image with the generated IF-THEN rules in a fully automatic way. Examples based on benchmark datasets demonstrate the validity and effectiveness of the proposed approach.

In order to improve the quality and visual effects of blurred images, we proposes an image deblurring algorithm based on dictionary learning. Firstly, we divides the blurred image into image block structure groups, then we recovers the image block through the K-SVD dictionary and the PCA dictionary, and finally the morphological operations is applied to the difference image to obtain restored image. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is better than others in peak structural similarity and visual effect.

In this work, we have developed a mathematical model of the convective drying process of natural products, showing the main phenomena observed during drying, that are heat and mass transfers. This phenomenon was examined by applying the pseudo bond graph methodology. Experimental drying tests were make on apple slices and a comparison between experimental and theoretical results was performed to validate the developed model. Also a sliding mode control applied to this drying process has been tested by simulations.

Fault tolerant control is an essential area of study for researchers and scholars, aiming to create resilient control systems. However, this subject has received limited attention when it comes to fractional systems in the presence of time delay. Hence, this paper proposes a novel approach to designing a tracking control system for a fractional order system with time delay. The primary objective of this approach is to attain the same performance as a time delay fractional reference model.

The controller parameters are computed under both nominal and faulty states, considering whether the system state is available or unavailable for measurement. Furthermore, the efficiency of the proposed approach is demonstrated through a numerical example. Overall, this paper contributes to the limited body of research on fault tolerant control for fractional systems with time delay.

Current efforts to understand how deep learning systems make decisions in medical tasks have primarily focused on visualizing the contributing factors. However, we argue that this approach is insufficient for "opening the black box" of these systems because it overlooks a crucial component in medical decision making - language. To address this, we propose a model-agnostic interpretability method that involves training a simple recurrent neural network to generate descriptive sentences that clarify the decision made by deep learning classifiers. Our approach was tested on the task of detecting hip fractures from frontal pelvic x-rays, requiring minimal additional labeling. The results indicate that our method produces sentences that consistently contain the relevant information, which was preferred by a cohort of doctors compared to current tools that produce saliency maps. We found that the combination of visualizations and generated text was more effective than either alone. Our approach represents a promising step towards making medical decision making more transparent and understandable.

Internet of Things (IoT) systems generate massive amounts of raw data in the form of log files. To extract valuable information from this raw data, it needs to be processed. Machine Learning (ML) algorithms have been effective in such tasks, but with a plethora of algorithms available, choosing the right one for different scenarios can be challenging. In this study, we have evaluated 22 up-to-date supervised ML classification algorithms on various IoT datasets to solve the anomaly detection problem. Our findings indicate that there is no single algorithm that dominates others, and numerous techniques perform equally well. Considering our results and dataset characterization, we recommend a framework that assists professionals in selecting a subset of the 22 ML algorithms that are most likely to deliver optimal performance on their data.

This paper discusses the challenge of practical Heterogeneous Wireless Charger Placement with Obstacles (HIPO) by deploying heterogeneous chargers on a 2D plane with obstacles. The goal is to maximize charging utility for distributed rechargeable devices while utilizing strategies consisting of charger positions and orientations. To achieve this, the paper proposes a piecewise constant function to approximate the nonlinear charging power and divides the area into multi-feasible geometric areas with constant charging power. The Practical Dominating Coverage Set extraction algorithm extracts a finite set of candidate strategies, limiting the solution space. Finally, the paper proves that the problem falls under the realm of maximizing a monotone submodular function subject to a partition matroid constraint, which allows a greedy algorithm to solve it with an approximation ratio of 1/2 - ε. The paper concludes by presenting experimental results that demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm, which outperforms comparison algorithms by at least 33.49 percent on average.

This Wireless Sensor Network is a network of devices that communicates the information gathered from a monitored field through wireless links. Small size sensor nodes constitute wireless sensor networks. A Sensor is a device that responds and detects some type of input from both the physical or environmental conditions, such as pressure, heat, light, etc. Applications of wireless sensor networks include home automation, street lighting, military, healthcare and industrial process monitoring. As wireless sensor networks are distributed across large geographical area, these are vulnerable to various security threats. This affects the performance of the wireless sensor networks. The impact of security issues will become more critical if the network is used for mission-critical applications like tactical battlefield. In real life deployment scenarios, the probability of failure of nodes is more. As a result of resource constraints in the sensor nodes, traditional methods which involve large overhead computation and communication are not feasible in WSNs. Hence, design and deployment of secured WSNs is a challenging task. Attacks on WSNs include attack on confidentiality, integrity and availability. There are various types of architectures that are used to deploy WSNs. Some of them are data centric, hierarchical, location based, mobility based etc. This work discusses the security issue of hierarchical architecture and proposes a solution. In hierarchical architectures, sensor nodes are grouped to form clusters. Intra-cluster communication happens through cluster heads. Cluster heads also facilitate inter-cluster communication with other cluster heads. Aggregation of data generated by sensor nodes is done by cluster heads. Aggregated data also get transferred to base through multi-hop approach in most cases. Cluster heads are vulnerable to various malicious attacks and this greatly affects the performance of the wireless sensor network. The proposed solution identifies attacked cluster head and changes the CH by identifying the fittest node using genetic algorithm based search.

In analyzing the epilepsy patient data it is necessary for a doctor to know where the epileptic focus are located. This information is related to the determination of the type of drug delivery and the therapeutic measures that will be performed for the epilepsy patient. In this research, a system that can visualize the state of the brains of epilepsy patients by performing an analysis of brain wave signals or electroencephalography (EEG) is built. Visualization is performed using topographic mapping techniques on each EEG signal sub-band, namely delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma sub-bands. The feature extraction process is conducted using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to transform signals from time domain into frequency domain. The absolute power and relative power data of EEG signals are used as input values in the visualization process. The results are compared to neurologist analysis and they indicate that this system can visualize the brain condition of epileptic patients to find out where the epileptogenic zone is located by adjusting data cutting process to the duration of the seizure wave that occurs.

People experience mental stress on a daily basis from a variety of different reasons, including environmental reasons (traffic, noise, or bad weather), social reasons (family issues, friends, and financial problems), or from events such as wedding planning or giving a presentation in front of large audience. A manageable amount of stress is healthy and can motivate a person; however, a large amount of continuous stress or a strong response to stress can be harmful. For this reason, the detection of mental stress, as well as its prediction, has become a significant area of research. In this paper, we review and summarize various approaches found in the literature for stress detection using machine learning and suggest directions for future research and interventions.

Simulated Kalman Filter (SKF) is a population-based optimizer introduced in 2015 that is based on Kalman filtering, which consists of prediction, measurement, and estimation processes. The original SKF algorithm employs synchronous update mechanism in which the agents in SKF update their solutions after all fitness calculations, prediction process, and measurement process are completed. An alternative to synchronous update is asynchronous update. In asynchronous update, only one agent does fitness calculation, prediction, measurement, and estimation processes at one time. In this study, synchronous and asynchronous mechanisms are combined in SKF. At first, the SKF starts with synchronous update. If no improved solution is found, the SKF changes its update mechanism. Using the CEC2014 benchmark test suite, experimental results indicate that the proposed adaptive switching synchronous-asynchronous SKF outperforms the original SKF significantly.

The traditional machine learning-based methods for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of rolling bearings lack the ability to provide adequate feature representation and adaptive extraction. Even the deep learning-based RUL prediction methods fail to produce satisfactory predictive results due to insufficient degradation data and inconsistency in data distribution across bearings. To address these issues, this paper proposes a new RUL prediction method that incorporates deep feature representation and transfer learning. 

The proposed method consists of an off-line stage and an online stage. In the off-line phase, the Hilbert-Huang transform marginal spectra of the raw vibration signal of auxiliary bearings are computed, and then the contractive denoising autoencoder extracts deep features with stable and fault-tolerant representations. These deep features are then used to divide the life of each bearing into a normal and a fast-degradation state using Pearson's correlation coefficient. Lastly, deep features and their RUL values are utilized to train an RUL prediction model for the fast-degradation state using least-square support vector machines.

In the online phase, a transfer learning algorithm, transfer component analysis, sequentially adjusts the features of the target bearing, and then the RUL is predicted using the corrected features. The results of this method show a significant performance improvement over the PHM Challenging 2012 data set in terms of predictive accuracy and numerical stability. Therefore, this method addresses the challenges involved in RUL prediction of rolling bearings, and it can provide more reliable estimates of RUL, which is crucial for equipment maintenance and management.

This paper presents a precision agriculture system for monitoring leaf temperature using RFID-based wireless transponders. The transponders are powered by flexible commercial solar cells and feature an integrated temperature sensor based on the EM4325 chip by EM Microelectronic. The PLA substrate antenna is manufactured using adhesive copper tape technology and is compact enough to be applied directly to leaves. Results from field tests demonstrate that the system is successful in monitoring leaf temperature and can be used to analyze the leaf-to-air temperature differential to check for water stress in crops. Overall, this system shows great potential for improving precision agriculture practices.

Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a rapidly evolving field with its own unique set of challenges. While designing a natural language system that can react and adapt to every situation is an incredibly daunting task, we can still create a system that responds seamlessly to specific instructions and scenarios. 

To address this issue, we propose a three-fold contribution. Firstly, we aim to design a set of instruction types that allow for the inclusion of conditional statements within natural language instructions. Secondly, we propose the creation of a modular system, built using Robot Operating System (ROS), that will facilitate more robust communication and integration. Finally, we aim to establish an effective interconnection between written text and derived instructions, thereby making sentence construction more natural and intuitive for the user. 

Our system has been designed to run on diverse sentence structures, allowing for the generation of robust and grammatically correct paragraphs. However, we acknowledge that finding the right balance between user-friendliness and accuracy is crucial. As such, we have taken great care to ensure that our system is easily adaptable to the exact parameters that the user requires. 

Ultimately, by addressing the aforementioned challenges, our system will provide an effective and accessible method of Natural Language Processing, enabling users to interact with technology in a more intuitive and natural way.

One of the popular measures of central tendency that provides better representation and interesting insights of the data compared to the other measures like mean and median is the metric mode. If the analytical form of the density function is known, mode is an argument of the maximum value of the density function and one can apply optimization techniques to find the mode. In many of the practical applications, the analytical form of the density is not known and only the samples from the distribution are available. Most of the techniques proposed in the literature for estimating the mode from the samples assume that all the samples are available beforehand. Moreover, some of the techniques employ computationally expensive operations like sorting. In this letter, we provide a computationally effective, online iterative algorithm that estimates the mode of a unimodal smooth density given only the samples generated from the density. Asymptotic convergence of the proposed algorithm using an ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based analysis is provided. We also prove the stability of estimates by utilizing the concept of regularization. Experimental results further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

The usage of multi-spectral improved vision systems is essential in achieving high-quality images. In order to enhance the image contrast, different algorithms have been tested. However, it has been noted that some of these algorithms create artifacts in areas with sharp brightness changes. In this regard, a new approach has been proposed to reduce such artifacts.

To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a full-reference quality assessment of contrast enhancement algorithms has been conducted. A multispectral image dataset has been created for this purpose. The results of objective and subjective multispectral image fusion quality assessments, as well as one subjective assessment, have been obtained. Furthermore, the correlation coefficients between subjective and objective assessments have been calculated.

The analysis has shown that the Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient between objective and specified subjective image fusion quality assessments is not less than 0.54. Therefore, it can be concluded that the proposed method is effective in improving contrast without creating artifacts in areas with sharp brightness changes. This study highlights the importance of using multi-spectral improved vision systems and emphasizes the need to develop effective image enhancement algorithms.

Effective storage, processing and analyzing of power device condition monitoring data faces enormous challenges. A framework is proposed that can support both MapReduce and Graph for massive monitoring data analysis at the same time based on Aliyun DTplus platform. First, power device condition monitoring data storage based on MaxCompute table and parallel permutation entropy feature extraction based on MaxCompute MapReduce are designed and implemented on DTplus platform. Then, Graph based k-means algorithm is implemented and used for massive condition monitoring data clustering analysis. Finally, performance tests are performed to compare the execution time between serial program and parallel program. Performance is analyzed from CPU cores consumption, memory utilization and parallel granularity. Experimental results show that the designed framework and parallel algorithms can efficiently process massive power device condition monitoring data.

This paper introduces a framework for how to appropriately adopt and adjust machine learning (ML) techniques used to construct electrocardiogram (ECG)-based biometric authentication schemes. The proposed framework can help investigators and developers on ECG-based biometric authentication mechanisms define the boundaries of required datasets and get training data with good quality. To determine the boundaries of datasets, use case analysis is adopted. Based on various application scenarios on ECG-based authentication, three distinct use cases (or authentication categories) are developed. With more qualified training data given to corresponding machine learning schemes, the precision on ML-based ECG biometric authentication mechanisms are increased in consequence. The ECG time slicing technique with the R-peak anchoring is utilized in this framework to acquire ML training data with good quality. In the proposed framework four new measure metrics are introduced to evaluate the quality of the ML training and testing data. In addition, a Matlab toolbox, containing all proposed mechanisms, metrics, and sample data with demonstrations using various ML techniques, is developed and made publicly available for further investigation. For developing ML-based ECG biometric authentication, the proposed framework can guide researchers to prepare the proper ML setups and the ML training datasets along with three identified user case scenarios. For researchers adopting ML techniques to design new schemes in other research domains, the proposed framework is still useful for generating the ML-based training and testing datasets with good quality and utilizing new measure metrics.

A wireless sensor system has been designed to evaluate seismic damage in constructions. This sensor system uses capacitive micro electro mechanical strain sensors and 3D acceleration sensors which operate on a low power state. Additionally, this system is equipped with specifically designed microcircuits to extend the battery life up to 12 years. The strain sensors are located at the base of the structure and measure the plastic deformation in the core regions of the construction during an earthquake. They can be set to function periodically or on demand from the base station. The accelerometers are installed on each floor of the building and measure the dynamic response of the building during an earthquake.

With the expansion of the data size, data mining techniques are gaining more and more importance. Data mining consists of methods such as classification, clustering, time series estimation and association rule. In this study, a time series analysis is carried out in order to make an estimation for the future in accordance with the structure of the data set. Time series are series in which the variables are recorded in chronological order. The data set was created by recording the gas concentrations in the air at a time interval. These data are used to estimate the changes in air quality. Three types of time series analysis training algorithm are used in the study. The results given by the algorithms are close to each other and high performance has been determined. As a result of experimental studies, it is observed that time series analysis is sufficient to estimate air quality.

Despite significant advances in the remote sensing of fluid flows, light detection and ranging (LIDAR) measurement equipment still presents the problems of having only radial (line-of-sight) wind speed measurements (Cyclops' dilemma). Substantial expanses of unmeasured flow still remain and range weighting errors have a considerable influence on LIDAR measurements. Clearly, more information needs to be extracted from LIDAR data. With this motivation in mind, this brief shows that it is possible to estimate the wind velocity, wind direction, and absolute pressure over the entire spatial region of interest. A key challenge is that most established estimation techniques cater for systems that are finite-dimensional and described by ordinary differential equations (ODEs). By contrast, many fluid flows are governed by the Navier-Stokes equations, which are partial differential-algebraic equations (PDAEs). We show how a basis function decomposition method in conjunction with a pressure Poisson equation (PPE) formulation yields a spatially continuous, strangeness-free, reduced-order dynamic model for which a modified DAE form of the unscented Kalman filter (UKF) algorithm is used to estimate unmeasured velocities and pressure using sparse measurements from wind turbine-mounted LIDAR instruments. The approach is validated for both synthetic data generated from large eddy simulations of the atmospheric boundary layer and real-world LIDAR measurement data. Results show that a reconstruction of the flow field is achievable, thus presenting a validated estimation framework for potential applications including wind gust prediction systems and the preview control of wind turbines.

A recent development in robotic control systems is the use of classification neural networks to produce discrete control signals. While the output of the neural network can be mapped directly to control signals, the possible control decisions are generally limited to the number of output classes. Fortunately, the neural network is also capable of producing a set of probabilities that a given input belongs to each class. This additional information can be used to expand the range of possible control signals. In this experiment, a fuzzy control system was applied to a robot that previously implemented a navigation-by-classification approach. The results of the experiment showed that the network is indeed capable of providing extra information in its probability designations, and this information can be exploited to smooth the discrete outputs of the system using fuzzy logic. In the case of the robot studied, the fuzzy control system outperformed the original discrete control system in navigating new courses. The robot's movements also appeared smoother when compared to the original solution. Thus, the additional information gained from the probabilities enabled the system to be more generalized and robust.

Sensors are essential in powertrain engineering and exhaust aftertreatment systems due to the increasing need for high performance and fewer emissions. Mostly in diesel oxidation catalysts, the upstream and downstream temperature sensors are attached to the vehicle until their models get calibrated then removed in the end-user version. The modeling process is both extravagant and time-consuming as it requires engine and chassis dynamometers. In fact, these temperature models are used in the monitoring of CO emission level and as inputs to calculate the other exhaust aftertreatment system components' efficiencies. The purpose of this paper is to investigate the use of long short-term memory networks in the automotive sector by generating a model for the diesel oxidation catalyst upstream and downstream temperatures as an example. Measurements from engine sensors and actuators position feedback were recorded from a vehicle and used as training and validation data. After sufficient training, the model was utilized to evaluate and predict the modeled oxidation catalyst upstream and downstream temperatures.

In this paper, we introduce an effective method for segmenting subcortical structures from magnetic resonance images (MRIs). Our proposed method is a multi-atlas guided 3D fully convolutional network (FCN) that utilizes both label information and image intensity information in a patch-based manner. We also employ a long skip connection strategy to embed convolutional layer outputs into deconvolutional layers, allowing the network to learn both local and global contexts and ensuring consistency between extracted features at different scales. To further enhance segmentation accuracy and reduce training time, we employ a region limited sampling method.

We validated our method on a dataset consisting of 16 T1-weighted MRIs and compared its performance to several existing state-of-the-art subcortical structure segmentation methods. Our proposed method outperformed both a multi-atlas joint label fusion method and a representative 3D FCN method for the majority of the subcortical structures tested. Overall, our method shows promising results for enhancing subcortical structure segmentation from MRIs.

This paper presents an efficient method for detecting image objects in a disaster prevention network that utilizes information-centric networking (ICN). ICN for disaster prevention involves a large number of surveillance cameras that capture disaster image contents, which are distributed directly to the user's node based on their request. However, these requests do not always correspond to the names of the images captured by the surveillance camera, which can result in a low hit ratio between users and cameras.

To address this issue, we propose using natural language processing (NLP) to process and name the content requested by the user and artificial intelligence technology for naming the image content from the surveillance camera. This approach enables us to establish an efficient method for improving the hit ratio between users and cameras.

Moreover, we leverage the information on the areas that often experience disasters to decrease the volume of interest packets. This results in an improvement in the network efficiency of ICN for disaster prevention.

Overall, our proposed method provides an efficient approach for image object detection in an ICN-based disaster prevention network.

Multiple microphones organized in an array can achieve substantial noise reduction and speech enhancement. However, when the microphone spacings are quite close, it can be quite limited. In such cases, introducing one or more external microphones (XMs) into the same physical space as the local microphone array (LMA) can resolve the degradation. In this paper, three methods of extending an LMA-based generalized sidelobe canceller (GSC-LMA) with multiple XMs are proposed, treating the relative transfer function pertaining to the LMA as a priori knowledge. 

Two methods involve a procedure for completing an extended blocking matrix, whereas the third uses the speech estimate from the GSC-LMA directly with an orthogonalized version of the XM signals to obtain an improved speech estimate via a rank-1 generalized eigenvalue decomposition. All three methods were evaluated with recorded data from an office room, and it was found that the third method offered the most improvement. Using this method, the speech estimate from the GSC-LMA was not compromised and would be available to the listener if so desired, along with the improved speech estimate that uses both the LMA and XMs.

This paper proposes a cross-realm authentication scheme based on federated identity, which is aimed at addressing the issue of allowing Windows domain users to access cloud computing resources. The scheme is founded on the concept of declaration, utilizing a federated identity provider to replace the traditional gateway-based cross-realm authentication model. This results in users being able to access the cloud resources without having to re-authenticate. The SAML protocol is employed to exchange user identity information between different domains, thus ensuring the versatility and security of the system, and enabling secure communication between different security domains. Additionally, this paper presents the design of the key components of the three modules: claim provider, federated identity provider, and application service provider. Finally, the feasibility of the scheme is verified by testing it with the popular cloud platform OpenStack.

Narrowband Internet-of-Things (NB-IoT) applications can be deployed in licensed and unlicensed bands. Spectrum allocation for Narrowband IoT is often in-between licensed spectrum or available white space frequency bands and the designer is expected to meet stringent spectral mask requirements. Further, Narrowband IoT applications have range requirements in the order of few kilometers to tens of kilometers, which necessitates the use of high power amplifiers. This introduces significant non-linearity for systems which employ multiple access techniques like orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA). This effects the quality of the transmitted signal as well as introduces undesired adjacent channel emissions. In this paper, we describe a design approach for implementing a digital pre-distorter (DPD) for Narrowband IoT applications. We use a memory polynomial DPD model to trade-off performance and implementation complexity. By careful tuning of the parameters of the model, we demonstrate the system meeting the expected spectral mask and transmission quality requirements.

In contrast to the host-centric model where the communication is directed using the destination address, Information-Centric Networking (ICN) adopts the content name as the pillar network element to provide data discovery and delivery process, as well as in other network functionalities. Named Data Networking (NDN) is an active ICN project that uses hierarchical unbounded names. These names are used in both interest and data packets and other data structures that may consume more memory with long lookup time. This paper targets the naming aspect in vehicular named data networks and proposes a Name-to-Hash Encoding scheme. The idea consists of hashing each name components separately to a fixed length, then perform a heuristic Wu-Manber-like algorithm lookup process. The former process enhances the NDN to consume less memory compared to hierarchical names, the latter process provides a fast lookup time. We have evaluated the proposed scheme against different related solutions using real domain datasets. Both theoretical analysis and experiments prove that the proposed scheme is efficient in terms of complexity, memory consumption, and lookup time.

Cognitive radio technology is proposed as a means to achieve real-time spectrum situational awareness (SSA) and signals intelligence (SIGNIT) over a wide spectrum range by designing a cognitive engine that performs machine-learning based hierarchical RF signal identification. This allows the radio to classify and associate a signal using as fewer a number of features as possible. The classification algorithms can be based on any suitably chosen machine-learning algorithm such as artificial neural networks (ANNs) or deep learning. The proposed design allows the user to define, and modify, the SSA parameters during field operations. The specific example design proposed in this paper allows these definitions to be based on two levels of signal classification: a broad type of signals such as communications or radar and specific signals within each of these classes. It is shown that not only the proposed cognitive engine design allows realizing a large number of SSA definitions using permutations of the same two stage classifiers, but also the hierarchical approach may outperform dedicated classifiers with similar computational complexity. The design can easily be generalized to handle more than two levels of signal classification.

This article presents the monitoring of water quality by means of wireless sensor technology that is powered by solar energy. The different constituents of water example pH level, turbidity, water level are measured by means of sensors that are powered by solar energy. The information from the sensors are gathered and afterward sent to the cloud server by means of WiFi module. The collected data is further analyzed, shown in visual format in LCD and graphical comprehension is demonstrated via ThingSpeak. In the remote areas, the quality of water is displayed in LCDS. If after analyzing the properties the water quality appears to be negative, necessary steps can be taken.

Remote sensing image super-resolution (SR) refers to a technique improving the spatial resolution, which in turn benefits to the subsequent image interpretation, e.g., target recognition, classification, and change detection. In popular sparse representation-based methods, due to the complex imaging conditions and unknown degradation process, the sparse coefficients of low-resolution (LR) observed images are hardly consistent with the real high-resolution (HR) counterparts, which leads to unsatisfactory SR results. To address this problem, a novel coupled sparse autoencoder (CSAE) is proposed in this paper to effectively learn the mapping relation between the LR and HR images. Specifically, the LR and HR images are first represented by a set of sparse coefficients, and then, a CSAE is established to learn the mapping relation between them. Since the proposed method leverages the feature representation ability of both sparse decomposition and CSAE, the mapping relation between the LR and HR images can be accurately obtained. Experimentally, the proposed method is compared with several state-of-the-art image SR methods on three real-world remote sensing image datasets with different spatial resolutions. The extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method has gained solid improvements in terms of average peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity measurement on all of the three datasets. Moreover, results also show that with larger upscaling factors, the proposed method achieves more prominent performance than the other competitive methods.

A modification of the confidence screening mechanism based on adaptive weighing of every training instance at each cascade level of the Deep Forest is proposed. The modification aims to increase the classification accuracy. It is carried out by assigning weights to training instances at each forest cascade level in accordance with their classification accuracy. Larger values of accuracy produce smaller weights. Two strategies for using the weights are considered. The first one when the weights are regarded as probabilities of choosing the corresponding instances in building decision trees. According to the second strategy, the weights are used in splitting rules. The modification increases the classification accuracy and may reduce the training time for many real datasets. Numerical experiments illustrate good performance of the proposed modification in comparison with the original Deep Forest proposed by Zhou and Feng.

An Internet of Vehicles (IoV) is a network that enables vehicles on roads to form a self-organized network and share information with each other. However, since the data are transmitted over an insecure network, it is crucial to implement an authentication mechanism to protect the privacy of vehicle users. Recently, Ying et al. proposed an authentication protocol for IoV, claiming that the protocol could prevent multiple attacks. 

Unfortunately, after further analysis, we found that their protocol was vulnerable to offline identity guessing attacks, location spoofing attacks, and replay attacks, and required an excessive amount of time for authentication. To address these shortcomings, we have developed a new and improved authentication protocol. We have also provided a formal proof to demonstrate that our protocol is genuinely secure. 

Our proposed protocol outperforms previous methods in both security and performance. We are confident that our improved protocol will create a more secure and reliable IoV network for vehicle users.

The number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has been rapidly increasing, giving rise to the need for new network architecture design. As IoT devices generate a significant amount of traffic that can be highly variable depending on the device type and usage time, maintaining Quality of Service (QoS) standards presents a challenge. To achieve this, it is crucial to model and understand these traffic patterns in order to adapt the architecture dynamically. Therefore, we propose a Smart Testing Framework that can detect bottlenecks and accurately predict the demand for computing resources in a dynamic IoT network. Our framework enables us to maintain a desired level of QoS, as evidenced by the promising results we have obtained.

Commensal rats and mice are a significant pest problem that requires frequent manual checking of rodenticide levels in bait stations and searching for activity evidence. To address this issue, we propose a low-power remote monitoring system that wirelessly transmits data on bait and battery conditions with a battery life of over 12 months. 

Initial testing of our system under laboratory and field conditions has shown its potential in detecting and communicating rodenticide depletion. This innovative approach offers a significant advantage in the commercial-scale control of rodent infestations.

Wireless visual sensor networks (WVSNs) are used extensively in areas where visual data needs to be collected and transmitted wirelessly. Due to their limited processing and transmission capabilities, energy conservation remains a critical concern in WVSNs. In-network data fusion is an effective scheme for reducing energy consumption in WVSNs.
