The majority of the previous methods have formulated the separation problem through the time–frequency representation of the mixed signal, which has several drawbacks, including the decoupling of the phase and magnitude of the signal, the suboptimality of time–frequency representation for speech separation, and the long latency in calculating the spectrograms. To address these shortcomings, we propose a fully convolutional time-domain audio separation network (Conv-TasNet), a deep learning framework for end-to-end time-domain speech separation. Conv-TasNet uses a linear encoder to generate a representation of the speech waveform optimized for separating individual speakers. Speaker separation is achieved by applying a set of weighting functions (masks) to the encoder output. The modified encoder representations are then inverted back to the waveforms using a linear decoder. The masks are found using a temporal convolutional network consisting of stacked one-dimensional dilated convolutional blocks, which allows the network to model the long-term dependencies of the speech signal while maintaining a small model size. The proposed Conv-TasNet system significantly outperforms previous time–frequency masking methods in separating two- and three-speaker mixtures. Additionally, Conv-TasNet surpasses several ideal time–frequency magnitude masks in two-speaker speech separation as evaluated by both objective distortion measures and subjective quality assessment by human listeners. Finally, Conv-TasNet has a significantly smaller model size and a shorter minimum latency, making it a suitable solution for both offline and real-time speech separation applications. This study, therefore, represents a major step toward the realization of speech separation systems for real-world speech processing technologies.

Mobile edge and vehicle-based depth sending and real-time point cloud communication is an essential subtask enabling autonomous driving. In this paper, we propose a framework for point cloud multicast in VANETs using vehicle to infrastructure (V2I) communication. We employ a scalable Binary Tree embedded Quad Tree (BTQT) point cloud source encoder with bitrate elasticity to match with an adaptive random network coding (ARNC) to multicast different layers to the vehicles. The scalability of our BTQT encoded point cloud provides a trade-off in the received voxel size/quality vs channel condition whereas the ARNC helps maximize the throughput under a hard delay constraint. The solution is tested with the outdoor 3D point cloud dataset from MERL for autonomous driving. The users with good channel conditions receive a near lossless point cloud whereas users with bad channel conditions are still able to receive at least the base layer point cloud.

Flatfoot is a prevalent condition in children and adolescents, and failing to control and treat it in time may lead to persistent discomfort and inconvenience in adulthood. While medical equipment and doctors can diagnose the disease, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising diagnostic tool. In this study, we propose a modified weights-and-structure-determination neural network (MWASDNN) to classify foot data and diagnosis flatfoot. The MWASDNN is a simple neural network with input weights determined using the pseudo-inverse method, and the output weights randomly generated within a specified range. The number of hidden-layer neurons is determined using an incremental approach. We introduce the stratified cross-validation method to choose the model structure that best suits the data set features, thus improving MWASDNN's generalization performance and robustness. We use the MWASDNN models to classify foot data and achieve an accuracy of 84.31% and 85.29% for the left and right feet, respectively. Furthermore, the MWASDNN achieves higher classification accuracy than traditional neural networks, pattern classification methods, and two improved neural networks, indicating its potential as a practical diagnostic tool for flatfoot.

Wireless sensor networks are becoming very popular nowadays. Sensors in such networks are used to gather data periodically about a given zone area and send the collected data to the sink. However, such networks face several challenges especially the limited energy source and the data management. Hence, data sampling approach is becoming one of the essential techniques that saves he sensor energies and extend the network lifetime. Adaptive algorithms are created to allow each sensor to adapt its sampling rate to the application under surveillance, which leads to reduced data collection thus, reducing energy consumption. In this paper, we propose a new adaptive sampling technique that is dedicated to periodic sensor network applications. Our technique consists of two stages: aggregation and adapting stages. The first stage is applied at sensor level and aims to reduce the amount of data collected by the sensor. The second stage is applied at an intermediate level node called cluster-head (CH). The CH receives data periodically from the sensors and computes the new sampling rate for each sensor based on the spatio-temporal correlation between the sensors. Our technique is evaluated based on real sensor data collected in the Intel lab. The obtained results show the effectiveness of our technique in terms reducing the energy consumption while ensuring a high level of data accuracy and coverage network.

Equivalent circuit network simulation is widely used in modeling solar cells in three dimensions. However, the computational time and numerical instability increases dramatically when the number of circuit element increases. This problem is exacerbated by increasing the number of junctions in the solar cells. We propose a downsampling algorithm to reduce the time complexity but retain reasonable accuracy within the appropriate parameter space of multi-junction solar cells. We also publish a full-featured software that implements this algorithm and the full circuit network simulation along with this paper.

Rapid improvements in machine learning over the past decade are beginning to have far-reaching effects. For communications, engineers with limited domain expertise can now use off-the-shelf learning packages to design high-performance systems based on simulations. Prior to the current revolution in machine learning, the majority of communication engineers were quite aware that system parameters (such as filter coefficients) could be learned using stochastic gradient descent. It was not at all clear, however, that more complicated parts of the system architecture could be learned as well. In this paper, we discuss the application of machine-learning techniques to two communications problems and focus on what can be learned from the resulting systems. We were pleasantly surprised that the observed gains in one example have a simple explanation that only became clear in hindsight. In essence, deep learning discovered a simple and effective strategy that had not been considered earlier.

In order to solve the problem that the teacher cannot monitor students e-learning status and evaluate the students e-learning effect during MOOC teaching, in this paper, we capture the student learning images by computer camera and adopt the "Three Angles Synthesis" to judge whether the student is watching the teaching video online. First locate the center of the iris by the Average Feature Point method to calculate iris deflection angle and the distance from the iris center to the eye center; and detect the face key feature points(eye, nose, mouth, etc.) by calling face key point detector in Dlib to determine the face rotation angel; then extract the student target body by Maximum Connected Domain Moment Characteristic method to calculate the student body tilt angle; last determine whether the three angles meet the giving conditions, further judge the student is watching the teaching video online or not.

In smart mariculture, the automatic and accurate prediction of key water quality parameters is a significant and challenging issue. This paper focuses on predicting pH and water temperature parameters using an improved preprocessing method, Pearson correlation coefficient analysis, and the Simple Recurrent Unit (SRU) deep learning model. The prediction model achieved a high accuracy rate of 98.91% with an average prediction time of 11.3ms per data, outperforming the method based on Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) when the time complexity is similar. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed prediction method in smart mariculture for accurate water quality monitoring.

In hospital, most stroke patients' rehabilitation training is assisted by rehabilitation physicians. However, this rehabilitation way is expensive and the number of physician cannot meet the demand. Therefore, surface electromyography (sEMG) and machine learning algorithms are introduced into the rehabilitation system, which can reduce the work of physicians and meet the needs of patients. We collect the sEMG signals of patients by picture guidance. Due to the mislabeling caused by the time mismatch, we re-calibrated the labels by means of peak detection. A model fusion algorithm, called stacking, is leveraged to improve the accuracy and robustness of hand action recognition. Before training, we will assess the patient's condition. Different rehabilitation training strategies will be adopted to patients under different conditions so as to each patient can receive effective training. According to rehabilitation psychology, virtual reality games were introduced to enhance the interest and pleasure of patients in the training process. At the same time, it can stimulate the development of nerve in the motor system and enhance the activity of the motor cortex in the cerebral cortex.

Recently, there has been significant research interest in WiFi fingerprint-based localization due to the widespread deployment of WiFi devices. However, the accuracy of indoor positioning based on a single fingerprint pattern is limited due to external influences. To address this, a multi-fingerprint and multi-classifier fusion (MFMCF) localization method is proposed in this paper, which improves accuracy by constructing multiple fingerprint patterns and integrating multiple classifiers.

MFMCF constructs a composite fingerprint set (CFS) using linear discriminant analysis (LDA), which includes signal strength difference (SSD), hyperbolic location fingerprint (HLF), and received signal strength (RSS). To obtain a more accurate estimate result, a special decision-structure of multiple classification is designed by calculating the entropy of the classifiers including K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF).

Experimental results show that MFMCF outperforms single fingerprinting patterns in terms of localization accuracy and robustness.

In this paper, we aim to solve the issue of self-triggered control of nonlinear systems in the presence of actuator delays. Our proposed approach leverages the Lipschitz properties of the system dynamics to develop a self-triggered strategy. Specifically, for globally asymptotically stabilizable systems, our strategy ensures the stability of the sampled closed-loop system even when faced with bounded actuator delays.

The article delves into the challenges faced in training specialists in the field of radio physics and electronics at Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University, and explores the experience gained in the context of higher education reform in Russia. 

To address some of the challenges faced, the article suggests the adoption of wider distance learning and Internet utilization. Another strategy involves motivating students to engage in scientific work as a way of encouraging their learning. The article also proposes the organization of specialized Olympiads as a means of generating interest in the field of study. 

However, one challenge noted in the article is the difficulty in balancing a flexible learning path with the necessity to master a fixed set of competencies. This presents a significant hurdle in developing effective learning models for trainees in this field. 

In conclusion, the article highlights some of the critical issues faced in training specialists in the field of radio physics and electronics at Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University. While solutions such as distance learning and scientific work have been adopted, overcoming the difficulties of a flexible learning path and fixed competencies remain crucial for success.

The double parallel cloud computing framework based on GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) and MapReduce is proposed, which aims at the low efficiency for the large data sets on the stand-alone by text classification algorithm, constructs the adaptive computation process of double parallel computing and combines the advantage of improved TFIDF (term frequency-inverse document frequency) algorithm, and improves TFIDF text categorization algorithm with double parallel adaptive computing. In different operating environments, the efficiency of improved TFIDF algorithm will be compared with different computing nodes. The result shows that massive data can be processed effectively in high speed by improved TFIDF algorithm which adopts double parallel adaptive computing. With the number of nodes increasing, the algorithm execution efficiency with double parallel adaptive computing is getting more and more effective.

This paper provides an overview of the Resource Space Model (RSM), which is a high-level semantic space model used for organizing and managing various resources. RSM is characterized by its multi-dimensional, classification-based and content-based approach to abstraction and specialization. Compared to traditional resource management models, RSM has more powerful representation capabilities. Applications of the RSM model are not only limited to resource management and retrieval, but can also be extended to other areas such as automatic text summarization and question answering systems.

The focus on Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) research is increasing day by day, due to the increasing requirement of intelligent input devices. Hand Gesture Recognition is a small sub-field but presents a significant number of applications and consumer products. Most researches target on the feasibility of recognition systems but give less weight to the device resources, so the cost and time. The time-consuming complicated algorithms' use is limited to special purpose devices such as expensive gaming consoles. The use of such systems in low cost embedded hardware in realtime circumstances is required, with the comfortability to use it. In this paper, we design an efficient real-time keyboard-like HCI using Static HGR. We have proposed and implemented new methods to reduce the time consumption while maintaining the high accuracy of 90% with scale and rotation invariance. Also, to maintain the comfort of use, we have eliminated complicated gestures and used only 11 gestures as input gesture set.

Lifelong learning is the newly introduced approach to machine learning. It follows the true essence of developing learning based intelligent agents. The idea is to build models that can learn with experience in order to become more knowledgeable, following a continuous learning mechanism. It has similarities with other approaches including online learning, transfer learning, reinforcement learning and cumulative learning but has maintained its differences. Lifelong topic modeling refers to the use of lifelong learning approach with topic modeling. The objective is to develop topic models that incorporate past knowledge to generate topics that easily represent the underlying concepts discussed in the dataset. The past knowledge is in the form of a collective sense that helps to give meaningful topics even to domains that have limited or noisy sample data. This review paper puts emphasis on the effectiveness of lifelong learning approach in comparison to the traditional machine learning approaches. It discusses the strengths of lifelong learning and the progress that it has made with topic models as a specific case. In addition the challenges faced by lifelong learning topic models are discussed and the new avenues are highlighted as decisive factors towards the future of lifelong learning approach.

Much has been written about teachers developing their humor so that they can improve the effectiveness of their teaching. Much less has been written, however, about training students to develop their humor - this is a significant shortcoming because research shows that the skill of humor can help a student's future career greatly. This paper explores the facilitation of humor in students within the context of an Electrical Engineering program, with a view to increasing students' long-term employability.

Revised:

Functional connectivity patterns disrupted in neuropsychiatric patients are increasingly being utilized as features in pattern recognition algorithms to distinguish them from healthy subjects. While deep neural networks (DNNs) have been recently employed in fMRI functional network classification, their application to EEG-based connectomes remains largely unexplored. In this study, we propose a DNN with deep belief network (DBN) architecture for automated classification of schizophrenia based on EEG effective connectivity. We utilized vector-autoregression-based directed connectivity (DC), graph-theoretical complex network (CN) measures, and a combination of both as input features. Using a large resting-state EEG dataset, we observed a significant reduction in synchronization of neural oscillations measured by partial directed coherence, and decreased network integration in terms of weighted degrees and transitivity in individuals with schizophrenia, compared to healthy controls. The proposed DNN-DBN outperformed three other traditional classifiers, surpassing them due to its inherent capability as a feature extractor to learn hierarchical representations from the aberrant brain network structure. The combination of DC-CN features resulted in further improvements over raw DC and CN features alone, achieving remarkable classification accuracy of 95% for the theta and beta bands.

Multi-agent consensus controllers typically use discrete communication and hence are restricted to fixed-rate or event-triggered communication. Fixed-rate communication suffers from inefficient use of communication and computational resources but is easy to implement, while event-triggered communication conserves resources but suffers from the ambiguity of all event-triggered systems-inability to distinguish failure from lack of new information. We propose a novel hybrid strategy of co-regulating communication with state disagreement amongst the agents obtaining the benefits of discrete fixed-rate and event-triggered consensus while mitigating the associated disadvantages. Our approach dynamically adjusts the communication rate in response to disagreement in the shared state variable, resulting in a discrete-time-varying, asynchronous network topology. We prove convergence properties of the proposed consensus algorithm, develop metrics to evaluate similar dynamic approaches, and demonstrate the results in simulation, showing our algorithm reduces communication resources, while maintaining fast convergence time.

In Wireless Sensor Network (WSN), localization stands as a major challenge which is intended to maximize with minimized traveling distance of the beacon node. Further, the important issue is to improve coverage and accuracy in calculation of the location. This paper mainly focuses on an enhanced path planning model using beacon node. The proposed model focuses to improve coverage of the network topology by moving in zig-zag fashion so that it will enhance the reachability of message in almost every corner of the deployed area. The proposed model is simulated extensively in a self simulator with different scenarios and compared with SCAN and anchor based model. The tested performance of the model is presented along with its analytical model. The simulation result shows that the proposed model outperforms by 1% to 2% than the existing model in terms of percentage of nodes settled and energy consumption.

As the fifth-generation (5G) communication systems continue to grow, future networks are presenting new challenges with diverse characteristics. This chapter analyzes wireless cooperative networks where relays can obtain energy from received radio frequency (RF) signals. It examines networks with one or multiple sources or destinations, considering one or more relays under the assumption that power consumption due to information processing is insignificant compared to power used for signal transmission. Additionally, the chapter explores future research directions, including cognitive energy harvesting (EH) relaying, which allows for secondary transmissions using primary users' resources such as bandwidth and energy.

Wireless backscatter communication is an innovative technique that enables data transmission without conventional energy supply from batteries or power outlets. It is similar to RF energy harvesting powered wireless transmission and offers numerous benefits. In this article, we introduce the concept of a hybrid radio that combines wireless-powered active RF communication and backscatter communication. 

The hybrid radio offers many potential applications and improved network performance through its use cases. One possible use case is its role as passive relays to assist active RF communication. The passive relays backscatter RF signals from the source to the receiver, thus enhancing the multi-path diversity gain, which leads to improved transmission rates.

We also introduce an optimization technique to quantify the performance improvement that can be achieved through the cooperation of radios in a hybrid radio network. 

Overall, the integration of wireless-powered active RF communication and backscatter communication in the form of a hybrid radio is a promising technique for data transmission. It offers numerous benefits and has various potential applications that can improve network performance.

The control problem of a class of parabolic distributed parameter systems (DPSs) is investigated by using mobile agents with capabilities of sensing and actuating. The guidance strategies of mobile agents based on coverage optimization methods are proposed to improve the control performance of the system and make the state norm of the system converge to zero faster. The coverage optimization problems are constructed based on the measurement of each agent. By solving the coverage optimization problems, the local optimal moving direction of each agent can be obtained. Then the gradient-based agent motion control laws are established. With the indicator function and the surface delta function, this method is generalized to n-dimensional space, and suitable for any sensing region with piecewise smooth boundaries. The stability and control performance of the system are analyzed. Numerical simulations show the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

Sign language is a language that uses hand gesture to present a word within the hearing impairment communication. But, the important problem is sign language is not usual for ordinary people which is misunderstand meaningful. However, the advancement in computer vision and recognition process could be adapt in computer system to learn or recognize sign language. These are useful for the system to recognized and translated sign language which ordinary people understand. In this article presents a study in process and method which related with the recognition of sign language using deep learning. The algorithm is 3D-CNN used for recognized process and the images received from Kinect sensor. We found that the sign language recognition using 3D-CNN was effective, the highest accuracy of the recognition was 91.23%.

This study investigated the impact of creativity training on creative self-efficacy, with passion and curiosity being the key determinants of creative self-efficacy. Using a design science research approach, a two-day course was created and administered to students who will eventually implement information systems. Partial Least Squares was used to evaluate the proposed model, which revealed that passion and curiosity account for 47% of the variance in creative self-efficacy. Pre- and post-intervention measurements show significant improvements in passion, curiosity, and creative self-efficacy.

In massive, dynamic and distributed P2P networks like Bitcoin, where thousands of updates occur per second, it is hard to obtain an accurate topology representing the structure of the network as a graph with nodes and links by using the traditional local measurement approaches based on batches, offline data, or on the discovery of the topology around a small set of nodes and then combine them to discover an approximate network topology. All of which present some limitation when applying them on blockchain-based networks. In this paper, we propose a topology discovery system, which performs a real-time data collection and analysis for Bitcoin P2P links with the use of a customized version of the Page-Rank algorithm that assembles incoming nodes information for deeper graph analysis processing. The topology discovery system allows us to gain knowledge on the Bitcoin network size, the network stability in term of well-connected Bitcoin nodes, as well as some data regarding the Bitcoin nodes geolocation.

With the rapid growth of radio services and monitoring facilities, the application of spectrum monitoring has entered the big data era. While the electromagnetic spectrum is a limited resource, it needs to be authorized for use. To detect abnormal spectrum usage and electromagnetic targets appearing in abnormal time or space, a new method has been proposed based on the spatiotemporal periodic characteristic of radio frequency usage. To detect differences between two spectrums in real-time, the piecewise modeling algorithm based on Mahalanobis distance has been proposed to handle frequency spectrum data. For electromagnetic target positioning data, the outlier detection and non-outlier classification algorithm based on Euclidean distance has been proposed to look for unknown target points that appear in unusual time or space by comparing them with spatiotemporal data of historical target points. The validity and applicability of these methods have been verified using real monitoring data collected by CS-S05F. It's of great significance in detecting targets that are using spectrum resources illegally.

The feasibility of a hybrid relay-assisted massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) downlink for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) is investigated. The system performance is investigated for a generalized wireless energy harvesting protocol, which facilitates performance analysis for both time-switching (TS) and power-splitting (PS) protocols in the presence of imperfect channel state information (CSI). The harvested energy and the achievable sum rate are derived, and thereby, the joint/individual effects of TS/PS ratios and pilot contamination are quantified. Our analysis reveals that the pilot contamination can be beneficial for energy harvesting, although it is detrimental for the achievable rates. This energy-rate trade-off is quantified in closed-form, and thereby, valuable system-design insights are obtained.

Physical layer security (PLS) technologies have recently gained significant attention for their remarkable potential in facilitating information-theoretically secure communications. Among these PLS technologies, Artificial Noise (AN)-aided transmission is regarded as one of the most practical ones, given its ability to enable secure transmission irrespective of eavesdropper's channel status. However, our research unveils that AN transmission is dependent on the channel condition of the eavesdropper, as we have introduced an attack method based on a supervised-learning algorithm that uses the modulation scheme, available from known packet preamble and/or header information, as supervisory signals of training data.

Through our numerical simulation results and comparison with conventional clustering methods, we have demonstrated that our proposed method enhances the success probability of attack from 4.8% to 95.8% for the QPSK modulation. This implies that transmission to the receiver in the cell-edge with low-order modulation can be compromised, provided the eavesdropper's channel is good enough and more antennas are employed than the transmitter. Therefore, our study provides new insights into the efficacy of AN schemes and valuable guidance for the design of robust PLS techniques for practical wireless systems.

Providing high data rates, regardless of user location in the network, is one of the major goals of 5G wireless networks. However, this goal becomes more challenging when users move from one cell to another, resulting in a degradation in the user's data rate. To solve this issue, the concept of Virtual Cells (VCs) that utilizes Coordinated Multipoint (CoMP) transmission has been proposed. VCs enable multiple base stations to coordinate with each other, creating a virtual cell that allows users to roam without the need for handovers. This technique reduces the number of handovers and improves the data rate, especially for cell edge users, by minimizing Inter-Cell Interference (ICI) within the virtual cell.

However, to enable VCs, quick decisions are required to enable/disable the VC mode and determine which base stations should be joining/leaving the VC as the user roams. This paper proposes a novel algorithm for predicting the triggering conditions for VC mode based on a modification in the hidden layer of the Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), known as Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs). The RNN-GRU model uses sequences of Received Signal Strength (RSS) values for different users in the network to predict future RSS values, which are then used for proactive decisions on enabling/disabling VC mode. The simulation results show that the proposed GRU-RNN model achieves 92% accuracy in predicting the triggering conditions for enabling and disabling CoMP mode based on the mobility of users. 

In summary, the proposed solution based on the RNN-GRU model is a promising approach for enabling Virtual Cells in 5G wireless networks. It ensures that high data rates are maintained, regardless of user location, and reduces the number of handovers to improve the user experience. It also provides an efficient and accurate method of making proactive decisions for enabling/disabling VC mode, enabling the network to adapt to the mobility of users efficiently.

High penetration of volatile renewable energy produces uncertainties in power system and poses severe challenges to transmission network planning (TNP). Usually, only one type of mathematical model of different uncertainties was considered in every single TNP method. However, in the process of TNP, different uncertainties may show different mathematical features and need to be represented by various types of mathematical models. Aiming at this problem, a TNP model taking into account interval uncertainty model of renewable energy generation and fuzzy uncertainty model of predicted load is proposed based on the expanded fuzzy chance constrained programming. In accordance with the features of the constructed planning model, the model is transferred to a robust TNP model considering interval uncertainty model of renewable energy generation and predicted load. Thus, the calculation burden for solving the planning model decreases. The analyses on the modified IEEE RTS 24-bus system and a 231-bus system verify the effectiveness and adaptability.

In order to deal with the power leakage of side lobes in physical layer security, this paper investigates a secure transmission system aided by Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) jamming. The receiver, located at the center of the beam, remains unaffected due to the power null of OAM radio wave. Based on its distinctive power null, a secure transmission system with imperfect Channel State Information (CSI) and random eavesdroppers is proposed in this paper. To be specific, the artificial noise and the desired information signal are transmitted by the radio wave with OAM and without OAM respectively. Meanwhile, a power allocation optimization algorithm is designed to acquire the target secrecy capacity. Simulations are implemented to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm compared with other methods. Furthermore, we find that there is a secrecy capacity upper bound in the presence of imperfect angle measurement and random eavesdroppers. Moreover, the proposed power allocation algorithm leads to a higher secrecy capacity upper bound.

RFID technologies have been used in retail industry over the last couple of decades. There are many examples of using RFID tags in retail stores as part of retail shop floor management. In this paper we will consider some of the most important solutions that are either being experimented with or already implemented to determine their potential in improvement of customer experience. Data collected through a well-organized RFID system in combination with mobile application can provide invaluable set of dynamic data that can further improve both back office operations and front office operations. Goal of this paper is to analyze the impact of employing this new technology and collected data on established customer experience services such as loyalty programs, promotions and overall customer experience. We propose establishing a dedicated specification that will cater for the information requirements of this type of applications in retail store in higher OSI layers.

Event detection is a crucial feature in data-driven systems as it facilitates the identification of both normal and abnormal behavior. The relevance of event detection in robotics is increasing due to the fact that robots are operating with greater autonomy in unstructured environments. In this research, we introduce a highly precise, robust, fast and adaptable measure for skill and anomaly identification. A theoretical validation establishes the correlation between the derivative of the log-likelihood of the HMM filtered belief state and the most recent emission probabilities. The crucial aspect is the inverse link between gradient analysis used for detecting both skill and anomaly. Our measure has demonstrated higher effectiveness across all parameters compared to all other related state-of-the-art works barring one. This outcome can be applied broadly to all domains that use HMMs for event detection. Additional information, data, code, and videos can be obtained from [1].

This paper presents a novel Brain Computer Interface (BCI) for controlling mechatronic devices. The method utilizes electroencephalogram (EEG) acquisitions, particularly the Movement Related Potentials (MRPs), to determine the user's intention and control the mechatronic device. The EEG data is collected by only five wireless smart electrodes placed on the central and parietal cortex area. The acquired data is analyzed by an innovative single-trial classification algorithm that significantly reduces the training and acquisition time for a reliable classification. The algorithm performs an EEG time-frequency analysis, followed by dimensionality reduction, statistical inference-based features extraction and classification model selection. A dedicated algorithm, the MLE-RIDE, is also proposed for dimensionality reduction, performing the features extraction. Finally, the best support vector machine (SVM) model is chosen for online classification. Two mechatronic devices, a three-finger robotic hand and an acrylic prototype car, have been brain-controlled by the proposed BCI algorithm as proof of concept. The experimental results, based on 3 subjects (aged 26±1), demonstrated an accuracy rate of 87.4%, with a computation time of 33.7ms, in real-time binary discrimination, thereby showing the potential for this system to be used in the field of mechatronic device control.

This work presents a lip reading deep neural network that fuses the asynchronous spiking outputs of two bio-inspired silicon multimodal sensors: the Dynamic Vision Sensor (DVS) and the Dynamic Audio Sensor (DAS). The fusion network is tested on the GRID visual-audio lipreading dataset. Classification is carried out using event-based features generated from the spikes of the DVS and DAS. Networks are trained separately on the two modalities and also jointly trained on both modalities. The jointly trained network when tested on DVS spike frames alone, showed a relative increase in accuracy of around 23% over that of the single DVS modality network.

The black box arc model is ideal for describing the arcing process of a hybrid circuit breaker, as it allows for the integration of the arc model into an electrical circuit. However, determining the parameters of the arc model based on circuit breaker performance is a more challenging task than solving the analytical equations of the model. To overcome this hurdle, a library of arc models, including Mayr, Cassie, and Kema, has been created and validated with MATLAB Simulink/Simscape.

To estimate the parameters of the arc models, heuristic optimization methods such as Genetic Algorithm, Simulated Annealing, and Particle Swarm Optimization have been utilized. The results indicate that the inverse modeling technique effectively identifies the appropriate parameters to represent the changing conductance of the arc plasma. Furthermore, the GA, when equipped with well-selected parameters, demonstrates a significant advantage over alternative methods.

In recent years, there has been an increased focus on research for deep neural networks that enable object classification for self-driving vehicles using electro-optical sensors. While public optical datasets and classification algorithms already exist, it is important to note that only radars can provide robust sensing in adverse conditions where optical systems may fail. As a result, the development of high-resolution radar is crucial for approaching radar imagery classification with neural networks in a similar way with optical images. With this in mind, a new method of classification using Convolutional Neural Networks has been developed for six different roadside targets in low-THz imaging radar. The results of this method have shown that neural networks can also be successfully employed for low-THz radar imagery classification with high resolution. Ultimately, this research could lead to the implementation of an all-weather sensing system for autonomous vehicles.

Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have a wide range of applications in military, security, internet, and scientific fields. The dynamic variation of channel gain and random topology in such networks makes it challenging to select operating parameters that can enhance their performance. While single channel MAC is typically used for statistical analysis, using multi-channel MAC can greatly improve network performance.

The 802.11b/g standard provides multi-channel support, with three different non-overlapping channels available. In this study, we implemented a multichannel MAC based on 802.11g using NS-2.34 and compared its performance to that of single channel MAC in terms of throughput, packet delivery ratio, and delay. Our results showed that the mulitchannel MAC outperformed the single channel MAC in terms of all three parameters.

The multichannel MAC utilizes a back off algorithm that switches between the three non-overlapping channels when the contention window of the distributed coordination function reaches the maximum threshold value. This technique improves network performance by reducing contention and increasing the utilization of available channels.

In conclusion, implementing a multichannel MAC in WSNs can provide significant performance improvements compared to single channel MAC. Our study highlights the benefits of using a multichannel MAC in terms of increased throughput, improved packet delivery ratio, and reduced delay. Such improvements are particularly valuable for applications that require high data rates and reliable transmission such as military and security systems.

The potential to characterize the electrical properties of cells as label-free biophysical markers for cell status evaluation has been recognized for some time. Nonetheless, prior research has largely focused on the electrical properties of cell populations. Single-cell analysis has the potential to provide distinct insights into the heterogeneous behaviors of cells, which may otherwise be concealed within the averaged response of a cell population. However, a robust approach for the study of the electrical properties of single cells has yet to be proposed.

In response to this gap in research, a microfluidic-integrated, optically-controlled electrodes chip has been developed for the real-time characterization of the electrical impedance of single cells. The approach involves the proposal and discussion of an equivalent circuit model for extracting the impedance of a single cell. Using this method, the impedance of a mouse myoblast cell line, C2C12, was characterized. 

Overall, this new approach to studying the electrical properties of single cells represents a promising advancement in the field. By providing a means to investigate the electrical properties of individual cells, the approach presents the opportunity to gain a more detailed understanding of the heterogeneity within cell populations. This in turn has the potential to provide crucial insights into a range of biological systems and processes.

The main reason of the extensive usage of the fuzzy systems in many branches of science is their approximation ability. In this paper, an interval type-3 fuzzy system (IT3FS) is proposed. The uncertainty modeling capability of the proposed IT3FS is improved in contrast to type-1 and type-2 fuzzy systems (T1FS and T2FS). Because in the proposed IT3FS, the membership is defined as an interval type-2 fuzzy set, whereas in T1FS and T2FS, the membership is crisp value and type-1 fuzzy set, respectively. An online fractional-order learning algorithm is given to optimize the consequent parameters of the IT3FS. The stability of the learning algorithm is proved by utilizing the Lyapunov method. The validity of the proposed fuzzy system is illustrated by both simulation and the experimental studies. It is shown that the proposed fuzzy system and associated learning algorithm result in better approximation performance in comparison with the other well-known approaches.

Deep neural networks have become increasingly popular for their ability to accurately classify images, and deep learning algorithms like multilayer perceptron artificial neural networks have played a significant role. However, optimizing these deep models can be challenging due to the complexity of the functions they approximate. This is where multilayer extreme learning machines (MLELM) come in, as they leverage both deep learning and extreme learning machines to approximate complicated functions without the need to iterate during the training process. In addition, online sequential extreme learning machines (OSELM) can adapt to new datasets by being trained on them alone, thus eliminating the need to retrain from scratch. Combining MLELM and OSELM results in a powerful new algorithm called Multilayer OSELM, which we apply to the Pneumonia Chest X-Ray image dataset in this study. Through simulation and analysis of our experimental results, we confirm the effectiveness of Multilayer OSELM in identifying cases of Pneumonia.

To address the issue of slow image feature extraction and poor matching accuracy in mobile augmented reality (MAR) scene recognition, this paper presents an enhanced natural feature recognition algorithm consisting of SURF and ORB methodologies. Initially, the image undergoes preprocessing techniques including Gaussian smoothing, gray-scaling and histogram equalization to diminish noise and facilitate image feature extraction. Next, useful image feature information is extracted and the image center is selected as the feature point. Thereafter, SURF and ORB algorithms are utilized to illustrate the feature points along with determining their orientation to ensure image rotation invariance. Subsequently, the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm is leveraged to select the SURF space and ORB spatial neighboring image, respectively. The image weight, known as the weighted KNN algorithm, is calculated to form a new image set, and the image with the smallest weight is chosen as the matching image. The results of the experiments reveal that when the feature extraction time and matching time are less than 3 ms on an Ordinary laptop, and image matching accuracy reaches as high as 92.5%, the computing speed and matching accuracy outperform traditional algorithms. These findings suggest that natural feature recognition of an image can be achieved in real-time with high accuracy.

High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) is the newest video codec that significantly increases the coding efficiency of its predecessor, H.264/Advanced Video Coding. This is achieved through the implementation of new features such as quadtree-based coding unit partitioning, a simple deblocking filter, and other advanced coding techniques. Unfortunately, the HEVC also demonstrates a significant increase in computational complexity, the primary cause of which lies in the exhaustive rate distortion optimization search of quadtree-based coding unit partitioning.

This paper presents a coding unit partitioning pattern optimization method based on a genetic algorithm to mitigate the computational complexity of hierarchical quadtree-based coding unit partitioning. The method efficiently considers the required coding unit partitioning pattern for exhaustive partitioning and the rate distortion cost as the chromosome and fitness function of the genetic algorithm, respectively. To further enhance computational efficiency, coding unit partitioning patterns of the key frame are searched and shared with other consecutive frames, accounting for high temporal correlation.

Evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 62.5% and 16.7% computational complexity reduction on average in comparison with HM16.5 and state-of-the-art support vector machine-based fast algorithms, respectively, under low-delay P configuration with rate control. This reduction further improves to 64.1% and 15.1% under low-delay configuration with rate control, with negligible average quality degradation.

Fuzzy Petri nets (FPNs) are a useful tool for representing and reasoning with knowledge in rule-based expert systems. To improve FPNs' ability to handle imprecise, fuzzy, and linguistic information, various fuzzy sets and linguistic models have been introduced. However, there are still two main issues with existing FPN models. The first is the incompatibility of knowledge representation parameters for linguistic variables, and the hesitancy of experts to provide linguistic evaluations. The second is that existing reasoning operators fail to guarantee the reasoning result satisfies essential properties like monotonicity, boundary, and idempotency.

To overcome these issues, we propose the q-rung orthopair fuzzy linguistic reasoning Petri nets (q-ROFLRPNs) using q-rung orthopair fuzzy linguistic sets (q-ROFLSs) to enhance the conventional FPN capability in dealing with fuzzy and linguistic knowledge. Our approach defines new closed operational laws of q-ROFLSs through linguistic scale functions (LSFs), which guarantee the validity and reliability of reasoning results and handle different semantic situations of the linguistic term set. We also introduce an enhanced reasoning algorithm based on the weighted ordered weighted averaging (WOWA) operator, considering the weights of propositions themselves and their ordered weights. This approach guarantees the monotonicity, boundary, and idempotency of the results.

Finally, we provide a case study on fault diagnosis for a metro door system to demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed model. Overall, q-ROFLRPNs offer a promising approach for improving the ability of FPNs to handle fuzzy and linguistic knowledge while satisfying crucial properties like monotonicity, boundary, and idempotency.

The Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) is a remarkable reinforcement learning method that typically involves actor and critic learning. However, since the actor learning highly relies on the critic learning, the performance of the DDPG method is often sensitive to critic learning, which ultimately leads to stability issues.

In order to enhance the stability and performance of the DDPG method, we propose the multi-critic DDPG (MCDDPG) method, which emphasizes reliable critic learning. This is achieved by using the average value of multiple critics to replace the single critic in DDPG, making the performance of the method more resistant even when one critic performs poorly.

Furthermore, by incorporating multiple independent critics, the MCDDPG method is capable of learning knowledge from the environment in a more comprehensive manner. To expedite the training process, we also introduce an extension of the experience replay mechanism.

The MCDDPG method was tested in simulated environments utilizing the OpenAI Gym platform, and the experiment results strongly support the effectiveness of the proposed methods. Overall, our MCDDPG approach represents a significant step towards more robust and stable reinforcement learning.

This paper describes a plant leaf disease diagnosis system that utilizes color imagery and unsupervised neural network technology. The system employs both color and texture features to process images, and employs a two-step process to perform disease feature extraction and disease classification. The disease feature extraction process utilizes a statistical-based gray-level co-occurrence matrix and texture feature equations to analyze feature appearance. The subsequent disease classification process employs an unsupervised simplified fuzzy ARTMAP neural network to categorize types of disease. A variety of different types of grape leaf disease images were employed to test the system's classification performance, including rust, scab, downy mildew, and no disease. The results show that the system is able to achieve desirable results with a classification accuracy of more than 90%, demonstrating its potential application for diagnosing other types of plant disease as well.

Research on facial action unit (AU) analysis typically require facial images that are labelled with those action units. While unlabelled facial images abound, labelling those images with action units or intensity is costly and time-consuming. Our approach makes it possible to analyze facial AUs when only some of the images have been labelled. We use many facial images to learn a deep framework that is able to take advantage of the facial representations. A restricted Boltzmann machine uses the available AU annotations to learn the AU label or intensity distribution. We train a support vector machine for AU recognition and a support vector regression for AU intensity estimation by maximizing the log likelihood of the AU mapping functions, taking into account the learned multiple AU distribution for all training data, while simultaneously diminishing errors between the predicted action units and ground-truth action unit occurrence or intensities for all labelled data. We perform experiments on two databases. The results demonstrate the superiority of a deep neural network for learning facial features, as well as the benefit of action unit label or intensity constraints for action unit occurrence recognition or intensity estimation in fully or semi-supervised scenarios.

In this study, we propose a particle swarm optimization (PSO) based method for designing a cylindrical-rectangular ring microstrip conformal antenna using support vector regression (SVR) models. The resonant frequency of the antenna is determined by employing PSO to optimize the trained SVR models. To build the SVR models, we have utilized two different kernel functions: radial basis function (RBF) and wavelet kernel function. The proposed approach is validated using simulation examples, and the obtained results are compared with the existing approaches.

Due to the excessive demand on multimedia, the network traffic requires new technologies to improve communication networks. The core data networks are formed of single and multichannel fiber optical transmission systems nowadays. The leading technology in a multichannel fiber optical communication is 10 Gbps DWDM (Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing), which is used worldwide. The 40 Gbps DWDM systems are still in the adaptation phase. The development of DWDM system increases the transmission speed, transmission distance and channel traffic. On the other hand, the multichannel transmission over single optical fiber induces nonlinear effects which degrades performance of DWDM system. The four-wave mixing (FWM) is the most dominant of all nonlinear effects, especially in dense division multiplexing systems. FWM appear as a crosstalk between the adjacent channels in DWMD system. In this paper we propose a strategy to mitigate the impact of FWM on optical signal transmission in a DQPSK modulated 32-channel Ultra-DWDM system with 1.28 Tbps (40 Gbps per channel) transmission capacity. The simulation model is based on the ITU-T G.694.1 and created in OptiSystem™ software. The resulting signal is mathematically analyzed and BER and Q factor values are calculated.

We investigate facial expression recognition using state-of-the-art classification models. Recently, CNNs have been extensively used for face recognition. However, CNNs have not been thoroughly evaluated for facial expression recognition. In this paper, we train and test a CNN model for facial expression recognition. The performance of the CNN model is used as benchmark for evaluating other pre-trained deep CNN models. We evaluate the performance of Inception and VGG which are pre-trained for object recognition, and compare these with VGG-Face which is pre-trained for face recognition. All experiments are performed on publicly available face databases, namely, CK+, JAFFE and FACES.

Liver lesion segmentation is a difficult yet critical task for medical image analysis. Recently, deep learning based image segmentation methods have achieved promising performance, which can be divided into three categories: 2D, 2.5D and 3D, based on the dimensionality of the models. However, 2.5D and 3D methods can have very high complexity and 2D methods may not perform satisfactorily. To obtain competitive performance with low complexity, in this paper, we propose a Feature-fusion Encoder-Decoder Network (FED-Net) based 2D segmentation model to tackle the challenging problem of liver lesion segmentation from CT images. Our feature fusion method is based on the attention mechanism, which fuses high-level features carrying semantic information with low-level features having image details. Additionally, to compensate for the information loss during the upsampling process, a dense upsampling convolution and a residual convolutional structure are proposed. We tested our method on the dataset of MICCAI 2017 Liver Tumor Segmentation (LiTS) Challenge and achieved competitive results compared with other state-of-the-art methods.

This paper proposes an efficient method for modeling and simulating soft robots. Soft robots can be simulated and controlled using finite element methods. However, these methods are limited by their high-dimensional system and are not suitable for real-time simulation or control design tools. To address this issue, the authors propose using model order reduction to create a reduced order system for building controllers and observers.

To account for model reduction errors, the low-order feedback is designed and then applied to the large dimensional and unreduced model. The control architecture is based on a linearized model of the robot and allows for control around the equilibrium point. The effectiveness of this control method is demonstrated through pose-to-pose and trajectory tracking experiments on a pneumatically actuated soft arm.

This soft arm has 12 independent interior cavities that can be pressurized to move the arm in three dimensions. It is made of rubber material and fabricated using a lost-wax technique. The results show that the proposed control method can effectively control the soft robot in different scenarios.

In summary, the presented method provides an efficient way of modeling and simulating soft robots, which can be useful in various fields such as medical and industrial robotics.

Objective: Vascular permeability is a critical mechanical parameter that plays a vital role in cancer growth, metastasis, and progression. However, there are only a few non-invasive techniques to image VP in solid tumors currently available. These methods require the use of contrast agents, which can be expensive and hinder widespread use. In this paper, we propose a new method for imaging VP in tumors using ultrasound poroelastography.

Methods: The proposed imaging method requires information about Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, and strain time constant in the tumor. To estimate VP, we determine the best fit ellipse for the tumor, regardless of its shape, using an eigen-system-based fitting technique. We then use Eshelby's elliptic inclusion formulation to estimate the Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio. Finally, a Fourier method is used to estimate the axial strain time constant, which is highly robust to the noise and does not require an initial guess.

Results: Our simulation results indicate that the proposed method can accurately estimate VP in irregularly shaped tumors with an accuracy of above 80%, with a signal-to-noise ratio of 20 dB or higher. Furthermore, the in vivo feasibility of the proposed technique has been demonstrated in an orthotopic mouse model of breast cancer.

Conclusion: The proposed ultrasound poroelastography imaging method provides a cost-effective and accurate means of assessing vascular permeability in cancers in a non-invasive manner.

Significance: Accurate and non-invasive assessment of VP has a significant impact on cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment, and the proposed method could pave the way for widespread use of non-invasive imaging methods to assess VP in solid tumors.

Stimulated by the emerging Internet of Things (IoT) applications and their massive generated data, the cellular providers are introducing various IoT functionalities into their networks architecture. They should integrate intelligent and autonomous mechanisms that are able to detect sudden and anomalous behavior issues. In this paper, we present an adaptive anomaly detection approach in cellular networks consisting of two parts: the detection of overloaded base-stations using machine learning algorithm (LSTM - Long Short-Term Memory) and the deployment of drones as mobile base-stations that support and back up the overloaded cells. The proposed approach is validated using real dataset extracted from the CDR of Milan combined with semi-synthetic eHealth data. Initially, The LSTM algorithm analyzes the impact of eHealth applications on cellular networks and identifies cells with peak demands. Then, drones are deployed to collect the requested data from these cells. The obtained results show that the use of drones improves the quality of service and provides a better network performance.

In the Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) environment, to successfully orchestrate a network service, first a Virtual Network Function-Forwarding Graph (VNF-FG) must be composed that realizes the required functionality. Second, this VNF-FG must be embedded onto the infrastructure, that is increasingly becoming heterogeneous. To avoid wasting precious resources during orchestration, intelligent resource allocation mechanisms and algorithms are needed to effectively tailor the VNF-FG to the cloud network onto which the service will be deployed. In this paper, we introduce an improved service model supporting network services that have bidirectional chaining constraints, comprise optional VNFs, and require traffic aggregation. Building on this service model, we propose placement algorithms that can optimize the order and number of instances of VNFs, to adapt the VNF-FG to the availability of resources in the network. Numerical experiments show that through coordination of composition and embedding tasks, our proposed algorithms can significantly improve the acceptance ratio, compared to algorithms that perform these tasks in two separate stages.

We explore the possibility of building learned models that can recognize the large-scale path loss characteristics of an environment by processing its geometry alone. These machine intelligence models can be trained by physics-based propagation analysis techniques such as ray-tracing or the parabolic equation method, to eventually develop an “electromagnetic vision”: the ability to provide the propagation properties of a channel based on a formally defined input file (or a sequence of images) that contains the channel's geometric specification. As a first step towards realizing this objective, we train a model to recognize the path loss exponent (PLE) in rectangular tunnels and show good correspondence of model predictions with measured and simulated data.

This paper proposed an indirect high frequency signal injection (HFSI) method of rotor position estimation for three-stage brushless synchronous machine (TSBSM) used as starter/generator in the variable frequency AC power system. The high frequency signal is injected into the stator windings of the main exciter of TSBSM during three-phase excitation method, then, the high frequency response signal within the AC excitation voltages is injected indirectly into the field winding of main generator through the rotary rectifier for the rotor position estimation in the starting processing. Due to the nonlinear property of rotary rectifier and side effect of rotor speed on the high frequency response signal, the frequency-response analysis for the rotor position estimation error is proposed for the optimized frequency selection of HFSI method, where the rotor position is detected by the asynchronous demodulation method and the initial position angle is calibrated according to the polarity of induced current in main generator stators during the establishment of excitation field. Finally, the proposed analysis of the frequency-response characteristics and the sensorless starting control method are verified to be effective and validated by the simulation and experimental results.

The Danger Theory proposes a robust defensive mechanism that underpins the human immune system, which utilizes a sophisticated classification metaphor known as the Dendritic Cell Algorithm (DCA). This algorithm has been demonstrated in a variety of real-life scenarios and has been adopted in the field of behavioural detection for operational training purposes. The algorithm employs a signal-based classification method which is capable of learning and self-organizing, with "danger signals" corresponding to safety and procedural activities differentiated from information captured in virtual environments such as Training of Ramp Operations in Virtual Environment (TROVE) and Detective Boulevard.

By applying the DC-inspired metaphor, the performance of trainees can be autonomously assessed and enumerated by the DCA, improving the quality of assessments made by trainers or coaches. In a benchmark study focusing on the operational training of aircraft door handling, the behaviours involved in operational procedures and safety concerns were analyzed. The study showed that Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) outperformed DCA in terms of classification accuracy and run time in the given domain.

Overall, the Dendritic Cell Algorithm has proven to be a powerful metaphor with diverse applications ranging from immunology to operational training. As with any classification algorithm, the choice of which one to use depends on specific needs and requirements. In the case of behavioural detection for operational training, the DCA has shown promise as a robust and trainable classifier.

This paper presents a new approach to inertial and magnetic sensing-based orientation estimation using a parallel Kalman filter. The proposed approach consists of two separate Kalman filters: one for attitude estimation using an external acceleration model, and the other for heading estimation using a magnetic disturbance model. In contrast to other model-based Kalman filters, the proposed approach implements disturbance models by inserting them into the measurement equations rather than relying on state-augmentation. This results in a significant reduction in computational cost, with no increase in the matrix size of the KF structure. Experimental verification of the proposed approach in magnetically disturbed conditions demonstrated its superior calculation efficiency and ease of use compared to traditional state-augmentation approaches.

This paper describes the design of an automatic identification system for the distinction between two common languages in Algeria which are MSA (Modern Standard Arabic) and Kabyle which is an Algerian Berber dialect. The characteristics used for this are prosodic (melody and stress) and cepstral (Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients) features extracted from a bilingual database formed by combining two databases. For the classification step Support vector machines are trained for language modeling because it is a recognition of two languages which puts him in a better position to establish this task. Experiments have shown the superior reliability of our system when using both types of characteristics when compared to the use of each type separately. It was found that when using prosodic characteristics the system gives an encouraging rate of 95.42% which was improved to 95.83% when adding acoustic features and 97.5% (so an improvement of 1.67%) when combining prosodic and acoustic features which has shown the superiority of this vector over those previously cited.

To gather information of human activities through brain wave - EEG (Electroencephalogram) signal, various algorithms have been introduced and researched relating to 3 main filters: digital filter, wavelet filter and neural network. By applying filters to identify some different states of EEG, this paper gives an insight of neural network performance, comparing with others, on simple activities of human brain. In details, researched human activities include states involving to eyes behavior, facial expression and thinking signal. The raw EEG signal has been acquired by Emotiv EPOC+and analyzed with Matlab. Furthermore, the comparison of algorithms efficiency has been done with Mean Square Error value and other parameters which demonstrate the possibility of using neural network to analyze EEG signal.

The study aimed at establishing the use and acceptance of e-books by book readers in a Namibian university. Applying a mixed methods approach, a survey questionnaire was administered to 35 undergraduate students initially and in a second phase telephonic interviews were conducted with 12 purposively selected surveyed students based on their questionnaire responses to get a deeper understanding of student experience utilising e-books. Findings revealed that the use and acceptance of e-books in Namibia is still in its infancy. Although there is an awareness of e-books among students, most of them prefer print books. One of the reasons for low e-book usage was due to insufficient training on how to access them. It was recommended that faculty officers at this university collaborate with librarians to ensure prescribed e-books are purchased or subscribed to and adequate Information Literacy training is provided to students. Future research that focuses on expanding the sample size to include all faculties, benchmarked against different universities nationally and internationally will give further insight into e-book uptake in the digital age in Africa and globally. Further studies also need to be conducted to establish why about 14% of students don't read books (print or electronic) at all whiles in school.

To provide personalized services to users and implement user-centric management, operators often need to collect varying information of users. However, obtaining accurate information can be challenging due to concerns relating to user privacy and avoiding interference in the user experience process. Traditional methods such as creating a laboratory network environment or conducting user research can also be difficult to apply in a live network setting. This paper proposes a new approach where a variety of data related to user behavior is extracted through the service log of the network device interface. The data is then analyzed and transformed into the expression of user behavior, which includes factors such as time, space and semantics. 

To capture the user behavior patterns, this paper suggests utilizing a user behavior symbolization method. This method varies depending on the application scenario and helps to mine the user behavior sequence patterns using a user behavior pattern mining method based on PrefixSpan. This mining method extracts patterns from user behavior data, thereby providing a foundation for personalized service and management. 

The experiments were conducted using the HTTP connection log of all mobile users of a carrier in a single city for one day, and the results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method. Overall, the proposed method provides a comprehensive, multidimensional approach to mining user behavior patterns for personalized service and management, without interfering with the user experience process or compromising user privacy.

Machine learning is becoming a powerful tool for cancer diagnosis and prognosis based on classification using high dimensional molecular data. However, extracting classification features from high-dimensional datasets remains a challenging problem. Principal component analysis (PCA) is a widely used method for dimensionality reduction. However, it is well-known that PCA and most PCA-based feature extraction methods are sensitive to noise, which may affect the accuracy of the subsequent classification. To address this problem, here we have proposed a robust fuzzy principal component analysis (PCA) with interval type-2 (IT-2) fuzzy membership functions for feature extraction. We have tested the performance of three widely used classifiers using the features extracted by proposed approaches and other feature extraction methods - PCA-based feature extraction methods (i.e. conventional PCA and fuzzy PCA), linear discriminant analysis (LDA), and support vector machine recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE). The proposed feature extraction approaches showed better performance on cancer transcriptome and proteome datasets.

In thin steel plate production lines widely used for various industrial products, thin steel plates are contact-conveyed by rollers in the conveying process. Owing to this conveying method, the quality of the surface deteriorates, resulting in degradation such as scratches or peeling of the plating layer of the thin steel plate. As a solution to these problems, we studied a noncontact magnetic levitation system for a rectangular thin steel plate using electromagnets and permanent magnets. We determined the optimal placement of permanent magnets using a genetic algorithm (GA), which searches for placements using an evaluation function. However, although the evaluation function was defined by the GA, since only a basic examination was conducted, the weight coefficient used in the evaluation was insufficient. In this paper, we changed the weight coefficient of the evaluation function and compared and analyzed the results of the permanent magnet arrangement determined by the GA. It is possible to obtain an optimum permanent magnet arrangement in which the levitation stability is improved by experimentally verifying the effects of the maximum deflection and average deflection on levitation performance. The levitation experiment is carried out using each weight coefficient for permanent magnet arrangement. Then, the levitation stability is evaluated.

Demands for accurate pedestrian indoor tracking on mobile platforms have been increasing rapidly these years, however, conventional tracking system based on dead reckoning suffers from inherent sensor drift, which leads to bad performance in long-term tracking. In this paper, an infrastructureless pedestrian dead reckoning system called iPDR is proposed and implemented on a ready-to-use smartphone, offering real-time indoor tracking for pedestrian without previous knowledge of the target area. The iPDR fuses the sensor data using a novel filter approach coined as hybrid orientation filter, which deploys a combination of the information filter and the complementary filter to achieve accurate heading estimation. A fast loop closure detection method called rapid loop detection is also presented in the iPDR to calibrate the tracking trajectory significantly whenever encountering a loop. Experiment results show that the iPDR system achieves typically sub-meter accuracy in localization and has an average orientation error of 2.89 degrees over a total turning of 1800 degrees.

In today's world, the majority of data is generated in the form of streaming data from various application domains. Due to the ever-increasing size of this data, it becomes a challenging task to detect unusual events or make intelligent predictions. Real-time detection of anomalous events in streaming applications is crucial because of the constantly evolving nature of the event streams and the infinite size of the data. 

To address this issue, we proposed a novel distributed real-time collective anomaly detection method. Our approach includes defining an event stream snapshot model, designing a distributed collective event stream detector, and evaluating the accuracy of the detection rates and detection processing runtime performance. 

Experimental evaluation of our method demonstrated its ability to detect a collection of events from high volumes of unbounded streams in real-time. Overall, our proposed approach provides a reliable and efficient way of detecting anomalous events in streaming data, which can be highly beneficial in various application domains.

With the advancement of big data analysis technologies, users can benefit from the usage of sensor data through IoT and WSNs. However, the occasional occurrence of sensor errors can lead to a failure in maintaining optimal conditions, and smart systems without user intervention are susceptible to intrusions via external networks. To address these concerns, this paper proposes a method to ensure optimal state even when the sensor network fails due to sensor failure or external intrusion in big data systems.

Artificial Neural Network (ANN) macromodeling is an active area of research in the field of modeling and simulation. The aim of this paper is to propose a Karhunen-Loeve Decomposition (KLD) Model Order Reduction (MOR) based ANN macromodel of a nonlinear electrical circuit that is excited by variable frequency input. 

This method involves obtaining solution sets, which are called snapshots, of the nonlinear circuit equations at specific time intervals. In order to reduce the order of the nonlinear circuit model, KLD is applied on the snapshot matrix. Another set of snapshots is obtained from the linearized equation of the nonlinear circuit. The ANN is then trained using the linear snapshots as input and the nonlinear output of KLD as the target. 

This procedure is repeated for different frequency inputs over a wide range of frequency spectrum. Finally, the trained ANN output is verified with the original circuit behaviour for an untrained frequency. This approach allows the modeling of a large and complex nonlinear electrical circuit with reduced computation cost and increased accuracy.

To address the issues of size and energy consumption imbalance in the LEACH protocol cluster, this study introduces an energy-equalized unequal clustering routing protocol. The proposed approach utilizes the energy decision factor and node density decision factor to improve the candidate cluster head threshold calculation formula. With this improvement, nodes with more residual energy and more neighbor nodes are more likely to become candidate nodes. The candidate cluster heads are then elected as real cluster heads based on a certain competition radius which takes into account the number of cluster heads and the distance between nodes and the base station.

The algorithm divides nodes into clusters of different sizes to keep the size of the cluster close to the base station smaller, effectively resolving the “hot spots” problem. Additionally, the number of cluster heads and distribution are more reasonable with this approach. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm effectively balances network consumption and prolongs the network life cycle.

Public sector all over the world is now facing the challenge of demonstrating better performance in managing budgetary resources. Performance auditing seeks to answer how effective budget funding to spend on public sector entities. This paper considers performance auditing as part of the government audit. The paper acquaints the reader with practice auditing in the public sector. Research materials for this paper came from various public sector organizations which audited by Supreme Audit Bodies. In the paper the scheme of performance audit in a public sector organisations are presented. Problem situations, order of reflection and the control of operations in practice of performance audit are considered. The method of performance audit coordinated to system of key performance indicators of public sector is offered.

Multi-view face synthesis from a single image is a complex computer vision problem that often leads to appearance distortions if not well-defined. Hence, it is necessary to produce photo-realistic and identity-preserving multi-view results by addressing the synthesis problem precisely. To achieve this, the paper proposes 3D-aided duet generative adversarial networks (AD-GAN) that can rotate an input face image to any specified angle.

AD-GAN decomposes the challenging synthesis problem into two subtasks that correspond to a face normalizer and a face editor. The normalizer frontalizes an input image, and the editor rotates the frontalized image to a desired pose guided by a remote code. The face normalizer estimates a novel dense UV correspondence field, which makes the model aware of 3D face geometry information.
