Mathematical models for the same have been verified with the help of numerical examples. Conclusively, sensitive analysis has been presented.

In the Cloud, computing loads found a new virtualized and dynamically scaling home. However, because of the pay-as-you-go business concept that is dominant in the Cloud, scenarios where a big percentage of requests turn up with low-value data (as in incomplete, meaningless or out-of-sync) can be financially detrimental to the Cloud tenant. Internet of Things offerings expand the list of data sources for a Cloud-based service. They also take the data filtering and pre-processing required of services to get to the core value-returning requests to a new level. The availability of Fog nodes offers an opportunity where some processing is done on the edge of the network in order to distribute the load and minimize the network congestion caused by low-value data. This poses a question to Cloud service designers on how to optimize this process. The decision as to where to perform each step of the data management can make the difference for Cloud providers in mitigating both the risk of pushing high loads to the Cloud servers and network which increases the cost and the risk of almost localizing the whole process and losing the benefits from Cloud services. This process is complicated by constraints pertaining to the Fog nodes capacity, and bandwidth available. Furthermore, the impact of realistic factors like Fog node ownership and device priority must be considered. To tackle this challenge, we consider the question of optimizing the decision process for a data-intensive highly distributed Cloud service. A novel optimization model is presented with 3 alternate objects (request computational delay, service provider cost and a weighted multi objective version). Initial experimental results using 4 heuristic algorithms are presented. Shown results offer some insight into the contradicting factors in play (cost, network capacity, node and Cloud capacity).

Mosaicking is a technique that can efficiently summarize geospatial content in aerial videos, which finds applications in various areas such as surveillance, activity detection, and tracking. However, the registration process is complicated by factors such as scene clutter, distractors, parallax, illumination artifacts, and large camera motion. To overcome these challenges, robust feature detection and description is essential.

This study evaluates selected feature detectors, including Structure Tensor with NCC (ST+NCC), SURF, and ASIFT, in the Video Mosaicking and Summarization (VMZ) framework on the VIRAT benchmark aerial video. While ST+NCC and SURF are fast, they fail in complex imagery with occlusion. ASIFT is more robust, but it is time-consuming. Therefore, an adaptive descriptor combining ST+NCC and ASIFT is proposed, which is 9x faster than ASIFT and has comparable robustness.

Overall, the study demonstrates the importance of feature detection and description in mosaicking and provides a solution to improve the efficiency and robustness of the process.

The success of the Internet of Things (IoT) and rich cloud services have helped create the need for edge computing, in which data processing occurs in part at the network edge, rather than completely in the cloud. Edge computing targets to address concerns such as latency, mobile IoT devices' limited battery life, bandwidth costs, security, privacy and so on. Extending potential cloud applications beyond data center at the networking edge is one of hot technical topics among global cloud service providers (CSPs) nowdays. P2SP CDN (aka PCDN), as the first Baidu deployment quality cloud edge computing application, Baidu innovated put their content delivery network (CDN) application to networking edge for bandwidth utilization and cost efficiency, also accelerates end customer response to address the latency requirement of the emerging applications. Compared with conventional data center environment, PCDN environment is more complicated for infrastructure devices maintained by multiple parties, such as dynamical temperature, high humidity, corrosion prone, power constraint, non-stand-ardized management interface and so on. This paper proposes a novel fanless box system architecture, adapting for Baidu PCDN edge computing environment. Then details the comparison of conventional server system for energy and cost efficiency from system thermal and power architecture perspective. Engineering practice result and best known methods are summarized in the end. This paper also introduces Baidu PCDN application architecture and the methodology of system energy efficiency optimization based on workload characteristic.

This paper presents a solution to the problem of finite-time stabilization of coupled reaction-diffusion partial differential equations using boundary time-varying feedbacks. The design of time-varying feedbacks is carried out through a backstepping approach, based on selecting a suitable target system with time-varying coefficients. The resulting kernel of the backstepping transformation is also time-varying, which allows for the control feedback to be time-varying as well. The target system is shown to be fixed-time stable, and two cases for the control design are presented to achieve either boundedness or fixed-time convergence of the original system. A simulation example is included to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

The accuracy of traffic big data prediction is an important issue in the development of vehicular cyber-physical systems (VCPS). While deep learning has shown great success in traffic prediction, the models currently in use cannot effectively learn the features of uncertain traffic data. This poses a challenge to accurate prediction in VCPS. This study proposes a new approach, the tensor-train fuzzy deep convolution (TFDC), to address this challenge. The TFDC uses a fuzzy deep convolutional network with a unified tensor data representation for spatio-temporal traffic flow data. Additionally, the Tucker deep computation (T-TFDC) approach is proposed to compress parameters for traffic flow feature learning. Both the TFDC and T-TFDC models are trained using the back-propagation strategy. Experimental results on the TaxiBJ and BikeNYC data sets demonstrate that these models outperform state-of-the-art methods in terms of effectiveness and efficiency.

An early detection of the disease status can play a vital role, as timely action can save patient's life. A disease status of the patient is a type of PHI (Protected Health Infonnation).In general the process ofidentifying the PHI is done manually on the structured dataset, this activity is prohibitively expensive, time consuming and error prone.In order to overcome the known drawback of the manual identification system an implementation of automated personal health information identification like disease status is required. In our work an effort has been done to build a model with a novel approach based on deep neural models for automatic identification of disease status (one of the PHIs) from free text clinical records. The experimental evaluation of the proposed models on two different datasets from i2b2 Challenge tasks, show the merit ofthe proposed scheme.

Although there are a variety of automated management systems available, their effectiveness in providing informational and decision support for production management at the operational level is limited. Numerous studies conducted by both Russian and foreign authors indicate that the informational aspect of management is essential for its efficiency. Therefore, the development and implementation of software that can collect, modify, interpret, and forecast information is significant for enhancing enterprise efficiency during the transition to the sixth techno-economic paradigm.

In assembling management, defect management is a critical process. Typically, defect management processes are supported by paper or electronic registers, catalogs, manuals, and the data of various corporate information systems. However, with the increasing intensification of production processes and the consequent increase in workers' informational workload, processing information required for decision-making related to defect processing can be challenging. To address this issue and enhance the quality and speed of processing information, an expert system that facilitates data collection and provides straightforward decision support resources should be utilized.

To improve the efficiency of engineering technologist work related to the processing of requests for registering defects revealed during aircraft assembling, a proposed solution would be the integration of an expert system. This system allows for the accumulation of data about typical solutions and offers simple resources for decision-making. Based on the first results of the expert system implementation, which was developed by the authors, it is evident that further research into expert systems as a tool for informational and decision support at the operational level of production management is necessary.

There is a need of the networks which can accommodate the requirements of high data rate with low blocking probability. Optical networks are used most commonly as the backbone. They support high data rates, but need to be provisioned with low blocking probability. Due to the use of traditional Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM), optical network are not that much bandwidth efficient as they could be. Elastic Optical Network (EON) configuration can be used to resolve this problem if Routing and Spectrum Assignment (RSA) problem is done efficiently. We are addressing the routing problem through an artificial intelligence-based algorithm. In earlier works, several optimization methods have been used for path-finding in the networks. Some of these studies has problem in terms of higher time complexity and incompleteness, due to which there is no guaranteed optimal solution. In this paper, we are using A* algorithm for routing, which is known for its best-estimated cost of a path from a source to a destination. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to study the use of A* algorithm in routing and spectrum allocation in the EON. We have modified this algorithm in a way such that, while reconstructing the path, we simultaneously check how many contiguous and continuous slots are available. So, while allocating the spectrum if the required slots are not available at that instant, we can either block or re-route the path. It saves time and decreases the blocking probability. Modified A* algorithm is expected to solve the problem only if initial seed values of the cost of the paths are not over estimated beyond a threshold. For the spectrum assignment, after evaluation of available slots while reconstructing the path, whichever slots are contiguously and continuously available, are allocated using different modulation formats. We have studied the algorithm for different network topologies, to check its validity and compared the results with the previously used algorithms.

One important aspect in the design of a generic radar target simulator is the level of complexity incorporated in the generation of scenarios. The trade-off between the expected fidelity in the generation of scenarios and the computational constraints in the target simulation system raises alternatives to model-based approaches. In this paper we present a data-driven method for the generation of road scenarios in the context of automotive radar target simulation. The method characterizes the scenarios relying on radar recordings and prior information on the testing set-up. The recorded data is processed in order to play back the scenario with a radar target simulator. This is relevant, for instance, so that certain functionalities of the radar under test can be evaluated and tuned in reproducible conditions. The presented data-driven method is applied to one particular road scenario and validated in simulation experiments.

In-network processing of spatial queries is a popular data collection method used in wireless sensor networks (WSN). Users generate SQL-like queries with specifications such as the type of information (temperature, humidity, etc.), duration of measurement, periodicity, data aggregation (Max, Min, average), and region of interest. Standard WSN geographic routing algorithms are used to route queries to nodes pertinent to the specific region of interest. However, the currently used Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) routing algorithm, RPL, is not effective for spatial queries as it floods messages to all nodes inside or outside of the target region. To address this, we introduced PA-RPL, a performance-enhanced routing algorithm that takes into account the importance of partition or region. In this work, we propose an extension to PA-RPL that allows efficient routing of spatial queries in an IoT enabled wireless sensor network. Our results show that this approach achieves high scalability for large size and density networks, significantly reduces message transfer, and results in a 20% gain in energy as compared to standard RPL.

Thermoelectric generators (TEGs) are devices that efficiently recover energy from automotive exhaust gas. In this study, the conversion efficiency and maximum electrical power output of an automotive TEG (ATEG) were improved by optimizing the number and distribution pattern of thermoelectric modules (TEMs). A numerical model was developed using Simulation-X software, which considered the heat transfer between adjacent TEM rows. A 3-step optimization process was applied, involving screening parameters, sensitivity analysis, and a multi-objective genetic algorithm. The optimized ATEG generated a maximum electrical power of 139.47 W and had a conversion efficiency of 2.51% under steady engine conditions. Furthermore, the optimized design achieved a 49.8% increase in maximum power generation and a 106.5% increase in efficiency when the exhaust inlet temperature was 805 K and the mass flow rate was 0.5 kg/s. These findings highlight the potential of optimizing TEM number and distribution patterns to improve ATEG performance.

With a rapid increase in the number of geostationary satellites around the earth's orbit, there has been a renewed interest in using Global Positioning System (GPS) to understand several phenomenon in earth's atmosphere. Such study using GPS devices are popular amongst the remote sensing community, as they provide several advantages with respect to scalability and range of applications. In this paper, we discuss how GPS signals can be used to estimate the amount of water vapor in the atmosphere. Furthermore, we demonstrate the importance of such precipitable water vapor (PWV) in the atmosphere for the task of rainfall detection. We present a detailed analysis in our dataset of meteorological data of 3 years. Test dataset shows that use of PWV in rainfall detection helps to reduce the false alarm rate by almost 12%.

In this article, we explore the vital role that cloud computing plays in today's tech-driven world. We delve into the impact that cloud computing has had on modern information technologies and the fundamental components that make up cloud platforms. Additionally, we examine the decision tree induction algorithms, which are crucial for effective data analysis and processing.

The significance of cloud computing in modern IT cannot be overstated. With cloud computing, organizations can store, process, and analyze vast amounts of data at a fraction of the cost of traditional on-premise solutions. Additionally, cloud platforms offer unparalleled scalability, allowing businesses to quickly and easily adapt to evolving customer needs.

To better understand how cloud computing works, we need to examine its core components. Cloud platforms consist of a variety of interconnected services, including storage, computing, networking, and security. These services operate seamlessly to enable the storage, processing, and analysis of vast amounts of data.

Furthermore, decision tree induction algorithms help organizations to effectively analyze and process data. These algorithms work by recursively splitting data into categories based on a set of predefined rules. Decision tree algorithms are becoming increasingly common in many industries, including healthcare and finance, where they play critical roles in data analysis.

Several cloud platforms are available that provide support for decision tree induction algorithms. One such platform is Microsoft Azure, which offers a wide range of machine learning algorithms to help organizations make informed decisions. Additionally, Google Cloud Platform offers support for decision tree algorithms, enabling businesses to process and analyze large volumes of data.

We have also offered an example of a software implementation of a simplified decision tree algorithm for categorized data on a cloud platform. This algorithm has various use cases, including medical research, where it can be used to identify key risk factors for specific illnesses.

In conclusion, cloud computing and decision tree induction algorithms play vital roles in modern IT. Cloud platforms offer unparalleled scalability and flexibility, while decision tree algorithms are becoming increasingly important for data analysis and processing. By leveraging these technologies, organizations can gain valuable insights and make informed decisions that drive growth and success.

We conducted a study in which several widely-used deep learning frameworks were benchmarked, and the field programmable gate array (FPGA) deployment was investigated for traffic sign classification and detection. The focus was on evaluating the training speed and inference accuracy of these frameworks on the graphics processing unit (GPU) by training FPGA-deployment-suitable models with various input sizes on the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB), a traffic sign classification dataset. 

The trained classification models and various object detection models that we trained on GTSRB's detection counterpart were evaluated based on inference speed, accuracy, and FPGA power efficiency by varying different parameters such as floating-point precisions, batch sizes, etc. The study revealed that Neon and MXNet demonstrated the best training speed and classification accuracy on the GPU in general for all test cases. TensorFlow, on the other hand, consistently performed among the frameworks with the highest inference accuracies. 

The study also demonstrated that with the current OpenVINO release, the performance of lightweight models (e.g., MobileNet-v1-SSD) typically exceeds the requirement of real-time detection without compromising on accuracy. However, other models (e.g., VGG-SSD, ResNet50-SSD) often fail to do so. The precision of bitstreams and the batch sizes can be adjusted to strike a balance between inference speed and accuracy of the applications deployed on the FPGA. 

Finally, the study established that for all test cases, the FPGA consistently achieved higher power efficiency than the GPU.

Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) has emerged as one of the most promising semi-supervised learning methods where two neural nets train themselves in a competitive environment. In this paper, as far as we know, we are the first to present a statistically trained Ternarized Generative Adversarial Network (TGAN) with fully ternarized weights (i.e. -1,0,+1) to massively reduce the need for computation and storage resources in the conventional GAN structures. In the proposed TGAN, the computationally expensive convolution operations (i.e. Multiplication and Accumulation) in both generator and discriminator’s forward path are converted into hardwarefriendly Addition/Subtraction operations. Accordingly, we propose a Processing-in-Memory accelerator for TGAN called (PIM-TGAN) based on Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory (SOT-MRAM) computational sub-arrays to efficiently accelerate the training process of GAN within non-volatile memory. In addition, we propose a parallelism technique to further enhance the training efficiency of TGAN. Our device-to-architecture co-simulation results show that, with almost the same inception score to the baseline GAN with floating point number weights on different data-sets, the proposed PIM-TGAN can obtain ~25.6× better energy-efficiency and 22× speedup compared to GPU platform averagely, and, 9.2× better energy-efficiency and 5.4× speedup over the best processing-in-ReRAM accelerators.

In this research paper, we conducted an analysis of happy moments and activities based on a collection of text responses shared by people through Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) - a crowd-sourcing platform. Collecting data through crowd-sourcing enabled us to understand the cause of happiness by studying real human experiences and words. MTurk workers were asked to share three specific happy moments from a given period. We then used text-based analysis to study the words and components that affect happiness, focusing on classifier subcategories to gain insights about their happiness based on specific factors. Using the bag of words approach, we extracted features from the text in HappyDB and were able to accurately predict the happiness category. We also discussed the ethical perspective of our research and its social implications.

The article focuses on enhancing the performance of direct model reference adaptive control (MRAC) for linear time-invariant (LTI) plants. The paper proposes three novel solutions that involve modifying and aggregating the dynamic regressor extension and mixing (DREM) estimator with standard gradient-based adaptation algorithms driven by augmented error. The dynamic extension of the regressor is proven to significantly improve tracking and parametric error convergence, while also generalizing existing results of MRAC. Comparatively, the proposed adaptive control algorithms demonstrate superior performance in simulated scenarios.

In recent years, the agriculture industry has become increasingly data-driven and enabled, thanks to the use of technologies like greenhouse and aquaculture technologies. To keep up with the demand for quality and quantity of food, there is a growing need to industrialize and intensify the agriculture sector. As a result, there is now a great emphasis on making the smartest technological investments in agriculture. 

The paper provides empirical measurement results from an Internet of Things (IoT) platform that utilizes remote telemetry applications specifically tailored for agriculture. The paper aims to showcase how the processing of Big Data and the concept of decentralized cloud operation can meet the demands of IoT applications in the agriculture industry, enabling farmers to operate more efficiently and securely. 

The architecture of the IoT platform is based on the ADCON Remote Telemetry Units (RTUs), Software as a Service (SaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS) represented by Grafana and influxDB database. With this framework, farmers can access crucial information about their crops in real-time. This includes data about the temperature, humidity, and other essential factors affecting plant growth. The IoT technology also enables farmers to make informed decisions regarding plant nutrition, pesticide application, and irrigation. 

Overall, this paper shows how IoT technology can help farmers achieve better yields, reduce costs, and optimize their resources. The ability to use and analyze big data also allows for better forecasting and predicting market trends, giving farmers a competitive edge in the industry. By investing in smart farming technologies, the agriculture industry can keep up with the growing demand for food while also improving the efficiency, security, and sustainability of operations.

Graphic Processing Units (GPUs) are highly parallel, power hungry devices with large numbers of transistors devoted to the cache hierarchy. Machine learning is a target application field of these devices, which take advantage of their high levels of parallelism to hide long latency memory access dependencies. Even though parallelism is the main source of performance in these devices, a large number of transistors is still devoted to the cache memory hierarchy. Upon detailed analysis, we measure the real impact of the cache hierarchy on the overall performance. Targeting Machine Learning applications, we observed that most of the successful cache accesses happen in a very reduced number of blocks. With this in mind, we propose a different cache configuration for the GPU, resulting in 25% of the leakage power consumption and 10% of the dynamic energy per access of the original cache configuration, with minimal impact on the overall performance.

The success of digital image pattern recognition and feature extraction using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) or Deep Learning was recently acknowledged over the years. Researchers have applied these techniques to many problems including traffic offense detection in video surveillance, especially for the motorcycle riders who are not wearing a helmet. Several models of CNN were used to solve these kinds of problem but mostly required the image pre-processing step for extracting the Region of Interest (ROI) area in the image before applying CNN to classify helmet. In this paper, we proposed to apply another interesting method of deep learning called Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) into helmet detection problem. This method is the state-of-the-art that is able to use only one single CNN network to detect the bounding box area of motorcycle and rider and then classify that biker is wearing or not wearing a helmet at the same time. The results of the experiment were surprisingly good. The classification accuracy of bikers not wearing a helmet was extremely high and the detection of the ROI of biker and motorcycle in the image can be done at the same time as the classification process.

We present a novel deep-learning-based approach for one-class transfer learning in which labeled data from an unrelated task is used for feature learning in one-class classification. The proposed method operates on top of a convolutional neural network (CNN) of choice and produces descriptive features while maintaining a low intra-class variance in the feature space for the given class. For this purpose two loss functions, compactness loss and descriptiveness loss, are proposed along with a parallel CNN architecture. A template matching-based framework is introduced to facilitate the testing process. Extensive experiments on publicly available anomaly detection, novelty detection, and mobile active authentication datasets show that the proposed deep one-class (DOC) classification method achieves significant improvements over the state-of-the-art.

In this paper, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based method that allows unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to execute navigation tasks in large-scale complex environments. This technique is important for many applications such as goods delivery and remote surveillance. The problem is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) and solved by a novel online DRL algorithm designed based on two strictly proved policy gradient theorems within the actor-critic framework. In contrast to conventional simultaneous localization and mapping-based or sensing and avoidance-based approaches, our method directly maps UAVs' raw sensory measurements into control signals for navigation. Experiment results demonstrate that our method can enable UAVs to autonomously perform navigation in a virtual large-scale complex environment and can be generalized to more complex, larger-scale, and three-dimensional environments. Besides, the proposed online DRL algorithm addressing POMDPs outperforms the state-of-the-art.

As is well known, the prototype coprime arrays consist of two collinear subarrays, whose physical sensor number is coprime to each other. Moreover, their larger inter-element separations and physical array apertures make them have less mutual coupling than uniform linear arrays. Even so, there is still mutual coupling existing in them, which has an adverse effect on the direction of arrival estimation. To reduce the effects of mutual coupling, several improved coprime configurations based on the concept of difference and sum coarray are proposed in this paper, which can be obtained through three operations. The first one is to shift the prototype coprime array to obtain the translational coprime arrays, which can help to reduce the redundancy between the difference coarray and sum coarray. Second, flip one of the subarrays in the translational coprime arrays with zero points as the symmetric center to get the flipped coprime arrays, which can expand the physical array aperture and inter-element separations further. Finally, move one of the symmetrically placed sensors in the flipped coprime arrays to zero points. Then, the proposed arrays are derived. They have almost the same consecutive degrees of freedom (DOFs) as the prototype coprime array but dramatically reduced mutual coupling due to their larger physical array apertures and inter-element separations, where the virtual arrays are constructed by their respective difference and sum coarray. In the end, the numerical simulation results confirm the superiority of proposed arrays.

The papers in this special section focus on cloud computing, fog computing, the Internet of Things, and Big Data analytics for the future healthcare industry, or Healthcare 4.0. Healthcare Industry 4.0 allows increasing flexibility in production, speeding up both manufacturing and market processes, increasing both the product quality and productivity, and changing business models modifying the interaction with value chain, competitors, and clients. Healthcare Industry 4.0 requires investments and mind-set change for cross-industry collaboration, agreements on data ownership, security, legal issue solving, product registration standards, new machine-to-machine communication protocols, and employment/skills development. Furthermore,Healthcare Industry 4.0 is revolutionizing the market of health service provisioning to patients and clinical operators.

Internet of Things (IoT) development is a very challenging topic, and the debate about the actual implementation is still wide open. Various studies have been conducted in term of smart home system based on IoT technology. However, resources that concern on how to practically implement the particular energy-saving and resource efficient technology for smart home need to be improved. In this study, presented the field experiment results related to implementation of low-power node modules using sub 1 GHz LPWAN (low-power wide area network) connectivity. LPWAN technology has unique characteristics, such as a transmit power that in SRD class (short range device) but cellular like coverage range. LPWAN network support star topology by default, so it can overcome the problem of power usage inconsistency, network delay and the complexity of the routing management process found on conventional mesh-based sensor networks. Based on the field experiment result, the furthest distance under outdoor condition could reach up to 350 meters (RSSI -85 dBm) and 150 meters (RSSI -95 dBm) under indoor condition. Based on the power usage test, life-span estimation could reach up to 1 year or 17 years depend on the scenarios and battery types.

In contrast to the traditional host-centric model that relies on destination address for communication, Information-Centric Networking (ICN) is based on content name as the fundamental element for data delivery and other network functionalities. Named Data Networking (NDN) is an ICN project that utilizes hierarchical unbounded names, which can be memory-intensive with long lookup time. This study focuses on naming in vehicular named data networks and proposes a Name-to-Hash Encoding scheme. Under this approach, each name component is hashed to a fixed length before being subjected to a heuristic Wu-Manber-like algorithm for quick lookup. By consuming less memory and providing fast lookup time, the proposed scheme has been shown to outperform other related solutions in real domain datasets. Comprehensive analysis and experimental evaluations validate the efficiency of the proposed scheme in terms of complexity, memory consumption, and lookup time.

This paper explores the discrimination ability and stability of electroencephalogram (EEG) and eye movement signals over time for classifying five emotions: happy, sad, fear, disgust and neutral. We develop a multimodal emotion dataset called SEED-V with 16 subjects. Two classifiers are trained based on the EEG and eye movement signals. Topographic maps are used to depict the neural patterns of EEG signal. The classification result based on EEG, eye movement, and feature level fusion (FLF) reaches the average accuracies of 70.8%, 59.87% and 75.13%, respectively. The experiment result indicates that: a) the EEG and eye movement signals have good discrimination ability for five emotion classification problem; b) the beta and gamma bands of EEG signal have better discrimination ability than the delta, theta and alpha bands; c) the stable neural patterns of different emotions do exist and are common across sessions; and d) the neural pattern of disgust emotion has high gamma response in the frontal area, while fear emotion has low activation at the top of brain in the gamma band.

In this paper, we propose a new model for color face recognition that involves the use of quaternion numbers and deep neural networks (DNN). Our goal in developing this model is to increase the classification accuracy of color face recognition. To achieve this objective, we have introduced an image represented in the quaternion domain as an input vector in the DNN model, which is frequently utilized in many vision tasks of pattern recognition.

The utilization of the quaternion representation aims to reduce the size of the input vector and consequently the computational complexity. Furthermore, this representation also preserves color information from the image, which is vital in obtaining the best classification results.

To demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model, we conducted simulations on color face databases. The results of our simulations clearly show that the proposed model outperforms other existing algorithms. In conclusion, our work presents a promising solution to the challenges of color face recognition using a novel combination of quaternion numbers and deep neural networks.

Grid-connected solar photovoltaic (PV) generation systems have gained significant popularity due to their ability to supply power to local loads and also pump excess power to the grid when local demand is low. However, the efficiency of the power pumping capability of such systems can be adversely affected by line impedance and load variations. In this paper, we investigate how line impedance and loading influence the voltage profile in the distribution network with distributed solar PV systems. We analyze the voltage profile in a representative low voltage (LV) distribution network due to the variation of load change and line impedance. To carry out our analysis, we simulate the system using the MATLAB/SIMULINK platform.

Motion artifact in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a common issue that impacts the ability of doctors to accurately diagnose a patient's condition. The motion artifact is caused by the natural physiological movements of the patient while the organ is being scanned. Current methods for reducing artifact and restoring images are inefficient and ineffective, resulting in limited clinical utility. This paper introduces a novel approach to combine deep learning and multi-scale mechanisms for MRI motion artifact correction. Specifically, the authors propose a deeper and wider residual block that results in a significant improvement in correction effect. Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity (SSIM) were used as evaluation metrics. The presented model can be trained end-to-end and tested in real-time, achieving state-of-the-art results for MRI motion artifact correction.

Flash memory can store large number of model weights for a deep neural network on edge devices. In this paper, we study the effects of Flash's bit-error-rate on the neural network's weights and prediction accuracy, given that error correction engine is disabled due to power constraint in edge devices. The reliability experiments on MLC NAND Flash show that DNN prediction accuracy remains above the acceptable level in the presence of different NAND reliability issues for the following memory usage: less than 5 years of data retention, ~100 program-erase cycle, and less than 30k read stress.

We consider general block sparse vectors, which consist of non-zero blocks placed at arbitrary non-overlapping locations and the block partitioning information is unavailable apriori. We propose a generalized block orthogonal matching pursuit (G-BOMP) algorithm to recover the general block sparse vectors, from a set of noisy compressive measurements. We then establish that the sinusoidal signal estimation problem can be solved using the G-BOMP algorithm, by exploiting the structure of spectral leakage in the Fourier domain. We study the performance of the G-BOMP algorithm via simulations and compare it with other algorithms such as OMP, BOMP, newtonized OMP (N-OMP) and spectral compressive sensing (SCS). We observe that our G-BOMP algorithm outperforms OMP, BOMP and SCS methods and is comparable to N-OMP with much lower computational complexity.

We study a communication scheduling and remote estimation problem within a worst-case scenario that involves a strategic adversary. Specially, a remote sensing system consisting of a sensor, an encoder and a decoder is configured to observe, transmit, and recover a discrete time stochastic process. At each time step, the sensor makes an observation on the state variable of the stochastic process. The sensor is constrained by the number of transmissions over the time horizon, and thus it needs to decide whether to transmit its observation or not after making each measurement. If the sensor decides to transmit, it sends the observation to the encoder, who then encodes and transmits the observation to the decoder. Otherwise, the sensor and the encoder maintain silence. The decoder is required to generate a real-time estimate on the state variable. The sensor, the encoder, and the decoder collaborate to minimize the sum of the communication cost for the sensor, the encoding cost for the encoder, and the estimation error for the decoder. There is also a jammer interfering with the communication between the encoder and the decoder, by injecting an additive channel noise to the communication channel. The jammer is charged for the jamming power and is rewarded for the estimation error generated by the decoder, and it aims to minimize its net cost. We consider a feedback Stackelberg game with the sensor, the encoder, and the decoder as the composite leader, and the jammer as the follower. Under some technical assumptions, we obtain a feedback Stackelberg solution, which is threshold based for the scheduler, and piecewise affine for the encoder and the decoder. We also generate numerical results to demonstrate the performance of the remote sensing system under the feedback Stackelberg solution.

This paper presents a robust human posture and body parts detection method under a specific application scenario known as in-bed pose estimation. Although the human pose estimation for various computer vision (CV) applications has been studied extensively in the last few decades, the in-bed pose estimation using camera-based vision methods has been ignored by the CV community because it is assumed to be identical to the general purpose pose estimation problems. However, the in-bed pose estimation has its own specialized aspects and comes with specific challenges, including the notable differences in lighting conditions throughout the day and having pose distribution different from the common human surveillance viewpoint. In this paper, we demonstrate that these challenges significantly reduce the effectiveness of the existing general purpose pose estimation models. In order to address the lighting variation challenge, the infrared selective (IRS) image acquisition technique is proposed to provide uniform quality data under various lighting conditions. In addition, to deal with the unconventional pose perspective, a 2- end histogram of oriented gradient (HOG) rectification method is presented. The deep learning framework proves to be the most effective model in human pose estimation; however, the lack of large public dataset for in-bed poses prevents us from using a large network from scratch. In this paper, we explored the idea of employing a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) model trained on large public datasets of general human poses and fine-tuning the model using our own shallow (limited in size and different in perspective and color) in-bed IRS dataset. We developed an IRS imaging system and collected IRS image data from several realistic life-size mannequins in a simulated hospital room environment. A pre-trained CNN called convolutional pose machine (CPM) was fine-tuned for in-bed pose estimation by re-training its specific intermediate layers. Using the HOG rectification method, the pose estimation performance of CPM improved significantly by 26.4% in the probability of correct key-point (PCK) criteria at PCK0.1 compared to the model without such rectification. Even testing with only well aligned in-bed pose images, our fine-tuned model still surpassed the traditionally tuned CNN by another 16.6% increase in pose estimation accuracy.

Recognizing lies in human communication is a significant and complex task for artificial intelligence. This task has many important applications, such as designing a human-computer interaction system capable of detecting deceit in conversations. Additionally, AI systems might need to occasionally tell a white lie in order to avoid hurting the user's feelings during interactions. 

To develop a liar detection system, we constructed a video corpus consisting of 540 question-answer pairs. The responses were given by nine individuals, with half being true answers and half being lies. The images in the corpus were manually analyzed to identify patterns of deception. 

We also applied machine learning techniques, specifically support vector machines with local binary pattern features and geometric features, to our corpus. Both approaches were used to determine whether an answer was truthful or deceptive. 

Our analysis of the corpus and the machine learning techniques used on it demonstrated promising results in detecting lies in human interactions. This research has significant implications for improving AI systems that interact with humans, and could lead to more effective liar detection and enhanced communication.

Social networks offer a platform for global communication and a plethora of opinions on various topics. With the abundance of raw data available, it is worthwhile to collect and analyze the data for insightful use, such as monitoring public opinion and aiding informed decision-making by the government. However, social media has also been used by radical thinkers to influence those with radical views to take violent action. To address this issue, we propose a framework for opinion mining and extremist content detection in online social media data. Our focus is on Facebook, the most popular social networking site, where machines can learn to automatically extract messages, filter non-opinion messages, determine sentiment, and detect violent or extremist content. This framework can help law enforcement and cybercrime analysts with analyzing and monitoring social media, aiding in the search for digital traces of violence or radicalism for further investigations.

Accurate evaluation of Ultra Low Power Systems on Chip (ULP SoC) is a huge challenge for designers and developers. In embedded applications, especially for Internet of Things end-node devices, ULP SoCs have to interact with their environment, but modelling a complete SoC and the peripheral components, their interaction and low-power policies, can be very complex in terms of developments and benchmarking. In order to cope with this challenge, an approach is to implement the desired system on FPGA with a monitoring infrastructure dedicated to fast and accurate evaluation. This paper presents a reconfigurable prototyping platform used for SoC architecture exploration and real-time application evaluation.

Brain computer interface translates electroencephalogram (EEG) signals into control commands so that paralyzed people can control assistive devices. This human thought translation is a very challenging process as EEG signals contain noise. For noise removal, a bandpass filter or a filter bank is used. However, these techniques also remove useful information from the signal. Furthermore, after feature extraction, there are such features which do not play any significant role in effective classification. Thus, soft computing-based EEG classification followed by extraction and then selection of optimal features can produce better results. In this paper, subband common spatial patterns using sequential backward floating selection is being proposed in order to classify motor-imagery-based EEG signals. The signal is decomposed into subband using a filter bank having overlapped frequency cutoffs. Linear discriminant analysis followed by common spatial pattern is applied to the output of each filter for features extraction. Then, sequential backward floating selection is applied for selection of optimal features to train radial basis function neural networks. Two different datasets have been used for evaluation of results, i.e., Open BCI dataset and EEG signals acquired by Emotiv Epoc. The proposed system shows an overall accuracy of 93.05% and 85.00% for both datasets, respectively. The results show that the proposed optimal feature selection and neural network-based classification approach with overlapped frequency bands is an effective method for EEG classification as compared to previous techniques.

In this work, we study the application of the supervised descent method to two-dimensional electromagnetic inverse problems. The inversion process contains two stages: offline training and online prediction. In the offline stage, the average descent directions of cost functions are learned from a set of training data; and in the online stage, model reconstruction is achieved through iterative minimization based on learned descent directions. This scheme offers a new perspective to incorporate prior information into inversion, and reduce the computational complexity in the online inversion. Numerical examples validate the accuracy and efficiency of this method.

Uploading vehicle sensor data is crucial for enabling autonomous driving, as it helps to understand the current traffic situation and make informed decisions. In this paper, we propose a peer-to-peer system for obtaining information in a vehicular network. Our system relies on vehicles equipped with cameras and communication capabilities to upload new snapshots to a datacenter, which then combines them to create a map.

However, the traditional approach of uploading data periodically from each vehicle is not practical when multiple vehicles are simultaneously uploading, as it causes a communication bottleneck. To overcome this challenge, we propose a distributed system that reduces data redundancy and thereby reduces the required bandwidth between vehicles and the datacenter.

Our distributed system takes advantage of location information, such as GPS coordinates, to simplify coordination among vehicles. We also utilize computer vision algorithms to identify important information to be uploaded and remove redundant data. The result is a more efficient and scalable system for processing vehicle sensor data.

Through simulation studies, we have verified the efficacy of our system. Our proposed system reduces the required bandwidth while ensuring that important information is still reliably transmitted to the datacenter. This peer-to-peer solution offers a practical solution for handling the massive amounts of data generated by autonomous vehicles.

We present in this document, an approach that uses artificial intelligence in the service of agriculture. We use convolutional neural networks to prevent the amount of agricultural production per hectare. First, we started with the massive collection of weather and meteorological data from the study area during the last 57 years. Secondly, we have moved to the data processing phase: normalization, filtering and segmentation of data. Thirdly, we design the learning and testing database, and then we looked for the most efficient neural architecture in terms of learning time and recognition rate. Finally, we tested the proposed neural model and presented our results and perspectives.

This article discusses the development of a system for classification of online handwritten text and non-text data in Devanagari script. The proposed system uses an elliptical region-wise feature extraction approach where online stroke information is divided into smaller elliptical regions that are further divided into sub-regions for extracting various structural and directional features. These features are then studied using Hidden Markov Model based classification platform. The system has been tested on a self-generated dataset and has yielded promising results. This approach appears to be a significant contribution to developing a robust system for handwritten document classification in online mode as no previous recognized work exists in any Indic script.

Identifying impact fault features in the fault vibration signal is highly significant in diagnosing faults and monitoring the condition of rotating machinery. However, due to the presence of background noise, detecting impact features amidst defects and working conditions can be challenging. To overcome this, researchers and engineers have been exploring a relatively new method, empirical wavelet transform (EWT), but this approach has two crucial drawbacks: using the local maxima method from Fourier spectra to detect boundaries and capturing impact features through Meyer wavelet, which can be inaccurate for non-stationary and noise frequency signals.

To address these issues, a reinforced empirical Morlet wavelet transform (REMWT) has been proposed to efficiently diagnose fault features. This method adaptively detects frequency spectrum boundaries from the inner product of spectral kurtosis and Gaussian function via scale space representation, enhancing the frequency characteristics of impact features in vibration signals. The constructed empirical Morlet wavelet is then used as an adaptive filter bank to decompose the signal into several empirical modes based on the spectrum boundaries. The maximum Pearson correlation coefficient method is used to select the most meaningful component, and the envelope spectrum is utilized to accurately extract fault features.

The proposed method has been applied to diagnose fault features in collected vibration signals, and the results demonstrate its outstanding performance and effectiveness. Overall, the REMWT method can significantly aid in identifying impact fault features in vibration signals, improving the fault diagnosis and condition monitoring of rotating machinery.

Using two electrically long dipoles to estimate the polarizations of impinging sources, this paper pioneers signal-processing algorithms in closed forms. The existing literature on crossed-dipoles polarimetry are restricted to electrically short dipoles with an electrical length of (L/λ) ≤ (1/10), which have subpar efficiency in radiation and in reception. In contrast, this paper allows electrically long dipoles-two of them here are perpendicularly oriented but may be collocated or may be separated by a known displacement. Using such a pair of electrically long dipoles for polarization estimation, this paper proposes new closed-form formulas and derives the associated Cramér-Rao bounds.

Partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) are commonly used for sequential decision-making in situations where there is uncertainty in state transitions and sensing. However, model uncertainty can arise when the models for which an action policy was optimized change over time, such as the decay of sensors leading to a drift in the observation function. Replanning a policy every time a model drifts is both time-consuming and computationally expensive, but ignoring the drift and following the original policy can result in high-risk actions with high costs. 

To address this issue, we propose an approach that post-processes a policy computed using initial models and selects actions that are robust to changes in the observation function, without excessive computational burden. Our approach is based on maintaining a belief region instead of a belief point about the system state, and performing online robust action selection with respect to the current belief region. We formulate a convex optimization problem to select actions that maximize the worst-case reward function for a convexified belief region. 

We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through simulation results, which show that it can help avoid high-risk actions when the system is in uncertain states. By considering model uncertainty and selecting robust actions, our approach can improve decision-making in POMDPs with changing models, while avoiding the computational burden of repeated policy replanning.

Information systems are one of the biggest crucial elements in today's education institutions. Nowadays, institutions are constantly under pressure to digitalize most of their processes. In order to improve information systems, or to have qualitative information systems, it is essential to have evaluation of application accordingly from users' perspective. This research offers an evaluation from user perspective of e-services dedicated to the education area. EMIS system was chosen as a case study. This system has been evaluated based on DeLone and McLean's information system success model. This paper is a quantitative study, and it uses all DeLone and McLean's variables to develop and validate measurement model of education information systems success, which has an impact specifically in the administrating process. The conclusions of this paper are that user has a weighty impact on improving information systems. Furthermore, application designers/developers should consider many factors when implementing an application that would be used by different categories of stakeholders.

In this paper, we propose a novel multimodal fusion framework, called the locally confined modality fusion network (LMFN), that contains a bidirectional multiconnected LSTM (BM-LSTM) to address the multimodal human affective computing problem. In the LMFN, we introduce a generic fusion structure that explores both local and global fusion to obtain an integral comprehension of information. Specifically, we partition the feature vector corresponding to each modality into multiple segments and learn every local interaction through a tensor fusion procedure. Global interaction is then modeled by learning the dependence between local tensors via an originally designed BM-LSTM architecture, establishing a direct connection of cells and states of local tensors that are several time steps apart. With the LMFN, we achieve advantages over other methods in the following aspects: 1) local interactions are successfully modeled using a feasible vector segmentation procedure that can explore cross-modal dynamics in a more specialized manner; 2) global interactions are modeled to obtain an integral view of multimodal information using BM-LSTM, which guarantees an adequate flow of information; and 3) our general fusion structure is highly extendable by applying other local and global fusion methods. Experiments show that the LMFN yields state-of-the-art results. Moreover, the LMFN achieves higher efficiency compared to other models by applying the outer product as the fusion method.

Recently, microgrids (MGs) have provided different advantages for electrical power systems, but they have created some challenges too. One of the most important challenges is the stability of the MG in islanded operations. To overcome this challenge, energy storage systems (ESSs) can play an effective role. On the other hand, each ESS has distinct characteristics that make them suitable for specific applications in the MG. The suitable cooperation among them can ensure reliable operation of the MG. Moreover, it affects the operation of ESSs and their lifetime. In this paper, cooperation between two types of ESSs (flywheel and battery) is studied. The flywheel ESS, which has high power density, is used during MG transient responses, and the battery ESS responds to long-term load changes. A new control method, based on droop equations, is proposed for each ESS unit. Then, the genetic algorithm is used to obtain the optimal controller coefficients. The simulation results show suitable cooperation between ESS units and stable operation of the MG. Finally, to analyze the proposed method's impact on the stability, a root locus analysis is presented.

In the present era of the world, Stock market has become the place of high risks, but even then it is attracting the mass because of its high return value. Stock market tells about the economy of any country. Today, Stock market has become one of the biggest investment place for general public. In this manuscript we put forward the various forecasting approaches for predicting the BSE SENSEX using various forecasting models like ARIMA, BoxCox, Exponential Smoothing, Mean Forecasting, Naive, Seasonal Naive, Neural Network, and then comparing their mean error for deducing the best suitable model. The analysis is done on the Bombay Stock Exchange(BSE) SENSEX. Results of this analysis shows that, the Exponential smoothing and Neural network gives the best results if we compare the mean error of the both models with the other models.

The concept of the Internet of Things (IoT) has given rise to a new concept called the Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT). In urban environments, decisions concerning our habitat are typically made by democratic or consensus-based methods. Future systems that incorporate IoT and IoRT will involve not just hard elements, but also software and social interactions, resulting in ambiguity and unclear requirements due to the involvement of multiple stakeholders.

To address these wicked problems, this research investigates the area of knowledge co-creation and Problem Structuring Methods (PSM). In the near future, we will be surrounded by software and hardware systems that use collaborative AI or co-dependent AI. Just as we have the science of human to computer interaction, we will soon have distributed social systems interacting with distributed AI.

This study highlights the importance of ethics as a socio-technical element when modeling robotic cities infrastructures. The paper considers full actuation autonomy and control by IoT/IoRT and explores the interdependencies of infrastructure hard-systems, including the addition of software bots and social soft systems into the mix.

Ethics has been a topic of debate in past robotics research, with one school of thought advocating for ethics to be taught to robots and another advocating for ethics to be hard-programmed into robots. A third school of thought examines the philosophical implications of this debate. This research provides definitions and establishes common ground for discussing how we can model our interactions with a distributed AI system, thus replacing the various human experts who currently oversee autonomous cities.

In conclusion, this study proposes a preliminary abstraction resulting from a literature review. It highlights the need to consider ethics as a crucial element when modeling robotic city infrastructures and provides guidelines for future research in this area.

The majority of applicants are unsure about which university and specialty to choose, while graduates with no experience are unfamiliar with how to search for employment. Surprisingly, more than 60% of young specialists in Russia are not practicing their chosen profession, according to data from Rabota.ru. However, businesses today are willing to invest in education, perceiving it to be both a pragmatic staffing problem and a social responsibility. Numerous approaches exist for collaboration between businesses and educational institutions. These include designing educational programs jointly, targeted specialist training in response to company requests, business participation in university endowment funds, and involvement of skilled employees in delivering educational programs. Not only will these measures decrease joblessness in regions, but they will also contribute to overall economic advancement in the country.

With the rising popularity of cloud computing applications, there is an increasing demand for efficient data processing in cloud computing. Users now demand higher quality services from cloud computing, and an effective task scheduling algorithm is crucial to ensuring high efficiency. It is important to find a way to schedule computing resources in the most efficient manner possible in order to complete all tasks in the least amount of time and at the lowest cost. 

In this research paper, a method of optimizing the crossover mutation probability of an adaptive genetic algorithm (AGA) using binary coded chromosomes is proposed. During experiments, the improved AGA is compared to both AGA and the standard genetic algorithm (SGA). The results demonstrate that the improved AGA is an effective cloud computing task scheduling algorithm. 

Therefore, this study is valuable because it explores an effective way to schedule cloud computing tasks. The proposed method optimizes AGA’s crossover mutation probability with binary coded chromosomes, a technique that has been proven to be effective. The experimental results confirmed that the improved algorithm is more efficient than the traditional AGA and SGA. This study contributes significantly to the cloud computing task scheduling algorithm research and can be of great practical use in cloud computing applications.

This paper presents a novel approach for direction of arrival (DOA) estimation using a multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar. The proposed radar, referred to as sparse arrays with flexible inter-element spacing (SA-FIS), utilizes two coprime expansion factors to enlarge the inter-element spacing of transmit and receive arrays. SA-FIS is shown to obtain the maximum unique lags and also suppress mutual coupling effects, making it superior to conventional nested or coprime arrays.

The FIS viewpoint is extended to sparse nonuniform linear arrays, where two-level nested and coprime arrays are employed to increase degrees of freedom. We propose a reduced-complexity two-step sparse representation algorithm to fully utilize the unique lags. By modifying and removing off-diagonal elements of the estimated target covariance matrix, the proposed method can efficiently identify diagonal ones for improved performance with lower computational complexity.

The Cramér-Rao bound on DOAs and correlated coefficients for SA-FIS is derived, and numerical simulations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in terms of DOFs, computation, estimation accuracy, and resolution capability compared to previous approaches. Overall, the SA-FIS MIMO radar offers a flexible and effective solution for DOA estimation of both coherent and uncorrelated targets.

The assisted technological device proposed in this paper is based on Internet of Things (IoT). Internet of things is anticipated to bridge the gap between all physical forms through a basic database in the future. Hence, using this advanced yet simple technology creates a platform, open to improvements in future. The basic functionality of the headset is for the visually impaired people who cannot perceive the upcoming obstacles. The headset not only detects the upcoming obstacle but also processes the distance between the source and the obstacle. The headset is capable in detecting approaching steps or any region of higher altitude and thereby warning the user. We also use new emerging technologies like Image Processing and Video Processing. We use Image Processing for identifying the type of obstacle and Video Processing for finding out the relative velocity. Initially, we have discussed about the working of the basic components of the headset and the process in which they work together. Finally, we have discussed about the prospects this research may contribute to society in the near future. We use different devices like the Raspberry Pi 3, ultrasonic sensors and earpiece. The device we have visualized is quite portable. Neither is it too heavy or too large in size. The model we have envisioned is far from perfect. There are still inputs and modifications which we need to do in the future, to make it completely functional. What we have presented in this paper is just a prototype, a rough sketch of the device we want to make, a device which we believe will make the people's lives a bit easier. We hope that in the future, our research forms the base for several other researches which target to help those in need.

In the task of the unsupervised query by example spoken term detection (QbE-STD), we concatenate the features extracted by a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) and features learned by an unsupervised GMM based model at the feature level to enhance the performance. More specifically, The SOM features are represented by the distances between the current feature vector and the weight vectors of SOM neurons learned in an unsupervised manner. After fetching these features, we apply sub-sequence Dynamic Time Warping (S-DTW) to detect the occurrences of keywords in the test data. We evaluate the performance of these features on the TIMIT English database. After concatenating the SOM features and the GMM based features together, we achieve an improvement of 7.77% and 7.74% on Mean Average Precision (MAP) and P@10 on average.

This paper presents a study on the concept of bounded transparent-scan and its potential to enhance test compaction capabilities. In contrast to conventional multicycle tests, the computational cost of transparent-scan is significantly lower. Transparent-scan considers the scan enable input of a standard-scan circuit as a regular primary input, thereby enabling arbitrary sequences of scan shift and functional capture cycles to be used for test compaction. However, the computational cost of sequential fault simulation over all the clock cycles of the test application process can be disadvantageous. To address this, bounded transparent-scan enables tests to start and end with scan-in and scan-out operations that do not require simulation while allowing arbitrary sequences of scan shift and functional capture cycles between these operations. The paper also presents a test compaction procedure under bounded transparent-scan and experimental results for benchmark circuits to demonstrate its effectiveness.

Emergency events are unpredictable and undesirable situations where the authorities must respond as quick as possible. Smart Emergency Management (SEM) is a machine intelligence concept to help the authorities extract knowledge from Social Big Data (SBD) automatically. This paper proposes a blueprint for machine intelligence based on machine learning for emergency management, applies it to the SEMs lifecycle framework. We present a conceptual-designed Bayesian Network as a contextual model for feature engineering which summarizes and discovers the values from the emergency-related SBD. This paper also discusses the challenges in feature engineering for the SBD-based conceptual model of SEMs.

Neighborhood area networks (NANs) play a vital role in the communication infrastructure of smart grids, enabling communications for numerous applications, including time-critical ones. The communication scenario in a typical NAN involves sending commands from a control center simultaneously to a large number of nodes, demanding low-latency broadcast communications. However, the limited bandwidth and large number of nodes in wireless NANs make this challenging. While general broadcast schemes, such as opportunistic flooding, have been developed for wireless sensor networks, they are not optimized for smart grid NANs that require low-latency and have unique characteristics. Therefore, a new constrained broadcast scheme with minimized latency (CBS-ML) has been proposed in this paper for low-latency NAN communications. CBS-ML constrains the broadcast to a small number of core nodes to avoid traffic congestion. The paper also presents theoretical developments demonstrating how to select core nodes based on network topology and link reliability. Finally, simulations have been conducted to showcase the advantages of CBS-ML.

Monitoring industrial machines can greatly benefit from the capabilities of Cloud Computing and the Internet of Things (IoT). To achieve this, a new approach to machine monitoring, primarily based on the low-cost board Omega2 Plus, has been proposed. The Omega2 Plus is an embedded system designed like a credit card-sized computer that can directly transmit data to the cloud server. In industrial factories, numerous machines perform different functions. Using this approach, machines' logical outputs are coupled with Omega2 Plus GPIO to send data to a web-based server for monitoring purposes. 

The Cloud Monitoring System (CMS) provides real-time data about production, current work status, employee ID, production rate, and downtime. All monitored machines can be overseen by supervisors or specialists in remote locations across the globe. Moreover, this simple system can be operated by untrained personnel employed at the basic level.

The importance of estimating occupancy in public busses is increasing due to its significance for effectively planning transport systems. Real-time bus occupancy data can assist transport companies in better understanding demand, which can result in improved customer satisfaction and long-term route optimization. Occupancy estimation is also beneficial in scenarios where busses replace other modes of public transport such as trains during stoppages. In this article, we present an affordable WiFi-based occupancy estimation system for busses. The proposed algorithm for occupancy estimation successfully addresses the problem of overestimation that occurs in current WiFi-based approaches. The effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed algorithm and WiFi-based occupancy estimation system are validated via a real-world experiment.

This tutorial paper delves into the Internal Model Principle (IMP) from various standpoints. It commences with an overview of the principle's application in control theory and further expands its scope to encompass other spheres where "internal models" are pertinent, with emphasis on biology and neuroscience. The research culminates by presenting a theoretical account of the IMP that is generalizable to a broad spectrum of systems.

Intelligent data analysis involves the analysis of large and unprocessed datasets, which are collected through electronic means. It encompasses the use of advanced algorithms and techniques to uncover hidden patterns and strategies, which can be utilized to classify, categorize, and make informed decisions about the communication between participants in the educational process. Data mining agents are utilized in this stage to determine the communicative strategies of students in the educational environment. This enables quick and efficient recommendations to be made for students on how to organize their learning process, as well as for teachers and methodologists.

An Echo State Network (ESN) is a type of Recurrent Neural Network that is adept at processing time-series data with dynamic behavior. However, when the condition signals are collected by low-cost sensors, the use of ESNs to enhance fault-classification accuracy remains challenging. In this context, a new deep network algorithm, called Deep Hybrid State Network (DHSN), is proposed for fault diagnosis of 3D printers using attitude data with low measurement precision. The DHSN is designed to reinforce features and recognize faults, where the output data of a Sparse Auto-Encoder serves as the abstract features of a Double-Structured ESN (DESN). The DESN comprises two functions, where the first is used for feature reinforcement, and the second for fault classification. This strategy replaces traditional overall feedback fine-tuning in deep models, improving learning efficiency, and overcoming the vanishing-gradient problem for deep learning. Experiments are conducted to evaluate the forecasting performance of the proposed approach, demonstrating its superiority over other intelligent fault-diagnosis technologies.

In recent years, brain hemorrhage has become increasingly prevalent and poses a significant threat to our health. Therefore, it is crucial for doctors to detect and classify brain hemorrhage accurately and efficiently. This paper proposes a new approach that employs convolution neural network technique and Hounsfield Unit values for the analysis of brain hemorrhage from CT/MRI images.

The proposed approach consists of two stages: first, the classification of brain hemorrhage utilizing convolution neural network technique, and second, the detection of brain hemorrhage areas and identification of brain hemorrhage time based on Hounsfield Unit values. The overall method is highly effective as doctors can recognize brain hemorrhage accurately, diagnose its location, time, and severity level, and provide prompt patient treatment.

The new approach employed in this paper is expected to significantly improve the detection and classification of brain hemorrhage. By utilizing convolution neural network technique and Hounsfield Unit values, doctors can diagnose brain hemorrhage quickly and accurately, which is vital for patients with brain hemorrhage. In addition, the proposed method can complement existing imaging techniques, which can improve the overall quality of patient care.

In conclusion, the approach proposed in this paper is an effective method for the automatic detection and classification of brain hemorrhage. With accurate and efficient diagnosis, doctors can treat patients promptly, preventing further complications and saving lives.

To enhance the security of smart meters and prevent electricity theft, an additional anti-tampering feature has been incorporated into the unit. A high definition camera has also been installed to capture pictures and videos of any unauthorized person attempting to cheat electricity billing. This paper investigates three abnormal events; namely, terminal cover opening, smart meter frame opening, and bypassing electrical lines. Using face detection technology, the camera controller unit inside smart meter detects and records the face of any person standing in front of an Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meter. The Haar cascades algorithm powers the face detection mechanism, which is operable for several face angles. As demonstrated in the experimental findings, the proposed system is highly effective and practical for real-world applications.

The cortical learning algorithm (CLA) is a prediction algorithm for time-series data which is based on the human neocortex. It utilizes multiple columns to represent an input data value at a particular time step, where each column has several cells to reflect the time-series context of the input data. While CLA is a popular technique, the traditional approach requires predetermined user-defined parameters for the number of columns and cells, which may not produce optimal results due to varying input data context. As a solution, this research proposes a self-structured cortical learning algorithm that adjusts the columns and cells dynamically based on the input data. Our tests on sine, combined sine, and logistic mapping data reveal that our algorithm produces superior prediction accuracy in comparison to conventional LSTM and CLA approaches. The dynamic adjustment of columns and cells based on input data is a clear improvement, making our self-structured cortical learning algorithm a promising option for time-series data prediction.

Recently, people tend to purchase through websites. This change allows e-commerce sites to collect user behavior data from web logs. E-commerce marketing forces usually make use of such data to come up with subsequent promotional campaign to drive more traffic, and converting into paying customers. In this paper we consider a special kind of e-commerce companies which sell products with similar property and usually at a high price. Therefore, the recommendation becomes less important than prediction of items(if any) bought. We want to discover potential buyers and deliver ads or even coupons to them, expecting them to be real buyers. In this paper, we model the buying behaviors from clicking records with patterns extracted using feature engineering approach. Our solution was to model two kinds of browsing behaviors, namely hesitant and impulsive respectively. In the model, we define some interaction features from click-streams which uncover users' purchase intention with the product pages, how long the user stays on that page, and then build a model which can predict users' preference. Experimental results on a real dataset from an e-commerce company demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The approaches in our work can be used to model user purchasing intent and applied to e-commerce sites which sell high-end products.

Detecting buildings from satellite multispectral imagery data is a challenging task as it requires precise recovery of building footprints from high-resolution images. To address this issue, we propose a deep learning approach for building detection that incorporates several enhancements throughout the process. The initial dataset is preprocessed by applying 2-sigma percentile normalization. Next, we use ensemble modeling that involves the creation of three models while taking into account OpenStreetMap data. Additionally, Binary Distance Transformation (BDT) is used to improve data labeling, and the U-Net is modified by adding batch normalization wrappers.

We explain how each component of our approach is related to achieving higher accuracy in building detection. Finally, we compare our results with the winning solutions of SpaceNet 2 competition for real satellite multispectral images of Vegas, Paris, Shanghai, and Khartoum.
