Our solution demonstrates the importance of accurately detecting buildings from satellite imagery, and the results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed methodology in achieving higher accuracy in building detection.

To reduce delays in accessing real-time data from various applications, such as healthcare and transportation, the usage of Tactile Internet (TI) technology has exponentially increased in recent years. In this paper, we propose a TI-based random forest (RF) learning algorithm for heart disease predictions. The aim is to monitor and analyze human activities for real-time data collection. The proposed approach focuses on analyzing heart ailments and can be used regularly for health monitoring. The RF model is trained to map collected sensor data features to output normal and abnormal states of patients suffering from heart disorders, reducing dependence on input values and covering possible alternate paths. Simulated results demonstrate that the proposed approach reduces average delay while providing faster training times compared to existing conventional techniques.

The Internet of Things (IoT) and connected devices are impacting enterprises, public sector bodies, and citizens in many ways. In parallel, upcoming 5G and Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) are aiming to enable ultra low latency use cases for IoT. This paper proposes to utilize MEC and IoT based architecture for automatic agent reconfiguration in smart manufacturing floors. The EURECOM IoT Platform is extended to achieve this purpose.

The fifth generation (5G) wireless technologies serve as a key propellent to meet the increasing demands of the future Internet of Things (IoT) networks. For wireless communication security in 5G IoT networks, physical-layer security (PLS) has recently received growing interest. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive survey of the PLS techniques in 5G IoT communication systems. The investigation consists of four hierarchical parts. In the first part, we review the characteristics of 5G IoT under typical application scenarios. We then introduce the security threats from the 5G IoT physical-layer and categorize them according to the different purposes of the attacker. In the third part, we examine the 5G communication technologies in 5G IoT systems and discuss their challenges and opportunities when coping with physical-layer threats, including massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO), millimeter wave (mmWave) communications, nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA), full-duplex technology, energy harvesting (EH), visible light communication (VLC), and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications. Finally, we discuss open research problems and future works about PLS in the IoT system with technologies of 5G and beyond.

The presence of phase imbalance in the U.K. and European low-voltage (LV) distribution networks causes additional energy losses, which continue to be a challenge due to the lack of high-resolution time-series data for LV networks. The estimation of imbalance-induced energy losses in LV networks with only the yearly average currents of the three phases remains a significant obstacle. To address the data insufficiency issue, this paper presents a new customized statistical approach known as the clustering, classification, and range estimation (CCRE) approach. 

The proposed approach matches the data-scarce network with only the yearly average phase currents with a cluster of networks with time series of phase current data, which have more data-rich networks. Moreover, CCRE performs a comprehensive range estimation of the imbalance-induced energy loss for the cluster of data-rich networks, which closely resemble the data-scarce network. The range is narrowed down by implementing Chebyshev's inequality, which represents the confidence interval of the imbalance-induced energy loss for the data-scarce network. 

The case study results demonstrate that with limited data from the data-scarce networks, it is feasible to classify over 80% of these networks into the correct clusters, and the confidence of the imbalance-induced energy loss estimates is 89%. The CCRE approach shows promising results and could prove to be effective in estimating the imbalance-induced energy losses in LV networks with limited data.

The quest for evidence-based decision making in hearing health has largely remained unfulfilled up until now. One of the main reasons is that comprehensive information on hearing-health related factors entangled with the opportunity to make objective comparisons between potential interventions. EVOTION is expected to provide a game-change in this area, by developing a Big Data Informed Decision System to support hearing health policy making at several levels. A framework featuring relevant links between hearing health related factors and models, as the latter have been developed in EVOTION, along with their scientifically proven impact is hereby established to facilitate the investigation for more effective hearing health related strategies in the future.

This paper focuses on the real-time object recognition based indoor humanoid robots like Nao robots. Improving the perceptive ability of service robot has always been a research hotspot. The breakthrough of computer vision technology represented by object recognition provides a broader idea for this purpose. We deployed a micro-cloud layer that connects the robot with the computer vision, thereby realized the concepts of RaaS (Robot as a service). In this paper, in order to make the Nao robot to detect objects faster. We present an architecture about real-time object recognition on Nao, and offload the task of control and data collection from robot to a PC. Next, the image data is transmitted over Ethernet to the workstation, which runs multiple parallel image processing services. These services are built with the current popular deep neural network by TensorFlow and running on a GPU GTX1080 Ti. In the micro-cloud layer, we designed a universal robotic visual task queue model, and a PC registers the task queue to the LAN. There are multiple workers in the LAN, and each worker is an independent service processer. Service processer obtains the task queue from the network and processes the queue, and then the processer puts the results back to the manager. The experimental results of the Nao robot in the simulation and real word show that our model and method are effective. The robot can recognize about 90 kinds of common objects, and each frame of image processing time is about 100 milliseconds.

This study presents a novel active contour model (ACM) driven by weighted global and local region-based signed pressure force (SPF) to segment images in the presence of intensity inhomogeneity and noise. First, an adaptive weighted global region-based SPF (GRSPF) function as the driving centers is designed based on the global image information, which is based on the normalized global intensity to update the weights of the inner and outer regions of the curve during iterations. Second, by introducing the normalized absolute local intensity differences as the weighs of the inner and outer regions, an adaptive weighted local region-based SPF (LRSPF) function is similarly defined. Third, instead of setting a fixed force, a force propagation function is introduced to automatically balance the interior and exterior forces according to the image feature. Meanwhile, by combing the adaptive GWSPF and LWSPF functions, a weighted hybrid region-based SPF function is defined, which can improve the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed model. The experimental results on real images demonstrate that the proposed model is more robust than the popular region-based ACMs for segmenting images with intensity inhomogeneity and noise. The code is available at https://github.com/fangchj2002/WHRSPF.

With the exponential growth in the number of mobile devices, providing Internet access via WiFi in trains is rapidly becoming a necessity. However, providing persistent In-ternet access inside a moving train has many challenges. Cellular network is predominantly used for the backhaul connection to the train. However, high deployment cost of a cellular network and presence of coverage holes in the existing cellular networks of telecom companies may dissuade the railway companies to go for such solutions. In this paper, we propose an SDN based architecture to provide Internet connectivity inside trains. The backhaul connection to the train, in the proposed architecture, is provided via WiFi. Deployment of such an architecture is more cost-efficient than that of a cellular network of the same capacity. Moreover, this architecture can also be used to provide connectivity in the coverage holes of the existing networks of the telecom companies. Through simulation, we show that the architecture can provide high throughput while maintaining per packet delay within reasonable limits inside a train.

Securing personal e-health record sharing is an essential measure to address privacy concerns. To this end, we propose a protocol for sharing personal e-health records among multiple parties that eliminates the need for passwords and a third-party provider to execute transactions. Our protocol is based on Fuzzy Clustering scheme, which creates a unique identity for each user. We call this proposed mechanism "Secret handshakes." 

To evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed protocol, we carried out a statistical analysis and performed simulations on IoT boards. The results of both the simulations and experiments demonstrate that the use of Fuzzy Clustering and Secret Handshakes considerably improves the scalability and performance of the protocol. 

Overall, our Secret Handshakes-based Fuzzy Clustering protocol presents a practical solution for addressing privacy issues in personal e-health record sharing. It is an efficient and secure mechanism that effectively secures shared data without the need for passwords and third-party providers.

This paper proposes a method that adopts deep autoencoders with binary distributed hidden units (BDAE) as feature extractors in generatively trained DNNs (GTDNN) for voice conversion (VC). In this method, the source and target speakers are modeled separately by two BDAEs, and the extracted high-level features are used to train a Bernoulli bi-directional associated memory network (BBAM) for feature mapping. Then, the estimated model parameters are copied to construct a DNN for voice conversion. Compared with other neural network-based features extractors, such as deep belief networks (DBN) and conventional deep autoencoders (DAE), BDAEs can obtain a better balance between reconstruction error and the degree of binarization of hidden units. Our experimental results show that the GTDNN using BDAEs achieved better naturalness and similarity of converted speech than the ones using DBNs and conventional DAEs. Further experiments show the BDAE model for target speaker played a more important role than the one for source speaker.

In modern manufacturing systems and industries, there is increasing research focused on recognizing abnormal processes using data-driven models to analyze the manufacturing process. However, it can be challenging to import sequence data into regression and classification models, necessitating the use of feature extraction methods to recognize abnormal processes. With the recent development of deep learning methods, which redefine the processing of raw data through neural network algorithms, researchers are now able to utilize these methods to address raw sensory data. 

This study uses multi-source perception signals from the machining process and applies a CNN algorithm with a convolutional layer to extract information features. BN is used to normalize retention feature information, and pooling layers are employed to reduce the feature matrix. The result is a state prediction model that can identify the degree of tool wear and abnormal states during the machining process. 

A tool wear test is then used to compare the results obtained using the traditional signal processing method with those obtained using the CNN algorithm. The feasibility of the CNN algorithm is demonstrated, marking a significant advancement in the development of state prediction models for use in modern manufacturing systems and industries.

This work focuses on recognizing the unknown emotion based on the “Third-Order Circular Suprasegmental Hidden Markov Model (CSPHMM3)” as a classifier. Our work has been tested on “Emotional Prosody Speech and Transcripts (EPST)” database. The extracted features of EPST database are Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). Our results give average emotion recognition accuracy of 77.8% based on the CSPHMM3. The results of this work demonstrate that CSPHMM3 is superior to the Third-Order Hidden Markov Model (HMM3), Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Vector Quantization (VQ) by 6.0%, 4.9%, 3.5%, and 5.4%, respectively, for emotion recognition. The average emotion recognition accuracy achieved based on the CSPHMM3 is comparable to that found using “subjective assessment by human judges”.

This paper presents two link adaptation techniques aimed at improving the performance of IEEE 802.15.4 wireless personal area networks (WPANs). Both strategies utilize a multi-rate signaling set and select the most appropriate modulation and coding scheme (MCS) based on the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of either a beacon or an acknowledgement (ACK) frame, in order to achieve the target bit error rate (BER) of the end device.

The first strategy, known as the beacon-based link adaptation scheme, is characterized by low complexity and overhead, as it performs link adaptation only once per superframe. Conversely, the ACK-based strategy adapts the link at every ACK frame. This approach provides faster and more effective link adaptation, but with a larger overhead.

To implement these strategies, a specific protocol design is generated by constructing the signal flow based on the service primitives between the protocol stack layers. The network simulator OPNET is used to create an IEEE 802.15.4 WPAN protocol stack and the simulation environment necessary for performance evaluation.

According to simulation results, these link adaptation techniques outperform the conventional WPAN strategy of auto-rate fallback. By exploiting the proposed link adaptation strategies, the received throughput of WPANs is improved.

The maximum value of an antenna array's sidelobe beampattern, or radiation pattern in the power domain, is an important parameter determining its performance. In this paper, when array antenna elements have random phase centers, we approximate the maximum sidelobe value, or peak sidelobe level, as a Gumbel distribution using the extreme value theory (EVT). Before the EVT result, an expression for the beampattern distribution at each angle in the array field of view is found. From this expression, the pointwise convergence of the difference between the beampattern and exponential distributions in the limit of a large number of antennas is obtained. Using the exponential distribution approximation, EVT is applied with samples of the beampattern. A bound is given for the difference between the beampattern sample maximum and its true maximum in the sidelobe region.

This paper discusses the use of computer-assisted human performance training to draw inferences regarding cognitive implications. Drawing upon psycho-neuro-motor control training, which utilizes bio-feedback-like methodologies, models are proposed to better understand and control the cognitive processes involved in improving human performance. Additionally, a case study is presented which explores the training remanence aspect in the short term.

Desirable properties of extensions of non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) include robustness in the presence of noises and outliers, ease of implementation, the guarantee of convergence, operation in an automatic fashion that trades off the balance between data approximation and model simplicity well, and the capability to model the inherently sequential structure of time-series signals. The state-of-the-art methods typically have only a subset of these aforementioned properties and seldom simultaneously possess them all. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that provides all these desirable properties by extending the automatic relevance determination framework in NMF from Tan and Févotte. Starting from an objective function derived from the maximum a posterior estimation of a Bayesian model, we develop majorization-minimization algorithms that work effectively to determine the correct model order, regardless of the impact of noise and outliers. Subsequently, we give a rigorous convergence analysis of the proposed algorithms. Moreover, convolutive bases are also incorporated in the basic model so that it is able to capture the richness of temporal continuity. We perform experiments on both synthetic and real-world data sets to show the efficiency and robustness of our approach.

The Internet of Things (IoT) regulates millions of terabytes of data for everyday commercial, industrial, technical and personal usage. Considered as the greatest technological revolution, all IoT-based transformations are now occurring to increase productivity and create a coordinated world across business and technologies. However, the exchange, storage, processing and transfer of tremendous amounts of sensitive information has also given rise to severe security and privacy concerns that compromise the efficiency and usability of IoT. It has become a challenge for users to depend on such a vulnerable technology, where the IoT security risks outweigh its benefits. Several defense techniques, algorithms and solution models have been proposed and implemented to counter these attacks. However, there are limitations involved as robust incursions make these solutions obsolete. It is vital to have an overview of the research done and find loopholes to fill in the security gaps to ensure a safe IoT ecosystem. Realizing the need of enhanced problem-solving strategies, this paper provides a systematic review of the existing strategies for IoT security and privacy, and provides an analytical approach in identifying the concerns and solutions. It discusses IoT architecture, classifies the various domains of security and privacy and presents a taxonomy and a comparative analysis to outline the security goals, threats and attacks, and solutions proposed in recent years (2015-2018). Our research methodology comprises of thorough qualitative analyses and a literature review to help evaluate the questions asked in this survey. We also highlight the limitations of the previous studies and the open issues. Our survey results focus on the problems that require further attention to improve the IoT progression.

In this paper, we study the problem of achieving average consensus over a random time-varying sequence of directed graphs by extending the class of so-called push-sum algorithms to such random scenarios. Provided that an ergodicity notion, which we term the directed infinite flow property, holds and the auxiliary states of agents are uniformly bounded away from zero infinitely often, we prove the almost sure convergence of the evolutions of this class of algorithms to the average of initial states. Moreover, for a random sequence of graphs generated using a so-called time-varying B-irreducible probability matrix, we establish convergence rates for the proposed push-sum algorithm.

This paper presents a characterization of the air-to-air (A2A) channel for an 802.11-based low altitude network using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Field experiments were conducted to measure user datagram protocol throughput, latency, received signal strength indicator (RSSI), and packet loss. Results showed that latency and packet loss were strongly related to flight stability, while UDP throughput and RSSI demonstrated a related variation trend based on communication distance and altitude. A modified model based on the classical log-distance path loss (PL) model was introduced to describe propagation path loss, showing a decreasing trend of multi-path effect and shadow fading with an increase in altitude. Simulations were conducted to further examine the characterization of A2A channels based on UAVs in short distance and low altitude environments.

In the context of smart cities, the innovative Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) have led to the development of systems aimed at improving the quality of life of citizens by offering a range of public services. This research proposes a smart city approach that leverages these technologies to deliver real-time interaction with citizens and enhance public service delivery. Specifically, we tackle the scalability problem faced by these systems by introducing a service providing framework based on the backend as a service approach on cloud. Our approach ensures that the digital services offered by smart cities are tailored to meet the needs of citizens while effectively handling large workloads. To illustrate the functioning of our approach, we have applied it to the administrative institutions in the city of Biskra.

This paper addresses the control design problem for continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR) systems with input saturation and unknown disturbances. Traditional control schemes and stability analysis are often complicated due to the appearance of the saturated control input within an unknown nonlinearity. In this work, an adaptive state-observer-based tracking controller is presented with only one adaptive parameter using the common Lyapunov function method. An anti-windup compensator is also designed to reduce the influence of actuator saturation. To approximate the unknown dynamics of CSTR, neural networks systems (NNs) are employed based on the universal approximation theorem. In the output feedback, a High-order sliding mode (HOSM) observer is employed to estimate the unmeasured states. The proposed method provides a simple and effective way for constructing the adaptive NN controller for CSTR systems with input nonlinearities, while ensuring the tracking performance and the boundedness of all signals in the closed-loop system. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

With the increasing capabilities and autonomy of smart watches, there is a need to introduce applications that can fully tap into their potential and establish their use in our daily routines. One promising field for developing such applications is personal safety and security. Smart watches could be utilized as tools for easy, discreet, and efficient reporting of incidents or suspicious behavior. However, current practices in report creation using smart watches reliant on methods and interfaces such as taking pictures and writing text, neglect gesture-based input.

This paper presents a smart watch-based approach that employs a Deep Learning model to recognize specific user gestures that could result in reporting hazardous situations and alerting authorities for assistance. We evaluated the model's performance by training it to distinguish 5 predefined gestures from a set of random gestures performed by 9 subjects wearing a smart watch on their dominant arm. By fusing automatically extracted features of 3-axial accelerometer signals, our Deep Learning model surpassed conventional classifiers' performances that relied on hand-crafted features, achieving gesture recognition accuracies above 98% in 26,061 motion signal samples.

Our proposed application faced related issues when used in real-time and requires future directions. However, employing Deep Learning techniques to recognize user gestures for reporting hazardous situations provides a promising foundation for developing smarter and safer communities.

To improve the accuracy of surface electromyography (sEMG)-based gesture recognition, we present a novel hybrid approach that combines real sEMG signals with corresponding virtual hand poses. The virtual hand poses are generated by means of a proposed cross-modal association model constructed based on the adversarial learning to capture the intrinsic relationship between the sEMG signals and the hand poses. We report comprehensive evaluations of the proposed approach for both frame- and window-based sEMG gesture recognitions on seven-sparse-multichannel and four-high-density-benchmark databases. The experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves significant improvements in sEMG-based gesture recognition compared to existing works. For frame-based sEMG gesture recognition, the recognition accuracy of the proposed framework is increased by an average of +5.2% on the sparse multichannel sEMG databases and by an average of +6.7% on the high-density sEMG databases compared to the existing methods. For window-based sEMG gesture recognition, the state-of-the-art recognition accuracies on three of the high-density sEMG databases are already higher than 99%, i.e., almost saturated; nevertheless, we achieve a +0.2% improvement. For the remaining eight sEMG databases, the average improvement with the proposed framework for the window-based approach is +2.5%.

Recent research into radio propagation and large-scale channel modeling has shown that frequencies above 6 GHz can be utilized for the new generation of mobile communications (5G). This paper presents a detailed account of measurement campaigns that were conducted using directional horn antennas in both co-polarization (V-V and H-H) and cross-polarization (V-H) scenarios, in line-of-sight (LOS) and obstructed-line-of-sight situations between transmitters and receivers. These measurements were carried out in a corridor and a computer laboratory situated at the Federal University of Para (UFPA).

The measurement data gathered during these campaigns were used to adjust path loss prediction models of radio propagation specifically for indoor environments within the frequencies of 8-11 GHz. The minimum mean square error (MMSE) method was applied to determine the parameters for the models, including path loss exponent (PLE), polarization exponent for both co- and cross-polarization channels, as well as effects of shadowing and wall losses. Statistical metrics such as standard deviation and standard deviation point by point were also included.

The results showed that the path loss models for frequencies of 8-11 GHz were adequately optimized, with the approximations closely converging with the measured data. The use of the MMSE method proved critical to the accuracy of the model parameters for indoor environments with potential applications for future 5G networks.

In recent years, the proliferation of modern technologies has led to the capturing and recording of vast data sets across various fields. However, it has also raised concerns about how to ensure the protection and security of this data during storage, transmission, processing, and access. The blockchain, a distributed ledger, provides a secure, flexible, verifiable, and permanent way to record transactions. These transactions can include asset exchanges, smart contract executions, or updates to records. Our research has resulted in a blockchain access control ecosystem that enables asset owners to have the sovereign right to manage access control of large data sets and prevent data breaches. To achieve this, we utilize the Linux Foundation's Hyperledger Fabric blockchain to power the business network, and the Hyperledger composer modeling tool to implement smart contracts and transaction processing functions on the blockchain network.

Communication is often regarded as one of the most expensive aspects of a wireless sensor node. As a result, numerous technologies and protocols have been developed to reduce energy consumption, particularly for the Internet of Things context. To aid in the selection of the most appropriate technology for a particular use case, a tool that enables comparison of these options is essential. This paper presents a new modular modeling framework that facilitates the comparison of various technologies based on analytical calculations. We focused on modeling the cost for a single data transfer with any application data size to provide flexibility with respect to the data amount and traffic patterns. Compared to other approaches, our modeling method encompasses the entire stack traversal of application data, including the required protocol overhead. By applying our models to different data amounts, we can identify tradeoffs between various technologies and enable comparisons under varied scenarios. Furthermore, our results underscore the impact of design choices, which can assist in identifying future development challenges.

Despite recent advancements in autonomous vehicle technology, it is still crucial to determine a driver's ability to operate a vehicle in case of a failure of the autonomous system. Accurately analyzing a driver's brain activity in real-time can help identify when they are not capable of driving safely, and prompt countermeasures to prevent accidents. This research presents a brain-computer interface (BCI) that uses functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to detect prefrontal cortex activity and a deep neural network (DNN) for classification. The fNIRS data is pre-processed by applying a high-pass filter and the least-squares method to remove noise. The DNN then analyses the time-series input vector extracted from the pre-processed signals to recognize the current driving mode (manual or autopilot) of the user. The study shows that the DNN-based classification of fNIRS signals has the potential to develop BCIs for monitoring mental states, with an average classification accuracy of 61.7%.

The new technological applications and the advancement of communication have allowed the generation of new applications for sending and receiving data, using low power and reduced costs, thus achieving the implementation of the Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). These networks allow the generation of measurements and analysis of data of short, medium and high scale, for which they have been taken in this investigation, obtaining a communication and sending of information, based on the following levels that are: Beginning of data transmission, process of the sending and receiving of the information received by the Gateway, storage of information and visualization and generation of information reports. In the transmission of data from nodes one and two to the Gateway, it was analyzed that the energy consumption in each sensor is approximately 74.4% (node 1) and 86.8% (node 2) on a bi-monthly basis. that the sensor one needs to be charged 5 times a year, while node 2 needs to be charged 4 times.

A multi-tenant Software as a Service (SaaS) application is a highly configurable software that allows its owner to serve multiple tenants, each with their own workflows, workloads and Service Level Objectives (SLOs). Tenants are usually organizations that serve several users and the application appears to be a different one for each tenant. However, in practice, multi-tenant SaaS applications limit the diversity of tenants by clustering them in a few categories (e.g. premium, standard) with predefined SLOs. Additionally, this coarse-grained clustering reduces the advantage of these multi-tenant ecosystems over single tenant architectures to share dynamically virtual resources between tenants based on their own workload profile and elasticity adaptation decisions. To address this limitation, we propose a multi-agent elasticity management where each tenant is represented by a reinforcement learning agent that performs elasticity adaptations based on a new technical debt perspective, and make use of debt attributes (i.e. amnesty, interest) to form autonomous coalitions that minimise the effect of the unavoidable imperfections in any elasticity management approach. We extended CloudSim and Burlap to evaluate our approach. The simulation results indicate that our debt-aware multi-agent elasticity management preserves the diversity of tenants and reduces SLO violations without affecting the aggregate utility of the application owner.

The combination of smart home platforms and automation apps introduce many conveniences to smart home users. However, this also brings the potential of privacy leakage. If a smart home platform is permitted to collect all the events of a user day and night, then the platform will learn the behavior patterns of this user before long. In this paper, we investigate how IFTTT, one of the most popular smart home platforms, has the capability of monitoring the daily life of a user in a variety of ways that are hardly noticeable. Moreover, we propose multiple ideas for mitigating privacy leakages, which all together form a “Filter-and-Fuzz” (F&F) process: first, it filters out events unneeded by the IFTTT platform. Then, it fuzzifies the values and frequencies of the remaining events. We evaluate the F&F process and the results show that the proposed solution makes the IFTTT unable to recognize any of the user's behavior patterns.

In this manuscript, an alternative system for finding a human position, known as the IPS technique, is introduced to overcome the limitations of the current GPS system. The projected method presented in this manuscript addresses the issues faced by GPS when an individual moves indoors or enters areas with poor signal connectivity. While the present GPS structure provides us with the necessary direction for people's location, its accuracy is limited under certain circumstances. With the IPS technique, individuals will have access to more accurate and reliable position tracking regardless of their location or signal connectivity.

This paper details the efforts taken towards the creation of an intelligent, network-enabled embedded system that aids in the acquisition and analysis of data concerning traffic movements. The article outlines the various components that constitute the sensor system and elaborates on their interaction. The design of the system is such that supplementary sensors can be added to complement the magnetic field sensors that are currently in use. The article also covers the testing procedures that were carried out both in laboratory conditions and in field trials on actual roads. The results of the experiments are presented in this paper.

Image similarity is a core concept in Image analysis due to its extensive application in computer vision. Our study of Quasi Euclidean distance metric displayed a potential in the metric viz-a-viz image similarity computation. Here, it has been used to calculate similarity between input images and images generated by the generative model, Wasserstein Auto-Encoder. Standard GANs are great generative models, but has the concerned training instability. Therefore, we have used Wasserstein Auto-Encoder, which also has proven to generate more accurate images, to produce images on which the performance of the metric has been observed.

Software Defined Network (SDN) is a new network construction. But due to its construction, SDN is vulnerable to be attacked by Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack. So it is important to detect DDoS attack in SDN network. This paper presents a DDoS detection scheme based on k-means algorithm in SDN environment. The establishment of this scheme is based on the two hypotheses that the daily network works normally most of the time, and there is a significant difference between the data characteristics of normal situation and abnormal situation. At the same time, these two hypotheses are also true to the daily network condition. After demonstrating the validity of k-means clustering algorithm, the paper proposes 5 flow table features that can be used to detect DDoS attacks. Finally, the DDoS detection scheme was tested by simulation experiment. The test results showed that the method proposed by the author could effectively detect DDoS, with an average success rate of 97.78%.

We propose UnLearnerVO, a jointly unsupervised learning framework for monocular depth, camera motion estimation from videos. UnLearnerVO is coupled with the relationships of 3D scene geometry and can estimate the 6-DoF pose of a monocular camera in an end-to-end pattern. There are two significant features of the proposed UnLearnerVO: one is an unsupervised depth learning pipeline based on the consecutive /inconsecutive frames, and the other is robustness in a scenario with large camera motion. Specifically, we deeply excavate the pose loop consistency loss, thus optimizing the camera pose and enforcing consistency of the estimated poses across consecutive and inconsecutive frames. Furthermore, a photometric loop consistency loss is proposed, which reduces the disturbance caused by factors such as the dynamic motion object and the photo inconsistency. The experiments on KITTI datasets show that our UnLearnerVO achieves the state-of-the-art results in large camera motion scenarios and performs better than the currently popular unsupervised approaches.

Most of the published research work mainly emphasizes one aspect of knowledge graph construction in isolation and neglects the big data processing flow in this process, which lacks of value in the practical construction of knowledge graph. Therefore, the paper proposes a construction method of domain knowledge graph based on big data-driven and build an artificial intelligence domain knowledge graph to prove the feasibility of this method, which covers artificial intelligence enterprises, patents, news, technology labels and other entities.

Traffic congestion is recognized as a significant problem in modern urban cities, and Jordan is considered one of the top countries worldwide in terms of frequency of traffic accidents. The increase in the number of vehicles on the roads has led to a rise in the number of traffic incidents, resulting in an increase in fatalities and injuries. Despite this, the current traffic signals system in Jordan is still controlled by fixed timers.

To address this issue, an Intelligent Road Traffic Management System based on Human Community Genetic Algorithm (IRTMS) has been proposed. The IRTMS was compared to the current traffic system in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan and found to have a minimum total time and waiting time compared to the current traffic lights system.

This automated road traffic management system employs genetic algorithms to generate optimized traffic light timings. The algorithm works by mimicking the natural selection process that is responsible for the evolution of species where the fittest individuals survive and the weaker ones perish. In the same way, the genetic algorithm selects the optimal timings that can accommodate the maximum number of vehicles passing through a particular intersection.

The IRTMS considers the real-time traffic conditions, such as the number of vehicles, their speeds, and the road network layout. This information is collected from various sources, including roadside sensors, surveillance cameras, and GPS-equipped vehicles. The system then processes all this data and calculates the optimal traffic signal timings.

The IRTMS has several advantages over the current traffic signals system. Firstly, it reduces traffic congestion by minimizing the waiting time for vehicles at intersections. Secondly, it minimizes the total time spent by vehicles at intersections, thereby reducing fuel consumption and air pollution. Thirdly, it improves traffic flow, reduces travel time, and enhances road safety by minimizing the potential for traffic accidents.

In conclusion, the Intelligent Road Traffic Management System based on Human Community Genetic Algorithm (IRTMS) is a promising approach to address traffic congestion and improve road safety in modern urban cities. By utilizing real-time traffic data and optimizing traffic signal timings, this system has the potential to reduce waiting times for vehicles, minimize total time spent at intersections, and improve traffic flow, ultimately leading to safer roads and a better quality of life for citizens.

Statically balanced spring mechanisms are widely used in various applications that play an important role in our daily lives. However, designing new mechanisms poses a significant challenge for designers as they must consider numerous factors such as the number of springs, their connectivity, attachment points, and other parameters. To address this problem, we propose a new optimization-driven approach to designing statically balanced mechanisms that is both interactive and semi-automatic.

Our approach is based on the principle of constant potential energy, which allows us to efficiently optimize the design of these mechanisms. Additionally, we have developed an automated sparsification method that simplifies spring topology design and a null-space exploration scheme that enables users to easily navigate the design space alternatives. Through a series of simulation examples and prototypes, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our design system.

Overall, our proposed optimization-driven approach presents an innovative solution to the challenging problem of designing statically balanced spring mechanisms. By offering designers increased levels of interactivity and automation, we believe our approach has the potential to revolutionize the field of mechanism design.

Short-duration text-independent speaker verification has been a popular research topic in recent years. Deep neural network-based embeddings have shown impressive results in such conditions. To achieve more discriminant speaker embeddings, we propose new approaches. Within the cascade framework, a neural network-based deep discriminant analysis is proposed to project i-vector to more discriminative embeddings. Within the direct embedding framework, a deep model with more advanced center loss and A-softmax loss is used, and the focal loss is also investigated. Additionally, traditional i-vector and neural embeddings are combined with neural network-based DDA to achieve further gain. Main experiments are carried out on a short-duration text-independent speaker verification dataset generated from the SRE corpus. The results show that the newly proposed method is promising for short-duration text-independent speaker verification and consistently better than traditional i-vector and neural embedding baselines. The best embeddings achieve roughly 30% relative EER reduction compared to the i-vector baseline, which could be further enhanced when combined with the i-vector system.

This paper focuses on a novel category of problems that leverage recent evidence of the fundamental links between information theory and estimation theory in noisy network-coded flows [1]. The study addresses the network modeled by a directed graph G=(V,E), under the assumption of uncorrelated noise over information flows between the directed links that connect transmitters, switches (relays), and receivers. Results reveal that closed-form connections exist in terms of the gradient of the mutual information concerning different components of the system matrix M of the forward and reciprocal networks, as well as the minimum mean square error (MMSE), known as the network I-MMSE. On one hand, these results enable analyzing the impacts of the error propagation and backward traceability in relation to topological modifications when nodes move or become "ad-hoc," influencing the network's capability. On the other hand, the research highlights compensation methods where a modification in the precoding process can be an alternative to adjusting the network topology or vice versa. The paper provides optimal precoding designs that cater to the network level, optimizing information flows and adapting to the network topology awareness. It's worth noting that this study is the first to demonstrate the inadequacy of RLNC in optimally managing topology awareness. In this regard, it highlights that deterministic matrix-based DLNC is optimal for a network topology.

This paper presents a new technique that dynamically estimates and updates the coefficients of a digital predistorter (DPD) for power amplifier (PA) linearization. The proposed technique is dynamic in the sense of estimating, at every iteration of the coefficient's update, only the minimum necessary parameters according to a criterion based on the residual estimation error. At the first step, the original basis functions defining the DPD in the forward path are orthonormalized for DPD adaptation in the feedback path by means of a precalculated principal component analysis (PCA) transformation. The robustness and reliability of the precalculated PCA transformation (i.e., PCA transformation matrix obtained off line and only once) is tested and verified. Then, at the second step, a properly modified partial least squares (PLS) method, named dynamic partial least squares (DPLS), is applied to obtain the minimum and most relevant transformed components required for updating the coefficients of the DPD linearizer. The combination of the PCA transformation with the DPLS extraction of components is equivalent to a canonical correlation analysis (CCA) updating solution, which is optimum in the sense of generating components with maximum correlation (instead of maximum covariance as in the case of the DPLS extraction alone). The proposed dynamic extraction technique is evaluated and compared in terms of computational cost and performance with the commonly used QR decomposition approach for solving the least squares (LS) problem. Experimental results show that the proposed method (i.e., combining PCA with DPLS) drastically reduces the amount of DPD coefficients to be estimated while maintaining the same linearization performance.

Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is increasingly important for ensuring system reliability and safety in various industrial fields. Deep convolutional neural network (CNN) has shown great potential for RUL prediction, and this paper proposes an intelligent RUL prediction method based on a double-CNN model architecture. The method utilizes the powerful feature extraction capability of CNN and is fed with original vibration signals without the need for feature extractors, maximizing the retention of useful information. The prediction involves two stages: identification of the incipient fault point using the first CNN model and a proposed “3/5” principle, followed by RUL prediction using the second CNN model. In practice, predicting the RUL of identical components is challenging. To overcome this challenge, an intermediate reliability variable is first calculated and used to map to RUL using a proposed mapping algorithm. The proposed method was evaluated using data from four tests of bearing degradation, and showed higher prediction accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method in RUL prediction.

Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) is a crucial technology that enables arbitrary computations to be performed directly on encrypted data, ensuring the security of cloud computing. This paper proposes an innovative approach to reduce the computation complexity of encrypted data by utilizing the concept of aggregate plaintext. Unlike existing works that encrypt plaintext in bit level, this approach achieves an efficient scheme to handle the comparison and swap operation, which is widely used for sorting and searching in cloud computing.

The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme not only reduces the required FHE data size, but also enhances the total computation time of the selected operation. Specifically, for 32-bit data comparison, the proposed scheme can operate 2.3 times faster, resulting in a significant reduction in the required FHE data size, as well as the transmission bandwidth to the cloud, by approximately 52 times compared to the related work. 

In conclusion, this paper presents a groundbreaking approach to reduce the computation complexity of encrypted data in cloud computing by utilizing the concept of aggregate plaintext. The experimental results show that the proposed scheme is highly efficient and can serve as a significant improvement over existing methods for sorting and searching operations in cloud computing.

The use of image processing technology for sports is increasing. By analyzing athletes and teams based on video analysis, scientific and objective analysis can be conducted separately from subjective analysis of experts, and individuals or teams can be evaluated with the same index. As can be seen from such a trend, recently, technological progress has made it possible to detect and analyze what can be visually confirmed in the sports video. It is certain that these technologies are helping coaches in the analysis of movement. However, these cannot play the role of coaches. The role is to judge what is important from what can be visually confirmed. There are also empirical and qualitative parts in coach's judgment, and no reproducibility of understanding the important parts unless it is a specialist. Based on this background, we thought that it would be useful to extract more important scenes during the game using quantitative information. Such technology can be applied to various sports, but this paper, we focused on tennis. In this thesis, the aim is to estimate which play was largely contributed to the tennis game result (score, failure). In addition, we don't use supervised information that can be obtained from an empirical point of view. This is to eliminate dataset dependency caused by using data created from qualitative information. Specifically, based on quantitative information such as athletes' movement and score result, we attempted to estimate the attention from unsupervised method.

A new feature-based forecasting framework of abnormalities is presented for early warning for cyber-physical control systems. The abnormalities may refer to intelligent cyber-attacks or naturally occurring faults and failures. Techniques presented here are aimed at protecting against unauthorized intrusions as well as fault prevention. Time series signals from system monitoring nodes are converted to features using feature discovery techniques. The feature behavior for each monitoring node is characterized in the form of decision boundaries, separating normal and abnormal space with operating data collected from the plant or by running virtual models of the plant. A set of ensemble state-space models are constructed for representing feature evolution in time-domain, where the ensembles are selected using Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering. The forecasted outputs are anticipated time-evolution of features, computed by applying an adaptive Kalman predictor to each ensemble model. The overall features forecast is then obtained through dynamic ensemble averaging. This is done by projecting evolution of feature vector to future times in a receding horizon fashion. The features forecast are compared to the decision boundary to estimate if/when the feature vectors will cross the boundary. Simulation results in a high fidelity GE gas turbine platform, show the effectiveness of our approach for forecasting abnormalities.

This paper presents a novel channel estimation scheme for massive multiple input multiple output (MIMO) millimeter wave (mmWave) communication system with massive uniform linear array (ULA) at base station (BS) and hybrid architecture. Through practical channel modeling, each channel path is composed of angle information and channel gain information that can be estimated separately. We first propose a general iterative index detection-based channel estimation algorithm (IDCEA) that can obtain both direction of arrival (DOA) and channel gain of each channel path. We then design an enhanced hybrid precoding scheme from the angle domain viewpoint to reduce the inter-beam interferences. Simulation results show that the proposed channel estimation can be better than traditional methods. Finally, numerical examples are provided to corroborate the proposed studies.

In today changing world, Internet of Things (IoT) is creating a new world, where people and businesses can make more timely and better informed decisions about what they want or need to do. Over the last years, agriculture industry in few countries has been expended to smart agriculture. Nevertheless, the agricultural site in Myanmar needs to be technologically advanced with the practice of IoT techniques to provide smart agriculture. But, most of the existing IoT middleware are built to be used by IT professional because of the difficulty of IoT middleware. To admit end users (non-IT professional) to configure the IoT middleware efficiently and effectively, the IoT middleware need to be fully supported network, syntactic and semantic interoperable requirements without recognizing the latent technical details of heterogeneous sensors and devices. In this paper, we propose an interoperable and configurable middleware that incorporates IoT and semantic web techniques with the existing Global Sensor Network middleware to solve the above challenges. The proposed IoT middleware will be implemented and evaluated mainly in plant growth and yields of agriculture area of Myanmar with different types of users and in addition, more diverse services in agricultural domain.

Ultra-wideband (UWB) radars which are mainly focused on contactless detection of breath, heartbeat and other biological signals are generally referred to as biometric radars. It is expecting that these radars will find a whole range of applications from the medical field, through supporting emergency situation solution, up to monitoring people in their dwelling (e.g. ambient assisted living programs). Motivated by promising applications of biometric radars, we will focus in this paper on contactless measurement of breathing frequency and heart rate of static persons by UWB radar. At first, the algorithm for the estimation of the breathing frequency of a person will be outlined. Then, the main emphasis will be placed on the development of an efficient approach for the heart rate estimation. The proposed solution will include radar signal processing procedure for static person ranging, methods for improvement of low-level echo of target-to-clutter and noise ratio (exponential averaging, low-pass filter, Savitzky-Golay filter and single delay line canceller), and finally the heart rate estimation itself (peak-to-average power ratio, Welch periodogram). The good performance of the proposed algorithms will be illustrated by experimental results.

This paper introduces the modeling and simulation of a spherical autonomous underwater vehicle that was developed for the exploration of underground flooded mines as part of the European Union H2020 innovation action UNEXMIN. The robot is equipped with thrusters and an internal pendulum for pitch control. Initially, a model of the vehicle is presented without the pendulum, followed by an extended formulation that accounts for a multibody dynamic description of the system. Additionally, experimental identification results for the determination of drag parameters are presented. To enable dynamic simulation of the vehicle, a Modelica based simulator is developed and integrated with the Matlab/Simulink environment. The simulator is then validated based on preliminary experimental results.

Shrimp is one of the most important aquaculture products in Taiwan but has suffered a decreasing breeding rate these recent years. It's difficult to observe their feeding, growth and health due to the muddy and turbid water conditions in shrimp farms. This paper presents the prototype of an underwater surveillance system, which consists of hardware and software to provide underwater observation and automatic analysis for the purpose of smart feeding control and water quality management, and thus improve the farm's productivity.

Managing trust in mobile networks requires addressing uncertainty arising from incomplete, duplicate or conflicting evidence. This study employs possibility theory to handle such uncertainty, developing a trust model that includes nodes' integrity, competency, and connections amongst them. Direct observation and active solicitation from other nodes generate possibility distributions (trust profiles) that can be updated and combined. Simulations of mobile ad hoc networks demonstrate that trust profiles in routing decisions conserve network resources and limit data exposure. Possibility theory facilitates evaluating information gained from different evidence forms, indicating that active trust evidence from authentication requests provides higher informational value than reputation solicitation. It is observed that passive evidence is inadequate in maintaining low-uncertainty trust profiles.

This study explores the concept of classification through dictionary learning, proposing a novel framework that optimizes both the components of a dictionary and a graph Laplacian. The framework, called self-taught semisupervised dictionary learning with nonnegative constraint, incorporates an atom graph Laplacian regularization that utilizes sparse coefficients to capture the underlying manifold structure. This regularization results in improved robustness to noise and outliers due to the atoms being more concise and representative than training samples. Additionally, a nonnegative constraint is imposed on sparse coefficients to ensure that each sample is in the middle of its related atoms, making the dependency between samples and atoms explicit. The framework also incorporates a self-taught mechanism to feed back the manifold structure induced by atom graph Laplacian regularization and the supervised information hidden in unlabeled samples to improve dictionary learning. The efficient algorithm used to optimize the unified framework combines a block coordinate descent method with the alternating direction method of multipliers. The experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

Monolithic 3D (M3D) integration brings notable advantages in terms of performance, power, and area. However, designing a reliable power-delivery network (PDN) for M3D is quite challenging since it requires dealing with high power density and current demand per unit area. To address this issue accurately, we suggest a framework that incorporates electrical and reliability models to design a dependable PDN for M3D ICs. We employ genetic programming to explore the design space and optimize the PDN for M3D. Moreover, to take the power-supply noise (PSN) into account during scan-based testing, we conduct a thorough analysis and compare it with the functional operation. The study quantifies the impact of PSN during the scan-based testing on the yield loss. Our results manifest that the PDN derived from the proposed approach enhances the reliability of at least 40% of the wire segments in the PDN substantially. The proposed PDN design reduces the worst-case power-supply droop by 50.5% compared to the baseline PDN. Additionally, our proposed design has resulted in significantly lower yield loss due to power-supply droop in comparison to the baseline.

In this work, we present a low-power receiver architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (WIPT) applications. The WIPT concept is designed for energy-constrained wireless nodes, without compromising the receiver's information performance characteristics. We aim to use digital modulation techniques suitable for 5G-oriented internet-of-things (IOT).

With the diplexer-based six-port receiver, we demonstrate that dedicated wireless power transfer is achievable in conjunction with simultaneous wireless information transfer. A multiport power recycling method is employed to exploit the unwanted harmonic signals arising from power detectors and signal interferers.

Our proposed receiver architecture enables efficient power management while ensuring high-quality information transmission. It offers a viable solution for powering energy-limited wireless devices in emerging IOT infrastructures.

With the introduction of Internet of Things (IoT), we are witnessing the greater use of the mobile Internet with the exponential explosion of smartphones, tablets, and laptops. The IoT paradigm is revolutionizing the way we live, work, and communicate. In this context, the availability of a connectivity technology, which is reliable, scalable, and efficient, will play a major role to develop the emerging IoT system. Certainly, the fifth generation (5G) networks are emerging as the key enabler supporting IoT systems. In this paper, we discuss the potential of 5G technologies and architecture for the future IoT systems. We review the main 5G enablers for the IoT systems. Besides, we also extensively discussed the security and privacy aspect of IoT system and the potential research directions.

Most conventional techniques for supervised classification of polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) imagery involve manually selecting a large number of samples, and the quality and size of these samples can considerably impact the accuracy of the classification results. In this paper, we present an improved deep Q-network (DQN) approach for PolSAR image classification that generates vast amounts of valid data by involving the agent in the ε-greedy scheme. The PolSAR information undergoes preprocessing to decrease the impact of speckle noise and to uplift the multidimensional features. The training image and the multidimensional feature image are then fed into a deep reinforcement learning model that is specifically designed for PolSAR image classification. After various rounds of training, the method was used to identify different types of land cover in two PolSAR images that were acquired from different sensors. The experimental outcomes indicate that the proposed approach achieves a better classification performance compared to traditional supervised classification techniques such as convolutional neural network (CNN), random forest (RF), and L2-loss linear support vector machine (L2-SVM). Furthermore, the method has a remarkable performance compared to CNN-SVM, a deep learning method that incorporates the synergy between the SVM and CNN techniques, especially in small sample sizes. This study also offers a toolset for DQN (kiwi.server) on the GitHub development platform for training and visualization.

Multimedia researchers have exploited large collections of community-contributed geo-referenced images to better understand a particular image, such as its subject matter or where it was taken, as well as to better understand a geographic location, such as the most visited tourist spots in a city or what the local cuisine is like. The goal of this paper is to better understand location. In particular, we use geo-referenced image collections to better understand what occurs in different parts of a city at fine spatial and activity class scales. This problem is known as land use mapping in the geographical sciences. We propose a novel framework to perform fine-grained land use mapping at the city scale using ground-level images. Mapping land use is considerably more difficult than mapping land cover and is generally not possible using overhead imagery as it requires close-up views and seeing inside buildings. We postulate that the growing collections of geo-referenced, ground-level images suggest an alternate approach to this geographic knowledge discovery problem. We develop a general framework that uses Flickr images to map 45 different land-use classes for the city of San Francisco, CA, USA. Individual images are classified using a novel convolutional neural network containing two streams: one for recognizing objects and another for recognizing scenes. This network is trained in an end-to-end manner directly on the labeled training images. We propose several novel strategies to overcome the noisiness of our user-generated data including search-based training set augmentation and online adaptive training. We derive a ground truth map of San Francisco in order to evaluate our method. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through geovisualization and quantitative analysis. Our framework achieves over 29% recall at the individual land parcel level that represents a strong baseline for the challenging 45-way land use classification problem, especially given the noisiness of the image data.

As an integral part of Chinese painting and calligraphy, seals not only possess immense artistic value but also provide important information about the artwork. In today's digital age, it is crucial to represent seals in a digital format while also utilizing image processing techniques for better understanding. With advancements in deep learning, convolutional neural networks are widely employed in feature learning, object localization, and classification. This article introduces the highly accurate Chinese Seal Recognition System (CSRS) based on deep learning technology. The CSRS comprises three units, namely a new Siamese network with multi-task learning, an automatic background generation algorithm, and a training method for Siamese network based on central constraint. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, two large-scale seal image databases have been established, and the results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other variants. The proposed method has significant potential for practical applications in Chinese seal recognition.

A key idea in improving color images in extremely low-light conditions is to merge noisy and blurred images in the color image sequence by using Close Infrared (NIR) images captured in such lighting conditions. Captured images in extremely low-light conditions often produce heavy noise and motion blur. Our objective is to enhance the color image sequence of an extremely low-light scene. In order to expand the imaging system and enhance the image fusion scheme in this project, we propose a novel imaging system that can simultaneously capture Red, Green, Blue (RGB) and NIR images with different exposure times. An RGB image is captured with a long exposure time to obtain sufficient color information and reduce the effects of heavy noise. On the other hand, NIR images are captured with a short exposure time to estimate the scene’s structure. Our imaging system, using different exposure times, enables us to ensure sufficient information to reproduce a realistic color image sequence. Using the captured image sets, we reconstruct a latent color image sequence using an adaptive smoothness condition based on gradient and color relationships. Our trials using both synthetic and real image sequences demonstrate that our method surpasses other state-of-the-art techniques.

We have examined how people use qualitative models to reason about the continuous world. In exploring how analogy interacts with qualitative representations to simulate based on experience (chapter 12), we have seen the beginnings of how such knowledge might be learned. This chapter delves into learning and conceptual change in more detail. I start by laying out the broad theory that Dedre Gentner and I have been building about the range of types of human representations that get constructed in the course of learning in physical domains. Then I will drill down into particul ar aspects of this framework, beginning with how prototypical behavi ors are constructed and used to build initial qualitative models. Because many of our concepts come from our culture, rather than discovered on our own, a model for conceptual change is described that accounts for how models are changed in response to new information. The use of analogy to learn expert models, both within and across domains, is also discussed.

An intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has the ability to adjust the phase shifts of its reflecting units to enhance the desired signal and weaken the undesired signal. This article investigates the use of an IRS in a secure wireless communication system where a multi-antenna access point (AP) sends confidential messages to a user with a single antenna in the presence of an eavesdropper with a single antenna. The scenario considered is one where the eavesdropping channel is stronger than the legitimate communication channel and they are highly correlated in space. The aim is to maximize the secrecy rate of the legitimate communication link by jointly designing the AP's transmit beamforming and the IRS's reflect beamforming.

However, the resultant optimization problem is complex to solve. To overcome this, an efficient algorithm is proposed which obtains high-quality suboptimal solutions by using alternating optimization and semidefinite relaxation methods. The simulation results indicate that the proposed design significantly improves the secrecy communication rate in the setup considered, as compared to scenarios where the IRS is not used. The proposed algorithm also performs better than a heuristic scheme.

In summary, the article illustrates the potential benefits of using an IRS for secure wireless communication systems. The efficient algorithm proposed by the authors can provide suboptimal solutions, which can improve the secrecy rate performance of the system. Overall, this research is a step forward in exploring the use of intelligent reflecting surfaces in enhancing wireless communication security.

As SoC (System-on-Chip) complexity continues to increase, the need for function and performance verification becomes crucial in the middle of the design process to minimize the potential risks, ranging from over-design to non-compliance with the design specifications, until the tape-out phase. In this paper, we propose a seamless SoC verification methodology that utilizes modern virtual platform (VP) technology. The proposed methodology harnesses the capabilities of high-level C++ firmware, SystemC models with timing-accurate characteristics, and RTL (register-transfer level) designs, enabling full-chip level verification at all stages of the development process. This paper presents experimental results that demonstrate the benefits and valuable insights of using virtual platforms for SoC verification.

The major drawback of surface electromyography (sEMG) is the considerable number of electrodes it requires, rendering its practical application undesirable. As a solution, this study aimed to investigate the effectiveness of a proposed sEMG-based speech recognition system in classifying 12 Thai syllables by reducing the number of electrodes. The study involved collecting sEMG signals from the 5 facial muscles of 7 volunteers. Subsequently, each signal was filtered using a band-pass filter with a cutoff frequency of 20-450 Hz, after which feature representations were extracted from the time, frequency, and statistical domains. Spectral regression extreme learning machine (SRELM) was employed to reduce the dimension of the data while retaining most of the relevant information. Finally, a feedforward neural network (NN) was used as a classifier. The experiment tested the performance of the system with a decreasing number of electrodes. Results demonstrated that the average classification accuracies of using 2, 3, 4, and 5 channel electrode combinations were 87.05%, 94.77%, 97.81%, and 99.01%, respectively.

The Internet of things systems (IoT) has a significant impact on different aspects of our lives. For that reason, IoT systems should be in high quality and clean of defects. The quality measurements for IoT systems vary according to the type of the IoT system and its applications. Therefore, IoT systems should be quality measured differently considering the presence of heterogeneous objects bound together to build the IoT system. This diversity leads to a variety of quality measurement model, which makes the process of measuring quality more challengeable, less accurate, and less applicable. In this research, different quality models for IoT systems have been studied and compared regarding the quality factors. Besides, a new quality model for IoT has been proposed. The new model focused on all the characteristics related to IoT systems, by introducing quality factors that measure them.

The access aspect of all cellular network generations is often plagued by issues associated with dead spots - parts of the network that are not covered - and hot spots - areas where the number of active cellular clients exceeds the network's resources. In recent years, numerous research proposals have been made to counter cellular network problems using MCN (Multi-hop Cellular Networks) architectures or D2D multi-hop communications, a novel paradigm that allows for the extension of the cellular access area through ad-hoc networks. 

In this research paper, we investigate the classification factors for D2D architecture, present various proposed D2D architectures, and establish an experimental platform within a real indoor environment. Our setup utilizes Android smartphones to compare uplink/downlink throughputs and latencies between single-hop and multi-hop communications via D2D architecture within a 4G cellular network.

Base station planning is a crucial and intricate issue in the wireless telecommunications system, particularly in the context of a heterogeneous network. In the electric power system, the wireless terminal communication network plays a vital role in addressing two significant obstacles in the development of smart grids: low degree of power distribution network automation and incomplete coverage of grid information data collection. There are two standards in China for power telecommunication, namely the 1.8GHz standard and the 230MHz standard. This paper presents a method for planning a wireless terminal access network based on Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) for selecting the appropriate standard for the base station. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach can effectively plan a two-standard heterogeneous network and ensure the communication requirements of the terminal.

The paper presents a wavelet-fuzzy controller of a field-oriented control system of belt conveyor drive. A discrete wavelet transform is used to decompose the speed error signal into various frequency components. The transformed error coefficients and scaling coefficients are used to generate the motor control signal The proposed controller is satisfied the speed control problem for a closed control system. The field-oriented control scheme with a wavelet-fuzzy controller under various dynamic operating conditions was investigated. The results of the comparison of the work of the traditional PI controller and the proposed wavelet-fuzzy controller are presented. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed wavelet-fuzzy controller. Application of the proposed approach of the wavelet-fuzzy controller allows reducing of electromagnetic moment vibrations.

High dynamic range (HDR) imaging is often challenging due to the issue of highlight clipping caused by overexposure. The clipping of information in the highlight area is a bottleneck in the generation of HDR images. However, a simple technique has been developed that can retrieve information from overexposed areas by creating a low dynamic range (LDR) image set from a single LDR image. These LDR images are then fused together to create the HDR image. Our results were evaluated using the single image HDR generation technique, and our technique outperformed other methods in terms of producing better visual results.

This article showcases the outcomes of a partnership between the Universidad Nacional de Educación a Distancia (UNED) and INOMA, a renewable energy firm based in Spain, in the Microelectronics Cloud Alliances Project (MECA Project). The project involved the creation of three open courses; two of which focused on microelectronics, while the other focused on renewable energy systems maintenance. All three courses were integrated into a cloud architecture, which made them available to everyone. 

The project lasted for three years and involved the design and development of the cloud architecture, content creation, implementation of the courses, and a brief pilot test. This article presents the results and conclusions of the project, as well as future considerations.

As a nondestructive diagnosis method, hammering test is a popular approach for detecting defect on concrete surfaces. However, as the number of concrete structures that require inspection is increasing, it is an important issue in recent years to reduce inspection time and human cost during hammering test. This paper introduces a novel method to detect defect on concrete surfaces in real-time during hammering test. The proposed method has two features; 1) automatically analyzing the acoustic data based on the statistical data of hitting sounds without prior training data, 2) the diagnostic results immediately displayed by projection mapping to the hit positions. We show the effectiveness of the proposed system through the experiments by using test concrete block with defects.

ICT are one of the most important value for the economic growth. Technology, information, and knowledge has an important impact in peripheral regions when they want to participate in the global market. Exists a lot of discussion about the digital divide between countries but little in relation to the regions and especially Less Favoured Regions (LFR). There is a clear evidence that these internal disparities can lead to the continued marginalization of people and regions “disconnected” from global information networks, which support the modern economy and causing strong inequalities. By other side, data available about the ICT use are normally from central regions and not Less Favoured Regions. With this study, we made a study to understand the ICT use by small enterprises and entrepreneurs from peripheral regions from Portugal and Spain: 5 Spanish regions (Leon, Zamora, Salamanca, Valladolid, Ávila) and 2 Portuguese (Alto Tâmega e Terras de Trâs-os-Montes). For that, 433 surveys were carried out (170 in the Portuguese regions and 263 in Spanish areas), included in project COMPETIC.

In this paper, we propose a novel scheme called polarization-based power-splitting full-duplex relaying (PB-PS-FDR). Our aim is to enhance the performance of simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) systems. This scheme enables the relay to perform energy harvesting and full-duplex information transmission simultaneously. Additionally, the relay can benefit from self-energy recycling (S-ER) based on power-splitting (PS) by receiving loopback interference signals with specific polarization states. 

We also propose a method to determine the optimal PS factor and derive the corresponding closed-form expression. Simulation results demonstrate a significant improvement in capacity compared to conventional power splitting relaying and time-switching relaying schemes. 

Our proposed approach contributes to the advancement of SWIPT technology by providing a reliable and efficient method for full-duplex relaying.
