The PB-PS-FDR scheme is a promising solution for energy-efficient wireless communication networks that require simultaneous information and power transfer.

The stator winding structure of the main exciter of the brushless synchronous starter/generator (BSSG) is changed at high speed for flux weakening, leading to a sudden excitation decrease of the main generator (MG) of BSSG. Consequently, when proportional-integral (PI) current loop-based control strategies are applied, large current overshoots will occur due to the lack of fast current control ability. This paper adopts model predictive current control (MPCC) to replace PI current control for a better dynamic performance. Besides, a parameter estimation scheme, based on the recursive least square (RLS) algorithm, is proposed to provide MG parameters for MPCC. An effectiveness analysis of the RLS algorithm is performed and two rules are given. According to the two rules, rather than the parameter dynamic characteristics adopted by traditional methods, three MG parameters, dq-axes inductances, and excitation flux linkage are estimated with two decoupled RLS estimators. In addition, a method is proposed to adjust the forgetting factor to track fast changing parameters of MG when the excitation changes suddenly. With the estimated parameters, MPCC is conducted to start BSSG. Experimental results show that fast current control of MG is achieved and large current overshoots caused by the sudden excitation change are avoided.

Passive behavior-sensing systems can accurately identify individual behaviors through modeling human behavior and wireless signal propagation. However, existing methods fail in multiperson scenarios due to time-varying environments. This paper proposes an online method for modeling the position-behavior feature of multiperson scenes. Firstly, a model for individual behavioral feature transformation based on position is proposed. This generates behavior features for other positions based on the behavior of the individual in a particular position. Secondly, a multiperson behavior feature generation method based on noise reduction is developed, allowing for online pattern generation of the same behavior feature. Finally, a multiperson fitness coaching system, named the multiuser fitness coach, is designed and implemented using these models. The system can successfully identify irregular behavior in multiperson environments, with evaluation results proving its precision in decision-making.

Breast cancer is a prevalent form of cancer that affects women around the world. Early diagnosis is crucial for successful treatment, which has led to a plethora of breast cancer screening techniques being developed by researchers globally. Infrared thermography is an effective screening method supported by various studies. In this paper, we propose a methodology that employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to classify infrared images of breasts as healthy or non-healthy due to anomalies like cancer. Our work's primary contribution is the use of deep learning architecture, which has not been adequately exploited in previous studies. Many methods rely on traditional classifiers and hand-crafted features, such as Support Vector Machines, but our approach's deep learning architecture allows for accurate classification. Our proposed technique achieved a competitive accuracy level of 98% for the static protocol and 95% for the dynamic protocol. Our methodology also leverages an appropriate modeling strategy that capitalizes on the strengths of CNNs.

The use of deep learning algorithms has improved fault classification accuracy in fault diagnosis. However, there is a lack of guidelines and parameters such as the layers of the deep learning architecture and dimension of each hidden level, which has limited further improvement. To address this, an optimized deep learning model called the manifold sparse auto-encoder (MSAE) neural network is proposed based on manifold mapping eigenvalues. The MSAE is constructed to diagnose machine faults and has two main contributions. Firstly, every encoding and decoding process is considered as a module to reduce the vanishing gradient problem. Secondly, the dimension of each hidden layer is determined by the manifold mapping eigenvalues of hidden neurones, while the layers of the deep learning architecture are determined by the clustering distribution of features. The proposed MSAE outperforms other machine learning methods in machinery fault diagnosis as demonstrated by the gearbox datasets, indicating that it can more effectively extract discriminative high-level features with greater accuracy.

Traditional power grids are being transformed into smart grids (SGs) to address the issues in the existing power system due to uni-directional information flow, energy wastage, growing energy demand, reliability, and security. SGs offer bi-directional energy flow between service providers and consumers, involving power generation, transmission, distribution, and utilization systems. SGs employ various devices for the monitoring, analysis, and control of the grid, deployed at power plants, distribution centers, and in consumers’ premises in a very large number. Hence, an SG requires connectivity, automation, and the tracking of such devices. This is achieved with the help of the Internet of Things (IoT). The IoT helps SG systems to support various network functions throughout the generation, transmission, distribution, and consumption of energy by incorporating the IoT devices (such as sensors, actuators, and smart meters), as well as by providing the connectivity, automation, and tracking for such devices. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive survey on the IoT-aided SG systems, which includes the existing architectures, applications, and prototypes of the IoT-aided SG systems. This survey also highlights the open issues, challenges, and future research directions for the IoT-aided SG systems.

This letter presents a digital predistortion (DPD) technique aimed at enhancing the linearity of limited range mobile front haul links used in both contemporary long-term evolution (LTE) and future (5G) networks. The technique is applied to radio-over-fiber links that are based on single-mode (SM) vertical cavity surface emitting lasers emitting at 850 nm and standard SM fibers. To identify the predistorter, both memory and generalized memory polynomial models are utilized via indirect learning architecture. The effectiveness of the DPD technique is demonstrated by the improvement in link performance, as measured by the normalized mean square error and the adjacent channel power ratio, which are evaluated using complete LTE frames of 10 ms and occupying 5-MHz bandwidth with 64-quadrature amplitude modulation format. Additionally, the DPD approach's effectiveness is evaluated under varying input power levels. Experimental results validate the promising linearization performance of the proposed DPD technique.

In this paper, we introduce a promising secure and privacy-preserving incentive mechanism in the vehicular cloud (VC). Such an incentive will convince vehicles with excess sensing data to join in the VC without the risk of privacy disclosure. The proposed scheme uses the Bargain Game theory to model the interactions between a VC server (VCS) and vehicles. With the proposed incentive mechanism, the VCS can select competent vehicles with which to collaborate for the announced task, while the vehicles can earn payment for participation. Further, our mechanism ensures fairness between all participants in terms of reward. We also exploit the signcryption technique to achieve mutual authentication between the VCS and vehicles as well as to prevent the private information of these vehicles from being disclosed. Simulation results are provided to show that the proposed privacy-preserving incentive mechanism is beneficial to both the VCS and vehicles, resulting in a win-win situation.

Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based brain computer-interfaces (BCIs) have shown its robustness in facilitating high-efficiency communication. State-of-the-art training-based SSVEP decoding methods such as extended Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) and Task-Related Component Analysis (TRCA) are the major players that elevate the efficiency of the SSVEP-based BCIs through a calibration process. However, due to notable human variability across individuals and within individuals over time, calibration (training) data collection is non-negligible and often laborious and time-consuming, deteriorating the practicality of SSVEP BCIs in a real-world context. This study aims to develop a cross-subject transferring approach to reduce the need for collecting training data from a test user with a newly proposed least-squares transformation (LST) method. Study results show the capability of the LST in reducing the number of training templates required for a 40-class SSVEP BCI. The LST method may lead to numerous real-world applications using near-zero-training/plug-and-play high-speed SSVEP BCIs.

We study the effect of close-proximity in the estimation of the Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) using a monopulse antenna array system, with application to angle-sensitive proximity WiFi readers. It is shown that in this scenario, it is necessary to consider near-field radiative effects to make an accurate angular estimation at short distances between the mobile terminal and the DoA proximity sensor. As a result, we define a range-dependent angular monopulse function, which provides a better DoA estimation in a Field of View of 60° and for distances ranging from 3 m to 50 cm.

This paper showcases the performance of various machine learning approaches using a recently collected, yet partially labeled dataset (derived from the Locked Shields 2017 exercise), along with the identification of the key features that were considered significant. Additionally, the outcomes were analyzed by a cybersecurity expert, who validated the fact that the models were proficient in distinguishing between known and malicious intrusions, and even uncovered novel attacks. The study included the detection of 500 anomalies, out of which 50 stood out as previously undiscovered incidences. Considering that such discoveries are typically rare, this indicates the potential of incorporating an unlabeled dataset to build and assess an effective network intrusion detection system.

Deep learning algorithms often involve solving complex non-linear and nonconvex unconstrained optimization problems. Currently, the class of first-order algorithms like stochastic gradient descent (SGD) are widely used to tackle optimization problems in machine learning and deep learning. However, SGD has limitations in escaping saddle points and usually requires extensive trial-and-error for parameter fine-tuning. The use of second-order curvature information to find search direction can lead to more robust convergence. Quasi-Newton methods, which construct an approximate Hessian matrix to build a quadratic model of the objective function, are superlinearly convergent and attractive alternatives to SGD. Limited-memory Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (L-BFGS) is a popular quasi-Newton method that constructs positive-definite Hessian approximations. However, since the true Hessian matrix may not be positive definite, an initialization condition is required to ensure no false negative curvature information is recorded. In this paper, we introduce various initialization methods for L-BFGS matrices within a trust-region framework and provide empirical results from classification tasks of the MNIST digits dataset. We compare the performance of different L-BFGS initialization methods to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

To enhance the precision and effectiveness of automatic fault localization, we propose an approach that employs Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). These two mathematical models possess excellent classification and prediction capabilities. Initially, we preprocess the training data utilizing the GMM-based clustering algorithm. We then replace the constant penalty factor of SVM with two adaptive ones. Subsequently, we use the robust learning ability of the modified SVM to establish the mapping relationship between the coverage information and the execution result of each test case. To evaluate the effectiveness of our technique, we conduct an efficiency comparison on the Siemens Suite. Our experiments verify that our localization approach achieves higher accuracy in both single and multiple faults localization without increasing testing cost.

As the urban population increases the urban density becomes denser. The first to be affected is the traffic, 30% of traffic is caused by vehicles cruising for parking. One of the solutions is to deploy a smart parking assisted by Wireless Sensor Network (WSN), thus the cities can optimize parking re-sources and provide a transparent and smart services. Drivers can get real-time parking availability information through their smartphone. The aim of this paper is to introduce an intelligent parking system based on WSN by identifying their benefits, challenges and constraints while providing real-time availability information. We will focus on the WSN MAC layer and protocols proposed. We start with a state of the art of smart parking solutions based on WSNs and their politics to solve the current parking problems. Then we discuss the different solutions of MAC protocols proposed in real time service context and we finish with a comparative of these solutions to identify their strengths and limitations.

This paper proposes a fast and efficient technique for constructing an equivalent model of patch antenna for predicting its radiation pattern. The equivalent model of the antenna is constructed based on its radiation properties. First, the initial model of the antenna is developed and then the arrangement of the initial model is optimized using FEKO optimization tool. The electric field of the magnetic dipole is determined based on numerical Green function derivation. The magnetic dipole is used to construct the equivalent model of patch antenna based on the radiation mechanism to predict its radiation pattern. Only two design parameters needed to be optimized making it more computational efficient. The derived radiation pattern from the equivalent model is validated with that of the original antenna model on FEKO to evaluate its efficiency. The simulation results show that the proposed equivalent model based on a magnetic dipole is fast and efficient and do not require the antenna's detailed material information.

Recent development in inventory management shows that the use of lateral transshipment to pool inventory promotes the customer service. Inspired by the existing works, this paper studies the lateral transshipment policy in an inventory system consisting of multiple retailers. We model this problem as Markov Decision Process (MDP), and several desirable properties of the optimal lateral transshipment policy are developed. The primary contribution of this study lies in its effort to extend the state-of-the-art results on two retailers to arbitrary number of retailers. Since the computational capacity required for solving large-scale MDP is prohibitive, a comprehensive heuristic lateral transshipment policy is proposed. The effectiveness of the heuristic is demonstrated through numerical experiments. This study brings new perspectives on seeking a balance between benefits and risks of lateral transshipment actions taken by retailers, and provides practical insights on inventory management problem involving lateral transshipment.

Neuroscience behavioral animal studies often require injecting DNA material or fluorescent dyes into specific brain regions within the animal's skull. Currently, these types of injections or surgical procedures are done manually by skilled researchers using mechanically based stereotaxic platforms. However, alignment can be very time-consuming and prone to error due to the small size of brain targets.Here we propose to develop a next generation stereotaxic platform for small animals by combining a three-dimensional (3D) computer vision sub-system and a full six degree-of-freedom (6DOF) robotic platform to improve spatial accuracy and surgical speed. With this approach, a video projector projects a series of structured illumination patterns onto an animal skull. Two video cameras are then used to capture two-dimensional (2D) images of the skull and the captured 2D images are processed to reconstruct an accurate 3D skull profile based on geometrical triangulation. Using the reconstructed 3D skull profile, the skull can be guided and repositioned using a 6DOF robotic platform to precisely and accurately align a surgical tool with the intention of reaching a specific brain target. This new stereotaxic system may improve accuracy and speed of small-scale brain surgeries for neuroscience studies.

Recently released 5G networks empower the novel Network Slicing concept. Network slicing introduces new business models such as allowing telecom providers to lease a virtualized slice of their infrastructure to tenants such as industry verticals, e.g. automotive, e-health, factories, etc. However, this new paradigm poses a major challenge when applied to Radio Access Networks (RAN): how to achieve revenue maximization while meeting the diverse service level agreements (SLAs) requested by the infrastructure tenants? In this paper, we propose a new analytical framework, based on stochastic geometry theory, to model realistic RANs that leverage the business opportunities offered by network slicing. We mathematically prove the benefits of slicing radio access networks as compared to non-sliced infrastructures. Based on this, we design a new admission control functional block, STORNS, which takes decisions considering per slice SLA guaranteed average experienced throughput. A radio resource allocation strategy is introduced to optimally allocate transmit power and bandwidth (i.e., a slice of radio access resources) to the users of each infrastructure tenant. Numerical results are illustrated to validate our proposed solution in terms of potential spectral efficiency, and compare it against a non-slicing benchmark.

Cloud computing (CC) is the emerging technology in the world for hosting and delivering services over the internet. It offers a variety of benefits such as cost saving, access to different services without any installation from anywhere and any time by internet, etc. Despite all the advantages offered by CC, this technology still susceptible to security threats. From user point of view, CC seems to be very insecure due to security attacks which threaten it and limit its widespread adoption. More motivations are required to provide more trustworthy solutions to secure the cloud as much as possible and preserve users trust. For that, we propose a new model called "profiling and preventing security attacks", abbreviated to PPSA, to detect and prevent the known attacks as well as the unknown attacks before accessing the cloud services/resources. Unlike the existing solutions, such as intrusion detection systems (IDSs), the proposed solution is able to be deployed in a wide area network in the basis of internet and prevent unknown attacks. In this study, we propose a new solution to profile and prevent security attacks in CC. Then, we define new security factors based on keystroke dynamic. Afterwards, we integrate a machine learning algorithm (classification based on associations) to our proposal in order to profile and predict security attacks and optimize as well the PPSA scheme. Eventually, the proposal is illustrated by a realistic case study.

In this brief introduction to tracking using state estimation, we compare two techniques. We compare the performance of the well known Kaiman filter to that of a simple receding horizon filter, a less well known technique. Our goal is to introduce the less well known family of techniques and show some of its advantages and disadvantages relative to Kalman-filter-based techniques.

The identification of persons through partial fingerprint is one of the basic biometrie matters. The context of use is situated particularly in forensics. The main issue is the insufficiency of information contained in the partial fingerprint, it depends from the size of the proportion found in the crime scene. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for the identification of persons through partial fingerprint which uses redefined characteristics of minutiae extracted from the fingerprint image. To validate our work, we exploit two complete databases FVC 2004 and POLYU HRF to form our dataset. The proposed approach reaches recognition rates up to 98.06% and 98.82% when using datasets extracted from POLYU HRF database and FVC 2004 database respectively. It outperforms four state-of-the-art methods in term of recognition rates in different percentage of incomplete fingerprint image.

Using EEG signals to access a security system has received substantial attention from researchers in recent years. EEG signals measure the electrical field generated by active neurons in the brain and provide a unique way of identifying users based on their brain activity.

While the use of EEG-based credentials is sensitive to affective states, few studies have addressed this issue when using brainwaves for authentication purposes. Therefore, this paper investigates the user-authenticating ability of an EEG-based person authentication (EBPA) system when clients are in a variety of brain states during mental tasks to login.

The results of the experiment, which are supported by neuropsychological evidence, show that the EBPA system has better accuracy when users are in "like" or "unfamiliar" brain states, compared to when they are in a "dislike" or "familiar" state. This finding highlights the importance of considering human affective states when designing a real-world EBPA system that is both stable and high security, as well as comfortable for users.

Overall, the use of EEG signals has the potential to revolutionize the way we approach security systems. However, it is essential to consider the nuances of human affective states to ensure that these systems are effective and user-friendly.

Starting in the mid-2000s, the number of malware samples began to grow exponentially. By the beginning of 2018, over 800 million samples were known, requiring security vendors to adjust their strategies. One approach has been to use machine learning algorithms for prediction. However, as the number of malware samples grows, so should the size of the benign sample set if a reliable and proactive model is desired. This paper addresses key considerations for creating a large cleanset (a collection of benign files) to be used in machine learning training.

Similarity measurements play a critical role in the design of classifiers for pattern recognition tasks. One of the popular classifiers, representative vector machines (RVMs), assigns a test example based on its nearest representative vector. This framework can be considered as a combination of other typical classifiers such as nearest neighbor (NN) classifiers, support vector machines (SVMs), and sparse representation-based classification (SRC). In this paper, we aim to investigate the performance of discriminant vector machines (DVMs), which are inspired by RVMs, using various similarity measurements. Our experiments on Yale and ORL databases reveal that the L3 norm surpasses the traditional L2 norm in DVMs. Moreover, we have provided preliminary summaries of some other similarity measurements. This study not only provides a deeper understanding of DVMs but also offers an opportunity to optimize other classifiers.

Hysteresis controllers are useful in regulating switching dc-dc converters with minimized filter components. The current hysteresis controller, which utilizes the inductor current ripple for generating PWM gate signal, provides tight regulation. However, the conventional method of sensing the current using a wide bandwidth current sensor and a high speed ADC proves to be expensive. In this paper, a new method is proposed for estimating the current without requiring a current sensing. The proposed method uses the switch node voltage of the converter for estimating the current, which is then used by the current hysteresis controller. Experimental results show that the frequency of converter for different hysteresis limits varies accurately between 961 kHz and 350 kHz, reflecting a 6% accuracy with respect to the theoretical calculations.

IP source spoofing can result in DoS and DDoS attacks due to the lack of packet level authentication in the Internet. To prevent such attacks, source address validation filtering is deployed. In this study, we propose a new scheme to analyze the deployment of source address validation-filtering by using special path backscatter messages generated by the spoofed traffic. The absence of these messages from an AS over a long period can classify it as a non-spoofer AS. Using Caida's backscatter dataset, we provide a list of spoofer and non-spoofer ASes and provide a mathematical analysis for determining the time required before declaring an AS as a non-spoofer. We also use the normal approximation of binomial distribution to calculate confidence intervals for the proportion of ASes allowing spoofing and test hypotheses regarding spoofing activity.

In the era of Network Function Virtualization (NFV) and Mobile Edge Computing (MEC), ensuring reliable network services is of utmost importance for network service providers. This is particularly critical for mission-critical applications, as poor service quality can lead to significant losses of users. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel approach to reliably provision virtual network function (VNF) instances in an MEC environment. 

Specifically, the proposed approach formulates a reliability-aware VNF instance placement problem that accounts for different users and their distinct service reliability requirements. The problem involves provisioning primary and secondary VNF instances at various cloudlets in an MEC system while ensuring reliability requirements are met, thereby maximizing network throughput. The authors demonstrate that the problem is NP-hard and propose an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) solution as well as an approximation algorithm with a logarithmic approximation ratio to solve the problem efficiently. 

Furthermore, for two special cases, the authors propose constant approximation algorithms and dynamic programming solutions respectively. The performance of the proposed algorithms is evaluated via experimental simulations, demonstrating promising empirical results that outperform their analytical counterparts, which tend to be very conservative. Overall, this paper introduces a reliable VNF instance provisioning approach that promises to be effective and efficient in today's increasingly connected world.

Cyber-physical systems (CPSs) security has emerged as a critical research topic due to the increasing impact of CPS applications in diverse industrial sectors. Unlike traditional information technology (IT) security, CPS security requires a distinct strategy because of the close interaction between cyber and physical components. To address this issue, we propose a novel machine learning-based attack detection (AD) scheme as part of our overall CPS security strategies. Our scheme performs AD at the physical layer, modeling and monitoring the physical behavior of the physical asset or process.

Our approach is based on intelligently deriving salient signatures or features from the large number of noisy physical measurements utilizing physical knowledge and advanced machine learning techniques. These derived features not only capture the physical relationships among the measurements but also have more discriminant power in distinguishing normal and attack activities. We conducted an experimental study to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed AD scheme by considering heavy-duty gas turbines of combined cycle power plants as the CPS application. We used data from both high-fidelity simulation and several real plants to show that our proposed AD scheme is effective in early detection of attacks or malicious activities.

Overall, our proposed machine learning-based AD scheme is a step towards enhancing the security of CPSs. By focusing on the physical layer, our scheme is capable of detecting attacks that cannot be detected by traditional IT security mechanisms. This approach shows great promise for mitigating the security challenges of CPSs and enhancing their reliability and safety.

Achieving optimal time-frequency (TF) resolution is essential in extracting valuable information from seismic data using TF algorithms and characterizing reservoir properties through frequency decomposition. The generalized S-transform (GST) is a prevalent TF algorithm, but it can be challenging to select an ideal parameter set for the entire seismic dataset. In this paper, we propose SAGST (self-adaptive GST), which sets the parameters of the GST adaptively using the instantaneous frequency (IF) of seismic traces. Our workflow begins by establishing a relationship between the parameter set of the GST and the IF through a synthetic wedge model. We use the IF as an indicator of the time thickness of each trace in the wedge model, compute the TF spectrum using the GST with different parameter sets, and compare it with the theoretical spectrum. The parameter set with the highest similarity is identified as the best parameter for each trace, and we create a relationship between the parameter set and IF value. We can finally choose the optimum parameter set for the GST according to the IF values of seismic traces. We apply SAGST to both synthetic and field data, demonstrating its validity and effectiveness in obtaining a high TF resolution in the TF representation.

In this paper, we propose a novel biomedical cyberphysical system for the automated and efficient detection of arrhythmia and seizure in time-series biomedical signals, such as electrocardiogram (ECG) and electroencephalography (EEG). Our proposed approach uses a multilayer, automated, and multistage deep residual network for anomaly detection in the biomedical signals. In order to address the class imbalance problem that is commonly found in biomedical datasets, we utilized undersampling techniques. We validated our algorithm on two widely used benchmark datasets - MIT-BIH Arrhythmia and CHB-MIT Scalp, and our results demonstrated a significant improvement in terms of sensitivity with 90% and 97.1% for supraventricular and ventricular beats, respectively. The accuracy of our results is comparable to most state-of-the-art methods, and for supraventricular beats, our proposed method outperforms all but one of the state-of-the-art methods. Another advantage of our proposed method is that it requires no preprocessing and is computationally efficient. Moreover, it provides reliable results with EEG samples of small duration. Finally, our algorithm provides 81% sensitivity for seizure detection in EEG signals which is similar to the existing deep learning methods.

Recent studies have made considerable advancements in the area of synthetic data generation using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). GANs have been widely used in various domains of computer vision, such as text-to-image conversion, image-to-video application, domain transfer, and super-resolution. Traditional GANs in computer vision rely on deep convolutional neural networks, which can be computationally expensive since they rely on convolutional layers with millions of trainable parameters. As a result, training GAN models can be complex and require a significant amount of time to reach an equilibrium point. 

This article aims to explore the use of depthwise separable convolutions to reduce training time while ensuring data generation performance. Our study compares the performance of a DepthwiseGAN architecture and a StarGan architecture and suggests that DepthwiseGAN architecture can produce realistic images in less training time than the StarGan architecture. However, model capacity remains a significant factor in generative modeling. Additionally, our study suggests that depthwise separable convolutions work best when applied only to the generator. 

To evaluate the quality of the generated images, we used the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), which compares the generated image distribution's similarity with that of the training dataset. Overall, our study highlights the potential of DepthwiseGAN architecture to generate high-quality synthetic data while reducing training time.

Recommender systems are used to analyze users' preferences through their past activities and to personalize recommendations for each user based on what they might be interested in. The performance of the recommender system is most commonly measured using only recommendation accuracy. However, recommending accurate items does not mean that the generated recommendation is the best for the user because it can be biased towards some items that have a higher chance of being liked by users, such as popular items. Recommendations become repetitive and obvious with biased item selection and are less likely to be personalized. To mitigate bias and repetitiveness, recommendation diversity has been studied. However, diversity has a trade-off relationship with accuracy. Modifying the recommendation algorithm to consider diversity while learning about user preferences would not only cause loss in accuracy, but also lead to less precise reading of user preferences. Instead, using ranking methods to re-rank the priority of items predicted, the recommendation algorithm would keep the preciseness of the algorithm. In this study, a ranking method using the appearance frequency of items to restrict the items from being frequently recommended will be proposed. The experimental results showed that the proposed method consistently improved diversity in multiple diversity metrics.

Compressive Sensing (CS) theory has revolutionized the field of signal processing by enabling the reconstruction of sparse signals using a small number of linear measurements. However, the non-linear and expensive signal reconstruction process has limited its application in practical scenarios. Recent literature has demonstrated that compressive image classification can be achieved directly in CS domain without the need for signal reconstruction.

This article introduces a novel approach for compressive image classification using a DCT-based method that directly extracts binary discriminative features from CS measurements. The CS measurements can be obtained using a random or a pseudorandom measurement matrix, or by using a matrix with elements learned from the training data to optimize the classification task.

In addition, the article presents feature fusion by concatenating the Bag of Words (BoW) representation of the binary features with one of the two state-of-the-art CNN-based feature vectors. The fusion of these features outperforms the existing state-of-the-art methods in both cases.

This method can be applied to a wide range of image classification tasks where both low-cost linear sampling and high classification accuracy are desired. It offers a practical solution for compressive image classification that eliminates the need for expensive signal reconstruction.

With the development of VR technology, simulation driving can provide diverse user experience. In this paper, we built an immersive simulation driving system by Unity 3D and VR technology and in this system Logitec G29 is served as an interactive device. In this system, the user can control the virtual vehicles in the traffic scenario through the behaviors of driver, including rotating steering wheel, braking, turning on the direction indicators and accelerating. The user-defined evaluation model can be introduced into the system easily to calculate the evaluation results through the user's operation data collected in real time, including braking time, steering wheel angle, etc. This feature makes our system can be used for drivingrelated training and assessment scenarios widely. We proposed a safety awareness assessment models and conducted related experiments to verify this feature. In addition, the system's scene can be changed according to different purposes, which make the system be more flexible to adapt to different types of virtual driving research.

A complex network is a network with non-trivial topological structures. It contains not just topological information but also attribute information available in the rich content of nodes. Concerning the task of cluster analysis in a complex network, model-based algorithms are preferred over distance-based ones, as they avoid designing specific distance measures. However, their models are only applicable to complex networks where the attribute information is composed of attributes in binary form. To overcome this disadvantage, we introduce a three-layer node-attribute-value hierarchical structure to describe the attribute information in a flexible and interpretable manner. Then, a new Bayesian model is proposed to simulate the generative process of a complex network. In this model, the attribute information is generated by following the hierarchical structure while the links between pairwise nodes are generated by a stochastic blockmodel. To solve the corresponding inference problem, we develop a variational Bayesian algorithm called TARA, which allows us to identify functionally meaningful clusters through an iterative procedure. Our extensive experiment results show that TARA can be an effective algorithm for cluster analysis in a complex network. Moreover, the parallelized version of TARA makes it possible to perform efficiently at its tasks when applied to large complex networks.

Biomedical event extraction plays a crucial role in extracting important biological information from large-scale scientific publications. However, current state-of-the-art systems often separate this task into multiple steps, which increases the potential for cascading errors. Additionally, the process of generating features from syntactic and dependency analysis separately can be complex. 

To address these issues, we propose an end-to-end model based on long short-term memory (LSTM) that optimizes biomedical event extraction. Our experimental results demonstrate that this approach significantly improves performance, achieving average F1-scores of 59.68%, 58.23%, and 57.39% on the BioNLP09, BioNLP11, and BioNLP13's Genia event datasets, respectively. 

Through our experimental study, we have shown that our proposed model has great potential in the field of biomedical event extraction. By using an end-to-end approach that integrates all steps into a single model, we can overcome the limitations of current systems and achieve better results.

The performance of salient object segmentation has been significantly advanced by using the deep convolutional networks. However, these networks often produce blob-like saliency maps without accurate object boundaries. This is caused by the limited spatial resolution of their feature maps after multiple pooling operations and might hinder downstream applications that require precise object shapes. To address this issue, we propose a novel deep model—Focal Boundary Guided (Focal-BG) network. Our model is designed to jointly learn to segment salient object masks and detect salient object boundaries. Our key idea is that additional knowledge about object boundaries can help to precisely identify the shape of the object. Moreover, our model incorporates a refinement pathway to refine the mask prediction and makes use of the focal loss to facilitate the learning of the hard boundary pixels. To evaluate our model, we conduct extensive experiments. Our Focal-BG network consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on five major benchmarks. We provide a detailed analysis of these results and demonstrate that our joint modeling of salient object boundary and mask helps to better capture the shape details, especially in the vicinity of object boundaries.

Driven by the tremendous technological advancement of personal devices and the prevalence of wireless mobile network accesses, the world has witnessed an explosion in crowdsourced live streaming. Ensuring a better viewers quality of experience (QoE) is the key to maximize the audiences number and increase streaming providers' profits. This can be achieved by advocating a geo-distributed cloud infrastructure to allocate the multimedia resources as close as possible to viewers, in order to minimize the access delay and video stalls. Moreover, allocating the exact needed resources beforehand avoids over-provisioning, which may lead to significant costs by the service providers. In the contrary, under-provisioning might cause significant delays to the viewers. In this paper, we introduce a prediction driven resource allocation framework, to maximize the QoE of viewers and minimize the resource allocation cost. First, by exploiting the viewers locations available in our unique dataset, we implement a machine learning model to predict the viewers number near each geo-distributed cloud site. Second, based on the predicted results that showed to be close to the actual values, we formulate an optimization problem to proactively allocate resources at the viewers proximity. Additionally, we will present a trade-off between the video access delay and the cost of resource allocation.

Contemporary power grids face significant challenges due to the rapid and substantial voltage fluctuations caused by the deployment of renewable generators, electric vehicles, and demand response programs. Real-time monitoring of grid operating conditions is becoming increasingly critical. However, traditional power system state estimation (PSSE) schemes are computationally expensive or often yield suboptimal performance, given the emergent large scale and nonconvexity of the systems. To overcome these hurdles, this paper proposes using physics-inspired deep neural networks (DNNs) for real-time power system monitoring. By unrolling an iterative solver developed using the exact ac model, a novel model-specific DNN is developed for real-time PSSE, which requires only offline training and minimal tuning effort. Furthermore, deep recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are used to enable system awareness ahead of the time horizon and to endow the DNN-based estimator with resilience. Deep RNNs leverage the long-term nonlinear dependencies present in historical voltage time series for successful forecasting. Numerical tests demonstrate improved performance of the proposed DNN-based estimation and forecasting approaches compared to existing alternatives. In real load data experiments on the IEEE 118-bus benchmark system, the novel model-specific DNN-based PSSE scheme outperforms competing alternatives by nearly an order-of-magnitude, including the widely adopted Gauss-Newton PSSE solver.

Aiming at the complicated problem of the radiation model in the traditional infrared image simulation and the practical problem that the model usability is difficult to verify, a simulation method of building object infrared image based on guided filtering enhanced feature prediction is proposed. Based on guided filter enhancing feature extraction of the measured images, the images are divided into different regions according to different properties of the material, and the infrared simulation images of the middle time are obtained by feature prediction and fusion. The experimental results show that the infrared enhancement image of the building object which is generated by this algorithm is consistent with the change of the enhanced image, whether it is from the subjective visual effect or the gray histogram. What's more, the algorithm effectively avoids the cumbersome data processing in the general simulation, and has an engineering practical value, low computational complexity, good real-time performance.

Ambient Assisted Living (AAL) is one of the most promising applications of the Internet of Things (IoT), as it has the potential to significantly improve the healthcare and quality of life of elderly individuals. With the recent integration of edge computing technology into the AAL IoT ecosystem, the ability to meet the demanding requirements of AAL and healthcare services has vastly improved. Edge computing offers benefits such as reducing the amount of data that needs to be transferred to the cloud, improving response time, and enhancing the overall quality of experience. Additionally, the deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies at the edge provides intelligence to improve decision making in a timely manner. 

Despite the numerous advantages that edge computing technology offers, it is still relatively unexplored in AAL scenarios. The few proposals that exist, which are based on deploying machine learning models at the edge, lack efficiency, security, mechanisms of resource management, service management, and deployment. They also do not offer a real and experimental AAL scenario. To address these issues, this paper proposes an innovative edge gateway architecture to support the deployment of deep learning (DL) models in AAL and healthcare scenarios efficiently. 

Our approach includes the addition of a predictive analytics module to deploy the models, and we employ a container-based virtualization technology on the edge gateway to manage the limited resources, provide security, and offer lifecycle services management. To evaluate the performance of our approach, we deployed a DL-based fall detection application on the edge gateway. The results showed that our approach significantly improves the inference time compared to cloud-based approaches, reducing it by 34 seconds and 8 seconds for similar approaches. 

In conclusion, our proposed edge gateway architecture provides an efficient and secure solution for deploying DL models in AAL and healthcare scenarios. This approach significantly reduces inference times, thereby improving the overall user experience. Furthermore, our framework provides a significant contribution to the future of AAL and healthcare services, which have the potential to revolutionize the way elderly individuals receive healthcare and support.

In order to achieve high accuracy of pixel-wise labeling and eliminate class-wise ambiguities for semantic scene segmentation, a balanced combination of coarsely and finely contextual details is required. Prior works have achieved impressive performance with deep learning integration, but have faced difficulties correctly labeling medium to small objects. To overcome this issue, this article proposes B-Net, a deep convolutional network with a bracket-style decoder that leverages features learned at middle layers in the encoder for constructing a final prediction map with densely enhanced semantic information. Through lateral connection modules, every feature map of interest combines with its adjacent version of higher spatial resolution to produce finer outputs that repeat such routine round-by-round until retrieving the finest-resolution map for dense prediction. On the CamVid dataset, benchmarking results showed the effectiveness of the proposed method with mean class-wise accuracy, pixel-wise accuracy, and mean union intersection of 76.2%, 87.1%, and 66.4%, respectively.

The current input-output table takes about 4 years from the start of the survey to the release, it is not suitable for analysis of real-time industries, and it takes a lot of labor to create. In order to solve this problem, the input-output table is being constructed using the corporate data possessed by Teikoku Databank (TDB) Co., Ltd. However, since the calculation of private consumption is based on the total sales of (BtoC) companies that are selling to consumers, it is not possible to record in the spent where it was consumed. Therefore, in this research, we estimate the sales ratio to consumers in the BtoC company and calculate the total sales amount to consumers in the sales of the company. Also, by dividing the total of the private consumption obtained proportionally according to the population size of each region, we construct an algorithm to calculate private consumption in each region.

Given the crucial role of optical networks in supporting vital societal services, it is imperative that they are protected against deliberate attacks that target the physical layer in order to prevent disruption. In order to ensure the robustness of these networks, advanced approaches for security assurance, diagnostics, and response are required. This paper examines the necessary advancements in optical network security that are necessary to achieve secure and self-diagnosable systems.

This paper presents a novel cluster-based distributed medium access control (CDMAC) protocol designed specifically for multichannel and multihop mobile cognitive radio ad hoc networks (CRAHNs). The proposed protocol leverages the channel-sensing model, which allows secondary users (SUs) to opportunistically obtain licensed channels from primary users (PUs) in the CRAHNs. We divide the CRAHN into clusters, with cluster heads determined based on the importance of the nodes. 

To dynamically select control and data channels, we consider the success probability and stability of the idle PU channels. We also propose a dynamic contention window mechanism to adaptively determine the contention window size, which reduces the MAC contention delay and achieves high throughput for a given contention window size. We develop a Markov chain model to characterize the performance of our proposed CDMAC protocol for a saturated network, which is also characterized by initial-state probabilities and a state-transition probability matrix. 

Extensive simulations are performed to verify the superiority of the proposed CDMAC protocol over other approaches in mobile CRAHNs. Our results demonstrate that the proposed CDMAC protocol achieves higher performance in terms of throughput, delay, and energy efficiency than other existing protocols. The proposed protocol can be a promising solution for enhancing the performance of medium access control in multichannel and multihop mobile CRAHNs.

The concept of situation awareness (SA) has been extensively studied by Mica Endsley in her articles over the past several decades. Her model of SA is based on empirical psychological research and has been tested and applied across various domains. Although there are several other descriptive models of human SA, most of them differ from Endsley's model. However, there are few computational process models of human SA available. The ongoing debate surrounding the proper form and functionality of descriptive SA models provides important insights into how computational process models can be evaluated for their adherence to human cognitive processes. 

In this article, we propose certain criteria for the assessment of computational process models' SA capabilities, taking reference from the descriptive SA model literature. Furthermore, a demonstration of the evaluation process is presented, and the usefulness of computational process models in testing theoretical claims about situation awareness is emphasized.

The protection of modern power systems is facing unprecedented challenges due to the emergence of distributed generation (DG). As microgrids can operate in both grid connected and islanded modes, it is pertinent to devise separate protection schemes for each. The reason being, the short circuit levels in both modes are vastly different. 

This paper proposes a novel approach to address this challenge by obtaining the settings of numerical directional overcurrent relay separately for both modes. This is achieved by formulating a non-linear optimization problem which is solved using three techniques. Additionally, the paper also proposes a scheme for the online update of settings based on operating mode.

To confirm the reliability of the proposed scheme, primary and backup relays are coordinated using optimal settings. The results obtained using the MATLAB/SIMULINK platform for the 9 bus test system design and coding conclusively demonstrate the reliability of this scheme in protecting a grid under both topologies.

The assessment of pathological samples by molecular techniques, such as in situ hybridization (ISH) and immunohistochemistry (IHC), has revolutionised modern Histopathology. Most often it is important to detect ISH/IHC reaction products in certain cells or tissue types. For instance, detection of human papilloma virus (HPV) in oropharyngeal cancer samples by ISH products is difficult and remains a tedious and time consuming task for experts. Here we introduce a proposed framework to segment epithelial regions in oropharyngeal tissue images with ISH staining. First, we use colour deconvolution to obtain a counterstain channel and generate input patches based on superpixels and their neighbouring areas. Then, a novel deep attention residual network is applied to identify the epithelial regions to produce an epithelium segmentation mask. In the experimental results, comparing the proposed network with other state-of-the-art deep learning approaches, our network provides a better performance than region-based and pixel-based segmentations.

In this research paper, our objective is to enhance the functions and capabilities of the Baxter robot [1] through the utilization of advanced data mining methods. Our study is situated within the field of robotics and is integrated into the context of Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM). The experimental data utilized consists of a vast array of parameters gathered throughout various robot activities such as arm movements and collision events. In this paper, we discuss the state-of-the-art data mining techniques and then present our solution which employs various data mining techniques. Our adopted techniques are thoroughly described and then the experimental observations are analyzed and discussed. We conclude by presenting the implications of our results and further areas of research potential in this emergent field. Our evaluation validates our model with an accuracy of over 98%.

Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification is a core task in the remote sensing community, and recently, deep learning-based methods have shown their capability of accurate classification of HSIs. Among the deep learning-based methods, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely used for the HSI classification. In order to obtain a good classification performance, substantial efforts are required to design a proper deep learning architecture. Furthermore, the manually designed architecture may not fit a specific data set very well. In this paper, the idea of automatic CNN for the HSI classification is proposed for the first time. First, a number of operations, including convolution, pooling, identity, and batch normalization, are selected. Then, a gradient descent-based search algorithm is used to effectively find the optimal deep architecture that is evaluated on the validation data set. After that, the best CNN architecture is selected as the model for the HSI classification. Specifically, the automatic 1-D Auto-CNN and 3-D Auto-CNN are used as spectral and spectral-spatial HSI classifiers, respectively. Furthermore, the cutout is introduced as a regularization technique for the HSI spectral-spatial classification to further improve the classification accuracy. The experiments on four widely used hyperspectral data sets (i.e., Salinas, Pavia University, Kennedy Space Center, and Indiana Pines) show that the automatically designed data-dependent CNNs obtain competitive classification accuracy compared with the state-of-the-art methods. In addition, the automatic design of the deep learning architecture opens a new window for future research, showing the huge potential of using neural architectures' optimization capabilities for the accurate HSI classification.

The Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) algorithm has recently emerged as a promising approach to solve complex optimization problems across various domains. To further improve the performance of GWO, researchers have attempted to modify the algorithm. This study proposes the Prey Phase GWO (PGWO) to enhance exploration during the initial search process.

The proposed PGWO algorithm was evaluated using various benchmark optimization functions and compared to both GWO and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Results showed that the PGWO algorithm outperformed both GWO and PSO in terms of its ability to find optimal solutions.

In summary, this work highlights the effectiveness of the PGWO algorithm in improving the GWO algorithm's performance in solving complex optimization problems. The results demonstrate the potential of the PGWO algorithm to address optimization issues across various domains.

As the amount of data available for analysis continues to increase, feature selection becomes an integral part of ensuring accurate classification results. Although selecting only a few features decreases computational complexity, choosing the right ones is essential for maintaining high levels of accuracy. In this paper, we propose a feature selection technique, HI-BQPSO, based on a hybrid improved quantum-behavior particle swarm optimization algorithm. The proposed method combines a filtering algorithm with the improved quantum-behavior particle swarm optimization algorithm to significantly reduce the dimensionality of data and overcome the shortcomings of BQPSO. 

To evaluate and compare the classification accuracy of HI-BQPSO's selected feature subsets against four other algorithms, tests were performed on nine gene expression datasets and 36 UCI datasets. Using a range of different classifiers, the results show that HI-BQPSO substantially decreases the number of features needed for classification, while maintaining a high level of accuracy in many cases. 

In conclusion, the proposed HI-BQPSO technique provides an effective way of selecting an optimal set of features for classification. With this method, it is possible to significantly reduce the dimensionality of the data while maintaining high accuracy levels. Therefore, this approach can be highly beneficial in classification algorithms where accurate classification results with low computational complexity are required.

With the rapid growth of location-based social networks (LBSNs), Point-Of-Interest (POI) recommendation has been extensively researched in recent years. One interesting extension to POI recommendation is the next POI recommendation, which aims to suggest the next POI to a user, based on their spatial and temporal context. This is a practical yet challenging task in various applications, and existing approaches mainly focus on modeling the spatial and temporal information and memorizing historical patterns through the user's trajectories for recommendation. However, they face the negative impact of missing and irregular check-in data, which can significantly affect the model's performance.

To address this issue, we propose an attention-based sequence-to-sequence generative model, namely POI-Augmentation Seq2Seq (PA-Seq2Seq), to address the sparsity of training sets by making check-in records evenly spaced. Specifically, the encoder summarizes each check-in sequence and the decoder predicts the possible missing check-ins based on the encoded information. To learn the time-aware correlation among user history, we employ a local attention mechanism to help the decoder focus on a specific range of context information when predicting a missing check-in point. We conducted extensive experiments on two real-world check-in datasets, Gowalla and Brightkite, to evaluate the performance and effectiveness of our proposed method.

A new methodology for extracting and modeling the BSIM3v3 junction capacitance of NMOSFET in VLSI has been proposed in this article. By using this method, improved accuracy can be achieved in the extraction of the p-n junction capacitance. The methodology takes into consideration the parasitic capacitance due to bottom area junction and side-wall capacitance components at the field oxide side and gate oxide side. Furthermore, the article proposes capacitance model parameters in BSIM3v3. The extraction methodology was conducted manually and a comparison was made to test the accuracy of the capacitance models. The results indicate that the capacitance models are highly accurate.

In recent years, intelligent fault diagnosis technology with the deep learning algorithm has been widely used in the manufacturing industry for substituting time-consuming human analysis method to enhance the efficiency of fault diagnosis. The rolling bearing as the connection between the rotor and support is the crucial component in rotating equipment. However, the working condition of the rolling bearing is under changing with complex operation demand, which will significantly degrade the performance of the intelligent fault diagnosis method. In this paper, a new deep transfer model based on Wasserstein distance guided multi-adversarial networks (WDMAN) is proposed to address this problem. The WDMAN model exploits complex feature space structures to enable the transfer of different data distributions based on multiple domain critic networks. The essence of our method is learning the shared feature representation by minimizing the Wasserstein distance between the source domain and target domain distribution in an adversarial training way. The experiment results demonstrate that our model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on rolling bearing fault diagnosis under different working conditions. The t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) technology is used to visualize the learned domain invariant feature and investigate the transferability behind the great performance of our proposed model.

The traffic landscape of present-day roads is undergoing a transformation through the adoption of light electrical vehicular transportation systems. One such system is the electronically power assisted cycle (EPAC). Due to the perceived vulnerability of this vehicle group, there is an increasing emphasis on enhancing cycling safety and analyzing rider behavior. A promising way of achieving these goals is through the incorporation of inertial measurement based brake detection systems. 

This paper sets out an approach that seeks to estimate the brake magnitude of electric bicycles by fusing state-of-the-art brake detection techniques with a model-based longitudinal dynamics system. The aim is to achieve not only a fast response time but a reliable detection of persistent braking situations as well. 

The experimental results indicate that the proposed method is highly accurate, and a sensitivity analysis has been conducted to evaluate the influence of pre-estimated parameters. As EPACs continue to gain in popularity, the use of advanced brake detection systems offers a promising avenue for improving the safety and performance of these vehicles on our roads.

In this paper we are mainly classifying cancerous or non-cancerous cells of human lung which was further classified into which category it falls benign or malignant. Area feature from region of interest (ROI) and Support Vector Machine is applied for classification and CLAHE as an enhancement technique. This paper concentrated on classification of lung nodules by Support Vector Machine technique.

The technology of physical-layer secret key generation (PSKG), which is based on reciprocal wireless channel, has been extensively studied in point-to-point (P2P) scenarios. This approach is known to be effective in solving the conventional security mechanism's key distribution problem. However, the complexity and energy consumption of PSKG increase when it is applied to group key distribution. Therefore, the issue of using PSKG to ensure group secret communication is still unresolved. To address this problem, we present a lightweight group key distribution (LGKD) technique designed for star network topology environment. In our LGKD method, the center node and each child node extract high-correlated channel characteristics instead of generating identical P2P keys, respectively. Then, the group key is transmitted to each child node, protected by the P2P channel characteristics that have high similarities. Our simulation results confirm the feasibility and effectiveness of our proposed LGKD approach.

This chapter provides a comprehensive review of the fundamental principles of artificial intelligence (AI) such as Expert Systems (ES), Fuzzy Logic (FL), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) or Neural Network (NNW), and Genetic Algorithms or Evolutionary Computation. This knowledge is essential to gain a better understanding of the applications of AI in renewable energy systems and smart grids. The chapter delves deeper into NNW, as it appears to be the foundation of the next generation of AI. It covers novel applications such as ES-based control concept of a smart grid system with a real-time simulator and permanent magnet synchronous generator-based wind generation system with FL-based control. It also includes adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system-based health monitoring of a wind generation system and fault identification of a smart grid subsystem by the neural network. The principles behind these applications can be implemented for various other utilities.

The prediction method plays crucial roles in the accurate prediction of rockfall runout range which could improve the protection of endangered residential areas and infrastructure. Recently, the Knearest neighbor (KNN) algorithm, one of many machine learning techniques, showed good performance in pattern classification. Therefore, the aim of this study was to use the K-nearest neighbor (KNN) algorithm to predict the rockfall runout range which is classified into different subintervals according to the distance from the slope toe. First, we proposed the prediction model of the rockfall runout range based on our improved KNN algorithm which could better offer robustness against different choices of the neighborhood size k, and it is the first work of applying our improved KNN algorithm to rockfall runout range prediction. Second, the shaking table tests of rockfall runout models were conducted for simulating the rockfall process, and the influence laws of factors-including types of an earthquake, peak ground acceleration, vibration frequency, slope angle, slope height, and block mass and block shape-on rockfall distance are investigated. Finally, there is a discussion of the performance of our proposed prediction model based on our improved KNN algorithm in the prediction of rockfall runout range. The extensive experimental results for rockfall runout range prediction demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed prediction model.

A mass measurement system using relay feedback of velocity was developed. In this system, the velocity of the object was fed back through a relay with a hysteresis. Although the efficacy of the proposed method has been already confirmed experimentally, it was subject to drift mainly because only the velocity was fed back. To prevent such drift, a spring element was added to produce restoring force. However, smaller drifts still occurred and the trajectory of the object fluctuated because the switching positions are not determined uniquely. In this paper, an estimation formula is derived, which can estimate the mass regardless of switching positions. The efficacy of the derived formula is confirmed experimentally.

The semi-formal verification method is a viable option when it comes to verifying the functionality of hardware designs. However, many existing methods derive the formal model from design implementation, which causes poor scalability and practicality. To overcome this challenge, we propose a specification-based semi-formal method for functional verification.

Our proposed semi-formal method makes use of a stage transition graph (STG) model to formally describe the function points in the specification. Additionally, we have developed an automatic test pattern generation (ATPG) method to generate the test vectors based on the STG model. The STG-based ATPG method ensures exhaustive exploration of functionality for both control-dominated designs and data-dominated designs while reaching possible corner cases.

Furthermore, to facilitate automatic verification, we have also developed an STG-based tool. Our experiments demonstrate that our method can automatically verify functional correctness from the specification while achieving similar code coverage as implementation-based semi-formal approaches.

Overall, our proposed specification-based semi-formal method offers a more feasible solution for functional verification that is scalable and practical.

Fixed network operators (FNOs) seek to improve their infrastructure with better investment strategies. Therefore, it is crucial for FNOs to migrate the existing technologies into new and high-income generating technologies. However, FNOs often hesitate to upgrade their existing services to end-users because of the possibility of service disruptions, even though the end-users have the infrastructure support to receive better services such as HD IPTV. In this paper, we propose a case study on Fiber-to-the-X (FTTX) migration strategy where subscribers with ADSL2+ connectivity can be migrated to VDSL2 technology through the proposed methodology that analyzes real operator data and acts based on the proposed criteria. After implementing the proposed mitigation strategy, HD IPTV services have been successfully offered to end-users with the potential to have upgraded services due to their infrastructure capabilities.

High integration densities and design complexity of printed-circuit boards make board-level functional fault identification extremely difficult. Machine learning provides an opportunity to identify functional faults with high accuracy and thereby reduce repair cost. However, the large volume of manufacturing data comes in a streaming format and exhibits time-dependent concept drift in a production environment. These drawbacks limit the effectiveness of traditional machine-learning algorithms. We propose a diagnosis workflow that utilizes online learning to train classifiers incrementally with a small chunk of data at each step. These online learning algorithms adapt to concept drift quickly with carefully designed update rules. A hybrid algorithm is also proposed to handle the scenario that data for varying numbers of boards are collected at different times. Experimental results using two boards in high-volume production show that, with the help of online learning and the proposed hybrid algorithm, the F1-score for diagnosis can be improved from 57.3% to 78.9%.

The interface between mobile phone technologies and innovation remains largely under-researched. Attempting to bridge this knowledge gap, this cross-sectional study of Kenyan enterprises examines the role of mobile phone technologies in innovation. The study applies probit estimators to a comprehensive dataset of 24, 164 micro, small and medium establishments in Kenya. The study reveals that; (1) mobile technologies are positively and significantly correlated with product and marketing innovation but are insignificantly correlated with process innovation. (2) The predicted probabilities of product, process and marketing innovation increase with the increase in the ICT index. (3) The effect of age and size on the propensity of innovation is concave: older and larger establishments tend to innovate more than relatively younger and smaller ones, but the relationships get reversed after a certain threshold. (3) The predicted probability of product, process and marketing innovation increase with increases in R&D, training, credit and foreign trade.

The five articles in this special section focus on data science and artificial intelligence (AI) for communications. The innovation in AI, machine learning (ML), and network data analytics provides a huge opportunity to revolutionize the world’s communications systems and user experience. Through gathering, processing, learning, and controlling the vast amounts of information in an intelligent manner, these analytics tools enable the possibility to automate and optimize systems in a way that was not previously possible. This is particularly important as the communications infrastructures evolve to support increasingly more complex human type as well as machine type communications and enable, through the connectedness of meters, sensors, and things, a plethora of new services. Supporting such immensely diverse traffic patterns and applications will require dynamic, highly adaptive network environments, all the while ensuring highly reliable, secure, and ultra-low-latency service performance guarantees.

Attack path discovery plays an important role in protecting network infrastructure. Unfortunately, previous attack path discovery algorithms are difficult for applying in reality because of the high computational complexity problem. To achieve effective attack path discovery, we proposed a compact graph planning algorithm to incorporate goal states related information into attack path discovery. Our model extracts goal states related information by calculating closure of goal states, and then construct planning graph structure given the closure, after which the backward search algorithm is used to extract the attack path solution. The experiments were done on the typical enterprise network, comparing the effectiveness of attack path discovery algorithms with existing known methods. The result turns out that our proposed compact graph planning algorithm shows great improvement in discovering attack paths.

Industrial/Engineering training act as a supportive role in developing students' working skills. However, traditional training only involves face-to-face learning environments. Therefore, enforcing learning among students with different learning speed would be difficult. In this work-in-progress paper, we proposed adopting the Flipped Classroom approach to an engineering training course (Internet of Things module). Students can have a flexible laboratory schedule in exploring on acquired technical skills. For streamlining the learning process, the “First Principles of Instruction” framework had been used for guiding the design of learning activities. Ways of adopting the framework for learning activity design had been described in details.

Recent researches in neural network models have shown great potential in image inpainting task, which focus on finding reasonable area from known content to predict missing pixel values of incomplete image and generate new images. However they still create distorted structures and textures that are inconsistent with surrounding areas and require further post processing to optimize the results. Especially for face repair problems, it is often necessary to generate semantically new images that contain a large number of appearance. In addition, many recent approaches limited their applications in the field center region inpainting, which have difficulties to repair border regions or large missing area. Motivated by these observations, we introduce dilated skip architecture, which combines the advantages of dilated convolution and U-net. With this combination, our proposed network can enlarge the perception area for better repairing, as well as preserve the completeness of the original image features during the repairing process. Experiments on CelebA show that our approach can effectively deal with image inpainting problems and obtain images with higher qualities than previous ones.

Traditional template attack is more severe to attack conditions. It requires a large amount of energy traces and plaintext and ciphertext pairs. In some cases, attackers cannot obtain plaintext or ciphertext so that traditional template attack fails. In this paper, Gaussian Mixture Clustering Algorithm is introduced to solve the problem, which enables attackers to still perform template attacks and relaxes the attack conditions. In addition, this paper uses a strategy to select appropriate plaintext to improve the accuracy of attacks.

Malicious insider attacks are a serious threat to organizations and governments today. To address this issue, a new user-centered machine learning based insider threat detection system has been proposed in this paper. The system operates on multiple data granularity levels, providing evaluations and analyses on normal and malicious insiders, as well as individual data instances. Insider scenario specific results and delay in detection are also reported and discussed.

The results of the evaluation show that the machine learning based detection system is able to learn from limited ground truth and accurately detect new malicious insiders. This highlights the importance of developing advanced detection systems that can identify insider threats before they cause significant damage to organizations.

In conclusion, this new framework provides a valuable contribution to the field of insider threat detection, demonstrating the efficacy of machine learning in predicting and preventing malicious insider activity. By leveraging cutting-edge technology, it is possible to develop smarter and more effective security measures that safeguard sensitive data and protect organizations against internal threat actors.

Indoor localization has been a hot topic in research for several years now, and more recent developments focus on device-free localization techniques. In this study, we aimed to enhance accuracy and robustness in relation to the device-free indoor-localization problem. Our survey included testing WiFi network signals for localization tasks, which resulted in achieving almost perfect accuracy. 

We built our experiments on top of recent works that also used WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) to test indoor localization accuracy at the room level. Our work involved evaluating achievable improvements using classical machine learning and deep learning models. 

Furthermore, we took into consideration the instability of CSI data because of its tendency to drift over time. Overall, our survey and experiments have shown promising results, particularly the potential of device-free localization techniques, which can have significant implications in various industries, including healthcare, security, and transportation.

The exchange of information between different scales is a crucial aspect of environmental sciences. Direct observations remain the primary source of fundamental information about natural phenomena. With this information, environmental scientists formulate hypotheses or scenarios to explain the workings of natural systems. Understanding the interactions between different components of a natural system requires models at varying scales.
