In this paper, we have reported an effective adoption of machine learning (ML) algorithms for wireless sensor networks (WSN) deployed for real-time monitoring and early warning of landslides. The WSN system performs real-time monitoring of landslide triggering parameters such as rainfall, soil moisture, pore-water-pressure (PWP), and movements. The challenges involved in landslide early warning and the data driven context for overcoming these challenges are being presented. Linear models were applied on real-time data from the WSN system and the data from laboratory experiments to discover the interrelationships existing between rain, soil, and moisture, PWP and construct the feature-set required for forecasting slope stability conditions. Two algorithms Current-PWP and 24-PWP based on the support vector regression (SVR) method is implemented for efficacious nowcast and 24 h forecast of the slope stability conditions for early warning notification of landslides. Comparison of the results from the Current-PWP and 24-PWP algorithms with the actual sensor measurements recorded by the WSN system revealed mean absolute error (MAE) values 4.2k and 4.7 kPa, respectively. The results section elaborates 1) on relevance of the Current-PWP algorithm towards ensuring the reliability of early warning WSN systems, constrained by data availability, 2) application of the 24-PWP algorithm to yield an additional duration of 24 h for landslide preparedness, 3) the empirical appraisal of the regression model from laboratory experiments for estimation of soil moisture from PWP, and vice versa, 4) the efficacy of multi-level decision making for the preclusion of false warnings, and 5) the timely early warnings issued from the proffered WSN system.

The sine cosine algorithm is a newly proposed optimization algorithm and it has shown remarkable performance in solving some optimization problems. However, its search ability deteriorates when facing complex problems because of premature convergence. To mitigate this drawback, we propose a population diversity based local refinement strategy to help it maintain population diversity in a high level. Twenty-nine test functions in CEC'17 benchmark suit is implemented to evaluate its performance. The experimental results indicate the flexibility of controlling diversity and the proposed strategy is promising to be applied to other algorithms.

This paper proposes a new method for congestion control in computer networks called Reactive Adaptive eXperience based congestion control (Rax). Rax utilizes online reinforcement learning (RL) to maintain an optimal congestion window in accordance with a given reward function based on current network conditions. To improve stability and convergence time, the proposed method employs a neural network-based approach that can be initialized with either random weights or a previously trained neural network. 

Since the arrival of acknowledgements in CC is delayed and received one-by-one, the processing of rewards is unsuitable for current Deep RL implementations. Therefore, the authors propose Partial Action Learning, a formulation of Deep RL that can handle delayed and partial rewards. The paper demonstrates that the proposed method converges to a stable, close-to-optimum solution within a few minutes of operation and outperforms existing CC algorithms in typical networks. The results indicate that Deep RL can be performed online and compete with conventional CC schemes, such as Cubic.

With the dramatic shrink of feature size and the advance of semiconductor technology nodes, numerous and complicated design rules need to be followed, and a chip design can only be taped-out after passing design rule check (DRC). The high design complexity seriously deteriorates design routability, which can be measured by the number of DRC violations after the detailed routing stage. In addition, a modern large-scaled design typically consists of many huge macros due to the wide use of intellectual properties (IPs). Empirically, the placement of these macros greatly determines routability, while there exists no effective cost metric to directly evaluate a macro placement because of the extremely high complexity and unpredictability of cell placement and routing. In this paper, we propose the first work of routability-driven macro placement with deep learning. A convolutional neural network (CNN)-based routability prediction model is proposed and embedded into a macro placer such that a good macro placement with minimized DRC violations can be derived through a simulated annealing (SA) optimization process. Experimental results show the accuracy of the predictor and the effectiveness of the macro placer.

Data aggregation is a key primitive in wireless sensor networks and refers to the process in which the sensed data are processed and aggregated en-route by intermediate sensor nodes. Since sensor nodes are commonly resource constrained, they may be compromised by attackers and instructed to launch various attacks. Despite the rich literature on secure data aggregation, most of the prior work focuses on detecting intermediate nodes from modifying partial aggregation results with two security challenges remaining. First, a compromised sensor node can report arbitrary reading of its own, which is fundamentally difficult to detect but widely considered to have limited impact on the final aggregation result. Second, a compromised sensor node can repeatedly attack the aggregation process to prevent the base station from receiving correct aggregation results, leading to a special form of Denial-of-Service attack. VMAT [1] (published in ICDCS 2011) is a representative secure data aggregation scheme with the capability of pinpointing and revoking compromised sensor nodes, which relies on a secure MIN aggregation scheme and converts other additive aggregation functions such as SUM and COUNT to MIN aggregations. In this paper, we introduce a novel enumeration attack against VMAT to highlight the security vulnerability of a sensor node reporting an arbitrary reading of its own. The enumeration attack allows a single compromised sensor node to significantly inflate the final aggregation result without being detected. As a countermeasure, we also introduce an effective defense against the enumeration attack. Theoretical analysis and simulation studies confirm the severe impact of the enumeration attack and the effectiveness of the countermeasure.

Leukemia originates in bone marrow. It massively affects the production of appropriate blood cells. Hence, its early detection is very crucial for human living. Generally, computational approaches for Leukemia detection use microscopic blood cells images. Then, machine learning based models are trained and tested for accurate measurement. The main challenge here is to achieve an acceptable accuracy with a scalable method. However, data inconsistency, missing values and data incompleteness made the researchers’ job much more difficult. In these consequences, this paper proposes a scalable Leukemia prediction method based on a publicly available ALL_IDB dataset using the HOG feature descriptor and Logistic Regression. Initially, the proposed method used Canny edge detector and noise reduction operators to detect the exact shape of Lymphocytes. Then, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to the detected image shapes. The PCA reduces the data dimensions without losing any valuable information and thus greatly minimizes the afterward computational cost. Finally, a classifier based model is produced for unforeseen events and it is tested. The results are validated using n-fold cross-validation technique, where n is a positive integer greater than or equal to three. The maximum average accuracy of the proposed model is 96% which is much higher than the state-of-the-art schemes.

The huge AC power girds of China have been all connected by dozens of HVDC links now. To understand the behavior of the complicated network and mechanism of interaction between AC and DC, there is a demand for a more precise simulation technology. Traditional power system analysis tools, such as electromechanical transient program and off-line electromagnetic transient program, the models of DC control and protections are simplified to some degree. Sometimes the simplification may not reflect the same act that grid may do as in the field. In order to get a detailed, panoramic view, it is believed that simulating the large-scale network model by electromagnetic transient software in real-time with actual DC control and protection devices linked will give a better performance. In this way, the simulation time step should be small enough so that the physical DC controllers can be connected to realize hybrid simulation. Normally, microsecond level is applied. However, running a tremendous AC/DC grid model of thousands of buses with a time step of microseconds is the precondition of digital-analog hybrid simulation, and also a great challenge to all experts in the field of power system real-time simulation of the world. Based on task mapping and parallel computing technology, power system real-time simulator HYPERSIM and supercomputer SGI UV300 are used in this paper to achieve the goal. Considering of the processor's computational capability, on account of naturally decoupling by long distributed parameter lines, this paper optimizes the method of large-scale grid decoupling, splits the sophisticated region grid model into distributed tasks reasonably. Exploring the automatic task mapping function in HYPERSIM, a synthetic method about multiple auto-assigned parameters optimization is proposed. Eventually, an electromagnetic transient network model of 17746 single phase buses can be operated in real-time, which is a breakthrough on scale expanding of real-time simulation. The precision of AC/DC grid simulation makes a step further. The realization of massive grid model real-time operation gives a new technical means for characteristic cognition, system planning, operating, decision-making and failure reproduction of Chinese future power system.

The conservation of tropical forests is an important social and ecological issue due to its vital role in the global ecosystem. The monitoring of forests is primarily conducted through the extraction and analysis of remote sensing imagery (RSI) information. Numerous studies have successfully classified remote sensing images using machine learning techniques. However, the traditional algorithms require a significant and representative training set, which can be costly, particularly in RSI where the imagery spectrum can vary based on the season and forest coverage. To tackle this issue, a semi-supervised learning approach, known as active learning (AL), has been proposed to efficiently develop training sets through iterative improvement of model performance. AL utilizes a user-defined heuristic to evaluate, rank, and label the most relevant unlabeled samples by an expert user, resulting in the construction of the training sets. In this study, we present two different AL approaches (Confidence Heuristics and Committee) for classifying remote sensing imagery. Our AL approaches achieve exceptional effectiveness results compared to the previous methods in the literature for two diverse datasets.

Blockchain has been regarded as a promising technology for IoT, since it provides significant solutions for decentralized networks that can address trust and security concerns, high maintenance cost problems, and so on. The decentralization provided by blockchain can be largely attributed to the use of a consensus mechanism, which enables peer-to-peer trading in a distributed manner without the involvement of any third party. This article starts by introducing the basic concept of blockchain and illustrating why a consensus mechanism plays an indispensable role in a blockchain enabled IoT system. Then we discuss the main ideas of two famous consensus mechanisms, PoW and PoS, and list their limitations in IoT. Next, two mainstream DAG based consensus mechanisms, the Tangle and Hashgraph, are reviewed to show why DAG consensus is more suitable for IoT system than PoW and PoS. Potential issues and challenges of DAG based consensus mechanisms to be addressed in the future are discussed in the last section.

Securing Internet of Things (IoT) devices and protecting their applications from privacy leaks is a challenge, due to their weak (computational and storage) capabilities, and their proximity with sensitive data. Considering the resource-constrains of such devices, their long lifetime, and the intermittent connections, classical security approaches are often too difficult or impractical to apply. Moving target defense is an established technique whose goal is to lower the attack surface to malicious users by constantly modifying device footprint. Changing the address to an IoT device without privacy leaks is, however, a nontrivial task. In this paper, we propose a novel method to perform a network-wide (Internet protocol and medium access control) address shuffling procedure, called address shuffling algorithm with HMAC (AShA), which is simple to implement, and whose network overhead is minimal. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we analyze our approach via theoretical analysis and simulations. Our analysis shows how AShA parameters can be adapted to various network sizes while our simulations results show how AShA can be used to successfully perform a global collision-free address renewal on networks of more than 2000 nodes using 16-bit addresses.

The system frequency is a very complex electromechanical variable in a power system. The complexity comes from an appropriate understanding of the phenomena related to the frequency creation and its measurement and estimation. The objective of this paper is to present a comprehensive explanation of the concept of frequency and its potential character in the operation and control of power systems. The significant contribution of this paper is an explanation of the electro-mechanical nature of the frequency, and the introduction of the non-pure frequency concept related to need to measure the frequency from the voltage signal at any bus and the pure-frequency coming from the electro-mechanical character of the frequency generated at the synchronous generators. An illustrative simulation example is used to demonstrate the two characters of the frequency proposed in this paper.

Position sensorless control of synchronous reluctance machines (SynRMs) is not easy due to nonlinear correlations caused by extensive magnetic saturation. Although the d-axis inductance that varies largely depending on the magnetic saturation is not required, the active flux (AF) method cannot utilize the q-axis current to estimate the rotor position. The fundamental saliency (FS) method can utilize both the d- and q-axis currents, but it suffers from a model mismatch that variable components of the inductances are not exactly sine or cosine functions of double the rotor position. This paper proposes the rotational frame fundamental saliency (RFFS) method which basically performs the FS method in the rotational frame. The RFFS method can overcome challenges regarding the model mismatch and utilize both currents for position estimation. Experimental verification revealed that the RFFS method improved torque accuracy at very low speed and increased the maximum torque for stable operation by exploiting both currents compared to the AF method.

Training operators for activities ran on automotive manufacturing lines is a long, thorough and laborious process that aims to generate a correct collection of information and actions as well as adequate staff training. Schooling operators has always been costly; therefore, developing an application will facilitate learning the necessary skills. The time until an operator will become productive will be significantly shorter and the exposure to certain risks will also be removed. Learning process can be monitorized for each operator, keeping track of his progress. This allows to estimate completion time of the training and to express an overview on future work activities. At the same time, the operator will acquire skills faster, which normally require long practice and a high level of dexterity. Thus, the authors' proposal is to develop an application for the operators training, within the manufacturing lines, aiming to experiment, in a virtual environment the simulation and the orderly assembly of objects as a stack form. Also, it will be necessary to develop a glove prototype that will have the ability to manipulate and control objects in a virtual environment. The end of this paper will reveal reasons for investing and implementing a new way of teaching, making use of such an application.

Traditional automated assessment of pathological speech involves two key steps: extracting features specific to the pathology and classifying or regressing the extracted features. However, the wide range of speech and language disorders makes the feature design process challenging but ultimately critical to the success of the assessment. This paper proposes an end-to-end method for automatic speech assessment of Cantonese-speaking individuals with aphasia. The assessment is framed as a binary classification task that distinguishes between PWA with low and high scores of subjective assessment. To accomplish this, a sequence-to-one GRU-RNN and CNN model is utilized to produce the end-to-end mapping from speech signals to classification results. The neural network model implicitly learns the speech features used for assessment. Preliminary experimental findings indicate that the end-to-end approach can achieve results that are comparable to the traditional two-step method. Additionally, the results suggest that the CNN model is better suited to this task than the sequence-to-one GRU-RNN model.

The purpose of this paper is to apply the finite element method (FEM) computation results to examine the flow field obstruction in nasal airway obstruction (NAO) patients, the consistency of the blocking site, and the elucidating the NAO phenomenon. In addition, the comparison between flow pattern of NAO patients and the healthy subject during a respiratory cycle was discussed in this article. The results of this research aimed to help optimize the treatment of NAO patients regarding the positioning and size of the surgical dissection.

Technological advancements in the field of Smart Systems are continuously expanding and are now being applied to various fields such as tourism. As a result, a smart system for Betawi culinary tourism has been developed by our researchers. However, identifying the traditional food names using images has been a challenge due to the varying shapes and directions of the images. To overcome this challenge, we have implemented deep learning architecture. However, selecting an effective architecture has also presented a problem. In response, we have compared several deep learning architectures to determine the most suitable for detecting culinary images. After conducting our experiments, it has been found that DenseNet169 provides the best performance in terms of accuracy, error rate, and training time when using a CPU, while ResNet50 is the ideal choice when utilizing a GPU.

One of the major challenges of hybrid cloud is discovering the most suitable cloud provider for scaling up applications, regardless of the non-standardized naming technologies. Currently, there is no framework for monitoring and recommending VM flavor during autoscaling based on utilization history. Administrators typically consider various heterogeneous sets of criteria and resource relationships to map cloud service providers for user preferences in hybrid environments. However, this manual intervention often results in underutilization because flavor selection remains constant, regardless of the application's resource usage in the hybrid cloud.

To overcome these limitations, a proposed framework has been developed that monitors applications and recommends flavors to adjust resource capacity at the lowest possible cost while maintaining stability and predictable performance. The framework employs the following techniques:

a) Predicting future workload using a deep learning technique, Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) with Long Short Term Memory (LSTM)

b) Recommending a flavor that aligns with optimized cost and Service Level Agreement (SLA) for the autoscale group depending on CPU or RAM utilization in the current and historical workloads.

c) Operating the recommended flavor on future workloads while ensuring zero application downtime in the current workload.

The proposed flavor recommender framework has been successfully implemented in hybrid cloud OpenStack and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Experimental results have shown a significant cost difference of 17.65% per hour on the autoscale group of instances using the proposed flavor recommender framework over traditional flavor selection.

Over the past few decades, LBP descriptor, which shown its high robustness in extracting discriminative features from an image, has been successfully applied in diverse challenging computer vision applications including face recognition. The efficiency and usability of the LBP operator and its success in various real world applications has inspired the development of much new powerful LBP variants. Indeed, after the appearance of the LBP operator, several renowned extensions and modifications of LBP have been proposed in the literature to the point that it can be difficult to recognize their respective LBP-related strategies, strengths and weaknesses according to a given application, and there is a need for a complete comparative study in face recognition application. This paper reviews the performance of 30 recent state-of-the-art handcrafted descriptors in face recognition through a comprehensive experimental study using widely used benchmarks. Simulated experiments on ORL, Extended Yale B and FERET databases proved that some evaluated descriptors realize good classification results which outperform many recent state-of-the-art face recognition systems.

In large scale mobile ad hoc networks, hierarchical routing by clustering of nodes is effective to reduce the load of routing. Since mobile ad hoc networks is autonomously structured, clustering must be realized in an autonomous manner. In our previous study, we have proposed an autonomous clustering technology, and have shown that stable clustering can be realized even in an environment where nodes move randomly. However, the number of nodes included in a cluster may tend to increase when user density increases like congestion in commuting hours around a train station. In this paper, by autonomously generating cluster-head nodes, we propose an autonomous clustering method. The proposed clustering can give stable cluster size that is adaptive even to dynamic environments where user density changes.

In this study, we conducted measurements on the time-variant vehicle-to-vehicle radio propagation channel in the frequency range of 59.75-60.25 GHz in an urban street in Vienna, Austria. Our experiment was aimed at investigating the impact of large overtaking vehicles on both the large-scale fading and small-scale fading, depending on the overtaking vehicle's position. We obtained a set of 30 vehicle-to-vehicle channel realizations during the experiment. Our results show that large overtaking vehicles can increase the mean receive power by up to 10 dB.

To analyze the small-scale fading of the channel, we found that the two-wave with diffuse power (TWDP) fading model was suitable for our experimental data. We also compared this model with the commonly-used Rician fading model to determine the regions where the TWDP model is preferable. Additionally, we analyzed the time selectivity of the vehicular channel, using a multitaper spectral estimator with discrete prolate spheroidal windows to determine the Doppler and delay resolutions. Based on our estimated local scattering function, we inferred the delay and Doppler profiles. We observed that spatial filtering by the transmitting horn antenna reduces the delay and Doppler spread values, which were found to be below one-tenth of the maximum Doppler shift (2f v/c), with a maximum RMS Doppler spread of 450 Hz and the largest observed RMS delay spread being 4 ns. 

In conclusion, our study provides valuable insights into the time-variant vehicle-to-vehicle radio propagation channel in an urban street. We found that large overtaking vehicles can significantly impact the receive power, and the TWDP fading model is preferred over the Rician fading model in certain regions. Our analysis of the vehicular channel's time selectivity highlights the importance of considering both delay and Doppler profiles in the design of vehicle-to-vehicle communication systems.

In this paper, we propose a novel semantic segmentation-based stereo reconstruction method that can keep up with the accuracy of the state-of-the art approaches while running in real time. The solution follows the classic stereo pipeline, each step in the stereo workflow being enhanced by additional information from semantic segmentation. Therefore, we introduce several improvements to computation, aggregation, and optimization by adapting existing techniques to integrate additional surface information given by each semantic class. For the cost computation and optimization steps, we propose new genetic algorithms that can incrementally adjust the parameters for better solutions. Furthermore, we propose a new post-processing edge-aware filtering technique relying on an improved convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture for disparity refinement. We obtain the competitive results at 30 frames/s, including segmentation.

Controller area networks (CANs) are vulnerable to attacks, such as frame falsifying attacks, as the electronic control units (ECUs) send and receive messages without any authentication or encryption. In this paper, a physical authentication scheme is proposed that exploits the voltage features of the ECU signals on the CAN bus. This scheme applies reinforcement learning to choose the authentication mode, including the protection level and test threshold, allowing a monitor node to optimize the authentication mode via trial-and-error without requiring knowledge of the CAN bus signal model or spoofing model. Furthermore, experimental results show that the proposed authentication scheme can significantly improve authentication accuracy and response compared with a benchmark scheme.

This paper proposes the use of Indirect Adaptive Control (IAC) philosophy to estimate Power System (PS) inertia. The method only requires frequency measurement from the Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) at the bus where inertia is being estimated, eliminating the need for additional system data or approximations. To implement IAC for inertia estimation, the swing equation of the synchronous generator is rearranged into a standard affine system form. The Radial Basis Function Network (RBFN) is used for swing equation emulation and feedback linearization technique generates control signals to track the desired frequency response. The parameters of the IAC structure are updated in real-time without prior knowledge. Results from Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) testing on the two area Prabha Kundur system demonstrate the accuracy of this approach.

Optical Character Recognition (OCR) of Arabic text from manuscripts images is virtually impossible, this is due to the semi-cursive nature of Arabic script which is very difficult to explore by algorithms and image processing methods.In this paper, we present a method of exploration and research in content of Arabic manuscript images. It's about characterizing segmented handwritten words with a set points of interest by providing a means of identification and research in these manuscripts. Each word segmented and described by key features will be compared to query words.The results of this method are encouraging in comparison with other methods, especially when it comes to the same of handwritten style used in the text.

Hemodialysis requires the insertion of a tube into the body to remove or deliver fluids. However, the cannulation process can lead to various problems if the needle punctures the bottom of the arteriovenous fistula or graft vessel wall. This is often due to a lack of skill in performing the various steps of cannulation such as palpation, needle entry, obtaining blood in the cannula, and threading the needle. 

To address this issue, a new method has been introduced for detecting needle insertion in a simulated fistula. This will enable assessment and training of cannulation skills, ensuring that the procedure is carried out more effectively. In initial validation studies, the algorithm was successful in detecting puncture within an average of 0.1 seconds and within 0.5 seconds in the worst case scenario. 

In the future, this needle insertion detection method will be incorporated into a simulator to objectively evaluate cannulation skills for hemodialysis. This will help to improve the quality of the procedure and reduce the incidence of complications.

With the great success of deep learning in computer vision, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based methods for object detection have garnered significant attention. However, building detection in remote sensing images poses a challenge due to the diversity of building orientations. To address this problem, this study integrates orientation regression into the axis-aligned bounding box and develops an algorithm to estimate the IOU overlap between arbitrarily oriented boxes for fast computation. CNN is used for feature extraction and bounding box regression, with the model trained to predict both orientation and location simultaneously. The proposed end-to-end model shows promising results in remote sensing images of different scales with higher mAP than the conventional method.

Controlling the propagation of electromagnetic waves through a dielectric medium is crucial for antenna miniaturization and beam-forming, and one efficient method to achieve this is by using a two-dimensional array of conducting strips on one side of a dielectric layer. In a recent study, researchers have introduced an innovative approach by embedding conducting micron-sized particles into the conducting strips. This approach allows for fine-tuned control of the EM response of the dielectric, which is achieved through the response of the particles to a magneto-static field.

The researchers demonstrated that when a field is applied, the particles within a dielectric cavity form columns in the direction of the field lines. As the particles are conducting, this results in conducting columns that connect various conducting strips. Notably, this approach does not require a directly connected biasing circuit, which allows for more flexibility in the placement of the particles in complex geometries. The theoretical and simulation results validate the effectiveness of this method.

In summary, embedding conducting micron-sized particles into conducting strips is a promising approach for controlling EM wave propagation through dielectric media. This method offers numerous advantages over traditional approaches and can be utilized for various applications in antenna design and beam-forming.

Mental workload (MW) assessment is important for numerous mentally-demanding applications, including first responders, air traffic control, amongst others, as it quantifies the cognitive capabilities of the operator. Recently, there has been a push for wearables based MW monitoring for real-time feedback and human performance augmentation. Most previous studies have focused on immobile subjects. Realistic applications, however, rely on ambulant users under varying types and levels of physical activity. Movement artifacts are known to hamper the quality of signals measured by wearable devices, thus the impact on MW assessment in situ is still unknown. In this study, we compare the performance of several automated artifact removal algorithms for electroencephalograms (EEG), as well as the robustness of two classical feature sets, for MW assessment under varying physical activity levels.

Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technology allows for effective communication between the brain and a machine. This innovative technology has been successfully used in epilepsy control by implementing a closed-loop system that focuses on seizure prediction and feedback treatment. Seizure prediction is a critical component of this approach, but it still faces several challenges.

To date, most existing seizure prediction methods have relied on empirical features, which are effective and easy to interpret but difficult to compose. Recent deep neural network-based approaches can learn effective features in a data-driven manner, but they often struggle to produce accurate predictions due to limited training data.

This paper proposes a methodology that combines empirical features with deep models to create effective seizure prediction techniques. The researchers design various deep architectures to integrate empirical features into different layers of the deep neural networks. The method is evaluated using data from nine patients in the Freiburg dataset, with the best average F1 score reaching 0.8622, demonstrating superior performance compared to both empirical features-based methods and deep neural networks.

The results also show that incorporating empirical features in the front layers of the network produces better seizure prediction performance. Overall, this approach provides a promising framework for improving automated seizure prediction technology in the future.

This article presents a solution to the problem of stabilizing the mobile elements of mobile robots during the transportation of goods. A neural network was developed using various types of perceptron in Python, tensorflow library, and its extension tflearn. The stabilization process of the technical system's mobile element position was simulated in the Open AI environment using the gym library. Data sets were formed for neural network training with subsequent training and testing of the neural network using Python and the gym library. Based on the test results, recommendations on the choice of neural network architecture for developing mobile object stabilization systems are provided.

It is a challenging task for computer systems to detect and interpret non-verbal cues. Despite extensive studies in the past decade, automatic recognition of emotions remains difficult. Most existing works focus on discrete stereotypical emotion categories, whereas we are interested in predicting continuous values of valence and arousal that are able to model a broader range of spontaneous emotions. Our goal is to analyze emotions in naturalist conditions, rather than controlled laboratory conditions. To achieve this, we propose to use tensor methods to leverage the structure in the data. These methods can preserve the structure and reduce the number of parameters in the models, improving computational performance. We investigate a Tucker Tensor Regression model with analytic solution and a deep, gradient based method called Tensor Regression Networks. We perform experiments on two public databases, AFEW-VA and SEWA, for facial affect estimation in-the-wild, in terms of valence and arousal levels. The experimental results demonstrate that tensor-based methods successfully leverage the data structure and outperform baseline methods on average.

Compressive sensing has been used in wideband spectrum sensing to achieve sub-Nyquist sampling. This involves utilizing prior information about the multiband spectrum occupancy, which can be obtained from a geo-location database. However, these priors can be incomplete and may also contain inaccuracies. To address this issue, we propose a compressive spectrum sensing (CSS) scheme that is robust to such imperfections in the priors. In addition, we present a novel and practical algorithm that can estimate the robust channel sparsity required by the CSS scheme.

Our simulations show that the proposed CSS scheme, which incorporates priors, yields a significant improvement in detection performance and requires lower iteration counts. This demonstrates the potential of our approach in enhancing the performance of CSS-based spectrum sensing in various applications.

The classic midpoint method for triangulation has been widely used for its speed but often criticized for its lack of accuracy. Our research investigates the cost function that the midpoint method minimizes and finds that it tends to underestimate the accuracy of measurements that are taken at a relatively far distance from the 3-D point. To address this issue, we have enhanced the cost function by introducing a weighting system that assigns a weight to each measurement, inversely proportional to the distance between the 3-D point and the corresponding camera center. 

By analyzing the gradient of the modified cost function, we propose to use fixed-point iterations to minimize it. This new method, called the iteratively reweighted midpoint method, is shown to have an approximation to Newton's method near the optimal point, thus inheriting the quadratic convergence rate. Our theoretical study also indicates that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art.

Our experimental results, using both synthetic and real datasets, demonstrate that the iteratively reweighted midpoint method is more efficient while achieving the same level of accuracy as the existing methods. Overall, our proposed method is a significant improvement over the classic midpoint method and holds great potential for various applications in computer vision and robotics.

This paper proposes an artificial neural network (ANN) technique, using an adaptive batch training rule-based principle with weight and bias, to estimate and predict the adaptive threshold-based detection of the received molecular signals based on the current cumulative concentrations. The proposed technique considers a single transmitter (Tx Bio-NM) and a single receiver (Rx Bio-NM) biological nanomachines to exchange the molecular packets through diffusion-based molecular communication (DMC) channel. This scheme is suitable for binary On-OFF keying (BOOK signaling); where the Rx Bio-NM adapts the 1/0-bit detection threshold based on all previous received bits to alleviate the inter-symbol interference (ISI) problem and reception noise. We evaluate the proposed technique in term of the bit error rate (BER), complexity cost and molecular throughput. The performance evaluation in various noisy channel sources shows a promising improvement in the un-coded BER and a slight number of molecules in transmission can be achieved extremely massive throughput of the DMC system compared to the other threshold detection schemes in the literature.

Building automation is increasingly used to minimize energy consumption and increasing comfort and flexibility in buildings. When the KNX Association was founded in 1999 the need for security was quite low. Systems were usually not connected to the internet and so the standard lacks of nowadays common security requirements. To get an idea where the most serious problems are located in installations we present in this paper a method to calculate a risk for the different network segments. Without limiting the generality KNX is used as one example of fieldbuses. The basic concepts in the communication of fieldbus devices are present in KNX and the results can easily be transferred to other fieldbus protocols.

Community detection methods pose a meaningful and challenging task in today's era of social big data. Typically, the data can be represented as a streaming graph, on which two machine learning techniques can be adopted. One such method is the time slice-based approach, which is time-consuming as the algorithms need to run repeatedly on each time slice. On the other hand, the incremental method may yield lower community detection accuracy since the algorithm frequently needs to update results for new data points. This paper proposes an incremental community detection method that balances the above limitations. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is much efficient than the time slices based one and more effective compared with other incremental community detection methods.

In this paper, we present a YOLO model for real-time recognition and localization of valve types on an experimental test bench unit. The camera captures video data in a hydrogen sulfide laboratory, and the model is designed to recognize valves and their positions from continuous video frames with input required after a specified period. The YOLO model is capable of identifying the type of valve labels based on a single frame. We demonstrate that pre-processing of training images plays a critical role in the performance of the YOLO model, and we utilize the concept of anchor and intersection over union (IOU) to achieve high accuracy. Over a specific time of the video stream, we show the valve type results achieved by our model. Our model has an average loss error value of less than 6 percentage, and the IOU between the predicted bounding box and the real bounding box in the final iterations is almost 95 percentage.

Nowadays, public traffic safety highly values the physiological status of a driver. One of the crucial indicators of a driver's health is their heart rate (HR). However, using traditional contact-type devices to measure HR could distract or make the driver uncomfortable. Instead, remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) technique using a web-camera is a better way to monitor the driver's HR without interference. Although most rPPG studies are focused on reducing facial motion or luminance changes, not much has been discussed on outdoor scenarios. Therefore, this paper proposes an enhancement to the rPPG technique suitable for outdoor driving scenarios and under different weather conditions. The proposed approach utilizes an artificial neural network (ANN) and trains multiple personalized ANN models for each driver. Additionally, an adaptive neural network model selection (ANNMS) approach is proposed to predict the driver's HR beat more accurately based on different noise conditions. The algorithm eliminates noise effects caused by facial luminance variations in eight outdoor driving scenarios. The proposed monitoring system is evaluated against state-of-the-art rPPG techniques, and the results show that the ANNMS reduces the mean absolute error from 14.71 bpm to 4.51 bpm and enhances the success-rate-10 from 44.1% to 91.5%.

Clap-clap switches find applications in various domains such as automation and security. A clap sound can be used as a triggering signal either to switch the relays on/off, or as an alert signal for security system. However, the sound is very directive and sensitive to noise floor. Also, being an impulse, it is difficult to distinguish between a clap and other similar impulsive sounds like bang, dog-barking, coughing, etc. We propose a device for detecting clap sound which can also distinguish it from other impulsive sounds. We have used band-pass filtering in frequency domain and correlation in time domain to effectively detect and distinguish clap sound from other sounds.

E-commerce is a business activity that uses modern information technology to process cash flow and logistics to achieve transactions. Under the e-commerce environment, an item can reach to the customer accurately is a key factor to enhance the company's image. Therefore, how to efficiently select the algorithm to solve the vehicle routing problem is an urgent problem to be solved. Aiming at the problems existing in the logistics distribution of e-commerce, this paper combines the genetic algorithm with the conservation algorithm based on the maximum travelable distance of the vehicle, and uses the conservation algorithm to generate the initial solution of the genetic algorithm, and constructs the conservation genetic algorithm to solve the e-commerce environment logistics distribution path optimization problem. The simulation results show that the conservation genetic algorithm is more globally optimal than the genetic algorithm.

The visual fidelity of bleeding simulation in a surgical simulator is critical since it will affect not only the degree of visual realism, but also the user's medical judgment and treatment in real-life settings. The conventional marching cubes surface rendering algorithm provides excellent visual effect in rendering gushing blood, however, it is insufficient for blood flow, which is very common in surgical procedures, since in this case the rendered surface and depth textures of blood are rough. In this paper, we propose a new method called the mixed depth rendering for rendering blood flow in surgical simulation. A smooth height field is created to minimize the height difference between neighboring particles on the bleeding surface. The color and transparency of each bleeding area are determined by the number of bleeding particles, which is consistent with the real visual effect. In addition, there is no much extra computational cost. The rendering of blood flow in a variety of surgical scenarios shows that visual feedback is much improved. The proposed mixed depth rendering method is also used in a neurosurgery simulator that we developed.

We present a modification of the Hegselmann-Krause model for opinion dynamics that takes into account external factors which may prevent interaction between certain pairs of agents. By incorporating a physical connectivity graph, we relax the assumption that every agent has knowledge of every other agent's opinion at all points in time. Contrary to the original Hegselmann-Krause dynamics which terminate in finite time, our model shows that for any connected but not complete underlying graph, there exists an initial condition under which the dynamics never terminate. Furthermore, we prove that for any continuous probability density function with the state space as its support, the expected termination time of our modified dynamics is infinity. Finally, we analyze the rate of convergence to the steady state and provide bounds on the maximum convergence time in terms of the properties of the physical connectivity graph.

Inspired by TOPSIS, we propose a new multi-attribute decision-making method for the interval normal type-2 fuzzy set environment. To obtain the ideal solutions, we define the expected value of INT2FS. Next, we use the Euclidean distance of INT2FS to depict the similarity between each alternative and ideal solutions. To demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach, we apply it to a supplier selection problem.

Failures, referred to as "incidences" by Airbus DS, can result in significant delays and costs for the company during aircraft testing. To address this issue, our team at the Electronic Technology Department in Spain collaborated with Airbus DS to develop a data mining framework for predicting incidences in the ground testing process of the A400M aircraft. The goal of this framework is to minimize the impact of failures on testing timelines and costs.

Urban trees provide essential ecosystem services such as regulating temperature and humidity, filtering urban pollutants, and improving air quality. However, increasing numbers of urban trees pose maintenance and public safety issues, resulting in a total compensatory value of more than $2 trillion USD for inspection, maintenance, and settlement of damages. At present, there is no known research on automated tree health assessment. The Internet of Things (IoT) offers a viable solution for deployment of wireless sensors and networks. This paper presents a concept of urban IoT trees, with various sensors for automated health monitoring and assessment. An Urban Tree Health Index (UTHI) is designed to facilitate preventive measures by indicating the health of urban IoT trees. To construct the indexing model, 7 dynamic (time-series) and 7 static features are extracted to explore the ambient effects on urban tree health. A Heterogeneous Neural Network (HNN) is introduced to analyze dynamic and static features in separate layers, and a fusion layer is applied to aggregate output from all layers, allowing exploration of unseen correlations among all features. Experimental results show that the HNN-based model achieves high accuracy and fitness, with an error rate of less than 5%, and outperforms other machine learning algorithms by 34% to 66%. The developed model is significant in that all indexing features can be predefined or monitored by IoT sensors, enabling automated and economic urban tree management.

The exponential growth of movie production around the world highlights the importance of predicting a movie's success. With billions of dollars invested in each movie, it has become essential to have prior knowledge of a movie's potential success or failure and the factors that affect it. For production houses, this information is critical as it helps in planning advertising and campaign strategies, which are an expensive affair. Hence, in this proposed research, we analyze the Internet Movie Database (IMDb) to predict a movie's IMDb score. The IMDb database contains categorical and numerical information, including the movie's director, budget, gross, and IMDb score. Our research proposes an efficient approach to predict IMDb scores before a movie's release, instead of relying solely on critics and others to predict its success. We aim to uncover the significant factors that influence a movie's IMDb score and have used various algorithms for analysis. Among all the algorithms, the Random Forest algorithm provided the best prediction accuracy. In our exploratory analysis, we found that the number of voted users, number of critics' reviews, number of Facebook likes, movie duration, and gross collection of a movie significantly affect its IMDb score. Drama and Biopic are the best movie genres to watch out for.

To address the issue of insufficient manual tuning for arc suppression coils, a fuzzy controller has been designed based on the principles of fuzzy control theory. By using the compensation network turning-off degree error as the input language variable and the arc suppression coil as the output language variable, a state query scale was established through fuzzy reasoning. This enabled automatic tuning to be achieved through computer searches at the state query scale, rendering the necessary equipment relatively simple and easy to acquire. The transition from manual to automatic tuning through this new trial approach has significant practical implications.

According to current energy efficiency labels, the majority of light-emitting diode (LED) lamps on the market are considered as highly efficient devices. This makes it difficult to distinguish between lamps with different operational characteristics and performance. This paper introduces a comprehensive experimental-based labeling methodology for comparing LED lamp performance with reference to two additional important characteristics: light flicker and power factor. The new labeling methodology reveals that there is high diversity between different LED lamps with different circuit topologies but also for a given topology with different design choices. General consumers and design engineers can benefit from the simple and clear information presented by the set of comparative labels when comparing LED lamp performance.

Major part of internet users are devices which are connected to each other on the internet and are exchanging data with internet brokers to receive requested services. Managing and accounting well to IoT requests needs maximum processing power, speed in data transfer and proper combining services in minimum time. This many devices in IoT, made solving problems in this area to use abilities and facilities of cloud environment. Hence combining services in cloud environment is paid attention recently. In this research we want to give an algorithm with approach of improving factors propounded in the problem combining service composition problem like number of clouds involved in giving services, number of services studied before fulfilling users requests and load balance between clouds. In this paper we use the factor, similarity measure, to find the most suitable cloud and composition plan in each phase which in addition to improving QoS metrics propounded in previous papers, it caused improving QoS metric of load balancing between clouds, prevention of formation of bottleneck in clouds entrance, decreasing the probability of temporarily failing of any of clouds and consequently increasing the users' satisfaction.

Automatic detection of risk areas is a critical requirement for both indoor and outdoor video surveillance systems. This technology serves as an essential tool for detecting potential dangers and providing timely warnings in the case of an imminent threat. For instance, swimming pools are a significant hazard, especially for children. Accidental drownings are the second leading cause of death among individuals under the age of 15, just after traffic accidents. Hence, the aim of this paper is to propose an automated method to detect aquatic risk zones with precision. 

We propose an innovative approach that leverages color and texture indices to segment water surfaces accurately. Our chromatic detection technique relies on empirically established color and brightness values in the HSV color space. On the other hand, we employ textural detection by analyzing the local shape properties of the water surface. Specifically, we calculate the variance and use the local binary pattern method. 

To validate our approach, we conducted several experiments on a proprietary image database containing pool images captured during the daytime. The results of the experiments demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in detecting aquatic risk zones with precision. As such, our proposed method holds promising potential for enhancing the safety of individuals around swimming pools, especially children who are more vulnerable to accidents.

Process controls (basic as well as advanced) are implemented within the process control system, which may mean a distributed control system (DCS), programmable logic controller (PLC), and/or a supervisory control computer. DCSs and PLCs are typically industrially hardened and fault-tolerant. Supervisory control computers are often not hardened or fault-tolerant, but they bring a higher level of computational capability to the control system, to host valuable, but not critical, advanced control applications. Advanced controls may reside in either the DCS or the supervisory computer, depending on the application. Basic controls reside in the DCS and its subsystems, including PLCs. Because we usually deal with real - world systems with real - world constraints (cost, computer resources, size, weight, power, heat dissipation, etc.), it is understood that the simplest method to accomplish a task is the one that should be used. Experts usually rely on common sense when they solve problems. They also use vague and ambiguous terms. Other experts have no difficulties with understanding and interpreting this statement because they have the background to hearing problems described like this. However, a knowledge engineer would have difficulties providing a computer with the same level of understanding. In a complex industrial process, how can we represent expert knowledge that uses vague and fuzzy terms in a computer to control it? In this context, the application is developed to control the pretreatment and pasteurization station of milk localized in Batna (Algeria) by adopting a control approach based on expert knowledge and fuzzy logic.

Time-Step method and Station-Pair method are prominent techniques for estimation of spatial gradients. Since GBAS is meant to serve a limited area of about 50km of an airport for aircraft Precision Approach and landing, these two methods were considered for gradient estimation within the GBAS service area. Much of the work on these techniques has been reported for GPS-based GBAS applications. In this paper, the suitability of these methods to IRNSS-based GBAS applications is investigated. It is observed that since IRNSS satellites are either GEO or GSO, the time interval (At), of Time-Step method should be significantly high (30min for GSO), to obtain gradient data for GBAS' service area. With the Station-Pair method, a dense network of stations, each separated by not more than 1-2 kms is required.

The detection of moving objects in stationary cameras has been extensively researched, however, this problem remains challenging for cameras with general motion. This is due to the fact that the movement of the target is linked with the motion of the camera platform as well as the scene structure. In addition, if thermal cameras are used, this problem can become even more complicated. This paper proposes an effective moving object detection technique for image sequences captured via a UAV's thermal camera. 

The proposed method involves extracting sparse feature trajectories of the thermal images in each adaptive sliding window of frames. This is followed by a group sparsity constrained low-rank decomposition to detect foreground in the trajectory domain. To evaluate the proposed method, the study includes three challenging thermal image sequences that reflect real-world settings alongside the VIVID sequence, as there is currently no standard benchmark dataset available for the freely moving thermal camera case. 

The results showed that the proposed method effectively detects moving objects and outperformed many other available methods.

The use of Metacognitive Training System (MTS) in Indonesia is still in its early stages. However, a prototype of the system has been developed and implemented at Universitas Gadjah Mada. In order to make it a widely used product, it is crucial to test it on a larger scale. This is done to gather user impressions about the system.

To achieve this, we conducted User Experience (UX) measurement for the developed MTS on a larger scale, involving 90 undergraduate students of informatics education at Universitas Negeri Malang. Two UX measurement methods were utilized, User Experience Questionnaires (UEQ) and short-interviews. UEQ was used to obtain general impressions, while short-interviews were conducted to gain more in-depth feedback regarding the efficiency of MTS in their studies.

The UX measurement result was very positive, with Attractiveness, Efficiency, and Stimulation categorized as excellent. More than 75% respondents gave positive answers in five questions asked during the interview. With these results, it can be concluded that MTS is ready to be widely used as a massive product.

In conclusion, the UX measurement for the developed MTS on a larger scale has proven its efficacy in improving the quality of higher education. It is expected to be implemented in other universities across Indonesia for the purpose of enhancing the students’ metacognitive skills.

Machine learning (ML)-based traffic classification has been gaining increasing importance due to the declining port-based and payload-based approaches. However, the packet-level method is the most common measure used in the previous works, which requires additional hardware device to manage and monitor, increasing cost as well as extra works of the network personnel. In this paper, we propose a methodology to build an efficient classifier from NetFlow which is the widely applied monitoring solution among network operators in the form of flow-level. First, we analyze the per-application performance through the C4.5 decision tree with the features derived from the NetFlow records. The result shows that the accuracy obtained is as good as the packet-level method. We further propose the ensemble feature selection (FS) method to improve the classification accuracy and to reduce the computational complexity. Lastly, we present the clustering-based under-sampling combining with synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) approach to solving the problem of the concept drift and the imbalanced dataset, and we extract insights and recommendation for practical application. With the combination of proposed methods, the experiment result reports high F-measure over two traces containing the wide range of applications with low computational complexity.

With the widespread application of deep learning systems, the robustness of deep neural networks (DNNs) is received increasing attentions recently. By studying the distribution of neurons outputs in DNN models, we found that the behavior patterns of neurons are different for different kinds of DNNs' inputs, e.g. test cases generated by different adversarial attack techniques. In this paper, we extract the neuron behavior patterns of DNNs under different adversarial attack techniques, use them as the guidance for test case selection. Experimental results show that this method is more efficient than random technology.

This paper introduces a chattering-free, adaptive, and robust tracking control scheme for a class of second-order nonlinear systems with uncertain dynamics. First, a proportional-integral-derivative control-fast terminal sliding function is proposed to enable the advantages of both the PID and non-singular fast terminal sliding mode approaches in the field of non-singularity, fast convergence time, defined time convergence, and stability with small steady-state errors. Second, to obtain the desired control target without chattering behavior, the proposed controller with a continuous approach has been applied. In detail, the proposed controller uses an integral of a switching term and an adaptive updating law to compensate the lumped system uncertainty (e.g., disturbances, unmodeled dynamics, nonlinearities, or unmeasurable noise). Our proposed controller does not require knowledge about bound values of those anonymous components. The robust behavior and the defined time convergence have been demonstrated rigorously by the Lyapunov principle. Finally, the position tracking computer simulations have been performed to demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of the suggested controller.

Cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, Litecoin and Ethereum remain unpredictable when it comes to their value, making it difficult for investors to make decisions. Therefore, it would be beneficial if a model could predict the future nature of the crypto market. This study aims to build a time-series model using Long Short-Term Memory Networks to help determine the value of cryptocurrencies in the future.

The study considers three cryptocurrencies - Bitcoin, Litecoin and Ethereum. As a comparison, opinion mining is used to interpret the mood of the market on the current day for different currencies. The sentiment scores obtained from the natural language processing of textual data are used as features in the model to predict future values. The time-series charts are plotted using the Plotly library in Python for graphical representation.

To evaluate the model's effectiveness, the Mean Absolute Error is calculated between the actual and predicted values. Additionally, uncertainty quantification methods are used to compare the present-day scenario of the market using opinion mining.

In conclusion, this study demonstrates the potential benefits of using a Long Short-Term Memory Network model for predicting the value of cryptocurrencies in the future. The comparison with opinion mining shows promising results. Further research can be conducted to enhance the model's accuracy and reliability.

A novel technique to recognize full range of shapes of Arabic handwritten characters is presented. This is done by combining statistical and structural approaches for character recognition. The statistical method first recognizes the main body of a character using modified direction features and Support Vector Machines. Then in structural classification, dot-descriptors are used to recognize the exact shape of an Arabic character. On IfN/ENIT benchmarking database, we achieved 96.71% accuracy for character main-bodies and 94.52% accuracy on the complete characters. Our results compare favorably with the state of the art.

Electric vehicle time-sharing rental is a novel urban transportation plan that aims to alleviate parking difficulties and enhance vehicle utilization. Nonetheless, simulating the pre-operation process and testing the rationality of data settings for electric vehicle rental expenses, vehicle and rental site numbers, and others can be challenging. Therefore, this paper proposes a virtual service system based on multi-agent technology for electric vehicle time-sharing rental. This system factors in complex user situations, such as range anxiety and accidental failure, temperature effects, and road condition effects. Additionally, simulation data predicts load capacity and financial accounting, laying a solid foundation for further studies on the efficient operation of urban electric vehicle time-sharing systems.

The ability to accurately estimate worst-case execution time (WCET) for multicores is crucial for avoiding costly timing violations. This is particularly important when integrating software from different providers onto critical systems. One existing methodology involves creating surrogate applications by executing target applications in isolation. These surrogate applications can then be used to estimate the upperbound multicore contention delay and generate WCET estimates. However, this methodology has only been tested on simulation environments. In this paper, we present our work on adapting this methodology to a real multicore processor for the space domain.

Electronic devices have been dabbled into houses to perform automatic tasks and fulfill different needs such as illumination, cooking, air conditioning, surveillance, among others. Furthermore, those elements can collect data from the environment in order to be processed and give better products and services, so, Internet of Things capabilities arises to home, highly cohesive with domotics. However, for developing countries, smart appliances are expensive, and old fridges, washing machines, etc., are still operative, so they must not to be discarded. Other very used appliances are stoves, which work with heating methods like electrical resistances, electrical induction or natural gas. The last one is the most used in a plenty of countries, due to its advantages regarding cost, for instance. Nonetheless, bad manipulation can cause gas leakages, and furthermore, injuries to people and conflagrations, affecting human lives and assets. Thus, a need has been identified regarding gas safety of gas stoves, conserving the installed base. This work shows the results of the main research and design considerations of a new cutting-edge technology that protects people of bad manipulation of already installed or new gas stoves, including the Internet of Things in order to monitor in real-time possible gas leakages and take actions.

In recent years, there has been increasing interest in automatic modulation classification (AMC) for both civilian and military applications. However, conventional AMC schemes have been primarily developed under the assumption of Gaussian noise, which has been widely challenged by the emergence of non-Gaussian noise in different wireless networked systems.

To address this issue, a novel modulation classification method has been proposed in this paper using cyclic correntropy spectrum (CCES) and deep residual neural network (ResNet). CCES is used to effectively suppress non-Gaussian noise while providing different CCES graphs for various modulation schemes, enabling AMC to operate directly without further feature extraction.

Moreover, an end-to-end deep ResNet-based AMC has been developed based on the CCES graphs, enabling the classification of correct modulation by iteratively evaluating the residual information in multiple learning layers. The proposed algorithm outperforms existing designs with much higher classification accuracy, requiring 3 dB less in the necessary generalized signal-to-noise ratio for 100% accuracy, even in non-Gaussian noise environments.

This paper outlines an innovative approach for conducting full-text searches on files that are stored in a MongoDB database and GridFS system. The solution is comprised of two main components: an API Rest interface that handles requests, and a MongoDB database that manages storage. A simple web application is also included to show how the system can be used. With no reliance on any external full-text engines, this solution is self-contained and can be easily integrated into existing document management systems or enterprise applications. By providing the ability to search file contents based on free-form text, it has the potential to significantly enhance the search capabilities of any system that relies on MongoDB for storage.

Clustering is a crucial aspect of data mining and machine learning. The density peaks clustering (DPC) algorithm is an important density-based clustering method for handling non-spherical clusters. However, the traditional methods of calculating local density and measuring distance may not consider the correlation and similarity between samples, and manual parameter setting can greatly impact clustering results, rendering DPC less effective for high-dimensional data sets. To address these issues, this paper introduces an adaptive DPC algorithm with Fisher linear discriminant, termed ADPC-FLD, for clustering complex data sets. 

The proposed algorithm includes several new features. Local density is calculated using a kernel density estimation function, and the weighted Euclidean distance function employs Pearson correlation coefficient to measure distance between samples, to consider both spatial structure and correlation. Novel density estimation entropy is introduced to adaptively select density estimation parameters based on distribution characteristics of the data. An adaptive strategy of cluster center selection is implemented to avoid selecting noise data as cluster centers and uncertainty in manual selection. Finally, Fisher linear discriminant is used to remove unnecessary information and reduce dimensionality of high-dimensional data, followed by the implementation of ADPC on synthetic, UCI, and gene expression data sets for comparison with related algorithms. 

The experimental results on 26 data sets indicate that the proposed algorithm outperforms several relevant clustering approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

Mist computing puts computing on the very edge of the network. With mist computing, the computation is performed in users' devices (smartphones, laptops, etc.) sensors or wearables (something fairly common in the context of the Internet of Things). Devices which are near may be part of a mist where each of these devices contributes to computation tasks. Each of them has computation capabilities which can be used in order to run tasks from other devices. However, devices in the network must be aware of available features in order to execute tasks within a device with the necessary hardware requirements. There is a compatibility problem between tasks and devices: not all devices satisfy all tasks needs. This article proposes a mist computing framework in order to tackle this compatibility problem.

Splat and antisplat events are commonly observed in three-dimensional turbulent flow fields. When fluid locally impacts an impermeable surface, splats occur, transferring energy from the normal component to the tangential velocity components. Antisplats, on the other hand, relate to the inverted situation. These events have a significant impact on various flow properties, including the transfer of kinetic energy between velocity components and the transfer of heat. Studying splat and antisplat events can provide new insight into these issues.

In this study, we propose the first Lagrangian method for detecting splat and antisplat events as features of an unsteady flow field. Using the concept of strain tensors on flow-embedded flat surfaces, our method effectively extracts disjoint regions where splat and antisplat events of arbitrary scale occur. To validate the method, we tested it on artificially generated flow fields of increasing complexity.

The results showed that our method can efficiently and reliably identify splat and antisplat events even in complex situations. We then used the method to analyze application data obtained from a direct numerical simulation of turbulent flow over a backward facing step. Our findings demonstrate that the proposed method is well-suited for the analysis of turbulent flows and provides a valuable tool for investigating splat and antisplat events.

With the emergence of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the growth of cloud computing technology, electronic health systems have become a significant and active domain, enabling the development of medical practices at an affordable cost. However, preserving the security and privacy of sensitive user information has become a crucial concern. To convince users to move their health record data to cloud networks, strong and secure access control schemes must be employed to protect their data.

Access control schemes play a critical role in protecting e-Health records, where several policies coexist to provide security and privacy in a network. Hence, retaining a secure access to health cloud services is an essential target of this work. In this paper, we propose a certificate-based access control strategy, introducing an access method for e-health cloud primarily based on trust assessment.

The proposed scheme integrates the trust concept with the monitoring process to ensure more security in access control. This approach's methodology is explained through appropriate evaluation results, improving system security and performance by minimizing the time needed to access services and optimizing overall system resource utilization.

As the next generation of the power system, smart grid develops towards automated and intellectualized. Along with the benefits brought by smart grids, e.g., improved energy conversion rate, power utilization rate, and power supply quality, are the security challenges. One of the most important issues in smart grids is to ensure reliable communication between the secondary equipment. The state-of-art method to ensure smart grid security is to detect cyber attacks by deep learning. However, due to the small number of negative samples, the performance of the detection system is limited. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that utilizes the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to generate abundant negative samples, which helps to improve the performance of the state-of-art detection system. The evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively improve the performance of the detection system by 4%.

One significant problem in the analysis of social networks (SN) is identifying the most influential members. This is a non-deterministic polynomial (NP-hard) problem, as proven by researchers. Influence maximization (IM) is the process of maximizing the spread of influence throughout the network and it involves an optimization problem. IM is a fundamental research problem in social networks as it is critical to social influence analysis. The influence maximization problem involves selecting a subset of k users as seed nodes in a graph to maximize the expected number of influenced users. 

In this study, centrality-based methods are employed to select the top k nodes based on their centrality values. Degree centrality is used to identify opinion leaders, while between-ness and Eigenvector centrality is used to choose early adopters. To avoid time complexity, a heuristic approach known as degree discount is suggested instead of Greedy algorithms utilized in other studies. In this study, a mixed diffusion model replaces the linear threshold and independent cascade models to be the main diffusion model.

Overall, this study provides new insights into identifying influential members in SNs by proposing a novel approach that uses centrality-based methods and a mixed diffusion model.

As aspects of our daily lives become more interconnected with the emergence of the Internet of Things (IoT), it is imperative that our devices are reliable and secure from threats. Vulnerabilities of Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA/WPA2) have been exposed in the past, motivating the use of multiple security techniques, even with the release of WPA3. Physical layer security leverages existing components of communication systems to enable methods of protecting devices that are well-suited for IoT applications. In this work, we provide a low-complexity technique for generating secret keys at the Physical layer to enable improved IoT security. We leverage the existing carrier frequency offset (CFO) and channel estimation components of Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) receivers for an efficient approach. The key generation algorithm we propose focuses on the unique CFO and channel experienced between a pair of desired nodes, and to the best of our understanding, the combination of the features has not been examined previously for the purpose of secret key generation. Our techniques are appropriate for IoT devices, as they do not require extensive processing capabilities and are based on second order statistics. We obtain experimental results using USRP N210 software defined radios and analyze the performance of our methods in post-processing. Our techniques improve the capability of desired nodes to establish matching secret keys, while hindering the threat of an eavesdropper, and are useful for protecting future IoT devices.

The Cascaded H-bridge topology is commonly utilized in grid-tied converters for battery energy storage systems due to its modular structure. However, to fully exploit the modularity of the converter, a hierarchical distributed control architecture is proposed. The architecture involves primary and secondary control. The primary control guarantees accurate current tracking, which may lead to unequal power output across the modules. Thus, the secondary control employs a distributed consensus algorithm to balance the power output across the modules.

Additionally, a carrier phase shift control is implemented to achieve multilevel output voltage and reduce harmonic distortion. The efficiency of this novel control strategy is confirmed through various experiments.

This paper proposes a novel method for predicting the magnetic field distribution and electromagnetic performance in surface-mounted permanent-magnet machines. The method is based on the principle that the magnetic potential drop in nonlinear iron can be replaced by equivalent current sheets on linear iron edges. To this end, a nonlinear subdomain and magnet circuit hybrid model (SMCHM) is introduced.
