The SMCHM computes the values of current sheets from a magnetic circuit and uses them as boundary conditions in the subdomain model. The proposed method is validated through finite element (FE) simulations, and the results show that the SMCHM can accurately predict the magnetic field distribution and electromagnetic performance, comparable to the nonlinear FE method. Notably, the accuracy of the SMCHM is significantly higher than the conventional subdomain model, which neglects nonlinearity effects. Moreover, the computation speed of the SMCHM is dramatically faster than that of the FE model. In conclusion, the proposed SMCHM is an effective and efficient method for predicting the magnetic field distribution and electromagnetic performance in surface-mounted permanent-magnet machines.

Modern approaches to motor rehabilitation for severe upper limb paralysis in chronic stroke involve decoding movements from the electromyography for controlling rehabilitation orthoses. However, muscle fatigue is a phenomenon that can interfere with these neurophysiological signals and reduce decoding accuracy. Thus, a better understanding of how potential signal changes during rehabilitation training affect decoding accuracy could improve outcomes. This study investigated the evolution of electromyographic indices of muscle fatigue in the Deltoid Anterior muscle during typical forward reaching movements of rehabilitation training in healthy subjects and a stroke patient. The findings indicated that muscle fatigue in healthy subjects caused changes in the neurophysiological signal, while no consistent change was observed in the patient over several sessions.

The health status of core router systems needs to be analyzed efficiently in order to ensure high reliability and timely error recovery. Although a large amount operational data is collected from core routers, due to high computational complexity and expensive labor cost, only a small part of this data is labeled by experts. The lack of labels is an impediment toward the adoption of supervised learning. We present an iterative self-learning procedure for assessing the health status of a core router. This procedure first computes a representative feature matrix to capture different characteristics of time-series data. Not only statistical-modeling-based features are computed from three general categories but also a recurrent neural network-based autoencoder is utilized to capture a wider range of hidden patterns. Moreover, both minimum-redundancy-maximum-relevance (mRMR) method and fully connected feedforward autoencoder are applied to further reduce dimensionality of extracted feature matrix. Hierarchical clustering is then utilized to infer labels for the unlabeled dataset. Finally, a classifier is built and iteratively updated using both labeled and unlabeled dataset. Field data collected from a set of commercial core routers are used to experimentally validate the proposed health-status analyzer. The experimental results show that the proposed feature-based self-learning health analyzer achieves higher precision and recall than the traditional supervised health analyzer as well the currently deployed rule-based health analyzer. Moreover, it achieves better performance than the three anomaly detection baseline methods under the transformed binary classification scenario.

In this research paper, we analyzed what moments and activities make people happy, based on a collection of happy moments. We are focusing on specific happy moments from a collection of text responses that people have shared through the crowd-sourcing platform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk). Using crowd-sourcing to collect our data allows us to advance our understanding of the cause of happiness, by focusing on words and real human experiences. Workers of MTurk were asked to reflect on what makes them happy in a given period and share three specific moments in complete sentences. Through text-based analysis, we will look to see what other components have a role in making a specific event happy and further analyze how we can classify such words. Also, we dive deeper into specific subcategories of classifiers in an attempt to form insights about their happiness level based on specific factors. With the goal to extract features from the text in HappyDB, in this study we used the bag of words approach. Through doing so, our results were successful at predicting the happiness category, concerning both accuracy and context. Our models were able to accomplish the goal of understanding a happy moment and fit such a moment into one of the seven ground truth happiness categories we set at the beginning of this study. We finished the article with the ethical perspective of such research works and related social implications.

The emergence of Cloud Native Microservices has resulted in new challenges, particularly in understanding and monitoring the complex and dynamic distributed systems that now power web applications. To address this, our team has developed an observability framework for microservices orchestration, which aims to provide a clear understanding of the internal behavior of microservices at various layers, lifetimes, and abstraction levels.

Using a cloud-based infrastructure, this demonstration showcases our observability framework, which can be accessed via a web-browser front-end. Our framework not only provides real-time visibility into the behavior of microservices, but it also facilitates root-cause analysis and enables users to make informed decisions concerning operations and performance optimization.

In summary, our observability framework is an essential tool for anyone operating Cloud Native Microservices. By providing deep insight into the behavior of microservices, our framework enables users to optimize performance, improve uptime, and effectively coordinate deployments across complex, distributed systems.

This paper presents a novel approach to multilabel classification of High-Voltage (HV) discharges captured using the Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) method for HV machines. The method involves feature extraction from EMI time signals emitted during the discharge events, utilizing 1D-Local Binary Pattern (LBP) and 1D-Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) techniques, and combining them to provide a feature vector. This feature vector is then implemented in a naive Bayes classifier that is designed to identify the labels of two or more discharge sources present within a single signal. The proposed approach is evaluated using various metrics, including average precision, accuracy, specificity, hamming loss, etc.

The results of this study demonstrate successful performance that is comparable to similar applications in other fields such as biology and image processing. This first attempt at multilabel classification of EMI discharge sources opens up new possibilities for research in the field of HV condition monitoring.

Intelligent Virtual Agents (IVAs) are becoming part of our everyday life, thanks to artificial intelligence technology and Internet of Things devices. For example, users can control their connected home appliances through natural voice commands to the IVA. However, most current-state commercial IVAs, such as Amazon Alexa, mainly focus on voice commands and voice feedback, and lack the ability to provide non-verbal cues which are an important part of social interaction. Augmented Reality (AR) has the potential to overcome this challenge by providing a visual embodiment of the IVA. In this paper we investigate how visual embodiment and social behaviors influence the perception of the IVA. We hypothesize that a user's confidence in an IVA's ability to perform tasks is improved when imbuing the agent with a human body and social behaviors compared to the agent solely depending on voice feedback. In other words, an agent's embodied gesture and locomotion behavior exhibiting awareness of the surrounding real world or exerting influence over the environment can improve the perceived social presence with and confidence in the agent. We present a human-subject study, in which we evaluated the hypothesis and compared different forms of IVAs with speech, gesturing, and locomotion behaviors in an interactive AR scenario. The results show support for the hypothesis with measures of confidence, trust, and social presence. We discuss implications for future developments in the field of IVAs.

In this paper, we present an I/O efficient distributed approximation framework to support approximations on arbitrary sub-datasets of a large dataset. Due to the prohibitive storage overhead of caching offline samples for each sub-dataset, existing offline sample-based systems provide high accuracy results for only a limited number of sub-datasets, such as the popular ones. On the other hand, current online sample-based approximation systems, which generate samples at runtime, do not take into account the uneven storage distribution of a sub-dataset. They work well for uniform distribution of a sub-dataset while suffer low I/O efficiency and poor estimation accuracy on unevenly distributed sub-datasets. To address the problem, we develop a distribution aware method called CLAP (cluster sampling based approximation). Our idea is to collect the occurrences of a sub-dataset at each logical partition of a dataset (storage distribution) in the distributed system, and make good use of such information to enable I/O efficient online sampling. There are three thrusts in CLAP. First, we develop a probabilistic map to reduce the exponential number of recorded sub-datasets to a linear one. Second, we apply the cluster sampling with unequal probability theory to implement a distribution-aware method for efficient online sampling for a single or multiple sub-datasets. Third, we enrich CLAP support with more complex approximations such as ratio and regression using bootstrap based estimation beyond the simple aggragation approxiamtions. Forth, we add an option in CLAP to allow users specifying a target error bound when submitting an approximation job. Fifth, we quantitatively derive the optimal sampling unit size in a distributed file system by associating it with approximation costs and accuracy. We have implemented CLAP into Hadoop as an example system and open sourced it on GitHub. Our comprehensive experimental results show that CLAP can achieve a speedup by up to 20× over the precise execution.

This study focuses on the problem of robotic grasping and introduces an estimator based on the Particle Swarm (PS) algorithm to improve the inference speed and accuracy of grasping points by a convolutional neural network (CNN). The PS algorithm's cost function considers two critical aspects - the classification of features as good or bad grasping features by a CNN and the use of a magnet mechanism to encourage particle convergence towards the object center. Furthermore, the algorithm uses a confidence factor to prevent misinterpretation between one and none grasping points. The results of the experiment showed a slight improvement in accuracy but a significant increase in inference speed. Unlike previous deep-learning methods, this approach is practical for robotic grasping applications.

Solid State Drives (SSDs) are popularly used for caching in large scale cloud storage systems nowadays. Traditionally, most cache algorithms make replacement at each miss when cache space is full. However, we observe that in a typical Cloud Block Storage (CBS), there is a great percentage of blocks with large reuse distances, which would result in large number of blocks being evicted out of the cache before they ever have a chance to be referenced while they are cached, significantly jeopardizing the cache efficiency. In this paper, we propose LEA, Lazy Eviction cache Algorithm, for cloud block storage to efficiently remedy the cache inefficiencies caused by cache blocks with large reuse distances. Specifically, LEA uses two lists, Lazy Eviction List (LEL) and Block Identity List (BIL). When a cache miss happens, if the candidate evicted-block has not resided in cache for longer than its reuse distance, LEA inserts the missed block identity into BIL. Otherwise, it inserts the missed block entry into LEL. We have evaluated LEA by using IO traces collected from Tencent, one of the largest network service providers in the world, and several open source traces. Experimental results show that LEA not only outperforms most of the state-of-the-art cache algorithms in hit ratio, but also reduces the number of SSD writes greatly.

VLSI design teams often face the challenge of reusing legacy RTL code that has been optimized for specific tasks within a given set of constraints. Unfortunately, these constraints cannot always be applied to future projects, leading to a lack of reusability. In order to address this issue, this study presents a method to abstract RTL descriptions into synthesizable behavioral descriptions, allowing for the generation of new micro-architectures with desired characteristics. The presented optimizations, which include array merging and loop fusing, produce a larger number of micro-architectures compared to current RTL to C compilers, resulting in increased re-usability of designs. The experimental results show that this optimization method is efficient in extending the variety of micro-architectures and consequently improving reusability.

The prevalence of Cloud Computing has appealed many users to put their business into low-cost and flexible cloud servers instead of bare-metal machines. Most virtual machines in the cloud run commodity operating system(e.g., linux), and the complexity of such operating systems makes them more bug-prone and easier to be compromised. To mitigate the security threats, previous works attempt to mediate and filter system calls, transform all unpopular paths into popular paths, or implement a nested kernel along with the untrusted outter kernel to enforce certain security policies. However, such solutions only enforce read-only protection or assume that popular paths in the kernel to contain almost no bug, which is not always the case in the real world. To overcome their shortcomings and combine their advantages as much as possible, we propose a hardware-assisted isolation mechanism that isolates untrusted part of the kernel. To achieve isolation, we prepare multiple restricted Extended Page Table (EPT) during boot time, each of which has certain critical data unmapped from it so that the code executing in the isolated environment could not access sensitive data. We leverage the VMFUNC instruction already available in recent Intel processors to directly switch to another pre-defined EPT inside guest virtual machine without trapping into the underlying hypervisor, which is faster than the traditional trap-and-emulate procedure. The semantic gap is minimized and real-time check is achieved by allowing EPT violations to be converted to Virtualization Exception (VE), which could be handled inside guest kernel in non-root mode. Our preliminary evaluation shows that with hardware virtualization feature, we are able to run the untrusted code in an isolated environment with negligible overhead.

The categorization of body types and measurement of human body has become an important tool for assessing health risks over the past century. Initially, the interest in body shape and anthropometrics was limited to mathematicians who established the "average man" concept, outlining the ideal proportion of the typical male during the 18th century. Later, the concept evolved into Body Mass Index (BMI), which was created by life insurance companies to assess the risk of fatality. The BMI methodology has been extensively used in various applications, including health and well-being industries, government policies, and national health surveys. Nevertheless, in recent years, the reliability of BMI has been called into question due to the limited parameters used to categorize an individual's body type. In some cases, BMI either overestimates or underestimates the category in which an individual falls. In order to address this issue, a non-invasive measurement tool has been developed using synthetic data sets that incorporate population characteristic models. The data sets are analyzed using machine learning models, specifically regression of anthropometric measures from images captured by depth sensors like Kinect. This approach is expected to enhance the accuracy of BMI measurements significantly.

The mobile edge caching is a promising way to reduce the user-perceived delay and improve the transmission data rates for the wireless networks. However, the cache capacities of base stations (BSs) tend to be limited and users' interests for the contents are diverse, which makes the content placement decision critical for the network performance optimization. Besides, due to the flexible user-BS association, it is more complicated to optimize the content delivery and placement which are coupled with each other. This paper investigates the content placement and content delivery strategies in the cache-enabled wireless networks. In particular, the effective capacity, which can characterize the end-to-end user-perceived delay and data rates simultaneously, is introduced as the user's utility metric. As the content caching and content delivery operate in different time-scales, they are investigated separately. For the content caching, a content placement problem is formulated, where both users' different active levels and diverse content preferences are considered. Due to the NP-hard nature, the problem is decomposed into two sub-problems, and an iterative association-aware content placement algorithm is proposed. For the content delivery, the user-BS association problem is formulated, and a cache-aware user-BS association algorithm is designed. The performance of the proposed algorithms is evaluated based on the simulations. The numerical results show that the proposed algorithms have a better capability to cope with users' diverse active levels, and achieve a better performance in terms of effective capacity and fairness level, compared with the existing algorithms.

This paper discusses the application of a nonlinear memristor-based neural network and circuit-based learning system. The neural network's weights are based on the memristor bridge synapse while the learning architecture is designed in an analog-digital mixed circuit. To overcome the nonlinearity issue in weight programming at the extremes due to the boundary effect of memristors, a modified memristor bridge synapse architecture is proposed, which shifts the programming origin to the middle of the linear region. The proposed method is tested using a multilayer neural network with the end-to-end learning architecture for classical learning problems. The simulation results demonstrate successful learning and correct behavior of replicated neural network, showing the effectiveness of the proposed method.

In recent years, development of an underwater observation system that is low cost and easy to operate is greatly required with the expansion of demand for marine resources survey acquiring rare metal and so on. The authors developed a free-fall type observation system of which body is glass sphere. Since the glass sphere has durability for high hydrodynamic pressure, retailed camera is able to be set inside the sphere to motion the sea environment. However, the positioning of the observation system is severe problem, because sinking motion is only provided by gravity or tidal force. To realize a low cost measurement system, we try to use MEMS IMU (Micro Electro Mechanical Systems Inertial Measurement Unit) for position estimation. The position by MEMS IMU has sensor noise and caused in large estimation error. In this paper, to reduce the estimation error, we propose the combination of optical range sensor. By adopting light rather than ultrasonic for range sensor, it is easy to adapt to systems using glass spheres. At first, sensor noise is modeled by allan variance calculated from measured stationary data, position estimation simulation using the modeled sensor data was performed. By adding the ranging data, the standard deviation of the position estimation can be reduced in (x, y) = (28.8%, 4.43%) with comparison of estimation by the sensor data of MEMS IMU and the depth sensor.

Handwritten digit recognition is a crucial step in various computer vision and machine learning applications. It is used extensively to read check numbers, among other practical applications. However, creating a computerized system that can recognize different individuals' unique handwriting is a challenging task. The selection of the appropriate classifiers and features significantly impacts classification accuracy. 

In this paper, we compare the performance of three classification algorithms - Naive Bayes, Multilayer Perceptron, and K_Star algorithm based on CFS - using the NIST handwritten dataset. Our objective is to identify the best classifier with acceptable accuracy using a minimal number of selected features. We evaluated the performance of each classifier individually using precision, recall, and F-measure.

Our results demonstrate that the K_Star algorithm provides a higher recognition rate at 82.36% than Naive Bayes and Multilayer Perceptron. Therefore, it is the best classifier among the three, making it a promising candidate for handwritten digit recognition tasks in the future.

The spatial and temporal distribution of active users across a given region greatly affects the activity of base stations (BSs) and the cumulative interference in a wireless network. In this letter, we propose a new approach for spatio-temporal analysis of wireless networks wherein stochastic geometry is used for the spatial domain and ON/OFF traffic models are used for the temporal domain. We illustrate the proposed approach through a mix of file transfer protocol (FTP) and video streaming (VS) traffic. With the aid of semi-Markov process, we derive the stationary probability for a given service request. Further, we develop a joint spatio-temporal model for the distribution of active users under a random BS.

This paper presents a novel nonlinear dictionary learning (DL) model to address the energy disaggregation (ED) problem, i.e., decomposing the electricity signal of a home to its operating devices. First, ED is modeled as a new temporal DL problem where a set of dictionary atoms is learned to capture the most representative temporal features of electricity signals. The sparse codes corresponding to these atoms show the contribution of each device in the total electricity consumption. To learn powerful atoms, a novel deep temporal DL (DTDL) model is proposed that computes complex nonlinear dictionaries in the latent space of a long short-term memory autoencoder (LSTM-AE). While the LSTM-AE captures the deep temporal manifold of electricity signals, the DTDL model finds the most representative atoms inside this manifold. To simultaneously optimize the dictionary and the deep temporal manifold, a new optimization algorithm is proposed that alternates between finding the optimal LSTM-AE and the optimal dictionary. To the best of authors' knowledge, DTDL is the only DL model that understands the deep temporal structures of the data. Experiments on the Reference ED Data Set show an outstanding performance compared with the recent state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of precision, recall, accuracy, and F-score.

Cancer detection is a significant application of clinical microarray data. One of the major challenges in microarrays is high dimensionality, where the majority of genes have no importance or contribution to class prediction. This results in a need for a considerable amount of resources and memory to process these genes. Therefore, reducing the number of dimensions becomes crucial in predicting cancer. This paper introduces a gene selection method that utilizes data complexity measures on microarray gene expression cancer data. Two measures of overlap, namely Fisher discriminant ratio and attribute efficiency, are applied to rank the genes based on their importance, and high-ranking genes are considered crucial in cancer diagnosis. Five well-known binary microarray cancer data are evaluated using three different classifiers, namely Decision Tree (DT), Naïve Bayes (NB), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN). Two approaches for gene selection are considered, including the fisher-based and (attribute +fisher)-based methods. The results indicate that the model created by genes selected using the fisher-based method can detect cancerous samples with high accuracy.

Epidural electrical stimulation (ECS) combined with rehabilitative training could improve behavioral function for stroke both in clinical and animal studies. Though the primary motor cortex (M1) ECS has some effects on recovery, the performance are not good enough and better sites for stimulation need further investigation. In this study, we compared the effects of ECS on M1 and premotor cortex (PM). Twelve rats were trained to the single-pellet retrieval (SPR) task before receiving photothrombotic ischemia model and electrodes implantation. They were randomly distributed to three groups: M1 stimulation, PM stimulation and no stimulation (Control) groups. The 100Hz monopolar cathodal stimulation were given concurrent with rehabilitation training over recovery days. The performance on SPR task were scored for analysis. Our results showed that M1 ECS had a better effect on behavioral improvement compared to the other two groups.

The emergence of Industry 4.0 revolution has increased the availability of data from various engineering components providing extensive information on different aspects of the industry. In the context of reliability and efficiency, features extracted from data can be utilized to predict performance degradation and optimizing product service as well as determining remaining useful life. The need for prediction models able to establish correlations between related variables and measured variables becomes obvious. In this work, a data driven approach is developed using a state machine concept to realize a lifetime model able to deal with the variability and uncertainties of industrial data. This concept provides a systematic solution for a system exposed to multi-state degradation by enabling the system to identify appropriate parameters autonomously, according to the state it belongs to. Due to the flexibility and scalability, this model can easily be deployed to various types of industrial data. Impressive findings using data from agricultural experiments validate the adaptability and potential of this approach as an alternative modeling strategy.

Raw signal simulation is an important tool to test the effectiveness of the system parameters and imaging algorithms. A fast raw signal simulation method for multi-circular synthetic aperture imaging is proposed based on the inverse processing of the imaging algorithm and the nonuniform fast Fourier transform. The analytical description and processing procedure are presented. Simulation results of an ideal point target and a human model demonstrate the validity and effectiveness. Compared with the common time-domain method, the proposed method can achieve equivalent performance with higher efficiency.

Correntropy has recently attracted great attention because of its robustness to non-Gaussian noise. Inspired by this robustness property, a spline adaptive filtering algorithm based on the maximum correntropy criterion (SAF-MCC) has been proposed. However, the steady-state convergence performance of the SAF-MCC has not been studied. This brief presents a steady-state performance analysis of the SAF-MCC for Gaussian and non-Gaussian noise. We derive and discuss the theoretical excess mean square error (EMSE) under these cases. Monte Carlo simulations are presented to corroborate the theoretical performance analysis results developed in this brief.

This paper presents a system applied in the automatic driving train using Case Based Reasoning (CBR) with Differential Evolution (DE). CBR was used to retrieve, reuse and revise experiences from real data during the journey. The DE was used to adapt the cases retrieved and optimize then considering multi-objective optimization. For this purpose, a train driving simulator used and the results compared the data of real train driving scenarios. Multi-objective optimization was used to reduce fuel consumption and also travel time. The results obtained concerning fuel consumption was entirely satisfactory because in some cases average savings of 45% in fuel consumption about the results obtained by human drivers. Adapting cases using the Differential Evolution approach led to a 5% gain in consumption over an adaptation of cases using Genetic Algorithm. It should also note that the time required for case adaptation was lower using Differential Evolution Algorithm than using Genetic Algorithm.

One of the main functions of battery management system (BMS) is to determine the current charge level, an incorrect estimate of which can lead to unforeseen situations in the operation of various communication systems. Due to the complexity of the analytical model of multi-cell lithium-ion storage devices, when developing algorithms for controlling them, it is effective to use fuzzy inference systems (FIS) that allow for the correction of the state of the charge level. The article presents the results, further improvement of such systems by combining several FIS depending on the state of the battery, which increases the accuracy of determining the charge state of the lithium-ion energy storage by modern BMS.

The increasing demands of users for better communication have resulted in mobile operators increasing the density of their base stations. However, the conventional static base station deployment is not always economical, especially in cases of short and infrequent peak loads. This is where unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can be used as flying base stations (FlyBSs) to effectively substitute the dense deployment of SBSs. In this paper, we propose an algorithm that identifies the most suitable SBS/FlyBS for users and determines the optimal positions of all FlyBSs to maximize user satisfaction with data rates. We investigate the performance of two proposed approaches based on genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) for joint association and positioning. Results indicate that both solutions outperform the competitive approach in terms of user satisfaction. Moreover, we show trade-offs between the GA and the PSO; while the PSO has lower complexity than the GA, the GA requires a slightly lower number of active FlyBSs to meet user demands.

An efficient representation of observed data has many benefits in various domains of engineering and science. Representing static data sets, such as images, is a living branch in machine learning and eases downstream tasks, such as classification, regression, or decision making. However, the representation of dynamical systems has received less attention. In this work, we develop a method to represent a dynamical system efficiently as a combination of a state and a local model, which fulfills a criterion inspired by the minimum description length (MDL) principle. The MDL principle is used in machine learning and statistics to quantify the trade-off between the ability to explain seen data and the model complexity. Networked control systems are a prominent example, where such a representation is beneficial. When many agents share a network, information exchange is costly and should thus happen only when necessary. We empirically show the efficiency of the proposed encoding for several dynamical systems and demonstrate reduced communication for event-triggered state estimation problems.

A competing risks model is a reliability system made up of two or more components with more than one failure mode. In this type of system, if any of the components fail, the whole system fails. Because the components are part of the same system, they may be correlated. In this study, we analyze a competing risks model with k failure modes whose lifetimes follow a joint k-variate Marshall-Olkin Weibull distribution. The data is multiply censored, meaning that the failure mode causing the failure of the system may not be observed.

To estimate the parameters and standard errors in this situation, we use the maximum likelihood approach via expectation-maximization algorithm with the missing information principle. We develop statistical inference methods for the model parameters, mean time to failure, and quantiles of the failure time for both the system and the components. To evaluate our proposed method, we conduct a simulation study and successfully apply it to two real datasets with two components.

Overall, our study presents a practical approach for analyzing competing risks models with censored data, which can be applied to a wide range of reliability systems with multiple failure modes.

Channel Coding has been one of the central disciplines driving the success stories of current generation LTE systems and beyond. In particular, turbo codes are mostly used for cellular and other applications where a reliable data transfer is required for latency-constrained communication in the presence of data-corrupting noise. However, the decoding algorithm for turbo codes is computationally intensive and thereby limiting its applicability in hand-held devices. In this paper, we study the feasibility of using Deep Learning (DL) architectures based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for encoding and decoding of turbo codes. In this regard, we simulate and use data from various stages of the transmission chain (turbo encoder output, Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channel output, demodulator output) to train our proposed RNN architecture and compare its performance to the conventional turbo encoder/decoder algorithms. Simulation results show, that the proposed RNN model outperforms the decoding performance of a conventional turbo decoder at low Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) regions.

Sentiment analysis is the study area in Natural language processing (NLP) that is concerned to identify the mood or opinion with in the text. This paper emphasizes on the different methods utilized for classifying the natural language text reviews in accordance with opinions expressed in text to analyze whether the extensive behavior is negative, positive or neutral. The abundance of discussion platforms, Weblogs, product reviews sites, e-commerce and social networking sites have encouraged stream of thoughts and articulation of opinions. Social media is considered to be a big platform of sentiments, reviews and opinion evaluation. Data used in this study are online product reviews collected from twitter and used to rank the best classifier for sentiments. The method of analysis on polarity classification was discussed in experimental work by using well known classifiers including Naïve byes, Support vector machine and Logistic regression for predicting the user reviews.

The theory of Rough set has proposed a method for approximating concepts by using a pair of thresholds on probability to defined three regions, namely, the positive, boundary and negative regions. These three regions generate three-way decision rules, which are acceptance, deferment and rejection decisions. In fact, the decision environment is prone to dynamic with the data changed continuously. As such, the three regions of a target decision will be changed inevitably. There are having been many studies on methods for incremental updating three-way decisions by adding or deleting objects in different threads. In this paper, we combine addition and deletion operators in a single updating step for three-way decisions in incomplete information system and mathematically proof our proposed methods.

Estimating requirements development effort is a critical activity in the software development process. Producing an accurate estimate, however, is extremely difficult, especially in the early stages of the software development process, where no clear and no complete description of the desired software behavior is available, hence leading to an estimate process with a high level of uncertainty. To handle this issue, in this paper, we present REEE (Requirements Elicitation Effort Estimation) - a framework for incrementally estimating software requirements elicitation efforts. We first categorize a project in terms of project's domain, different types of project parameters and requirements - functional requirements (FRs), non-functional requirements (NFRs), constraints and domain properties (DPs), while taking into consideration relationships among them. We then present an incremental approach to software requirements elicitation effort estimation that uses similar past projects in a case-based reasoning (CBR) model. In this approach, semantic similarity is quantified, once classification and normalization of requirements are done. To see the strengths and limitations of REEE, a dataset of 36(students') projects have been analyzed. Experimental results show that the use of REEE is a viable alternative to other cost estimation techniques, and can provide better results, with less uncertainty, for requirements elicitation effort estimation.

Extracting useful relationships from domain-specific texts, for later use, is not an easy task, especially when it comes to railroad accidents. These accidents have cost the US over $4.6B from 2001 to 2016. The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) mandates railroads to submit accident reports, which include a fixed field representing the primary cause of the accident (with 389 coded variables), and a narrative field with a short description of the accident. However, the medical terminologies used in the narrative field are often hard to comprehend, and as such, providing an assisting method to fill in the primary cause from such narratives would help to label accident causes more accurately. Additionally, it is crucial to determine whether the reported accident cause corresponds to the narrative description. To tackle these questions, we have applied deep learning techniques and powerful word embeddings such as Word2Vec and GloVe to classify accident causes for the primary cause field, using the text in the narratives. Our results show that such approaches can accurately classify accident causes based on report narratives and uncover inconsistencies in accident reporting, making them a valuable tool for transportation safety.

This manuscript explores the evolving roles of semiconductors in the development of autonomous driving in the context of Vehicle IoT and deep learning. The rise of autonomous driving is transforming the transportation industry with shorter product life cycles and new modes of business profitability, which presents both opportunities and challenges for semiconductor companies. As a result, these companies must adapt their business models to keep pace with changing technologies and markets.

As a novel signal control method, signal Cooperative Control with traffic Supply and Demand (CCSD) is superior to the traditional control methods and could satisfy the control requirements under all traffic conditions. However, the optimization solution of CCSD cannot meet the real-time control requirement for its exhaustive search. To overcome the problem, in this paper, the optimization problem of CCSD is reconstructed by the time-varying traffic supply and demand, and the problem is reduced as a problem of space search. Then, the krill herd (KH) algorithm is introduced and employed to realize the fast solution of CCSD (named KH-CCSD). During the process of optimization, the search space representation and fitness function for the KH algorithm are constructed to satisfy the solution of CCSD. The optimal signal timing plan is obtained by an iterated search of krill swarm in a multi-dimensional time-varying space cooperatively constrained by traffic supplies and demands. The convergence and effectiveness of KH-CCSD are validated by comparing experiments, in which the convergence of KH-CCSD is tested by different initializations and KH-CCSD is compared with the Webster method and capacity-aware back-pressure (CABP) control under unsaturated, saturated, and oversaturated conditions. The experiments results show that KH-CCSD performs a fast convergence and KH-CCSD is superior to the Webster method and CABP. As a result, KH-CCSD could satisfy the application of CCSD under all traffic conditions.

The rising popularity of ride-hailing services such as Uber has given drivers new opportunities for high-income earning. However, to increase their earnings, many drivers resort to taking on more trips, which can lead to increased stress levels and, in serious cases, poor driving quality and accidents. Since each driver handles stress differently, personalized trip recommendations are necessary to minimize the adverse effects of stress on driving.

In this paper, we leverage historical trip data and vehicle-mounted GPS and inertial sensors to compute driving stress and its impact on different driving behavioral features. We use a Multi-task Learning based Neural Network model to learn both common and personalized driving features and predict each driver's stress level. We also establish a causal relationship between stress levels and driving behavior to develop a trip recommendation system that helps drivers avoid stress driving.

Our models were tested on publicly available datasets with 6 drivers and an in-house dataset collected from 8 drivers over a 5-month period spanning 1700 trips. On average, our proposed models yielded a prediction accuracy of 94% with minimal false-positive rates. We also observed that recommended trips helped boost driving behavior among the drivers.

High-voltage circuit breaker is one of the most critical equipment in power system, and the operating mechanism fault is the main fault state of circuit breaker. This paper uses the coil current and K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN) classification methodology for diagnosing and recognizing the operating mechanism fault of circuit breaker. Firstly, to collect the coil current of normal state and common fault states, we conduct an experiment to simulate three common fault working states of operating mechanism from a 126kV SF6 circuit breaker; extract the feature vectors from the different states according to the characteristic of the close coil current; and, use KNN classification algorithm to establish the fault diagnosis model. Finally, we use the testing samples to verify the diagnosis model. The result shows that the new proposal can diagnose and recognize the fault states of the high-voltage circuit-breaker operating mechanism objectively, accurately and effectively.

Multiple-antenna devices are set to play a significant role in 5G wireless communications. However, it is imperative to ensure that such devices comply with safety regulations and standards with regards to Specific Absorption Rate (SAR). We previously introduced a fast technique to estimate the maximum SAR of such devices.

This paper aims to address practical issues that could affect the accuracy of the estimation of maximum SAR of multiple-antenna devices. Key issues include incorrect phase setting, imprecise probe re-positioning, choosing “area scans,” and simplified assumptions during the estimation process.

Incorrect phase setting can significantly impact the measurements taken during the estimation process, as an incorrect setting could lead to different SAR values. To ensure accurate measurements, it is essential to have the correct phase settings.

The placement of the probe during measurement is also crucial. Imprudent probe re-positioning can lead to inaccurate measurements since the position of the probe influences the SAR values. As such, following a set protocol for probe positioning can minimize errors.

When conducting scans, choosing “area scans” (i.e. scanning an entire area) versus “point scans” (i.e. scanning at particular points) can impact the accuracy of the measurements taken. Area scans provide a more comprehensive estimate of the SAR, but it can be challenging to ensure that all points have been scanned correctly.

Finally, it is essential to note that the estimation process often relies on simplified assumptions. Some notable assumptions include assuming that the antennas are of equal dimensions or that the antennas are spaced equally. While these assumptions can simplify the estimation process, it is vital to recognize that in reality, the antennas may differ in dimensions and placement.

Overall, determining the maximum SAR of multiple-antenna devices is essential to ensure compliance with safety regulations and standards. Addressing the practical issues outlined in this paper can improve the accuracy of the estimation process.

Introduction:

This paper presents a graph computation-based power flow algorithm designed to solve large-scale AC/DC hybrid systems with multiple LCC (Line Commuter Converter) based DC grids. The proposed approach focuses on improving the computational efficiency of constructing related matrices and obtaining power flow results without altering the existing sequential iteration method.

Methodology:

The hybrid system is modeled as a graph of vertices and edges that contains relevant topology and parameter information. This enables local computation to be performed independently for formulating mismatch vectors of ΔP, ΔQ, Δθ, ΔV, as well as matrices of B', and B", only with parameters associated with its linked edges and adjacent vertices.

By leveraging hierarchical parallel computing, the fast decoupled power flow (FDPF) of the AC system, calculation of DC grids, and mismatch comparisons for each iteration of the sequential method can be done in parallel. The proposed method is implemented on a graph database platform and tested on IEEE 300-Bus, modified South Carolina 500-Bus system, and a Chinese system to verify its accuracy and time-saving performance.

Results:

The graph computation-based power flow algorithm exhibits superior time-saving performance as compared to traditional power flow algorithms. This method can solve large-scale AC/DC hybrid systems with multiple LCC based DC grids with high accuracy and efficiency.

Conclusion:

The proposed graph computation-based power flow algorithm is a viable solution to the computational challenges posed by the large-scale AC/DC hybrid systems with multiple LCC-based DC grids. Its advantages lie in constructing related matrices and getting power flow results without modifying the conventional sequential iteration method.

In recent years, Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) has been extensively researched in various languages because it aims to detect the sentiment of each aspect of the text. The ABSA problem can be divided into three subtasks as follow: the aspect detection, Opinion Target Expression (OTE) and Sentiment Polarity. In this paper, we present a Convolutional Neural Network architecture for the aspect detection for Vietnamese. The aspect detection is to aim to identify of the entity E and attribute A pairs expressed in the text (Pontiki et al., 2016). The experimental results show the superiority of our model over the winning systems on datasets of the VLSP 2018 challenge for aspect detection task. Our method achieves the F1 score of 80.40% for the restaurant domain and 69.25% for the hotel domain.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become popular in medical image analysis for disease diagnosis and to assist human experts in processing large amounts of images efficiently. While handcrafted features have been used for eye disease detection for several decades, the recent adoption of DNNs in this area has shown promising performance. In this paper, we propose three different frameworks to integrate handcrafted and deep features for optical coherence tomography image-based eye disease classification. We suggest integrating handcrafted features at the input and fully connected layers using existing networks like VGG, DenseNet, and Xception, and introduce a novel ribcage network (RC Net) for feature integration at middle layers. RC Net is designed with two rib channels for processing deep and handcrafted features and a spine channel for integration. Dense blocks are the main components of the channels, and sum operation is proposed for feature map integration. Experimental results demonstrate that integrating handcrafted features with deep networks improves classification accuracy significantly, achieving better accuracy compared to deep features alone. The RC Net outperforms all other proposed feature integration methods.

With the growing complexity of customized orders in production processes, new software models are required to automate the integration of digital technologies and modular systems in a standardized coordinate system. This will enable the merging of the real factory with its digital shadow, and facilitate the efficient flow of modular production systems. In this paper, we have presented a software control that follows the ultra-flexible production system characteristics of using modular robots, and their digital models as prototypes. The results show that the robot, viewed as a module of the factory, can be easily modeled, manipulated and modified by using an interface that conveniently employs a game engine. This makes the entire process more user-friendly and intuitive.

In recent years, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely used for image super-resolution (SR) to achieve a range of sophisticated performances. Despite the significant advancement made in CNNs, it is still difficult to apply CNNs to practical SR applications due to enormous computations of deep convolutions. In this paper, we propose two lightweight deep neural networks using depthwise separable convolution for the real-time image SR. Specifically, depthwise separable convolution divides the standard convolution into depthwise convolution and pointwise convolution to significantly reduce the number of model parameters and multiplication operations. Moreover, recursive learning is adopted to increase the depth and receptive field of the network in order to improve the SR quality without increasing the model parameters. Finally, we propose a novel technique called Super-Sampling (SS) to learn more abundant high-resolution information by over-sampling the output image followed by adaptive down-sampling. The proposed two models, named SSNet-M and SSNet, outperform the existing state-of-the-art real-time image SR networks, including SRCNN, FSRCNN, ESPCN, and VDSR, in terms of model complexity, and subjective and PSNR/SSIM evaluations on Set5, Set14, B100, Urban100, and Manga109.

Hardware neural networks that implement synaptic weights with embedded non-volatile memory, such as spin torque memory (ST-MRAM), are a major lead for low energy artificial intelligence. In this work, we propose an approximate storage approach for their memory. We show that this strategy grants effective control of the bit error rate by modulating the programming pulse amplitude or duration. Accounting for the devices variability issue, we evaluate energy savings, and show how they translate when training a hardware neural network. On an image recognition example, 74% of programming energy can be saved by losing only 1% on the recognition performance.

Recent advancements in remote sensing, in situ measurements, and numerical modelling have made ocean data more readily available. This has paved the way for the development of data-driven strategies for the interpolation of high-resolution, gap-free, and regularly gridded sea surface geophysical fields. These strategies serve as an alternative to model-based approaches and are computationally efficient, making them highly viable. Our paper investigates data-driven strategies for the interpolation of sea level anomaly (SLA) fields in the Western Mediterranean Sea from satellite-derived altimetry data. Specifically, we introduce and evaluate the analog data assimilation (AnDA) framework, which utilizes patch-based operators within a classic Kalman-based data assimilation scheme. Our focus is on mesoscale features, ranging from 20 to 100 km horizontal scale, and we assimilate two different types of altimetry data - along-track nadir data and wide-swath SWOT altimetry data. Our observing system simulation experiment demonstrates the superiority of AnDA as an improved interpolation method, with an SLA reconstruction RMSE (correlation) improvement of 42% (14%) with respect to optimal interpolation. Furthermore, results show a clear gain when the joint assimilation of SWOT and along-track nadir observations are considered. Our study provides valuable insight into the use of AnDA for the spatio-temporal interpolation of SLA fields and its effectiveness when applied to satellite-derived altimetry data.

The paper considers the way for controlling a grip mechanism. A program code for controlling the movement of mechatronic complex mechanisms is presented. The software is written in the LAD programming language used for programming logical controllers Siemens s7-1200. The software model is written in the environment TiaPortal v14.1. An algorithm for calculating the time delay based on fuzzy logic has been developed and is presented. This algorithm allows increasing the productivity and reducing the energy costs of the system. The results of the experiment showing the advantages of the proposed algorithm are given.

In this paper, our focus is on accelerating a primal-dual quadratic program solver that is associated with linear model predictive control. To achieve this, we have developed an innovative architecture that utilizes the saddlepoint structure of the quadratic program. Additionally, our architecture enables the seamless introduction of pre-conditioning and relaxation, which not only improves solution robustness but also enhances convergence.

Our architecture has been implemented on a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), and we have utilized fixed-point arithmetic to achieve efficiency. By taking advantage of the sparsity of the problem data, we have been able to increase scalability and solution speed significantly. 

Overall, our solution offers an efficient and effective means of accelerating a primal-dual quadratic program solver associated with linear model predictive control. By leveraging the saddlepoint structure of the quadratic program and incorporating pre-conditioning and relaxation, our architecture is capable of delivering superior solution robustness and convergence.

How to make the machine better understand human language has always been a hot topic. It greatly influences the efficiency and accuracy of knowledge extraction, intelligent question answering and other nature language processing applications. For this reason, researchers put forward multilingual analysis and language modeling methods, for example, the distributed feature representation fitting for the neural network models and so on. This paper argues that language analysis and modeling should start with the characteristics of the language itself. In seeing this, we have thoroughly studied a series of basic NLP analysis techniques and present our own three-layer language processing and analysis model. This model takes into account the characteristics of language at all levels, and tries to preserve most of the attributes of the sentence. Such design deals with the analysis and representation of language from a brand new perspective, which may inspire many other applications in the field of NLP.

Network embedding is a powerful technique that provides low-dimensional representations for machine learning applications. The existing work focuses on two approaches: unsupervised learning to preserve the structural connectivity in the network, and supervised learning of a specific task using deep neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new approach that combines these two lines of research, called generative adversarial network embedding (GANE). Our model uses a generator to create link edges and a discriminator to distinguish between generated and real connections. We train GANE using Wasserstein-1 distance to increase stability and extend it to preserve the structural information in the original network. Our experiments with real-world datasets show that GANE consistently outperforms existing models and provides significant improvements for tasks like link prediction, clustering, and network alignment.

Flower plays an extremely important role in our life, which has high research value and application value. The traditional methods of flower classification is mainly based on shape, color or texture features, and this methods needs people to select features for flower classification lead to the accuracy of classification is not very high. This paper aims to develop an effective flower classification approach using convolution neural network and transfer learning. In this paper, based on VGG-16, VGG-19, Inception-v3 and ResNet50 models were used to compare the network initialization model with the transfer learning model. The results show that transfer learning can effectively avoid deep convolution networks are prone to local optimal problems and over-fitting problems. Compared with the traditional methods, the accuracy of flower recognition on Oxford flowers dataset is obviously improved, and has better robustness and generalization ability.

Histological analysis is widely accepted as the gold standard for validating measures of tissue microstructure derived from MRI. However, due to several reasons such as lower costs, ease of acquisition, and a higher number of available contrasts, most histological investigations are usually 2D. Therefore, it is of great interest to be able to learn 3D tissue microstructure from 2D histology. In this study, a combination of dMRI and myelin-stained sections of a monkey brain was used to create a convolutional neural network to estimate the 3D fiber distribution from 2D histology. The results showed that the network was able to estimate the 3D fiber distribution with moderate to high angular agreement with the ground truth. This network can be used to validate dMRI neuronal structural measurements in 3D, even if only 2D histology is available for validation. Moreover, this network can be extended to infer the 3D fiber distribution at resolutions currently unachievable with dMRI, allowing for diffusion fiber tractography at unprecedented resolutions. Similar networks can be used to learn other 3D microstructural measures from various common 2D histology contrasts.

Computational Intelligence applications in banking and finance have been developed and deployed in the recent past and have been offering business solutions in both front end and back end processes in order to create efficiency and exceptional customer experience. In recent times, AI and machine learning are perceived to be the most valuable enabler to achieve competitive advantage by enhancing the decision making capabilities and transforming the banking industry. This paper will highlight the applications of AI and evaluate its utility in different functional areas of financial industry focusing primarily on automation of banking operations and customer engagement. It concludes with an analysis of how banking and financial organizations frame their environment and effectively use computational intelligence to improve their business.

In this paper, our focus is on the channel estimation for the millimeter-wave (mmWave) band multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) in the satellite-based Internet of Things (S-IoT). We present the establishment of a sparse geometric-based mmWave MIMO channel model between a high throughput satellite (HTS) and multiple terrestrial user equipments (UEs) for the S-IoT downlink system. By exploiting the sparsity inherent to the mmWave band channel, we propose an efficient adaptive random-selected multi-beamforming (ARM) estimation scheme that can estimate the mmWave MIMO channel state information (CSI) for multiple UEs simultaneously in the angle domain. Our ARM estimation scheme measures the CSI between the HTS and multiple UEs by utilizing a series of random combinations of transmitting beamforming vectors and receiving UEs' antennas. The required number of measurements can adaptively reduce as the signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) increase. 

To further enhance the performance of the ARM estimation scheme, we buffered the number of each beamforming that was selected for the channel measurement and modified the probability of the random selection of beams and UEs. Additionally, two improved ARM estimation schemes were proposed - the ARM forcing adaptation beam selection (ARM-FABS) scheme and ARM partially estimated beam selection (ARM-PEBS) scheme. Our simulation results demonstrate that the proposed ARM estimation schemes can reduce the required number of measurements and achieve a better tracking performance over a wide range of SNRs.

As parallelism is becoming increasingly prevalent on various levels in modern computers, it is beneficial to examine the extensive range of parallel computing advancements that have emerged in recent decades. Although we will not provide a comprehensive overview, we will instead focus on parallel programming patterns, parallel program design, parallel programming models, parallel programming languages, the design of parallel algorithms, and offer a perspective on parallel computing. In addition to presenting patterns, models, and design frameworks, we will touch on languages, implementation strategies, and tools.

Commercial High-Level Synthesis (HLS) tool vendors have started to enable ways to protect Behavioral IP (BIPs) from being unlawful used. The main approach is to provide tools to encrypt these BIPs which can be decrypted by the HLS tool only. The main problem with this approach is that encrypting the IP does not allow BIP users to insert synthesis directives into the source code in the form of pragmas (comments), and hence cancels out one of the most important advantages of C-based VLSI design: The ability to automatically generate micro-architectures with unique design metrics, e.g. area, power and performance. This work studies the impact to the search space when synthesis directives are not able to be inserted in to the encrypted IP source code while other options are still available to the BIP users (e.g. setting global synthesis options and limiting the number and type of functional units) and proposes a method that selectively controls the search space by encrypting different portions of the BIP. To achieve this goal we propose a fast heuristic based on divide and conquer method. Experimental results show that our proposed method works well compared to an exhaustive search that leads to the optimal solution.

Social media networks have experienced unprecedented growth in recent years, and with this growth comes the generation of massive social data that can provide insights into the behavior and emotional tendencies of users. As a result, many social researchers have turned to machine learning technology to build social media analytic models that can effectively detect abnormal behaviors or mental illnesses from social media data. While researchers typically only publish the prediction interfaces of these models, these interfaces can potentially leak information about individual data records used to train the models, thereby compromising user privacy.

To address this fundamental problem, known as membership inference, we introduce SocInf. The primary objective of SocInf is to construct a mimic model that can replicate the prediction behavior of the public model. By utilizing the mimic model, we can disclose the differences between the training and testing data sets and infer whether a particular record is in the victim model's training set or not. 

Our empirical analysis of SocInf's attack performance on machine learning models trained by Xgboost, logistics, and an online cloud platform revealed impressive results. While using realistic data, SocInf achieved a 73% average inference accuracy and an 84% average precision, with 83% and 91% at best.

In conclusion, the development of SocInf is a significant step in addressing privacy concerns in the application of machine learning technology to social media analytic models. Its ability to infer membership information from prediction interfaces can help researchers better protect user privacy in their work, and we look forward to further testing and development of the SocInf framework.

This paper is concerned with distributed multiagent optimization with inequality and equality constraints based on exact penalty methods. In the literature of exact penalty methods, constrained optimization problem is solved through optimization of penalized objective function and, under mild assumptions, the set of the optimal solutions of the penalized objective function coincides with that of the original constrained optimization problem. Exploiting the exactness of the penalized objective function, this paper proposes a new distributed multi-agent optimization protocol which simplifies the update law of previous protocols based on exact penalty methods with equality constraints. Also more concrete proof of the convergence of the protocol is provided under the assumption of the exactness of the penalized objective function.

A feature learning task involves training machine learning models to create good representations of input data by transforming the original information. However, when there is a limited amount of data or the data is unlabelled, relying on large annotated datasets, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), may not be feasible. This paper explores auto-encoder (AE) architectures that require no labels and investigates different training strategies to learn representations from images. 

Both the reconstruction error of the images and the feature spaces' discriminative power are evaluated to analyze the models' efficiency in creating good representations. The study examines the role of dense and convolutional layers in the results, as well as the depth and capacity of the networks, which can impact the ability to generalize for different visual domains and dimensionality reduction. 

Results of classification with AE features were as effective as pre-trained CNN features in terms of their discriminative power. This research can guide the development of unsupervised representation learning methods for designing models that can operate within and across domains with limited or unlabelled data.

With the rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT), vehicles can now be recognized as mobile smart agents that communicate, cooperate, and compete for resources and information. The main objective for these vehicles is to learn and make decisions based on policies in order to improve the efficiency of a multi-agent system (MAS) that deals with a constantly changing environment. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is now considered one of the most effective learning frameworks for finding reliable solutions in a highly dynamic vehicular MAS. 

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of research issues related to vehicular networks such as resource allocation, data offloading, cache placement, ultra-reliable low latency communication (URLLC), and high mobility. In addition, we highlight the potential applications of MARL that enable decentralized and scalable decision-making in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) scenarios. This survey aims to inspire new research ideas and shed light on current advancements in the field of vehicular networks and MARL, which hold great promise for future developments in smart transportation technologies.

The selection of appropriate resources and efficient allocation of tasks in a parallel application is crucial for an optimal outcome. This involves mapping tasks to the appropriate resources in a manner that balances the execution time and resource usage. In this study, we explore the mapping and scheduling of parallel applications with inter-task communications in a cloud environment. Our proposed method employs fuzzy logic and minimizes communication overhead to reduce execution time and resource usage time. The results of our study show a significant improvement over the Max-Min-C and Min-Min-C algorithms.

In recent years, the growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has been exponential. However, this surge in IoT devices has resulted in the generation of a vast amount of data that needs to be transmitted to the cloud for computing. Consequently, cloud consolidation and centralization have led to many network hops between IoT devices and their associated clouds, which has created two critical issues: (i) high latencies and (ii) high bandwidth consumption in the IoT domain. To address these problems, Network Function Virtualization (NFV), Software Defined Network (SDN), and fog computing have emerged.

In the Fog-to-Cloud (F2C) architecture, fogs and clouds work together to provide computing, storage, and application services in the IoT domain. The Service Function Chaining (SFC) technique involves chaining a specific set of virtual network functions together in a specific order to construct complex services. The joint VNF placement and traffic routing are known as SFC mapping. In this article, we introduce an Integer Linear Program (ILP) model to solve SFC mapping in the fog-to-cloud Computing System. Our aim is to minimize the overall end-to-end (e2e) latency of IoT devices. Our results have shown significant reductions in the overall e2e latency of IoT devices using our approach. Furthermore, our approach allows us to analyze the impact of the number of instances on the end-to-end latency of IoT devices.

The Australian Defence Forces (ADF) have been known to share resources, especially when it comes to helicopter training. In this training, the resources required are frequently people, such as instructors. However, understanding the current and future needs of the helicopter pilot training process can be quite challenging. New trainees and cadets join the Defence forces regularly, and they could either pass or fail the exams at the specialised flying schools. Depending on their circumstances, they may progress through the Defence forces, become trained pilots or instructors, and ultimately train future students. 

To address this challenge, the ATHENA platform has been developed as a strategic discrete event simulation, optimisation and analysis system for manpower planning with a specific focus on the needs and demands of the helicopter pilot training process for the ADF. This platform has been designed to operate as a simulation system running on a Cloud infrastructure. 

The ATHENA platform has been implemented to leverage container technologies to scale up automatically across the Cloud. The platform's focus is on the Kubernetes orchestration technology, which allows for the efficient allocation of resources and the management of container deployments. 

In conclusion, the ATHENA platform offers a solution for the optimisation challenge associated with the helicopter pilot training continuum within the ADF. It has been designed to ensure that manpower planning for this process is accurate, efficient, and effective. ATHENA enables the ADF to leverage cloud infrastructure and Kubernetes to scale up resources automatically and manage container deployments.

A stand-alone microgrid can face challenges related to inconsistent voltage and frequency, which can cause discrepancies in the active and reactive power values. Therefore, this paper aims to address the voltage customization of a microgrid network to maintain power and enable demand-side management (DSM). To achieve this, an outer voltage and inner current loop were employed, and an adaptive control structure was proposed to set the voltage and current of the microgrid based on modified voltage in the droop characteristics. This approach aims to prevent potential power catastrophes in the new era. Additionally, a dynamic frequency controller was used to maintain the frequency within a predetermined range. The effectiveness of this control structure was demonstrated through simulation results conducted in MATLAB.

Objective: The evaluation and testing of cardiac electrical devices in a closed-physiologic-loop can aid in the design of safety measures. However, this approach is not always practical or comprehensive. In addition, in silico closed-loop testing with biophysical computer models may not meet the time-critical requirements of cardiac device systems. Simplified models that meet these requirements may lack necessary dynamic features. In this paper, we present a new high-level physiologically-based computational heart model that is both time-critical and dynamic.

Methods: Our model includes cardiac regional cellular-electrophysiology types connected by a path model along a conduction network. The regional electrophysiology and paths are modeled with hybrid automata that capture non-linear dynamics, such as action potential and conduction velocity restitution and overdrive suppression. The hierarchy of pacemaker functions is incorporated to generate sinus rhythms, while abnormal automaticity can be introduced to form a variety of arrhythmias such as escape ectopic rhythms. Model parameters are calibrated using experimental data and prior model simulations.

Conclusion: Our heart model accurately captures the regional electrophysiology and paths of human action potentials, dynamic behavior, and cardiac activation sequences. When connected in closed loop with a pacing device in DDD mode, the model generates complex arrhythmia such as atrioventricular nodal reentry tachycardia. This allows us to establish the key physiological features of the heart model that influence device operation.

Significance: Our findings demonstrate the potential of an abstract heart model in device validation and personalized treatment design.

Shadow detection and removal are complex tasks that require an understanding of the overall image semantics. This paper presents a new design for detecting and removing shadows through the use of a deep neural network that analyzes the spatial image context in a direction-aware manner. The design includes a direction-aware attention mechanism in a spatial recurrent neural network (RNN), which introduces attention weights when aggregating spatial context features in the RNN. By learning these weights through training, the network can recover direction-aware spatial context (DSC) for detecting and removing shadows.

The DSC module is embedded in a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the DSC features at different levels. To make the training effective for shadow detection, the network employs a weighted cross entropy loss. The network is further used for shadow removal by using a Euclidean loss function and formulating a color transfer function to address the color and luminosity inconsistencies in the training pairs.

Two shadow detection benchmark datasets and two shadow removal benchmark datasets were utilized in this study, and various experiments were conducted to evaluate the proposed method. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method performs favorably against the state-of-the-art methods for both shadow detection and shadow removal.

Overall, the proposed deep neural network design provides an effective solution for the challenging tasks of shadow detection and removal by analyzing the spatial image context in a direction-aware manner. The results of this study are promising and suggest that this design can be further extended to other image analysis tasks in the future.

Security and safety have been traditionally considered as different disciplines addressed by different professionals. However, a close look at their characteristics and their analogies leads to the conclusion that they are actually interdependent. Specifically, we argue that safety requires system security and dependability.

The typical inaccuracy of data gathering and preparation procedures makes erroneous and unnecessary information to be a common issue in real-world applications. In this context, feature selection methods are used in order to reduce the harmful impact of such information in data analysis by removing irrelevant features from datasets. This research presents a novel feature selection method in the field of unsupervised learning, in which the complexity arises from the fact that the class labels cannot be used to select the most discriminative features as it is traditionally performed in supervised learning. The technique designed, which is called Kolmogorov-Smirnov test-based Unsupervised Feature Selection (KSUFS), is based on the computation of estimated feature distributions that are later compared to the original ones using non-parametric statistical tests to provide the most representative input variables. Two versions of the KSUFS are presented in this study: one of them is particularly designed to deal with standard data, in which the accuracy of the method prevalences over other of its aspects; the other version is designed to treat with big data problems, in which the computational complexity is improved due to the characteristics of this type of datasets. The KSUFS is successfully compared to other state-of-the-art unsupervised feature selection techniques in a thorough experimental study, which considers both standard and big data problems. The results obtained show that the method proposed is able to outperform the rest of reference unsupervised feature selection methods considered in the comparisons, selecting the first most influential features for standard datasets and particularly highlighting when big data problems are treated.

Big data analytics (BDA) is a powerful tool that can help uncover patterns, relationships and trends within massive data sets. This research paper applies BDA to criminal data, conducting exploratory data analysis and using state-of-the-art data mining and deep learning techniques to predict trends. By analyzing data from San Francisco, Chicago, and Philadelphia, some interesting patterns have been discovered. The results show that predictive models like Prophet and Keras stateful LSTM perform better compared to other neural network models. Furthermore, the optimal size of the training data is found to be three years. This study provides valuable insights that can help law enforcement agencies to understand crime issues, predict the likelihood of crimes and effectively deploy resources to mitigate them. Ultimately, BDA can optimize the decision-making process and result in a safer community.

The majority of control schemes for doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) wind turbine systems rely on the internal states or functions based on these states to achieve maximum power capture. However, practical implementation of such control schemes requires availability of these states which may not always be measurable or available.
