To address this issue, this paper proposes the use of estimation to determine unobservable states for the maximum extraction control of DFIG-based wind energy conversion systems. This approach involves the use of the Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF), a discrete-time nonlinear estimator, for the estimation of unobservable states. The active power and stator voltage control are achieved through rotor flux control approach. This method enables the practical implementation of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and stator terminal voltage control even when some of the internal states are not readily available.

This paper presents an algorithmic framework that enables the real-time optimization of distributed energy resources (DERs) at the distribution level. The framework considers both individual controllable DERs as well as groups of DERs that are jointly controlled at an electrical point of connection, accounting for wye and delta single-phase and multiphase connections. The algorithm ensures that DERs meet given performance objectives while adjusting their power to respond to grid operator requests and maintain electrical quantities within engineering limits. The algorithm is designed using a time-varying bilevel problem formulation, capturing various performance objectives and engineering constraints, along with an online implementation of primal-dual projected-gradient methods. The gradient steps are modified to accommodate appropriate measurements from the distribution network and the DERs, allowing the algorithm to cope with inaccuracies in the distribution system modeling. The resulting algorithm avoids the need for pervasive metering to gather the state of noncontrollable resources, and it naturally lends itself to a distributed implementation. The proposed method is shown to be stable and convergent in terms of tracking the solution of the formulated time-varying optimization problem, and it is tested using real data in a realistic distribution system.

The Encoder-Decoder architecture is a popular deep learning model for biomedical image segmentation. This architecture involves an encoder that compresses input and generates encoded features, and a decoder that produces dense predictions using these encoded features. However, while the encoder is well-studied, decoders are still relatively unexplored.

In this paper, we take a closer look at the state-of-the-art Encoder-Decoder architectures and propose a new universal decoder that we call the cascade decoder. Our cascade decoder is designed to improve semantic segmentation accuracy and can be easily embedded into existing networks, allowing for end-to-end training. 

Specifically, the cascade decoder is structured to perform more effective decoding of hierarchically encoded features and is more compatible with common encoders than other known decoders. To evaluate our new decoding method, we replaced decoders in several state-of-the-art models with our cascade decoder for various challenging biomedical image segmentation tasks. 

The results of our experiments showed significant improvements in segmentation accuracy, demonstrating the efficacy of our new decoding method. Overall, our study highlights the importance of exploring new and innovative decoders to further advance the Encoder-Decoder architecture for biomedical image segmentation.

The piezoresistive silicon based stress sensor has the potential to detect a precursor for the Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) implementation in automotive electronics. One solution to enforce reliability in automotive electronics is the use of Machine Learning (ML). One or more physical parameters are being monitored, and algorithms are used to illustrate the health state and predict remaining useful life based on the current and past health information. Piezo-resistive stress sensors are employed to measure the internal stresses of electronic packages, an Acquisition Unit (AU) to read out sensor data and a Raspberry Pi as PHM server to perform evaluation. Accelerated tests in air thermal chamber are performed to get time series data of the stress sensor signals, with which we can know better about how delamination develops inside the package. In this study stress measurements are performed in several electronic packages during the delamination. The delamination is detected by the stress sensor due to the continuous change of the stiffness and the local boundary conditions causing the stresses to change. Moreover, the stress change in multiple cells can give more information regarding the delamination such as the location and its state. Data preprocessing methods to remove outliers and filter raw measurement results, and feature extraction methods to capture only meaningful information by reducing the data are chosen and applied to raw data. A logical assumption is made regarding the data behavior and delamination state, based on data analytics and with Scanning Acoustic Microscope (SAM) images confirmed the delaminated area. FEM simulation are used to provide a qualitatively physical explanation of the stress change due to the delamination. A prognostic model using neural network is trained to estimate the degradation grade. Back Propagation Neural Networks are chosen to provide a fast and quick training for the mechanical stress data.

Nuclei segmentation is a crucial task in modern computer vision methods, especially with the use of convolutional neural networks. Although recent advancements in open-source software have made these tools more accessible, expert knowledge is still needed to select the appropriate model architecture and training setup. In this study, we compared the performance of two popular segmentation frameworks, namely U-Net and Mask-RCNN, in the nuclei segmentation task. Our findings showed that each framework has its strengths and limitations. Consequently, we developed an ensemble model to combine their predictions, which significantly outperformed both models. This ensemble model should be considered when aiming for the best nuclei segmentation performance.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has gained widespread attention for its ability to monitor and control the environment. IoT enables data-driven decision-making through the use of everyday devices that have been equipped with sensing, processing, and communication capabilities. A key aspect of any IoT device is its communication capability, which enables it to transfer and share data with other devices. Wireless communication technologies are commonly used in IoT systems. 

The industry and research community have proposed numerous communication technologies for IoT systems. In this study, the authors present the findings of an in-depth analysis of the benefits and limitations of these technologies.

Feature selection is an essential task for data mining, as it can eliminate irrelevant and redundant features and improve learning performance. In this paper, a novel feature selection method for unsupervised text clustering – the binary multi-verse optimizer algorithm (BMVO) – is proposed. This method uses the MVO algorithm to select essential text features and improve the performance and reduce the computation cost of the k-means clustering algorithm. The BMVO algorithm's effectiveness is evaluated on six published datasets, including Classic4, Wap, tr41, tr12, 20Newsgroups, and CSTR. The results show that the BMVO algorithm outperforms other comparative algorithms in terms of evaluation measures. Overall, the proposed BMVO algorithm is a promising feature selection method for unsupervised text clustering.

Dimensionality reduction is a crucial aspect in classification problems, and a new cascaded approach has been proposed to achieve this. The method involves the use of an improved clustering thought (ICT) to initially screen the features. Then, an improved particle swarm optimization (IPSO) algorithm, which adopts mutation into the PSO iteration rule, is used to filter out feature subsets whose fitness value is above a certain threshold. Subsequently, the support of each feature can be calculated using these selected subsets, and the best feature subset can be identified based on the sorted support.

To evaluate the efficacy of this approach, 1588 tobacco leaf images from 41 grades were used in the experiments. The results indicated that the proposed deep feature screening method can significantly improve image recognition rate and speed. Overall, this cascaded approach holds promise in augmenting the classification accuracy of datasets with large numbers of features.

This paper presents a new zonotopic constrained approach for the Kalman filter that takes advantage of the particular structure of the original optimization problem. This technique consists in projecting the state estimation by solving an optimization problem, to ensure that the estimated state belongs to a zonotope. Based on a classical gradient algorithm method, i.e. the iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (ISTA), this paper proposes a reduced complexity approach suitable for the state estimation of systems subject to a large number of state constraints. The algorithm's speed is improved via a faster ISTA approach, called FISTA.

Super-resolution (SR) and MRI reconstruction are currently trending topics in computer vision and medical imaging. With the advent of deep learning, both fields have seen tremendous progress over recent years. This work focuses on exploring some of the most effective CNN-based SR algorithms and their applications in MRI reconstruction. To this end, we divide the MRI reconstruction network into a data-consistency sub-network and an image prior sub-network, and evaluate the reconstruction performance with various CNN-based SR networks. Our experimental results show that hybrid SR networks resembling ResNet and DenseNet significantly outperform current state-of-the-art approaches in terms of reconstruction performance.

Network Function Virtualization (NFV) is becoming an increasingly popular solution, allowing for the transformation from dedicated hardware to software instances on a virtualized platform. In NFV, Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) are utilized to provide services through a predetermined order known as Service Function Chaining (SFC). In this paper, we investigate the importance of delay and resiliency in NFV services and provide quantitative models for flow delay in both totally ordered and partially ordered SFCs. We also explore the mathematical calculation of VNF placement for unprotected and protected SFCs. Additionally, we examine the Virtual Network Function placement and routing problem with delay concerns and the incorporation of resiliency. We prove that this problem is NP-hard under two cases and propose an Integer Nonlinear Programming (INLP) formulation and heuristic solution for each. Finally, we assess our proposed algorithms through extensive simulations, evaluating their performance based on acceptance ratio, average node usage, and total running time.

Inverted pendulum is a highly unstable, nonlinear and an under-actuated system. Its dynamics resembles many real-time systems such as segways, self-balancing robots, vertical take-off and landing aircraft (VTOL) and crane lifting containers etc. These real-time applications demand the need of a robust controller. In literature, many different control strategies have been discussed to stabilize an inverted pendulum, out of them, the most robust being fuzzy control and sliding mode control. The former is difficult to tune and has a problem of rule explosion for multivariable system, whereas the latter has a problem of discontinuity and chattering. To address the issues in fuzzy controller, a novel robust linear quadratic regulator (LQR) based adaptive-network fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) controller is proposed and implemented on the stabilization of x-z inverted pendulum. The proposed controller is able to solve the problem of robustness in the LQR controller as well as the difficulty in tuning along with rule explosion in fuzzy controller. Furthermore, the designed controller is tested for different pendulum masses and the results show that as compared with conventional PID controller, the proposed controller gives better performance in achieving lesser overshoot and settling time along with better robustness properties.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) have become an increasingly popular solution for text classification, including aspect extraction. However, while state-of-the-art CNN architectures have been proposed for aspect extraction, they do not incorporate improvements such as non-static CNN, multi-kernel convolution layers, and dropout regularization that have been shown to be beneficial for general text classification tasks.

Thus, in this research, we introduce an enhanced CNN architecture for aspect extraction, which includes these improvements. Our modifications to the basic CNN model aim to improve the feature extraction by convolutional layers while allowing dense layers to represent complex non-linear relationships between selected features and the output layer. We also demonstrate that using non-static CNNs can fine-tune the word embedding features better than static CNNs for domain-specific corpora when training word2Vec models is not feasible.

Moreover, our experiments show that using Skip-gram trained word2vec models rather than Continuous bag of word (CBOW) architecture can improve the quality of word2vec embedding features for aspect extraction and text classification tasks.

We evaluate our new CNN model and baseline CNN using SemEval-2016 Task 5 Restaurant and Laptop domain datasets, demonstrating that our CNN model significantly outperforms the baseline CNN model for aspect extraction of customer reviews in both restaurant and laptop domains. Furthermore, it surpasses the available state-of-the-art systems for the restaurant domain.

In conclusion, our proposed CNN architecture with enhancements for aspect extraction achieves superior performance over existing approaches and demonstrates the effectiveness of incorporating these improvements in CNN-based text classification.

The processing and analysis of big data sets in real-time requires the high computational power of extreme-scale high-performance computing (HPC) systems. To schedule massive task/thread sets on these systems, various scheduling algorithms and virtualization techniques have been developed. However, these strategies do not guarantee the meeting of timing constraints such as deadlines, which are crucial in real-time science workflows. 

To address this issue, a new project has been developed that focuses on real-time scheduling for extreme-scale HPC Message Passing Interface (MPI) tasks and ensemble workloads found in fine-grain many-task computing (MTC) applications. This new approach abstracts information about the tasks or threads and continuously dispatches the workload to ensure the meeting of deadlines and other timing constraints. The framework also aims to reduce execution time and energy consumption.

The new framework introduces a deadline-based scheduling approach in the tasking programming model. This approach guarantees that tasks are completed within their specified deadlines, allowing for efficient processing and analysis of real-time data sets. The new project departs from the established trend of best-effort scheduling in large-scale HPC systems, providing a solution that meets the evolving demands of real-time science workflows.

In this paper, vehicle counting is investigated using various machine methods on four datasets. Vehicle counting is needed to complete the data required for short term predictions using highway traffic model, which is in turn, applicable for road design and usage planning. The goal of this research is to show that automatic car counting using machine methods, can be obtained from utilizing existing CCTV image data or from better cameras. Then by applying quantitative evaluation, F1 and precision scores are obtained, so that a few recommendations can be given. Through numerous simulations, F1 scores ranging from 0.32 to 0.75 have been successfully obtained for one low resolution dataset, using Background Subtraction and Viola Jones methods, on existing CCTV data. It has been found also that Viola Jones method can improve F1 score, by about 39% to 56%, over Back Subtraction method. Furthermore, the use of Deep Learning especially YOLO has provided good results, with F1 scores ranging from 0.94 to 1 and its precision ranges from 97.37% to 100% involving three datasets of higher resolution.

This paper presents a MATLAB-based Hardware-In-Loop compatible model for a three phase cage induction motor with the ability to simulate eccentricity fault. The model is compatible with commercially available real-time simulators, making it possible to test motor control units of electric vehicles under the influence of eccentricity fault. The use of the modified winding function approach for modeling the eccentricity fault is widely adopted. In addition, the model is capable of real-time simulation for varying severities of eccentricity fault. The model utilizes pre-computed inductances, which ensures that real time execution is achievable. The study concludes by discussing the major challenges encountered in the development of this model, paving the way for further research.

Opioid Use Disorder (OUD) is rapidly becoming a widespread public health crisis, characterized by physical or psychological dependence on opioids. However, new research shows that supervised machine learning can aid in predicting adults at risk for OUD. By considering numerous demographic, socioeconomic, physical, and psychological features in an integrated manner, this research demonstrates the potential of a random forest classifier to accurately predict adults at risk for OUD (sensitivity = 0.81, specificity = 0.76, AUC = 0.86) despite the low prevalence of OUD (approximately 1%). Surprisingly, this research reveals that early marijuana use (prior to 18 years of age) is the dominant predictor for developing OUD in adult life, surpassing both mental illness and disability. This knowledge underlines the critical role that educators, counselors, and parents can play in mitigating the opioid overdose crisis by curbing early marijuana use as a preventative measure.

Data collection using mobile elements can substantially improve the equilibrium degree and lifespan of wireless sensor networks (WSNs). A mobile sink typically traverses the sensing field periodically, collecting data from multiple Anchor Points (APs) that make up a traveling tour. However, this can cause significant latency due to long-distance traveling. In this paper, we propose a path planning strategy for mobile data collection, known as the Dual Approximation of Anchor Points (DAAP), to achieve full connectivity for partitioned WSNs and construct a shorter path while ensuring the least calculational complexity compared with existing works.

DAAP is novel in two regards. Firstly, it is designed explicitly for disconnected WSNs, where sensor nodes are scattered across several isolated segments. Secondly, it has a straightforward and efficient calculation complexity. DAAP is formulated as a location approximation problem and is solved using a greedy location selection mechanism, which follows two principles. Firstly, the APs of periphery segments must be located as near the network center as possible. Secondly, the APs of other isolated segments must be located as close to the current path as possible.

Experimental results indicate that DAAP outperforms existing works in delay-sensitive applications, underlining the effectiveness of the proposed location approximation solution.

In large-scale web image search, bag-of-visual-words-based (BOW) approaches are used to efficiently match features. However, popular feature coding techniques such as K-means-based vector quantization and scalar quantization have their drawbacks such as requiring expensive visual codebook training and low stability of individual components of feature vectors, respectively. To address these issues, we propose a multiple distance-based feature coding scheme that demonstrates that the corresponding sub-vectors of similar features have similar distances to multiple reference points in feature subspace. Based on this, we transform each feature to a set of feature codes, where one code is treated as a visual word required to construct the inverted index file and the others are embedded into the index file to further verify the feature matching based on the visual words. This coding scheme does not require visual codebook training and shows desirable stability and discriminability. Additionally, we propose a feature-distance estimation method to accurately verify matches. Experimental results show the superiority of our approach over other feature quantization methods for large-scale web image search.

Compressive sensing is a technique that enables the compression and reconstruction of sparse or compressible signals using fewer samples than that required by the Nyquist-Shannon theorem. To cater to the demands of wireless sensor networks with regards to storage, energy efficiency, and security, we present an efficient and secure model for transmission based on compressive sensing and hash-chain theory. In contrast to conventional compressive sensing, our proposed model employs only the initial key and hash function in the sensor node, thereby reducing the storage space. Furthermore, the characteristics of the hash-chain ensure the security of data transmission. We conducted numerical experiments to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed model.

Piecewise-linear particle swarm optimizer (PPSO) is one of swarm-based optimization algorithms. Although PPSO is a deterministic particle swarm optimization (D-PSO) algorithm, its performance is better than the classical PSO's performance in solving various optimization problems. In particular, PPSO is effective in solving non-separable problems such as rotated problems. In our previous study, we have investigated that PPSO particles can move not only in a direction parallel to the coordinate axes, but also in various directions. We therefore assumed that PPSO particles do not depend on reference frame. In this paper, we analyzed that PPSO algorithm is reference frame invariant (i.e., scaling, translation, and rotational invariants) theoretically, and in order to study effectiveness of the theoretical analysis, we performed numerical experiments and clarified whether PPSO algorithm is reference frame invariant or not.

The Dexmo glove is a haptic exoskeleton that provides kinesthetic feedback in virtual reality. Unlike many other gloves based on string-pulleys, the Dexmo uses a free-hinged link-bar to transfer forces from a crank to the fingertips. It also uses an admittance-based controller parameterized by position, as opposed to an impedance-based controller parameterized by force. When setting the controller's target position, developers must use its native angular coordinate system. The Dexmo has a number of uninstrumented degrees of freedom. Mature forward models can reliably predict the hand pose, even with these unknowns. When it comes to computing angular controller parameters from a target pose in Cartesian space however, things become more difficult. Complex models that provide attractive visuals from a small number of sensors can be non-trivial or even impossible to invert. In this letter, we suggest side-stepping this issue. We sample the forward model in order to build a lookup table. This is embedded in three-dimensional space as a curve, on which traditional queries against world geometry can be performed. Controller parameters are stored as attributes of the sample points. To compute the driver parameters for a target position, the application constrains the position to the geometry, and interpolates them. This technique is generalizable, stable, simple, and fast. We validate our approach by implementing it in Unity 2017.3 and integrating it with a Dexmo glove.

Radio-frequency (RF) energy harvesting is one of the promising technologies in wireless networks. This paper considers wireless powered communication networks (WPCNs) where one hybrid access point (H-AP) coordinates RF energy/information transmissions to/from a set of nodes. For the important type of WPCNs where the nodes have throughput requirement, we aim to minimize H-AP's energy provision (EP) via jointly optimizing the time allocation of energy/information transmissions and H-AP's transmission power while satisfying node throughput requirement. More specifically, the half-duplex WPCN is considered first. We prove that H-AP's energy transmission power must be the maximum allowed value to achieve the minimal EP, then show that the problem is convex under this condition and finally design an algorithm applying golden section search and bisection search jointly to efficiently obtain the optimal time allocation. Second, the full-duplex WPCN is considered. Its EP minimization problem is proved convex. However, due to the hardness of solving it directly, we turn to solve the feasibility problem (FP) for a given EP per unit time. We construct a convex optimization problem based on this FP and design a dual subgradient algorithm for finding its optimal solution, which indicates whether this FP is feasible. The minimal EP per unit time and its corresponding optimal solution are found by using the bisection search method. Simulation results show that, the EP-minimized schemes are able to greatly reduce H-AP's EP as compared to the baseline schemes.

Recently, there has been a rise in mobile ransomware, which poses a significant threat to mobile users who rely on their devices to store sensitive information. In 2017 alone, there were over 468,830 unique mobile ransomware samples discovered, which represents a 415 percent increase from the previous year. While traditional methods of detecting malicious applications have relied on bytecode and XML-based permission files, attackers are now using obfuscation techniques that involve repackaging apps with malicious content in native machine code. As a result, these methods are no longer effective in detecting modern mobile ransomware.

This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of using native instructions in detecting ransomware. The researchers used machine learning models to analyze opcodes in native instructions and found that they can be used to detect mobile ransomware with near-perfect accuracy. Additionally, they found that the number of instruction opcodes required to detect ransomware is significantly less than the full range of supported opcodes within a contemporary instruction set, making it easier to detect.

The researchers also tested the robustness of their approach against six different ransomware families in a state-of-the-art Android malware dataset. They found that their approach was effective in detecting all six ransomware families, making it a viable solution for protecting mobile devices from ransomware attacks.

In conclusion, the emergence of mobile ransomware is a growing concern for mobile users, but the use of native instructions has been found to be an effective method for detecting and preventing these attacks. By utilizing machine learning models and analyzing opcodes in native instructions, mobile users can better safeguard their sensitive information and prevent the devastating consequences of ransomware attacks.

Project-Based Learning (PBL) is a teaching approach that revolves around projects as drivers of knowledge, without sacrificing coverage of technical material in dedicated subjects. This paper focuses on the implementation and delivery of PBL in the field of computer science engineering, with a major project that encourages undergraduate creativity and emphasizes real-world, open-ended projects.

The aim of this innovative project is to demonstrate how a trained machine model can predict cryptocurrency prices with the right amount of data and computational power. By displaying a graph with predicted values, this project showcases the most popular technology - a technological solution that could help mankind predict future events.

Given the vast amount of data generated and recorded on a daily basis, we are finally approaching an era where predictions can be accurate and based on concrete factual data. Additionally, with the rise of the crypto digital era, more investors are turning towards the digital market for investments, presenting the opportunity to create a model capable of predicting crypto currency prices, primarily Bitcoin. This can be accomplished through a range of machine learning techniques and methodologies.

Through these projects, students not only develop content knowledge and technical skills but also practical skills that are widely applicable across various contexts. Thus, this project-based learning approach creates a holistic learning experience that prepares students for the challenges and opportunities present in the real world.

Broadcast-and-select (B&S) technology is primarily used in high-speed local area networks and access networks. In B&S single-hop networks, the most common physical topologies are the star, folded bus, and tree structures. This chapter explores the different multiplexing and access techniques that are utilized in B&S networks. It discusses the general concepts of traffic and connections in optical networks, as well as resource and capacity sharing principles. Using these concepts, this chapter calculates the relevant quantities for B&S single-hop networks.

Packet switching in the optical layer is also covered, as well as the media access protocols used in B&S networks to ensure smooth and efficient operation. These networks offer several advantages, including simplicity, natural multicasting capability, and low cost. Overall, this chapter provides a comprehensive overview of B&S technology and its practical applications in LANs and access networks.

The utilization of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) and Industrial Control Systems (ICS) networks for smart technologies has resulted in an increased exposure to a plethora of security threats. However, there is a lack of investigations conducted in this area from an Internet (cyber) perspective. Therefore, this paper aims to examine unauthorized, malicious, and suspicious SCADA activities by utilizing the darknet address space. Specifically, this study focuses on the Modbus service, which is a widely-used protocol to connect electronic devices in critical and industrial infrastructures. 

This research is based on actual Internet data that was collected over a duration of one month. The study identified 8 different inferred scanning activities, with TCP distributed portscan being the only atypical Modbus scan. Additionally, the analyses conducted were able to identify various Modbus scanners and discovered that six other services were associated with Modbus approximately 74% of the time. Finally, the paper presents several case studies that discuss synchronized and automated SCADA scanning campaigns that originated from unknown sources.

In today's industrial automation era, mobile robot plays an important role. And continuous improvement of mobile robot performance can be an important research topic. We use Matlab 2018 Simulink to simulate these results. In the paper genetic algorithm based parameters tuning for the hybrid intelligent controller design for the manipulation of the mobile robot is proposed. By way of the combination of traditional PID controller and Fuzzy Logic controller, an intelligent controller or Fuzzy PID controller is set up. Then, using Genetic Algorithm to tune the parameters of membership function of Fuzzy Logic Controller is provided so that the performance index of the mobile robot can be achieved. From simulation results it can be found that the response speed is raised and the settling time is decreased. The proposed intelligent controller is then implemented on a mobile robot to verify the superior performance of the intelligent controller.

Inexact computing generally involves trading a reduction in accuracy for an improvement in circuit area and power-consumption. The multiply-accumulate (MAC) operation is used extensively in convolutional neural networks and such applications stand to benefit greatly from the introduction of approximation to the MAC operation. This paper introduces an unsigned approximate MAC unit architecture in which approximation is introduced to both the multiplication and accumulation stages. Four variations of the proposed design are implemented using the TSMC 65 nm technology and are used in an image smoothing application. The proposed architecture is compared to that of the exact MAC unit and is shown to reduce circuit area and power-consumption by 67% and 49% respectively. When compared to other approximate MAC architectures, the proposed design improves area-power product by up to 66%.

The system grabs data packets from campus network routers, divides the collected basic data into seven basic databases, preprocesses all the basic data and preprocesses the text. Through the statistics and calculation of the data, it extracts the frequency of user browsing web pages, the frequency of using application categories, the time period of surfing the Internet, the time of surfing the Internet, the total flow of surfing the Internet, the amount of Posts and the mail. Based on the emotional dictionary, the key words of emotional features and topic features are extracted from the text information such as the content of browsing web pages and the content of posting, and the user's emotional orientation values are obtained. The obtained behavioral, emotional and topic features are stored in the feature database. Finally, through the functional test and performance test, the system can extract the daily characteristic quantity according to the daily data, get the characteristic data table, and use the characteristic data to judge the depression tendency of college students by the depression recognition and warning model.

In power domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), which is used for uplink random access (RA) systems, users must control their transmit power to ensure that the received power at the base station falls within predetermined values. However, selecting one of these predetermined values incurs different transmission costs for each user. In addition, users may choose to withdraw their transmission, resulting in a waiting (or regret) cost.

This letter presents an analysis of N-user non-cooperative games in uplink NOMA RA systems, taking into account the waiting cost. The results demonstrate the conditions for the existence of a unique mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium (MNE) and its efficiency in terms of social welfare maximization (SWM).

In this paper, we present a method that uses computer vision, specifically projective geometry, to map a known distribution of points on a sphere with a known diameter, along with an arbitrary image of these points on an image plane, to identify the configuration of the camera. In simpler terms, this method can extract the camera matrix and its parameters - intrinsics and extrinsics - by knowing the sets of 2D-3D corresponding points. We validated this method by code, which explains in detail how to set up a theoretical world and camera coordinate frame. By applying our knowledge of the correspondence, we can display the solution to the optimization problem. We analyzed the results and noted the relative error between the retrieved and actual camera matrices.

Automatic modulation classification plays a crucial role in wireless communications, and its usefulness has recently been expanded by applying deep learning techniques, which have provided improved performance. However, in convolutional neural network (CNN)-based modulation classification, the input size is typically fixed, despite the fact that the duration of the radio signal burst can vary. This poses a challenge to making full use of the complete signal burst to enhance classification accuracy.

Given this challenge, this paper proposes three different fusion methods: voting-based fusion, confidence-based fusion, and feature-based fusion. These methods are used to leverage the complete signal burst to enhance the performance of CNN-based modulation classification for variable-length radio signal bursts. To evaluate the effectiveness of these fusion methods, we conduct simulation experiments to analyze their performance.

Our results demonstrate that all three proposed fusion methods perform better than the non-fusion method. Remarkably, the performance of the confidence-based and feature-based fusion methods is comparable and better than that of the voting-based fusion method.

In conclusion, with the advent of deep learning, the automatic modulation classification has witnessed significant improvement in its performance. However, as the input size is typically fixed in CNN-based modulation classification, the fusion methods proposed in this paper offer an innovative approach to leverage variable-length radio signal bursts to further enhance the classification accuracy.

In this article, the implementation of decoupled double synchronous reference frame (DDSRF) theory is demonstrated using one dc voltage, two ac voltage, and two ac current sensors. By using these sensors, the control of grid-side converter (GSC) can be achieved during balanced and imbalanced grid conditions in a three-phase, three-wire system. As there is no path for the flowing of zero sequence current, the estimation of unknown voltage and current can be assumed to be correct. Additionally, two line-to-line connected voltage sensors provide information on voltage imbalance during imbalanced grid conditions, allowing for the estimation of the third phase voltage and current by making the sum of two sensed quantities and one unknown variable equal to zero. The decoupled vector control of GSC is experimentally verified in this paper, utilizing DDSRF to decouple the positive and negative sequence voltages while also implementing enhanced DDSRF techniques to decouple currents in the respective dq-axes. The experimental setup utilized a TI-2407A DSP controller.

Python is experiencing a surge in popularity, particularly in the field of data science. As a result, there has been a proliferation of free libraries available for usage. This review paper aims to describe and compare the characteristics of various data mining and big data analysis libraries in Python. Although no paper has yet dealt with this topic and examined the pros and cons of all availalbe libraries, this paper considers more than 20 libraries and organizes them into six groups: core libraries, data preparation, data visualization, machine learning, deep learning, and big data. In addition to examining the functionality of the various libraries, important factors for comparison include the number of contributors involved in the development and maintenance of the library, as well as the size of the community supporting the library. Larger communities mean a greater chance of finding easy solutions to problems. We currently recommend pandas for data preparation, Matplotlib, seaborn, or Plotly for data visualization, scikit-learn for machine learning, TensorFlow, Keras, and PyTorch for deep learning, and Hadoop Streaming and PySpark for big data.

Brain-Inspired Systems (BIS) are an emerging field of brain and intelligence sciences that studies natural intelligence models of AI and cognitive systems in one direction, and the formal models of the brain simulated by computational intelligence in another direction. A typical BIS is the cognitive robots that mimic and implement the brain through all cognitive levels. BIS provides insights for brain-machine interfaces (BMI), which may lead to novel man-machine interactions and hybrid intelligent systems. BIS may also advance classic computers from dada processors to the next generation of knowledge processors mimicking the brain. BIS will underpin a wide range of engineering paradigms such as cognitive systems, cognitive computers, cognitive robots, machine learning systems, semantic comprehension systems, big data systems, unmanned systems, self-driving vehicles and hybrid man-machine systems.

This paper addresses the Unrelated Parallel Machines Scheduling Problem with Sequence-Dependent Setup Times (UPMSPST). The objective is to minimize the scheduling maximum completion time, known as makespan, which is crucial in practical applications since UPMSPST is commonly encountered in industries. Moreover, UPMSPST belongs to the NP-Hard class in a theoretical sense. The study evaluates five algorithms to find solutions for UPMSPST and compares the results obtained from their execution. The VNS and F&O heuristic, with the VNS metaheuristic generating the initial solution, demonstrated the best outcomes among all algorithms studied, even outperforming [1] in some cases.

To design Microstrip Antennas (MPA), various strategies are used such as transmission and cavity models that show differences in the way the antenna radiates. However, these methods often lead to errors when detecting the antenna parameters. Numerical techniques are more accurate but require vast resources and considerable time to process electromagnetic knowledge. In this study, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was employed to demonstrate the relationship between the antenna parameters (Permittivity, Substrate height, and freq.) for the examination and design of MPA in a range of 0.3-3 THz.

This paper discusses our work on using software engineering metrics (i.e., source code metrics) to classify an error message generated by a Static Code Analysis (SCA) tool as a true-positive, false-positive, or false-negative. Specifically, we compare the performance of Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Random Forests, and Repeated Incremental Pruning to Produce Error Reduction (RIPPER) over eight datasets. The performance of the techniques is assessed by computing the F-measure metric, which is defined as the weighted harmonic mean of the precision and recall of the predicted model. The overall results of the study show that the F-measure value of the predicted model, which is generated using Random Forests technique, ranges from 83% to 98%. Additionally, the Random Forests technique outperforms the other techniques. Lastly, our results indicate that the complexity and coupling metrics have the most impact on whether a SCA tool with generate a false-positive warning or not.

This study evaluates the performance of two different controllers for a DC-motor control system that features a time-delay in the feedback loop. One controller is based on the Smith predictor while the other is an optimization-based controller. Our findings indicate that the optimization-based controller is better suited for preserving stability when there are large variations in the system parameters and time-delay, as compared to the Smith predictor-based controller. Simulations and real-life experiments conducted in the study confirm that the optimization-based controller performs better, particularly as the time-delay and system parameters change.

In recent times, computer systems have evolved into complex structures comprising of a multitude of infrastructure and software technologies, which often interact with each other, making it challenging to identify the root causes of system faults while the system is in operation. It becomes even more challenging for software engineers to resolve faults that arise due to a combination of software and infrastructure issues. To tackle this complexity, we have proposed a framework to identify the causes of system faults that address these software and infrastructure problems.

The goal of this research is to identify software and/or infrastructure-related faults. The framework relies on both software and infrastructure logs, which are collected when a fault occurs. These logs are compared with a database of historic logs to quickly identify the underlying cause of the fault. After that, debug mode and configuration logs are collected to pinpoint source code and configuration file issues. To validate the framework, we have illustrated two examples of true system faults where the first one resulted only from software bugs while the second one had both software bugs and infrastructure problems causing it. Furthermore, we developed a tracing and replay tool based on the framework to determine the true causes of system faults. This tool was implemented, and it was able to detect 96% of the differences between the fault and normal cases, including two concrete session error cases caused by infrastructure and software bugs.

In conclusion, our framework provides a solution for software engineers to identify the causes of faults, even when they are struggling to untangle software and infrastructure issues. By leveraging historic logs, software and infrastructure logs, and debug mode and configuration logs, our framework can accurately pinpoint the causes of system faults.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are a rapidly growing technology that is being utilized in Internet of Things (IoT)-related applications. The IoT has the potential to revolutionize the way we live by implementing automated power control, theft prevention monitoring, and other applications. One such application is the subject of this paper, which proposes a WSN-based IoT system that focuses on passive infrared (PIR) motion sensors and a camera.

The proposed system uses three PIR motion sensors in tandem with a camera to capture images of individuals entering or leaving a home. These images are relayed to a central server where they can be analyzed and stored for later use. The system can also be used to switch OFF or ON power appliances such as fans or lights, reducing energy consumption.

To facilitate communication between the sensors and the server, the system employs a river formation dynamics-based multi-hop routing protocol (RFDMRP). This allows for the efficient transfer of information on the number of occupants in a given room, as well as the images captured by the sensors, to the central server.

A prototype of the proposed system has been developed, installed, and put through extensive testing. With its ability to provide efficient monitoring and power control, the WSN-based IoT system has the potential to be utilized in a wide range of applications.

Digital Screens (DS) can be considered harmful to the eyes, if used for a prolonged time, leading to such health issues as computer vision syndrome (CVS) and digital eyestrain. A wearable device able to inform the user about the time spent looking at DS could be helpful in order to suggest him the proper break timings and avoid CVS. In this study, a new Digital Screen Detection (DSD) approach using a new generation of head mounted wearable color light sensor has been proposed. Data from five subjects during common activities of daily living (ADL) in different environments (indoor, outdoor, office, meeting room) characterized by the presence of various DSs (Tablet, PC, large screen) have been acquired. The best performing machine learning algorithms already applied in a previous in-lab controlled study have been analyzed. The results showed that, in ADL context, the Random Forest algorithm reached the best accuracy in DSD with the proposed system (79.3%).

Delineation of right ventricular cavity (RVC), left ventricular myocardium (LVM) and left ventricular cavity (LVC) are common tasks in the clinical diagnosis of cardiac related diseases, especially in the basis of advanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques. Recently, despite deep learning techniques being widely employed in solving segmentation tasks in a variety of medical images, the sheer volume and complexity of the data in some applications such as cine cardiac MRI pose significant challenges for the accurate and efficient segmentation. In cine cardiac MRI we need to segment both short and long axis 2D images. In this paper, we focus on the automated segmentation of short-axis cardiac MRI images. We first introduce the deep layer aggregation (DLA) method to augment the standard deep learning architecture with deeper aggregation to better fuse information across layers, which is particularly suitable for the cardiac MRI segmentation, due to the complexity of the cardiac boundaries appearance and acquisition resolution during a cardiac cycle. In our solution, we develop a modified DLA framework by embedding Refinement Residual Block (RRB) and Channel Attention Block (CAB). Experimental results validate the superior performance of our proposed method for the cardiac structures segmentation in comparison with state-of-the-art. Moreover, we demonstrate its potential use case in the quantitative analysis of cardiac dyssynchrony.

In this article, we discuss a numerical simulation-based design method for a marine propulsor that is suitable for towing Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs). Due to the drag of the payload, the thrust loading coefficient of the propulsor is very high. The base geometry of the propeller utilized in this study is the Ka-4-70 propeller with nozzle no. 22. Validation of the CFD model is done using experimental results from open-water performance tests. The stator for the propulsor is designed using basic principles of axial compressor design techniques, and the effect of the stator's thickness is calculated on the propulsor's performance. The geometry of the propulsor is parameterized in CAESES, and the performance is calculated using the high-fidelity CFD RANSE solver in StarCCM+.

In this paper, we propose a new model for the multi-objective multiple allocation hub network design and routing problem which contains determining the location of hubs, the design of hub network, and the routing of commodities between source-destination pairs in the given network. The selected hubs are not assumed to be fully connected, and each node and arc in the network has capacity constraints. The multiple objectives of the problem are the minimization of total fixed and transportation costs and the minimization of the maximum travel time required for routing. We propose a mathematical formulation for the multi-objective problem and present a meta-heuristic solution based on a well-known multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. Using the proposed formulation, we are able to find the optimal solution for small networks of five nodes and seven nodes. To evaluate the performance of our heuristic approach on real data, the computational experiments are conducted on Turkish postal system data set. The results demonstrate that our heuristic approach can find feasible solutions to the problem in reasonable execution time, which is less than 10 min.

Cloud computing and big data have risen to become the most popular technologies of the modern world. Apparently, the reason behind their immense popularity is their wide range of applicability as far as the areas of interest are concerned. Education and research remain one of the most obvious and befitting application areas. This research paper introduces a big data analytics tool, PABED (Project - Analyzing Big Education Data), for the education sector that makes use of cloud-based technologies. This tool is implemented using Google BigQuery and R programming language and allows comparison of undergraduate enrollment data for different academic years. Although, there are many proposed applications of big data in education, there is a lack of tools that can actualize the concept into practice. PABED is an effort in this direction. The implementation and testing details of the project have been described in this paper. This tool validates the use of cloud computing and big data technologies in education and shall head start development of more sophisticated educational intelligence tools.

In this paper, an energy efficient transport protocol is proposed to enhance the traffic capacity of complex networks. The new algorithm is derived on the basis of router betweenness centrality, which gives an estimate of traffic handled by the node as router. As one bottleneck node will degrade the traffic performance of the whole network, the improved routing aims to bypass nodes with heavy load to diminish the congestion. Particularly, depending on a parameter that controls the optimization scale, the new transport protocol can achieve smaller average path length while guaranteeing the required packet generation rate. Comparing results of previous routing strategies, it is shown that the presented improved routing strategy performs more effectively.

The prevalence of small, low-cost, wireless cameras has made it increasingly difficult to detect surreptitious observations of people. Previous methods for detecting hidden cameras have only been effective in limited environments where the user has significant control of the surroundings. To address this issue in a less constrained scope of settings, we propose the concept of similarity of simultaneous observation. This involves using a camera (such as a Wi-Fi camera, mobile phone camera, or laptop camera) to compare timing patterns of data transmitted by potentially hidden cameras with the timing patterns expected from the known camera's recorded scene.

We applied several similarity measures to analyze these patterns and demonstrated an accuracy of over 87% and an F1 score of 0.88 using an efficient threshold-based classification. To further improve our results, we trained a neural network with our dataset, achieving accuracy as high as 97% and an F1 score over 0.95 for both indoor and outdoor settings.

Our study shows that similarity of simultaneous observation is a feasible method for detecting hidden wireless cameras that are streaming video of a user. This approach removes significant limitations that previous detection methods have faced.

A low-power and stable “static-type” neural network (NN) circuit based on CMOS and resistive synaptic devices was developed and evaluated. The circuit is composed of a comparator as a firing function for binary output, current sources, cross switches for inputs, and variable resistors for synaptic weights. Nonlinearity analysis of operating points in such circuits was performed in terms of the types of current sources and the resistance-change ratios of the variable resistors. The operation window to realize both operation stability and low power consumption of less than 1 mW for 1024 synapses was thus clarified. To improve the NN performance, memristive synaptic devices with WOx/MgO were fabricated and characterized in terms of spike-timing-dependent plasticity and nonlinear switching for learning.

Applying deep learning for medical imaging classification suffers from limited labeled data, especially for those relying on biopsy proven labels. In this work we approach this challenge by leveraging other available datasets with focus on answering what dataset can be used, and how to use them optimally. An application was considered, classifying benign or malignant colonic polyps given colonoscopy narrow-band imaging (NBI). Experiments were conducted with 5 auxiliary datasets with various characteristics, and multiple training schemes involving transfer learning, multitask learning (MTL) with a DenseNet backbone. Results consistently suggest an optimal scheme of MTL initialized from ImageNet pretrain model and followed by fine tuning on the main task. An auxiliary dataset helps better if it's not only similar in terms of imaging mechanism or fine-grained variability, but also easy to train itself. A NBI classifier trained with such scheme and auxiliary dataset improved accuracy from 62.6% (baseline without using other dataset) to 70.7% with performance on par with 5 human experts.

The aim of this project is to develop an efficient event-driven wireless sensor nodes based network for an effective and power efficient monitoring of plants health and larva population in a remote crop field. In this framework, an event-driven approach is proposed to detect larva and measure other system parameters like Acoustic Complexity Index (ACI), temperature, humidity and soil moisture. The sensors' data is collected by the front end event-driven sensing node, developed with a STM32F407VG board, via a serial port. The STM32F407VG board is based on the ARM processor. In contrast to the clock driven classical sensing nodes, the devised sensing nodes only acquire and transmits the sensors data in the case of a significant change. It significantly reduces the power consuming data acquisition and transmission activity as compared to the classical solutions. It improves the proposed solution power efficiency and autonomy as compared to the counter classical ones. The data from the node is transmitted to a base station by using a wireless ZigBee interface. The base station collects data from a group of event-driven sensing nodes. This data is transmitted to the Central Processing Unit (CPU) via the USB liaison between the base station and the CPU. On CPU this data is analyzed via the MATLAB based specifically developed application. The findings are displayed and logged on the CPU. It allows the terminal user to access this and to achieve a timely interaction and cure of the intended crop field. The system parameters are adjusted in order to achieve the effective modules integration and performance. The proposed system operation is validated with an experimental setup. Results have shown a promising system realization.

Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) is a commonly implemented method in brain computer interfaces (BCIs). The traditional pattern flip paradigm has the disadvantages of easy to fatigue and high stimulation intensity. In the application of brain-controlled virtual reality(VR) systems, there are many problems such as limited by devices and the paradigm induced effect was not good. In this paper, we propose a new SSVEP-BCI paradigm based on illusory pattern motion perception. Using the basic principle of pattern peripheral drift illusion, the visual motion stimulation effect is alternately presented in double-frame graphics, and the accurate SSVEP induction effect. The brain activate degree is greater and the functional connection is stronger. The experimental results show that the new paradigm adaptability is an effective SSVEP-BCI paradigm, and it is not easy to fatigue. It can be applied to brain-controlled virtual reality system and other human-computer interactive systems.

This paper introduces a recursive algorithm that efficiently computes tight enclosures of the set of states consistent with a given nonlinear discrete-time model, observed output sequence, and given bounds on disturbances and measurement errors. This method, known as set-based state estimation, has various applications in verification, fault detection, and robust control. The proposed algorithm is based on the theory of differential inequalities (DI) which has been extensively developed for nonlinear reachability analysis. The contemporary DI methods effectively utilize redundant model equations to yield tight reachability bounds at a lower cost. In this paper, we have extended these methods to set-based state estimation, and results show this approach outperforms other commonly used recursive algorithms. An important caveat is that this approach is only applicable to forward-Euler-discretized systems satisfying a step size bound.

To ensure the safe and reliable operation of railway systems, precise control is crucial, and this relies on collecting highly accurate measurement data from various onboard and wayside sensors. In this paper, we propose a solution that aims to improve the accuracy of the measurement data during train movement using a multi-sensor data fusion approach based on Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF). The sensors used in this approach include indoor positioning systems, radio frequency identification, and rotary encoders. Our experimental results, conducted on a train model, demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in providing more accurate measurement data on the train's position.

The aim of this paper is to efficiently and accurately detect changes in observations, specifically in the context of localizing using time difference. This is achieved through a method called sequential detection, or quickest detection. In our model, we consider a system being monitored by distributed sensors, where an abrupt change, such as a jamming signal, could occur at any unknown moment. To address this challenge, we propose a framework utilizing the well-known Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) test, which is optimal for non-Bayesian statistical change-point detection formulations. This enables the distributed sensors to make decisions regarding the presence or absence of any jamming signal at each time. Once a decision is made and transmitted to the fusion center, the jammer can be located. Computer simulations are used to evaluate the effectiveness of our approach.

Satellite image semantic segmentation, including extracting road, detecting building, and identifying land cover types, is essential for sustainable development, agriculture, forestry, urban planning, and climate change research. Nevertheless, it is still unclear how to develop a refined semantic segmentation model in an efficient and elegant way. In this paper, we propose attention dilation-LinkNet (AD-LinkNet) neural network that adopts encoder–decoder structure, serial–parallel combination dilated convolution, channel-wise attention mechanism, and pretrained encoder for semantic segmentation. Serial–parallel combination dilated convolution enlarges receptive field as well as assemble multi-scale features for multi-scale objects, such as long-span road and small pool. The channel-wise attention mechanism is designed to advantage the context information in the satellite image. The experimental results on road extraction and surface classification data sets prove that the AD-LinkNet shows a significant effect on improving the segmentation accuracy. We defeated the D-Linknet algorithm that won the first place in the CVPR 2018 DeepGlobe road extraction competition.

For scientific or commercial offshore operations, optimization should primarily be focused on minimizing time and costs to ensure safety and affordability. ROV vehicles, which are crucial for underwater operations, are susceptible to underwater uncertainties and require modularity to accommodate instrument or tool changes specific to the task. As a result, parameters for these vehicles must undergo frequent tuning, including the automatic controllers. This paper presents a new proposed controller, called Neuro Sliding Control, that utilizes a combination of a Back Propagation Neural Network and Second Order Sliding Mode to enable the vehicle to adapt to changes in parameters. Experimental results of the proposed controller have been demonstrated to be effective in operating small dimension ROVs in one degree of freedom.

We demonstrate a compact polarization decoding module with the size of 2 cm × 2 cm × 1 cm for a free space quantum key distribution based on micro-optics. The insertion loss and polarization extinction ratio (PER) of this module are <;4.6dB and >22.8 dB, respectively, and large alignment tolerance is achieved owing to multimode fiber pigtailing. The quantum bit error rate (QBER) are measured to be 0.67% with the sifted key rate of 576 kb/s at the clock rate of 100 MHz.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have proven to be highly effective in recognizing actions from a fixed viewpoint. However, these methods are limited in their ability to recognize actions from arbitrary viewpoints. To address this issue, we present a deep multi-view framework for cross-view action recognition. Our approach integrates spatiotemporal convolutional features from multiple viewpoints using deep multi-view representation learning, enabling the extraction of highly discriminative cross-view convolutional features for action recognition. To speed up action detection and recognition, we train a feature-based correlation filter for each action class. Our proposed framework enables accurate recognition of actions from different viewpoints, with increased accuracy. Extensive experimentation on four publicly available datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach in solving the problem of view variations in a single action class through the learning of discriminative information from multiple viewpoints.

The constitutive equation model has been established for a specific aluminum thin film that was deposited using the Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) process, which is typically employed during wafer fabrication Back End of Line (BEOL) processes. The model was derived by matching the data collected from experimental nanoindentation and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulation. Based on this data, the model used is an adaptation of the Voce isotropic hardening model, which is defined by three distinct coefficients.

The three coefficients that were determined for this particular aluminum thin film were the Linear Hardening Coefficient, the Saturation Flow Stress, and the Saturation Exponent. These were determined to be 21937 MPa, 135 MPa, and 25, respectively. 

Overall, this new constitutive equation model offers invaluable insights into the mechanical properties of aluminum thin films deposited during PVD processes for wafer fabrication BEOL. Its discovery provides researchers with a new resource that can be further developed to improve the quality and reliability of these critical processes in the future.

With the increasing use of Big Data, security has become a top concern for businesses. Cyberattacks continue to grow, making information security a global problem. However, simply relying on prevention methods is not enough to protect against intrusions. Intrusion detection systems have become an essential part of the network security infrastructure and are crucial for detecting a wide range of attacks.

Intrusion refers to hacking a network or system, which can have serious implications for information security. IDS plays a vital role in identifying and detecting such attacks. This paper provides an analysis of network security issues and current research related to Big Data intrusion and detection systems. Specifically, this article focuses on recent approaches used for intrusion detection in Big Data, particularly the use of predictive analysis to minimize security risks.

This work implements a hydrodynamic model-based localization and navigation system for low-cost autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) that are limited to a micro-electro mechanical system (MEMS) inertial measurement unit (IMU). The hydrodynamic model of this work is uniquely developed to directly determine the linear velocities of the vehicle using the measured vehicle angular rates and propeller speed as inputs. The proposed system was tested in the field using a fleet of low-cost Bluefin SandShark AUVs. Implementation of the model-based localization system and fusing of the solution into the vehicle navigation loop was conducted using backseat computers of the AUV fleet that run mission orientated operating suite -interval programming (MOOS-IvP). With the model-based navigation system, the maximum localization error (i.e., in comparison to a long baseline (LBL) based ground-truth position) was limited to 15 m and 30 m for two 650-second and 1070-second long missions. Extrapolation of the position drift shows that the model-based localization system is able to limit the position uncertainty to less than 100 m by the end of hour-long mission; whereas, the drift in the default IMU-based localization solution was over 1 km per hour. This is a considerable improvement by only using a MEMS IMU that generally costs less than $100. Furthermore, this work is a step towards generalizing and automating the process of hydrodynamic modeling, model parameter estimation and data fusion (i.e., fusing the localization solution with those from other available aiding sensors and feeding to the navigation loop) so that a model-based localization system can be implemented in any AUV that has backseat computing capability.

Mobile capability development is necessary as the need for mobile devices increases. However, mobile devices still face challenges due to lack of computational resources. To overcome these challenges, extensive research has been conducted, resulting in the development of many new techniques. One such technique involves partitioning and offloading applications to the cloud to tap into its full computational and storage availability. Other methods involve offloading part of the applications while retaining the rest for processing on the smartphone, with decision making based on metrics such as power and CPU consumption. However, security issues are often overlooked in these solutions.

To address these challenges, a new elastic framework called Secure Framework for Mobile Capabilities Augmentation using Cloud Computing (SMCACC) has been proposed. This framework enables the transparent use of cloud resources to augment the capabilities of resource-constrained mobile devices. One significant feature is the partitioning of a single application into multiple components, which can be executed on the mobile device or offloaded to the cloud clone for execution. This results in an elastic application that can augment the capabilities of a mobile device while saving energy. 

To ensure data security, a hybrid cryptography method is employed. The proposed security protocols use a combination of both symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic techniques to minimize energy consumption and avoid the disadvantages of existing methods. These methods protect users by securing data that is offloaded to the cloud. Results of testing without security showed that resource consumption for executing the application on mobile and cloud decreased to approximately half of the memory used for running the app on mobile-only. When incorporating the security framework, resource consumption for executing the application on mobile is still reduced. 

In summary, SMCACC is a promising framework that addresses the challenges of mobile device resource constraints and data security. Its elastic application and hybrid cryptography method make it a valuable tool for mobile capability development.

The current input-output table is not suitable for analyzing real-time industries and takes a significant amount of labor to create, often taking up to four years from the start of the survey to the release. To address this issue, Teikoku Databank (TDB) Co., Ltd is constructing an input-output table using corporate data. However, the calculation of private consumption based on total sales of (BtoC) companies selling to consumers cannot record where the consumption occurred.

This research aims to estimate the sales ratio to consumers in BtoC companies and calculate the total sales to consumers. Additionally, a proportional division of the total private consumption according to each region's population size is used to construct an algorithm to calculate private consumption in each region. This approach enables the construction of a more timely and accurate input-output table, providing valuable insights into real-time industries.

The computer vision and robotics community is increasingly interested in visual scene classification, thanks in part to the availability of low-cost and compact visual sensing devices. To address this growing interest, we propose a framework for embedded system design aimed at visual scene classification. Our approach employs data fusion of local and global descriptors to create feature vectors for scene classification, using Local Quinary Patterns (LQP), Bag of Visual Words (BoW), and Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) to construct the feature vector. To classify these feature vectors, we utilize multiclass Support Vector Machines (SVM). We conducted experiments on the MIT indoor scene classification database, and found that our approach outperformed other methods in terms of overall accuracy.

This paper presents a method for time-series classification using fuzzy cognitive maps. We argue that fuzzy cognitive maps are an effective way to represent time series and propose a classification mechanism based on them. The classifier is designed to distinguish maps constructed for time series belonging to different classes. Our proposed classification procedure evaluates the similarity of fuzzy cognitive maps by comparing weight matrices that are based on the same set of concepts. These concepts are extracted from the underlying data via a data-driven clustering procedure. Each data point of a time series is related to each concept, and the strength of these relationships is evaluated using a membership function.

The performance of our approach is investigated on a variety of real-world datasets, and we compare our classification accuracy with 37 state-of-the-art time-series classification methods. Our experimental results demonstrate that our method performs well and often outperforms its competitors. Overall, we propose a novel approach to time-series classification that utilizes fuzzy cognitive maps and achieves competitive classification accuracy.

This paper extensively investigates unsupervised deep learning solutions for multiuser single-input multiple-output (MU-SIMO) coherent detection. Two groups of deep learning solutions are analyzed based on their exploitation of the channel state information at the receiver side (CSIR): equalization and learning, and direct learning. Equalization and learning utilize CSIR for channel equalization and then employ deep learning for multiuser detection, while direct learning directly feeds the CSIR and the received signal into deep neural networks for MUD. The study finds that direct learning solutions outperform equalization-and-learning solutions due to their better exploitation of sequence detection gain. However, current DNN architectures cannot efficiently handle many co-channel interferences in SIMO networks, limiting the scalability of direct learning. To address this challenge, the paper proposes a novel direct learning approach that combines feedforward DNN and parallel interference cancellation, achieving a tradeoff between complexity and learning scalability. The study demonstrates that the proposed approach's complexity can be managed due to the parallel network architecture.

Drug behavior in the body is described by using pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) models. Relationship between the drug behavior and elapsed time is complicated, and even a nonlinear regression algorithm is not easy to be applied to the identification of the relationship. In this paper, the PK/PD model is simplified for the purpose of facilitating the identification. A logistic model and a Gompertz growth model are analytically derived by applying the perturbation method to the PK/PD model which is based on the 3-compartment model. The simplified models are applied to the identification of clinical data, and it is confirmed that the errors from the PK/PD model are less than 5 %. The new models are simpler than the PK/PD model and easier to be identified. They make it possible to predict the transition of the drug effects and to be applicable to the automatic correction of affected biosignals, and so on.

This paper presents a novel geometric adaptive control scheme designed for a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle to mitigate the effects of unknown, unstructured disturbances. The controller incorporates a multilayer neural network that adapts online to the disturbance, promoting effective mitigation. The stability of the proposed controller is analyzed using Lyapunov stability theory on the special Euclidean group. It is proved that the tracking errors are uniformly ultimately bounded with an ultimate bound that can be abridged arbitrarily. 

Additionally, this paper presents a mathematical model of wind disturbance on the quadrotor dynamics. The proposed adaptive controller is capable of rejecting the effects of wind disturbances effectively. This is demonstrated through numerical simulations. Overall, this paper proposes a novel adaptive control scheme that can successfully mitigate unknown disturbances in quadrotor systems, thus making them more robust and reliable.

Modular multi-level converters (MMCs) have emerged as a promising topology for medium or high voltage applications in recent years. They are considered to be the next generation DC/AC converters for medium/high voltage (MV/HV) motor drive applications due to their transform-less structures, high efficiency, and modularity. However, reliability is a major challenge in MMCs as a large number of power switching devices are used and each of these devices can be considered as a potential failure point.

To address this challenge, this paper investigates the behavior of the failure submodules and healthy submodules and proposes the use of artificial neural network (ANN) classification algorithms for single-submodule open-circuit fault diagnosis. The ANN algorithm is implemented in a field programmable gate array (FPGA) and the ANN parameters training is completed offline in Matlab.

The experimental results of the proposed fault diagnosis for a single-module open-circuit fault are presented in this paper. The results show that the ANN algorithm is capable of accurately detecting and locating the fault and applying appropriate protections in a timely manner. 

Overall, this study presents a valuable contribution in the field of MMCs and fault diagnosis. The proposed approach can be extended to other types of faults and can ultimately lead to improved reliability of MMCs in medium or high voltage applications.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is an emerging paradigm that is having a significant impact on our lives. However, one challenge facing the deployment of IoT is the inability to provide terrestrial access networks to remote areas. This is where Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems come into play. LEO satellites could be pivotal in the evolution of 5G and become critical for scenes relying on its limitations. Furthermore, the integration of terrestrial and satellite communication in 5G provides technical support for the 5G system. 

In this context, the specific application scenarios and traffic distribution characteristics of LEO satellite-based IoT call for a simulation method to assess traffic flow. This paper presents a simulation approach for traffic in LEO satellite-based IoT. The simulation results reveal that the business distribution in LEO satellite systems has marked suddenness and variability both in time and space. The non-uniformity of business distribution poses a threat to system stability, necessitating the construction of LEO satellite-based IoTs in accordance with the distribution characteristics and laws of the business.

Reversible computing is so far the only way to circumvent the Landauer limit of CPU power efficiency, thus has attracted more and more attention recently due to its prospect in energy-efficient computing.
