To make reversible computing possible, much ground work needs to be studied, especially on reversible algorithms. We focus on designing reversible shortest path algorithms in this paper.

Leucorrhea routine is a common way of female physiological examination, which is detected by recognizing and counting the visible components in microscopic images. At present, the research in this field is still blank. Based on the deep learning theory, an improved R-CNN model is proposed to realize the intelligent recognition of the visible components in leucorrhea microscopic images. The detection precision of the algorithm is high, reaching 93.6%, and the detection time is 300 ms. The proposed algorithm provides a theoretical basis for the realization of leucorrhea routine automation and intellectualization.

In computer science, consensus theory has been studied for decades. “Consensus” in a multi-agent system means reaching an agreement regarding a certain quantity of interest. The modular multilevel converter (MMC) is a promising topology for medium- and high-power applications owing to its salient features. In MMC operation, one key point is to regulate the capacitor voltage of each submodule (SM). The SMs in MMCs are interconnected both physically and via a control system, and these SMs can be regarded as a multi-agent system, with the control objective of regulating their capacitor voltages, which could formulate a consensus problem. In this paper, through mathematical derivation, it is found that individual capacitor voltage regulation control of phase-shifted-carrier pulse-width modulation (PSC-PWM) MMC is one special case of consensus theory. Furthermore, based on the consensus theory, the influence of different communication structures on the MMC voltage regulation performance is discussed. The analysis proves that the existing one has the highest rate of convergence. The impact of current-tracking dynamics on consensus-based interpretation is also analyzed. In addition, the proportional relationship between the rate of convergence and the P controller parameter is also justified. The experiments on a seven-level down-scaled prototype are conducted to confirm the analysis.

The goal of any facility layout problem is proper arrangement of facilities without overlapping. Most of facility layout problems are two-dimensional and single-floor. In this study, facility layout problem is considered in three-dimensional and multi-floor. This will increase the flexibility of the problem. Also, many of layout problems are deterministic, while it is possible that parameters of the problem can be changeable. Therefore, robust planning should be used in overlapping constraints. We develop a mathematical model considering some flexible assumptions. In order to measure the validity of the model, we solve some examples using the appropriate software. Computational experiments show that the objective function of mathematical model increases by considering flexibility in parameters.

A mobile-based virtual try-on system is proposed to deal with the problems of high cost and conflicts between computational complexity and simulation effects. In this paper, several modules are included, such as automatic 3D face reconstruction based on a single image, auto-skinning and realtime local simulation of cloth. According to the experiments, the virtual try-on system introduced in this paper is able to achieve better fitting effects with lower constructing and computing costs, in which case good experience of mobile-based virtual try-on system is provided.

This paper proposes the use of the Shewhart test to minimize the number of data-transmissions in IoT networks. Results show that this method outperforms the widely-used LMS-based data reduction method in terms of the number of data-transmissions, implementation complexity, and MSE in prediction of time-series data at the sink node. Additionally, piggybacking and interpolation techniques are suggested to further decrease MSE without increasing the number of packet transmissions. The study compared the performance of data reduction algorithms on a set of measured temperature values from custom-designed wireless sensor nodes in indoor and outdoor scenarios over four days. The effectiveness of the piggybacked transmissions on battery lifetime was also examined. Results show that the proposed piggyback approach significantly reduces the MSE at the slight cost of battery-lifetime.

Improved Automatic Segmentation of the Prostate and its Internal and Surrounding Structures

Accurate and automatic segmentation of the prostate and its surrounding structures has significant implications for various medical applications. While several methods have been proposed for the segmentation of anatomical zones limited to the peripheral and transition zones, we present a novel multi-class segmentation approach that includes the anterior fibromuscular stroma and distal prostatic urethra, and is based on the spatial division according to PI-RADS v2 sector map.

Our approach utilizes a anisotropic convolutional neural network to generate a topologically correct division of the prostate into the four structures. We evaluated the proposed method on a dataset of 98 subjects, where T2-weighted axial MRI scans were obtained. The obtained results showed that for the majority of the zones, the segmentation method achieved segmentation performance in the range of inter-rater variability.

The proposed method not only enhances computer-aided detection methods, but also enables more precise therapy planning. Therefore, our model represents a significant step forward in automatic segmentation and analysis of MRI scans of the prostate, particularly in clinical settings where manual segmentation is not always practical or accurate.

The H2020 project 5G-DRIVE (5G HarmoniseD Research and TrIals for serVice Evolution between EU and China) cooperates with the Chinese twin project to trial and validate key functions of 5G networks operating at 3.5 GHz bands for enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) and 3.5 GHz and 5.9 GHz bands for V2X scenarios. 5G-DRIVE will instil significant impact on the validation of standards and trigger the roll-out of real 5G networks and V2X innovative solutions driving new business opportunities and creating thereby new jobs and brand new business models. This paper presents the overall approach of 5G-DRIVE, the advances beyond the current state of the art for key 5G enabling technologies, as well as the considered use cases.

Summarizing a cricket match is a time-consuming and demanding task that requires expertise. However, a new approach has been proposed in this paper to automatically identify and summarize crucial events in a cricket match.

The approach makes use of the video recording of the entire match as input and outputs the most significant clips of the game. Optical character recognition, sound detection, and replay detection techniques have been utilized to extract essential moments like boundaries, wickets, and other playfield scenarios in a cricket match. These events are then pieced together to create the entire highlight reel for the game.

The efficacy of the model was evaluated through several qualitative and quantitative experiments. The results of the experiments show that the model can detect events, such as wickets, fours, and sixes, with an accuracy of 89.45%. This indicates that the model could potentially be useful in real-life scenarios.

To conclude, this new model for automatically summarizing cricket matches provides a promising step towards improving the efficiency and accuracy of summarizing these events.

It is difficult to realize the effective separation of signal and noise in the vibration signals, owing to the traditional signal filtering method. This paper puts forward an algorithm which was based on Hasudorff distance and nonlocal means (Hasudorff-Non Local Means, HDNLM). This algorithm makes use of Hasudorff distance more efficient than Euclidean distance distance in preserving signal details. It is aim to improve the weight model of traditional NLM of Euclidean Distance. Experimental and simulation show that: The improved NLM is superior than the simple morphology, traditional NLM, and db8 wave transform in the noise denoising of vibration signal aspect. The newly method is combined with the power spectral density, and it is well applied in the fault feature extraction of on-load tap changers.

Perspective distortions have long been a problem in crowd counting, as they can create estimation errors. In this paper, we introduce a new loss function that enables filters in convolutional neural networks to learn features that can adapt to the scale and perspective variations of individuals in crowd images. By focusing on the crowd count error in regions close to the vanishing point of a perspective distorted image, we can penalize underestimations. This helps to train a network that is resistant to perspective distortion and produces accurate density estimations. Our proposed approach is applicable to various crowd scenes, regardless of their physical layout. We undertook extensive comparative evaluations that demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods on the challenging ShanghaiTech and UCF-QNRF datasets.

We address the problem of attack detection and isolation for a class of discrete-time nonlinear systems under (potentially unbounded) sensor attacks and measurement noise. We consider the case when a subset of sensors is subject to additive false data injection attacks. Using a bank of observers, each observer leading to an Input-to-State Stable (ISS) estimation error, we propose two algorithms for detecting and isolating sensor attacks. These algorithms make use of the ISS property of the observers to check whether the trajectories of observers are "consistent" with the attack-free trajectories of the system. Simulations results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms.

To ensure undisrupted web-based services, operators need to closely monitor various KPIs (Key Performance Indicator, such as CPU usages, network throughput, page views, number of online users, and etc), detect anomalies in them, and trigger timely troubleshooting or mitigation. There can be hundreds of thousands to even millions of KPIs to be monitored, thus operators need automatic anomaly detection approaches. However, neither traditional statistical approaches nor supervised ensemble approaches satisfy this requirement in practice when facing large number of KPIs. A state-of-art unsupervised approach Donut offering promising results, but it is not a sequential model thus cannot deal with the time information related anomalies. Thus, in this paper we propose Bagel, a robust and unsupervised anomaly detection algorithm for KPI that can handle time information related anomalies, using CVAE to incorporate time information and dropout layer to avoid overfitting. Our experiments using real data from Internet companies show that, compared to Donut, Bagel improves the anomaly detection best F1-score by 0.08 to 0.43.

Cloud-loT Applications consist of thousands of smart devices sending sensor data to processing cloud applications. If the processing rate of the cloud application is limited it may be unable to cope with an increasing number of connected devices. If such a situation is not addressed, the cloud application is overloaded with messages, resulting in a high processing delay or loss of data. For this reason we propose a TCP-inspired congestion avoidance which reconfigures the send rate of devices at runtime aiming for a low processing delay and a high throughput. We show, that it is able to avoid congestions by adapting the send rate of devices to a fair share of the processing rate of the cloud application.

In this paper, we present the CLAP framework, an I/O efficient distributed approximation method that supports arbitrary sub-datasets of large datasets. Existing offline sample-based systems provide high accuracy results for only a limited number of sub-datasets due to the prohibitively high storage overhead of caching offline samples. Meanwhile, online sample-based systems lack support for the uneven storage distribution of sub-datasets, resulting in poor estimation accuracy and low I/O efficiency. To address these issues, CLAP utilizes a distribution-aware method that collects sub-dataset occurrences at each logical partition of a dataset and uses this information to enable I/O efficient online sampling. 

CLAP has three main components. First, it uses a probabilistic map to reduce the exponential number of recorded sub-datasets to a linear one. Second, it implements a distribution-aware method for efficient online sampling using unequal probability cluster sampling. Third, it supports more complex approximations such as ratio and regression using bootstrap-based estimation and allows users to specify a target error bound when submitting an approximation job. Additionally, the optimal sampling unit size in a distributed file system is quantitatively derived by associating it with approximation costs and accuracy. 

We have implemented CLAP into Hadoop as an example system and have open-sourced it on GitHub. Our experimental results show that CLAP achieves significant speedup (up to 20×) over precise execution.

Emotions play a crucial role in various aspects of human life, including daily behavior, decision-making, human interactions, and health. These emotions are expressed through language, and the words people use can affect our emotions. However, it remains unclear if emotions can also impact the structure of language. Can emotions influence the length of sentences, choice of grammar, and transition between grammatical categories? This paper proposes using Natural Language Processing techniques to analyze emotionally rich text and explore the relationship between emotions and language. Results suggest that emotions have a significant impact on the length of text and a lesser effect on the choice of parts of speech (e.g. nouns vs. verbs), while having little influence on the sentence structure and the transition between grammars.

The Brainstorm Optimization Algorithm (BSO) is a population-based optimization algorithm that was recently proposed. It is inspired by the human brainstorming process and is designed to solve global optimization problems. BSO has shown great performance in solving large-scale multidimensional multimodal problems. However, it has a significant weakness in that it relies heavily on the cluster center to update the population. This makes it challenging to exchange information within the population, leading to frequent falling into local optimal solutions that are difficult to escape. 

To counter this weakness, the Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm has been studied as a way to improve BSO's global search abilities while avoiding local optima. By combining GWO with BSO, the resulting algorithm has been shown to improve on BSO's limitations. Experimental results on the CEC'17 benchmark function confirm the feasibility of this combination.

We propose a model-based deep learning architecture for the correction of phase errors in multishot diffusion-weighted echo-planar MRI images. This work is a generalization of MUSSELS, which is a structured low-rank algorithm. We show that an iterative reweighted least-squares implementation of MUSSELS resembles the model-based deep learning (MoDL) framework. We propose to replace the self-learned linear filter bank in MUSSELS with a convolutional neural network, whose parameters are learned from exemplary data. The proposed algorithm reduces the computational complexity of MUSSELS by several orders of magnitude, while providing comparable image quality.

This paper focuses on discussing the training of specialists in the field of Technosphere safety. The importance of forming professional and essential qualities in the future is highlighted, along with early vocational guidance. Additionally, an emphasis is placed on the significance of studying the values and motives of learners.

The development of Technosphere safety is a crucial aspect of modern society. It encompasses the protection of human health, the environment, and technological systems from accidents, failures, and disasters. Therefore, it is essential to provide high-quality training in this area to produce competent specialists who can work effectively to prevent and mitigate potential risks.

One of the main issues in the training of specialists is the formation of their professional and essential qualities. It is crucial that future specialists possess a strong foundation of knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to succeed in their profession. Additionally, the development of teamwork, leadership, and problem-solving skills is crucial to ensure that specialists can act swiftly and effectively in emergency situations.

Another critical component in the training of specialists is early vocational guidance. It is essential to provide learners with relevant information about the profession, as well as potential career paths, to motivate and inspire them to pursue this specialty. This can help learners identify their strengths and weaknesses, level of interest, and motivation to achieve success.

Studying the values and motives of learners is also of great importance in the training of specialists. Understanding learners' core values and what drives them towards their profession can aid in their development and success. This information can help tailor training programs to meet the learners' specific needs and motivations, effectively enhancing their performance.

In conclusion, the paper stresses the significance of training competent specialists in the field of Technosphere safety. It implies that the formation of professional and essential qualities, early vocational guidance, and understanding learners' values and motives are crucial aspects of the training process that must be considered.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is profoundly influencing our daily lives in many areas, covering small devices to large network systems. An IoT system may be a set of directing rules that rearranges the usage of IoT applications. This paper details a trust management model and security of IoT systems. Trust management models and security play a critical part in IoT to protect information and devices from attacks since it supplies security for all layers and networks. This review focuses on how a trust management model has a significant function in IoT in enhancing reliability, privacy, and security. In this survey, we explained the challenges along with the solutions in terms of IoT security and privacy and recognized the main security problem in the IoT framework. In addition, this paper explored the characteristics of trust and pointed out some IoT security challenges, explaining how middleware can affect the security of IoT.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are adopted in a variety of fields where coverage enhancing is a critical challenge because of the requirements of service quality, cost, and energy consumption. Coverage-enhancing approaches have currently attracted a lot of interest owing to their superior abilities in the deployment of the WSNs, e.g., maximum coverage, minimum sensors, and minimum energy. In this paper, a differential evolution-based regional coverage-enhancing algorithm is proposed for directional 3D WSNs, which is able to maximizing coverage while minimize the number of sensors. First, a directional cone perception model is designed to better display the actual sensing performance of sensor nodes. Subsequently, the coverage region is established to describe the perceptual range of nodes. Thereafter, a three-stage coverage-enhancing method is derived, which includes the pitch angle optimization, the deflection angle optimization and the redundant node sleeping. These strategies are designed to maximize the perception range of a single sensor node, maximize the coverage rate, and minimize the number of nodes, respectively. Finally, simulation results show that our method is able to ensure better performance compared to the state-of-the-art frameworks.

Hashing is widely recognized as an efficient representation learning technique for handling large quantities of data due to its low computational complexity and memory cost. However, most existing hashing methods focus on learning low-dimensional binary features based on high-dimensional vectorized features. There has been limited research exploring how to obtain optimal binary codes from the original 2D image features for retrieval purposes. This paper presents a novel approach, the bilinear supervised discrete hashing (BSDH) method, for generating binary codes from 2D image features. The method utilizes bilinear projections to binarize the image matrix features, preserving the intrinsic characteristics of the 2D image space in the learned binary codes. The final learning framework is formulated by seamlessly integrating bilinear projection approximation and vectorization binary codes regression. Moreover, a discrete optimization strategy is developed to update each variable alternatively in order to obtain high-quality binary codes. Two 2D image features, the traditional SURF-based FVLAD feature and the CNN-based AlexConv5 feature, are also designed to further improve the performance of the proposed BSDH method. Extensive experiments conducted on four benchmark datasets indicate that the proposed BSDH method outperforms all other hashing methods with different input features using different evaluation protocols.

To address the current deficiencies of distribution line classification models, which includes low accuracy and limited robustness, a new rating classification model based on dynamic classification has been introduced. The proposed model combines the K-PAM method with the C4.5 decision tree classification approach to better leverage predicted information from the base classifier and improve overall classification accuracy. Real-world data from three distribution networks were used in the experimental analysis to compare the effectiveness of the three methods in terms of classification efficiency, accuracy, and robustness.

We describe a methodology for extracting and identifying pores in high resolution fingerprint digital images. The key strategy is based on an image subtraction between two fingerprint images with different smoothness levels. The anisotropic diffusion filter is employed to obtain such smoothed fingerprints, in which the pores are preserved in the first fingerprint, while the second one only presents ridges and valleys, but pores are blurred. The subtraction procedure results in a difference image, in which the pores are characterized by the lower magnitudes. After that, we perform a histogram equalization for enhancing pores and a global thresholding to obtain the pores as binary regions. Finally, such binary image is post-processed for removing false pore detections. Experiments were conducted using the PolyU HRF fingerprint image set and the results showed that the proposed methodology outperformed other filtered-based pore extraction methods considering the true and false pore detection rates.

The problem of imbalanced data occurs when there is a skewed distribution of data amongst each class. Learning from imbalanced data poses a challenge for both research and industry applications, and can negatively impact the performance of even powerful machine learning algorithms, such as Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DNN). However, a neuroscience-inspired approach has been proposed in this paper to address this problem. The proposed approach involves training DNN neurons to filter the input and minimize training error through error backpropagation. This approach takes inspiration from two important characteristics of biological vision systems; namely, the non-uniform receptive field distribution in each layer of the visual hierarchy, and the visual cortex's ability to control its attention during development. By using this approach, each neuron learns to react only to a specific input range, which encourages some neurons to learn from imbalanced samples. We have shown through experiments that the proposed model achieves improved performance in various imbalanced data-learning scenarios.

Self-driving cars are becoming popular topics in academia. Consumers of self-driving cars and vehicles have different concerns, for example, safety and security, to name a few. Also, the public sector has interests in self-driving cars such as amending policies to enable the management of self-driving vehicles in cities, urban planning, traffic management and, etc. In this paper, more than 2700 corpus are extracted from literature from several subject areas to identify latent (hidden) topics of self-driving cars. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) is used for topic identification. The result of this study shows that topics identified are valid research areas such as urban planning, driver car (computer) interaction, self-driving control and system design, ethics in self-driving cars, safety and risk assessment, training dataset quality and machine learning in self-driving cars are among the topics identified. Furthermore, the network visualization of association graph of terms shows that the most frequently discussed concepts reveal that control of self-driving cars is based on algorithms, data, design, method, and model. The methods used in this study and the results can be used as decision tools, if carefully applied, in diverse disciplines that are disrupted by the introduction of self-driving cars. For future study, we plan to extend this study with a larger dataset and other data mining techniques.

Automatic seizure detection has been often treated as a classification problem that aims at determining the label of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals by computer science, as the EEG monitoring is a helpful adjunct to the diagnosis of epilepsy. In most existing work, the traditional signal energy of the EEG has been applied for classification, since the energy pattern of epileptic seizures differs from that of non-seizures. Although they are effective, the accuracy either heavily depends on additional information besides energy or is limited by the shortcoming of energy-based features. To address this issue, the proposed approach achieves the classification based on the instantaneous energy of the EEG signals instead. The proposed approach first measures the instantaneous energy related to changes in the EEG signals. Then, energy behavior over time is characterized by instantaneous energy-based features from different aspects. Finally, the classification is carried out on the features to produce output labels. By processing instantaneous energy, the information of energy evolution is involved. As such, the accuracy is improved without bringing in extra information besides energy, or complicated transformation. In multi-class problems, the proposed approach has obtained promising results for identifying the ictal EEG, which indicates the tremendous potential of the proposed approach for epileptic seizure detection.

The paper proposes a bio-inspired model for an imitative sensorimotor learning, which aims at building a map between the sensory representations of gestures (sensory targets) and their underlying motor pattern through random exploration of the motor space. An example of such learning process occurs during vocal learning in humans or birds, when young subjects babble and learn to copy previously heard adult vocalizations. Previous work has suggested that a simple Hebbian learning rule allows perfect imitation when sensory feedback is a purely linear function of the motor pattern underlying movement production. We aim at generalizing this model to the more realistic case where sensory responses are sparse and non-linear. To this end, we explore the performance of various learning rules and normalizations and discuss their biological relevance. Importantly, the proposed model is robust whatever normalization is chosen. We show that both the imitation quality and the convergence time are highly dependent on the sensory selectivity and dimension of the motor representation.

Social media services such as Facebook and Twitter have become a go-to source for daily news for many people around the world. However, this has also led to the exploitation of social media by spreading false information for financial and political gain, which has a negative impact on society. To combat this issue, this paper proposes using machine learning to identify fake news in Arabic tweets through a supervised classification model.

Arabic tweets often have a high level of uncertainty and noise, making it challenging to extract relevant features for classification purposes. Therefore, this paper utilizes content-and user-related features, along with sentiment analysis to generate new features to detect fake Arabic news.

Using four machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, Decision Tree, AdaBoost, and Logistic Regression, the experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed system can accurately filter out fake news with an accuracy of 76%. Moreover, incorporating sentiment analysis enhances the accuracy of the prediction process.

This study showcases the potential of using machine learning algorithms to identify and combat the spread of fake news on social media. It also highlights the importance of developing tailored approaches to tackle specific challenges in different languages and contexts.

Keyframe extraction is important for video retrieval. In order to realize frequency adaptive human motion sequence resampling and achieve high quality keyframe, we propose a new keyframe extraction method for human motion sequence. First, we define the inter-frame similarity metric based on the features of human body parts. Then, the keyframe extraction is realized by the affine propagation clustering algorithm. The proposed method starts from the information distribution of the video itself, adaptively searches for the optimal keyframe of the video, and the operation speed is fast. Finally, the evaluation of the sequence reconstruction based on keyframe is verified. A comparative experiment conducted on the CMU database verified the efficiency of our method.

The NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCD COE) in Tallinn, Estonia is a NATO-accredited knowledge hub that offers a unique interdisciplinary approach to cyber defence. The Centre conducts research, training and exercises in four core areas: technology, strategy, operations, and law. The team comprises a diverse group of international experts, including military, government, academia, and industry professionals from currently 21 member nations.

NATO CCD COE aims to support member nations and NATO in the fields of cyber defence research, training, and exercises. The Centre provides expertise in the areas of technology, strategy, operations, and law, using an interdisciplinary approach. In embodying the cooperation of like-minded nations in cyber defence, NATO CCD COE's member nations are allies within NATO and like-minded partners beyond the Alliance.

With almost half as many nations aspiring to become members in the future, CCD COE is committed to fostering cooperation and delivering state-of-the-art expertise to safeguard against cyber threats.

Rational use of medicines is of great importance in pediatric clinical medication. As the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the pediatric group is highly dynamic, it is a great challenge to determine the rational dosage for pediatric patients. Traditional clinical decision support systems for dosage guidance largely rely on manual collection of medication information, which usually suffers from incomplete and missing evidences for the pediatric group. In this paper, we propose a data-driven approach to accurately predict pediatric medication dosages by leveraging prescription big data. More specifically, we first identify two relevant factors of pediatric medication dosage, i.e., the physiology factors including patients' body weight and age group, and the indication factors that affect clinical dosage patterns. We then extract the corresponding physiology and indication features, and propose a hybrid-learning-based method to adaptively integrate the two sets of heterogeneous features into a model for accurate pediatric dosage prediction. We evaluate our method on real-world prescription datasets from two tertiary children's hospitals. Results show that our method predicts pediatric medication dosages with an accuracy above 81.3%, and consistently outperforms other baselines.

This research presents implementation guidelines and techniques for applying the MQTT protocol on an embedded system to construct smart sensors/actuators and many IoT applications. The proposed system is based on a small and low-cost microcontroller. A firmware of the microcontroller is designed and implemented based on a custom operating system using the special technique. The powerful implementation technique is called the Asynchronous Event-Driven Non-Blocking I/O. All peripheral drivers used in the proposed system are implemented based on event-driven queue and callback functions. With this implementation approach, we can achieve the very high efficiency of the microcontroller. The proposed system can connect to the internet network using WiFi module of Ethernet Controller. It is fully evaluated in real-world environments and tested in many possible conditions. The experimental results show that the proposed system can work correctly as expected in all situations.

Traffic Light detection and recognition has become one of the critical research areas when it comes to autonomous driving vehicles. Developing an algorithm to detect different shaped traffic lights such as traffic lights (TLs) with arrowheads, circular shapes, horizontally and vertically oriented TLs and TLs in different illumination conditions during daytime still remains a challenge. This paper evaluates the existing algorithms, which uses heuristic or template matching based image processing methods and other learning based systems, that consumes higher time and processing power for training and map based systems and proposes a novel optimized algorithm using machine vision techniques to meet those challenges. The experiments were carried out using videos taken by front camera of vehicles. The results of the algorithm show a higher accuracy for precision and recall evaluations.

There are numerous onomatopoeias in the Japanese language. These serve as a direct means for Japanese people to convey their own senses and images to others. Onomatopoeias are characterized by sound symbolism, allowing those familiar with Japanese to metaphorically associate images with even new coined words. However, for those with different linguistic backgrounds, it can be difficult to grasp the semantic usage of Japanese onomatopoeias in a metaphorical sense. To address this issue, research has focused on the phonological and acoustic features of onomatopoeias. Attempts have been made to automatically classify onomatopoeias into appropriate semantic usage categories using these features. This paper employed mimetic words associated with "human action" as an example for automatic classification. Through investigation, we have identified useful features among the phonological and acoustic features for classifying mimetic words.

In this paper, a novel super nested sparse circular array (S-NSCA) is presented for high resolution direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. The S-NSCA maintains the same properties as the nested sparse circular array (NSCA) but also yields the sparsest possible array configuration similar to super nested arrays. This innovative configuration reduces the number of sensor pairs with small inter-sensor spacing which leads to a significant improvement in DOA estimation resolution, while maintaining the same physical aperture and degrees of freedom as the NSCA. The effectiveness of the proposed array is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

The tremendous growth of Wireless Sensor Networks and embedded devices, along with their integration into the Smart Homes system, has paved the way for new breakthroughs in the eHealth sector. With this in mind, a new concept was introduced to merge personalized health data collected through wireless sensors, such as personal trackers, with the formal Electronic Health Record (EHR) used in the Croatia's Central Health Information System. The primary aim of this initiative is to develop simple, yet flexible schemas for the different types of healthcare data, while also modeling an ETL process (extract, transform, load) that is comprehensible, transparent and automated to ensure data integrity. The critical challenge of ensuring privacy is also considered in this process, as patient confidentiality is of utmost importance.

The applications of deep learning-based methods are rapidly expanding to assist individuals with disabilities, such as helping the blind to see or enabling the deaf to hear and speak. In computer vision, one of the latest challenges is the re-identification of a person among a set of cameras. Person re-identification involves matching images of the same person across multiple non-overlapping camera views and is commonly broken down into three sub-modules: detection, tracking, and matching. However, most techniques rely on manually annotated bounding boxes, which is not ideal in a real-time environment where object localization is not available. To address this issue, researchers have developed an end-to-end deep learning technique that not only targets matching but localization of objects as well, handling detection and re-identification together. The proposed method has been tested in diverse situations, resulting in higher retrieval accuracy and outperforming state-of-the-art methods on PRW datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness and generalization ability of this approach.

Access to safe and affordable surgery remains a major challenge for five billion people globally. Studies have consistently shown that hospitals in low-and-middle income countries lack access to basic surgical equipment, including theatre lights, anesthesia machines, and electro-surgical units. Moreover, most equipment is designed with a focus on high income countries, which fails to consider financial resources and access to maintenance, spare parts, and consumables in low-and-middle income countries. 

To address this issue, a roadmap for designing surgical equipment for worldwide use has been proposed. The roadmap consists of four phases, starting with identifying the need for certain surgical equipment and thoroughly researching the context in which the equipment will be used. Design requirements should be determined in Phase 2, with prototyping and close interaction with local end-users starting in Phase 3. Throughout this process, designers should prioritize safety and quality, while also ensuring that the equipment is optimized for the local context and easily applicable in comparable settings globally. 

By following this roadmap, we can work towards ensuring access to safe and affordable surgery for all, regardless of income level or geographic location.

During the process of smart city construction, city managers always spend a lot of energy and money for cleaning street garbage due to the random appearances of street garbage. Consequently, visual street cleanliness assessment is particularly important. However, the existing assessment approaches have some clear disadvantages, such as the collection of street garbage information is not automated and street cleanliness information is not real-time. To address these disadvantages, this paper proposes a novel urban street cleanliness assessment approach using mobile edge computing and deep learning. First, the high-resolution cameras installed on vehicles collect the street images. Mobile edge servers are used to store and extract street image information temporarily. Second, these processed street data is transmitted to the cloud data center for analysis through city networks. At the same time, Faster Region-Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN) is used to identify the street garbage categories and count the number of garbage. Finally, the results are incorporated into the street cleanliness calculation framework to ultimately visualize the street cleanliness levels, which provides convenience for city managers to arrange clean-up personnel effectively. The overall approach is illustrated and visualized using the street images of Jiangning District in Nanjing, China. The practical application shows the feasibility and usability of the approach.

Recovering missing values is an essential task in time series applications. However, replacing the missing data and building dependency relationships from incomplete sample sets remains challenging. Previous research has shown that residual networks (ResNet) can cope with the degradation problem through shortcut connection, while gated recurrent unit (GRU) can reduce training parameters and improve the network model by using update gates instead of forgetting and output gates in long short-term memory (LSTM). Inspired by these findings, we propose decay residual mean imputation GRU (DRMI-GRU), an imputation network that uses a decay residual mean unit (DRMU) to model incomplete time series with the help of previous and global revealed information. The decay factor balances previous long-term dependencies and all non-missing values, while a mask unit is designed to check missing data. Extensive empirical comparisons with existing imputation algorithms on real-world data and public datasets with different ratios of missing data demonstrate the superior performance of our model.

Despite its significance, modulation classification of constant envelope modulations (CEM) has not gained worthy attention in AMC literature so far. Two neural network-based architectures, i.e., radial basis function network (RBFN) and sparse-autoencoder-based deep neural network (DNN) are proposed and analyzed for the classification of spectrally efficient CEM modulations. A blind classification method which does not require any a-priori information about the channel or CEM specifics is based on the effectiveness of proposed hybrid feature space (HFS), used to train the trending neural network classifiers. Classification performance of both networks is analyzed for the typical additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel and less explored, unfriendly, frequency-selective fading environment under the impact of Doppler shift.

The goal of upper extremity Prosthetic Research is to design and develop an anthropomorphic artificial limb having sufficient grasping strength, response speed and a visual appeal. The paper describes the design and assembling of a prosthetic arm that has the flexibility and motion as that of a human arm. A finger of the designed arm is modeled using Neural Networks. Pertinent results verify the system identification using Neural Network.

Fingerprint matching is one of the extensively used tools to authenticate users. It has been accepted by governments of various countries to authenticate their citizens. The common practice in a fingerprint based system is to store minutiae points of fingerprints as the user template. The minutiae points information can be accessed through an attack by an adversary and the original fingerprint of users can be obtained using this information. Unlike passwords, a compromised fingerprint is irreparable and there is a necessity to protect user data. In this paper, a technique called Polynomial Vault is proposed to secure fingerprint information. The fingerprint features and a unique user key-set are used to generate a secure template for a user by using a non-invertible transformation. This obtained template is used to authenticate the user. In case a user template is compromised, the proposed technique provides a way to construct a new template by changing the user key-set values. To demonstrate the efficiency and the robustness of the proposed technique, a thorough experimental analysis is being conducted using IIT Kanpur, FVC2004 (DB1 and DB2), FVC2002 (DB1, DB2, DB3, and DB4), and FVC2000 (DB1 and DB2) databases.

When implemented in the digital domain with time, space and value discretized in the binary form, many good dynamical properties of chaotic systems in continuous domain may be degraded or even diminish. To measure the dynamic complexity of a digital chaotic system, the dynamics can be transformed to the form of a state-mapping network. Then, the parameters of the network are verified by some typical dynamical metrics of the original chaotic system in infinite precision, such as Lyapunov exponent and entropy. This article reviews some representative works on the network-based analysis of digital chaotic dynamics and presents a general framework for such analysis, unveiling some intrinsic relationships between digital chaos and complex networks. As an example for discussion, the dynamics of a state-mapping network of the Logistic map in a fixed-precision computer is analyzed and discussed.

This paper presents a novel approach to detect abnormalities in dynamic systems based on multisensory data and feature selection. The proposed method produces multiple inference models by considering several features of the observed data. This work facilitates the obtainment of the most precise features for predicting future instances and detecting abnormalities. Growing neural gas (GNG) is employed for clustering multisensory data into a set of nodes that provide a semantic interpretation of data and define local linear models for prediction purposes. Our method uses a Markov Jump particle filter (MJPF) for state estimation and abnormality detection. The proposed method can be used for selecting the optimal set features to be shared in networking operations such that state prediction, decision-making, and abnormality detection processes are favored. This work is evaluated by using a real dataset consisting of a moving vehicle performing some tasks in a controlled environment.

Drone-cell technology is emerging as a solution to support and backup the cellular network architecture. cell-drones are flexible and provide a more dynamic solution for resource allocation in both scales: spatial and geographic. They allow to increase the bandwidth availability anytime and everywhere according the continuous rate demands. Their fast deployment provide network operators with a reliable solution to face sudden network overload or peak data demands during mass events, without interrupting services and guaranteeing better QoS for users. With these advantages, drone-cell network management is still a complex task. We propose in this paper, a multiagent reinforcement learning approach for dynamic drones-cells management. Our approach is based on an enhanced joint action selection. Results show that our model speed up network learning and provide better network performance.

Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) is a network in which it employs wireless sensor technology and it forms a network to continuously observe the surrounding area. For human body communication WBAN is a best reasonable system yet observing of physiological and biochemical parameters in human body are quiet challenging. Maintenance of sensor nodes is a real problem and prohibits their widespread used in health monitoring application. This work deals with the implementation of Ad Hoc On-Demand Distance Vector routing (AODV) and Dynamic Source Routing (DSR) protocols, comparative analysis of routing proto-cols has been performed based on the end to end delay, packet delivery ratio, and throughput.

In view of the massive data transmission and storage of various types of ocean data, and the limitations of IPv4 transmission protocols on marine projects, we propose a digital ocean cloud platform architecture based on IPv6 intelligent gateway, which utilizes an unlimited number of address resource pools of IPv6. The characteristics of efficient and secure data dissemination combined with cloud computing service technology, based on distributed storage technology, provide a safe and reliable storage environment for marine sensor data, ocean images and text, and ocean data through cloud computing technology and ocean data can be aggregated, classified and processed and through cloud computing technology can deepen the value of ocean data.

In this paper we examine data fusion methods for multi-view data classification. We present a decision concept which explicitly takes into account the input multi-view structure, where for each case there is a different subset of relevant views. The proposed method, which we dub Mixture of Views, is implemented by a special purpose neural network architecture. It is demonstrated on the task of classifying breast microcalcifications as benign or malignant based on several mammography views. The single view decisions are combined by a data-driven decision, according to the relevance of each view in a given case, into a global decision. The method is evaluated on a large multi-view dataset extracted from the standardized digital database for screening mammography (DDSM). The experimental results show that our method outperforms previously suggested fusion methods.

Container management frameworks, such as Docker, pack applications and their complex software environment in self-contained images, which facilitates application deployment, distribution, and sharing. Currently, container images are organized in a multi-layer file-system manner. For example, Docker uses AUFS to organize its container image storage. However, when a new version is created, all the changes are stored in a new layer via a Copy-On-Write mechanism, which can trigger a heavy burden for the network and storage. There are also other image storage approaches such as chunk-based technology. In this paper, we suggest that the container image storage system should not use one storage technology for all images, but should choose different technology for concrete images according to the image's distinct features. We design some experiments to compare the layer-based and chuck-based technology. And based on the analysis of the collected data, this paper gives some principles for the selection of image management techniques and discusses some interesting potential research topics.

With the rapid growth of information, feature selection has become an important step before data classification. Evolutionary algorithms can be used to solve feature selection given their effective search capabilities since the traditional feature selection cann't consider the combination effect. In this paper, we present a novel filter feature selection using a niching binary particle swarm optimization. The entire population is divided into several niche groups to maintain the diversity of evolutionary environment. A new framework based on three different kinds of topologies is proposed which can avoid falling into the local optimum and enhance global search capabilities. In this framework, when the optimal fitness value has stagnated for 20 generations, the connection between particles in each niche group and the connection between niche center particles will change to improve the optimal fitness value. The above procedure can produce a subset of features. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, we have tested on five data sets in the UCI database. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively search for the feature space and verify the efficiency of the obtained feature subsets under different classifiers.

The female physiological examination known as leucorrhea routine is a standard practice for determining the health of women. In this procedure, visible components in microscopic images are detected and counted to identify any abnormalities. Unfortunately, there are no significant research findings in this field. However, based on the principles of deep learning, an improved R-CNN model has been created to enable intelligent recognition of visible components in leucorrhea microscopic images. With a detection precision rate of 93.6% and a detection time of only 300 milliseconds, this algorithm holds enormous potential for automating and intellectualizing leucorrhea routine procedures. The accomplishment of this algorithm provides a solid theoretical foundation for making leucorrhea routine a more efficient, intelligent and accurate procedure.

This paper explores the relationship between the AC capacitor bushing core and its impact on the electric field. The research shows that the plate distribution of the capacitor core has a unique feature, known as the electric field determining feature. This feature remains independent of the details of the step, layer thickness, and margin but influences the electric field. Capacitor cores with the same material and electric field determining feature exhibit similar electric field distributions and impact on the external electric field, even with varying amounts and distributions of plates. 

When the plate distribution is infinitely dense, the electric field determining feature is equivalent to its envelopes. However, for actual plate distributions with a limited number of plates, the electric field determining feature has no direct relationship with its envelopes. Despite this, it can be approximated to the envelopes of the infinitely dense plate distribution, which helps in simplifying the bushing model using a conversion method between different plate distributions. 

In light of these findings, the paper proposes a new design method for the AC capacitor bushing core based on the electric field determining feature.

Illegal fishing poses an existential threat to global fisheries and is responsible for causing significant damage and depletion to fish stocks, food security and national economies. We describe a method through our agent-based high-level information fusion system to automate the detection of illegal fishing, thereby providing analysts with real-time indicators, warnings, and a question and answering capability. By automated reasoning over fused human-and sensor-derived sources we demonstrate the capacity to automatically infer candidate cases, which may enable authorities to take action in a timely fashion.

In order to model nonlinear industrial processes for on-line estimating those quality-related but difficult-to-measure variables, this paper proposes an inferential sensing approach based on Gaussian mixture model and extreme learning machine which is referred to as the `GMM-ELM'. In the GMM-ELM, mixture of ELMs is developed under the framework of GMM to deal with nonlinear and non-Gaussian characteristics, where localization and localized ELMs are completed unifiedly instead of separately. In addition, Bayesian regularization is exerted for the weight vector that connects the hidden and output nodes for each ELM to handle overfitting. We also develop an efficient learning algorithm to train the GMM-ELM. Experiments are carried out on a real-world industrial process to evaluate the performance of the GMM- ELM, which demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach as well as its promising foreground in monitoring or automatic control of the quality-related variables.

The angle-based repetitive controller (RC) has been applied successfully in the literature for torque ripple suppression in variable speed permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs). The RC is preferred because of its learning capability, which allows the cancelation of all periodic ripples from multiple sources. However, its tuning method has not yet been proposed. Since the structure of the RC is found similar to the disturbance observer (DOB), which is convenient to tune through pole placement, this paper merges the angle-based RC and DOB into a novel angle-based repetitive observer (ARO) for the first time for the torque ripple reduction in PMSMs. ARO takes advantages of its DOB structure that it can be designed separately and can easily be added into an existing control loop. Taking advantage of its RC nature, ARO can tackle a wide frequency range of torque ripple even in the presence of measurement noise. The experimental test results have confirmed the robust performance of ARO under five conditions, including the ideal integral delay, the fractional delay, the load transient, the speed transient, and the detuned mechanical parameters conditions. The execution time of the ARO is less than 10 μs.

Current deep supervised learning methods often require a large amount of labeled data for effective training, which can be challenging to acquire due to the significant cost associated with clinical data acquisition and labeling. Medical datasets used for such training are therefore relatively small in size. To address this limitation, we propose a variational generative model coupled with a data augmentation approach that utilizes the generative model to synthesize data. Our model learns the probability distribution of image data conditioned on a latent variable and corresponding labels, enabling it to synthesize new images for data augmentation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on two independent clinical datasets - ultrasound images of the spine and magnetic resonance images of the brain. Using our method, a baseline and a residual model achieve an accuracy of 85% and 92%, respectively, on the spine dataset compared to 78% and 83% using conventional training approaches for image classification tasks. Furthermore, the accuracy of a baseline and a U-net network is 84% and 88%, respectively, in the Dice coefficient in tumor segmentation on the brain dataset compared to 80% and 83% obtained by conventional training approaches.

Traffic signs are essential for regulating daily traffic, providing crucial information to drivers. In the case of unmanned driving systems, the real-time and reliable detection and recognition of traffic signs is of utmost importance. To tackle this issue, a system for autonomous radio-controlled cars has been proposed, aimed at detecting and recognizing these signs. This system combines traditional image processing methods with deep neural network techniques. The process involves streaming online video from the car camera and assessing the input frame of the region of interest. Then, a convolutional neural network is deployed to recognize the candidate images. The experimental results indicate that the proposed system worked efficiently in up to 87.36% of the images. However, it is crucial to calibrate the image processing techniques for diverse environments.

Due to recent advancements in cellular communication systems, stochastic processes are required for optimal performance. The randomness in user behavior with respect to geographical patterns, population density, architecture, data usage, and mobility necessitates the utilization of stochastic processes to accurately analyze these processes. The stochastic-geometry-based Poisson point process technique is a suitable solution that considers transmitters and receivers as elements of stochastic point processes. Heterogeneous network topologies cannot utilize the hexagonal method, and stochastic geometry serves as a viable solution for predicting probabilistic parameters. Relay nodes can be utilized for homogeneous random models, and the proposed PPP realistic model utilizes various metrics for evaluating the results. The results validated the proposed PPP model approach as superior to the grid model and conventional multi-antenna ultra-dense network approaches.

Dropout is a regularization technique used to prevent over-fitting in neural networks by randomly removing some neurons from the original network structure. However, as neural networks become larger and more complex, the number of linearly correlated neurons increases resulting in data redundancy and waste of resources. Additionally, the correlated neurons negatively affect the sparsity of neural networks which in turn hampers the efficiency of algorithm execution. To address this issue, this paper presents an innovative approach to integrate the concept of relevance into Dropout, resulting in an improved regularization method known as R-Dropout. This technique enhances sparsity by increasing the probability of eliminating highly correlated neurons. Results obtained from public datasets indicate that the R-Dropout technique not only improves accuracy marginally but also enhances the convergence speed and efficiency of the algorithm.

Modern cloud architectures encompass computing and communication elements that span from traditional data center computing nodes to edge-computing and IoT devices. The OPERA project has developed a cloud architecture that provides new levels of energy efficiency as a full chip-to-Cloud solution. This paper focuses on a smart vision application, namely road traffic monitoring, and presents novel architectural solutions optimized for high energy efficiency at any level. 

The computing elements supporting the acceleration of State-of-the-Art Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are optimized for high-density acceleration. An innovative wireless communication subsystem, unlike conventional designs, exploits the advantages of software-defined radio (SDN) firmware to control a reconfigurable antenna. A reconfigurable antenna amplifies the signal while also increasing the range of transmission. 

To further extend the application range, an energy harvesting module is used to supplement the power supply. This innovation ensures that Cloud architecture remains high-performance coupled with high energy efficiency over the whole system. The effectiveness of the whole architecture has been tested in a real context at two installation sites. In-field measurements demonstrate the claim that the OPERA project's Cloud architecture offers high-performance coupled with high energy efficiency.

We present a solution to the issue of robust state estimation and attack isolation for discrete-time nonlinear systems with positive-slope nonlinearities that are susceptible to sensor attacks and measurement noise. Specifically, we focus on scenarios where a subset of sensors are vulnerable to additive false data injection attacks. Our proposed estimator is based on a bank of circle-criterion observers, each resulting in an Input-to-State Stable (ISS) estimation error. This approach enables the provision of robust estimates for the system state, despite the presence of sensor attacks and measurement noise. Additionally, we introduce an algorithm for detecting and isolating sensor attacks. Our method employs the ISS property of the observers to verify whether the observer trajectories are consistent with those of the attack-free system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method through simulations.

This article presents a low-cost Internet of Things (IoT) node for customized smart-applications, showcasing its concept, methodology, architecture, and physical implementation. The node is designed to efficiently integrate state-of-the-art discrete electronic components suitable for supporting a variety of smart applications. It includes an ARM CortexM based microcontroller, power management unit, and several sensors, each having specialized adapters. 

The IoT node is currently being tested and validated in vineyard fields as part of the framework of precision agriculture. The node's primary function is to collect critical environmental parameters, which will then serve as input to algorithmic models for detecting and preventing related agricultural diseases. 

Overall, this IoT node serves as an innovative and cost-effective solution for developing customized smart applications, offering advanced and efficient integration of state-of-the-art electronic components, with the potential to revolutionize various industries.

This paper proposes a simplified simulation and modelling tech for microgrid. This method can save simulation time and computational memory, compared with the simulation of the detail model. Firstly, the grid-tied inverter, the integrated load, and the nonlinear load in microgrid are analyzed and modeled. Next, their models are simplified as Thévenin-Norton equivalent models. Moreover, the consistency between hardware equivalent model and control equivalent model of power electronics devices is proved. Finally, the correctness of the simplified simulation and modelling tech is confirmed during voltage sag in the improved IEEE 13 Node Test Feeder system in MATLAB/SIMULINK. The results show that the outputs characteristics of the simplified models are consistent with those of their detailed models.

This paper presents an adaptive neural control approach for nonstrict-feedback nonlinear systems with unmodeled dynamics. The controller design process is complicated due to the presence of unknown functions and unmodeled dynamics, which are common in practical applications. To approximate the unknown functions, the radial basis function neural networks (RBF NNs) method is utilized. Additionally, a dynamic signal is introduced to tackle the problem of unmodeled dynamics. The innovation of this study lies in utilizing the properties of Gaussian functions to address the nonstrict-feedback form. Based on these preconditions, the authors develop an adaptive NNs controller design scheme by applying the backstepping recursive design. The proposed approach guarantees that all signals in the closed-loop system are semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded (SGUUB), and the tracking error converges to a small neighborhood around the origin. The paper concludes by providing a simulation example that demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method.

To create an electric shoulder prosthesis that can be used without extensive training, we have developed an intuitive shoulder prosthesis system. This system is composed of four degrees of freedom joints and a control system that adapts to the user through machine learning techniques and surface myoelectric potentials of the trunk. To identify the optimal myoelectric potential measurement location on the trunk, we analyzed the surface myoelectric potential of healthy subjects by performing a principal component analysis. Our findings revealed that the optimal measurement points were located in the chest and back.

Furthermore, we evaluated the performance of our developed system by conducting a pick-and-place task in a three-dimensional space. In this task, the developed system was controlled by myoelectric potential obtained from the optimal measurement points. As a result of the experiment, we found that our developed shoulder disarticulation prosthesis was able to grasp and move objects in both vertical and horizontal directions with minimal learning time (approximately 35 seconds). 

In summary, our study highlights an innovative approach to the development of electric prostheses. By utilizing machine learning techniques and surface myoelectric potentials, we have created an intuitive system that requires minimal training and can be effectively controlled by the user.

Modeling cyber-attacks is a very attractive area of research because of its practical importance. However, most of the related research in the literature does not consider the simultaneous (or coordinated) attacks, which, in fact, is an important attack instrument in practice. This is mainly because of the complicated evolution of cyber-attacks over networks. In this paper, we propose a novel model, which can accommodate different types of simultaneous attacks with possible heterogeneous compromise probabilities. Our results show that simultaneous attacks have a significant effect on the reliability/dynamics of network systems. In particular, we present a sufficient condition for the epidemics dying out over the network, and upper bounds for the time to extinction. We also provide upper bounds for compromise probabilities of network systems when the evolution enters the quasi-equilibrium state. The effects of strength of simultaneous attacks and heterogeneity among successful attack probabilities on epidemic spreading are studied as well. The theoretical results are further validated by the simulation evidence.

Microblogging networks have gained popularity in recent years as a platform enabling expressions of human emotions, through which users can conveniently produce contents on public events, breaking news, and/or products. Subsequently, microblogging networks generate massive amounts of data that carry opinions and mass sentiment on various topics. Herein, microblogging is regarded as a useful platform for detecting and propagating new hot events. It is also a useful channel for identifying high-quality posts, popular topics, key interests, and high-influence users. The existence of noisy data in the traditional social media data streams enforces to focus on human-centric computing. This paper proposes a human-centric social computing (HCSC) model for hot-event detection and propagation in microblogging networks. In the proposed HCSC model, all posts and users are preprocessed through hypertext induced topic search (HITS) for determining high-quality subsets of the users, topics, and posts. Then, a latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA)-based multiprototype user topic detection method is used for identifying users with high influence in the network. Furthermore, an influence maximization is used for final determination of influential users based on the user subsets. Finally, the users mined by influence maximization process are generated as the influential user sets for specific topics. Experimental results prove the superiority of our HCSC model against similar models of hot-event detection and information propagation.

A Ship Detection Method based on Recurrent Neural Network in a Marine Radar System is investigated. Considering that the characteristics of the single-frame radar image are not obvious, we selected image sequences concatenated by single-frame radar images as research objects and designed a coding mode to complete the mapping of radar targets to vectors. Our model based on RNN made a good performance on the dataset made by ourselves.

An event-based state estimation problem for a discrete-time system when the measurements are corrupted with multiplicative noise is considered in this letter. A general event-based sampling is employed to obtain the measurements, where the event-based strategy is implicitly utilized to obtain state estimate and covariance. To deal with multiplicative noise, maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator is used in conjunction with the Newton-Raphson iterative method. The proposed results are depicted using a numerical example.

This paper discusses a comparative analysis of automated screening procedures for Pap smear using deep learning technology. The study employed three different convolution neural network models, namely AlexNet, densenet161, and resnet101, to identify the presence of cervical cancerous or precancerous cells within the Pap smear database. The study compared accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and computation time for each deep learning model. The densenet161 emerged as the best model due to its high sensitivity and accuracy, both of which are essential for identifying cervical cancer at an early stage and achieving better treatment outcomes. An automated Pap smear screening procedure that utilizes the densenet161 lead to an enhanced early detection of cervical cancer, thus reducing the burden of the disease.

With the rapid advances of wireless technologies and popularization of mobile devices, edge computing boosts mobile social networks (MSNs) to allow mobile users to deliver, share, and exchange contents with each other. In particular, with edge caching, various content services can be provided to mobile users with improved Quality-of-Experience (QoE). However, edge caching is vulnerable to cache pollution attack (CPAttack), degrading content delivery. To tackle these problems, in this paper, we propose a hidden Markov model (HMM) based detection scheme against CPAttack in edge computing enabled MSNs. Specifically, we first present the CPAttack model with the observations of malicious behaviors. According to the CPAttack model, the caching state of each edge device is characterized in terms of request rate and cache hit rate. The HMM is exploited to detect the CPAttack with observation sequence of caching states. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can efficiently improve edge devices' capability to detect CPAttack.

Collaborative filtering is one of the most effective and adequate technique used in recommendation. The fundamental aim of the recommendation is to provide prediction of the different items in which a user would be interested in based on their preferences. Recommendation systems based on collaborative filtering techniques are able to provide approximately accurate prediction when there is enough data. User based collaborative filtering taechniques have been very powerful and success in the past to recommend the items based on user's preferences. But, there are also some certain challenges such as scalability and sparsity of data which increases as the number of users and items increases. In a large website, it is difficult to find the interested information in a certain time. But the recommendation system filter out information and items that are best suitable for us. Although there are different recommendation approaches, yet collaborative filtering technique is very popular because of the effectiveness. In this work, movie recommender system has been described, which basically uses item-based technique of collaborative filtering to provide the recommendations of items, which is dynamic and will learn from the positive feedback.

Public cloud storage is a fundamental cloud computing service. Currently, most owners of large data outsource their data to cloud storage services-even high-profile owners such as governments. However, public cloud storage services are not optimal for ensuring the possession and integrity of the outsourced data, a situation that has given rise to many proposed provable data possession check schemes (PDP). A PDP scheme allows data owners to efficiently, periodically, and securely verify that a cloud storage provider possesses the outsourced data. Most of the currently available provable data possession check schemes make selective (i.e., probabilistic) checks using random data blocks to verify data integrity rather than checking the entire dataset. Therefore, these schemes are considered inadequate by critical infrastructure sectors that involve highly sensitive data (critical data). In this paper, a new and efficient deterministic data integrity check scheme called cryptographic-accumulator provable data possession (CAPDP) is proposed. The CAPDP surpasses the common limitations exhibited by other currently proposed schemes. The underlying scheme of the CAPDP is based on a modified RSA-based cryptographic accumulator that has the following advantages: 1) it allows the data owner to perform an unlimited number of data integrity checks; 2) it supports data dynamics; 3) it is efficient in terms of communication, computation and storage costs for both the data owner and the cloud storage provider; 4) the verification operation in the proposed scheme is independent of the number of blocks being verified; 5) it minimizes the burden and cost of the verification process on the data owner's side, enabling verification to be performed even on low-power devices; and 6) it prevents tag forgery, data deletion, replacement, and data leakage attacks and detects replay attacks. Moreover, the prototype implementation and experimental results show that the scheme is applicable in real-life applications.

Computational storage is an emerging concept in big data scenario where the demand to process ever-growing storage workloads is outpacing traditional compute server architectures. To enable this paradigm there is a call for developing accelerators that off-load some of the management routines that are usually demanded to the smartness inside the storage. For enterprise solid-state drives (SSD) this translates into a dedicated hardware that exploits the interconnection fabric of the host with the goal of improving SSD reliability/performance. In this brief, we have developed an field-programmable gate array-based neural network accelerator for the moving read reference shift prediction in enterprise SSD. The accelerator high prediction accuracy (up to 99.5%), low latency (6.5 μs per prediction), and low energy consumption (19.5 μJ) opens up unprecedented usage models in the storage environment.

Convolutional neural network (CNN) based face recognition algorithms learn a discriminative feature mapping by enforcing separation between different classes and/or aggregation within the same class. However, these algorithms may be biased due to uneven sampling density in the training data since they do not consider the proximity of underlying faces. Additionally, these algorithms may fail to indicate the relationship between other attributes such as gender or ethnicity, which may be important in some face recognition applications. 

To address these issues, we propose a CNN-based face recognition approach that incorporates these attributes into the training process. We achieve this by using an attribute-aware loss function that regularizes the feature mapping using attribute proximity. By doing so, our approach learns more discriminative features that are correlated with the attributes. 

We train our face recognition model using a large-scale RGB-D data set with over 100K identities captured under real application conditions. Our experiments show that the depth channel and attribute-aware loss significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of face recognition compared to existing methods. We believe that our approach provides a more comprehensive and effective solution for face recognition tasks, particularly in scenarios where attributes such as gender or ethnicity play a crucial role.

With the technological advancements and the evolution of smart cities, people's daily lives have changed drastically. However, this shift has also brought privacy concerns and the need to protect sensitive data generated by these smart environments. This paper addresses the issue of protecting and classifying sensitive data using homomorphic encryption and the Naive Bayes algorithm. The proposed approach is tested on three datasets - Road Traffic Data, Pollution Data, and Parking Data - provided by the City Pulse Smart City Dataset. Results show that the method is promising and outperforms existing methods, achieving an accuracy rate of 89.24%, 92.17%, and 86.39% for Road Traffic Data, Pollution Data, and Parking Data, respectively. It is clear that as the world becomes more intelligent, the need for advanced data protection methods is essential to ensure the privacy and security of sensitive information.
