This paper delves into the theoretical boundaries of resource allocation overheads in vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs), recognizing that the allocation procedure can consume extensive system resources. To determine these boundaries, a permutation-based model is proposed, analyzing the overhead limits while assuming the unordered resource allocation patterns as a permutation process. Using this model, one can calculate the minimum bits required to represent resource allocation information. To apply this theory to real-world applications, the bipartite graph is used to describe resource reuse in respective domains, considering dynamicity. 

The proposed permutation-based model is applied to analyze the resource allocation overheads of two typical resource allocation schemes in VANETs: time-division multiple access (TDMA) and cluster-based algorithms. The new methodology provides a tradeoff analysis between overheads and system efficiency when evaluating the capacity of the VANETs. 

Overall, this paper contributes valuable insights into the understanding of resource allocation overheads in VANETs, presenting a permutation-based model that can provide new ways to analyze and improve these wireless networks.

Modern power networks face increasingly difficult challenges in controlling their transient frequency behavior at acceptable levels due to the low inertia and highly dynamic units. This paper proposes a distributed control strategy based on a subset of buses in the power network to maintain their transient frequencies within safe ranges while ensuring the overall stability of the system. Using Lyapunov stability and set invariance theory, constraints for the transient frequency requirement and asymptotic stability requirement are formulated for the control input. For each bus of interest, a distributed and Lipschitz controller is synthesized to satisfy both constraints. This ensures the uniqueness and existence of the trajectories of the closed-loop system. The results are demonstrated through simulations on the IEEE 39-bus power network.

Many computer systems and data storage are accessed by unauthorized parties, due to the lack of authentication quality possessed by the system. Face Recognition is one of the evolving authentication systems at this time, which can use 2D or 3D data. However, 2D face recognition is easily influenced by environmental circumstances, facial orientation, facial expressions, and makeup. The use of 3D data can help to overcome the intrinsic problems possessed by the 2D approach. 3D face recognition system using a 3D camera has a weakness, i.e. it cannot be used in outdoor. We proposed the usage of DSLR commercial cameras to overcome such problem. The algorithms used in this research is are DLT and neural network. DLT is an algorithm that can determine the 3D coordinates of a point obtained from some 2D images. The neural network is used to recognize faces. In this study, an authentication system is made using DLT and neural network algorithms using DSLR cameras for capturing the faces. The best combination of neural network architecture is the number of hidden nodes 20 with 1 layer, learning rate 0.005 with an accuracy of 95%, the percentage of FAR and FRR of 5% and 5%

With the advent of big data era, data driven quality management decision-making has become an important means to seek new quality improvement opportunity for manufacturers. Quality accidents (QAs) can cause severely economic and reputational damage to manufacturer, accurate identification of root causes for severe quality accident is the primary task and always a big challenge for quality managers. Because of the fuzzy nature of incomplete and noisy data for big data, the fuzzy concept is proposed, and the fuzzy weighted association rule mining (FWARM) method is adopted into the root cause identification of quality accident novelly. Firstly, Quality Accident formation mechanism and modeling of big data for quality accident are defined; Secondly, root cause identification framework of quality accident based on the relevance tree is established; Then, the FWARM method is used to identify product functional defects and physical defects through big data for quality accident. Finally, a case study of root cause identification of quality accident is adopted to validate the proposed approach.

In this paper, we investigate the degrees-of-freedom (DoF) region of a class of two-unicast wireless networks assuming delayed channel state information at the transmitters. We examine a layered topology with arbitrary connectivity and propose new outer-bounds on the DoF region of such networks through the use of bottleneck nodes. These nodes serve as informational bottlenecks only under the assumption of delayed channel state information. 

Additionally, we present novel transmission schemes that achieve the outer-bounds established in our study. The results we obtained indicated that the sum DoF of two-unicast networks with delayed channel knowledge can take on an infinite set of values, unlike the instantaneous model for channel state information. 

Furthermore, we compare our current findings to the best-known outer-bounds and demonstrate that there can be a significant gap in favor of our proposed model. Overall, our study contributes to a better understanding of the DoF region of wireless networks with delayed channel state information and offers new insights into the role of bottleneck nodes in such scenarios.

Detecting community structures in social networks presents a significant challenge, and numerous methods have been developed to address this issue. Recently, a mapping-reduction model has gained attention as a promising solution, where data and algorithms are distributed among several process nodes to reduce the complexity of time and memory needed for community detection in large social networks. 

This paper introduces a new mechanism called distributed cache memory, which stores different values assigned to different keys and can distribute them to various computational nodes as required. The proposed framework is implemented using SPARK tools and tested on various major social networks, demonstrating its effectiveness through experiments that involve various parameter values. 

Overall, this study contributes to the advancement of community detection in social networks, and it is expected to support the development of more efficient and accurate community detection methods in the future.

In order to improve the quality of peak characteristics extraction in chromatographic data, an automatic peak fitting method based on wavelet ridges and morphology (WMPF) was proposed. In handling overlapping peaks and weak peaks, WMPF gave solution to deal with the shortcomings of existing peak detection methods. The ridge line of the signal was obtained by wavelet transform of the original chromatogram signal, and the signal was divided into peak areas and non-peak areas. Then, we processed morphological operations with an adaptive window, and combined Gaussian fitting with wavelet ridge information. Finally, the peak characteristics of the signal were extracted. Through the analysis of high-density lipoprotein electrophoretogram data, it was confirmed that the proposed method was effective for baseline separation, noise elimination, peak detection and overlapping peak recognition.

Prediction of bus travel time and/or delay time is a useful tool for passengers who want to plan their journey, e.g., when they should leave from the origin bus stop, what they will do after arriving at the destination bus stop, and so on. Many studies have tackled this task using probe data and/or the real time data provided by automatic vehicle location (AVL) systems. Most of them only targeted a small number of routes, short time periods, e.g. less than one week, and used few machine learning models to evaluate their methods. However, different routes generally show different characteristics. In fact, there are big differences between urban routes and rural routes. Furthermore, the performance of machine learning models also varies according to the data dealt with by the models. In this paper, we propose prediction models for bus delay over all intervals between pairs of adjacent bus stops. To build the models, we use one month of bus probe data, which includes more than 80 routes, and apply several machine learning models: linear regression (LR), artificial neural network (ANN), support vector regression (SVR), random forest (RF), and gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT). Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the GBDT-based prediction model and the effects of considering travel time over prior intervals.

This paper addresses the adaptive neural fault-tolerant control (FTC) problem for a class of stochastic switched nonstrict-feedback nonlinear systems, which have actuator faults that incorporate loss of effectiveness, stuck, and outage. Based on the character of the Gaussian function, the problem of nonstrict-feedback form is solved well. In the process of designing the controller, neural networks (NNs) are utilized to estimate the unknown functions. The problem of actuator faults is handled by designing the FTC method that is obtained by introducing a smooth function and backstepping technique. Then, the control effect satisfies that all the signals in the resulting closed-loop system are bounded and the tracking error converges to a small neighborhood around the origin. To illustrate the high efficiency of the proposed control method, a vivid simulation example is given in the end.

In a braking environment, a pilot's head can collide with the head-up display (HUD), potentially causing injury due to the pilot's forward-leaning inertia. To address this safety concern, a test component was designed to investigate the influence of preload on head injury during such collisions. The motion characteristics of the pilot were analyzed, and a head injury criteria tester was established. Hydraulic ejection was employed to simulate the high-speed and short-time characteristics of the head impact, overcoming traditional limitations such as space and non-reusability. Computational fluid dynamics and kinematic models were used to simulate the acceleration process, and AMESIM simulation was utilized to study the system parameters that affect velocity, angle, and acceleration during collision, optimizing the system and confirmed through experimental studies. The ultimate goal was to achieve a linear velocity of 11 m/s when the test component rotates at a certain angle. This research can be useful in designing a component HIC tester and optimizing fluid flow dynamic characteristics.

Discovering insights about Virtual Network Function (VNFs) resource demand characteristics will enable cloud vendors to optimize their underlying Network Function Virtualization (NFV) system orchestration and dramatically mitigate CapEx and OpEx spendings. However, analyzing large-scale NFV systems, especially in mobile network environments, is a challenging task and requires tailor-made approaches for each particular application. In this demo, we showcase NFV-Inspector, an open source and extensible VNF analysis platform that is capable of systematically benchmark and profile NFV deployments. Based on its pluggable framework, NFV-Inspector classifies VNFs resource demand characteristics and correlate their Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) with system-level Quality of Service (QoS) measurements.

This paper addresses the issue of a PV array fed water pumping system being affected by power outages. To solve this problem, one potential solution is to use a utility grid as a backup source in case the PV array cannot meet the necessary power demand. To regulate the unidirectional power flow control, a current multiplier approach is implemented through a power factor improved boost converter. This system is cost-effective due to its utilization of fewer sensors. The proposed system ensures that the consumer receives the required quantity of water without being affected by varying durations or weather conditions. The system has undergone simulation and testing, demonstrating its reliability under different operating conditions.

This paper shows that with bandwidth and round-trip time statistics, data analytics can be used to classify three characteristic phenomena in wireless signal use: decreases in bandwidth due to signal over-saturation, signal attenuation due to increasing distance, and signal improvement due to decreasing distance. Using a K-Means algorithm, bandwidth and round-trip time trends were clustered correctly by signal loss type with a 99.98% accuracy rating with 10,000 validation samples.

Optimal transport is becoming increasingly important in image processing, particularly in applications such as medical imaging and scientific visualization. The theory of optimal transport provides a versatile tool for modeling problems related to image registration, allowing different optimization resources and matching models to be used effectively. In this paper, we present an automated framework for fundus image registration that combines optimal transport, image processing tools, and graph matching schemes in a concise and functional approach. Our method constructs representative graphs from ocular fundus images, embedding spatial and topological information from the eye's blood vessels. These graphs are used to establish a correspondence between the images using optimal transport, and geometric transformations are applied to achieve proper registration. Our approach is based upon the solid mathematical foundation of optimal transport and is robust when dealing with matching outliers. We demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of our framework through comprehensive qualitative and quantitative comparisons with state-of-the-art methods on several fundus image databases.

As a result of globalization and the massive expansion of cyber services, the number of crimes perpetrated at both the local and global levels is increasing. Law Enforcement Agencies and governments are aware of this growing threat and are searching for potential countermeasures that go beyond traditional solutions. While technological countermeasures are important, there is an increasingly urgent need to cultivate a Culture of Cyber Security. 

This paper proposes an innovative Cyber Range that can be integrated within the larger European Cyber Range Network. This solution provides tools to test the resilience of networks and systems by exposing them to realistic cyber threats posed by nation-states within a secure facility equipped with the latest tools, techniques and malware. This facilitates the testing of critical technologies that require enhanced agility, flexibility and scalability, while strengthening the stability, security and performance of cyberinfrastructures and IT systems used by government and private organizations. 

The platform described in this document makes it easy to create virtual environments used for cyberwarfare training and cyber technology development. The solution will feature typical simulator's features, but with extensive real-world case studies to create a knowledge base of cyber threats and extended effects, as well as identifying mitigations and counteractions. A key feature of this platform is its ability to identify zero-day vulnerabilities in order to reduce or eliminate the Window of Vulnerability (WoV), as well as identifying main attack vectors.

The main outcomes of this innovative Cyber Range include improved situational awareness of cyber warfare scenarios, rapid identification of zero-day vulnerabilities, an environment for the development of countermeasures, and a training environment for practitioners.

Revised: 

Industrial control systems (ICS) are critical infrastructures that manage supervisory control, data acquisition, and industrial automation. They are made up of complex, component-based architectures and are influenced by multiple hardware, software, and human factors in real-time. Despite the importance of security concerns in ICS, a comprehensive study examining common security architectural weaknesses in the domain has not been conducted. 

As a result, this study presents the first detailed analysis of 988 vulnerability advisory reports developed by 277 vendors, aiming to measure the impact of known vulnerabilities on ICS components and security tactics. The findings of the study indicate that Human-Machine Interfaces, SCADA configurations, and PLCs are the most affected components, and 62.86% of vulnerability disclosures in ICS had an architectural root cause. 

Furthermore, the most common architectural weaknesses identified include “Improper Input Validation”, followed by “Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation” and “Improper Authentication”. Moreover, the vulnerabilities related to security tactics, such as “Validate Inputs,” “Authenticate Actors,” and “Authorize Actors,” were also common. 

In conclusion, the paper highlights the importance of addressing architectural security weaknesses in ICS to ensure the protection of critical infrastructure against potential attacks.

Aiming at the problem of automatic image annotation of Chinese ancient pottery figurines, this paper proposes a novel automatic annotation method based on Pottery Figurine Classification Ontology (PFCO), in which we use the Jseg algorithm to segment the pottery figurine images into regions, and adopt the multi-SVM to establish the relationship between low-level features and PFCO attribute concepts, finally implement inference rules of semantic concepts of the PFCO to capture the high-level semantic concepts of pottery figurines. Experimental results on cultural relic images and ECCV datasets demonstrate the utility and efficiency of the proposed approach as compared to the state-of-the-art algorithms.

In this study, two V-band direct down-conversion receivers were designed, fabricated, and tested based on the multi-port concept. The first receiver used a Miniature Hybrid Microwave Integrated Circuit (MHMIC) process on a thin film ceramic substrate, while the second receiver used rectangular waveguide (WR12) technology on a brass block with high precision machining. Both structures were characterized through an experimental setup, and their performance was evaluated in terms of Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) for various M-ary PSK modulated signals.

The fabricated MHMIC prototype demonstrated superior performance with an EVM that did not exceed 5.7% for all demodulation schemes. However, this was achieved despite the complexity involved in the integration process and high sensitivity to fabrication errors. 

In conclusion, this study successfully designed and tested two V-band direct down-conversion receivers and compared their performance when using different fabrication technologies. The results highlight the advantages and disadvantages of each fabrication process, and emphasize the importance of careful design and evaluation in order to achieve optimal performance.

Ensuring the safe and stable operation of the power grid relies heavily on the reliable operation of relay protection equipment and its secondary circuit. Improving the operation and maintenance efficiency of this equipment is therefore crucial. This paper presents the design of a relay protection intelligent mobile operation and maintenance management system based on power wireless virtual private network (VPN). The system architecture and communication network deployment mode are discussed in detail. 

Furthermore, the paper covers information synchronization methods between the system and relay protection statistical analysis and operation management modules, the condition-based maintenance assistant decision-making module, and other system data modules. By enabling the collection, collation, interaction, and sharing of intelligent information in substations, the system achieves mobile, paperless, and standardized management and control of equipment information. This improves the convenience and efficiency of on-site operation and maintenance work, as well as management level, ultimately ensuring the safety and stable operation of the power grid. 

In practice, the system has been successfully applied in substation operations and has yielded positive results.

Location-based services in vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) have to protect user privacy and address the challenge due to the disclosure of the vehicle movement trajectory. In this paper, we propose an reinforcement learning (RL) based differential privacy mechanism that randomizes the released vehicle locations to protect the semantic trajectory of the vehicle and uses RL to select the obfuscation policy. Based on the semantic location of the vehicle and the attack history, this scheme enables a vehicle to optimize the obfuscation policy in terms of the privacy gain and the quality of service loss without being aware of the current attack model in a dynamic privacy protection game. Simulation results show that this scheme can increase the privacy gain, decrease the quality of service loss, and thus improve the utility of the vehicle in comparison with a benchmark scheme.

With the tremendous revival of artificial intelligence, predictive maintenance (PdM) based on data-driven methods has become the most effective solution to address smart manufacturing and industrial big data, especially for performing health perception (e.g., fault diagnosis and remaining life assessment). Moreover, because the existing PdM research is still in primary experimental stage, most works are conducted utilizing several open-datasets, and the combination with specific applications such as rotating machinery is especially rare. Hence, in this paper, we focus on data-driven methods for PdM, present a comprehensive survey on its applications, and attempt to provide graduate students, companies, and institutions with the preliminary understanding of the existing works recently published. Specifically, we first briefly introduce the PdM approach, illustrate our PdM scheme for automatic washing equipment, and demonstrate the challenges encountered when we conduct a PdM research. Second, we classify the specific industrial applications based on six algorithms of machine learning and deep learning (DL), and compare five performance metrics for each classification. Furthermore, the accuracy (a metric to evaluate the algorithm performance) of these PdM applications is analyzed in detail. There are some important conclusions: 1) the data used in the summarized literature are mostly from public datasets, such as case western reserve university (CWRU)/intelligent maintenance systems (IMS); and 2) in recent years, researchers seem to focus more on DL algorithms for PdM research. Finally, we summarize the common features regarding our surveyed PdM applications and discuss several potential directions.

In many applications the process of generating label information is expensive and time consuming. We present a new method that combines active and semi-supervised deep learning to achieve high generalization performance from a deep convolutional neural network with as few known labels as possible. In a setting where a small amount of labeled data as well as a large amount of unlabeled data is available, our method first learns the labeled data set. This initialization is followed by an expectation maximization algorithm, where further training reduces classification entropy on the unlabeled data by targeting a low entropy fit which is consistent with the labeled data. In addition the algorithm asks at a specified frequency an oracle for labels of data with entropy above a certain entropy quantile. Using this active learning component we obtain an agile labeling process that achieves high accuracy, but requires only a small amount of known labels. For the MNIST dataset we report an error rate of 2.06% using only 300 labels and 1.06% for 1,000 labels. These results are obtained without employing any special network architecture or data augmentation.

Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation is an essential area of research in data mining, and it has gained significant importance with the rise of location-based social networks (LBSNs). However, most existing POI recommendation models only consider explicit social relationships within the geographic space, ignoring the implicit relationships among users in a given area that have a substantial impact on user behaviors. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach, the Deep Potential Geo-Social Relationship mining model for POI Recommendation (DPGSR-PR).

Our proposed model utilizes kernel density estimation to personalize geographical features and determine user check-in behaviors and choices in specific domains. Furthermore, we incorporate user preferences and personalized geo-social influence into a holistic geo-social recommendation framework. Our model specifically incorporates deep potential geo-social relationships, including explicit-implicit user geo-social relationships between users (EIU-GSR) and implicit common check-in POI-based geo-social relationships (ICP-GSR). We employ kernel density estimation and a two-hop random walk approach to mine the EIU-GSR, while the ICP-GSR is discovered by determining and considering the Jaccard similarity coefficient and kernel density estimation.

Our approach uses the combined impact of both EIU-GSR and ICP-GSR as regularization terms to obtain a unique recommendation model utilizing matrix factorization. We tested the proposed DPGSR-PR approach on two datasets, demonstrating that it outperforms other well-established models in terms of recommendation accuracy. Overall, our deep potential geo-social relationship mining model provides a more holistic view of user behavior and preferences, leading to better POI recommendations in LBSNs.

In the service industry, human resources and physical resources are considered as the most crucial service resources. The language training services provided for children under the e-commerce age are intangible, interactive, and produced and consumed simultaneously. The service personnel and venues bring about a unique blend of educational and learning activities, thereby requiring more complex quality characteristics that shape the quality of the language training services for children.

The combination of growing competition and inexpensive connectivity has made the Internet of things (IoT) an ongoing topic in manufacturing. Sensors, devices, and machines all connected via the Internet are the “things” in IoT. The flood of IoT data can provide the information needed to stay competitive, by applying analytics and artificial intelligence—with the goal to improve operations’ efficiency, safety, and flexibility.

Cloud computing is an innovative technology that has numerous applications in today's era. When combined with distributed computing and parallel processing, its benefits can be enhanced significantly. This combination allows us to access massive computing power from light processing devices such as personal computers, laptops, and smartphones remotely. In this paper, we propose a system design for a platform that utilizes distributed parallel processing via distributed cloud computing to address specific and complex client problems that require exceptional processing power and minimal time. Our design comprises several servers located in different geographical locations to process clients' tasks through parallel processing operations based on cloud computing principles. Some of the servers will be located in Iraq, including Duhok Polytechnic University (DPU) and Slaimani Polytechnic University (SPU), while others will be placed in Firat University in Turkey. The system is automated, and the servers can self-register on a central server that acts as an intermediary between the servers and clients. Clients can benefit from the processing power provided by the registered servers, specify tasks for processing, and the number of servers required to participate in data processing. Finally, clients receive a detailed report about the time and CPU usage of the servers involved in the process. In conclusion, this proposed system design is a promising solution for clients who need massive computing power to solve complex and specific problems at a minimal time.

The purpose of this paper is a rigorous accuracy analysis of the parameters affecting the solution convergence of the method of auxiliary sources (MAS). This study concerns the electromagnetic scattering of a transverse wave by a perfectly conducting, infinite, cylinder with an arbitrary shape. It is shown that convergence of the MAS depends on the relation between the number of auxiliary sources and their position in the cylinder. It is demonstrated that it is possible to study the convergence of the MAS by using the characteristics of the obtained MAS matrix. The essential characteristic is the matrix condition number defining the linear system. The effect of the variation of the auxiliary distance and the position of auxiliary sources on the convergence of the solutions also demonstrated. For this, many plots are represented and discussed in this paper.

In this paper, a cooperative distributed optimization method via sliding mode extremum seeking (ES) control for a class of large-scale interconnected systems is presented. In this approach, a consensus algorithm is exploited to communicate the value of the global cost function to the ES controllers. Then, each sliding mode ES controller is designed such that a multivariable cost function is optimized in a cooperative fashion. The stability and convergence conditions for the ES controllers are determined and sufficient conditions for the distributed scheme to converge to the vicinity of the optimal points are driven. The application of the proposed scheme to a real-world example is investigated and simulations are provided to illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate their potential use.

The objective of person reidentification (Re-ID) is to recognize a specific pedestrian from a network of surveillance cameras that do not overlap. The majority of existing methods follow the supervised learning paradigm, which requires pairwise labeled training data for each pair of cameras. However, this approach is not scalable to real-world scenarios where there is an abundance of unlabeled data. In order to address this limitation, we propose an unsupervised Re-ID model that combines multi-feature fusion with adaptive graph learning. This model ensures a comprehensive evaluation of the consistent graph structure of pedestrians, utilizing special information of feature descriptors. To achieve this, we integrate multi-feature dictionary learning and adaptive multi-feature graph learning into a single model so that the dictionaries are discriminative and the subsequent graph structure learning is accurate. To solve the final optimization objective, we utilize an alternating optimization algorithm that has been proven to converge in practice. Our proposed approach outperforms existing methods on four benchmark datasets, demonstrating its superior effectiveness.

This paper provides an overview of the Information Communication Technology (ICT) training initiatives underway in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. ICT is transformative, changing the way people communicate, learn and conduct business. This includes the availability of mobile phones and the internet, even in some of the most remote and underdeveloped regions. However, the ubiquitous nature of these tools also presents risks, especially with unethical use by some users. Therefore, raising awareness of both the opportunities and dangers of using ICTs is essential.

The paper focuses on the Eastern Cape e-Skills CoLab (EC e-Skills CoLab) and its efforts to provide training aligned to the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) across the province. The CoLab has conducted various training and awareness initiatives, including Computer Literacy, Cybersecurity, Internet of Things (IoT) and Robotics. The training targets a range of users, including learners, teachers, sector users, ICT practitioners and e-Leaders with tailored training models.

For instance, learners receive workshops on both Cyber Awareness and Robotics, whereas ICT practitioners are offered training on Cyber Security and IoT. The paper aims to present and share the experiences of the EC e-Skills CoLab on the range of ICT training initiatives it has conducted. By doing so, it hopes to provide insights into the path the province is taking to prepare people for the ever-changing digital landscape.

5G, the upcoming wireless technology, is set to be launched in 2020. However, the increased exposure to electromagnetic radiations emitted by mobile phones has raised concerns about the potential health effects from exposure to Radio Frequency (RF) and Millimeter (mm) wave radiations on human brain tissue. Hence, this paper aims to investigate the effects of 5G radiations for different frequency candidates on the human brain through the use of Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software. We conducted simulations on Specific Anthropomorphic Mannequin (SAM), a model designed according to various international standards, to represent the average material properties of the head. The calculations obtained by comparing the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) of the human brain with the safety limit of exposure to high frequency radiations set by different international standards have shown that the resulting exposure of 5G radiations is safe.

This work shows the design, development and evaluation of an automatic object recognition system, which implements a classification methodology that makes it possible to recognize objects from different contexts and environments. The evaluated categories are input as digital images by users through a mobile application. This system is also able to learn new categories and enhance its performance according with the user's feedback. The proposed architecture achieved an initial generalization error of 20% on the first 50 categories and we showed that this error decreased after a few days of interaction with users. Finally, the system learned three completely new categories with images collected through the mobile app.

The diffusion of new digital technologies renders digital transformation relevant to nearly every economic activity sector, including in the agriculture sector. Farming and how farmers work is changing, the use of Information and Communications Technology (ICT) together with the increased use of the Internet of Things (IoT) is developing a concept that is called Smart Farming. Smart Farming benefits are tremendous, smart data can be used for seed traits and to treat soil conditions, the use of new technologies can offer unprecedented conveniences and improve the management and quality of agriculture farming. The use of new information systems and services will be more and more used to sustain and improve operations, competitiveness, and profitability in the agriculture sector. However, the massive use of technology comes with inherent security risks and vulnerabilities, and the sector finds itself targeted as never before. In this paper, using an empirical methodology, are highlighted some reflections regarding the security challenges that Smart Farming systems face.

Current anomaly detection systems (ADSs) apply statistical and machine learning algorithms to discover zero-day attacks, but such algorithms are vulnerable to advanced persistent threat actors. In this paper, we propose an adversarial statistical learning mechanism for anomaly detection, outlier Dirichlet mixture-based ADS (ODM-ADS), which has three new capabilities. First, it can self-adapt against data poisoning attacks that inject malicious instances in the training phase for disrupting the learning process. Second, it establishes a statistical legitimate profile and considers variations from the baseline of the profile as anomalies using a proposed outlier function. Third, to deal with dynamic and large-scale networks such as Internet of Things and cloud and fog computing, we suggest a framework for deploying the mechanism as Software as a Service in the fog nodes. The fog enables the proposed mechanism to concurrently process streaming data at the edge of the network. The ODM-ADS mechanism is evaluated using both NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15 datasets, whose findings indicate that ODM-ADS outperforms seven other peer algorithms in terms of accuracy, detection rates, false positive rates, and computational time.

The finger knuckle print (FKP) based personal identification has achieved much interest. One of the disadvantages of the generally used Gabor filter based Competitive Coding method is that it is sensitive to variations caused in image acquisition stage. To handle this problem, researchers have proposed a reconstruction based scheme in original image pixel domain. However, the reconstruction in original image domain may lose much valuable directional information extracted by Gabor filters with different orientations. Compared with the previous methods, in this paper, we propose to perform reconstruction in Gabor filter response domain. For each orientation, we reconstruct the Gabor response of a query image using the responses in the template database. Thus, the directional information contained in the image is fully utilized. Then, we binarize each reconstructed responses for feature coding and matching with the constructed "mask", which considers not only the reconstructive error but also the Gabor response in a specific location. The mask can characterize the significance of a specific location along a specific orientation. Finally, by using a score level adaptive binary fusion rule, the matching distances before and after reconstruction are adaptively fused. The experimental results conducted on the benchmark PolyU FKP database show the performance advantage of the presented method.

Voice assistants are becoming increasingly popular in home healthcare, as they enhance the quality of patient care by increasing efficiency and providing a novel experience through the provision of an extensive range of tools and capabilities. Patients can conveniently access medical information, analyze and monitor their health issues, as well as communicate with healthcare providers through the utilization of various useful applications and services, which is particularly beneficial to elderly patients. This paper highlights the voice and web services, which cater to the needs of patients, developed for Amazon's Alexa and Google Assistant, and delineates the advantages of this technology, which patients can utilize from the comfort of their homes.

Natural Language processing is a growing field. Although it is difficult to create a natural language system that can robustly react to and handle every situation, it is quite possible to design the system to react to specific instructions or scenario. The contributions of this work are (1) to design a set of instruction types that can allow for conditional statements within natural language instructions, (2) to create a modular system using Robot Operating System (ROS) in order to allow for more robust communication and integration, and (3) to allow for an interconnection between the written text and derived instructions that will make the sentence construction more seamless and natural for the user. As the results will show, this system can be run on a diverse set of sentence structures, allowing for robust paragraphs. This system must also then be carefully set to fit the exact parameters that the user is looking for, trying to strike the balance between how much the user needs to learn and how accurate to the instruction the system needs to run.

Trust is a crucial yet often overlooked aspect of Cloud Manufacturing. In order to address this gap in research, this paper employs the noncommittal phase of the grounded theory method to explore the various facets of trust in Cloud Manufacturing. Through a comprehensive literature review, the authors were able to define the problem domain and identify key areas for future research. As a result, this approach can serve as both a snapshot and a blueprint for future studies on trust in Cloud Manufacturing. By building upon the insights gained from this paper, researchers can advance towards a more integrative phase in grounded theory, thus building a more complete understanding of trust within the context of Cloud Manufacturing.

In the near future, most of the industrial robots will serve as assistants involved in targeted complex manufacturing tasks which are difficult to be automated. To achieve this, it is crucial to enhance the ability of manipulators to pick and place objects from the assembly line. Reorienting and picking up pieces for assembly are difficult to be done by manipulators since, for different pieces, shapes and physical properties vary. In this work, we use Convolutional Neural Networks for recognizing a selected production piece on a cluster. Once the selected piece has been recognized, a grasping algorithm estimates the best gripper configuration so that the robot is able to pick the piece up. We tested our algorithm on grasping experiments with an ABB robot and using a common webcam as image input. We found that our implementations perform well and the robot was able to pick up a variety of objects.

This work deals with the implementation of energy-efficient monocular depth estimation using a low-cost CPU for low-power embedded systems. It first describes the PyD-Net depth estimation network, which consists of a lightweight CNN able to approach state-of-the-art accuracy with ultra-low resource usage. Then it proposes an accuracy-driven complexity reduction strategy based on a hardware-friendly fixed-point quantization. Finally, it introduces the low-level optimization enabling effective use of integer neural kernels. The objective is threefold: (i) prove the efficiency of the new quantization flow on a depth estimation network, that is, the capability to retaining the accuracy reached by floating-point arithmetic using 16- and 8-bit integers, (ii) demonstrate the portability of the quantized model into a general-purpose 32-bit RISC architecture of the ARM Cortex family, (iii) quantify the accuracy-energy tradeoff of unsupervised monocular estimation to establish its use in the embedded domain. The experiments have been run on a Raspberry PI board powered by a Broadcom BCM2837 chipset. A parametric analysis conducted over the KITTI date-set shows marginal accuracy loss with 16-bit (8-bit) integers and energy savings up to 6.55× (9.23×) w.r.t. floating-point. Compared to high-end CPU and GPU the proposed solution improves scalability.

Automatic detection of vowels is a challenging yet significant problem in speech analysis. To accurately mark vowels and analyze speech signal, it is essential to identify both vowel onset points (VOPs) and vowel offset points (VEPs). However, the transition in signal magnitude at VEPs is distinct from that at VOPs, making it difficult for existing front-end features to detect VEPs. Moreover, the performance of these features diminishes in noisy speech signals. 

To address these challenges, a robust frontend speech parametrization approach is proposed in this work. This approach assigns weight values to each sample point by computing the similarity present in samples belonging to two different frames within a search neighborhood. Weight values (WVs) are computed from non-local similarity (NLS). When the frames under consideration are similar, WVs computed from NLS are significantly less as compared to dissimilar ones. 

Since vowels are longer regions and exhibit periodicity, there is more similarity in frames belonging to these regions. Conversely, frames belonging to non-vowel regions and noises are dissimilar. The proposed method integrates WVs computed from NLS as a feature for detecting VEPs in a given speech signal. 

The results indicate that the proposed approach outperforms the deep neural network - hidden Markov model based classifier under both clean and noisy test conditions, even after the inclusion of a speech enhancement module recently proposed. Therefore, the proposed approach is effective in enhancing discrimination at VEPs and accurately detecting vowels in speech signals.

The three phase separator plays a crucial role in oil and gas production facilities, as it separates the gas, water and condensate from the raw gas generated from gas wells. To optimize the process and design controls, a dynamic model of the three phase separator is deemed essential. Since creating a first principles model of the system is an intricate process, a data-based model known as the Wavelet Network based Nonlinear AutoRegressive eXogenous model (WN-NARX) has been utilized to capture the process dynamics. However, the over-parameterization of the identification problem due to redundant terms in the WN-NARX expansion poses a significant challenge. To address this issue, a sparsity constraint on the parameter vector is considered, and sparse estimation algorithms such as Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) and Least Angle Regression (LAR) are employed to identify the WA-NARX model. The efficacy of these sparse estimation methods has been demonstrated through their application in the identification of an industrial three phase separator process.

An intelligent tutoring system (ITS) is designed to provide and simulate the behavior of the existing educational process. Interactive learning environments deploy simple to complex tools for providing mindful feedback to students. The effect is measured and reflected on learners' academic performance and achievement of subsequent learning outcomes. The study examines contemporary research on instructional designing, feedback strategies and intelligent tutoring systems to understand effect of intelligent tutoring in the form of "informed feedback" on learners reported satisfaction with an interactive learning environment. The study is based on primary data, whereby intervention of intelligent tutoring system (ITS) is included by simulating human-tutors, acting as intelligent-tutors and providing informed feedback as per Interactive Tutoring Feedback Model factors; namely i) Requirement Engineering, ii) Characterization of learners on the basis of meta-cognition and motivation, and iii) Characterization of informed feedback for mindful acceptance. The study was able to conclude that despite being many difficulties in contextual interpretation, intelligent tutoring can bring about positive change in satisfaction score of learners in an interactive learning environment.

This live demonstration is designed to showcase the capabilities of a two-layer neural network when applied to predictive maintenance. The first layer of the network encodes relevant features based on prior knowledge, while the second layer is trained in real-time to detect anomalies. The entire system is implemented on an FPGA, which captures data from sensors attached to a motor, thereby allowing the detection of faults in real-time. Faults can also be artificially triggered to demonstrate the effectiveness of anomaly detection.

Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) technology has shown great potential for communication systems. In this study, we aimed to investigate the impact of unknown noise variance on the energy detection based spectrum sensing scheme for OFDM cognitive radios over multipath fading channels.

To study the effects of unknown parameters on the energy detector, we proposed a new maximum-likelihood estimation of noise and signal powers using the cyclic prefix of OFDM. The mean values and Cramer-Rao lower bounds of the estimation were obtained. The performances of the energy detector for both hypotheses, i.e., false-alarm rate and detection probability, under the influence of unknown noise variance were validated through both simulation and analytical results.

We also conducted an assessment on the required number of samples for the proposed energy detector, which showed that an amount of 40-50% samples can be saved compared to the conventional energy detector. These findings highlight the potential benefits and advantages of the proposed energy detector in cognitive radios over multipath fading channels.

In summary, this study provides insight into the impacts of unknown noise variance on the energy detection based spectrum sensing scheme for OFDM cognitive radios over multipath fading channels. Our proposed approach can effectively estimate noise and signal powers, which leads to improved performance and reduced sample requirements for energy detection.

Energy efficiency is a crucial aspect of modern data-communication systems, and recently, a lot of work has been done on analyzing system energy consumption. However, most of this work has focused only on communication and computation costs, without taking into account data caching costs, which is a significant problem given the growing interest in cache networks. In this paper, we address the issue of energy consumption in communication, computation, and caching (C3) while ensuring a quality-of-information guarantee in a communication network. Our objective is to identify the optimal data compression rates and cache placement over the network that can minimize the overall energy consumption while maintaining a quality-of-information guarantee. We formulate the problem as a mixed integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem with nonconvex functions, which is generally non-deterministic polynomial-time hard (NP-hard). To address this issue, we propose a variant of the spatial branch-and-bound algorithm (V-SBB) that can provide an $\epsilon$-global optimal solution to the problem. Our numerical experiments showed that the C3 optimization framework improves energy efficiency by up to 88% compared to any optimization that only considers either communication and caching or communication and computation. Furthermore, our V-SBB technique provides comparatively better solutions than some other MINLP solvers but at the cost of additional computation time.

Learning to predict human body motion has become an important area of research in both computer vision and artificial intelligence. This paper presents a study on predicting human body motion from video sequences by proposing a human body motion prediction network that integrates advanced 2D feature extraction and video sequence prediction. Our network leverages temporal characteristics extracted from video sequences to make predictions about human motion. We trained our network using video-based human pose datasets, and were able to demonstrate its excellent performance through both quantitative and qualitative results. Our experimental findings definitively confirm the feasibility of our method.

Finding the rising stars is an interesting problem and has been recently studied in various domains including academic networks. This study formulates the problem of rising stars prediction as a machine learning task. Classification models are applied and features are classified as co-authors, author, and venues. The impact of the categorization of these features is empirically analyzed. The experimentation is performed on data of Pakistani researchers retrieved from Web of Sciences ranging from 2008 to 2014. After collection of the dataset, feature sets are calculated and classification techniques are applied. The researchers predicted by the proposed method are compared with top researchers of Pakistan in 2016 and 2017. The proposed technique solves the problem of finding rising star researcher of Pakistan in the field of computer sciences based on authors' contribution, mutual influence, and venue citations scores.

Network motifs are a valuable tool for understanding the structural design principles of complex networks across various disciplines. However, the measures for network motifs have received relatively little attention in the literature. To address this gap, this paper reviews the measures for network motifs, categorizing them into structural measures and statistical measures. The paper also summarizes the application scenarios for each measure and highlights the distinctions between measures in similar scenarios. Finally, the challenges for using these measures and potential future directions in this field are discussed. Overall, this survey aims to provide insight into the theory and practice of complex networks through an overview of motif measures.

Plants show different beauty since the leaves and structures are in a variety of colors, shapes, sizes and texture in our vision. Thus, noise and edge bonding in plant modeling reconstruction are highly challenging. In order to separate the adhesive and gain ideal point cloud, we present a method of limited detail multi-density point reconstruction. The core of proposed method is a point-to-surface approach, which constantly refines the density of points so as to generate the fuzzy surface. Comparing with traditional mesh reconstruction, our method can solve the problem of adhesion between the branches and leaves. Results show that the limited detail multi-density point reconstruction is feasible, and as well as good effect and fast speed.

Multi-hop broadcast communication is one of the main schemes for supporting message dissemination in vehicular ad hoc networks. In this paper, we propose an efficient receiver-oriented broadcast scheme in which the receiving vehicles' probability of forwarding is modeled by the symmetric volunteer's dilemma game. Based on this game, the vehicles that receive the broadcast message are players. At least one of the players should pay a cost and be a volunteer to rebroadcast the message, and then all will benefit from this volunteering. Utilizing fuzzy logic techniques and considering information from the network layer about local density and probability of transmission, the contention window size at the MAC layer will be adjusted. We develop ns-3 simulations to evaluate the performance of the proposed volunteer's dilemma inspired broadcast (VDIB) scheme in terms of reachability, number of rebroadcasts per covered vehicle, number of bytes sent per covered vehicle, and per-hop delay. VDIB performance is compared with that of the distance-to-mean broadcast method, broadcast component of contention-based forwarding, distribution-adaptive distance with channel quality, statistical location assisted broadcast, fuzzy logic-based broadcast, bandwidth efficient fuzzy logic assisted broadcast, and intelligent hybrid adaptive broadcast protocols in both highway and urban environments.

Finding a qualitative model to study the thermo-mechanical effects inside the Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor power Integrated Circuits (MOS power IC's) is needed even from the design stage of such devices. The high number of geometry details contained by these devices, especially at the level of the metallization system, rise difficulties in the Finite Element Method (FEM) analyze, thus some simplifications are needed. In this paper a simple method of geometry details reduction is proposed, in order to eliminate some geometrical details such as vias between two different metal layers. While the geometry details are simplified, the thermo-mechanical behavior is assessed on a simple Double-Diffused MOS (DMOS) substructure with an open source software (Code_Aster) based on FEM. In order to understand the influence of vias at the metallization level, temperature and strain distributions are compared for three different cases with vias, no-vias and equivalent materials properties block respectively. The no vias model approach capture with less computational effort and good accuracy the thermal induced metal deformation.

Compared with the pattern recognition of discrete human motions, the continuous human motion estimation is more significant for the motion control of wearable power-assisted robots. In previous studies, researchers estimated human motion from the surface electromyography (sEMG) signal based on the Hill-type muscle model or using the traditional machine learning algorithms with the hand-crafted features. However, these methods generally require the domain knowledge about the muscle dynamics or complicated signal processing. In this study, 3-channel time series mechanomyography (MMG) signals were detected on clothes from the thigh muscles, and a CNN-SVM combined regression model was proposed to estimate the knee angle under different motion velocities. The convolutional neural network (CNN) model was used to automatically extract the features from the MMG signals, and the support vector machine (SVM) regression was used to process the features for angle estimation. The results showed that the CNN-SVM combined regression model obviously improved the estimation performances and avoided using the muscle model or hand-crafted features. The methods used in this paper would promote the development of motion control system for wearable power-assisted robots, and could be further extended to the fields of rehabilitation training, medical diagnosis, etc.

The present study aims to use the smart home application practically to enhancing control management of the home, security, increase comfortably, and decrease energy consumption using biometric technique and cloud services. At the first stage, the proposed system works to identify member identification by using the face recognition method as a tool to enhance the home security, and home control management. The recognition procedure captures a member face image in a controlled environment by using a digital camera as a test image. The AdaBoost technique is utilized to detect and extract a member's faces for the train, and test member images. DWT with PCA methods have used to extract image features and dimension reduction. At the classified procedure, Euclidean distance method has been used for the matching process to verify home member's identification index. As well as, a special MATLAB procedure has been used to transmit the member's index to the cloud server. The cloud server analyses the received member identification in order to retrieve the verified member's profile, which contains specified appliances for each individual member. The home appliances are controlled by the highest priority member who has been registered in real time at home by the recognition stage. Then, the cloud server transmits a home member's privilege to the microcontroller through a Wi-Fi network submitting the required actions. The designed proposed smart home system provides a secure, energy reduced, and cost- effective design that automatically responds to the home member's needs.

This paper reports on a high-resolution channel measurement campaign conducted at 67 GHz in a street canyon in Tokyo, Japan. The study focuses on an extended evaluation method that includes map-based side information, which not only validates the accuracy of the path estimation but also enables main sources of interaction to be identified, and differentiation between first and higher order interactions. 

Overall, the analysis provided a comprehensive understanding of the channel characteristics within a street canyon environment at 67 GHz, which is vital for the development of advanced wireless communication systems.

In this paper, an optimization method, Golden Ratio Algorithm (GRA), is introduced for biometric fusion at score level. Some experiments have been conducted, and the results show that the proposed method can optimally balance the contributions of different modalities for biometric person recognition. And the test results have also indicated that an Audio-Visual (AV) bimodal biometric system normally outperforms the respective single modality systems when biometric fusion is done properly. Furthermore, the experiments demonstrate that the performance of a biometric system relies on the accurate extraction of features from original biometric sources.

Load Monitoring (LM) is a fundamental step to implement effective energy management schemes. LM includes Intrusive LM (ILM) and Non-Intrusive LM (NILM). Compared with intrusive approaches, non-intrusive approaches enjoy low cost, easy installation, and promising scalable commercialization potentials. This paper provides a survey of effective NILM system framework and advanced load disaggregation algorithms, reviews load signature models, presents existing datasets and performance metrics, summarizes commercial applications such as demand response, highlights the challenges, and points out future research directions.

This paper presents a novel nonlinear dictionary learning (DL) model that addresses the energy disaggregation (ED) problem. The ED problem aims to decompose the electricity signal of a home into its operating devices. To accomplish this, the paper proposes a new temporal DL problem, where a set of dictionary atoms is learned to capture the most representative temporal features of electricity signals. The sparse codes associated with these atoms depict the contribution of each device in total electricity consumption. 

To create powerful atoms, the paper proposes a deep temporal DL (DTDL) model that computes complex nonlinear dictionaries in the latent space of a long short-term memory autoencoder (LSTM-AE). The LSTM-AE captures the deep temporal manifold of electricity signals, while the DTDL model identifies the most representative atoms within this manifold. To optimize the dictionary and deep temporal manifold simultaneously, the paper proposes a new optimization algorithm that alternates between finding the optimal LSTM-AE and the optimal dictionary.

The authors highlight that the DTDL is the only DL model that understands the deep temporal structures of the data. Results based on the Reference ED Data Set show an outstanding performance compared to recent state-of-the-art algorithms. Precision, recall, accuracy and F-score were all improved when using the DTDL model.

In this study, we have developed a new friction variable surface to facilitate the manipulation of objects by soft robotic hands. These hands possess high elasticity, which enables them to grasp various objects with stability due to their large frictional force. However, this also creates difficulties in manipulating objects due to the inhibition caused by the large contact area and frictional force. To overcome this challenge, we have created a novel surface called Contact Area Variable Surface (CAVS), which can transition its contact area through structural deformation. This enables the surface to passively activate friction change, allowing for easy object manipulation by the soft robotic hands. Moreover, the CAVS maintains the soft surface of the hands, making them ideal for delicate object manipulation. Our experiments have shown the effectiveness of this mechanism, providing a new direction in the development of robotic manipulation technology.

Millimeter wave (mm-wave) communication with large-scale antenna array configuration is seen as the key enabler of the next generation communication systems. Accurate knowledge of the mm-wave propagation channels is fundamental and essential. In this contribution, a novel complexity-efficient high resolution parameter estimation (HRPE) algorithm is proposed for the mm-wave channel with large-scale uniform circular array (UCA) applied. The proposed algorithm is able to obtain the high-resolution estimation results of the spherical channel propagation parameters. The prior channel information in the delay domain, i.e., the delay trajectories of individual propagation paths observed across the array elements, is exploited, by combining the high-resolution estimation principle and the phase mode excitation technique. Fast initializations, effective interference cancellations, and reduced searching spaces achieved by the proposed schemes significantly decrease the algorithm complexity. Furthermore, the channel spatial non-stationarity in path gain across the array elements is considered for the first time in the literature for propagation parameter estimation, which is beneficial to obtain more realistic results as well as to decrease the complexity. A mm-wave measurement campaign at the frequency band of 28-30GHz using a large-scale UCA is exploited to demonstrate and validate the proposed HRPE algorithm.

The purpose of this paper is to showcase the parallel implementation of the Haralick feature extraction technique utilized in our texture image segmentation approach. This process involves using the CUDA environment on an NVIDIA GPU to compute the gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) and Haralick features for each pixel in the image simultaneously. The clustered approach is based on the training of a Kohonen map using parallel features extracted from each pixel in the image, followed by the extraction of modal regions from that map. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we conducted experiments comparing the performance of the parallel GPU implementation to that of the CPU-based sequential technique. Additionally, we compared our segmentation rate results to those obtained from the K-means method.

In this paper, we introduce our recent studies on human perception in audio event classification. In particular, the pre-trained model VGGish is used as feature extractor to process audio data, and DenseNet is trained by and used as feature extractor for our electroencephalography (EEG) data. The correlation between audio stimuli and EEG is learned in a shared space. In the experiments, we record brain activities (EEG signals) of several subjects while they are listening to music events of 8 audio categories selected from Google AudioSet. Our experimental results demonstrate that i) audio event classification can be improved by exploiting the power of human perception, and ii) the correlation between audio stimuli and EEG can be learned to complement audio event understanding.

Electronic Medical Records (EMRs) have become an essential tool in the healthcare industry, providing a digital format of the patient's health data. By eliminating the complexities of paper-based medical records, EMRs ensure accuracy and legibility of health data, leading to improved quality care. However, the vast amounts of EMRs generated can quickly overwhelm traditional medical systems, making it essential to outsource EMRs to cloud servers, which provide flexible and cost-effective data management.

Despite the benefits of cloud storage, outsourcing EMRs to a third-party server poses significant challenges to data integrity and confidentiality, making it critical to establish secure ways of storing EMRs in the cloud. In this paper, we present an efficient certificateless provable data possession (CL-PDP) scheme that eliminates the need for bilinear pairing in securing EMRs in the cloud medical server. We offer a formal security proof based on the random oracle model, demonstrating the robustness and security of our proposed scheme.

Our CL-PDP scheme is designed with the following properties in mind: unconditionally anonymous, privacy preservation, public verifiability, and reliability of the trusted third party. These features allow healthcare providers to maintain control over their patient's data while ensuring that the data stored in the cloud can be verified without revealing sensitive information to third parties.

A detailed performance analysis of our scheme with related schemes indicates that our proposal is efficient and practical. In summary, our proposed CL-PDP scheme provides an efficient and secure approach to store and manage EMRs in the cloud.

The modern digital society is characterized by the widespread use of internet communications in the everyday lives of all social groups. However, this has led to an increased level of information noise, posing a challenge for communication practitioners to overcome (Joseph Turow, Couldry, N.). To address this problem, experts have also reviewed the importance of communication hygiene. In order to formulate an effective communication strategy in the current communication pattern of digital society, case studies of big data and smart data are presented as valuable tools.

This paper presents the design and real-time application of an efficient and adaptive neural-fuzzy inference system for regulating the climate within a greenhouse. The neural-fuzzy inference system is a combination of artificial neural networks and fuzzy logic techniques. The control system presented in this paper significantly enhances the ability to track temperature and relative humidity references, which are crucial for optimal crop growth.

The training datasets for the adaptive neural-fuzzy inference system are extracted from a fuzzy logic controller model that was developed using MATLAB Simulink. Experimentally, the system has been verified for its robustness. This technique exhibits remarkable performance in terms of set-point tracking, response time, robustness to external parameters variation, non-linearity, and energy optimization.

In summary, the presented design and real-time application of an adaptive neural-fuzzy inference system for regulating greenhouse climate is a remarkable contribution to the field of agricultural engineering. The system's performance is superior to traditional control systems and ensures optimal crop growth.

One of the major limitations of brain computer interface (BCI) is its long calibration time. Due to between sessions/subjects nonstationarity, typically a big amount of training data needs to be collected at the beginning of each session in order to tune the parameters of the system for the target user. In this paper, a number of novel weighted multi-task transfer learning algorithms are proposed in the classification domain to reduce the calibration time without sacrificing the classification accuracy of the BCI system. The proposed algorithms use data from other subjects and combine them to estimate the classifier parameters for the target subject. This combination is done based on how similar the data from each subject is to the few trials available from the target subject. The proposed algorithms are evaluated using dataset 2a from BCI competition IV. According to the results, the proposed algorithms lead to reduce the calibration time by 75% and enhance the average classification accuracy at the same time.

The power communication network service plays an important role in the production and operation of the power system. Therefore, the power communication department needs to solve the problem that how to reduce the security risk of the bearer service and distribute the service path properly. However, most of the existing algorithms do not take the difference of service importance into account, thus resulting in unbalanced traffic channel segment distribution and increase of the overall network risk. In this paper, a risk balancing routing assignment mechanism based power communication network service importance (SIRBRM) is proposed. And the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is introduced and a model of risk balancing routing assignment problem is established. Then the routing decision based on the principle of maximum and minimum fairness constraint can choose the optimal route for the service. Finally, the simulation is carried out based on the power communication network topological data of a certain prefecture-level city. Simulation results show that compared with the other two methods, the SIRBRM can effectively reduce the link risk and the overall network risk, make the service distribution more uniform, and reduce the operational risk caused by excessive concentration of the service on some specific links. SIRBRM has broad application prospects in the existing routing optimization and future arrangements for new business methods.

Data mining technology is a revolutionary information processing technique that entails extracting valuable data models and regularities from massive datasets. By analyzing the data from e-commerce websites, data mining technology can be used to provide individually tailored services to different types of clients while simultaneously combining customer relationship management strategies. This approach can be used to establish customer feature models that reflect their personality traits, and a dynamic service mechanism for adaptive customer service. To accomplish this, clustering technology is applied to e-commerce websites. This application utilizes commercial databases to classify customers using clustering technology, which involves generating customer clustering vectors based on frequent item sets, and calculating dissimilarity matrices of customers.

The tremendous growth of interconnected things/devices in the whole world advances to the new paradigm, i.e., Internet of Things (IoT). The IoT use sensor-based embedded systems to interact with others, providing a wide range of applications and services to upper-level users. Undoubtedly, the data collected by the underlying IoTs are the basis of the upper-layer decision and the foundation for all the applications, which requires efficient energy protocols. Moreover, if the collected data are erroneous and untrustworthy, the data protection and application becomes an unrealistic goal, which further leads to unnecessary energy cost. However, the traditional methods cannot solve this problem efficiently and trustworthily. To achieve this goal, in this paper we design a novel energy-efficient and trustworthy protocol based on mobile fog computing. By establishing a trust model on fog elements to evaluate the sensor nodes, the mobile data collection path with the largest utility value is generated, which can avoid visiting unnecessary sensors and collecting untrustworthy data. Theoretical analysis and experimental results validate that our proposed architecture and method outperform traditional data collection methods in both energy and delay.

Currently, the planetary gear box health monitoring system has collected a huge amount of data, and the data needs to be quickly learned and real-time monitoring diagnostic requirements. The traditional fault diagnosis methods mostly need a complex signal processing process in advance and there are fewer layers, the feature extraction and classification effect are not ideal. In order to diagnose the planetary gearbox effectively, this paper presents a fault diagnosis method for planetary gearbox based on hierarchical extreme learning machine (H-ELM). This method analyses the time domain signal of fault vibration instead of the frequency domain signal, thus eliminates the time for complex signal processing to adaptively mine available fault characteristics and automatically identify machinery health conditions. The Stacked Denoising Auto-encoders (SDAE) and the Deep Belief Network (DBN) were used to test the diagnosis data of planetary gearbox, and make the comparison with hierarchical extreme learning machine methods. The experimental results show that the method has good effect and application value in the fault diagnosis of planetary gearbox.

A novel layer jamming variable stiffness technique for soft robotics is proposed in this paper, which we call electrostatic layer jamming (ELJ). The basic principle of the ELJ is using electrostatic attraction to squeeze material layers to generate friction and then engage jamming. Based on this technique, several specimens used in two common application scenarios including variable tensile stiffness and variable bending stiffness are fabricated, and their stiffness adjustment characteristics are investigated experimentally. Surprisingly, the test data are much larger than the theoretical prediction, which we think is because of the formation of local low air pressure regions between the contact surfaces. Also, the experimental results show that the ELJ technique possesses a large capability of stiffness changing and is space saving. The potential values of the ELJ have been shown by performing with a soft linear actuator for three representative practical applications in the soft robotic field. Finally, the existing problems and advantages of the ELJ technique are discussed, and we believe that this technique will inspire new ways and new opportunities for the soft robotic community.

A low-power and high-speed embedded classifier with a small footprint is essential for various real-time applications, including brain-machine interfaces and closed-loop neuromodulation for neurological conditions. While deep neural networks perform exceptionally well in large datasets with unstructured data such as images, they require significant computational effort during inference and can be challenging to train with limited data. Additionally, the computation-intensive nature of deep models can negatively impact the classification latency, making them less suitable for real-time closed-loop applications. 

Recently, decision tree ensembles have shown promising results in neural data classification tasks. Decision trees can process a limited number of features successively, resulting in lower computational and memory overhead. In this study, we compared the hardware complexity of DNNs and gradient boosted DTs for real-time electrophysiological data classification in epilepsy. Our analysis showed that using an ensemble of DTs can significantly improve efficiency compared to alternative DNN models, while achieving better classification accuracy, thus relaxing the strict energy-area-latency trade-off.

With efficient appearance learning models, discriminative correlation filter (DCF) has been proven to be very successful in recent video object tracking benchmarks and competitions. However, the existing DCF paradigm suffers from two major issues, i.e., spatial boundary effect and temporal filter degradation. To mitigate these challenges, we propose a new DCF-based tracking method. The key innovations of the proposed method include adaptive spatial feature selection and temporal consistent constraints, with which the new tracker enables joint spatial-temporal filter learning in a lower dimensional discriminative manifold. More specifically, we apply structured spatial sparsity constraints to multi-channel filters. Consequently, the process of learning spatial filters can be approximated by the lasso regularization. To encourage temporal consistency, the filter model is restricted to lie around its historical value and updated locally to preserve the global structure in the manifold. Last, a unified optimization framework is proposed to jointly select temporal consistency preserving spatial features and learn discriminative filters with the augmented Lagrangian method. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations have been conducted on a number of well-known benchmarking datasets such as OTB2013, OTB50, OTB100, Temple-Colour, UAV123, and VOT2018. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over the state-of-the-art approaches.

In the current practice, locational marginal prices (LMPs) are computed every few minutes by solving an optimization problem with continuous variables only.
