MulMapper utilizes Target Device Resource, Target Core Mode and Target Data Width as design dimensions to explore and propose optimum design points. The framework was tested on CNN architectures such as LeNet, CNP and CIFAR-10, and it has been verified that early-stage MulMapper can lead to synthesis of resource-optimized CNN processor hardware IP. Additionally, architectures designed using MulMapper obtained up to 25-29× reduction in DSP48 and 13-20× reduction in on-chip memory, with up to 0.35 GOP/sec performance, surpassing state-of-the-art designs.

In this paper, a design for an optimized fuzzy power system stabilizer is presented using the differential evolution algorithm (DEFPSS) combined with the sliding mode controller (SMC). The purpose of this design is to adapt the power system in various operation conditions by adjusting the control parameters, which improves stability and dynamic response. The DE algorithm optimally tunes the input-output scaling factors of the fuzzy power system stabilizer (FPSS) to obtain a robust controller. SMC is used to ensure the trajectory tracks the desired value under perturbation while providing excellent damping of oscillations. The proposed approach's robustness is validated through simulations under fault conditions for a Single Machine Infinite Bus (SMIB) power system, demonstrating excellent performance in reference tracking optimization.

The increasing use of consumer electronics and rapid development is directly linked with globalization and a rise in living standards. This necessitates high security authentication systems to protect personal information stored on mobile devices. The complexity and security of existing biometric systems is becoming a prime concern, which makes automated personal identification using finger-vein biometric a trending topic in both practical and research applications. In this paper, we use MATLAB 2016a to present the application of two machine learning methods, discriminant analysis and KNN (K-nearest neighbor algorithm), to verify and calculate the accuracy of finger vein image features. Our results show that the accuracy obtained from KNN is 55.84% while that obtained from discriminant analysis is 92.21%. Hence, we conclude that discriminant analysis is more accurate than KNN technique.

Recommendation systems for mobile phones play a crucial role in helping mobile operators achieve their desired profit targets. In a market where clients determine the number of contract users and phones, these systems are particularly important. With the increasing number of mobile cellular telephone contracts available, it has become imperative to develop recommender systems that help users find suitable contracts based on their usage patterns. To achieve this, a hybrid of both collaborative and content-based filtering was used in this study. A prototype of a mobile recommender system was developed and evaluated based on precision and recall. The results showed that the developed recommender system was able to successfully recommend packages to subscribers. This was evidenced by the precision-recall curve, which demonstrated the outstanding performance of the system. The study conclusively showed that a hybrid system was capable of providing effective recommendations to mobile subscribers.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a new revolution in the capabilities of endpoints that are connected to the internet. Its advancement is driven by the capabilities of sensor networks, mobile devices, wireless communications, networking, and cloud technologies. The demand for highly individualized products and services is continuously increasing, further adding to the complexity of this field. A key challenge in warehouse management is visibility, as accurate and timely information on shipments is crucial. Due to its increasing complexity, ordinary planning and control practices are no longer sufficient. To overcome the competitive business environment, actions must be taken through the implementation of IoT in warehouses. This research proposes an IoT architecture for the order picking process in a warehouse, with real-time tracking and inventory visibility, reduced warehouse operation costs, improved safety, and reduced theft and pilferage outcomes. While full automation is still relatively rare, even traditional man-to-goods warehouse operations have been impacted by new technologies, though people may still shoulder the greatest part of the workload. The future scope of IoT in warehouses is expected to continue growing as technology advances.

Low power wide area network (LPWAN) technology has been widely adopted in different Internet-of-things (IoT) services. Long range wide area network (LoRaWAN) is an evolution of wireless sensor network (WSN) directed to IoT concept, mostly used in private outdoor applications. The existing LoRaWAN operates following the simple ALOHA standards. Therefore, it suffers from high packet loss and supports a very limited number of nodes. For the application of LoRaWAN in dense networks, an efficient channel access mechanism is required in order to improve the efficiency and robustness. In this paper, we investigate a modified listen-before-talk (LBT) mechanism. Specifically, we propose LoRa-BED, LoRa-BEB and LoRa-BEH, channel access protocols to reduce collisions in high density environment. Our results demonstrate that the proposed protocols significantly improve the channel utilization and efficiency with a slight increase in energy per device while sensing the channel.

Chest X-ray (CXR) is a widespread method for the identification and diagnosis of thorax diseases in radiology. To aid in this process, computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) has been developed to help radiologists achieve fast and accurate diagnoses, improving patient healthcare outcomes. With this in mind, we have developed a new method to improve the performance of the CAD system in thorax disease diagnosis. Our approach combines the advantages of CNN models in image feature extraction with the benefits of problem transformation methods in multi-label classification tasks. We conducted an experimental study using two public CXR datasets (ChestX-ray14 and CheXpert), which included frontal and lateral views. Our findings revealed that our proposed method outperformed the current state of the art.

Ants are believed to be workaholics, though biologists report that many ants are literally inactive in nest move. An open question on this ants swarm behavior is whether such an active-to-population rate improves or deteriorates precise and swift nest move. In this study, we use an algorithm which is based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulate ant nest move. The simulation of our PSO-based algorithm has revealed that the swarm which comprises 60% of active ants in the population obviously outperforms the swarm of full active population in both precise and swift nest move. Our simulation results are supported with the field researches carried by external ant experts.

This article details the Versatile Tensor Accelerator (VTA), which is a programmable Deep Learning (DL) architecture that has been designed to be extensible and adaptable to evolving workloads. VTA is able to achieve "flexible specialization" through its parameterizable architecture, two-level Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), and a Just in Time (JIT) compiler.

This paper describes the integration of Google Assistant into an Android test application. With this integration, users can use voice commands to control content playback on a TV or set-top box, including starting or stopping playback, skipping to the next or previous segment, and skipping a specified number of seconds. Additionally, a visual solution for the application was developed and tested to confirm its functionality.

This study develops a service quality assessment system, based on the SERVQUAL, to assess the existing service performance of interior design companies. A real case study from interior and architecture experts is applied to conduct the service quality improvement processes. The result reveals that the proposed approach can be provided a guideline for companies seeking to improve sustainable business advantages and would be an effective decision tool for interior design company strategy optimization.

Predicting the price movements of stocks based on deep learning and high-frequency data has been studied intensively in recent years. Especially, limit order book which describes the supply-demand balance of the market is used as features of a neural network. However, these methods do not utilize the properties of market orders. On the other hand, this study encodes information of time and prices of orders into images. This encoding method can take advantage of these properties. Then, we apply machine learning methods, convolutional neural network (CNN) and logistic regression (LR), to order-based features to predict the direction of short-term price movements. The results show that the execution has the highest prediction power than the order and cancellation information. Moreover, the difference between CNN and LR are small and depends on kinds of stocks.

Online romance scams are a significant problem in the Western world, and it is essential to develop a data-driven response to address this issue. This kind of fraud involves fake profiles created by scammers who manually interact with their victims. Traditional detection methods used in spam filtering have proved to be ineffective due to the way dating sites operate. In this paper, we investigate the characteristics of online dating profiles used in romance scams, including demographic information, profile description, and images. The study aims to reveal the strategies employed by scammers to appeal to victims and the traits of the victims themselves. 

Moreover, in response to the financial and psychological harm caused by dating fraud, we have developed a system to detect romance scammers on online dating platforms. Our focus is on providing an early detection system to prevent scammers from creating fraudulent profiles or engaging with potential victims. Our ensemble machine-learning approach incorporates a range of structured, unstructured, and deep-learned features that capture the idealized romantic beliefs of the victims based on previous research. 

Our detection system is robust and performs with high accuracy (97%) in a validation set. The system can be used to develop automated tools for dating site providers and individual users. With the help of our system, we hope to stop romance scammers in their tracks and prevent harm to innocent victims.

This paper presents the development and evaluation of a simulated environment for autonomous task performance incorporating the LentiMark augmented reality marker-based pose estimation. The performance of the marker-based pose estimation was assessed within different simulated conditions that included variations in camera position, marker yaw and roll, illumination, shadow, and potential occlusion. Although the findings do not necessarily reflect the marker system's real-world performance, notable limitations were identified, including pose estimation inaccuracies due to pixelisation effects, detection failures due to background confusion, and performance degradation resulting from occlusion.

Entity resolution involves identifying and integrating records belonging to distinct entities. Standard techniques include rule-based or machine learning models that assign points to indicate matching or non-matching pairs of records. However, with a comprehensive comparison of all record pairs comes second-order matching complexity. To address this, blocking methods group identical entities into smaller blocks before conducting a comprehensive matching operation. One such method is token blocking, which groups records with similar tokens into the same block. However, most previous methods do not consider any semantic criteria. This paper proposes a new method called DeepBlock that employs deep learning to block entities in entity resolution by combining semantic and syntactic similarities to calculate record similarity. Evaluations show that DeepBlock outperforms token blocking significantly with respect to pair quality (PQ) measure, indicating that semantic and syntactic similarity can greatly enhance blocking quality.

This paper studies positioning fundamentals in low-power wide area (LPWA) Internet of Things (IoT), where those devices with locations known operate as anchors. A tractable model is developed to analyze localizability of target devices. A random scenario is investigated, where anchors are randomly distributed. The model first studies the positioning of a target which can be anywhere. Then, from the point of view of system level, target randomness is further considered so that the study can be conducted over the whole network area. The model has no limitations on area shape but can consider any arbitrary polygonal one. It incorporates the ability for participating anchors to coordinate transmissions, and the interference effect on positioning is theoretically investigated. The model is then extensively validated in comparison with simulations, and the effects of a set of parameter settings are investigated. Compared to the existing positioning performance studies targeting deterministic scenarios, the proposed model considers location randomness through distance distributions using a powerful probabilistic distance-based tool from geometric probability. The model considers both interference and system-related parameter settings, investigating anchor transmission coordination and traffic load, which reveals how participating anchors in general impact positioning performance in LPWA IoT.

Routing network packets is crucial to the functionality of the internet, but it also poses serious security risks. IP hijacks and misconfigurations are frequent occurrences that are challenging to detect. Although visual analytics approaches to tackling these issues have existed in the past, they rarely incorporated geographical references. Geo-IP data, which is typically only used as a lookup table, has untapped potential. To draw more attention to this resource, we present a visual-centric system solely grounded on Geo-IP data. We demonstrate that observing changes in Geo-IP data over an extended period—coupled with IP block proprietorship and location details—can unveil suspicious activity. In conjunction with our design study, we also provide a preprocessing algorithm for the Maxmind GeoIP2 City and ISP databases to motivate the community to incorporate this data into future approaches.

Over the past two decades, one of the most rapidly developing and sensitive research areas has been the detection of diabetic retinopathy (DR). Currently, in fundus images, the detection of retinal lesions relies on grading the severity of diabetic retinopathy and computer-aided screening, which has led to the implementation of automatic telemedicine systems. However, despite significant contributions to the field of detection, detection accuracy remains an ongoing concern. One issue of the existing algorithms used for the classification of DR images is that they are unable to encode directional information in both two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) planes. 

To address this limitation, the proposed approach encodes the directional information from the reference pixel to its surrounding pixel in four different directions (0°, 45°, 90°, and 135°) in 3D plane. The proposed model includes three steps, namely preprocessing, feature extraction using spherical directional local ternary pattern (SDLTP), and classification using both traditional distance measure and learning-based distance measure with an artificial neural network (ANN). 

SDLTP extracts directional features in 3D plane, and a principle component analysis (PCA) technique is applied to reduce the feature vector length. Two techniques are employed for classification purposes, distance measure and ANN. The proposed method is assessed by measuring classification accuracy in terms of precision. Experimental analysis demonstrates that the proposed method yields a significant improvement in classification accuracy in both unsupervised and supervised domains, as the feature extraction process takes directional information into account.

Piscirickettsia salmonis is a highly contagious pathogen that can lead to significant losses in farmed salmonids. To combat this issue, researchers have developed a new platform that utilizes both mass spectrometry (MS) and machine learning techniques to classify and predict the presence of this pathogen. By analyzing serum samples from healthy and diseased salmonids using MALDI-MS coupled with machine learning analysis, researchers were able to obtain a specific and sensitive pattern (m/z) for every pathogen, ensuring high reproducibility. Results showed that the combination of these two techniques was a powerful tool in early detection of the pathogen, with an accuracy rate of over 80%. This platform has the potential to serve as an effective tool for early disease control in the salmon farming industry.

This paper introduces a novel approach to efficiently manage Antimalware databases using a BlockChain-based distributed framework. As technology advances, computing and network performance have improved drastically. Unfortunately, this has also led to an increase in malicious activities through malwares. To combat this issue, we propose a distributed framework for managing Antimalware databases, implemented using a customized BlockChain that initiates a distributed malware prevention program. The use of BlockChain technology ensures that data management is secure and decentralized, without the need for any third-party involvement.

Driver distraction is one of the leading causes of vehicle accidents and injury. Automated systems for identifying driver distraction are of great interest for improving road safety. This study develops a smartphone sensor based driver distraction system using an ensemble learning method. After data collection, linear velocity data is first linearly interpolated. Then, 3-axial acceleration and 3-axial gyro signals are filtered for reducing noise. Next, a sliding window is applied to IMU and GPS data collected by the smartphone for feature extraction, where temporal features are calculated. Ensemble learning of four standard classifiers is used to recognize distraction events: K-Nearest Neighbor, Logistic Regression, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Random Forest. To evaluate the proposed approach, 24 drivers were recruited to participate in a user study, driving on a route consisting of suburban and highway driving. Driver cognitive distraction was induced by asking the driver questions while driving. The experimental results show that the best weighted F1-score of our proposed system is 87% with all smartphone sensor signals.

In this paper, we explore the complexities and potential benefits of cellular networks powered by the smart grid (SG) and local renewable energy (RE) sources. Our focus is on the interaction between network operators and the SG, and the possibility of cellular networks providing ancillary services to the grid. We propose a new approach for configuring and operating base stations (BSs) to provide these services, using a Markov chain model that takes into account the energy state of the BS, the randomness of SG requests, and RE generation. By using real data and evaluating the system's performance, we find that significant cost savings are possible without any noticeable degradation in quality of service. Proper consideration of RE generation, SG patterns, and storage sizes are crucial in achieving these results. Our proposal outperforms other approaches, showcasing the potential of this configuration to promote energy savings, cleaner energy, and cost reduction.

Majority of Defense Systems utilizes rectangular enclosures and shelters in mobile systems for carrying various equipment such as communication, surveillance, CBRN sensors, power supplies etc. The electromagnetic compatibility at sub-system level as well as at system level of such equipment is necessary in view of the operational conditions as defined in various military standards. The overall electromagnetic compatibility depends on shielding effectiveness of enclosure used in such systems. The effects of external electromagnetic interferences due to various sources, its coupling to subsystems needs to be under control. Emission control is desired depending upon the deployment and operational requirements. One such fully EM compatible rectangular enclosure is designed and developed. The analysis, simulation and test results are presented in this paper.

Many cloud encryption methods have been proposed to achieve the encryption and decryption of users' data stored on public cloud database, and there are also some studies on heterogeneous database connection access methods, but none of them can implement the users's transparent (cross-language and cross-platform) or heterogeneous access to encrypted database on public cloud. To solve these problems, we modularly comply a middleware system in a private cloud by using the Mysql protocol and heterogeneous database data integration technology, which is applied in a hybrid cloud environment to achieve the users' transparent access to heterogeneous encrypted database. We talk about the preliminary assessment on the system security. Besides, the experimental evaluation testifies the system performance through separately testing time costs for the users to execute transparent access to individual and heterogeneous encrypted database.

Over the last decade, artificial intelligence (AI) has become the driving force behind many technological innovations. To implement AI in computing systems, a wide range of algorithms have been proposed, with extreme learning machine (ELM) emerging as one of the most effective training algorithms for simple applications based on single layer feed-forward neural networks (SLFN). However, it is critical to have hardware implementation of neural network algorithms for time-sensitive applications.

This paper presents a simplified AI accelerator based on CMOS technology that implements an ELM-based inference engine. The analysis of implementing such an accelerator on different technology nodes with comparative analysis shows the impact of technology node scaling on performance of the proposed accelerator in terms of power and area. The workload used for this analysis was a network of dimensions 81x18x1. This study observed a remarkable benefit in speed (1.3x), area (14x) and power (7x) by scaling the design from 180 nm to 45 nm.

Additionally, the study analyzed the benefits of emerging non-volatile memory (NVM) technologies like RRAM as the primary memory technology for the accelerator. Results showed that replacing conventional CMOS with RRAM would give significant benefits in leakage (4.5x) and area (33x). Overall, this study presents a promising solution for implementing AI in time-sensitive applications with the use of ELM-based inference engines and incorporating emerging NVM technologies.

Most software defect prediction models usually assume that enough historical training instances with labels are available. Additionally, the training data and the predicted instances should share the same features to ensure the prediction accuracy. However, in practice, there are many datasets with different granularities containing information in different dimensions. Therefore, it is valuable to effectively use the small scale and different dimensions of data as training instances to improve the prediction performance of the model. We propose a heterogeneous data orienting multiview transfer learning for software defect prediction, denoted as MTDP, which can achieve different dimensions and granularities features to automatically learn labels through neural network models. With this multiview transfer method, lots of training instances are provided for software defect prediction model to ensure the effectiveness of training labels. The proposed MTDP method has four main stages: 1) build heterogeneous transfer models; 2) transfer heterogeneous instances to generate quasi-real instances; 3) label quasi-real instances through co-training and then expand the training set; and (4) construct improved software defect prediction models. The experimental results show that the quasi-real instances have similar effects compared with real instances. Moreover, the software defect prediction performance can be improved by introducing the quasi-real instances into the training dataset.

For the sake of positioning the illegal unmanned aerial vehicle operators, the paper proposes a direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm based on the reconnaissance plane with multiple array sensors. First, the number of unmanned aerial vehicle signals is determined by information theory criteria. Then combined support vector regression, the direction of the operator is calculated according to some approximating function through training. Finally, the location can be estimated by integrating the DOAs acquired with the array sensors on the reconnaissance aircraft. This algorithm is convenient and fast to be realized, moreover, as a result of adopting super resolution and multiple kernel learning, it can locate numerous radio signals simultaneously and performs well in the circumstance that signals impinge on the sensor array with small-angle interval, as well as the conditions of small samples and low signal to noise ratio, besides, the algorithm also applies to the array which gain-phase inconsistency exists among the sensors.

Hyperspectral image classification is a challenging task when a limited number of training samples are available. It is also known that the classification performance highly depends on the quality of the labeled samples. In this work, a cluster-based conditional generative adversarial net (CCGAN) is proposed as an effective solution to increase the size and quality of the training data set. The proposed method is able to automatically select the most representative initial samples with a subtractive clustering-based strategy, which keeps the diversity for sample generation. Moreover, compared to the traditional semisupervised classification frameworks, the CCGAN is able to generate realistic spectral profiles by considering the class-specific labels. Experiments on well-known Pavia University data set demonstrate that the proposed CCGAN can significantly boost the classification accuracy, even using a small number of initial labeled samples.

With the explosive growth of cloud manufacturing (CMfg), a plethora of functionally equivalent cloud services are available on the Internet, and as a result, predicting quality of service (QoS) has become a pressing issue. Due to wide variability of QoS among service users, Collaborative Filtering (CF) approaches have been recently introduced, which extend the Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) similarity to predict unknown QoS. However, most existing approaches are either limited regarding similarity computation or fail to address the data sparsity problem, leading to results that are not reliable. To overcome these issues, we propose a hybrid approach, named HAP, for QoS prediction. Firstly, to achieve improved prediction accuracy, we implement a similarity-enhanced CF (L-CF) for local QoS prediction, which factors in the personalized influence of similar users and services while computing PCC similarity. Secondly, to overcome the data sparsity problem, we propose a global QoS prediction approach based on case-based reasoning (G-CBR), which fully utilizes both user and service information. Lastly, we create an ensemble model that combines the results of the two approaches. Comprehensive real-world experiments are conducted to demonstrate the efficacy of our approach compared to other state-of-the-art approaches, particularly when QoS data is very sparse.

Time series forecasting has been regarded as a key research problem in various fields. such as financial forecasting, traffic flow forecasting, medical monitoring, intrusion detection, anomaly detection, and air quality forecasting etc. In this paper, we propose a sequence-to-sequence deep learning framework for multivariate time series forecasting, which addresses the dynamic, spatial-temporal and nonlinear characteristics of multivariate time series data by LSTM based encoder-decoder architecture. Through the air quality multivariate time series forecasting experiments, we show that the proposed model has better forecasting performance than classic shallow learning and baseline deep learning models. And the predicted PM2.5 value can be well matched with the ground truth value under single timestep and multi-timestep forward forecasting conditions. The experiment results show that our model is capable of dealing with multivariate time series forecasting with satisfied accuracy.

It is troublesome to obtain the fused state estimation for multi-sensor multi-delay systems with correlated noises. The previous conventional fused estimation method uses the information, sent by several different filter, smoothers and predictors, to get one-step estimation, which increases the complexity of the method, so that it is not suitable for real application. In order to get more convenient estimators, the augmented state equation is introduced, and then an augmented steady-state Kalman estimator can be got, which conceals the time delays. Extracting the partial component of that augmented steady-state estimator yields the suboptimal estimator, which ignores the correlation between the components of the augmented estimator, but possesses more excellent rapidity and convenience compared with the previous fused estimator. Then by Sequential Covariance Intersection (CI) fusion method, a fast fusion steady-state suboptimal Kalman filter is obtained. Simulation examples show that although the proposed fusion steady-state estimator is suboptimal, its accuracy is higher than each of the local estimators and approximate to the optimal information fusion estimator.

This paper tackles the challenge of Community Question Answering (CQA) in Arabic and proposes a novel approach that leverages both lexical and semantic features to improve answer retrieval. The authors conduct a thorough evaluation of their method using the SEMEval2017 CQA dataset for Arabic and achieve a Mean Average Precision (MAP) score of 62.85% using a supervised machine learning approach (linear SVM), outperforming the best reported results on the dataset to date. Their approach incorporates a variety of features including word embeddings, latent semantic similarities, and other lexical similarities.

Fog computing is a promising approach to address the challenges of Cloud computing in IoT by providing low latency and real-time services. However, in cases of high load on some fog layer, offloading is required to handle the load quickly, which results in increased latency. To overcome this, a cognitive and context-aware horizontal offloading mechanism has been proposed. This mechanism uses three technologies, Virtualization, Containerization, and Microservices, to keep the computations as much as possible in the same fog layer using the same available resources. By offloading the computations from the loaded fog nodes to less loaded ones in the same fog layer, high load can be horizontally handled using the same available resources. The mechanism depends on dividing the IoT application into microservices, where each microservice is responsible for only one function and isolated in containers hosted in the fog nodes. The offloading is performed at the level of the microservices by watching, analyzing, and considering their load patterns and availability for offloading. The mechanism is cognitive and context-aware and selects the most appropriate fog nodes for offloading in a real-time fashion to avoid affecting their performance. By simulating the mechanism on the traffic management system, each fog node can horizontally handle extra requests up to 30% for each hosted microservice by offloading to 2 microservices, and up to 100% in case there are 7 available offloading microservices. This research shows that the proposed cognitive and context-aware horizontal offloading mechanism is an effective approach to handle high load in fog computing to provide low latency and real-time services.

There are some concerns that education professionals seek to solve. The first to be able to promote learning is through the change of pedagogical methodology, pedagogical projects of courses or new learning strategies. The second refers to people with disabilities or specific classes of users accessing digital information. This article has been published in the following languages: How are students through the use of interesting projects, such as the use of PBL methodology and how other serious connected games. The phases of PBL were applied to the development of games, aimed at improving memory, are presented and discussed in this work, as well as their results and discussions.

According to recent studies hemodynamic conditions play an important role in initiation and development of several disorders of the cerebral circulation, such as atherosclerosis and aneurysm. One of the common sites of the aneurysm formation is the middle cerebral artery (MCA). In the present study, the flow conditions in the individualized model of the MCA aneurysm are investigated in detail and correlated with the aneurysm genesis. A patient-specific model of the saccular aneurysm of MCA was derived from the real clinical imaging data. A realistic physiological pulse curve was scaled to ensure the normal inlet flow rate in the artery. A transient computational fluid dynamics simulation was performed employing the Local viscosity fluid model, which takes into account non-Newtonian blood behavior and increases a precision of hemodynamic parameters evaluation, especially at low shear rate zones. The complex flow pattern was observed in the aneurysm sac, producing a swirling blood flow. A flow impingement zone near the aneurysm fundus was characterized by the high velocity values, about 0.9 m/s, which could potentially affect the endothelial cells at this zone and contribute to further arterial wall degeneration. Moreover, the zone of low wall shear stresses (<;2 Pa) was observed on the aneurysm dome, producing conditions for further growth of the aneurysm. The results of the study are consistent with hemodynamic theory of aneurysm genesis and correlate well with available clinical data. CFD simulation could be used as an additional tool for clinical decision support during the treatment of the cerebral aneurysms.

We study the properties of the Frank-Wolfe algorithm to solve the m-EXACT-SPARSE reconstruction problem, where a signal y must be expressed as a sparse linear combination of a predefined set of atoms, called dictionary. We prove that when the signal is sparse enough with respect to the coherence of the dictionary, then the iterative process implemented by the Frank-Wolfe algorithm only recruits atoms from the support of the signal, is the smallest set of atoms from the dictionary that allows for a perfect reconstruction of y. We also prove that under this same condition, there exists an iteration beyond which the algorithm converges exponentially.

This study focuses on the estimation and prediction of the sparse time-varying channel in underwater acoustic communication systems. The channel estimation approach takes advantage of the sparse structure of the delay-Doppler representation of the channel. Several state-of-the-art matching pursuit (MP)-type algorithms for sparse signal reconstruction are compared, and sparsity adaptive MP (SaMP) and its variant adaptive step size SaMP are found to outperform other algorithms in terms of mean squared error (MSE), without requiring a priori knowledge of the sparsity level.

Because of the fast time-varying nature and extremely limited bandwidth of underwater acoustic channels, accurate channel prediction is essential for reliable symbol detection. This study proposes an adaptive channel prediction scheme that extrapolates the channel knowledge estimated from a block of training symbols. The predicted channel is then used to decode consecutive data blocks. The proposed scheme does not require any a priori knowledge of channel dynamic model and noise statistics, and is able to provide future channel estimates based solely on current channel estimates. Moreover, the proposed scheme operates in the delay-Doppler domain, which leads to a remarkably lower computational complexity compared to time domain prediction methods.

To further enhance the prediction accuracy, the proposed predictor is fed with past detected symbols to assist with an up-to-date channel estimate. Simulation results of the proposed channel estimation and prediction demonstrate good tradeoff between the MSE/bit error rate and computational complexity.

This paper introduces a novel control strategy for the multi-phase induction machine (MPIM) drive, which utilizes a fuzzy logic controller (FLC) in conjunction with cascaded hybrid multi-level inverters (CHMI). Two control methods were presented and evaluated, with the first one relying on a linear PI controller and the second one utilizing a nonlinear FLC. Simulation results obtained from both control strategies were analyzed and compared, with clear evidence demonstrating that the FLC provided superior performance and robustness when applied to the CHMI-based electrical drive.

A Data Centre is a physical space that groups together computer equipment such as servers, storage arrays, among other equipment. It can be used for storage, processing and data protection. The majority of data centres operate 24 hours a day, and must provide the user with guarantees in terms of security and performance. Energy consumption is therefore permanent and the level of assistance and maintenance high. Data Centres have an ecological impact that is almost invisible to many users. In this paper a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model of the airflow and thermal distribution of a real data centre room with 208 racks is proposed. Two case studies are presented and simulated with a high thermal load subjected to the minimum and maximum air flow velocity, respectively. The objective is to assess if the computer room air conditioning unit (CRAC) can cool the racks of the data centre in order to efficiently refrigerate all the hot spots.

Water level control in open channels used for hydroelectric production is addressed in this paper. In order to use classical methods of controller design, a new reduced order model based on Saint-Venant equations is proposed. It is derived from irrational transfer functions developed with the WKB method for any non-uniform subcritical flow regime. The reduced model captures the first two modes. A comparison of open-loop simulations with the proposed 5th order plus delay transfer functions and with numerical non linear model is performed. The inputs of the simulations are given by on-site measurements to show the accuracy of the model in realistic conditions. Based on the resulting model, a robust tuning of controller is developed. It consists of a two-degree-of-freedom proportional integral controller. Time domain scenarii are shown to illustrate the closed-loop performance.

Label propagation algorithm (LPA) is one of the classical community detection algorithms, with high efficiency, quick speed and no need for any prior information. However, it has the disadvantage of poor stability, which causes the detection results to be random. In order to improve the stability of label propagation algorithm, an algorithm with an adjustable parameter based on clustering coefficient and label propagation is proposed in this article. The algorithm is divided into two steps. The first step is to prioritize the nodes according to their degree and clustering coefficient, and initialize the label according to the ranking result. In the process of initializing the label, only the nodes with clustering coefficient in a certain range are selected to filter out the noisy nodes. The second step is based on the first step. In order to avoid randomness, the neighbor nodes are sorted according to their clustering coefficient and degree, the optimal neighbor node is selected to update the label. By applying the algorithm to LFR artificial network data sets and real networks data sets, the results show that the algorithm reduces the randomness of the label propagation algorithm, enhances the stability and accuracy of detection result, and its adjustable parameter make it possible to have a good quality of community division for various types of networks.

Despite the importance of competency modeling for both individuals and organizations, there is a lack of a comprehensive literature review and a cartography for it. This paper aims to provide an in-depth overview of different approaches to competency modeling reported in the field of technology-enhanced com petency-based learning. This literature review is complemented by an additional overview of related initiatives toward modeling intended learning outcomes, learning opportunities, achieved learning outcome profiles of learners and competency maps. In addition, a cartography illustrating the relationships between some important models is proposed. The main purpose of this work is to provide researchers with a comprehensive review of the current status in this field as well as to highlight ongoing issues and challenges that need to be addressed.

Experimentation in the modern age, and electronic engineering teaching and learning should be efficient and effective. The first course on analog electronics appears in engineering curricula in the third semester or earlier, and laboratory experiments often suffer from student's lack of breadboard circuit manipulation and data acquisition skills, which frequently leads to erroneous results and loss of time. The pocket sized EZ-TBOARD and its associated didactic resources is an experimentation system project that speeds up learning related to basic operation and application of semiconductor transistors. By means of a reconfigurable compact design, the training board helps students to setup the major different biasing, amplification and switching schemes suggested for all kind of three terminal transistors, in order to focus the experimenter's attention on the key aspects of device and application circuit theory, enhancing the student's capacity to analyze, design and reconfigure a circuit for a required behavior. The provided educational materials cover typical analysis and design methods to observe system outputs dependency on value of circuit element parameters, instead of common circuit assembly mistakes. It is expected for the training system to become an important reference for open educational resources in analog electronics engineering.

The recent advanced in the low-cost, small-scale EEG scanners open the doors for many innovations in the domains of disease detection, social sciences, cyber security, and much more. In this paper, we investigate the possibility of using EEG signals as an indication of deception or lies. Further, we exploit one of the new EEG scanners, MUSE, to investigate its ability to provide what is needed to detect potential lies. Our experiments showed great success for the MUSE in providing what is needed for a moderate-quality lie detector, with very low-cost and complexity. Integrating machine-learning techniques into the presented results would provide a much more accurate detection opening the door for a vast number of potential applications.

This paper considers the task of indoor subarea localization by acoustic sensing. In many practical scenarios, such as ordinary office rooms, subarea localization based on a single acoustic property without subsidiaries is always tricky due to similar space physical structures. To combat the indoor subarea localization problem without any dedicated devices, we propose a framework allowing the ordinary smartphone to quickly and easily determine its indoor subarea location. The proposed structure is to first construct the multidimensional fingerprint of each environmental background audio in a room using the auditory scene analysis method; then extract the room-level fingerprint by the acoustic background spectrum method, and cluster the subarea-level fingerprints using the Pearson correlation coefficient technology; subsequently, together with the offline stage long short-term memory recurrent neuron network and online stage least variance algorithm, the effective indoor subarea localization was achieved; finally, the localization results are presented not only in text form but also in a privacy-protected color sound pattern which is built by chroma DCT-reduced log pitch. Our experiments with real-world audios, which include 96-h environment background audios of 14 different rooms, presents that the room-level localization accuracy was higher than 90% and the subarea-level accuracy could be up to 97.64%. These results strongly proved that the proposed framework could perform well even in small complicated rooms.

Currently, autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is mainly diagnosed by the observation of core behavioral symptoms. Consequently, the window of opportunity for effective intervention may have passed, when the disorder is detected until 3 years of age. Thus, it is of great importance to identify imaging-based biomarkers for early diagnosis of ASD. Previous findings indicate that an abnormal pattern of the amygdala and hippocampal development in autism persists through childhood and adolescence. However, due to the low tissue contrast and small structural size of amygdala and hippocampal subfields, our knowledge on their growth in autistics in early stage still remains very limited. In this paper, for the first time, we propose a volume-based analysis of the amygdala and hippocampal subfields of the infant subjects with risk of ASD at around 24 months of age. Specifically, to address the challenge of low tissue contrast, we propose a novel deep-learning approach, i.e., dilated-dense U-Net, to automatically segment the amygdala and hippocampal subfields. Experimental results on National Database for Autism Research (NDAR) show the advantages of our proposed method in terms of segmentation accuracy. Our volume-based analysis shows the overgrowths of amygdala and CA1-3 of hippocampus, which may link to the emergence of autism spectrum disorder.

This article describes a high school educational tool that generates problems for a test on plasma chemistry courses. The tool utilizes the Algorithm for a wave functions, which calculates the behavior of many-electron atoms in a central field approximation. The method is based on an iterative procedure similar to the Hartree-Fock method. Additionally, the article details the interface of the resulting program, which is used for generating the test problems. This tool marks a first step towards a more comprehensive program which deals with calculating rate constants in plasma chemistry.

We present a new Arabic annotation web application that aims to associate tags to the words of the vocalized Hadiths corpus. The application assures a collaborative space between many annotators. Each annotator treats one or more Hadith from his/her personal session. We analyze each Hadith using AlKhalil morphological analyzer. The annotator rectifies the analysis and assigns the accurate annotation values. Annotation includes the segmentation of a word, the POS tag, the root and the pattern. The final annotation results of the corpus are structured in XML files. We can display, also, the annotation results in a Treebank. Our tool is considered as a crowdsourcing solution that uses contributions from various annotators to obtain an annotated Arabic coprus. This resource may be used as a standard collection to experiment NLP researches.

Phishing is a security attack to acquire personal information like passwords, credit card details or other account details of a user by means of websites or emails. Phishing websites look similar to the legitimate ones which make it difficult for a layman to differentiate between them. As per the reports of Anti Phishing Working Group (APWG) published in December 2018, phishing against banking services and payment processor was high. Almost all the phishy URLs use HTTPS and use redirects to avoid getting detected. This paper presents a focused literature survey of methods available to detect phishing websites. A comparative study of the in-use anti-phishing tools was accomplished and their limitations were acknowledged. We analyzed the URL-based features used in the past to improve their definitions as per the current scenario which is our major contribution. Also, a step wise procedure of designing an anti-phishing model is discussed to construct an efficient framework which adds to our contribution. Observations made out of this study are stated along with recommendations on existing systems.

The goal of health monitoring systems is to offer continuous and high-quality service to users, which requires the system to operate without interruptions for an extended period of time. This paper examines methods to maximize the lifetime of Wireless Body Sensor Networks (WBSN) in order to provide sustainable e-health service with energy harvesting enabled nodes. Maximizing the lifetime is equivalent to minimizing the energy budget of the network, which can be achieved by optimizing the time resource allocation for all the involved sensor nodes. This ensures a sufficient energy level is maintained for a longer duration after each packet transmission. 

To achieve this objective, the energy harvesting process is modelled as a discrete-time Markov chain, and the instant energy budget is evaluated to decide which node occupies a specific time slot. The net energy is calculated as the gap between the consumed and harvested energies, and prioritizing nodes with a minimum net energy level ensures sustainability. Nodes with high net energy levels can harvest more energy and increase their capabilities to submit data continuously. 

The proposed algorithm is assessed in terms of uninterrupted lifetime of the sensor and packet loss due to energy shortage by conducting simulations. Results indicate longer uninterrupted lifetime compared to the benchmark, and a low probability of packet loss for the users.

With the increase in the number of connected objects around us, the concepts of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Big Data are expanding to cover a wide variety of areas of application. This chapter reviews the objects of the IoT as the agents in multi‐agent systems, with the goal of modeling and implementing a multi‐agent architecture in the field of the IoT. It also reviews the different paradigms of the IoT and the links that have been established in the literature between the IoT and multi‐agent systems. In order to experiment the multi‐agent architecture in a real‐world context, the chapter then presents an application of IoT‐a through a set of connected “brick‐screens” that allows programmers to build an interactive and reconfigurable wall of screens. It illustrates this application by visiting the eco‐distributed resolution of the N‐Puzzle algorithm and applying it to the resolution of an N‐puzzle video.

In this paper, we introduce a household Electric Vehicle (EV) scheduling scheme based on a deep neural network (DNN) demand forecast. We present a novel approach for Short Term Load Forecasting (STLF) using DNN with clustering methodology to forecast both household and EV demand. The forecasting was conducted on demand profiles for 200 households in the Midwest region of the United States. We utilized a Tensor-flow based deep learning platform to develop the DNN structure. The households were clustered based on their demand profiles and the clusters were used as forecasting parameters. The scheduling model was developed using the forecasted household and EV demand values to create a linear programming-based optimization model aimed at minimizing the electricity costs for consumers. The optimization model takes into account household and cluster constraints to prevent sudden surges in power demand during low-price periods.

Inverters are widely used as electrical drive systems in many industrial applications. The inverter IGBT switch open-circuit fault; object of our study; is one type of the inverter faults that attracts the attention of many researchers. In this paper an open-circuit fault detection technique is proposed using the artificial neural network (ANN) aided by the Clarke transform. The technique is presented according to two approaches. The first approach calculates the Clarke stator currents and other quantities such as the intervals fault angles α and the trajectory surface S. Once all these quantities are obtained, they are then introduced to the ANN structure for the learning process; the output obtained from the ANN corresponds to the exact angle related to the inverter IGBT switch open-circuit fault. The second approach follows exactly the same calculation steps as the first approach except that in this case all the computation is performed within the ANN architecture. To illustrate the effectiveness of the technique and validate the results, some experimental works are conducted using a three-phase voltage inverter fed induction motor.

Three-dimensional (3D) volumetric neural image segmentation is crucial to reconstructing accurate neuron structures. However, due to the structural complexity of neurons and the diverse imaging qualities of the microscopes, it is challenging to achieve both accuracy and efficiency. In this paper, we propose a teacher-student learning framework for fast neuron segmentation. The segmentation inference is performed using a light-weighted student network which benefits from knowledge distillation of a teacher network with a higher capacity. Evaluated on the Janelia dataset from the BigNeuron project, our proposed framework achieves competitive performance for segmentation accuracy while reducing the computational cost to facilitate large-scale processing.

Weakly-supervised semantic segmentation has gained increasing attention in recent years since it eliminates the need for obtaining dense pixel-wise ground-truth annotations for training images. Image labels, on the other hand, can be acquired quite efficiently. In this paper, we explore weakly-supervised semantic segmentation with image label annotations, which has made significant progress with the quality of generated pseudo-annotations. To improve upon this, we propose a decoupled spatial neural attention network that is inspired by spatial neural attention for image captioning. Our proposed structure allows for simultaneous identification of object regions and localization of discriminative parts, which generates high-quality pseudo-annotations in one forward path. The generated pseudo-annotations lead to segmentation results that achieve the state-of-the-art in weakly supervised semantic segmentation.

With the widespread use of the Internet of Things (IoT), the collaboration of various smart devices to provide smart services without human intervention is becoming more prevalent. However, this also raises concerns regarding privacy and security. In large-scale IoT applications, such as Smart Grids or Smart Cities, access authorization is a critical security challenge for resource sharing and information protection. The current centralized authorization server used in access control (AC) is a weakness as it can be a performance bottleneck or a single point of failure.

To address such concerns, BlendCAC proposes a blockchain-enabled decentralized capability-based AC for IoT security. This approach aims for effective access control to devices, services, and information in large-scale IoT systems while avoiding a centralized authority. A capability delegation mechanism is suggested to propagate access permission based on a blockchain network, and a robust identity-based capability token management strategy that utilizes smart contracts for registration, propagation, and revocation of access authorization.

In the proposed BlendCAC scheme, the IoT devices are self-managed, which enables them to control their resources rather than being supervised by a centralized authority. Experimentally proven to be feasible, BlendCAC offers a decentralized, scalable, lightweight, and fine-grained AC solution to IoT systems. This approach ensures secure access authorization while avoiding the weaknesses of centralized authorization servers.

This research concerns the detection of unauthorised access within hospital networks through the real-time analysis of audit logs. Privacy is a primary concern amongst patients due to the rising adoption of Electronic Patient Record (EPR) systems. There is growing evidence to suggest that patients may withhold information from healthcare providers due to lack of Trust in the security of EPRs. Yet, patient record data must be available to healthcare providers at the point of care. Ensuring privacy and confidentiality of that data is challenging. Roles within healthcare organisations are dynamic and relying on access control is not sufficient. Through proactive monitoring of audit logs, unauthorised accesses can be detected and presented to an analyst for review. Advanced data analytics and visualisation techniques can be used to aid the analysis of big data within EPR audit logs to identify and highlight pertinent data points. Employing a human-in-the-loop model ensures that suspicious activity is appropriately investigated and the data analytics is continuously improving. This paper presents a system that employs a Human-in-the-Loop Machine Learning (HILML) algorithm, in addition to a density-based local outlier detection model. The system is able to detect 145 anomalous behaviours in an unlabelled dataset of 1,007,727 audit logs. This equates to 0.014% of the EPR accesses being labelled as anomalous in a specialist Liverpool (UK) hospital.

Recent research in Software-Defined Networking (SDN) advocates for the adoption of distributed controller architectures. The performance of the network heavily depends on the scheduling function (SF) that appropriately dispatches requests from each switch to suitable controllers. However, most literature focuses on SFs designed for specific network settings, thus limiting their applicability. This paper proposes a reinforcement-learning-based approach to automatically learn a general, efficient, and effective SF. The approach introduces a dispatching system where the SF is a neural network that assigns priorities to each controller. Based on the priorities, the scheme selects a controller using a proposed probability selection process that balances exploration and exploitation during learning. To train the SF, the scheduling function design problem is formulated as a reinforcement-learning problem. A new training approach is then developed using a state-of-the-art deep RL algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the RL approach rapidly designs optimal performance SFs. Additionally, the trained SF generalizes well and outperforms commonly used scheduling heuristics under various network settings.

Millimeter wave (MmWave) is a promising technology nowadays because it provides users with ultra-high data rate links with low latency time. Hence, internet of things, tactile internet and cloud computing applications which becomes an essential matter in 5G networks can be supported using it. MmWave standard, IEEE 802.11 ad, proposed using scheduled medium access control (MAC) based on time division multiple access (TDMA) to share radio resources among active mmWave users. MmWave has a highly dynamic time-variant channel with high blocking probability which highly degrades the entire system performance. Hence, applying simple channel independent scheduling schemes, e.g., round robin (RR), will be inefficient. Thus, an efficient radio resource scheduling with considering the changes in mmWave channel is needed for maximum benefit from available resources. This paper presents the performance evaluation of one of the channel sensitive scheduling schemes, proportional fairness scheduling (PFS), in downlink mmWave network by executing numerical simulation in different channel conditions and various mmWave beamwidths regarding the total system data rate and fairness between users.

An online dual estimation algorithm is developed to jointly estimate in real-time traffic quantities such as queue lengths, occupancies and flows, as well as the parameters of a macroscopic model of a signalized junction. These parameters include turning ratios and saturation flows, together with model uncertainties. The proposed novel methodology is based on the Expectation-Maximization algorithm, modified for real-time estimation, with a Kalman filter implementing the expectation step and a multivariate gradient-based approach for the maximisation step. The algorithm is validated by simulating the typical signalized 3-arm and 4-arm junctions. This work is aimed to form a part of the adaptive control loops for traffic light systems that are able to autonomously adjust with changing traffic conditions, so as to ensure efficient vehicle flows.

In the current information age, data has become more valuable to organizations than ever before. By utilizing machine learning and deep learning techniques to analyze historical or transactional data, groundbreaking insights can be derived to make better-informed decisions and adopt the best strategies to face future events. This paper attempts to establish a correlation between climatic factors and a forecasted malaria outbreak, while also determining the most suitable algorithm for modeling the discovered relationship. The study collected six years' worth of meteorological data and recorded malarial cases to analyze with various classification techniques, including KNN, Naive Bayes, and Extreme Gradient Boost. After evaluating each algorithm's accuracy, the recall score, precision score, Matthews correlation coefficient, and error rate, the best performing models were identified. Results indicate that weather forecasts can legitimately predict malarial outbreaks and enable necessary preventive measures to prevent loss of life due to malaria.

The paper describes the comparison of saliency maps calculated for a specific type of images to the ground truth fixations obtained in eye tracking experiment. The images being analyzed contained camouflaged animals. Because of the camouflage, it was expected that calculation of saliency would be the hard case. Several saliency maps were compared to the ground truth with a set of standard measures and a ranking based on their averaged performance was proposed. The results reveal that for the saliency map models, images of camouflaged animals are harder to analyze than ordinary ones, although, one model - Judd - appeared to work particularly well. Additionally, susceptibility of saliency maps to the perceived difficulty of the camouflage was discussed.

Image segmentation plays a key role in many medical imaging applications, especially in Computer-Aided Detection (CAD) system for mammography. A good segmentation allows increasing the performance and efficiency of CAD system that enables the radiologist to conduct a clear diagnostic analysis and to make better decisions; this requires effective tools and techniques. This paper proposes a new method to extract the mass from the Region of Interest (ROI) based on texture features and Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering with setting c= 2, whereas the user selects the region of interest manually. The process of clustering is applying within an appropriate range limited by the maximum of intensity and a threshold defined by the big changes in the texture features levels. The proposed method is applied to Mini-MIAS database and then its performance is compared with some explored methods. In this study, the result of overlap measure (AOM) was achieved approximately 81%.

In this paper, the problem of the model parameter estimation for in-pipe walking robots has been studied. Three estimators (regressor function-based method and the least squares-based methods with and without damping) are studied and analyzed. The study is focused on the influence the sensor resolution has on the accuracy of the estimation. The influence the accuracy of the initial estimation has on the methods' performance was also discussed. Two performance functions are proposed in order to simplify the analysis. It was shown that the least squares method has a significant advantage when the exact information about the robot's state is known; however, when the sensors have finite resolution, the performance of this method changes significantly while the regressor-based method is affected much less.

Nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM) has attracted tremendous attention owing to its cost efficiency in electricity and sustainable development. NILM aims at acquiring individual appliance power consumption rates using an aggregated power smart meter reading. Each individual appliance's power consumption enables users to monitor their electricity usage habits for rational saving strategies. This is also a valuable tool for detecting failure in appliances. However, the major barriers facing NILM schemes are issues of accurately capturing the features of each appliance and decreasing the computing time. Motivated by these challenges, we propose a new, efficient, and accurate NILM scheme, consisting of a learning step and a decomposing step. In the learning step, we propose the fast search-and-find of density peaks (FSFDPs) clustering algorithm aimed at capturing the features of the power consumption patterns of appliances. In the decomposing step, we propose a genetic algorithm (GA)-based matching algorithm to estimate the power consumption of each individual appliance using the aggregated power reading. Using elitist and catastrophic strategies, this step reduces the searching space to achieve considerable efficiency. Experimental results using the reference energy disaggregation dataset (REDD) indicate that our proposed scheme promotes accuracy by 10% and reduces the decomposing time by half.

Water quality is influenced by an array of factors, ranging from climate patterns and geographical location to chemical makeup and aquatic diversity. Given the critical connection between water quality, environmental conditions, and human health, this paper explores an IoT-centered solution for water sensing and classification, using a practical example of real-time water quality measurement and learning algorithms that can be integrated in an IoT network. The paper uses pisciculture breeding as a case study to illustrate its key points. The proposed methodology could serve as a precursor for a large-scale platform that would enable mapping different water traits, as well as simultaneous sensing and classification of water properties. A smart bio-material has been deployed as the data acquisition interface. Acquired data is promptly saved and analysed in a fog device, thus facilitating appropriate decision-making and triggering alarms, when appropriate.

Multicore fibers have emerged as a promising solution for Radio over Fiber (RoF) transmission of millimeter wave (mmwave) signals in 5G networks. However, the inter-core skew can introduce distortion in the radiation pattern, thereby affecting the overall system performance. To tackle this issue, we propose an efficient method for compensating for the differential delays in multicore fibers.

Our method focuses on reducing the inter-core skew by compensating for the differential delays, without the need for full equalization of transmission path lengths or increasing the system's complexity. By doing so, we can mitigate the power loss caused by the inter-core skew and improve the overall performance of the system.

In conclusion, our proposal offers a simple yet effective solution for compensating differential delays in multicore fibers for RoF transmission of mmwave signals.

The paper introduces an Efficient and Adaptive Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) for mitigating harmonics. The implementation of the ANN based reference current generation is carried out via Neural Synchronous method while training algorithm is achieved through the utilization of Levenberg Marquardt method. The paper also depicts the realization of ANN based Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (ANN-SVPWM) controller, which is essential for the effective control of SAPF. The performance of the proposed ANN-SVPWM controller is then compared with the conventional Hysteresis Current Controller (HCC). Therefore, both the reference compensating currents and controller of the proposed SAPF are realized using Artificial Neural Network. The simulation results obtained through MATLAB demonstrate the successful compensation of load harmonics and good dynamic response of the ANN based SAPF. Furthermore, the proposed SAPF successfully compensates the load harmonics in both steady state and dynamic conditions.

In outdoor vision systems, images taken by digital cameras can be significantly distorted by bad weather conditions, negatively affecting system performance. Rain is one such condition, randomly causing intensity fluctuations in images. A new low rank recovery based algorithm has been proposed to remove rain streaks from single images taken in rainy weather. This method uses weighted nuclear norm (WNN) and total variation (TV) regularization for efficient rain removal. WNN assigns different weights to different singular values based on the details each singular value holds, while TV regularization discriminates most of natural image content from sparse rain streaks by preserving piecewise smoothness of images. Simulation results illustrate that the rain streaks are more effectively eliminated by this method.

Heterogeneous architectures are commonplace in mobile platforms, where multiple processors are integrated alongside accelerators like GPUs and DSPs. However, this often results in the underutilization of resources like DSPs due to the strict partitioning of application execution. To address this issue, we conducted a case study using a mix of widely used data-parallel workloads (e.g. CNNs, computer vision filters, and graphics rendering kernels) on mobile devices. Our study demonstrates that by deploying underutilized compute resources synergistically, both performance and energy consumption of mobile platforms can be improved.

We executed our experiments on the Snapdragon 835 platform, both under single application and multiple application scenarios, demonstrating remarkable performance and energy improvements. Our results showed an average improvement in performance of 15-46%, and an average energy improvement of 18-80%, by deploying all available compute resources, particularly the underutilized DSP. 

Overall, our case study highlights the importance of leveraging underutilized compute resources in mobile platforms to improve performance and energy consumption. This can be achieved through the synergistic deployment of heterogeneous compute resources, thereby unlocking the full potential of mobile platforms.

In this digital age, it has become customary for consumers to read reviews before buying a product or service. The five-star rating system has made it much easier for consumers to get an idea of the quality of the product, instead of just having a good, neutral, or bad rating. However, it is common for a single review to contain both positive and negative comments, which can make it difficult to judge the overall sentiment. Additionally, the order in which the comments are presented can significantly affect the star rating. 

To address these concerns, we developed the STAR model, which takes into account the variations in sentiment in reviews to improve the accuracy of the star rating. Our approach uses a two-phase transfer learning framework to analyze the reviews, exploiting the variations in human emotions. 

We conducted experimental analyses and found that the STAR model outperforms other state-of-the-art models. By considering the subtle nuances in consumer feedback, our approach provides a more accurate measure of the quality of a product or service, helping consumers make more informed choices.

This paper presents a new event-triggered (ET) adaptive neural control approach for discrete-time nonlinear systems in strict-feedback form. Rather than relying on virtual control laws, the proposed recursive design process derives the ideal control input based solely on system states. High-order neural networks approximate this ideal input, and an adaptive neural controller is developed utilizing the event-triggering mechanism. To ensure uniformly ultimate boundedness (UUB) for all sampling times, a nonperiodically tuned NN weight updating law is employed. An ET condition is then constructed, which together with an adaptive ET threshold coefficient and a dead-zone operator, guarantees the UUB of the closed-loop networked control system based on Lyapunov stability theory. This significantly reduces network communication load since there is no need for intermediate ET conditions, computation of virtual control laws, or redundant triggering of events. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

Telemedicine offers a remote medical service that overcomes distance barriers and improves access to medical care in rural communities. With the advent of cloud computing, these services are now provided by Cloud Service Providers (CSPs), which connect patients and medical staff in different locations. However, outsourcing healthcare data to public cloud platforms poses the challenge of maintaining security. Although the Attribute-Based Encryption (ABE) algorithm offers flexible access control, the high number of patients subscribing and unsubscribing to different medical services incurs substantial membership management costs. In this article, we present an ABE scheme that achieves dynamic authentication and authorization for the MoD services in telemedicine with increased flexibility and efficiency. Our proposed independent-update key policy ABE scheme enables patients to update their keys separately, without requiring updating on parameters for others whose statuses remain unchanged. Moreover, we use blockchain and distributed database technologies to protect private healthcare data on public clouds, ensuring its integrity and avoiding misdiagnosis accidents caused by malicious users or authorities. We also analyze and formally prove the protocol's security in situations with multiple authorities, demonstrating better performance through comparison and simulation.

This article discusses computer modeling of radio systems and presents a method for automated solutions for direct and inverse problems of mathematical modeling of nonlinear radio engineering systems. Nonlinear radio engineering systems perform crucial signal generation and conversion operations such as amplification, modulation, detection, frequency multiplication, and conversion. The modeling of such systems is essential for improving the design and research efficiency. However, existing modeling systems are limited to a set of valid tasks and usually solve only direct problems. Therefore, there is a need for automated modeling systems that can solve various direct and inverse problems of systems modeling within a single program complex using elements of artificial intelligence, replacing the existing application packages.

To address this need, the article proposes a method to use functional grammars to construct an automated modeling system for nonlinear semiconductor systems. The scientific research result is the development of a logical-mathematical model using terms of functional context-free grammars, substantiated through a logical conclusion using lambda calculus. The practical application of the method is demonstrated through examples of solving direct and inverse modeling problems. By using this modeling method, radio engineers can improve the efficiency of their design and research and provides a more comprehensive range of solutions for direct and inverse problems of systems modeling.

Voice disorders, which can help in the diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD), can be measured with acoustic tools. In this work, demographic data and vocal phonation records /a/ from the available mPower database were analyzed to identify PD patients. A parsimonious model was then found that achieved a reduction from 62 to 5 phonation characteristics, which were considered in addition to gender and age. Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Logistic Regression (LR) neural networks were used to obtain a model with high prediction capacity (area under receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC-ROC, over 0.82). This work contributes to the monitoring of EP patients from the recording of a few phonation features collected by means of a mobile phone.

The analysis of genes expression data in large matrices poses challenges in terms of applying analytical methods, interpretation, and drawing conclusions. The goal of this study was to assess the accuracy of genes expression classification on different maize lines and organs (Apex, Root, Shoot, Ear, and Tassel) based on Maize Nested Association Mapping (NAM) datasets using the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) approach. The KNN analysis with k = 5 resulted in an accuracy value and AUC value of 0.926 and 0.992, respectively. Additionally, we demonstrated the classification of genes expression datasets for organ-specific expression differentiation.

Facial image kinship verification is a challenging topic in computer vision research, garnering increasing interest in recent years. While previous methods have not been strong enough to accurately predict kinship relationships based solely on facial appearance, we propose a new approach called Deep-Tensor+ELM. This method utilizes deep (VGG-Face descriptor) and tensor (BSIF-Tensor & LPQ-Tensor using MSIDA method) features through the implementation of Extreme Learning Machine (ELM). Our method accounts for the small size training feature dimension typical of kinship verification studies while also providing significant enhancement over shallow features or vector-based methods. We evaluated our approach using the largest kinship benchmark, the FIW database, and specifically focused on four Grandparent-Grandchild relations (GF-GD, GF-GS, GM-GD, and GM-GS). Our results demonstrate marked improvement compared to contemporary methods, even those that depend on deep learning.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a dynamic and large-scale infrastructure of uniquely identifiable, potentially resource-constrained, and heterogeneous devices. These devices are capable of sensing and influencing their environment to provide services with or without human intervention.
