Recent developments in communication technology have led to cloud resources becoming ubiquitous. These resources enable many new applications by offering computational power for remote embedded devices. In combination with advances in the area of smart driving, this seems to be especially beneficial for applications such as remote maintenance of vehicles or integration with smart city services. As autonomous driving continues to gain traction, Car-to-Cloud communication can support transferring collected data to the cloud, e.g., for dynamic learning of new map information. Additionally, passengers can benefit from novel entertainment services. All these developments require a stable connection between a mobile vehicle and the cloud resources. In this vision paper, we survey Car-to-Cloud communication applications. Based on the analysis of the varying requirements for these applications, we formulate research questions and challenges. Further, we discuss how these challenges can be addressed by means of an adaptive Car-to-Cloud communication middleware. We conclude with an overview on our activities in this area and an outlook on our planned future work on adaptive communication.

Background: Requirement prioritization plays key role in software development process. It is essential to prioritize the requirements for making the correct decision for either a single or multiple release of a product. In this paper we performed a systematic analysis on some of the significant factors like importance of requirements, risks, cost and time in context of requirement prioritization. Objective: With benefits these prioritization methods also have some limitations and shortcoming that are brought up in this paper. Stakeholders, managers, developers or their representatives make decisions for prioritization of requirements. Many techniques are analyzed how to manage these prioritizations considering general goals and limitations. Method: For the identification and analyzing of research articles published during 2009-2017, Systematic Literature Review based method is used in this paper. Results: In recent researches 40 different requirement prioritizations techniques has been used. This SLR also shows the major research gaps regarding techniques and tools for software requirements prioritization. Conclusion: This research shows the major prioritization techniques and tools for requirements elicitation. Tools & techniques identified in this study will assist future researchers to expend their views in the context. Moreover, it will help requirement engineers and practitioners to choose requirement prioritization techniques and tools according to their needs.

In this paper, we present a regression model to establish a relationship between knee joint angles and surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. Our proposed model consists of a wavelet coefficient correlation dimension (WCCD) feature extraction method and an Elman network for estimating the model. The experiment was conducted on five muscles that are responsible for knee joint motion, while the Codamotion system was used to record knee joint angles simultaneously. Firstly, we utilized the WCCD method for optimal feature extraction from the multichannel sEMG signals. Then, we used the Elman network to map these features to the knee joint angles. The findings indicate that the proposed WCCD method outperforms time-domain and frequency-domain methods. Consequently, our model has promising applications in intelligent prosthetics, exoskeleton robots, and medical rehabilitation robots.

This paper investigates the distributed recursive filtering problem for a type of discrete-time stochastic nonlinear systems subject to state delays as well as the communication topology of geographically distributed wireless sensors. The Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy model is introduced to deal with nonlinearities in system states and measurements. In the simultaneous consideration of system nonlinearities, state delays as well as topology, we aim to obtain a set of filter parameters over a finite-time horizon, minimizing the traces of permitted upper bounds for the filtering error covariance matrices. Via elaborate mathematical analysis, two sets of filter gains are derived in virtue of solving two Riccati-type difference equations, which are dependent on the latest estimation states and are with the online recursive form. In the end, the validity of the designed scheme is illustrated by an inverted pendulum system.

This paper presents a new technique based on nonlinear least square (NLSQ) algorithm for estimating the mean curve and parameters of the standard lightning impulse (LI) waveform as required by IEC 60 and IEEE Std. 4. The proposed NLSQ technique is applied to analytical LI waveforms to estimate the mean curve of the impulse using a bi-exponential model after removing high frequency components from the simulated (measured) impulse. The effectiveness of the proposed technique is assessed by conducting several cases of LI impulse waveforms with front and tail oscillations and LI waveform with overshoot. The results of the NLSQ technique are compared with those obtained by the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The simulation results show that the proposed NLSQ technique is robust and effective in estimating the peak value, front and tail times of the impulse waveform accurately.

The present scientific attempt is devoted to investigating the fuzzy nonconvex optimization problems (NCOPs) utilizing the concepts of recurrent neural networks (RNNs). To the best of our knowledge, this paper is the first study on finding a solution for fuzzy NCOP using RNN models. For this purpose, the original problem is reformulated into an mth power form, the interval, and then the weighting problem. Then, the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions are provided for the weighting problem. The KKT conditions are used to propose the RNN model. Besides, the Lyapunov stability and the global convergence of the RNN model are proved. Finally, several illustrative examples are given to demonstrate the performance of this approach. The obtained results are compared with previous approaches for solving fuzzy NCOP.

Blockchain and smart contract technology provide a means of decentralised computational agreements that are trusted and automated. By integrating Internet of Things (IoT) devices with blockchain systems and smart contracts, agreements can not only be confined to in-blockchain manipulation of state, however can enable agreements to interact on the physical world. This integration is non-trivial due to the limited resources on IoT devices and the heterogeneity of such an architecture. Such blockchain connected IoT devices typically require programming of smart contracts, edge blockchain nodes and the IoT devices. IoT embedded systems require expertise in low level development. Similarly, smart contract programming requires expertise with an extensive attention to detail, as even minor bugs can have catastrophic consequences. In this paper, we propose a macroprogramming approach for developing the different system components required for blockchain connected IoT devices including smart contracts, edge nodes and IoT devices from a monolithic description. In this manner, one can use a higher level of abstraction to develop an application, while still being able to generate code automatically which can be deployed on different nodes.

The internet of Things (IoT) architecture was originally envisaged as a two-layer technical platform, with sensors collecting data at the edge with minimal compute requirements, solely to prepare and transporting the data to a centralized or cloud based infrastructure for processing. This model is suitable in some scenarios, for example where data is being stored for historical, regulatory or trending usage however in other use cases such as health monitoring for acute illness or autonomous vehicle computer vision the latency in transporting this data to a remote location for processing may cause latencies that would seriously affect performance of the application. There are many different and sometimes overlapping definitions of IoT topologies being discussed within industry. This paper reviews this original topology of an IoT solution, and different techniques and layers available to alleviate the issues inherent of the original paradigm, and how a new method of defining at these topologies is gaining speed.

IBM's brain-inspired processor is a massively parallel neural network inference engine containing 1 million spiking neurons and 256 million low-precision synapses. Now, after a decade of fundamental research spanning neuroscience, architecture, chips, systems, software, and algorithms, IBM has delivered the largest neurosynaptic computer ever built.

This paper proposes a novel event-triggered (ET) adaptive neural control scheme for a class of discrete-time nonlinear systems in a strict-feedback form. In the proposed scheme, the ideal control input is derived in a recursive design process, which relies on system states only and is unrelated to virtual control laws. In this case, the high-order neural networks (NNs) are used to approximate the ideal control input (but not the virtual control laws), and then the corresponding adaptive neural controller is developed under the ET mechanism. A modified NN weight updating law, nonperiodically tuned at triggering instants, is designed to guarantee the uniformly ultimate boundedness (UUB) of NN weight estimates for all sampling times. In virtue of the bounded NN weight estimates and a dead-zone operator, the ET condition together with an adaptive ET threshold coefficient is constructed to guarantee the UUB of the closed-loop networked control system through the Lyapunov stability theory, thereby largely easing the network communication load. The proposed ET condition is easy to implement because of the avoidance of: 1) the use of the intermediate ET conditions in the backstepping procedure; 2) the computation of virtual control laws; and 3) the redundant triggering of events when the system states converge to a desired region. The validity of the presented scheme is demonstrated by simulation results.

Due to its lightweight features, the combination of container technology and microservice architecture offers a more efficient and agile cloud environment compared to VM-based environments. However, the dynamism and complexity of container-based environments also increases the uncertainty of security issues, resulting in an effectiveness drift problem for defense mechanisms, particularly proactive mechanisms like moving target defense (MTD). To address this issue, we propose the DSEOM framework, which automatically perceives updates in the cloud environment, rapidly evaluates the effectiveness change of MTD, and dynamically optimizes MTD strategies. We establish a multi-dimensional attack graph model to formalize complex attack scenarios and introduce the concept of betweenness centrality to evaluate and optimize MTD implementation strategies. We also present security and performance metrics to quantify the effectiveness of MTD strategies in DSEOM and conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate its usability and scalability.

While the path-loss models of propagating wireless signals may provide different results if they are employed in an environment that differs from the original settings that they were structured for, their formulation may also become irrelevant as a result of topographic and rapid civil growth of urbanization. In this paper, we analyze the aging effect in path-loss models of wireless signal propagation in a deployed 3G network. The study utilizes measurement data form a first-phase roll-out in 2010 in Amman, Jordan to conduct comparative analysis in conjunction with the data of a similar measurement campaign in 2018 in the same area of interest. Machine Learning (ML) techniques, including Artificial Neural Networks and Decision Trees classifiers, were utilized to uncover and verify the age progression of the environment on path-loss modeling. The collected measurements are then compared to the Log-distance propagation model. ML classification algorithms proved to be a powerful tool for analysis through numerical results in verifying these progression trends.

This paper introduces an innovative software designed to visually showcase the physical burden on the human body during movement. The primary purpose of this software is to aid factory workers by tracking the risk of physical health issues like low back pain. The software incorporates wearable sensors such as IMUs to monitor the measurement process at a work-site while real-time musculoskeletal computations provide various physical information such as joint angles, joint torques, muscle tensions, and joint reaction forces. The software integrated with an ergonomic assessment software DhaibaWorks records and plots musculoskeletal data on a visualization interface.

In this paper, we propose a new learning architecture named cosine activation in a compact network (CACN). The CACN is derived from kernel approximation and establishes a nonlinear hidden layer with the cosine activation function. By inheriting fusion ability in kernel approximation while learning parameters in a supervised way, the CACN is a well-directed solution to scene classification. By seamlessly connecting with convolutional neural networks (CNNs), it is easy to construct an end-to-end network. To compensate for the loss of spatial layout information in CNNs, the CACN is further combined with spatial pyramid matching to fuse various information into one holistic picture. The experiments on the MIT indoor and SUN397 datasets show that the CACN delivers high performance and demonstrates its great effectiveness for scene-classification tasks.

Recently the high-order multiple-history long short-time memory (MH-LSTM) is proposed for speech recognition. The high-order connections to an MH-LSTM cell come from signals similar to the original one but running with progressively longer time lags. Each time-lagged signal keeps a slightly different history of the input, and the history ensemble helps improve the model's robustness against mis-labeling or mis-alignments in the training targets. When an MH-LSTM cell is unfolded in time, it becomes a deep neural network with wider and wider layers towards the inputs. Although a wider MH-LSTM is more resilient to noisy data, we notice that when it is too wide, it is easily under-trained and the increased history/input contexts are not effectively utilized. In this paper, LSTMs are replaced by the faster simple recurrent units (SRUs), which remove the dependency on the hidden states of an MH-LSTM, and high-order connections are instead directly applied to the inputs of an MH-SRU. The high-order connections are further modeled by a WaveNet block which makes use of dilated causal convolution to provide a wider receptive field more effectively. Experimental results on NTIMIT and CHiME-2 demonstrate the effectiveness of the new WaveNet MH-SRU. For example, on CHiME-2, it achieves 1.8% and 0.6% absolute WER reductions over the SRU and MH-SRU baseline models that have similar number of model parameters.

Edge computing systems allow for data analytics applications to be performed within one-hop wireless distances from mobile devices. By utilizing proximal mobile edge servers for data analytics applications opportunistically, network latency can be minimized, the need for internet connectivity can be reduced, and the cost of using cloud services can be decreased. This paper details various experimental evaluations that were conducted to assess the feasibility of using mobile edge servers in an opportunistic manner. Additionally, the paper identifies key challenges and suggests directions for future research in this area.

Single-stream recycling poses a significant challenge as object sorting is a labor-intensive task that requires manual handling. Soft robotics provides a promising solution since compliant robots need less computational power to navigate and grasp objects in a cluttered environment. However, most soft robots are not robust enough to handle the many sharp and hazardous objects present in a recycling facility.

To address this challenge, a team of researchers has developed a soft sensorized robotic gripper that is fully electrically driven and can differentiate between paper, metal, and plastic. The gripper employs handed shearing auxetics with high deformation capacitive pressure and strain sensors, presenting a new puncture-resistant design.

The research team found that their materials classifier has an accuracy rate of 85% with a stationary gripper and 63% accuracy in a simulated recycling pipeline. This classifier can handle various objects, including those that might mislead a purely vision-based system.

This new soft sensorized robotic gripper offers a natural solution to the challenges posed by single-stream recycling, reducing the labor involved in manual object sorting. The gripper's resistance to sharp and hazardous objects makes it a promising solution in creating a safer and more efficient recycling process.

In this study, we present a new framework for equipment development called "Automatic Ladder Training". Our equipment improves upon traditional agility ladder training by incorporating image processing techniques. Ladder training is essential for athletes to improve their physical fitness, but traditional methods require an instructor or coach to record the athletes' training results, which can be costly and time-consuming. Our framework addresses these issues by performing three distinct steps. 

First, it extracts features of binary images and detects objective pixels from the trainees' feet. This allows us to accurately track foot movements during training. Second, our equipment uses perspective transform to visualize a real ladder and adjust its alignment to match the trainee's movements. Finally, our equipment records the start and end of training time by tracking the pixels of the athlete's feet entering and leaving the ladder area. 

To ensure the reliability of our framework, we tested our equipment using 240 videos containing 400 Thai youths. We compared our results to those of humans and found that our accuracy and achievement were comparable. With our framework, athletes can train more effectively and coaches can save time and resources by eliminating the need for manual record-keeping.

Speaker recognition is a technique used to automatically recognize a speaker from a recording of their voice or speech utterance. Speaker recognition technology has improved over recent years and has become inexpensive and and reliable method for person identification and verification. Research in the field of speaker recognition has now spanned over five decades and has shown fruitful results, however there is not much work done with regards to South African indigenous languages. This paper presents the development of an automatic speaker recognition system that incorporates classification and recognition of Sepedi home language speakers. Four classifier models, namely, Support Vector Machines, K-Nearest Neighbors, Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) and Random Forest (RF), are trained using WEKA data mining tool. Auto-WEKA is applied to determine the best classifier model together with its best hyper-parameters. The performance of each model is evaluated in WEKA using 10-fold cross validation. MLP and RF yielded good accuracy surpassing the state-of-the-art with an accuracy of 97% and 99.9% respectively, the RF model is then implemented on a graphical user interface for development testing.

Arabic is a language that has a highly complicated morphological structure and is highly inflected, which makes it difficult for stemming mechanisms to be developed, especially for dialectal Arabic. Unlike standard Arabic, dialectal Arabic does not conform to standard Arabic grammar rules for term conflation and affix attachment. In this study, a new stemmer was proposed that integrates two techniques that can be used to stem Saudi words - the Information Science Research Institute (ISRI) Arabic stemmer and a rule-based stemmer developed in-house. The stemming approach was applied to a corpus that was collected from Saudi dialect tweets, and the results showed improved stemming accuracy compared to existing techniques.

Microgrids are small-scale electric power systems that emerge as an alternative to solve the current problems of conventional networks. The main objectives that they pursue are the reliability, diversification of energy resources, reduction of carbon emissions, minimization of costs and the introduction of intelligent control techniques, which increase the dependence on communication networks. Some research related to communications in electrical networks has been developed, but few are related to the appropriate communication system, according to the control algorithm. This paper proposes the best architecture for intelligent microgrid applications based on latency, QoS, bandwidth and capital cost, to improve control and operation. In addition, the fundamentals of communications and control strategies are described. The results show that communication technology affects the control performance of intelligent applications and the smartness of the grid, which causes poor quality of service. This analysis is very useful for the grid planning and the developers, who can select the appropriate architecture according to their needs.

Nowadays, the construction industry is facing numerous challenges, with one of the key concerns being the management of construction and demolition waste. This waste poses a threat to the environment and requires significant financial resources to be properly handled. However, considering all the contributing attributes for waste management is beyond the limits of human capacity. Therefore, there is a dire need for artificial intelligence (AI) to help direct waste management efforts. The generation of construction and demolition (C&D) waste is inevitable, and waste management is always a challenge for managers, requiring technical expertise and substantial resources for proper waste control. This paper aims to develop a conceptual framework for an effective construction waste management system (EMS) using AI technology. The proposed EMS will help construction practitioners to determine the most suitable, viable, feasible and economical waste management technique, based on the type and capacity of waste produced. A comprehensive review of waste generation attributes, waste management techniques, and adaptability and feasibility is carried out to identify loopholes and limitations of each method. By implementing this AI-based approach, it is hoped that the construction industry can address the challenges of construction and demolition waste management in a more efficient and sustainable manner.

We have conducted a study on the recently proposed cell-free massive multiple input multiple output (MIMO) architecture for the uplink. In this study, we have focused on joint detection using global channel state information (CSI), which is different from most previous works. Our aim was to develop strategies for transferring CSI to the central processing unit with consideration of the fronthaul capacity. As CSI quantization is limited by the fronthaul capacity, we have considered two pilot-based CSI acquisition strategies: estimate-and-quantize and quantize-and-estimate. To analyze these strategies, we have used the Bussgang decomposition.

Our primary goal was to determine the achievable rate per user with zero forcing for a given quantization constraint for the data and CSI. We have found that quantize-and-estimate strategy is similar to or better than estimate-and-quantize at low resolution, especially for 1-bit.

Our numerical results provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of different strategies for pilot-based CSI acquisition in cell-free massive MIMO systems. We believe that our study will contribute to the development of more efficient and effective massive MIMO architectures for uplink communication.

This paper investigates the control design for a type of linear systems using a stochastic hybrid framework. The system is subject to external disturbances, which are modeled by stochastic differential equations. The control law is calculated based on state feedback and is applied randomly at discrete time intervals. However, uncertainties in the control law may exist due to factors such as faulty actuators or system noise.

To address this issue, we derive exact solutions for the first two moments of the system and use them to determine the stability conditions. We also design a control law that steers the system to the desired mean and variance. Moreover, we demonstrate that randomness in the application times of the control law can even decrease the variability caused by disturbances under certain conditions.

Finally, we explore the trade-off between stability and achievable mean and variance. We find that the system can be steered to any mean value without violating stability conditions. This study provides insights into designing control laws for linear systems that are subject to external disturbances, which can be useful in practical applications.

Aiming at the problem of cooperative localization of swarm UAVs in complex flight environment, a cooperative positioning algorithm of swarm UAVs based on posterior linearization belief propagation is proposed. According to the belief propagation algorithm, the cooperative localization of drones using belief propagation is proposed. To deal with the contradiction between positioning accuracy and computational complexity, statistical linear regression is used to design the posterior linearization method of measurement model, and the linearized measurement model is used on the algorithm framework of cooperative positioning which is based on belief propagation. Finally, simulation comparison analysis is carried out for different algorithms. The simulation results show that, compared with the non-cooperative case, the proposed algorithm improves the positioning accuracy of the follower UAVs in X, Y and Z directions (earth-centered earth-fixed coordinate system, ECEF) by 8.9, 13.9, 17.3 times respectively.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for accurately extracting the unknown parameters of a single-diode photovoltaic (PV) cell model under changing weather conditions. The proposed approach involves the implementation of an adaptive wind-driven optimization (AWDO) algorithm, which is a new and improved version of the wind-driven optimization algorithm. One of the key advantages of the AWDO algorithm is its ability to effectively handle complex multi-modal and multi-dimensional optimization problems.

Additionally, the paper presents a generalization model to extend the application of the proposed methodology to any I-V characteristic curve of PV cells and weather condition on a 15-minute time interval. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology is validated through comprehensive testing of 1307 I-V characteristic curves of a PV module under various weather conditions using both simulation and outdoor measurements. 

Moreover, the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed methodology are compared with five other well-known extraction methods, such as Villalva's model, particle swarm optimization, biogeography-based optimization, Gang's model, and bacterial foraging optimization. Results show that the AWDO algorithm outperforms these methods in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy of parameter extraction. 

Therefore, the proposed methodology (AWDO based on Chenlo's model) can be recommended as a reliable, feasible, valuable, and fast optimization algorithm for accurately extracting the unknown parameters of a single-diode PV cell model, even under changing weather conditions.

Motion mass based approach is adopted in this paper to describe gait movements of patients with Parkinson's disease. In spite of the recent advances in the areas of motion capture and motion analysis, medical community remains sceptical about applying computer aided systems to support modelling and diagnostics of the Parkinson's disease. The set of measurable parameters is limited by the time, step lengths and in some cases angles between the limbs. To complement these data, motion mass parameters describing amount and smoothness of the motions, are computed for each step. Decision tree classifiers a trained to distinguish between the gait motions of patients with diagnosed Parkinson's disease and healthy individuals of the same age. Moreover it is demonstrated that inclusion of the time does not increase model quality.

This paper introduces a new backup resource allocation model for virtual networks that provides probabilistic protection against multiple facility node failures through joint consideration of backup computing and bandwidth resource allocation. Unlike previous work that only considers backup computing resource allocation, this proposed model takes into account the constraints from network aspects. 

The paper analyzed the types of backup paths necessary for each virtual link in the event of multiple facility node failures, and identified the substrate link capacity constraints and flow constraints for backup paths, which highlight the interactions between backup computing and bandwidth resource allocation. The model determined the routings of backup paths when the backup computing resource allocation was decided. 

Using robust optimization and multiple mathematical operations, the proposed model was formulated as a mixed integer linear programming problem with the objective of minimizing the total required backup computing capacity. Finally, the optimal backup resource allocations for a sample cloud provider were presented, considering and not considering the constraints from network aspects. 

In conclusion, the proposed model provides a more comprehensive backup resource allocation approach that takes into account network constraints, leading to more effective and reliable protection against facility node failures in virtual networks.

Advances in IoT and cloud computing are revolutionizing industrial control system architecture, transforming them from isolated to decentralized structures. However, this change also leads to increased complexity, exposing the systems to cyber threats from the cloud and control environment. To secure these systems, different cybersecurity standards have been proposed based on a set of security requirements. Unfortunately, these requirements are often specified in natural language, making formal verification of security properties against the standards challenging. 

This paper proposes a framework for formally verifying compliance with the IEC-62443-3-3 standard for cloud-connected SCADA systems. The proposed framework models the system and the security requirements using a formal modeling language called TLA+. The model is then verified for compliance with the standard using the TLC model checker. The technique is demonstrated using an industrial case study, proving the applicability of the approach.

Multi-oriented text detection is a difficult task due to various challenges such as differing scales, orientations, illumination, and languages. Traditional anchor mechanisms used for object detection cannot generate proposals for multi-oriented text regions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a convolutional regression network (CRN) which has two components: region proposal extractor and text locator. The approach includes a hierarchical deconvolution module (HDM) and a text-line and geometry segmentation module (TGM) which use fully convolutional networks to accurately segment multi-oriented proposals. This is followed by a classification and regression module (CRM) which processes proposals to obtain the final localization results. The proposed method can be trained end-to-end and shows promising results on three mainstream scene-text datasets.

Vector fields play an essential role in a large range of scientific applications. They are commonly generated through computer simulations. Such simulations may be a costly process since they usually require an intensive computational time. When researchers want to quantify the uncertainty in such kind of applications, usually an ensemble of vector fields realizations are generated, making the process much more expensive. The main contribution of this paper is to present a new method, based on the inverse projection technique, to quickly and consistently generate 2D vector fields similar to the ones in the ensemble, which after an evaluation of a specialist could enlarge the ensemble in order to better represent the uncertainty. Through the Helmholtz-Hodge Decomposition, we obtain the divergence-free, rotational-free and harmonic components of a vector field. With those components and the original ensemble in hand, it is possible to derive new realizations from their projections into a 2-dimensional space. To do so, we propose the use of an inverse projection technique individually in each component projected space. Results are obtained in real-time, through an interactive interface. A set of multi-method wind forecast realizations were used to demonstrate the results obtained with this approach.

Fuzzy Co-Clustering induced by Multinomial Mixture models (FCCMM) is a reliable approach for analyzing object-item co-occurrence based on document-keyword frequencies and customer-product purchase history transactions. However, dealing with co-occurrence datasets that are stored as large matrices with conventional batch algorithms is difficult. For effective big data analysis, Online algorithms that adjust parameters on a single object sequentially, and mini-batch algorithms that adjust parameters on a small chunk (mini-batch) of objects sequentially are promising alternatives. 

In this study, we have proposed two approaches - an online algorithm and a mini-batch algorithm - for FCCMM clustering. We have also conducted a series of numerical experiments to observe their characteristics and performances. Our comprehensive analysis demonstrates that both the online and mini-batch algorithms effectively handle large datasets. 

Overall, our study showcases the efficiency and reliability of FCCMM clustering schemes, which are essential for analyzing co-occurrence based data. Our proposed online and mini-batch algorithms have the potential to solve problems with conventional batch algorithms and will be of significant value to researchers and industry for big data analysis.

Minimizing power consumption in always-on sensors is essential to extend the battery life of devices that continuously monitor events for extended periods. This study presents a novel programmable μW event-driven acoustic detector that employs "always-on" audio pattern recognition. The event-driven detector can detect up to eight spectral-temporal features using a low-power single-channel analog circuit and classify the features by an onboard microcontroller. The detector is combined with microbial fuel cells (MFCs) to achieve self-sustaining monitoring in an underwater scenario. Results show that the detector's power consumption is only 26.89 μW during always-on mode, with a sensitivity up to 59-dB sound pressure level. An accuracy of up to 95.89% in recognizing acoustic patterns has been confirmed experimentally. Accurate measurements using commercial MFCs have demonstrated the detector's ability to achieve self-sustainability in always-on monitoring.

This paper covers the development of quantitative metrics for the automatic recognition of exercise types in a system designed for remote monitoring of the physical rehabilitation process. The aim of this study is to develop metrics that can accurately estimate the performance accuracy of physical exercises. These metrics will provide quantitative characteristics of treatment protocol fulfillment accuracy, thereby increasing the objectivity and reliability of remote control. 

In order to achieve this, the paper proposes the use of an algorithm called time scale warping, with additional metrics that localize function properties to the minimum warping path. The scientific novelty presented in this study is a method for remotely quantifying exercise performance correctness, which is based on the comparison of trajectories using the DWT metric. 

Furthermore, this paper includes additional metrics that expand the capabilities of DWT in localizing trajectory changes. Overall, these metrics will enhance the accuracy and reliability of remote monitoring for physical rehabilitation, providing valuable data for healthcare professionals to measure performance and adjust treatment protocols accordingly.

To handle missing attributes when acquiring knowledge from data in real-world problems, this paper proposes XCS for Missing Attributes in Data (XCS-MA). XCS-MA complements the value of the missing attributes of the input data and estimates the correct output for its complemented input. If the correct output is the same for all possible complemented inputs, XCS-MA uses the missing attribute data for the learning. In experiments, XCS-MA correctly estimated the accuracy of the classifiers (represented by the if-then rules) and acquired the optimal classifier subset in the 11-Multiplexer problem with the missing attributes. Once the optimal classifier subset is acquired, XCS-MA selects the correct output for any input even if many missing attributes are included in the data.

Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) has become a vital tool for power systems monitoring and protection purposes. Power systems state estimation (SE) can be done with the help of synchro-phasor measurements which requires complete observability of the system through PMUs. A new algorithm based on maximum connectivity of buses to lines has been suggested in this paper to find out optimal locations and number of PMUs in normal condition, in addition to several contingencies like single or double PMU failures and also single line outages. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm has been evaluated by testing it on IEEE 6, 14, 30, 57, 118 bus test systems, as well as Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) 38 bus practical system. Further, a new state estimation algorithm has also been proposed in this paper which utilizes the measurements from optimally placed PMUs in the aforesaid manner. For completeness, this algorithm also incorporates a method for detection and identification of bad data. The test results presented reveal the effectiveness of the proposed methods for online application.

In the last fifteen years, physical unclonable functions (PUFs) have been introduced as a promising tool for hardware security applications. Despite the ongoing race between complex PUF architectures and new attack schemes to break their security, some delay-based PUF architectures, such as double arbiter PUFs (DA-PUFs), remain unbroken against modeling attacks utilizing conventional machine learning techniques. These stronger complex PUFs have the potential to be a candidate for key generation and authentication applications.

This paper presents an in-depth analysis of modeling attack using deep learning (DL) techniques against DA-PUFs. The results of DL show enhanced prediction accuracy of the attacked DA-PUFs, thus pushing up the boundaries of modeling attacks to break more complex architectures. The attack on 3-1 DAPUFs has improved accuracy of over 86% (compared to previous research achieving a maximum of 76%), and the 4-1 DAPUFs accuracy ranges between 71%-81.5% (compared to previous research of maximum 63%). This research is crucial for analyzing the security of existing and future PUF architectures, confirming that as DL computations become more widely accessible, designers will need to hide the PUFs CRP relationship from attackers.

In this paper, we propose an objective function for the convolutional neural network to acquire the variation separability as opposed to the categorical cross entropy which maximizes according to the target labels. This approach is an unsupervised learning method which tends to separate the classes according to their variation in the subspace. Finally, the features extracted are classified using support vector machines (SVM). The deep representative features from the CNN are directly from the data, and thus additionally increase the variance between the images making it more discriminative. The idea is to build a CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) and perform the principal component analysis on top of this while training it in an end-to-end fashion. The backpropagation is done to update the parameters according to the eigen representation of the training data. Experimental results on the widely used MEDNODE database which consists of clinical (non-dermoscopic) images shows that our approach is efficient for the classification of melanoma skin cancer detection task.

In this paper, we introduce an innovative autonomous vision-based power line inspection system that utilizes unmanned aerial vehicle inspection as the main inspection method, optical images as the primary data source, and deep learning as the core of the data analysis. To implement the system effectively, we tackle three major challenges of deep learning in vision-based power line inspection, namely the scarcity of training data, class imbalance, and detection of small components and faults. 

Initially, we establish four medium-sized datasets for training component detection and classification models. Additionally, we employ several data augmentation techniques to balance out the imbalanced classes effectively. Lastly, we propose the multi-stage component detection and classification using the Single Shot Multibox detector and deep Residual Networks, targeting the identification of small components and faults. 

The results exhibited that the proposed system is fast and precise in identifying common faults on power line components, including missing top caps, cracks in poles and cross arms, woodpecker damage on poles, and rot damage on cross arms. The field tests indicate that our system holds great potential in intelligent monitoring and inspection of power line components and serves as a valuable addition to smart grids.

A nonlinear dynamic emergency public event information diffusion system and mathematical model for public events are proposed based on the propagation dynamics. First, public emergency information communication is analyzed and designed, the opinion evolution is divided into and the viewpoint of value, influence, interest, conformity, intimacy five factors of information diffusion for public emergencies; second, the dynamic diffusion network is designed; information propagation mathematical public emergencies the final model is constructed; the proposed model and social reality and the true statistics of empirical experiments are simulated and analyzed. The experimental results show that the model and the real emergency public event propagation process are consistent, the development trend can predict public events, and the proposed mathematical model is reasonable and effective.

Mission Critical Services (MCS) have recently garnered the attention of network operators who are looking to offer communications beyond the traditional trunked radio systems. These services simplify the management of cloud and radio resources for service deployment. However, it is important to adapt network capabilities to ensure low-latency and high reliability for these applications. 

This paper discusses an ongoing effort to utilize 5G technology for Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) services. The paper outlines various design elements and evaluates the 5G ESSENCE architecture, which is specifically designed to support mission critical applications. 

Through this research, network operators hope to offer more reliable and efficient communication services for mission-critical applications. By leveraging the advancements in 5G technology, network operators can better serve first responders, emergency workers, and other organizations that depend on reliable and fast communications.

The detection of nodal road network features in remote sensing imagery is a crucial task with various applications. It enables the tracking of urban sprawl, updating and validating maps, and evaluating macro-scale infrastructure damage. To perform this task successfully, we created a unique dataset containing nodal road network features such as bridges, cul-de-sacs, freeway exchanges and exits, freeway overpasses, intersections, and traffic circles. We then used deep machine learning techniques to recognize these features across two variations of the image datasets, expanded versus semantically coalesced classes. Two deep convolutional neural networks, ResNet50 and Xception, were evaluated to detect these features, and class-specific data augmentation was employed to enhance the performance of the models trained for nodal road network feature recognition.

When evaluated on four variations of the nodal road network feature dataset, the models produced F1 scores ranging from 0.81 to 0.96. We observed that coalescing highly specific, semantically challenging classes into more generalized classes had a significant impact on the models' accuracy. Our analysis provides insight into how these techniques can improve the performance of machine learning models, making them applicable to broad area imagery analysis in a multitude of application domains.

This paper focuses on the development of a method for classifying English and Russian texts into positive, negative, and neutral sentiments. The proposed technique utilizes the Multinomial Naive Bayes classifier, together with the application of additional n-grams. The classifier can be trained on either three classes, or two contrasting classes with a threshold to distinguish neutral texts. In various experiments conducted across different topics, the classification quality of reviews from a particular domain has been found to be significantly improved. Furthermore, the application of thesaurus relationships to sentiment classification into three classes was also analyzed; however, it did not show any significant improvement in the classification results.

In-memory computing has emerged as a promising solution to address the logic-memory performance gap. We propose design techniques using monolithic-3D integration to achieve reliable multirow activation which in turn help in computation as part of data readout. Our design is 1.8x faster than the existing techniques for Boolean computations. We quantitatively show no impact to cell stability when multiple rows are activated and thereby requiring no extra hardware for maintaining the cell stability during computations. In-memory digital to analog conversion technique is proposed using a 3D-CAM primitive. The design utilizes relatively low strength layer-2 transistors effectively and provides 7x power savings when compared with a specialized converter in-memory. Lastly, we present a linear classifier system by making use the above-mentioned techniques which is 47x faster while computing vector matrix multiplication using a dedicated hardware engine.

In this paper are analyzed the main methods of wireless transmission of electrical energy, as well as their applications. For the beginning, there is a brief history of the development of the wireless electric power transmission technology. There are presented the principles of functioning of the main methods of wireless transmission of electrical energy, as well as the technical problems that need to be solved in the future. There are also presented the main applications of this technology, as well as the main companies that produce commercial wireless electrical power transmission equipment. Finally, we present the future opportunities of these wireless power transmission technologies and recommendations for future research topics in this field.

The millimeter-wave (mmWave) bands present a wide range of possibilities for fifth-generation cellular networks, offering multi-gigabit-per-second data rates. However, these high-frequency signals are susceptible to blockages and delays, resulting in highly variable links. This variability poses unique challenges for adaptive control mechanisms in transport layer protocols and end-to-end applications. One of the most widely used transport protocols, TCP, may face difficulties in operating in mmWave cellular systems. 

To address this issue, a comprehensive simulation study was conducted considering various factors such as congestion control algorithm, edge vs. remote servers, handover and multi-connectivity, TCP packet size, and 3GPP stack parameters. The study found that the performance of TCP on mmWave links is highly dependent on the combination of these parameters. Furthermore, the study identified open challenges in this area, highlighting the need for further research.

In conclusion, while the mmWave bands offer significant potential for fifth-generation cellular networks, challenges remain in ensuring the reliable operation of transport protocols such as TCP. Further research is necessary to address these challenges and fully realize the potential of mmWave technology.

The high-impedance faults (HIF) occurring on distribution lines go undetected by the conventional relays due to their low current magnitude. In addition to low current, HIFs also exhibit typical characteristic features, such as randomness, nonlinearity, etc., which are similar to the characteristics of the switching events, such as harmonic load switching. The advent of distributed generators (DG) into the distribution system, changes the current contribution through the substation, which also affects the HIF detection. This paper presents an intelligent HIF detection technique for distribution lines incorporating the DGs. Variational mode decomposition (VMD) is used to extract the input patterns. The commonly used empirical mode decomposition has limitation of modal aliasing that is overcome by VMD. VMD decomposes the signal into different modes that are further converted to singular values so as to obtain the analytic signal. These are finally used as an input to an efficient classifier known as the support vector machine, to create an intelligent classifier. The proposed methodology is verified on a modified IEEE 13-bus feeder for various events considering the changes in DG parameters and also the noise levels.

Integrating low-power profile networks, such as LPWAN (Low Power Wide Area Network) and WPAN (Wireless Personal Area Networks), will economically enable new IoT (Internet of Things) applications for SC (Smart Cities). The technologies LPWAN LoRA and WPAN BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy) are found in low-cost devices making use of unlicensed frequencies. The merge of their features would allow the emergence of applications that transmit long-range data (up to 45 km) using low energy consumption, low manufacturing cost, and simplified implementation, eliminating mobile operators dependence. In this work, we integrate LPWAN and WPAN using LoRa and BLE in a paradigm of Fog/Edge Computing, allowing the execution of the procedures at the edges of the network, making possible the transmission of only consolidated data to the cloud. We implemented a LoRa-BLE testbed using Lopy4 - Pycon, and simulated SC scenarios using LoRaSim. The set of results obtained by the testbed and the simulation allows us to evaluate the viability of merge LoRa-BLE to IoT SC applications.

Starting from our previous research where we in- troduced a general framework for supporting data-driven privacy-preserving big data management in distributed environments, such as emerging Cloud settings, in this paper we further and significantly extend our past research contributions, and provide several novel contributions that complement our previous work in the investigated research field. Our proposed framework can be viewed as an alternative to classical approaches where the privacy of big data is ensured via security-inspired protocols that check several (protocol) layers in order to achieve the desired privacy. Unfortunately, this injects considerable computational overheads in the overall process, thus introducing relevant challenges to be considered. Our approach instead tries to recognize the “pedigree” of suitable summary data representatives computed on top of the target big data repositories, hence avoiding computational overheads due to protocol checking. We also provide a relevant realization of the framework above, the so- called Data-dRIven aggregate-PROvenance privacy-preserving big Multidimensional data (DRIPROM) framework, which specifically considers multidimensional data as the case of interest. Extensions and discussion on main motivations and principles of our proposed research, two relevant case studies that clearly state the need-for and covered (related) properties of supporting privacy- preserving management and analytics of big data in modern distributed systems, and an experimental assessment and analysis of our proposed DRIPROM framework are the major results of this paper.

Numerous models of slip-ring induction motor (SRIM) can be found in literature. However, this paper presents new extended state-space SRIM models developed using reference frame theory. The focus of this study is on the effectiveness of these models in detecting rotor turn-to-turn short-circuit faults, which requires distinct residuals to be generated. A discriminatory ability index is proposed to compare the performance of different models and identify the most suitable one. Calculations are carried out for a 4-hp four-pole SRIM using MATLAB software, and simulation results are presented to validate the proposed index.

Network Function Virtualization (NFV) has been emerging as an appealing solution that transforms from dedicated hardware implementations to software instances running in a virtualized environment. In NFV, the requested service is implemented by a sequence of Virtual Network Functions (VNF) that can run on generic servers by leveraging the virtualization technology. These VNFs are pitched with a predefined order, and it is also known as the Service Function Chaining (SFC). Considering that the delay and resiliency are two important Service Level Agreements (SLA) in a NFV service, in this paper, we first investigate how to quantitatively model the traversing delay of a flow in both totally ordered and partially ordered SFCs. Subsequently, we study how to calculate the VNF placement availability mathematically for both unprotected and protected SFCs. After that, we study the delay-sensitive Virtual Network Function placement and routing problem with and without resiliency concerns. We prove that this problem is NP-hard under two cases. We subsequently propose an exact Integer Nonlinear Programming (INLP) formulation and an efficient heuristic for this problem in each case. Finally, we evaluate the proposed algorithms in terms of acceptance ratio, average number of used nodes and total running time via extensive simulations.

In this letter, a direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation method for the uniform-circular array (UCA) in the presence of gain-phase errors is proposed. Thanks to UCA properties, the virtual steering vector, which is constructed with the Hadamard product of the steering vector and its conjugate to eliminate phase errors, is considered to correspond to virtual 2-D sources impinging on the virtual UCA. This finding indicates that the azimuths and elevations of virtual sources, which are related to DOAs of original sources, can be decoupled and estimated via UCA-estimating-signal-parameter-via-rotational-invariance-techniques with the help of the recursive relationship of the Bessel function in the mode space of the virtual steering vector. We also propose the spatial filtering method, which is based on the linear independence of steering vectors in different directions, to eliminate one component in the virtual covariance matrix, which affects the DOA estimation of adjacent sources. This method can avoid the 2-D multiple-signal-classification search and cope with the one-component problem. Simulations verify its effectiveness.

Image fingerprinting is a valuable method for digital rights management, yet traditional algorithms may not capture the abstract visual characteristics of digital images. In this paper, we propose a data-driven image fingerprinting algorithm utilizing neural networks to automatically discover the optimal mapping from image to fingerprint. To achieve this, we start by training the fingerprint-computation network in a layer-wise manner to improve its robustness against content-preserving distortions. The network is then re-trained holistically to maximize its content identification accuracy. Additionally, a key-dependent version of the neural network-based fingerprinting algorithm is developed, with its security quantified using information-theoretic metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed work exhibits superior content identification accuracy compared to state-of-the-art algorithms, while also boasting millisecond execution speeds.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has a wide range of applications, from consumer services like smart home technology to strategic uses like infrastructure and energy management. Numerous technologies have been suggested to support the IoT, and this paper focuses on analyzing one such technology: Long Range (LoRA). The article first outlines the key principles of the physical layer and then presents a theoretical performance analysis. In this analysis, closed-form expressions for both symbol and bit error probabilities are derived and verified through simulation testing.

This paper introduces improved versions of a Sine-Cosine algorithm called Adaptive Sine-Cosine algorithms. It is made adaptive through incorporation of a linear and an exponential term with respect to an individual agent's fitness. Based on the newly introduced formulas, an individual agent moves with a dynamic and different step sizes compared to other agents through the whole searching process. It also introduces a balance exploration and exploitation strategies. The proposed algorithms in comparison to the original algorithm are then tested with several test functions that have different properties and landscapes. The algorithms performance in terms of their achievement of finding a near optimal solution is analyzed and discussed. Numerical result of the test shows that the proposed algorithms have achieved a better accuracy. The finding also shows that the proposed algorithms have attained a faster convergence toward the near optimal solution.

A robust cloud architecture is essential for the global Internet of Things, requiring scalability to support various forms of data and event producers and consumers. In addition, such architectures must provide low-latency delivery to not only power real-time analytics but also produce real-time actionable data for operational business logic and automation triggers activation. The shift from microservices to cyber-physical microapplications necessitates a distributed event-driven application design, which is complex and difficult to handle at the code level. To streamline this process and abstract the underlying architecture complexities, several well-known patterns have been established. However, this paper proposes a common framework that combines and extends these patterns to address all the needs of a production application. These patterns are implemented and incorporated within a middleware library, which has been tested on a proof-of-concept architecture based on Apache Kafka.

At the core of any inference procedure, deep neural networks are dot product operations, which are the component that requires the highest computational resources. For instance, deep neural networks, such as VGG-16, require up to 15-G operations in order to perform the dot products present in a single forward pass, which results in significant energy consumption and thus limits their use in resource-limited environments, e.g., on embedded devices or smartphones. One common approach to reduce the complexity of the inference is to prune and quantize the weight matrices of the neural network. Usually, this results in matrices whose entropy values are low, as measured relative to the empirical probability mass distribution of its elements. In order to efficiently exploit such matrices, one usually relies on, inter alia, sparse matrix representations. However, most of these common matrix storage formats make strong statistical assumptions about the distribution of the elements; therefore, cannot efficiently represent the entire set of matrices that exhibit low-entropy statistics (thus, the entire set of compressed neural network weight matrices). In this paper, we address this issue and present new efficient representations for matrices with low-entropy statistics. Alike sparse matrix data structures, these formats exploit the statistical properties of the data in order to reduce the size and execution complexity. Moreover, we show that the proposed data structures can not only be regarded as a generalization of sparse formats but are also more energy and time efficient under practically relevant assumptions. Finally, we test the storage requirements and execution performance of the proposed formats on compressed neural networks and compare them to dense and sparse representations. We experimentally show that we are able to attain up to ×42 compression ratios, ×5 speed ups, and ×90 energy savings when we lossless convert the state-of-the-art networks, such as AlexNet, VGG-16, ResNet152, and DenseNet, into the new data structures and benchmark their respective dot product.

Parkinson's Disease can be modelled in rats to investigate the impact of dopamine loss. Unilateral lesions, using 6-OHDA, cause a degeneration of the dopaminergic neurons of the nigrostriatal pathway resulting in motor deficits. The experiments performed in this study aimed to compare the motor and non-motor behaviour of healthy rats vs. lesioned rats (PD). We also assessed the effect that deep brain stimulation (DBS) has on the animals' locomotor activity. This paper covers the rotarod, open field, and cylinder tests, as well as sleep-awake analysis. The results of the rotarod test show that healthy rats are able to stay on the rod for longer than PD rats. The open field test revealed that PD rats spend more time freezing and close to walls or corners, whereas healthy and stimulated rats are more motivated to explore. In the cylinder test, during DBS, there is an increase in both right and left paw touches on the cylinder wall compared to pre- and post-DBS. It has also been shown that PD and control rats show different sleep patterns, further experiments could be helpful to better understand this difference.

We present a new approach for estimating the orientation of motion sensor units. Our method utilizes the physical and geometrical characteristics of acceleration, angular rate, and magnetic field vectors. The goal is to estimate the orientation of the sensor unit with respect to the Earth coordinate frame. We achieve this by ensuring that the measured acceleration vector is as close as possible to the Earth's vertical (up) axis, and that the estimated magnetic dip angle aligns as closely as possible with the detected magnetic field vector.

Our algorithm employs a rotational quaternion transformation to obtain the orientation of the sensor unit relative to the Earth. We validate the effectiveness of this technique by incorporating it into an activity recognition system for sports and daily activities. The accurate estimation of sensor unit orientation is essential to achieve invariance to the orientation of the sensor unit on the body.

We evaluate our proposed method by applying it to a public dataset with four different classification algorithms. Our approach achieves higher average activity recognition accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its superior performance. Furthermore, our approach is computationally efficient and can be executed in real-time applications.

Esophageal cancer is the fastest rising type of cancer in the western world. Also, early neoplasia in Barrett's esophagus (BE) is difficult to detect for endoscopists and research has shown it is similarly complicated for Computer-Aided Detection (CAD) algorithms. For these reasons, further development of CAD algorithms for BE is essential for the wellbeing of patients. In this work we propose a patch-based deep learning algorithm for early neoplasia in BE, utilizing state-of-the-art deep learning techniques on a new prospective data set. The new algorithm yields not only a high detection score but also identifies the ideal biopsy location for the first time. We define specific novel metrics such as sweet-spot flag and softspot flag, to obtain well-defined computation of the biopsy location. Furthermore, we show that combining white light and blue laser imaging improves localization results by 8%.

Though large-scale datasets are essential for training deep learning systems, it is expensive to scale up the collection of medical imaging datasets. Synthesizing the objects of interests, such as lung nodules, in medical images based on the distribution of annotated datasets can be helpful for improving the supervised learning tasks, especially when the datasets are limited by size and class balance. In this paper, we propose the class-aware adversarial synthesis framework to synthesize lung nodules in CT images. The framework is built with a coarse-to-fine patch in-painter (generator) and two class-aware discriminators. By conditioning on the random latent variables and the target nodule labels, the trained networks are able to generate diverse nodules given the same context. By evaluating on the public LIDC-IDRI dataset, we demonstrate an example application of the proposed framework for improving the accuracy of the lung nodule malignancy estimation as a binary classification problem, which is important in the lung screening scenario. We show that combining the real image patches and the synthetic lung nodules in the training set can improve the mean AUC classification score across different network architectures by 2%.

The proposed approach aims to predict abnormal heart rhythms by utilizing standard electrocardiograph topographies and a radial basis algorithm. In order to identify and separate the P, QRS, and T waves, a combination of general and adaptive techniques are employed. The intervals within the ECG signal are then detected and compared against previously stored records to predict ventricular arrhythmia. 

To analyze the ECG signal, four methods are employed: ECG preprocessing, QRS complex detection, feature extraction, and classification. Through the use of these methods, an accurate and noise-free ECG signal can be obtained. 

The proposed project also considers the logic size, area, and power consumption of this approach to ensure that it is both efficient and effective.

In partial label learning, the label of instance is represented by a label set, among which only one is the true label. The existing partial label learning algorithm only use features of instances to measure the similarity, and lacks of utilization of information hidden in the label set. In this paper, we proposes a candidate label-aware similarity graph constructing method for partial label data which effectively combines candidate label information using Jaccard distance and linear reconstruction to measure the similarity between instances. First, we calculate the similarity between instances and candidate label-sets. Then, the similarity graph is constructed by combining the instance similarity and the label-set similarity. Extensive experiments on artificial as well as real-world PL data sets show that our method can measure the similarity of partial-label data better and improve the performance of graph-based partial label learning algorithm obviously.

Haze removal is an intellectually challenging object of scientific study. There is a myriad of methods has been proposed hitherto, ranging from histogram-based, contrast-based to machine learning-based. Haze removal approaches founded upon machine learning require a large and reliable training database. Researchers are currently using the synthetic database due to the complexity of real database acquisition. To introduce the synthetic haze into the clear images, they assume that the depth map is drawn from the standard uniform distribution. In this paper, we present a new methodology for preparing the synthetic training database, in which the proposed equidistribution is employed instead of standard uniform distribution. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been verified by a large number of experiments.

Collaborative filtering combined with various deep learning models has become an attractive option for recommender systems due to its positive impact on accuracy improvement. However, many deep learning models require abundant information in addition to raw rating data, resulting in stringent data requirements. Moreover, most of these models ignore the interaction effect between users and items when building the recommendation system, further reducing its effectiveness. 

To address these issues, we propose a Deep Collaborative Conjunctive Recommender (DCCR) for rating prediction tasks that rely solely on raw ratings. The DCCR is a hybrid architecture consisting of two neural network models, an autoencoder, and a multilayered perceptron. The autoencoder extracts latent features simultaneously from both user and item perspectives, while the multilayered perceptron represents interaction between users and items by fusing the user and item latent features. 

We propose an advanced activation function that can be specified with input vectors to further improve the performance of DCCR. Extensive experiments conducted with two real-world datasets analyzed the performance of DCCR with varying settings. Results show that the DCCR model outperforms other state-of-art methods, and we discuss the performance of DCCR with additional layers to show the extensibility of our model.

The integration of technology and machines has opened up numerous opportunities in medical industries, particularly in rehabilitation. Post-operative physical rehabilitation support plays a crucial role in ensuring patient recovery. This paper proposes an EMG-based framework that controls a mechanized gadget capable of simulating upper limb exercises.

The framework involves two biometric sensors that capture the biceps EMG signal, which is then subjected to filtering and processing. The output/control signal is then transmitted to the actuators that simulate the upper limb movements. The goal is to predict the movements of the lower arm and restore them through advanced EMG signal analysis.

This proposed framework could have a significant impact on post-operative rehabilitation support for patients by providing a more effective and efficient solution than traditional methods. By utilizing cutting-edge EMG signals analysis, patients can experience improved recovery outcomes and faster return to normal activities. Further research and development in this area can lead to the introduction of additional technologies and improvements to existing frameworks to provide better treatment modalities to support patient recovery.

In recent years, the area of human-robot collaboration (HRC) has gained significant attention from the intersection of control, robotics, and psychology. While current HRC research primarily focuses on low-level human-aware motion planning and HRC interface design, our interest lies in the formal design of HRC at the high-level for complex missions, where obtaining a precise and practical human model is vital. Instead of assuming the human model, we propose the learning of the human model from observed data, such as gestures, eye movements, and head motions.

To accomplish this, we employed a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) model, as psychology studies reveal Markovian properties of human behavior. POMDP offers a general modeling framework for sequential decision making with hidden states and stochastic consequences of actions. Unlike traditional POMDP model learning that presumes the state, transition structure, or the number of states, we utilize a Bayesian non-parametric learning approach to identify the potential human states from data. Furthermore, we adopt an approach inspired by probably approximately correct (PAC) learning, deriving an estimate of the transition probability and a confidence interval with the estimation. The control policy derived from the estimated model is guaranteed to have a performance adequately close to the true model.

Finally, we illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed learning method using data collected from a driver-assistance test-bed. Our approach shows significant promise in providing an accurate and tractable model of human behavior for HRC's high-level complex missions.

The widespread issue of missing values (MVs) in real-world datasets has hindered the use of many statistical and machine learning algorithms for data analytics, as they are not equipped to handle incomplete data. Although there are various MVs imputation methods available, most of them are suitable for datasets with specific types or low missing rates. In an effort to address this issue, we propose a new method that caters to missing completely at random (MCAR) data with high missing rates. 

Our method is based on the generative adversarial networks (GAN) architecture, which involves the training process on discrete datasets with missing values. This ensures that the generated dataset is identical to the feature distribution of the original dataset. We conducted experiments on two different types of datasets to demonstrate the feasibility and efficiency of this method - a public authority dataset consisting of wireless sensor records and a large group of datasets collected from an industrial production monitoring process. 

The results of our experiments compared with the traditional missing values imputation methods have shown that our method performs better in terms of robustness and accuracy when the missing rate is higher than 30%. Our method has proven to be a valuable tool for data analysts and researchers dealing with incomplete datasets and has the potential to revolutionize the way MVs are imputed.

The present work is part of a broader research related to the improvement of the teaching methodology, in the undergraduates degree of Architecture and Building Engineering through the application of new technologies. The aim of the proposal is to confirm that changes in the teaching methodology improve the learning experience, in our case using a learning analytics approach. In this case study, we focused in one First Year subject: Descriptive Geometry, which has a high rate of repeating students, as well as an early dropout. We have implemented an educational data mining mixed approach related to the mid-semester exams (midterm), and we stablished a relation with the final marks of the subject in two periods with differentiated methodologies, Pre-Bologna (2006-09), and Post-Bologna (2015- 18). The objective of this analysis is to predict what students are closer to leave the course after the midterm results based on the topics examined, so that we can influence and implement new methodologies, technologies and systems to improve these topics.

Online dating is a popular service accessible through the Internet nowadays. However, it has become prone to dubious users who use Japanese dating services for purposes other than dating, such as sales and multi-level marketing. This paper introduces a new detection system that identifies these users. The system analyzes user profile data, user actions during their early hours, and data retrieved from Facebook to ascertain the likelihood of the user being a spammer. This system has been successfully detecting a number of spammers daily, making it a valuable tool for the customer service team in Eureka Inc, where it has been deployed.

In today's world of continuous information flow and easy access to knowledge through the internet, teachers need to be actively involved in using technology to acquire knowledge, build their professional expertise, and enhance their personal value and competitiveness. This process of personal knowledge management is essential for teachers to stay up to date with the latest trends and developments in their field.

To address the challenges and issues in teacher's personal knowledge management, this article proposes a framework based on the four knowledge transformation modes of the SECI model and the four processes of personal knowledge management. These processes are acquisition, creation, sharing, and application.

In order to improve their personal knowledge management, teachers should use a range of tools and strategies to support these processes. Some of these tools include online research databases, social media platforms, and professional development programs. Teachers can also collaborate with colleagues and experts in their field to share information and seek guidance on how to improve their knowledge management skills.

Overall, the effective management of personal knowledge is essential for teachers to stay relevant and effective in their profession. By adopting the strategies and tools proposed in this article, teachers can enhance their skills and stay ahead of the curve in the rapidly changing landscape of education.

Observability is a crucial concept in the field of control theory as it reflects the possibility of state estimation. Controllability, on the other hand, forms the theoretical foundation of modern control theory which is based on state space description. However, traditional observability theory has limitations in dealing with deterministic systems, and the qualitative results can only provide binary value outcomes. To overcome these limitations, the concept of observable degree has been proposed to quantitatively characterize the observability of a system.

This paper is aimed at exploring observable degree analysis theory based on an observability judgment matrix. It begins by reviewing the traditional observability theory for deterministic systems and introduces a method of observable degree calculation based on an observability Grammian matrix. However, the paper examines the limitations and shortcomings of this approach.

Furthermore, the paper moves on to discuss the difficulty and challenge of applying the observability and observable degree concepts to time-varying systems, nonlinear systems, and stochastic systems. By analyzing the research on the observability and observable degree of these systems, the paper provides guidance and suggestions for a more comprehensive approach to the research on the observability judgment theory and observable degree analysis for complex systems.
