In conclusion, the paper emphasizes the importance of considering observable degree as a unified whole with observability. It highlights the need to develop a comprehensive observability theory that can handle the complexities of modern control systems. By doing so, it will enable better state estimation and control of complex systems, advancing the field of control theory.

Security metrics have become crucial in assessing and making effective decisions regarding system security risks. Despite many security metrics relying on mathematical models, they often lack accuracy due to their dependence on empirical data, qualitative methods, or compliance checking. This paper presents a unique method that involves calculating the probability distribution of cloud security threats utilizing Markov chain and Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). The application of this approach in cloud systems demonstrates its effectiveness in assessing security risks.

To improve the accuracy of contour following tasks, researchers have focused on real-time contouring error in order to enhance contouring performance. However, accurately estimating the contouring error for multiaxis motion systems remains challenging, particularly for free-form spatial contours. In response, this paper proposes a method for estimating contouring errors using double Taylor expansion.

The proposed method uses a third-order Taylor equation to express the contouring error, which is based on the kinematics information of a datum point. This datum point is then determined by the Taylor approximation expanded at the desired point. Unlike existing Taylor expansion-based contouring error estimation strategies, the proposed method achieves higher order accuracy and eliminates inaccurate estimation caused by the distance between the datum point and the actual one.

To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, simulations and experiments were conducted on a three-axis motion system. The results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully estimates contouring errors for free-form spatial contours, achieving greater accuracy than existing methods. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for improving contour following tasks for multiaxis motion systems.

Power load forecasting is an important part of electrical company operations. An accurate forecast can help the company makes various important decisions. Two known models for power load forecasting are ARMA model and its variants and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). The ARMA model has been used for decades while ANN can be considered as a more recent approach. In this paper MLP and SARIMAX are proposed to model the power load of Java and Bali power system. Both models can be used to forecast the load of Java and Bali power system with MAPE of 2.4% for SARIMAX and 2.7% for MLP. The time needed to build a SARIMAX model is shorter compared to MLP. In general, SARIMAX performs better compared to MLP. An application is also developed to facilitate data transformation, model training, and forecasting based on the proposed models.

Point cloud registration plays a critical role in workpiece positioning and error evaluation. The Iterative Closest Points (ICP) algorithm is typically utilized for fine registration. However, it requires a suitable initial condition to avoid getting trapped in the local minimum. As a result, ICP exhibits poor robustness and adaptability when the point cloud has measuring noise and outliers, complex surface, or a far distance between the measured and the design. In this study, an enhanced ICP method is proposed that employs simulated annealing (SA) and the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) to achieve the global minimum regardless of the initial conditions.

The SA mechanism based on Pincus theorem is used to calculate the rotation angles and translation vectors of the correspondences. To enhance the utility of SA, the MCMC method is also used to improve its sampling effectiveness in satisfying the Pincus distribution. Consequently, the MCMC-SA ICP algorithm for point cloud registration is developed. To test the practicality of the developed MCMC-SA ICP approach, three different complex curved surfaces were examined. The results indicate that the improved ICP using MCMC-SA displays stronger global optimization ability than traditional ICP.

In this paper, we propose a method of retrieving posts on social networking services (SNSs) by specifying a pair of queries: a topic query and an entity query. A topic query specifies the topic of the posts to retrieve (e.g., "iPhone") and an entity query specifies the type of users who posted them (e.g., "students"). In the existing search systems for SNS posts, we can specify topics of posts by keywords, but we cannot specify types of users. Even if we include keywords specifying types of users in a query, such keywords are not usually included in tweets or user profile data. In our method, we estimate types of users by learning vocabulary whose appearance is correlated with specific types of users. We learn it from the datasets obtained through Web search. We retrieve Web documents through the search with a keyword specifying the type of users (e.g., "student"), and we also retrieve Web documents by using a keyword specifying its opposite (e.g., "adult"). We regard the documents retrieved by these queries as positive and negative examples of documents describing the target type, and we train a model for recognizing users of the given type. We recognize users of the target type by inputting their posts and their profile data into the model. We use Web documents instead of SNS posts for training the model because the Web has more documents describing types of people.

This paper presents a method to extract interconnect capacitance in three-dimensional integrated circuits (3D ICs) using a neural network (NN). The procedure is as follows: (1) create training datasets (by obtaining capacitance values from the complicated 3D interconnect structures using a 3D electromagnetic field solver), (2) build the trained models by inputting the training datasets to the NN, and (3) extract capacitance values by inputting structural parameters regarding the objective interconnect. The structures of general interconnects, interconnects surrounding a through-silicon via (TSV), and whole interconnects are examined. Experimental results show that the proposed NN-based extraction method can obtain reasonable accuracy and processing time. They also show that good trained models are obtained even if training datasets that integrate two structures into one are input to the NN.

Microvascular invasion (MVI) of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a crucial histopathologic prognostic factor associated with cancer recurrence after liver transplantation or hepatectomy. In this study, we propose a deep learning framework based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) to extract discriminative information of HCCs from Contrast-enhanced MR images for MVI prediction. Specifically, 3D CNN is adopted to extract high-level deep features (spatial information) of HCC, and LSTM is used to extract sequential information (temporal information) of Contrast-enhanced MR for MVI prediction. Furthermore, we propose a deeply supervised loss function to improve the prediction performance by taking advantage of both the spatially and temporally discriminative features from Contrast-enhanced MR. Experimental results of 63 clinically confirmed HCCs with Contrast-enhanced MR demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework as follows: (1) 3D deep feature outperforms texture features in the radiomics approach for MVI prediction. (2) 3D CNN and LSTM used in the proposed deep learning framework yields better results than that of the 3D deep feature concatenation for MVI prediction. (3) Deeply supervised loss function that makes full use of the spatially and temporally discriminative features from Contrast-enhanced MR can further improve the performance of MVI prediction.

This paper proposes wireless ad hoc network simulation based on virtual reality technology. Functional components provided by a game engine such as scene management, animation, rendering, scripting, and physics engine can provide suitable interfaces for ad hoc network simulation. Using these components, simulation of ad hoc networks can be easily implemented. The ad-hoc network simulation technology can be carried out in virtual reality by game engine, which is illustrated by advantages of the game engine and the simulation process in this paper. The workability and accuracy of the simulation scheme are demonstrated, with the metrics of comparing the experimental data with other simulation techniques commonly used.

Radomes protect antennas from structural damage due to wind, precipitation, and bird strikes. In aerospace applications, radomes often double as a nose cone and thus have a significant impact on the aerodynamics of the aircraft. While radomes should be designed not to affect the performance of the underlying antennas, they also must satisfy structural and aerodynamic requirements. In this paper, we demonstrate a multiphysics approach to analysis of airborne radomes not only for electromagnetic (EM) performance, but also for structural, aerodynamic, and bird strike performances, as depicted in figure 1. We consider a radome constructed using composite fiberglass plies and a foam core, and coated with an anti-static coating, paint, and primer. A slotted waveguide array is designed at X-band to represent a weather radar antenna. The transmission loss of the radome walls is analyzed using a planar Green's function approach. An asymptotic technique, Ray-Launching Geometric Optics (RL-GO), is used to accurately simulate the nose cone radome and compute transmission loss, boresight error, and sidelobe performance. In addition to EM analysis, Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analysis is used to predict pressures resulting from high air speeds, which are then mapped to an implicit structural solution to assess structural integrity using the Finite Element Method (FEM). We also demonstrate damage prediction due to a “bird strike” impact using an explicit structural FEM solver. The multiphysics simulation techniques demonstrated in this paper will allow for early design validation and reduce the number of measurement iterations required before a radome is certified for installation.

Lightning is a global phenomenon that can occur at any time and in any place, particularly in tropical regions such as Malaysia. Its effects can cause significant damage to human life, animals, and property. Therefore, there have been efforts to design models to forecast lightning occurrences. This study explores the use of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to predict the likelihood of lightning occurrence by utilizing meteorological data provided by the Malaysian Meteorological Department. A case study was conducted at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). The meteorological data used in the model consisted of temperature, mean relative humidity, mean msl pressure, mean surface wind speed, and rainfall amount. The output target was the number of lightning occurrences. The ANN model was developed using MATLAB toolbox and trained using the Levenberg-Marquardt training algorithm. The simulations derived from the model indicated that it was capable of predicting lightning occurrences with a high Best Fit, low RMSE, and good R-value. These values were 94.64%, 0.000786, and 0.99999, respectively.

The article delves into the current scenario in modern manufacturing enterprises, which is heavily influenced by the digital virtualization of various aspects of the production process. The overview highlights that the extensive use of technology in all areas has resulted in the replacement of real components and relationships with their digital counterparts, often in a virtual environment. The study identifies key features of systems that use digital twin technology, along with the crucial requirements for deploying intelligent products. The aim of this article is to propose the use of digital twin technology as a complement to standardized concepts for Industry 4.0 to develop a production system. The central idea emerging from this proposal is that the ongoing adoption of new technologies and communication methods between industrial facilities is eliminating the barriers between the physical and virtual domains. The concluding section presents an approach to implementing this concept using the AVEVA Wonderware software.

In this paper, our proposed method aims to solve the positive semidefinite Hankel structured low rank approximation (PHSLRA) of a given matrix. To tackle this problem, we formulate it as an unconstrained optimization problem using the Vandermonde decomposition of the positive-semidefinite Hankel matrix. We then implement the alternating minimization method to optimize the objective function.

To the best of our knowledge, no prior literature has proposed an alternating minimization method for solving PHSLRA. As such, our approach offers a unique solution to this problem. We test our algorithm on various numerical examples to demonstrate its superiority over existing methods.

This letter addresses the issue of accurate object detection in large-area remote sensing images. Although many convolutional neural network (CNN)-based object detection models can achieve high accuracy in small image patches, the models perform poorly in large-area images due to the large quantity of false and missing detections that arise from complex backgrounds and diverse groundcover types. To address this challenge, this letter proposes a sample update-based CNN (SUCNN) framework for object detection in large-area remote sensing images. The proposed framework contains two stages. In the first stage, a base model—single-shot multibox detector—is trained with the training data set. In the second stage, artificial composite samples are generated to update the training set. The parameters of the first-stage model are fine-tuned with the updated data set to obtain the second-stage model. The first- and second-stage models are evaluated using the large-area remote sensing image test set. Comparison experiments show the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed SUCNN framework for object detection in large-area remote sensing images.

With the quick advancements in technology and the growing amount of data, data analysis has become more challenging. In this day and age, it is crucial to be able to record, store, and access data in an electronic environment. However, data alone has no value until it is processed. Data mining is a process that extracts useful information from large-scale data, enabling meaningful insights to be obtained. Furthermore, it involves the use of software to predict future trends based on patterns found within the data.

This study introduces a new method, the Fast Weighted Bayesian Classifier, which has been compared with the Naïve Bayes Classifier and the Weighted Naïve Bayes Classifier. All three methods fall under data mining classification methods. The comparison was carried out using various data sets, and the results showed that the accuracy rate of the Fast Weighted Bayes Algorithm exceeds that of the Naïve Bayes Classifier, and it is quicker than the Weighted Naïve Bayes Classifier. 

In conclusion, the Fast Weighted Bayesian Classifier is a powerful tool in data mining that can help analysts and researchers to gain valuable insights from large volumes of data quickly and efficiently. Its superiority over traditional methods highlights its potential for application in various industries and research fields.

Freeform surfaces exist widely in the stock cutting process of clinical prosthesis preparation, aviation, ship, and other manufacturing industries. The free-form contours of surfaces need to be packed before they are machined from raw materials. The existing methods search a contour position by rotating the contour and translating it to connect other contours for packing. The relative position between two contours will be changed after the rotation as the contour description is lack of geometric invariance. These methods easily miss the best layout position resulting in interspaces in the raw material. Moreover, this result seriously reduces the performance and efficiency of an automatic packing system. Therefore, a new packing algorithm is proposed in this paper by combining the geometric invariant description and coding matching for contours to solve the contour rotating and position connecting problems. The optimal position of a contour can be found directly and then connected by the extracted similar complement features of the contour. The experimental results show that the proposed method can greatly improve quality and efficiency of the layout, especially in the material utilization.

One of the most promising alternatives to train, compensate or rehabilitate patients after cerebrovascular accidents, spinal cord injuries, head trauma and physiological pathological tremors causing gait disorders are the motor neuroprosthestic devices (NP). However, there are not portable and flexible NP devices capable of fulfilling the requirements of different rehabilitation scenarios. In this work, the novel and flexible H-GAIT NP for lower limbs training and compensation is presented. This NP is able to detect four subphases of gait cycle and provide configurable surface stimulation patterns at each subphase. The H-GAIT NP can stimulate 4 independent channels for each subphase, allowing to reproduce diverse muscle activation patterns that can be needed in different rehabilitation scenarios. In order to validate the concept, several tests were carried on with 5 neuromuscularly intact participants and three different gait speeds in order to validate detection of the subphases. The algorithm showed an acceptable performance (over 95 % of gait) subphases successfully detected in all cases at three different gait speeds (0.7, 0.85, and 0.97 m/s). The results were consistent among participants. To show the potential use of the NP in different rehabilitation scenarios, one stimulation profile was configured for hemiplegic gait compensation.

An analysis of existing methods for solving the problems of risk assessment showed that they are based on the lack of computational capabilities and the lack of necessary information about the conditions of the problem. Therefore, in such cases it is advisable to use fuzzy mathematical methods. In this paper, we consider approaches to solving the problem of risk assessment with fuzzy source information.

Distribution Automation (DA) has become a crucial element to achieving a Smart Grid, and its popularity continues to grow rapidly among power utilities worldwide. This paper aims to provide an example of a protection application scheme and explain how the IEC 61850 application profile can be defined to ensure interoperability in a Distribution Automation (DA) application.

The protection application scheme discussed in this paper is particularly essential in the context of Distribution Automation as it enables utilities to respond swiftly to faults and enhance the reliability of the electrical grid. In this regard, the use of IEC 61850 is recommended due to its capability to achieve interoperability and standardized communication protocols. 

To define the IEC 61850 application profile for DA, there must be a comprehensive understanding of the different devices within the network and their communication requirements. The application profile defines the required communication services, data models, and protocols needed for successful communication between devices. It also determines the configuration features necessary for the protection application to operate efficiently.

For instance, DA typically comprises protection, automation, and control (PAC) functions. These functions are implemented in Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) on the communication network. To ensure that these devices can communicate with each other effectively, the IEC 61850 application profile must specify communication services such as GOOSE messaging and sampled values. 

In summary, DA is a crucial component of a Smart Grid, and the IEC 61850 application profile is a critical enabler of interoperability in DA applications. By defining the appropriate communication services, data models, and protocols required for the protection application to operate effectively, utilities can ensure reliable and efficient communication between different devices in their network.

METRO-HAUL Targets the design and the building of a smart optical metro infrastructure able to support traffic originating from 5G New Radio (5G NR) networks, addressing the anticipated capacity increase and its specific characteristics e.g. mobility, low latency, low jitter, etc. This infrastructure will also support a wide variety of services and use cases with special emphasis on services from various industries vertical to the ICT.

Nowadays, service providers need to align their offerings with the needs of their users to ensure customer satisfaction and gain a competitive edge. The IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) is one such implementation of the Next Generation Network (NGN) that aims to provide users with seamless access to a diverse range of services regardless of their access technology. However, the sheer number of services available can make service exposure challenging. To address this, we propose a proactive service exposure approach based on event prediction in this paper. Our approach is based on an online service recommendation that is implicitly initiated by the service requestor. We compare our approach to the classic service exposure approach and to the predictive collaborative service exposure approach we proposed in a previous work. Our approach performs well in terms of response time, CPU utilization, and memory use, but service targeting accuracy is relatively lower than the other approaches.

Humanoid robots are seen as perfect education partners for students these days. Many researchers are working on educational humanoid robots to make them more effective in educating students. One of many approaches to realize it is to make the robots educate children in two-way communication. In this case, robots can recognize students' progress and provide suitable learning materials according to their progress. In a simple scenario for basic mathematics learning, the robot educates a student on how to solve mathematical expressions. As the student understand the concepts, the robot gives some simple exercises to further improve student's ability. While completing the exercise, the partner robot supervises each mathematical expression solved by the student, acknowledges mistakes and provides correct solutions. Thus, the robot must be equipped with a system which can recognize mathematical expressions and give the solutions. Such system is an inherent foundation to build much smarter robots in delivering education to students. This paper covers detail design and implementation of the system which recognizes handwritten mathematical equations and provides the corresponding solutions. Testing results show that the system performs quite well with 97.4% accuracy with slight errors for characters with similar shapes.

This paper deals with iterative Jacobian-based recursion technique for the root-finding problem of the vectorvalued function, whose evaluations are contaminated by noise. Instead of a scalar step size, we use an iterate-dependent matrix gain to effectively weigh the different elements associated with the noisy observations. The analytical development of the matrix gain is built on an iterative-dependent linear function interfered by additive zero-mean white noise, where the dimension of the function is M 1 and the dimension of the unknown variable is N 1. Necessary and sufficient conditions for M N algorithms are presented pertaining to algorithm stability and convergence of the estimate error covariance matrix. Two algorithms are proposed: one for the case where M N and the second one for the antithesis. The two algorithms assume full knowledge of the Jacobian. The recursive algorithms are proposed for generating the optimal iterative-dependent matrix gain. The proposed algorithms here aim for per-iteration minimization of the mean square estimate error. We show that the proposed algorithm satisfies the presented conditions for stability and convergence of the covariance. In addition, the convergence rate of the estimation error covariance is shown to be inversely proportional to the number of iterations. For the antithesis M <; N, contraction of the error covariance is guaranteed. This underdetermined system of equations can be helpful in training neural networks. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the performance capabilities of the proposed multidimensional gain while considering nonlinear functions.

Recently, it has been standardized by the 3rd generation partnership project (3GPP) that device-to-device (D2D) communications should use uplink resources when coexisting with conventional cellular communications. With uplink resource sharing, both cellular and D2D links cause significant co-channel interference. In this paper, we address the critical issue of interference management in the network considering a practical path loss model incorporating both line-of-sight (LoS) and non-LoS (NLoS) transmissions. To reduce the severe interference caused by active D2D links, we consider a mode selection scheme based on the maximum received signal strength (MRSS) for each user equipment (UE) to control the D2D-to-cellular interference. Furthermore, we analyze the performance in terms of the coverage probability and the area spectral efficiency (ASE) for both the cellular network and the D2D one. Analytical results are obtained and the accuracy of the proposed analytical framework is validated through Monte Carlo simulations. Through our theoretical and numerical analyses, we quantify the performance gains brought by D2D communications in cellular networks and we find an optimum mode selection threshold β to maximize the total ASE in the network. This insight is expected to provide a design guideline for D2D mode selections.

Acceleration coefficients are critical parameters in the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, controlling the movement of particles by modifying their cognitive and social components. While several variants have been proposed to enhance the convergence speed of PSO in continuous search space, less effort has been devoted to improving the convergence speed of binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO). Additionally, BPSO treats all particles equally, ignoring their distinct positions in a search space and resulting in poor performance. To address this issue, we proposed a fitness-based acceleration coefficients Novel BPSO, named FAC-NBPSO. In our algorithm, we utilize the fitness of each particle to modify both its cognitive and social components, enabling more effective and efficient search. To validate our approach, we applied it to four benchmark test functions, and the experimental results showed that FAC-NBPSO outperformed the compared algorithm with faster convergence speed.

The use of the airborne electromagnetic (AEM) method has proven to be an effective approach in assessing conductivity structures near the earth's surface. However, the huge amount of data collected over survey areas of large sizes presents a significant computational challenge. Fortunately, a volume of limited scale beneath each transmitter and receiver (Tx-Rx) station, known as the footprint, contains the majority of the induced current, and the EM response at the receiver. 

In this letter, we present a novel approach known as the footprint-guided compact finite element method (CFEM). This technique efficiently models the inhomogeneous conductivity structure in the entire survey area by dividing it into small sub-areas based on the footprint. The forward modeling for each sub-area is performed efficiently using this approach.

Each computational domain for a single Tx-Rx station consists of a small sub-area and a surrounding layer, which ensures that the algorithm's accuracy is maintained. Verification of the algorithm's accuracy was conducted by comparing its solutions with semianalytical solutions on a layered earth model. Additionally, a more complex 3-D model with a large inhomogeneous structure was used to demonstrate the algorithm's applicability and efficiency.

Overall, the development of the CFEM approach presents a significant advancement in the utilization of the AEM method. It is expected that this approach will be particularly useful in the mining and geothermal sectors, where large-scale surveys are typically conducted, and computational efficiency is crucial.

Energy management is a major concern in the design of wireless sensor networks, especially those meant to function over a prolonged period. The primary energy-consuming task in these networks is radio transmissions, and researchers have explored several strategies to improve the lifetime of these networks, including adaptive transmission power and relaying protocols. A new MAC protocol has been proposed for multihop wireless sensor networks that utilizes emerging wake-up receivers to address this issue. The protocol utilizes an energy-based back-off mechanism that enables nodes to select the best transmission scheme and corresponding power level. This approach has been implemented on real hardware, and testing has demonstrated a potential lifetime gain of up to 1.7 when two relays are employed. The proposed solution represents a promising solution to extend the lifetime of wireless sensor networks while minimizing energy consumption.

Turkish is a language that is rich in morphology. This results in a major problem of data sparsity for language modeling tasks in the context of automatic speech recognition (ASR). To address this issue, researchers have proposed two strategies: using sub-words as language modeling units and incorporating sub-word features into word-level models. In this study, we propose a novel model architecture that directly incorporates sub-word features. Specifically, we use a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn (sub)word embeddings as sub-word features from character or sub-word level input. We evaluate our proposed model on a Turkish ASR task, using both word and morph (sub-word) as language modeling units. Our results demonstrate that the consistency between language modeling units and ASR system units is crucial for the effectiveness of rescaling. Our proposed method also shows promising results, reducing the word error rate (WER) of word and statistical sub-word level system by absolute 1.56% and 1.87%, respectively.

As an important part of the aircraft, the protective shell can protect the aircraft and other payloads. But it will become an irregular body falling into water when it is abandoned. The hydrodynamic force of the irregular body is complex and hard to express. In this paper, a semi-cylindrical shell is taken as an irregular body example to study the hydrodynamic characteristics and its expression. By using the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) method, the hydrodynamic force of the irregular body is obtained, and its characteristics is analyzed in detail. It can provide a basis for further research of the irregular body.

This paper attempted to study the efficiency of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with metaheuristic algorithms for electricity consumption modeling in Thailand. The objective was to compare the study between ANN with Backpropagation algorithm (ANN-BP) and ANN combined with different metaheuristic algorithms: ANN with Harmony Search (ANN-HS), ANN with Artificial Bee Colony (ANN-ABC), ANN with Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (ANN-TLBO) and ANN with Jaya Algorithms (ANN-JA) models. The models selected Population, Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Imports of goods and services, Exports of goods and services as inputs. The experiment results showed that the ANN-TLBO model had optimal efficiency, while ANN-JA was one of the competitive metaheuristic algorithms that could be implemented to modelling for use in future studies.

Due to the dynamic topology of ad hoc networks, many routing protocols and service discovery protocols primarily rely on flooding algorithms. Despite the crucial role of these algorithms in wireless ad hoc networks, experimental studies of small-scale ad hoc networks have not been adequately explored. To tackle this problem, we present a paper where we implement several flooding algorithms on Raspberry Pi and evaluate their performance. We provide an in-depth analysis of the implementation process and present the packet delivery ratio in small-scale ad hoc networks.

In order to discriminate the real targets, the clutter and the dense multi-false targets, we propose a factorized convolutional neural network-based algorithm for radar targets discrimination. We establish the factorized convolutional neural network model with depthwise separable convolution. To reduce the parameters of the model, we establish the simplified factorized convolutional neural network by reducing the numbers of both convolutional filters and connection nodes of fully connected layers. The result of the measured data demonstrates that, as compared with the existing model, the simplified factorized convolutional neural network has higher discrimination rate for the real targets, the clutter and the dense multi-false targets, and its parameters are less than ten percent counterpart of a recent proposed model.

The Bayes-optimal classifier is a type of binary classifier that aims to minimize the prediction error for any given sample. Unfortunately, finding the Bayes-optimal classifier is a difficult task due to its intractability. Nevertheless, research has demonstrated that it is approximately equivalent to the center of mass of the version space - the set of all classifiers consistent with the training set. Previous solutions have presented high computational costs and performed inadequately in non-linear separable problems, prompting the need for an alternative approach. This paper proposes the Dual Version Space Reduction Machine (Dual VSRM), a kernel method that effectively approximates the center of mass of the version space. Dual VSRM utilizes successive reductions of the version space based on the oracle's decision. To this end, we propose the Ensemble of Dissimilar Balanced Kernel Perceptrons (EBPK) as the oracle. EBKP enhances the accuracy of each individual classifier by balancing the final hyperplane solution and maximizing the diversity of its components by applying a dissimilarity measure. Experimental evaluations on seven datasets demonstrate that our proposed methods outperform several baselines. Our results for EBKP indicate that the strategies for improving individual accuracy and diversity of the ensemble components work effectively. Furthermore, the Dual VSRM consistently generates a better approximation to the center of mass than the baselines.

In this paper, we begin by describing our model for the channel impulse characteristic, which involves a combination of the Monte Carlo method with the Fournier-Forand phase function. We then investigate the impact that different field of views (FOVs) and transmission distances have on the channel impulse response, and conclude that temporal dispersion can impose strict bandwidth limitations on undersea wireless optical communication (UWOC) systems in harbor water.

To address this issue, we propose the use of the maximum likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) method at the receiver to mitigate bandwidth limitations. Our analysis shows that MLSE has the potential to greatly improve overall system performance.

Self-adaptive software has the capability to sense a change in its environment and its own behaviour, and then adjust itself accordingly during runtime to meet the desired requirements. Analysing and evaluating quality attributes is popular in self-adaptive software research. In recent years, several studies have proposed runtime models which analyse and evaluate quality attributes of self-adaptive software. This paper focuses on runtime models used for analysis and evaluation of quality attributes of self-adaptive software. Firstly, self-adaptive software, runtime models, analysis and evaluation of quality attributes based on runtime models, and related concepts are introduced. Studies describing runtime models are investigated and the meaning of runtime models used in analysis and evaluation of quality attributes of self-adaptive software is clarified. Two types of typical construction methods and their general construction processes are described. Runtime models were analysed and categorized considering multiple aspects, including type, modelling language, application scenarios, and relationship between runtime models and quality attributes. The extension mechanisms for runtime models were also analysed and extracted into two types. The weaknesses of current research are listed and analysed, with future research directions suggested.

Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is an advanced Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) architecture that is specifically designed to model sequences with long-range dependencies more accurately than conventional RNNs. In this paper, we propose the use of deep bidirectional LSTM for sequence modeling as an approach to perform sequence alignment based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). The deep bidirectional LSTM is used to learn LSH features, and the obtained LSH is then used for sequence alignment. 

To demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed LSTM-based model for sequence modeling, we aligned short read queries over the human reference genome. We used the Illumina sequencing technology to generate a set of short reads and the human reference genome as a training dataset. Initially, we decomposed the reference genome into multiple sequences, which were then fed into the bidirectional LSTM model to map them into fixed-length vectors. These vectors were trained to generate LSH, which was used for sequence alignment.

Our case study showed that using the proposed LSTM-based model, we achieved higher accuracy with an increase in the number of epochs. The trained LSH vectors accurately aligned the query sequences into the reference genome. Therefore, the LSTM-based model proved to be a reliable approach for sequence modeling and sequence alignment using LSH.

It is important to understand the factors that contribute significantly to increasing the student's motivation to perform academically and their soft skills. This paper discusses the implementation of My UiTM Engineering (MUE) to help students with cumulative grade point average (CGPA) below 3.0 to obtain better results. A meaningful mind setting talk with the comprehensive module for group training was designed for this program. To understand the characteristics of students with CGPA below 3.0, a survey was distributed to a batch of new students to analyze their opinions of their self-motivation, the level of familiarization on fundamental electrical and electronic subjects and the level of soft kills they acquired throughout their study. For the older batch of students who underwent the MUE program, the results showed that 73% of them were able to increase their CGPA as compared to the previous semester after participating in the MUE program.

Nowadays Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs) receive important attention in the scientific and commercial fields due to the increasing number of devices and applications concentrating on safety, efficiency and infotainment in transportation infrastructure. One of the most promising applications is the streaming of video data which presents a suitable tool especially for warning drivers and preventing dangers on roads. However, video streaming over vehicular environment is a daunting task due to high movement of vehicles and the specific requirements of video data in terms of performances and quality of service (QoS)/quality of experience (QoE). To this end, this paper presents a survey of video streaming techniques in vehicular networks and discusses the different QoS/QoE related to video streaming issues. A comparative study of QoS/QoE aware video streaming schemes classified according to the technique used is elaborated. Furthermore, major challenges in video streaming are identified as future trends of research.

The paper pays attention to particularities concerned with the defuzzification procedure in adaptive neural network based fuzzy inference systems. Specifically, the problem of constructing recursive parameter estimation algorithms is considered with regard to their convergence and stability. In the combination with various forms of the quadratic criterion, such an approach enables on to obtain strongly consistent estimation algorithms under essential generality of modeled system description; and the convergence properties are demonstrated in the comparison with conventional algorithms.

Vibration and acoustics emission based methods are commonly used in condition monitoring and fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. However, condition monitoring of low-speed bearings may be more difficult than that of high-speed bearings due to its low signal-to-noise ratio. A detailed discussion on vibration and acoustic emission based methods implemented in recent years for fault detection and health condition monitoring of low-speed bearings is presented in this paper. The comparison of these two methods is given, and some suggestions and considerations are included as well.

In this paper, a new statistical model for received signal strength (RSS) is proposed and formulated. This model is designed to accurately detect location in fingerprint offline mode and online mode. The model employs range and midrange methods to determine a new mean and standard deviation. Additionally, the frequency distribution patterns are calculated and used in the RSS model. To test the efficacy of this method, an Android Smartphone application for WLAN indoor localization was developed and tested in City Center Mall in Nasr City, Cairo, Egypt using unknown location access points (APs). The RSS model was utilized by the application for constructing a radio map of the testing area in fingerprint offline mode. In fingerprint online mode, a new searching method was employed that matched predefined locations of the radio map to online locations. Results indicate that the model accurately determined location, with the exception of a few locations that were not determined precisely.

In this paper we discuss the signal processing of a cylindrical object, a pipe (in air), subjected to random excitations by a hammer-like surface from a cam-driven motor. The overall objective of this effort is to develop real-time hardware capable of monitoring mechanical systems (structures) for potential anomalies. We briefly discuss the development process: (1) theoretical modeling; (2) sophisticated simulations; (3) analysis; (4) controlled experiments; (5) signal processing; (6) modal frequency estimation; and (7) modal tracking. The primary emphasis is on the signal processing, modal extraction and tracking for single and multi-channel data.

Sign language is physical communication for contributing the meaning instead of using voice to demonstrate communicator's opinion. This paper introduces a simple and efficient algorithm for feature extraction to recognize American Sign Language alphabets from both static and dynamic gestures. The proposed algorithm comprises of four different techniques: Number of white pixels at the edge of the image (NwE), Finger length from the centroid point (Fcen), Angles between fingers (AngF) and Differences of angles between fingers of the first and last frame (delAng). After extracting features from video images, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is used to classify the signs. The result of these experiments is achieved up to 95% recognition rate, which is clearly to be the highest accuracy comparing with the other research worked in this field.

We propose a novel regression method named kernel partial least square regression II, which utilizes a combination of partial least square (PLS) technique and kernel method. This proposal extends the basic framework of conventional kernel PLS regression, which only projects independent variables into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). In contrast, our proposed method not only projects independent variables into the RKHS, but also dependent variables, thereby establishing a coordinator system where both variables have a stronger correlation.

To evaluate our proposed method's effectiveness, we conducted two function regression cases and compared them with the conventional kernel PLS regression. The results show that our proposed method has almost the same regression accuracy, which depends on the specific regression tasks. We also examined the correlation calculations of our proposed method, conventional kernel PLS regression, and PLS regression. Furthermore, we discussed several algorithm implementation issues, correlation meaning, and other aspects to encourage further development of our proposed method.

The target of security protection of the power distribution automation system (the distribution system for short) is to ensure the security of communication between the distribution terminal (terminal for short) and the distribution master station (master system for short). The encryption and authentication gateway (VPN gateway for short) for distribution system enhances the network layer communication security between the terminal and the VPN gateway. The distribution application layer encryption authentication device (master cipher machine for short) ensures the confidentiality and integrity of data transmission in application layer, and realizes the identity authentication between the master station and the terminal. All these measures are used to prevent malicious damage and attack to the master system by forging terminal identity, replay attack and other illegal operations, in order to prevent the resulting distribution network system accidents. Based on the security protection scheme of the power distribution automation system, this paper carries out the development of multi-chip encapsulation, develops IPSec Protocols software within the security chip, and realizes dual encryption and authentication function in IP layer and application layer supporting the national cryptographic algorithm.

This paper presents a methodology for characterizing and linearizing a high-efficiency wideband radio frequency power amplifier. The approach involves multi-tone excitation to extract nonlinear behavior of the device under test and optimize model parameters. A hybrid model consisting of memory polynomial and dynamic deviation terms is used to evaluate different training methods under the multi-tone stimuli. The resulting compensator achieves an ACLR and NMSE of -46 dBc and -38 dB, respectively, with linearity improvements within 3 dB of the theoretical limit compared to the optimal solution. The model parameters are robust and work well up to 80 MHz instantaneous bandwidth, including contiguous and non-contiguous carrier configurations.

Many e-Government services require qualified electronic signatures (QES) for secure authentication of citizens. However, the use of traditional server signature solutions that require two separate devices (PC and mobile device) to provide two separate communication channels for authentication has caused usability issues, especially for mobile-only services. 

To address this challenge, modern smartphones with secure hardware elements and biometric authentication methods can provide secure authentication for a server-based signature solution using only one channel. Thus, a new server-based signature solution for QES that only requires a single mobile device for authentication against a remote trust service provider has been developed. 

This solution enhances the usability of authentication by reducing the requirement to only one mobile device and integrating new authentication methods, such as fingerprint technology, in the authentication procedure. This novel concept is now implemented as a productive solution and rolled out on a national level in Austria for the national electronic identity management (eID).

Virtual worlds are an integral part of the educational landscape and offer unique learning opportunities that are unmatched by traditional methods. One important aspect of 3D virtual worlds is the presence of intelligent pedagogical agents designed to enhance user interaction and improve learning experiences. This research aims to evaluate the impact of pedagogical agents on student engagement and learning experiences during training activities in virtual worlds. Specifically, we examine the role of pedagogical agents as learning companions during specific exercises and activities, and the influence of their guidance on student engagement and learning.

In order to assess the impact of pedagogical agents, an experimental evaluation study was conducted in a 3D virtual world educational environment that focused on aspects of environmental engineering. Results from the study demonstrate that the assistance and guidance offered by pedagogical agents have a significant impact on student engagement and learning experiences. This indicates that pedagogical agents play a vital role in facilitating effective learning in virtual worlds.

Overall, this study shows that the use of pedagogical agents in virtual worlds can greatly enhance the learning experience of students. Their ability to assist and guide students in their learning journey can lead to increased engagement and improved performance. Therefore, the implementation of pedagogical agents should be considered an essential element in the development and use of virtual worlds for educational purposes.

Agriculture plays a significant role in boosting the economic growth and development of a country. However, a major challenge that affects the productivity of crops is the inappropriate choice of crops by farmers. To address this issue, a crop recommendation system that employs ensembling techniques of machine learning is recommended. The ensembling technique combines multiple machine learning models to create a model that can accurately recommend crops based on soil specific characteristics. The base learners used in this ensemble model include Random Forest, Naive Bayes, and Linear SVM. Each of these classifiers provides its set of class labels, which are then combined using the majority voting technique. 

The crop recommendation system classifies input soil datasets into two categories namely Kharif and Rabi, based on physical and chemical attributes and climatic conditions such as average rainfall and surface temperature samples. The system provides a high accuracy rate of 99.91% in recommending the right crop for cultivation. Thus, a crop recommendation system that uses ensembling techniques of machine learning can help increase crop productivity and promote agricultural development in the country.

With explosive growth of Android malware and due to the severity of its damages to smart phone users, efficient Android malware detection methods are urgently needed. As is known to us, different categories of applications divided by their functions use sensitive data in distinct ways. Besides, in each category, malicious applications treat sensitive data differently from benign applications. We thus propose TFDroid, a novel machine learning-based approach to detect malware using the related topics and data flows of Android applications. We test TFDroid on thousands of benign and malicious applications. The results show that TFDroid can correctly identify 93.7% of all malware.

In wireless sensor networks (WSNs), self-organization and localization capabilities are crucial requirements. Current methods of localization primarily focus on improving accuracy and minimizing position error; however, reducing the implementation cost of the localization algorithm has recently received particular attention. This paper revisits the theory of the wireless sensor network localization problem (SNLP) as a multi-objective optimization problem (MOO-SNLP), aiming to maximize location accuracy and minimize localization cost. Evaluation criteria and performance metrics are discussed to illustrate the trade-off between location accuracy and implementation cost, including energy consumption and communication overhead.

With the emergence of Internet-of-Things (IoT) and ever-increasing demand for the newly connected devices, there is a need for more effective storage and processing paradigms to cope with the data generated from these devices. In this study, we have discussed different paradigms for data processing and storage including Cloud, Fog, and Edge computing models and their suitability in integrating with the IoT. Moreover, a detailed discussion on low latency and massive connectivity requirements of future cellular networks in accordance with machine-type communication (MTC) is also presented. Furthermore, the need to bring IoT devices to Internet connectivity and a standardized protocol stack to regulate the data transmission between these devices is also addressed, while keeping in view the resource-constraint nature of IoT devices.

A significant number of IoT applications that seek to connect a wide range of low-complexity IoT devices are driving the digital revolution, making an interconnected daily life a reality. However, when it comes to the connectivity sector, a comprehensive technical solution seems unlikely. This is where future 5G networks come in, aiming to provide unified connectivity with an ambitious node density of 1,000,000 devices per square kilometer in the area of 5G massive Machine Type Communication (mMTC). In this context, this work analyzes the capability of LoRaWAN as a complementary solution in unlicensed frequency bands to meet specific mMTC applications' 5G requirements in large-scale deployments.

The performance evaluation indicates that regulatory requirements for the 868 MHz short-range device (SRD) frequency band lead to limited downlink capabilities. However, the uplink can cover approximately 10% of the 5G mMTC connection density objective. Hence, LoRaWAN showcases a high potential to contribute to 5G mMTC application areas, particularly for non-time-critical sensor use cases with low or no Quality of Service (QoS) requirements.

To guarantee high precision control and assure the reliability and safety of the railway systems operation, highly accurate measurement data from different onboard and wayside sensors are needed. This paper proposes a solution approach to obtain more accurate measurement data which are collected during train movement using an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF)-based multi sensors data fusion. Several sensors that are used in the proposed approach include indoor positioning systems, radio frequency identification, and rotary encoder. Experimental results that were conducted on a train model show how the proposed method effectively able to provide more accurate measurement data about the train position.

Repair of multiple partially failed cache nodes is studied in a distributed wireless content caching system, where r out of a total of n cache nodes lose part of their cached data. Broadcast repair of failed cache contents at the network edge is studied; that is, the surviving cache nodes transmit broadcast messages to the failed ones, which are then used, together with the surviving data in their local cache memories, to recover the lost content. The trade-off between the storage capacity and the repair bandwidth is derived. It is shown that utilizing the broadcast nature of the wireless medium and the surviving cache contents at partially failed nodes significantly reduces the required repair bandwidth per node.

Nowadays, Soft Computing approaches are frequently used in Computer and Information Technology. Soft Computing techniques, such as Fuzzy Logic, Genetic Algorithms, and Artificial Neural Networks, have become fundamental in solving complex computational problems. However, some Soft Computing approaches, like deep neural networks, require a significant amount of computational power, which can often lead to longer execution times. 

Fortunately, Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) can provide an efficient way to use all computational resources in the form of streaming processors. Moreover, Computed Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) is a parallel framework specifically designed for GPUs, and it is used widely to implement different Soft Computing techniques. 

In this article, we provide a brief introduction to GPU and CUDA and various Soft Computing techniques. We also provide an analytical review of the implementation of different Soft Computing techniques, which leverage GPU and CUDA's parallel processing capabilities, leading to faster execution times and increased efficiency.

Overall, the use of GPU and CUDA has significantly improved the ability of Soft Computing techniques to solve complex computational problems, and this trend is likely to continue in the future.

Extractive text summarization is to find the important sentences from texts and concatenates these sentences as a summary. However, sentences selected according to ranking rules are usually not coherent. Is a larger language unit such as a group of sentences or a paragraph more appropriate to be selected for summarization? This paper is to answer this question. Investigating the summarization algorithm based on ranking semantic link networks of texts, we find the following three results: 1) comparing with the summaries composed by sentences, the summaries composed by larger language units have similar ROUGE scores but have better readability; 2) using a group of sentences is more effective than using sentence and paragraph; and, 3) the quality of summaries composed by group becomes better when the average length of the source texts increases.

Stakeholder analysis is a crucial element in the elicitation of requirements, and the SIG (Stakeholder Intention Graph) model provides a data-driven approach to this process. The SIG model is an extension of the property graph model that represents stakeholders' intentions and their relationships. The system uses a structural analysis and SIG generation method from speech data to elicit the stakeholders' intentions during meetings. 

The analysis of stakeholders' intentions and their structure is done using graph theory, with both global and local graph analyses. Using the graph database Neo4j, the speech data-driven stakeholder analysis system automatically generates the stakeholder matrix as output. 

By applying the analysis method and system to actual development meetings on public service systems, the effectiveness of the proposed method has been demonstrated. This data-driven approach to stakeholder analysis can significantly improve the requirements elicitation process, ensuring that stakeholders' intentions are thoroughly understood and represented.

Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a respiratory disorder characterized by interruption to breathing during sleep. Usually, the OSA is more severe in the supine sleeping position. Recent studies also demonstrated that the head position may play an important role in the pathophysiology of the OSA. Therefore, monitoring the sleeping body and the head position has high clinical importance to optimize the treatment of the OSA. In this paper, three machine learning approaches were used to detect the head position during sleep in infrared images. In the first two methods, supervised classifiers were trained to estimate the head position based on different feature sets extracted from infrared images. In the third method, three different convolutional neural network (CNN) structures (ResNet50, MobileNet, and Darknet19) were trained to detect the head position during sleep. To detect the body position, the same CNN architectures were trained on infrared images. Overnight sleeping data (sleep duration =5±1h) from 50 participants (age: 53 ± 15 years, BMI: 29 ± 6 kg/m2, and 30 men/20 women) with various levels of OSA severity as measured by the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI =25±29 events/h and OSA severity: 12 normal, 13 mild, 11 moderate, and 14 severe) were collected for this paper. The models were trained on the data collected in one laboratory room from half of the participants and tested on the data from the other half collected in a different laboratory room. The best performing model (Darknet19) correctly estimated the lateral versus supine head position with 92% accuracy and 94% F1-Score and the lateral versus supine body position with 87% accuracy and 87% F1-Score.

Microgrid platforms are increasingly integrating distributed and cooperative control, combined with communication links to ensure the safe and reliable operation of distributed power generators. However, these networks are vulnerable to attacks due to the widespread use of communication networks in their control layers. In this paper, we demonstrate the practical feasibility and the impact of a novel attack, named measurement as reference attack (MaR), on the distributed control mechanism of a microgrid.

Our work involves building a hardware platform that simulates a microgrid with DG units based on Raspberry Pi and Arduino boards, DC motors for power generation, and light bulbs as electrical loads. We study two variations of the MaR attack, using man-in-the-middle (MITM) and malware techniques to demonstrate the impact on the microgrid synchronization and its voltage stability, which can affect end-user's electrical devices.

Overall, this research sheds light on the vulnerabilities of microgrid platforms and highlights the importance of strengthening their security measures to ensure the safe and reliable operation of distributed power generators.

The Extended Kalman Filter (EFF) is often used for speed estimation in sensorless control of induction motors (IM). The major issue with implementation is the selection of the process of calculating system and noise covariance matrices; traditionally determined using trial-and-error “tuning” or genetic algorithm optimization. In this paper, we study the Enhanced Fireworks Algorithm (EFWA) as a method of optimizing the Extended Kalman Filter parameters for estimating the rotor speed. The EFWA algorithm explores and exploits the search space for the optimal solution by using cooperative “swarm” intelligence. A Simulink model of a system comprised of an induction motor controlled by a variable frequency drive (VFD) operating in constant volts/hertz (V/Hz) mode is used to experiment with the method under varying operating conditions. Our results indicate that EFWA optimization provides better results than the alternative state-of-the-art genetic algorithm (GA) for a comparable number of parameter set trials.

Feature selection is a vital technique to reduce the dimensionality of data, alleviate irrelevant information and enhance the learning accuracy of the model. However, the curse of dimensionality imposes a significant challenge to the existing feature selection methods, rendering them inefficient and ineffective. 

To overcome this challenge, this research employs three feature selection algorithms, namely Fast Correlation Based Feature Selection (FCBF), a variant of FCBF called Fast Correlation Based Feature Selection # (FCBF#), and Fast Correlation Based Feature Selection in Pieces (FCFBiP). These algorithms are compared, and the experimental results indicate that the FCFBiP algorithm is more efficient than the FCBF and FCBF# algorithms.

The FCFBiP algorithm is designed to tackle the curse of dimensionality by dividing high-dimensional data into small pieces and then conducting feature selection on each part separately. This approach significantly reduces the computational complexity of the algorithm and enhances its efficiency.

In conclusion, the use of feature selection algorithms is crucial in managing high-dimensional data. The FCFBiP algorithm provides a comprehensive solution to the problem of dimensionality by being efficient and effective. This research demonstrates the significance of feature selection algorithms in enhancing the accuracy and computational efficiency of machine learning models.

Social media have become increasingly popular for the sharing and spreading of user-generated content due to their easy access, fast dissemination, and low cost. Meanwhile, social media also enable the wide propagation of cyber frauds, which leverage fake information sources to reach an ulterior goal. The prevalence of untrustworthy information sources on social media can have significant negative societal effects. In a trustworthy social media system, trust calculation technology has become a key demand for the identification of information sources. Trust, as one of the most complex concepts in network communities, has multi-criteria properties. However, the existing work only focuses on single trust factor, and does not consider the complexity of trust relationships in social computing completely. In this paper, a multi-criteria trustworthiness calculation mechanism called Info-Trust is proposed for information sources, in which identity-based trust, behavior-based trust, relation-based trust, and feedback-based trust factors are incorporated to present an accuracy-enhanced full view of trustworthiness evaluation of information sources. More importantly, the weights of these factors are dynamically assigned by the ordered weighted averaging and weighted moving average (OWA-WMA) combination algorithm. This mechanism surpasses the limitations of existing approaches in which the weights are assigned subjectively. The experimental results based on the real-world datasets from Sina Weibo demonstrate that the proposed mechanism achieves greater accuracy and adaptability in trustworthiness identification of the network information.

Zero-determinant strategies provide a novel perspective for revealing the relation between a game strategy and the cost, and play an important role in effectively controlling and optimizing the costs against virus spreading in vaccination games. We explore in this paper how the social cost can be optimized when a self-interested individual adopts the newly proposed admin-cost-based zero-determinant strategy (AZDS) to unilaterally control his own cost. In contrast to the traditional belief of the conflicts between personal interest and public (social) interest, we find that the AZDS is a win-win mechanism which presents the advantage in optimizing both the individual cost and social cost simultaneously. Taking into account the differences between the individuals (nodes) in a network, we investigate the topological influence on the performance of the AZDS implemented by the administrator, and conclude that the control capability of the administrator depends on not only one's degree but also the network average degree, and the AZDS implemented by the administrators with different degrees have different sensitivities to the change of economic incentive. Some real social networks with community structure illustrate the effectiveness of the AZDS by introducing the coarse graining method.

Remote shell sessions via protocols such as SSH are essential for managing systems, deploying applications, and running experiments. However, combined with weak passwords or flaws in the authentication process, remote shell access becomes a major security risk, as it allows an attacker to run arbitrary commands in the name of an impersonated user or even a system administrator. For example, remote shells of weakly protected systems are often exploited in order to build large botnets, to send spam emails, or to launch distributed denial of service attacks. Also, malicious insiders in organizations often use shell sessions to access and transfer restricted data. In this work, we tackle the problem of detecting malicious shell sessions based on session logs, i.e., recorded sequences of commands that were executed over time. Our approach is to classify sessions as benign or malicious by analyzing the sequence of commands that the shell users executed. We model such sequences of commands as n-grams and use them as features to train a supervised machine learning classifier. Our evaluation, based on freely available data and data from our own honeypot infrastructure, shows that the classifier reaches a true positive rate of 99.4% and a true negative rate of 99.7% after observing only four shell commands.

Since the introduction of the bacterial foraging optimization algorithm (BFO), numerous variants have been designed to improve its performance in various fields. However, researchers are constantly exploring new methods to enhance its capabilities and create new variants with superior performance. One such variant, the bacterial foraging optimization using strategies of progressive exploitation approximating local optimum and adaptive raid (BFO-DX), was recently proposed. 

The BFO-DX variant incorporates two unique strategies to improve the original BFO algorithm. Firstly, the progressive exploration approximating local optimum (PELO) strategy was introduced to enhance BFO's ability to exploit local spaces. This allows the algorithm to better determine global optima. Secondly, the adaptive raid for the leader (ARL) strategy was adopted to strengthen the exploration capacity and increase convergence speed. 

Numerical experiments have shown that the BFO-DX variant has a better ability to find global optima, higher stability, and acceptable iteration and running times compared to existing algorithms such as the classical genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm algorithm (PSO), and conventional bacterial foraging optimization (BFO).

New IoT applications are demanding for more and more performance in embedded devices while their deployment and operation poses strict power constraints. We present the security concept for a customizable Internet of Things (IoT) platform based on the RISC-V ISA and developed by several Fraunhofer Institutes. It integrates a range of peripherals with a scalable computing subsystem as a three dimensional System-in-Package (3D-SiP). The security features aim for a medium security level and target the requirements of the IoT market. Our security architecture extends given implementations to enable secure deployment, operation, and update. Core security features are secure boot, an authenticated watchdog timer, and key management. The Universal Sensor Platform (USeP) SoC is developed for GLOBALFOUNDRIES' 22FDX technology and aims to provide a platform for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) that typically do not have access to advanced microelectronics and integration know-how, and are therefore limited to Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) products.

In long-term evolution (LTE) systems, there is an option to extend the size of the cyclic-prefix (CP) when the propagation environment is characterized by severe time dispersion. Such a peculiar feature makes the system more resilient against multipath distortions, but inevitably complicates the downlink synchronization task, which cannot be accomplished through conventional techniques devised for a specified CP size. In this paper, we study the problem of CP length detection in the LTE downlink in the presence of a timing uncertainty and frequency offset. In contrast to previous investigations based on heuristic arguments, our approach relies on the maximum likelihood (ML) estimation criterion. Furthermore, it accounts for the irregular LTE symbol (characterized by a different CP size), which is present in the normal CP operation mode. The resulting scheme operates in the time-domain and computes a different metric for each possible position of the irregular symbol within the observation window. Due to its flexibility, the proposed ML approach can be applied to any future multicarrier standard for the design of a CP length detection algorithm, either in the presence or in the absence of irregular symbols.

With the continuous development of the demand of electric power users, the analysis of users' electric power consumption(EPS) is becoming more and more important. The frequency of data acquisition and the dimension of data analysis are increasing, which makes the analysis of EPS behavior more precise. The development of user tag and portrait technology brings a more intuitive and concise expression to the analysis of user's EPS. Based on massive user archives, power load and EPS data, considering the user's power consumption characteristics and influencing factors, a user behavior tag library is built, and k-means algorithm is used to tag clustering to achieve different types of EPS behavior. The tag clustering results of 2000 industrial and commercial users show that the selected tags of EPS behavior is reasonable and the clustering algorithm is effective. The research results of this paper can provide powerful data support for power companies to understand the user's EPS habits, mining user's electric power needs and improve the service level.

In this paper, we address the hyperspectral image (HSI) classification task with a generative adversarial network and conditional random field (GAN-CRF)-based framework, which integrates a semisupervised deep learning and a probabilistic graphical model, and make three contributions. First, we design four types of convolutional and transposed convolutional layers that consider the characteristics of HSIs to help with extracting discriminative features from limited numbers of labeled HSI samples. Second, we construct semisupervised generative adversarial networks (GANs) to alleviate the shortage of training samples by adding labels to them and implicitly reconstructing real HSI data distribution through adversarial training. Third, we build dense conditional random fields (CRFs) on top of the random variables that are initialized to the softmax predictions of the trained GANs and are conditioned on HSIs to refine classification maps. This semisupervised framework leverages the merits of discriminative and generative models through a game-theoretical approach. Moreover, even though we used very small numbers of labeled training HSI samples from the two most challenging and extensively studied datasets, the experimental results demonstrated that spectral-spatial GAN-CRF (SS-GAN-CRF) models achieved top-ranking accuracy for semisupervised HSI classification.

This paper presents a novel technique for estimating the key parameters of a Universal Filtered Multicarrier (UFMC) waveform using a cyclostationarity based algorithm. The parameters of interest include the symbol duration, filter length, number of subbands and their size, as well as the number of subcarriers. The proposed algorithm is designed to function proficiently under low Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) in multipath channel conditions. The performance of the algorithm is evaluated via simulations, and the results indicate that the algorithm outperforms existing methods. 

In addition to assessing the algorithm's performance under various low SNR conditions, the authors compare its performance under different processing times using various parameters. The results show that the proposed technique improves estimation accuracy, outperforms existing estimation techniques, and provides superior performance in a shorter amount of processing time.

One major advantage of this algorithm is that it requires no prior knowledge of the received signal, thus making it well-suited for use in cognitive radio. This technique can be used for spectrum monitoring or communication signal demodulation. It is worth mentioning that this is the first work to propose an algorithm for blind estimation of UFMC parameters, providing a significant contribution to the field of signal processing. 

Overall, this paper presents a promising method for blind UFMC parameter estimation that demonstrates superior performance in low SNR multipath channel conditions. The proposed technique has the potential to have significant implications in the field of signal processing, especially in the context of cognitive radio.

This paper describes a high speed image retrieval method executable on smartphones in real-time. This method will enable us to develop an application of smartphones which assists the visually impaired to shoot a video of an object and to distinguish that object without using the internet. Taking a video makes a visually impaired user to put the object in the camera frame correctly, and the smartphone without the internet protects the user's privacy. Our method is constructed by ORB local features and a data structure of binary decision tree. Under the experimental environment of 3.1 GHz Intel Core i7 platform with Windows 10, our system performs 54.5 ms processing time and 96.1% accuracy. Furthermore, our method achieves 30 fps processing time on a smartphone.

This live demonstration presents a brain-inspired amygdala model. Amygdala is an area of the brain that is associated with fear conditioning, which is a type of classical conditioning. The model can learn preferences through humanrobot interactions by application of classical conditioning to the model. Additionally, to develop a high speed and low power system, we design a hardware of the amygdala model, and implemented the hardware into field programmable gate array.

In this paper, we present a multi-channel convolution neural network (CNN) for blind 360-degree image quality assessment (MC360IQA). To be consistent with the visual content of 360-degree images seen in the VR device, our model adopts the viewport images as the input. Specifically, we project each 360-degree image into six viewport images to cover omnidirectional visual content. By rotating the longitude of the front view, we can project one omnidirectional image onto lots of different groups of viewport images, which is an efficient way to avoid overfitting. MC360IQA consists of two parts, multi-channel CNN and image quality regressor. Multi-channel CNN includes six parallel ResNet34 networks, which are used to extract the features of the corresponding six viewport images. Image quality regressor fuses the features and regresses them to final scores. The results show that our model achieves the best performance among the state-of-art full-reference (FR) and no-reference (NR) image quality assessment (IQA) models on the available 360-degree IQA database.

Parameter estimation is a crucial aspect of controlling permanent magnet synchronous motors, enabling fast adaptation to changing conditions and thermal monitoring by tracking resistance estimations. Model-based approaches are commonly used for this purpose, but their accuracy depends on the quality of the model used.
