There are many pieces of research about improving the ID3 algorithm by using various strategies. We improved the ID3 algorithm by addressing the equally important attributes problem in our previous work. In this paper, we extend our previous algorithm by changing the attribute selection to allow the neighboring second-place important attributes to be combined with the most important attributes. The proposed algorithm is tested on four standard benchmarks from the UCI repository. The experimental results indicate the significant reduction in the maximum depth and the classification depth of the decision tree. In addition, the testing time is also reduced while the classification accuracy is satisfying stable.

Biomedical signals like Electrocardiogram (ECG) contain crucial information related to the functionality of the heart. Computer-designed algorithms can aid in reducing cardiac emergencies by analyzing ECG disturbances. In this study, a hybrid feature extraction method involving the dual tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) was used for denoising and dimensionality reduction of non-linear features. The dataset was classified into normal and abnormal beats using five independent classifiers including support vector machine (SVM), decision tree (DT), backpropagation neural network (BPNN), feedforward neural network (FNNN), and K nearest neighbor (KNN). The proposed method was compared with pre-existing methods, and the highest percentage accuracy of 99.7% was achieved using BPNN, SVM, and KNN. The simulation results demonstrate that the shift-invariant nature of DTCWT provides a robust technique for analyzing non-linear and non-stationary ECG signals.

The development of an automatic age estimation method for human faces continues to play a crucial role in computer vision and pattern recognition. Previous studies have primarily focused on facial aging feature extraction and classification or regression model learning. However, our work considers a different aspect of the problem: how to design a framework to improve age estimation performance given a fixed feature type and learning method.

To address this issue, we present a four-stage fusion framework for facial age estimation. Beginning with gender recognition, the framework proceeds to classify individuals into gender-specific age groups. From there, age estimation is performed within each age group, leading to the final fusion stage.

In order to validate our approach, we tested the framework on three benchmark datasets: MORPH-II, FG-NET, and CLAP2016. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves age estimation performance compared to several state-of-the-art methods.

In conclusion, we propose a novel approach to facial age estimation by focusing on system structuring under a constrained condition. Our four-stage fusion framework provides a promising solution for improving the accuracy of age estimation, and we expect it will inspire further research in the field of computer vision and pattern recognition.

The interpretation of power flows from a probabilistic perspective is an important topic in the development algorithms of complex network theory for power system analysis, as it is conceived as the theoretical foundation for many new techniques such as machine learning and artificial intelligence. In this paper, we first show that power flow can be mathematically represented as the equilibrium of probabilistic energy movements on a graph. We demonstrate that such an equilibrium can be reached if the energy movements follow the commonly known random process of Markov chains. This work advances the current state of the art by showing a way that connects the power flow models and the random walk models of complex networks. Moreover, several new insights on the electrical betweenness centrality measures used in power grid vulnerability analysis are presented from this new probabilistic perspective.

Machine learning (ML) on edge computing devices is becoming popular in the industry as a means to make control systems more intelligent and autonomous. The new trend is to utilize embedded edge devices, as they boast higher computational power and larger memories than before, to perform ML tasks that had previously been limited to cloud-hosted deployments. In this work, we assess the real-time predictability and consider data privacy concerns by comparing traditional cloud services with edge-based ones for certain data analytics tasks. We identify the subset of ML problems appropriate for edge devices by investigating if they result in real-time predictable services for a set of widely used ML libraries. We specifically enhance the Caffe library to make it more suitable for real-time predictability. We then deploy ML models with high accuracy scores on an embedded system, exposing it to industry sensor data from the field, to demonstrates its efficacy and suitability for real-time processing.

In order to increase the capacity and improve the spectrum efficiency of wireless communication system, this paper proposes a rate-based iterative one-to-one matching game algorithm to realize multi users access an energy-harvesting small cells considering NOMA (non-orthogonal multiple access) in heterogeneous cellular networks. First, we use a heuristic clustering based channel allocation algorithm to assign channels to small cells and reduce the interference. Then we model user access problem as an iterative one-to-one matching game with rate as its utility, where one user matches with one small cell at each matching game and so is the small cell. After that, we propose an algorithm to iteratively enable users to access small cells in terms of proposed matching game and prove its stability. Finally, a power allocation algorithm to reallocate transmission power for each user is presented to fully use the harvesting power. Simulation results show that this algorithm outperforms OMA (orthogonal multiple access) system in efficiency besides improving the system capacity.

Emojis have evolved as complementary sources for expressing emotion in social-media platforms where posts are mostly composed of texts and images. In order to increase the expressiveness of the social media posts, users associate relevant emojis with their posts. Incorporating domain knowledge has improved machine understanding of text. In this paper, we investigate whether domain knowledge for emoji can improve the accuracy of emoji recommendation task in case of multimedia posts composed of image and text. Our emoji recommendation can suggest accurate emojis by exploiting both visual and textual content from social media posts as well as domain knowledge from Emojinet. Experimental results using pre-trained image classifiers and pre-trained word embedding models on Twitter dataset show that our results outperform the current state-of-the-art by 9.6%. We also present a user study evaluation of our recommendation system on a set of images chosen from MSCOCO dataset.

We have conducted a national survey of computing education at Japanese universities in 2016. We then developed computing curriculum standard J17 for the departments majored in computing. In this paper, we perform a comparison analysis between achievement and requirements for computing program. We collect requirements for computing programs through a survey at five J17 curriculum development committees: CS, CE, SE, IS and IT. We also compare the achievement of existing computing programs and the requirements of the committees using the proposed framework. Reasons of the differences are analyzed also in this paper. Furthermore, we find many computing programs which do not correspond to neither of the requirements. Although the analysis is performed under the context of Japan, it can also be applied to computing education at other countries.

Pedestrian detection, which has broad application prospects in video security, robotics and self-driving vehicles etc., is one of the most important research fields in computer vision. Recently, deep learning methods, e.g., Region Proposal Network (RPN), have achieved major performance improvements in pedestrian detection. In order to further utilize the deep pedestrian features of RPN, this paper proposes a novel regional proposal network model based on feature fusion (RPN_FeaFus) for pedestrian detection. RPN_FeaFus adopts an asymmetric dual-path deep model, constructed by VGGNet and ZFNet, to extract pedestrian features in different levels, which are further combined through PCA dimension reduction and feature stacking to provide more discriminant representation. Then, the low-dimensional fusion features are adopted to detect the region proposals and train the classifier. Experimental results on three widely used pedestrian detection databases, i.e, Caltech database, Daimler database and TUD database, illuminate that RPN_FeaFus gains obvious performance improvements over its baseline RPN_BF, which is also competitive with the state-of-the-art methods.

Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a childhood-onset neurodevelopmental disorder that often persists into adulthood. However, as lacking objective measures, several studies have questioned the stability in diagnosing of ADHD from childhood to adulthood. In this study, we propose a novel feature selection framework based on functional connectivity (FCs) pattern, the so-called ‘FS_RIWEL,’ which could classify ADHD from age-matched healthy controls (HCs) with $\sim 80$% accuracy (both for children and adults). More importantly, the feature space learned from child ADHD dataset can discriminate adult ADHD from HCs at $\sim 70$% accuracy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to perform a cross-cohort prediction between the adult and child ADHD using FC features. In addition, the most frequently selected FCs indicate that ADHD exhibit widely-impaired FC patterns in frontoparietal, basal ganglia, cerebellum network and so on suggesting that FCs may serve as potential biomarkers for ADHD diagnosis.

When considering agricultural industry paddy is principal food in Asian countries. Measuring the quality of rice is main challenge in agricultural industry. Quality of the rice depends on the output of the rice mills and according to the rice category, quality measurements can vary. Nowadays evaluation of rice quality is mostly doing by manually but it is relative, time consuming, costly and may be varying from person to person. This paper describes the process of rice category identification by using guided visual feature based machine vision approach. Segmented rice seed images are the basic inputs and pre-processing is done to the images of rice seeds. By using these pre-processed image samples, morphological features are extracted and by using original color image samples, color features are extracted. Then features are optimized for getting highest accuracy of classification. Extracted optimized features are given to the artificial neural network model and this neural network model is trained according to the training rice seed images. This proposed method is able to identify rice category of unknown rice seeds sample and it is able to give rice category as final output. Overall method is shown an average accuracy of 82.21%.

This paper is mainly to solve the path planning problem of swarm robots. If swarm robots work in the same environment at the same time, it is necessary to have appropriate planning methods to enable individuals in the group to complete their tasks. The solution is to use the artificial bee colony algorithm for the problem of robot path planning. Because the artificial bee colony algorithm has a high efficiency to solve the optimization problem, it tries to solve the problem of robot path planning in a distributed manner. The concept of organizing robots achieves efficient task of information processing and group working in the environment.

Refining user preferences and developing an exhaustive user profile are crucial components in creating customized recommendations for multiple applications. However, the current models cannot establish important knowledge-level relationships. In this paper, we argue that accurately processing feedback from users is critical to gaining insights into user needs and making recommendations for applications. As a result, we develop an ontological model for user feedback, which helps construct a knowledge graph pertaining to user reviews and user ratings. Specifically, we enhance the graph with reviews and topics for each application, which resolves the issue of limited user feedback. Additionally, we delve deep into the knowledge from the graph by identifying three noteworthy meta-paths, which play a significant role in calculating user similarity and providing recommendations. Our proposed feedback-based similarity calculation model (FSCM) aims to forecast the applications that are of interest to specific users. In our study, we evaluated our model with 1386 reviews from a mobile application store. The results of our approach demonstrate an improvement in prediction accuracy and an enhancement in the interpretability of analytical results.

The article proposes a fault diagnosis method for transmission machinery by extracting fault features from vibration signals of rolling bearings. The method combines the use of VMD and fast kurtogram to extract the IMF containing fault information and determine the center frequency and bandwidth of the reconstructed signal, respectively. The fault characteristic frequency is then extracted through band-pass filtering and squared envelope spectrum. Experimental data shows that this method is effective for fault feature extraction of rolling bearings.

A prominent contender for connecting low-power IoT devices on a city-wide scale are LP-WANs that facilitate long-distance communication with minimal power consumption, albeit with limited throughput. However, deploying and maintaining such networks pose significant challenges and opportunities to enable innovative sensing applications. This paper outlines our vision for a cloud-based LPWAN infrastructure that enables such capabilities, while addressing key challenges associated with the network. We also emphasize the immense potential of LPWANs in enabling unique applications that conventional wireless technologies struggle to deploy. Ultimately, we envision connected cities of the future where LP-WANs play a pivotal role in their realization.

Cloud Computing (CC) is a paradigm that offers a wide range of services to individuals and organizations through a scalable and distributed computing environment. With minimal management required from clients, it provides a shared pool of resources that can be dynamically adjusted to meet the demands of users. However, despite the growing number of businesses and individuals using public and private CC services, there is still skepticism regarding their security risks. Research on CC security to improve security is essential, but there is still no consensus on how to achieve a satisfactory level of trust for CC clients.

This paper presents two proposals to contribute to this area of research. The first proposal suggests the implementation of a uniform CC service model that will help earn the trust of clients. The second proposal proposes the use of Context-sensitive Role-Based Access Control (CRBAC) to establish identity and enforce security and privacy for CC service transactions. 

The uniform CC service model will provide standardization to the way CC services are delivered, ensuring a consistent level of security for all clients. This model will address the current fragmented approach towards CC service delivery and help reassure clients that their assets are secure in the cloud.

Furthermore, the application of CRBAC method will provide a more granular approach towards security and privacy for CC service transactions. It will enable the implementation of policies that regulate access control and ensures that authorized users are granted access to resources they require, while preventing unauthorized access from malicious entities. 

In conclusion, the implementation of a uniform CC service model and the application of CRBAC method will provide a practical approach towards addressing the security concerns linked to CC services. By implementing these proposals, clients can be more confident about their asset security and privacy when using CC services.

Ontology is the foundation of knowledge graphs. However, traditional ontology description and representation methods, which rely on ontology descriptional language, make it challenging for individuals to understand and utilize ontology's structure. To address this issue, we propose a method to convert ontologies into complex networks. Through ontology visualization and examination of degree distribution, clustering coefficient, average path length, and eigenvector centrality, we analyze the structural characteristics of ontologies. Our findings indicate that many ontologies have tree-like structures, and a concept's importance is positively related to its degree and eigenvector centrality. Our method has been tested on university ontology and showed a significant improvement in intuitively comprehending the ontology structure.

Convolution Neural Network (ConvNet) offers a high potential to generalize input data. It has been widely used in many application areas, such as visual imagery, where comprehensive learning datasets are available and a ConvNet model can be well trained and perform the required function effectively. ConvNet can also be applied to network intrusion detection. However, the currently available datasets related to the network intrusion are often inadequate, which makes the ConvNet learning deficient, hence the trained model is not competent in detecting unknown intrusions. In this paper, we propose a ConvNet model using transfer learning for the network intrusion detection. The model consists of two concatenated ConvNets and is built on a two-stage learning process: learning a base dataset and transferring the learned knowledge to the learning of the target dataset. Our experiments on the NSLKDD dataset show that the proposed model can improve the detection accuracy not only on the test dataset containing mostly known attacks (KDDTest+) but also on the test dataset featuring many novel attacks (KDDTest-21) - about 2.68% improvement on KDDTest+ and 22.02% on KDDTest-21 can be achieved, as compared to the traditional ConvNet model.

A new method has been developed to solve optimal control problems containing nonsmooth optimal control solutions. The paper proposes a modified version of the Legendre-Gauss-Radau (LGR) orthogonal direct collocation method, which includes an additional variable and two extra constraints at the end of each mesh interval. The extra variable is the switch time where a discontinuity occurs, and the two extra constraints comprise a collocation condition on each differential equation (a function of control) and a control constraint at the endpoint of the mesh interval (which determines the location of the nonsmoothness).

These additional constraints modify the search space of the non-linear programming (NLP) problem, providing an accurate approximation to the location of the nonsmoothness. An example with a nonsmooth solution is used throughout the paper to demonstrate the superiority of this method over the standard Legendre-Gauss-Radau collocation method.

The Internet of Things is growing at a dramatic rate and extending into various application domains. We have designed, implemented, and evaluated a resilient and decentralized system to enable dynamic IoT choreographies. We applied it to maintaining the functionality of building automation systems so that new devices can appear and vanish on-the-fly.

This paper proposes an optimal fault-tolerant control (FTC) method using a zero-sum differential game for a class of nonlinear systems with actuator faults. The FTC problem is shown to be equivalent to a zero-sum differential game problem, where the controller and the fault are regarded as two opposite players. The Nash-equilibrium is then established by minimax principle, and the coupling Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs (HJI) equation is further solved by adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) method. Additionally, a FTC learning law of the weight is proposed, which only utilizes a critic network. Finally, an example is provided to demonstrate the practicality and effectiveness of the obtained theoretical results.

Neighbor discovery, meaning that a node receives other nodes' radio frequency (RF) signals to be aware of their existence, is an indispensable procedure in Internet of Things (IoT)-oriented peer-to-peer (P2P) networks with energy-limited nodes. The main objective of neighbor discovery methods is to improve the energy efficiency, since node energy is usually very limited. As the neighborship maintaining time is very short in the mobile networks, neighbor discovery should be achieved in a very energy-efficient manner. The existing neighbor discovery methods only consider the received RF signals from other nodes (or neighbor table information derived from the received RF signals) as the basis of neighborship evaluation. The neighborship evaluation is inaccurate when the single source of neighbor information is employed. Inaccurate neighborship causes incorrect active slot scheduling and low energy efficiency of neighbor discovery. This paper proposes a generalized and probabilistic neighborship evaluation model to unify a variety of neighborship information in IoT-oriented P2P networks into neighborship probability values. Based on the model, we propose an energy-efficient neighbor discovery middle-ware algorithm by carefully replanning active slots of nodes according to the neighborship probability. The simulation evaluation results show that our proposed method decreases the average discovery delay by up to 11.46%, approximately, compared with other methods at the same energy budget.

The rapid depletion of global fossil fuel resources has necessitated urgent research for renewable energy sources. Nowadays, there are many forms of renewable energy, the most commonly used are: solar, wind and hydraulic. Wind water pumping system is considered as a promising application of renewable energy industry sustained by the increased interest on sustainable development and the reduction of greenhouse effect.This paper focuses on developing of pumping system supplied by wind turbine source; and to reach the maximum power point (MPPT), this technique is based on Artificial Neural Network to get better performance especially because these intelligent techniques do not require a precise model, we added to our system a battery and DC voltage controller based also on ANN.Finally, simulation results are given to show the effectiveness and feasibility of the approach.

Double-peaked profiles in spectral data are a rare yet valuable phenomenon for astronomers. However, identifying them has traditionally relied on visual inspection due to the complex and distinctive nature of astronomical data. To address this challenge, we propose a search algorithm called DoPS, which utilizes a relevant subspace (RS) mining algorithm and support vector machine (SVM) to automatically detect double-peaked profiles.

The DoPS algorithm first extracts a characteristic subspace using the RS mining algorithm, which incorporates a local density factor λ to measure data sparsity. Next, the characteristics of double-peaked profiles are represented by the locations, interval spaces, and strength ratios of double peaks. These characteristics are analyzed and grouped based on the correlations among them using frequent patterns and rough set theory. 

The double-peaked profiles search algorithm is then proposed by using the support vectors trained from labeled samples as thresholds. Finally, we test the DoPS algorithm using several spectral datasets from the LAMOST survey. The experimental results demonstrate that DoPS outperforms other similar algorithms in terms of time efficiency, noise immunity, and recall, as well as reduced rates.

In conclusion, the DoPS algorithm provides a reliable and efficient method for automatically detecting double-peaked profiles in astronomical data. Its ability to handle complex and unique features of spectral data makes it a valuable tool for astronomers in their research endeavors.

Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a significant cause of ischemia, yet diagnosing it is challenging due to the lack of specific screening measures. In a 2014 National Research Consensus Conference on Gender-Specific Research in Emergency Care, CMD was identified as one of the five priority areas for investigation. In an effort to diagnose CMD more accurately, this study utilized machine learning methods that incorporate both structured and unstructured narratives in clinical notes. The study found that structured data alone were not sufficient to diagnose CMD, but integrative unstructured data significantly increased the accuracy of the diagnostic model.

This contribution discusses the power handling issues related to the effective exploitation of time-modulated arrays (TMA) for multi-sine wireless power transmission (WPT), in the UHF band. It is shown that the co-design of the antenna array and of the nonlinear feeding network is a mandatory procedure during which both the slow modulation switching regime and the fast RF regime need to be simultaneously accounted for. The resulting final topology has to be determined as the best compromise between the on- and the off-states switches conditions. We also discuss the rules to select the proper device for switching operations over a wide range of power levels. Finally the performances are provided in terms of the far-field behavior of the entire TMA designed for multi-sine WPT.

Finding the optimal location for wind turbines is a challenge due to the various effects of the turbine wake. If turbines are placed too close, there is a loss of power due to the wake effect. To address this issue, this paper proposes the RC-MPGA method, a Real Coded Multi-population Genetic Algorithm, to search for the optimal location of wind turbines in a square-shaped wind farm installed on a 4000000 m2 area. The goal is to maximize the electrical power generated by all turbines and increase the WF's annual economic profitability. Results show that the proposed method is promising and improves maximum power generation when compared to other studies in the literature.

Malware poses a significant threat to Internet security today, and researchers have made substantial efforts to develop effective malware detection methods. However, existing approaches lack the ability to detect new variants of malware, thereby rendering them ineffective. To address this challenge, we present a new method for detecting malware that utilizes a family graph. Our approach begins by monitoring the API calls of the target application and creating a dependency graph based on the relationships among the API calls. We then cluster the dependency graphs of known malware families to construct a family dependency graph. This allows us to determine whether a new sample is a member of a known malware family. Our evaluation results demonstrate that our approach is highly effective and imposes minimal overhead compared to existing solutions.

In this paper, we address the downlink in a heterogeneous network with K tiers. We account for the impact of Nakagami-m fading and noise and develop closed-form approximations for the achievable average rate and coverage probability. To simplify the expressions, we utilize a piece-wise linear approximation. Our proposed results are validated through numerical simulations, which demonstrate that our approach provides a good approximation compared to existing work.

In this article, we present system for dynamic dimensional music emotion recognition (MER) and comparison of the system efficiency depending on different audio features. Experiments were performed on the database provided within the Emotion in Music task of MediaEva12015 benchmark (EiMME2015). In addition to the baseline features that were defined by the EiMME2015 organizers and included in the development data, we selected two-dimensional cepstral coefficients (TDC), linear prediction (LP) based coefficients, and the group of musical descriptors to evaluate their discriminative properties for recognition of music emotion. The experiments show that a combination of the EiMME2015 baseline features, LP coefficients and proposed set of music features significantly increases system performance for both arousal and valence emotional dimensions.

When designing complex cyber-physical systems, engineers have to integrate numerical models from different modeling environments in order to simulate the whole system and estimate its global performances. Co-simulation refers to such joint simulation of heterogeneous models. If some parts of the system are physically available, it is possible to connect these parts to the co-simulation in a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) approach. In this case, the simulation has to be performed in real-time where models execution consists in periodically reacting to the real (physically available) components and providing periodic output updates. This paper deals with the parallelization and scheduling of real-time Hardware-in-the-Loop co-simulation of numerical models on multi-core architectures. A method for defining real-time constraints that have to be met is proposed. Also, an ILP formulation as well as a heuristic are proposed to solve the problem of scheduling the co-simulation on a multicore architecture while satisfying the previously defined real-time constraints. The proposed approach is evaluated for different sizes of co-simulations and multi-core processors.

Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (Massive MIMO) is expected to be one of the key feature technology for the next cellular communication networks due to its significant benefits in terms of energy efficiency and increased spectral. To fully exploit these advantages, an accurate estimation of the Channel Impulse Response (CIR) between each transmit-receive antenna pair is crucial. In literature, it has been demonstrated that wireless communication tends to have a sparse structured CIR in delay and/or spatial domains. Several channel estimation strategies have exploited the sparsity in the massive MIMO channel based on additional assumptions on shared common support between uplink channels. In this paper, we propose a general approach which highlights the individual sparsity in the different uplink channels without any other additional assumption. To achieve this purpose, a training sequence, also known as pilot sequence and compressed sensing based CIR estimation techniques have been proposed for the massive MIMO sparse uplink channels. In order to underline the performance of proposed techniques, a comparison in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER) and Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) is performed with other CS algorithms. The simulation results have shown that proposed algorithm presents a performance gain between 5 dB and 10 dB in terms of NMSE, and a gain of 1dB to 9dB in terms of BER.

In recent years, Thailand has installed a state-of-the-art lightning detection network known as the LINET system, which employs the VLF/LF frequency regime and the TOA technique for maximum accuracy. The system is capable of providing high-quality detection efficiency, accurate location information, and 3D cloud stroke reporting. Additionally, several useful application tools have been implemented, including cell recognition and nowcasting, which enable warning and alarm and are particularly valuable to those industries sensitive to lightning danger, such as aviation and power grid operation. As a result of these advances, network expansions around Thailand are now underway.

The drastic rise of data in the World Wide Web (WWW) causes the problem for the data organization and usability of data in real life. Through constant innovations, the WWW has become a part of our everyday life and is routinely used to reach other people through various web-based applications. This paper reveals a novel similarity measure which helps to retrieve more relevant documents from the repository thus contributing considerably to the effectiveness of Web Information Retrieval (WIR) system. Bio-inspired PSO methodology is used to retrieve the top ranked documents with a reduced response time and optimizes WIR process, hence contributes to the efficiency of the system. This paper also demonstrates a comparative study of the proposed system with the existing method. Experiments are conducted on CACM collections. Better precision-recall rates are achieved than the existing system.

The security of the Internet of Things (IoT) has become increasingly concerning, and there is a pressing need to rapidly detect and fix device vulnerabilities. However, with the vast number of IoT devices, conducting regular security inspections is challenging. Current vulnerability detection technology relies on simple feature matching, which lacks the accuracy to detect firmware vulnerabilities, while direct control flow graph matching is costly. To address this problem efficiently and accurately, we propose a staged firmware vulnerability detection method based on code similarity.

Our method uses function embedding based on neural networking in the first stage to analyze function similarities, enabling the efficient inspection of large-scale firmware security. In the second stage, the similarity of function local call flow graphs is calculated, providing fine-grained firmware security analysis and improving the accuracy of vulnerability detection. Compared with state-of-the-art approaches, our method demonstrated superior accuracy in experimental results. The average retraining time for our method is just one hour, with real-world firmware vulnerability detection experiments showing an 86% true positive rate for the top 30.

Overall, our method offers an effective solution for detecting and fixing vulnerabilities in IoT devices in a timely and accurate manner. This is critical in mitigating security threats associated with the increasing prevalence of the Internet of Things.

This paper aims to address two key aspects in the field of education. Firstly, it explores the possibility of financing academic programmes and supporting students through partnerships with companies located in France. By establishing such partnerships, academic institutions can create mutually beneficial relationships with businesses that are invested in the education and training of future professionals. 

The second aspect of this paper focuses on pedagogical approaches for classes of students who participate in sandwich part-time studies. These pedagogical adaptations take into account the competencies required for these students, and aim to provide them with the most effective and efficient means of learning. 

Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the ways in which academic institutions can work with industry partners to support students and advance their education, while also exploring innovative approaches to pedagogy that can benefit both students and the institutions that provide their education.

When attempting to identify a specific module in a dynamic network, one must typically formulate a multi-input single-output (MISO) identification problem. This involves identifying all modules in the MISO structure and determining their model order. However, this can be computationally challenging in large networks, and can result in estimating a large number of parameters that are of no interest. 

To address these challenges and increase the accuracy of identified modules, a regularized kernel-based method was employed. By keeping a parametric model for the module of interest and modeling the impulse response of remaining modules as zero mean Gaussian vectors with a covariance matrix (kernel) given by the first-order stable spline kernel, noise affecting the target model output is accounted for. 

Using an Empirical Bayes (EB) approach, the target-module parameters can be estimated by maximizing the marginal likelihood of the module output. This approach is solved using the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate that this method has great potential in comparison to other state-of-the-art techniques for local identification.

Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems have the potential to significantly improve the reliability and efficiency of melanoma recognition. However, the accuracy of skin lesion segmentation in CAD is still unsatisfactory due to the large variability in lesion appearance and artifacts. To address this issue, we propose a framework that utilizes multi-stage UNets (MS-UNet) in the auto-context scheme to accurately segment skin lesions end-to-end. To enhance the performance of MS-UNet, we incorporate two approaches. Firstly, we couple UNet with a context information fusion structure (CIFS) to integrate low-level and context information in the multi-scale feature space. Secondly, we use a deep supervision mechanism to alleviate the problem of gradient vanishing by supervising MS-UNet through a weighted Jaccard distance loss function. Our approach outperforms the current state-of-the-art deep learning based methods on the ISBI 2016 Skin Lesion Challenge dataset, as shown by three out of five commonly used performance metrics, including Jaccard index and Dice coefficient.

The use of clustering in VANET has proven to be an effective technique in enhancing QoS. Current research has focused on clustering-based solutions that consider geographical distances and network dynamics (mobility). Nevertheless, the failure of infrastructure has not been taken into account, which can significantly hamper QoS when the quality of infrastructure is poor. In this paper, we propose the Intelligent Cluster Head Routing (ICHR) protocol to efficiently handle RSU failure conditions in VANET networks. We have also modified the method of selecting cluster heads to improve QoS significantly. In the event of RSU failure, the Intelligent CH (ICH) is selected among all CH nodes based on the maximum probability of three parameters. The ICH then transmits the data over an alternate neighboring RSU through the LTE network, which is already in use for providing internet connection.

Network Function Virtualization (NFV) and Software Defined Networks have completely revolutionized data networks. When deploying Virtual Network Functions (VNFs), it is crucial to consider the queuing delay that occurs in the NFV servers. In this study, we propose the incorporation of the Poisson distribution of packet arrival rate and packet size, in conjunction with the limited processing capacity of NFV servers, to improve the placement of VNFs. We frame this as a 0-1 fractional programming problem, which is solved using a 0-1 MILP to obtain the optimal solution. Due to the fact that the VNF placement problem is an NP-hard problem, we propose two heuristic algorithms for gaining solutions. Our investigations demonstrate that our algorithms effectively reduce delay by 72.9% compared with the universal algorithm Improve Service Chaining Performance (ISCP).

The internet of things (IoT) is being used more and more in our lives and this area attracts interest in studying new methods. One of these methods is mesh networking technique, which is increasingly becoming more popular and is suitable for use in places where wired connectivity is unavailable. Researchers are mostly focused on developing new and efficient services for systems running on this method, but the management of devices on mesh networks remains as an important issue. The management of an increasing number of devices can become inexhaustible. IoT management is to monitor and take action on the communication from and between connected devices and also control the devices from a remote server. This is similar to traditional network management when mesh network devices are considered. There is also a critical precaution for objects which is to complete administrative operations securely. In this article we have adapted a protocol, that is mainly used in traditional network management, for using in the management low powered personal area network (LoWPAN). We made some experimental analysis and compared our approach with other well-known IoT protocols for device management perspective.

In recent years, mobile advertising has gained popularity as a mean for publishers to monetize their free applications. One of the main concerns in the in-app advertising industry is the popular attack known as “click fraud”, which is the act of clicking on an ad, not because of interest in this ad, but rather as a way to generate illegal revenues for the application publisher. Many studies evaluated click fraud attacks in the literature, and some proposed solutions to detect it. In this paper, we propose a click fraud detection model, hereafter CFC, to classify fraudulent clicks by adopting some features and then testing using KNN, ANN and SVM. In fact, based on our experimental results, the different featured classifiers reached an accuracy higher than 93%.

The estimation of the direction of arrival for sources impinging on an antenna array is an essential aspect of mobile communications. In this article, we aim to illustrate how to obtain DOA information using Matrix Pencil (MP) with Uniform Circular Arrays (UCA) and Uniform Linear Arrays (ULA) by analyzing the receiving signals.

The primary function of the Least Mean Square algorithm (LMS) in ULA is to focus the power in the requisite direction and nullify interference. The simulation results reveal that MP is remarkably performant and stable compared to previously published methods.

Overall, this approach offers a promising solution to the problem of DOA estimation, and it can be valuable in enhancing the performance of mobile communication systems.

Mixed Weibull distributions are extensively used for lifetime modeling of products that have multiple failure modes. However, the estimation of parameters of the mixed Weibull distribution presents a difficult task due to the inclusion of multiple parameters. To address this issue, this study proposes a parameter estimation model for mixed Weibull distributions using nonlinear least squares estimation (LSE). 

The proposed method involves determining approximate values and rough bounds for the parameters, which are used as starting points for the particle swarm optimization (PSO) optimization procedure. The PSO solution of the nonlinear LSE method is developed through a step-by-step approach. 

A case study is conducted to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method outperforms the genetic algorithm (GA)-based nonlinear LSE method in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibits significant advantages over the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) method in terms of efficiency. 

Therefore, the proposed method can be considered as a powerful tool for parameter estimation of mixed Weibull distributions in lifetime modeling of products with multiple failure modes. Its effectiveness in real-world applications has been demonstrated, making it a reliable choice for researchers and practitioners.

Mission-critical applications demand UPS to provide power conditioning and backup, and the redundancy of multiple UPS units is necessary to maximize reliability. However, the upfront investment and operating costs associated with deploying excess capacity can be costly. As a result, a more cost-effective and efficient alternative is the Iso-parallel or Ring Bus architecture, which utilizes rotary UPS systems. This paper proposes the utilization of static UPS in a Ring Bus arrangement to further extend this concept. The paper initially discusses the characteristics of rotary and static UPS topologies. It then outlines the Ring Bus architecture and the associated load-sharing technique. Finally, the paper focuses on how to handle fault scenarios, as the main challenge with static UPS is their limited fault current capability. By overcoming this limitation, the deployment of static UPS in Ring Bus systems can greatly enhance their benefits.

Java-based malicious software attacks have been rapidly evolving in recent years, with attackers initially relying on finding malicious Applets and exploiting methods to gain access to victims. However, as browsers implement stronger security measures, attackers have shifted their focus to distributing malware through spear-phishing emails. This paper presents two methods for detecting Java-based malware, utilizing both unsupervised machine learning algorithms and the Perceptron algorithm to create more effective detection models. By combining these methods, we can proactively detect Java-based threats and ensure that known malware variants are still detected. Detection is particularly focused on class files, as these are often targeted by Malware as a Service attacks.

Nowadays, Information Technologies (IT) play a crucial role in various areas of organizations and their processes. However, their effectiveness largely depends on how users interact with these technologies and make use of them. Therefore, the acceptance of IT is dependent on the relationship that users have with the technologies. There are several models that have been developed to explain the acceptance of technology by the respective users. This paper introduces a new model, named the Information Technology Acceptance and Use Model (MAUTI), which helps to understand the acceptance and use of IT in an organizational environment. It can be utilized during the design, development, use, improvement, or replacement of a system. 

MAUTI is based on some of the factors that are considered in the most popular models, but it also includes new factors to provide a better explanation of the phenomenon of acceptance and use of technologies. It has a high degree of explanation, reaching an explained variance of 58%. Therefore, organizations can use it as an instrument to evaluate the role of their IT, reorganize or remodel it, with a view to its effective use by employees.

Fringe projection profilometry (FPP) is a popular optical 3-dimensional (3D) scanning method. However, existing FPP methods often suffer from the ambiguity problem that only the wrapped phase information can be measured while the true phase information is required for 3D measurement. Although various phase unwrapping methods were suggested to recover the wrapped phase in FPP methods, most of them will fail when the target objects have complex structures. To solve this problem, we propose in this paper to embed the fringe pattern with a set of textural patterns to encode the period order of the true phase information. During the offline phase, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is trained to learn a set of filters that will be activated when they see the code patterns. When the encoded fringe image is captured, the modified morphological component analysis is first performed to extract the code pattern. It is then decoded by the trained CNN to estimate the K-map, which contains the period order of the true phase information. Experimental results show that the proposed method can measure the 3D profile of objects with abrupt jumps in height profile, where the conventional approaches often fail to perform. It also has a much higher computational efficiency due to the effective utilization of GPU by CNN.

The Australian Defence Forces (ADF) including the army, navy and air force often share resources. This is the case for helicopter training where the resources are often people, e.g. instructors. Understanding the current and future needs of the helicopter pilot training continuum is challenging. New students are continually entering the Defence services as trainees/cadets; passing or failing exams at specialist flying schools; progressing through or leaving the Defence services and potentially becoming trained pilots or instructors that can subsequently train future students. This continuum has an associated optimisation challenge. The ATHENA platform has been developed as a strategic discrete event simulation, optimisation and analysis system for manpower planning with specific focus on addressing the needs and demands of this helicopter pilot training continuum for the ADF. ATHENA has been developed as a simulation platform running on a Cloud infrastructure. This paper introduces ATHENA and describes the way in which the platform leverages container technologies to auto-scale across the Cloud with focus on the Kubernetes orchestration technology.

The cloud computing model is the most complex computing model that requires the implementation of effective techniques to manage the infrastructure resources of datacenters. Poorly scheduled tasks can lead to an increase in the operational cost of the cloud provider, ultimately increasing the cost of cloud services at the consumer side. One effective technique to address these issues is elasticity, which allows for dynamic resource provisioning based on current demand and varying workloads running on virtual machines (VMs) over time. This leads to increased resource utilization and reduced power consumption by turning off idle physical machines. However, dynamic resource provisioning due to growing service demands and higher quality of service requirements of users can violate the service level agreement.

In this paper, we propose a linear regression-based model to manage and reformulate cloud user requests. The proposed model dynamically generates rules based on historical data of user requests to update association functions, address changes in different types of workloads and adapt to cloud provider datacenter. The experiments and simulation results based on dynamic workloads show that the proposed algorithm significantly increases resource utilization in cloud datacenters.

The identification of fault signals in rolling bearings can be challenging due to the presence of irrelevant harmonics and background noise that distort the feature information. In this paper, we propose a novel diagnostic approach to identify incipient periodic impulsive features in rolling bearings. To achieve this, we employ the Over-Complete Rational-Dilation Wavelet Transforms (ORDWT) to decompose the original fault signal into multiple sub-bands. 

Next, we introduce a periodic impulsive index that combines the advantages of ACFHNR, kurtosis, and Pearson's correlation coefficient index to adaptively track the most suitable fault frequency band. Finally, we obtain the envelope spectrum of the best fault frequency band for fault diagnosis. 

Our simulation and experiment results demonstrate the effectiveness of our adaptive fault frequency band detection (AFFBD) method. With this approach, it becomes possible to identify the fault symptom in time and prevent significant damage to the bearing.

This paper describes the use of differential evolution (DE) to improve the performance of an echo state neural network (ESNN). In particular, DE is used to optimize the weights of the ESNN and determine the number of fuzzy rules that should be used to model the input to the network. The goal is to develop a high-quality reservoir for the ESNN that leverages the strengths of DE and fuzzy rule base systems.

The authors demonstrate that DE can effectively pre-train the fixed weight values of the network. The fuzzy rule base system is then used to formulate a set of rules that guide the network's inferences for the inputs presented to it. The performance of the optimized network is evaluated using error metrics and computational time.

The authors compare the results of the DE-based fuzzy ESNN model to those of an ESNN without optimization and fuzzy rule, as well as to other existing techniques. They demonstrate that the DE-based fuzzy ESNN outperforms the other models in terms of both effectiveness and efficiency.

The authors test the DE-based fuzzy ESNN model on a set of time series forecasting benchmark problems and demonstrate its superiority and effectiveness. Overall, the results of this study suggest that DE can be an effective tool for optimizing the performance of ESNNs, especially when combined with fuzzy rule base systems.

This paper addresses the challenges of power grid planning data integration and the difficulty in meeting the development needs of the current power grid planning simulation and calculation capability. To overcome these limitations, the study proposes a power grid planning data structure system and power grid consistency planning decision-making system that utilize big data and cloud computing technology.

The paper proposes key technologies, functional and network architecture for the implementation of the power grid consistency planning decision-making system. The system aims to provide distributed maintenance, structured consistency management, and intelligent cloud storage of power grid planning data resources. Furthermore, the system aims to achieve dynamic allocation, overall coordination of calculation and verification, and meet the needs of power grid consistency planning simulation calculations at different management levels and voltage levels.

The developed decision-making system for power grid consistency planning was field-tested in over 120 power grid companies, illustrating its economic benefits. The system can provide technical support for large-scale power grid planning decision-making and help overcome the challenges of power grid planning data integration.

Task deployment has become a hot topic for load balancing in edge computing. In view of the problem that most of the hosts are overloaded in the edge computing, the central load is unbalanced. Much work focuses on the load balancing of the cloud data center or the short-term load balancing of edge data centers. In order to solve the host selection problem of task deployment in joint cloud data centers with edge computing while achieving the overall long-term load balancing, this paper utilizes that the deployment mode of joint cloud model, on this basis, proposes a deployment strategy HEELS based on the analysis of heuristic task clustering method and glowworm swarm optimization algorithm. Its main idea consists of two parts. First, the task with large resources in the current task set is filtered out by the clustering analysis, and the task offloading technology is exploited to upload the result to the cloud computing center for deployment and calculation. Then, the optimized GSO algorithm is exploited in the edge computing center, and the idea of SCA is combined into the optimization of step size so that the optimized GSO algorithm has an adaptive step size, achieving better global search ability in the early stage and better local convergence ability in the later stage. The experimental results show that compared with the existing research, HEELS realizes better load balancing effect and makes the joint datacenter more green and efficient.

A key aspect of smart cities is the prevalence of numerous mobile multimedia terminals. However, accommodating these devices via device-to-device (D2D) communication can lead to serious interference and energy consumption when D2D pairs reuse cellular users' channels. Thus, this paper aims to maximize the energy efficiency of D2D communication while considering the constraints of D2D pairs and cellular users' quality of service.

Since the resource allocation problem is often difficult to solve, the problem is divided into power control and channel allocation sub-problems. Specifically, a power control algorithm based on the Lambert W function is proposed to maximize a single D2D pair's energy efficiency. Then, preference values for D2D pairs and cellular users are calculated using the power control results. A channel allocation scheme based on the Gale-Shapley algorithm is then employed, which uses the preference values to match the two sides, aiming to maximize the signal-to-interference plus noise ratio of cellular users and the energy efficiency of D2D pairs.

Simulation results demonstrate that this proposed algorithm not only ensures the transmission rate of cellular users but also improves the energy efficiency of the system and D2D pairs. Overall, this approach provides a promising solution to the energy efficiency maximization problem in D2D communication.

Raw data of point cloud is often noisy and with topological defects (such as holes), which cause problems including faulty connection and inaccurate structure. As a result, the surface reconstruction of point cloud data is a highly challenging problem. This work proposes a novel method, which improves the surface quality compared with existing methods. Our method combines both the local detailed features and the global topological information during the reconstruction process. To facilitate the feature refinement, we first pre-process the point cloud data by relocating each point, upsampling the point data, and optimizing normals to enhance the features and geometric details. We then identify the topological information by segmenting the geometry and constructing curve skeletons for each part and guide the surface reconstruction with the skeletons by minimal user interaction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods with various examples, where our reconstruction can fill out missing data and preserve sharp features.

Object recognition is a key field in computer vision, with numerous applications. The aim is to identify objects of the same type despite changes in viewpoints or orientation. However, this is a challenging problem due to factors such as translation, rotation, and scaling. Shape descriptors such as Fourier and Moments are invariant to these changes, but the challenge lies in selecting the appropriate number of descriptors for a given object. Furthermore, not all descriptors may be equally important, so selecting the best descriptors through optimization techniques is crucial for maximizing recognition rate. In this study, we compare two common optimization techniques, Genetic Algorithm and Simulated Evolution, and find that Genetic Algorithm outperforms Simulated Evolution in terms of recognition rate. Extensive simulations in MATLAB were conducted to demonstrate this result.

Frame coalescing is a highly effective approach for managing low power idle (LPI) mode in energy efficient Ethernet (EEE) interfaces. This technique allows EEE interfaces to remain in LPI mode for a set period of time after receiving the first frame, or until a certain amount of traffic accumulates in the transmission buffer. In this paper, we examine the efficiency limits of both time-based and size-based coalescing techniques and propose new open-loop adaptive variants of each. Our proposals adjust the length of sleeping periods to achieve energy savings while maintaining a set average frame delay. Analytical and simulation results demonstrate that both of our proposals are comparable to the fundamental limits, making them highly efficient. We recommend the usage of the time-based algorithm in most scenarios due to its simplicity and ability to limit maximum frame delay.

This paper introduces an IP address lookup architecture using a vectored-Bloom filter (VBF) to carry out longest prefix matching. By employing the VBF, the proposed architecture can successfully determine the output port for each input IP address without relying on an off-chip memory. The study further shows how implementing the IP address lookup architecture on an FPGA in a parallel fashion can result in high-performance outcomes when it comes to search speed and throughput.

This paper details the creation and execution of a compiler that is capable of boosting the performance and energy efficiency of a deep neural network accelerator. By automating the creation of data transfer code and outer loops surrounding highly-tuned inner-loops, the compiler enables deep learning frameworks, such as TensorFlow, to take full advantage of the accelerator hardware. This process streamlines the development of deep learning libraries without compromising performance. Our team has tested and evaluated the prototype compiler, demonstrating its ability to produce code for the most important deep learning operators, yielding comparative performance to hand-crafted code.

This paper proposes a novel approach to detect replay attack by utilizing the reverberation and channel information from non-voiced segments of utterances. Non-voiced segments are identified by a voice activity detector and are likely to contain crucial information about reverberation and channel. Multiple feature representations are employed to capture the remains of vocal tract information in non-voiced segments. Gaussian mixture models are constructed to develop three different baseline systems, each corresponding to different features. Voting is executed to determine whether an input utterance is replayed or not. The likelihood ratio of the genuine and spoofed model is computed to calculate the equal error rate (EER) from the best baseline system. Experimentation on the ASV-Spoof-2017 challenge dataset shows that the proposed approach surpasses the best baseline system with a relative improvement of 37% concerning EER.

It is crucial for doctors to fully understand the interaction between drugs in prescriptions, especially when a patient takes multiple medications at the same time during treatment. The purpose of drug drug interaction (DDI) extraction is to automatically obtain the interaction between drugs from biomedical literature. Current state-of-the-art approaches for DDI extraction task are based on artificial intelligence and natural language processing. While such existing DDI extraction methods can provide more knowledge and enhance the performance through external resources such as biomedical databases or ontologies, due to the difficulty of updating, these external resources are delayed. In fact, user generated content (UGC) is another kind of external medical resources that can be quickly updated. We are trying to use UGC resources to provide more available information for our deep learning DDI extraction method. In this paper, we present a DDI extraction approach through a new attention mechanism called full-attention which can combine the UGC information with contextual information. We conducted a series of experiments on the DDI 2013 Evaluation dataset to evaluate our method. Experiments show improved performance compared with the state of the art and UGC-DDI model achieves a competitive F-score of 0.712.

The uses and applications of VR and AR technologies have been widespread in the last few years. One of its most important areas of use is the use of virtual and augmented reality in education, learning and training. Hence, this research paper examines the latest developments and the scientific findings in the field of augmented software industry, its applications, and uses in teaching, learning and training. Tens of augmented reality applications, their areas of application, and practical uses were studied with the aim of: Identifying strengths and weaknesses and selecting the appropriate ones in teaching, learning and training. To achieve the objectives of the research: The method of content analysis based on the applied approach was used, The researcher recommended: It is necessary to adopt the application and usage of augmented reality technologies in education, learning and training at the highest levels, and recommended the use of a set of software and platforms that would enhance the quality of teaching, learning and training and improve its outcomes.

The traditional mixed-criticality (MC) model only allows critical tasks to execute during an error or exception. However, the imprecise MC (IMC) model has been introduced to provide some (degraded) service to less critical tasks even during exceptional events, such as when a task overruns its execution demand. We are currently working on extending the IMC model to precise scheduling of tasks and integrating it with a dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) scheme for energy minimization.

Scheduling precise MC systems is a challenging task since all tasks must be guaranteed to be timed correctly under both pessimistic and less pessimistic assumptions. To achieve this, we propose a utilization-based schedulability test and sufficient schedulability conditions for the earliest deadline first with virtual deadline (EDF-VD) scheduling policy. Using this unified model, we perform a quantitative study in the forms of a speedup bound and approximation ratio.

Finally, we conduct both theoretical and experimental analysis to demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of our algorithm. This work presents a significant advancement in the MC model and will enable energy-efficient, precise scheduling of tasks in mixed-criticality systems.

An effective way to approach non-parallel voice conversion (VC) is to use deep neural networks, specifically variational auto encoders (VAEs), to model speech's latent structure in an unsupervised way. A previous study has confirmed the effectiveness of VAE using STRAIGHT spectra for VC. However, VAE using other spectral features, such as mel-cepstral coefficients (MCCs), which are related to human perception and frequently used in VC, have not been adequately studied. Instead of using just one type of spectral feature, VAE is expected to benefit from using multiple types simultaneously, which will improve its capability for VC. We propose a new VAE framework, called cross-domain VAE (CDVAE), for VC. The proposed framework uses both STRAIGHT spectra and MCCs, explicitly regulating multiple objectives to constrain the learned encoder and decoder's behavior. Experimental results show that the proposed CD-VAE framework outperforms conventional VAE frameworks in subjective tests.

Haptic guidance is an effective method for repetitive motor training, in which an haptic interface is used to physically guide the subject through an ideal motion. Additional sensory feedback, such as visual modality, enhances the effectiveness of haptic guidance by increasing the learner's active participation and engagement. To investigate this hypothesis, we analyzed the brain state of learners during haptic training, focusing on sensorimotor rhythms (SMR) as they are associated with engagement in motor tasks. In our circle-drawing haptic training experiment, we recorded electroencephalogram (EEG) while subjects memorized guided trajectories in an unimodal haptic workspace. We found a clear trend that subjects who demonstrated performance improvement showed stronger desynchronization of beta rhythms over the contralateral hemisphere, which is associated with motor skills retention. Therefore, our results provide accumulating evidence that active participation is crucial for haptic training.

This paper explores the application of the dilated convolution algorithm, typically used in image segmentation, in the field of image classification. Convolution neural networks (CNN) have traditionally played a crucial role in image classification algorithms, but their resource-intensive nature has been a challenge. To address this issue, the paper introduces a dilated CNN model that leverages dilated convolution kernels to reduce computation requirements. The model is tested on the Mnist handwritten digit recognition dataset. 

To mitigate the detail loss problem in the dilated CNN, the paper proposes a hybrid dilated CNN (HDC) model, generated by stacking dilated convolution kernels with varying dilation rates. The HDC model is evaluated against a wide-band remote sensing image dataset, and the results indicate that it outperforms both the traditional CNN and dilated CNN models. 

Compared to traditional CNNs, the dilated CNN model reduces training time by 12.99% and boosts training accuracy by 2.86% on average. The HDC model cuts training time by 2.02%, with corresponding improvements of 14.15% and 15.35% in training and testing accuracy, respectively. These results highlight the efficacy of dilated CNN and HDC models in improving image classification performance.

The utilization of event-triggered scheduling for network transmissions has been widely adopted in cyber-physical systems to optimize system resource utilization. This paper aims to investigate the distributed gradient method with event-triggered consensus protocols for solving convex constrained problems in large-scale systems. Our analysis shows that convergence is guaranteed if the event-triggering threshold bound is square summable and the stepsize satisfies specific constraints that incorporate the Lipschitz constant of the gradient and the spectrum of the mixing matrix linked to the network topology. We also showcase stronger convergence results for the strongly convex case in which the local estimate of the minimizer converges linearly to the minimizer until an error floor is reached. The magnitude of this error floor is proportional to the stepsize if the triggering threshold bound linearly converges. Through comprehensive numerical experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and its superiority over existing approaches.

In this case study, we develop a stacked ensemble learning method to predict the extraction efficiency of the porous network. We generate the porous network data using computational fluid dynamics numerical method. Based on this data we train several machine-learning models. The machine learning models are then used to train a super model on the predictions. Our results show that the stacked ensemble learning is significantly more efficient than every single machine-learning model. The finding of this approach has direct applications in understanding the extraction of oil from porous media.

In this paper, a nonlinear approach to modeling DC-DC PWM converters in continuous conduction mode (CCM) has been presented. The study includes the implementation of a converter nonlinear model in MATLAB and SIMULINK for both ideal and non-ideal cases, considering the impact of parasitic components. The analytical computation of periodic solutions in the high frequency steady-state operating condition allows for the systematic analysis of the dynamical behavior induced by various perturbation sources acting on the converters. 

The study reports a comparison of the dynamics generated in the ideal and non-ideal cases for both the boost and buck converters. This comparison was performed by varying the duty cycle, input voltage, and load resistance, causing step changes that reveal the behavior of the converters under different operating conditions. 

Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the behaviors of DC-DC PWM converters and highlights the importance of taking into account parasitic components in such analyses. With the implementation of the nonlinear model in MATLAB and SIMULINK, further research can be conducted to develop more efficient and reliable converter designs.

This paper provides a critical review on the state-of-the-art pedestrian and evacuation dynamics so as to comprehensively comprehend the motion behaviors of pedestrians from observations to simulation aspects. Types of typical data collection methods, namely the field survey, the controlled experiment, and the animal experiment, are classified, and the connections and differences of these three observation methods are explored. Pedestrians' complex behaviors characterized by the self-organization phenomena and movement data characterized by the fundamental diagram are then studied after the data collections, which can be used to calibrate and validate the pedestrian models. The mathematical models for pedestrian dynamics from both tactical level and operational level are also highlighted. The simulation data produced by the mathematical models could further reproduce pedestrian behaviors during the observations and contribute to decision makings for improving the evacuation efficiency. The applications of pedestrian models for behavior analysis, evacuation simulation, and layout design are also presented. Some challenges and future directions in the pedestrian and evacuation dynamics are also put forward. Findings presented in this study are helpful for researchers who want to understand the pedestrian and evacuation dynamics and to perform further research in this field.

The conventional inverse kinematics (IK) solutions for robot manipulators have various drawbacks such as no closed form solution, dependency on starting point, and limited applicability of Jacobian. To resolve these issues, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) are gaining popularity for IK analysis. However, a high number of training samples and hidden neurons can lead to computational burden. This research aims to determine the optimum number of training samples for ANN to be applied in IK solutions. The study was conducted using a 3 degrees-of-freedom (DOF) manipulator model. Through practical experimentation, it was found that the smallest sample set required was approximately 20 times greater than the allowable tracking error size. In the case study, an acceptable tracking result was achieved with only 125 training sets.

Information recommendation strategies can be broadly classified into two categories, namely collaborative filtering and content-based methods. Among these, collaborative filtering is the most commonly used technique for making personalized recommendations to users. It relies on mining user preferences from a group or community with similar interests or experience, and recommends items that may be of interest to the users. However, collaborative filtering suffers from data sparsity and cold start issues, which can affect the quality of the recommendations made.

To address this challenge, we propose a film recommendation model that builds upon the strengths of both collaborative filtering and content-based methods. Our model is based on the Doc2Vec algorithm, which uses neural networks to extract the semantic, syntactic, and ordering information of a sentence, and maps this information to a fixed dimensional feature vector. These vectors are used to model the relationships between movies and users, and the similarity between the vectors is calculated and integrated with the collaborative filtering recommendation algorithm to generate personalized recommendations for each user.

Our experiments show that the proposed model outperforms traditional collaborative filtering techniques in terms of both accuracy and recall. The accuracy of the recommendations made by our model was measured using the Mean Average Precision (MAP), which was found to be significantly higher than that of the baseline collaborative filtering model. Similarly, our model was able to achieve higher recall rates, indicating that it is able to recommend a greater number of items that are relevant to the users' interests. Collectively, our findings suggest that the proposed model may offer an effective solution to address the limitations of traditional collaborative filtering methods, and can enhance the quality of personalized recommendation systems.

The tremendous growth in ubiquitous sensor networks and IoT has led to Human Activity Recognition (HAR) emerging to be an exciting challenge. Machine learning approaches proposed in this direction have proved to be competent solutions. HAR data treatment in a recurrent form, and further analysis using deep networks such as RNNs or LSTM is largely unexplored. In this work, we treat data generated from a smart home setup towards HRA, as a series of events and perform feature extraction using a the popular LSTM variant of LSTMs. We use the Aruba dataset from the CASAS project [2]. We apply LSTM to extract features and perform annotations. Additionally we apply standard classification techniques to recognize and evaluate the different activities in the newly annotated data. From experimentations using our method we can achieve annotation accuracies of up to 79.5% which is 13.6% better than other state-of-the-art solutions.

In addition to voice, sign language and artificial larynx can serve as communication options for people with speech disorders. However, these methods may have limitations such as requiring extensive training and high costs. To address these challenges, researchers have explored the use of electromyography (EMG) analysis of lip movements to detect speech sounds.

One important application of EMG-based speech recognition is personal authentication, which can confirm the identity of a speaker based on their unique muscle signals. In this study, a small and dry sensor with two electrodes was used to capture muscle activity in the orbicularis, zygomatic, and depressor muscles during the production of Japanese vowels. The EMG signals were recorded and processed using P-EMG plus software, which involved signal cutting, spectrums analysis, noise removal, and reconstruction.

To train a machine learning model for speaker identification, a convolutional neural network was employed to analyze the EMG data sets. However, the accuracy of the model was found to vary significantly depending on the measurement date and the intra-individual variation of the subjects. Therefore, further refinement of the data and normalization of the individual differences are needed to improve the reliability of the system in the future.

Overall, EMG-based speech recognition shows promising potential as a non-invasive and accessible solution for individuals with speech impairments. By enhancing the accuracy and usability of the technology, we can help more people to communicate effectively and confidently in various situations.

We aim for a robot capable to learn sequences of motor policies to achieve a field of complex tasks. In this paper, we consider a set of interrelated complex tasks hierarchically organized. To address this high-dimensional mapping between a continuous high-dimensional space of tasks and an infinite dimensional space of sequences of policies, we introduce a framework called "procedure", which enables the creation of sequences of policies by combining previously learned skills. We propose an active learning algorithmic architecture, capable of organizing its learning process in order to achieve a field of complex tasks by learning sequences of primitive motor policies. Based on heuristics of goal-babbling, social guidance, strategic learning guided by intrinsic motivation, and the "procedure" framework, our algorithm can actively decide on which outcome to focus and which exploration strategy to apply. We show that a simulation industrial robot can tackle the learning of complex motor policies and adapt this complexity to that of the task at hand. Owing to its exploration strategies, it can discover the levels of difficulty of the tasks, and learn the hierarchy between tasks so as to combine simple tasks to complete a complex task.
