Finally, a few real-life examples are given in order to demonstrate the goals and purposes of a few different types of agents.

Content Based Image Retrieval (CBIR) is a challenging ground to retrieve the images based on feature description and extraction. Salient image features are the potential candidates to search and index the images based on primitive features. This paper presents a novel way to extract and describe the image features based on their object and color signatures. Gaussian of variance is used along with image convolution and the resultant features are approximated using matrix hashing. The high range frequency feature information is then separated to carry out the spatial indexes. High resolution images from versatile image semantic groups are resulted in massive image signatures which are computation effective. Principal component analysis is performed on these feature vectors to obtained reduced statistical information. These grey level information carriers are then combined with RGB channel based spatially arranged features to possess to color and object information. Bags-of-Word (BoW) architecture is applied to these information carriers to index and retrieve the images. Competitive results show that the proposed method outperforms in many categories of benchmarks Caltech-101 and Corel-1000 datasets. The proposed method shows outstanding results in complex and occluded image categories.

This article discusses various challenges faced during the construction of a modern intelligent traffic information physical fusion network. Problems such as complex object types, large amount of data collection, high demand for transmission and calculation, and weak real-time scheduling and control ability were identified as major obstacles. To tackle these challenges, a cloud-based control system theory was introduced, and a modern intelligent traffic control network was studied as the research object.

The article proposed a physical design of the intelligent transportation information fusion cloud control system scheme that includes two important technologies- intelligent transportation edge control technology and intelligent transportation network virtualization technology. By using intelligent traffic flow data, the central cloud control management server implemented deep learning and machine intelligence study methods to predict urban road short-term traffic flow and congestion.

Furthermore, the article introduced an intelligent optimization scheduling algorithm for real-time traffic flow control strategy. Simulation results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed method in controlling the traffic flow. Overall, the article contributes to the ongoing discussion about modern intelligent traffic information physical fusion networks and highlights the importance of implementing advanced technologies to overcome the challenges faced in such networks.

This study examines the impact of corporate social responsibility (CSR) news reports on corporate operating performance forecasting using a large database of publicly-listed electronics firms in Taiwan. By executing latent topic modelling, we can break down CSR news reports into multiple dimensions and then examine which dimension(s) affects operating performance. To offer decision-makers with a comprehensive, overarching view of the corporate's operations, the data envelopment analysis (DEA), that can handle multiple input and multiple output variables simultaneously, was conducted to generate the performance rank. The analyzed results were then fed into support vector machine (SVM) to construct the model for performance forecasting. The inherent parameters were decided by harmony search (HS) algorithm. The proposed approach, supported by real samples, can assist both internal and external stakeholders in allocating scarce resources to specific CSR dimensions to enhance a corporate's growth potential as well as to achieve a win-win situation.

This paper presents a methodology for the forward estimation of thermal risk in offshore wind farm cables under scenarios where the farm is overplanted for economic purposes. A dynamic thermal rating assessment of the cable is proposed to estimate the thermal effects of probable load current scenarios considering actual temperatures. Calculated future temperatures are used to estimate the probability of the cable being overheated. Due to the ability of the method to estimate forward thermal risk, unnecessary power curtailment can be reduced while avoiding thermal damage to the cable. Simulated results of online thermal risk estimation and curtailment show additional power delivery of 7.26%, 9.16%, and 9.67% per year for a 6%, 9.9%, and 13.7% wind farm overplanting, respectively. The additional power is calculated compared to the annual power delivered (Wh/year) with the use of the traditional continuous rating limits for the case studied.

Forecasting of consumer electricity usages plays an important role to make total smart grid system more reliable. As the activities of individual residential consumers has many uncertain variables, it is hard to accurately forecast the residential load levels. For planning of the electrical resources and to balance demand and supply, accurate forecasting tasks are critical. This paper presents Deep Neural Network (DNN) based short term load forecasting for Residential consumers. In this work, we compare the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) value for residential electricity dataset using different types recurrent neural network (RNN). Our preliminary results indicate that Long short-term memory (LSTM) based RNN performed better compared with simple RNN and gated recurrent unit (GRU) RNN for a single user with 1-minute resolution based on one year of historical data sets.

Transmission of data among constrained wireless sensor devices is critical due to their limited resources, such as power, bandwidth, memory, and processing. These data, generated from sensing different physical events with diverse traffic types, have to reach their destinations with a specific Quality of Service (QoS) requirement. With the increasing usage of sensors in various Internet of Things (IoT) applications, there is a need to address the resource allocation for handling these critical data while satisfying their respective QoS requirements.

In this study, we proposed a mechanism using Software Defined Networking (SDN) to manage traffic and allocate queue resources among flows through a centralized controller. The mechanism is called Value-Based Utility traffic management mechanism. It ensures that the demand for sensor data is satisfied by managing traffic while allocating queue resources.

The proposed mechanism was evaluated in a simple and low-cost OpenFlow testbed with various sensor devices having different QoS requirements. The results showed that each wireless sensor device achieved the level of satisfaction based on their required resource network utility.

In conclusion, the Value-Based Utility traffic management mechanism effectively manages traffic and allocates queue resources among flows in constrained wireless sensor devices, while satisfying QoS requirements. This mechanism can be used in various IoT applications to ensure efficient utilization of resources and effective transmission of critical data.

A new approach for designing a decentralized observer to estimate the un-measurable states of a discrete-time large-scale Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy system is considered in this paper. The interconnection terms of the large-scale system in this study is with an arbitrary nonlinear form and unnecessary to satisfy the bounded constraints. On the basis of the Lyapunov theory, the conditions for observer design which are expressed under the framework of LMIs are derived in the main theorems. Finally, an example is introduced to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

In this letter, we explore methods for secure transmission of millimeter wave simultaneous wireless information and power transfer unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) relay networks. Specifically, we consider a scenario in which a source must transmit confidential information to a destination on the ground with the help of a UAV-based relay, in the presence of multiple independent eavesdroppers. To address this challenge, we derive a closed-form expression for the lower bound of average secrecy rate using a 3-D antenna gain model, and then propose a solution algorithm to maximize this lower bound. This algorithm involves optimizing the source/UAV transmit power, power splitting ratio, and UAV's location, and employs an alternate optimization approach by iteratively solving three sub-problems. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm significantly improves the average secrecy rate in this challenging wireless communication scenario.

This paper presents a high-precision network time synchronization algorithm that is based on the theory of machine learning. The proposed algorithm aims to address the issue of low time synchronization accuracy by taking the network port delay into consideration. To achieve this, the machine self-learning theory is utilized to study the network port delay under varying environmental conditions. Through experimental verification, it has been demonstrated that this approach greatly improves the accuracy of network time synchronization.

Even though face recognition has been a widely explored area for last many decades, real time face recognition is still, a challenging issue due to variations in pose, illumination, occlusion, aging and expression. In addition, with advancement of technology in medical field variation in faces due to plastic surgery has also emerged as a new challenge to face recognition. Furthermore, compared to other challenges mentioned such as pose, illumination etc., the facial plastic surgery changes some of the facial features permanently making face recognition under plastic surgery even more complex problem. In this paper, we proposed a patch-based face recognition using k-NN classifier for plastic surgical faces. Experimentation is carried on IIIT-D plastic surgery face database for three different facial surgeries such as, Rhinoplasty, Blepharoplasty and Lip-augmentation to evaluate the performance of the proposed approach.

In this work, we focus on building style transfer, which transforms ruin or old buildings to modern architecture. Inspired by Gaty's and Goodfellow's style transfer and generative adversarial network (GAN), we use CycleGAN to conquer this type of problem. As we know, image style transfer usually generated unexpected artifacts. To avoid the artifacts and generate better images, we add so called “perception loss” into the network, which is the feature loss extracted by VGG pre-trained model. In the part of “cycle” structure, we adjust cycle loss by changing the ratio of weighting parameters. Finally, we collect images of both ruin (or old) and modern architecture from websites and use unsupervised learning to train the model. The experimental results show our proposed method indeed realize the modern architecture style transfer for ruin or old buildings.

The upward trend in using both Cloud computing and Internet of Things (IoT) is changing the way of conceiving information and communication systems. We can talk about IoT Cloud to indicate a distributed complex system which is able to provide IoT-as-a-Service (IoTaaS). At the edge of the system, multisensors electronic devices make smart the “things” they control also enabling the interconnection with a remote Cloud infrastructure, platform, or software through the Internet. In such scenario, achieving energy-aware IoTaaS is a challenge which needs appropriate choices in all the environmental, economic and ethical aspects of sustainability. The use of Fog computing can help to discover new business opportunities taking into account the above “green” goal. In this paper, we discuss the advantages from using Fog computing to offer energy-aware IoTaaS in sustainable smart environments. Moreover, we present an experimental use case proving the feasibility of our proposal.

We propose and evaluate the deployment of multi-core Erbium-Ytterbium-doped fiber amplifiers in conventional multi-fiber-based optical transport networks. We demonstrate system feasibility and show that design strategies like launched power adaptation and core-to-span connection optimization ensure good performance for different realistic links.

Many important and critical applications use wireless sensor/actuator networks (WSAN). These applications are spanning widely that range in several environments, including industrial, commercial, and residential. Most of these applications need a certain level of real-time communication in addition to reliable data delivery service. Data distribution service (DDS) is a known standard for supporting real-time distributed systems based on the publish/subscribe model. The DDS specification offers two disparate quality-of-service levels of data reliability, namely: best-effort and fully-reliable. TinyDDS is a lightweight and partial porting of DDS middleware to sensor-based platforms, specifically for platforms with limited resources. However, TinyDDS in its current form lacks the reliability support for data delivery. In this paper, we extended the DDS data reliability service and integrated it into TinyDDS, which resulted in Reliable TinyDDS. Moreover, we provide a prototype and comprehensive performance evaluation of the reliability functions taking into account: number of hops, number of publishers, and several other network parameters. The achieved results indicate that reliable data delivery in real-time for WSAN is possible with optimized system parameters, such as retransmission time-out value of 400ms and number of hops not exceeding 10 for an end-to-end delay ranging from 10 to 100s of milliseconds.

This is the third chapter of the book, and it appears that we have not yet defined the topic at hand. Let me address that now. AI simply stands for "artificial intelligence." As the term "artificial" is self-explanatory, it is important for us to provide a definition for "intelligence." Surely, there must be a sound definition of intelligence available for us to use.

Conventional robots have demonstrated reliable and precise positioning capabilities in numerous environments. However, their lack of flexibility makes them unsuitable for certain applications. As a result, a soft robotic system's adaptability and flexibility should be taken into account. This paper presents a novel soft robot with multiple degrees of freedom (DOF) that is actuated by shape memory alloy (SMA) technology. The robot can theoretically support up to nine DOF motions, while still maintaining good positioning accuracy. The proposed multi-DOF soft robot was subjected to motion testing and positioning evaluation, and its structural design, control method, and kinematic and coordinate system analysis are comprehensively discussed.

This paper presents a new approach for determining the impact of lightning strike currents on transmission network elements failures, based on fuzzy logic (FL) and expert systems. The location of lightning strike is determined by means of lightning location system (LLS) and failures in the transmission network, sorted by type of the equipment, are obtained from supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system. The input data set includes two sets. The first set consists of lightning strike locations and current values between the cloud and the ground. The second set consists of current values from SCADA system before and after the fault, protection tripping information, and the state and position of the switches. The proposed FL-based solution is based on a fuzzy decision-making system (DMS), including both data sets in order to provide a power system operator (PSO) with a precise and accurate decision needed in time of emergency. The described model has been tested for functionality and correct results have been obtained, which confirms the membership function (MF) assessment and proves the efficiency and authenticity of the proposed DMS.

A significant challenge faced by network providers is the creation of a network that can efficiently provide differentiated quality-of-service for different traffic classes while being cost-effective. Traditional differentiated services are employed in IP networks, where differentiation is achieved through code points present in the IP packet headers. However, this approach is not sufficient to cater to traffic engineering requirements.

In an SDN environment, traffic engineering can be efficiently managed as there is more control over flows or a group of flows, making it easier to differentiate QoS traffic classes and optimize the network accordingly. This research focuses on network optimization in an SDN environment where differentiated QoS traffic is provided through various latency bounds. 

The problem is tackled using a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) formulation. The study shows that this approach can maintain more stringent QoS requirements by reducing the maximum allowable latency without significantly increasing bandwidth costs. 

Overall, the study suggests that SDN networks can provide efficient traffic engineering and differentiated QoS traffic classes to meet the requirements of different traffic types while ensuring cost-effectiveness.

We evaluated a deep learning-based data demodulation method for multi-level recording data in holographic data storage. This method demodulates reproduced data as pattern recognition using a convolutional neural network. The network learns the rule of demodulation in consideration of optical noise that deteriorates the quality of reproduced data. Unlike with a conventional hard decision method, the learnt network demodulated the noise-added data accurately and decreased demodulation errors.

This article describes a novel approach that utilizes nonlinear least square (NLSQ) algorithm for estimating the mean curve and parameters of the standard lightning impulse (LI) waveform as per the specifications of IEC 60 and IEEE Std. 4. The authors propose a two-step methodology whereby the NLSQ technique is applied to analytical LI waveforms. The high frequency components from the simulated (measured) impulse are initially removed, and the mean curve is subsequently estimated using a bi-exponential model. The proposed technique is evaluated by testing several LI impulse waveforms with front and tail oscillations, as well as LI waveforms with overshoot.

The simulation results indicate that the NLSQ technique is effective and robust because of its ability to estimate the peak value, front and tail times of the impulse waveform with high accuracy. The article compares the results of the NLSQ technique with those obtained by the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. Overall, this study highlights the usefulness of the proposed NLSQ technique in lightning impulse waveform analysis.

We propose an embedded/integrated feature selection method based on neural networks with Group Lasso penalty. Group Lasso regularization is considered to produce sparsity on the inputs to the network, i.e., for selection of useful features. Lasso based feature selection using a multi-layer perceptron usually requires an additional set of weights, while our Group Lasso formulation does not require that. However, Group Lasso penalty is non-differentiable at the origin. This may lead to oscillations in numerical simulations and make it difficult to analyze theoretically. To address this issue, four smoothing Group Lasso penalties are introduced. A rigorous proof for the convergence of the proposed algorithm is presented under suitable assumptions. To verify the effectiveness, a three-step algorithmic architecture is adopted in implementation. Experimental results on several datasets validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the competitive performance of the proposed method.

Airborne Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) is a popular active remote sensing technology that has been developing very rapidly in recent years. To solve the problems of low filtering accuracy of airborne LiDAR point clouds in complex terrain environments and avoiding too much human intervention, this paper proposes a point cloud filtering method based on active learning. In the proposed method, the initial training samples are acquired and marked automatically by multi-scale morphological operations. In so doing, no training samples are selected and labeled manually, i.e., the training samples are added gradually according to the oracle used in active learning. In this paper, the oracle is set to a sigmoid function of residuals from the points to the fitted surface. Subsequently, the training model is revised progressively using the updated training samples. Finally, the classification results are further optimized by a slope-based method. Three datasets with different filtering challenges provided by the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ISPRS) were used to test the proposed method. Comparing with the other ten famous filtering methods, the proposed method can achieve the smallest average total error (5.51%). Thus, it can be concluded that the proposed method performs very well toward different terrain environments.

Lightweight Temporal Compression (LTC) is an energy-efficient lossy compression algorithm that maintains a memory usage and per-sample computational cost in O(1). The method provides a trade-off between compression ratio and accuracy using an error bound. In this paper, we present the Refined LTC (RLTC) algorithm, which uses a binning approach to widen the search space and increase the LTC's compression ratio and reduce its dynamic energy consumption, which is characterized by CPU computations and radio transmissions, without compromising the error bound. The proposed RLTC algorithm adds negligible overhead to the memory usage and latency of LTC. Experimental results on an environmental sensor dataset have shown that the LTC's compressed byte stream can be further reduced in size by up to 18%, while the dynamic energy consumption is reduced by 9.5% on average.

This paper investigates the issue of sampled-data stabilization for Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy memristive neural networks (FMNNs) with time-varying delay. First, the concerned FMNNs are transformed into the tractable fuzzy NNs based on the excitatory and inhibitory of memristive synaptic weights using a new convex combination technique. Meanwhile, a switched fuzzy sampled-data controller is employed for the first time to tackle stability problems related to FMNNs. Then, the novel stabilization criteria of the FMNNs are established using the fuzzy membership functions (FMFs)-dependent Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional. This sufficiently utilizes information from not only the delayed state and the actual sampling pattern but also the FMFs. Two simulation examples are presented to demonstrate the feasibility and validity of the proposed method.

Cardiac autonomic regulation is impacted by respiratory training, as has been evidenced through linear analysis of heart rate variability (HRV). In frequency domain analysis of HRV, the low frequency (LF) and high frequency (HF) bands are the most important and represent parasympathetic and sympathetic activity respectively. The use of deep breathing in research has been widespread, although the interaction between LF and HF during deep breathing has not been extensively studied. In order to investigate this, we conducted a deep breathing experiment on 12 healthy young adults (7 males and 5 females). We utilized transfer entropy (TE) of HRV to analyze the changes in information transmission between LF and HF during baseline and deep breathing. Our results indicate that the mean TE(LF→ HF) value was significantly lower during deep breathing compared to baseline. Furthermore, the mean TE(LF→ HF) value was significantly higher at baseline when compared to TE(HF→ LF) value. Our results also illustrated a significant increase in the LF/HF ratio during deep breathing. In conclusion, our study suggests that deep breathing reduces the information transmission from the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) to the parasympathetic nervous system (PNS).

Organ segmentation, also known as annotation, is a crucial step in radiologic processes such as automated organ and lesion detection and radiotherapy. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) are a type of neural network that requires extensive training data for effective image analysis. However, obtaining medical image annotations from experienced professionals is both costly and time-consuming. In this study, we assess the feasibility of using crowdsourcing as a viable modality for large-scale organ segmentation data annotation. 

To evaluate this, we used crowdsourcing to annotate kidney segmentations in 42 CT scans. 72 users labeled these scans on the Robovision AI platform, and an average of their submissions was taken. To validate this approach, we compared the crowd's segmentations to reference segmentations. We then used both the crowdsourced segmentations and expert-labeled segmentations independently and together as training data for separate CNN models. 

Our findings demonstrate that the performance of the CNN model trained on crowdsourced data was not significantly different from the performance of the expert-labeled model. Additionally, the CNN performance achieved a comparable result when trained on a combination of both the crowdsourced and expert-labeled data. Overall, our results indicate that untrained workers can provide a cost-effective alternative to expert segmentation in radiologic kidney segmentation, presenting a new modality for scalable medical imaging data generation.

We focus on the problem of crosstalk-aware lightpath provisioning in a dynamic, spectrally and spatially flexible optical network, in which spectral super-channels are carried over multi-core fibers with distance-adaptive transmission. The problem involves establishing a lightpath for a connection such that the inter-core crosstalk (XT) between the new lightpath and any exiting lightpaths does not cause the quality of transmission of any of these light-paths to be below an acceptable level. To this end, we analyze and compare two broad classes of schemes that aim to ensure acceptable XT levels in the network. The first is based on static/worst-case XT, whereas the second uses dynamic/ precise XT estimation. These methods are implemented in a dynamic XT-aware routing, spatial mode, and spectrum allocation algorithm that solves the lightpath-provisioning problem efficiently with the goal of minimizing bandwidth blocking. Extensive simulation experiments performed in realistic network scenarios indicate that the utilized XT estimation methodology has a significant impact on network performance, with the precise XT approach favored over the worst-case XT strategy.

Modern face recognition systems have become increasingly accurate, but they still face a major vulnerability in the form of spoofing attacks. Conventional solutions typically add another module to authenticate the liveness of the input faces before feeding it into the face recognition module. However, this two-stage design incurs longer processing times and a need for more storage and resources—which are often limited on mobile and embedded platforms. Consequently, in our paper, we propose a more efficient and effective solution in the form of a multi-task Convolutional Neural Network, LiveFace, for face authentication. The LiveFace network provides two outputs using a single stage, namely facial representation to verify or identify individuals, and a liveness score indicating the probability of the face being live. Additionally, the two tasks share lower layers to reduce computation costs. Our experimental results, using three datasets, reveal that LiveFace achieves comparable performance on both face recognition and anti-spoofing tasks while being considerably faster than traditional authentication systems. Furthermore, we have implemented a prototype of our scheme on Android phones and successfully demonstrated its real-time operation on three tested devices.

Vehicular transportation networks are formed by interconnection of multiple networks leading to a particular class of complex networks called multi-layer networks. These networks are formed due to interaction between vehicles, vehicles and infrastructure (like a cloud), and data exchange at the infrastructure level. The interaction between these networks, and particularly the dependency of the networks formed between the infrastructure and on-road (possibly connected) vehicles at different geographical areas, affect the behaviour of all the elements in these networks. An integrated architecture of vehicular transportation networks for a multi-commodity heterogeneous traffic in an urban scenario is proposed in this paper. The heterogeneity exists due to different detection abilities of vehicles, owing to connectivity facilities and sensing capabilities, and the mode of driving (autonomous or manual) in the vehicles. Considering the multi-layer network architecture, the interconnection between the infrastructure network and the vehicle mobility network is studied. Using game theoretic tools, the impact of path prediction via infrastructure network on decision-making in vehicles and vice-versa is analyzed. The problem is formulated and modelled as a repeated Stackelberg game with incomplete information.

The paper proposes a framework that provides common guidelines for a successful and effective data collection method for educational data mining research. The framework is designed to identify potential issues and methodologies to overcome key challenges, ensuring an efficient and comprehensive data collection process. Further, useful validation techniques are included to guarantee the minimal redundancy and internal consistency of the data.

With the help of the framework, researchers can overcome common challenges such as data variability, bias, and incompleteness. The proposed methodology emphasizes the value of standardizing data collection processes to minimize errors and inconsistencies that may affect data quality.

Moreover, the framework identifies some validation techniques such as cross-checking data sources and using statistical methods to validate data consistency. These techniques ensure minimal redundancy and internal consistency of data that can be used to obtain accurate and reliable insights.

Overall, the proposed framework provides a comprehensive approach to collecting educational data for mining purposes. By following the common guidelines and methodologies proposed, researchers can obtain accurate and reliable data that can be used to create actionable insights and inform decision-making.

Assume-guarantee (A/G) contracts are a powerful tool for modular and hierarchical design and verification of complex systems. They decompose system-level specifications into component-level specifications, enabling rigorous analysis of system behavior. However, existing A/G contract frameworks do not adequately capture the behaviors of cyber-physical systems where multiple agents interact with each other and the environment to achieve their objectives.

To address this limitation, we propose an extension of the A/G contract framework known as optimizing A/G contracts. This extension enables the specification and reasoning about component interactions that involve optimizing objectives. The framework includes methods for creating new contracts through conjunction and composition, as well as algorithms for verifying system properties via contract refinement.

We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework using a set of case studies from connected and autonomous vehicles. These case studies highlight the importance of considering optimizing objectives in the design and verification of cyber-physical systems. The framework provides a powerful tool for engineers and designers to ensure the safety and performance of these systems in the presence of multiple agents and dynamic environments.

In summary, the proposed framework of optimizing A/G contracts extends the existing A/G framework to enable modeling and analysis of complex systems with optimizing agents. This provides a valuable tool for designers and engineers working on cyber-physical systems, enabling them to ensure the safety and performance of systems in complex and dynamic environments.

Deep supervised hashing is a popular technique for semantic image retrieval in computer vision. Existing methods rely on pairwise or triplet labels for similarity preservation, but these labels do not capture complex semantic concepts and result in limited retrieval performance. To overcome this, a new deep supervised hashing model is proposed in this paper that directly takes semantic labels as supervised information and generates discriminant binary codes. The model uses a novel cubic constraint loss function based on Gaussian distribution to preserve semantic variations and penalize overlapping parts of different classes in the embedding space. To address the discrete optimization problem introduced by binary codes, a two-step optimization strategy is proposed. Extensive experiments on large-scale benchmark databases demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance.

Saving data stored and transferred is a critical topic in modern era, especially after the evolution in the numbers of surveillance cameras in the world. So an extra level of compression is needed to contribute in solving the problem of the huge data produced by those cameras. The proposed system: “An Efficient multi-view panoramic imaging and Extra Compression of surveillance cameras' footage using Stitching” (ECS) aims to contribute in the solution of this problem by merging feature extraction stitching techniques with geometric relational matrix calculations. ECS creates a new real-time efficient stitching algorithm to minimize the sending and storing of the redundant pixels between the footage of the surveillance cameras. The limitations of using stitching on video footage and not on still images is due to the high complexities of stitching algorithms; the proposed system, in this paper, uses the projective affine transformation matrix between images of camera footage to reduce this limitations. The work presented in this paper introduces, for the first time, an algorithm to reconstruct images of each camera from the panoramic view. The experimental work of this research tests multiple feature extraction algorithms for stitching; Scale Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), Speed Up Robust Feature (SURF) and Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB) with different order of stitching, and the amount of compression per image after reconstruction is analyzed. Moreover, the panoramic view is mostly a better monitoring option rather than multiple monitors in complex surveillance cameras' control rooms. Experimental results show that the proposed method could be faster than other state-of-the-art image stitching methods and accurate panoramic image. The system also gives a better visual effect in a large view panorama due to the high speed real time stitching introduced in this paper.

Transmission of data among constrained wireless sensor devices is critical due to its limited resources such as power, bandwidth, memory, and processing. These data, generated from sensing different physical events with diverse traffic types, have to reach their destinations with a specific Quality of Service (QoS) requirement. With the increasing usage of sensors in the various Internet of Things applications, there is a need to address the resource allocation for handling these critical data while satisfying their respective QoS requirements. In this work, we implemented a Value-based Utility traffic management mechanism using Software Defined Networking (SDN) to cope with QoS requirement in constrained sensor devices. The SDN-enabled mechanism ensures that the demands of sensor data are satisfied by managing traffic while allocating queue resources among flows through a centralized controller, which utilizes network packet statistics. We evaluated the performance of the proposed mechanism in a simple and low-cost OpenFlow testbed with various sensor devices having different QoS requirements. Results show that each wireless sensor device achieved the level of satisfaction based on their required resource network utility.

Current web crawlers, document databases, and change monitoring systems for web sites have limitations when it comes to dealing with modern dynamic web applications. These systems are commonly restricted to static content and analyzing code retrieved from the server, which is not effective for the changing web applications of today. To address this issue, this study proposes DOMdiff, an algorithm designed to identify changes between two different DOM instances, and classify these changes based on a ranking that represents the distance between the two trees.

The canonical representation of the contents of a single web page at any given time is an instance of the Document Object Model (DOM) which enables rendering and processing of the page within the browser. The algorithm presented in this work compares two different instances of the DOM, identifying changes and categorizing them based on established ranking criteria. The study compared a manually derived classifier with results produced by PRank, a ranked version of the Perceptron algorithm, and the established statistical classifier C5.0.

The results suggest that DOMdiff is effective for large-scale change identification, and entropy-based statistical classifiers are more accurate than the simple predicate-based classifier proposed here. However, the entropy-based classifiers require a larger decision tree. Additionally, PRank showed a shortcoming when dealing with features with low information gain/high entropy.

In conclusion, the DOMdiff algorithm proposed in this study is a valuable tool for identifying changes in modern dynamic web applications. Further research is needed to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the classification models used to categorize changes.

Although generative adversarial networks (GANs) have the ability to generate high-resolution faces from low-resolution ones, the issue of identity preservation during face reconstruction remains a challenge. The reconstructed faces may not resemble the original identities, making it difficult to recognize them. To tackle this problem, we introduce a Siamese GAN (SiGAN) that generates high-resolution faces in a manner that captures the original identity. In SiGAN, we use a Siamese network consisting of two similar generators and one discriminator. The loss function of SiGAN includes both identity information and reconstruction error, paired together. We improve the generator and discriminator of SiGAN through iterative optimization of the loss functions. This process not only leads to visually-pleasing reconstruction, but also ensures that the identity information is preserved. Our experimental results demonstrate that SiGAN performs better than existing GANs in face verification performance, while producing high-quality reconstruction. Even for new identities not seen in the training dataset, SiGAN can still achieve satisfactory results on low-resolution input faces.

In this paper, we investigate the use of the proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method as a means to numerically solve the forward Kolmogorov equation (FKE). The goal of our method is to identify low-dimensional structures in the solution space of the FKE and to develop efficient numerical techniques accordingly. Our main focus is on solving nonlinear filtering (NLF) problems using the real-time POD algorithm proposed by Yau and Yau. 

The POD algorithm comprises two stages, namely the offline and online stages. In the offline stage, we construct a small number of POD basis functions that effectively capture the dynamics of the system. We also compute the propagation of the POD basis functions under the FKE operator. In the online stage, we synchronize the incoming observations on the fly using the POD algorithm. We have discussed the convergence analysis of the algorithm as well. 

In order to demonstrate the feasibility of our algorithm and verify its convergence rate, we have carried out several numerical experiments in the context of NLF problems. Our numerical results show that the POD algorithm leads to significant computational savings compared to existing numerical techniques.

This paper addresses the algorithmic approach to optimize the placement and sizing of shunt capacitor banks in radial distribution networks. The proposed algorithm utilizes load flow calculation algorithm and integer genetic algorithm for the effective placement and sizing of shunt capacitor banks. Initially, the paper discussed the constraints associated with the optimal placement and sizing of shunt capacitor banks. Moreover, the paper presented a comprehensive algorithm for calculating the load flow in radial distribution networks. In addition, the integer genetic algorithm employed in the proposed algorithm was described in detail. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, the IEEE 34 bus test distribution network was utilized. Finally, a practical application of the proposed algorithm was demonstrated on a 10 kV distribution network in Bosnia & Herzegovina.

This technical report aims to provide a Chandrasekhar-type recursion for the maximum correntropy criterion (MCC) Kalman filtering (KF). The original Chandrasekhar difference equation was introduced in the 1970s as an alternative to the commonly used Riccati recursion for classical KF. The resulting Morf-Sidhu-Kailath-Sayed KF algorithms are known for their computational efficiency, as it propagates matrices of smaller sizes than the n x n error covariance matrix used in the Riccati recursion. However, deriving the Chandrasekhar-type recursion within the MCC estimation methodology has not been explored in engineering literature before. 

This technical report takes the first step in deriving the Chandrasekhar MCC-KF estimators using an adaptive kernel size selection strategy with a constant scalar adjusting weight. Numerical examples confirm the practicality and accuracy of the presented theoretical derivations, showing the potential for using the newly suggested MCC-KF implementations.

Device-to-Device (D2D) communication system is increasingly applied as an essential element in serving and supporting the Internet of Things (IoT) devices at the 5G mobile networks. Since a potential D2D pair can switch between different modes (i.e. direct and cellular communication mode), there is a challenge in identifying mode selection between communicating devices. This study aims to increase the capability of the D2D communication system in the IoT devices to match the user and network operator demands. This study aims to design mode selection mechanism based on Multi-Attribute Decision Making (MADM) theory to address the above challenges. So, the mode selection mechanism is based on Simple Additive Weighting (SAW) technique to intelligently choose and switch among the available modes. The performance of the proposed model, which can be applied in the network to enhance the quality of service for meeting user demands is tested. The improvement in the performance of the proposed mechanism is verified when the user is moving in the network at different speed rates from 5 to 40 km/h compared with Received Signal Strength (RSS) approach and Joint Mode approach. The improvement in the performance of the proposed mechanism can be obtained and compared with those of two other approaches. The results show that the proposed model has an excellent performance at different speed rates based on evaluation metrics which are delay, throughput, SINR and delivery ratio.

A novel technique for controlling the unmanned marine vehicle (UMV) amidst the presence of complex marine environment disturbance is presented. The technique is based on a robust adaptive fuzzy neural network control (RAFNNC) algorithm which uses a generalized dynamic fuzzy neural network (GDFNN), proportional-integral-differential (PID), and an improved bacterial foraging optimization (BFO) algorithm. 

The inverse dynamic model of the UMV motion control is established using the GDFNN to account for uncertain disturbance caused by the complex marine environment. The adaptive rate of the fuzzy neural network is then obtained through the error between the actual heading of the UMV and the reference heading angle, to adjust the weight parameter of the GDFNN. The output control value of the neural network is then processed. 

To minimize computation amount and time, the PID control algorithm parameters were optimized in advance using the improved BFO algorithm. The BFO algorithm used fractal dimension step size and intelligent probe operation to increase its efficiency and accuracy. 

The stability of the RAFNNC algorithm for the UMV heading control is proven through Lyapunov stability theory. Semi-physical simulation experiments conducted in the laboratory verify the accuracy and effectiveness of the control algorithm proposed.

In this paper, the testing for the extent of the lightning voltage that occurs from the actual low voltage distribution line is presented. Simulations are performed using MATLAB Simulink environment. Analyses are Implemented in two scenarios. In the first scenario, the system is considered without any Surge Arresters along the powerline; and in the second scenario the effect of appropriate Surge Arresters connected to the network is observed. The results of simulations show that in the first case, lightning overvoltages exceed the withstand level of the powerline's insulators. Therefore, the overvoltages must be reduced. In the second scenario, one set of surge arresters is installed along the distribution line and their impact on excessive lightning is analyzed in different cases.

Hydroponics is the practice of growing plants and crops in soilless culture. It is becoming more prevalent nowadays because of decreasing available land due to urbanization, and the various advantages it has as compared to soil-based farming. To study and optimize the various factors that affect plant growth in hydroponics set-ups (such as ambient temperature, light intensity, humidity, etc.), a hybrid sensor network system, with both wireless (6LoWPAN) and wired (CAN Bus) components, was proposed. The proposed system was then implemented using off-the-shelf devices such as the CC2650 MCU, MSP432 launchpad, Digilent PMOD CAN, and the Raspberry Pi 2. The total number of 6LoWPAN nodes in the intended application setup was shown to be reduced by 87.26% compared to fully-wireless setup. The system was shown to be functional and the packet drop rate when time interval between messages is 800ms drops to almost 0%. An initial design for the visualization of the web application was also presented.

This paper proposes and analyzes a mmWave sparse channel estimation technique for OFDM systems that uses the Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) algorithm. This greedy algorithm retrieves one additional multipath component (MPC) per iteration until a stop condition is met. We obtain an analytical approximation for the OMP estimation error variance that grows with the number of retrieved MPCs (iterations). The OMP channel estimator error variance outperforms a classic maximum-likelihood (ML) non-sparse channel estimator by a factor of approximately 2L̂/M where L̂ is the number of retrieved MPCs (iterations) and M the number of taps of the Discrete Equivalent Channel. When the MPC amplitude distribution is heavy-tailed, the channel power is concentrated in a subset of dominant MPCs. In this case OMP performs fewer iterations as it retrieves only these dominant large MPCs. Hence for this MPC amplitude distribution the estimation error advantage of OMP over ML is improved. In particular, for channels with MPCs that have lognormally-distributed amplitudes, the OMP estimator recovers approximately 5-15 dominant MPCs in typical mmWave channels, with 15-45 weak MPCs that remain undetected.

For the suppression of transient artifacts in time series data, we propose a non-convex generalized fused lasso penalty for the estimation of signals comprising a low-pass signal, a sparse piecewise constant signal, and additive white Gaussian noise. The proposed non-convex penalty is designed so as to preserve the convexity of the total cost function to be minimized, thereby realizing the benefits of a convex optimization framework (reliable, robust algorithms, etc.). Compared to the conventional use of L1 norm penalty, the proposed non-convex penalty does not underestimate the true amplitude of signal values. We derive a fast proximal algorithm to implement the method. The proposed method is demonstrated on the suppression of artifacts in near infrared spectroscopic (NIRS) measures..

Current techniques for gesture classification assign categorical labels to each gesture instance, limiting their adaptability to new or unseen gestures. To address this issue and enable zero shot learning (ZSL), we propose identifying the properties of gestures and inferring the categorical label instead of recognizing the class label directly. However, the lack of benchmarks and specialized datasets has hindered research in ZSL for gesture recognition. To address this, we introduce the first annotated database of attributes for gestures in ChaLearn 2013 and MSRC-12 datasets. We identified a finite set of 64 discriminative and representative high level attributes of gestures from literature and used crowdsourced human studies to gather attribute annotations for 28 gesture classes. Through our dataset, we trained existing ZSL classifiers to predict attribute labels and provide benchmarks for unseen gesture class prediction on CGD2013 and MSRC-12. The public release of this dataset aims to encourage further research in this area.

Enhancing traffic safety and acquiring vessel messages in complex and diverse marine environments has become a paramount concern in recent years. To address this issue, the Automatic Identification System (AIS) has been employed to gather information about vessel behaviors. In this article, we propose a vessel behavior analysis framework based on the JPPF parallel processing framework, which can be utilized to obtain the spatial-temporal characteristics of vessel behavior in coastal waterways. To demonstrate the efficacy of our framework, we input 1 billion AIS data from Tianjin Port in China and successfully obtain vessel behaviors that can be utilized in vessel traffic simulation, safe navigation of vessels, supervision of the maritime sector, and macroscopic dispatch of the country.

The research interest in distributed decision-making in multi-agent networks has significantly increased due to its broad applicability in various fields, such as computer networks, power systems, robotic teams, sensor networks, and consumer markets. These problems can be represented as inter-dependent optimization problems or game-equilibrium seeking problems, where noncooperative agents seek an equilibrium by communicating over a network. The agents can decide to update their decision variables by using proximal dynamics to achieve a network equilibrium. 

In this paper, the authors provide an operator-theoretic characterization of convergence with a time-invariant communication network. They also consider the time-varying case, where adjacency matrices may switch subject to a dwell time. To illustrate their investigations, the authors provide an example of a distributed robotic exploration.

Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of distributed decision-making in multi-agent networks and provides valuable insights into achieving a network equilibrium.

Emotion recognition is an increasingly critical area in human-computer interaction technology, particularly in multimedia communication. Currently, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used as the primary method for information extraction from spectrograms. However, this may not be the most effective approach since it does not optimize the use of hand-crafted features. To address this issue, this study proposes a model based on a weighted feature fusion method to improve variable-length speech emotion recognition. The model combines Chroma-based features and CNN-based features to leverage the useful information in the Chromaticity map related to speech emotions. Evaluation on the Interactive Emotional Motion Capture (IEMOCAP) dataset shows a more than 5% increase in weighted and unweighted accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

To develop protocols for highly specialized rehabilitation, it is crucial to understand the impact of specific exercises and rehabilitation robotic treatments on locomotor adaptation. Experimental results are necessary to determine how adaptive mechanisms depend on shared training variables for optimal rehabilitation outcomes. This study aimed to assess the combined effects of active body weight support (BWS) and robot-applied resistance/assistance training on muscle function during robotic-assisted treadmill walking. Ten healthy participants were enrolled, walking with varying levels of BWS (0%, 15%, and 30% of their body weight) and robot-applied resistance/assistance force (0%, 5% and 10% of their body weight). Temporal gait parameters and muscular activity were recorded. BWS increased activity in pelvic stability muscles (e.g., Biceps Femoris) and decreased activity associated with weight loading and foot clearance (e.g., Rectus Femoris and Tibialis Anterior). Resistance training did not show superiority over assistance training in activating gait-related muscles, although different motor adaptations may be involved. Keywords: Body weight support, Gait, Muscle weakness, Rehabilitation robotics, Robot-assisted gait training, Robotic assistance/resistance training.

The segmentation of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) images has been a long-standing problem in medical imaging. The convolutional networks used for CMR segmentation often struggle with adequate communication between semantic and spatial information. To address this issue, we propose an innovative approach called the aggregated parallel cross-scale pyramid network (APCP-Net) for CMR segmentation. This network utilizes parallel cross-scale spatial pyramid to improve multi-scale feature fusion. To reduce computational complexity while maintaining performance and minimizing time consumption, a convolution decomposition strategy is employed. This strategy decomposes a regular convolutional layer into lightweight layers. Additionally, deep aggregation is applied among parallel spatial pyramids to enhance the representation ability of our APCP-Net. We evaluate our method on the segmentation dataset of ACDC 2017 Challenge and find that our APCP-Net performs comparably to state-of-the-art methods, while requiring 54 times fewer parameters than existing methods.

Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) is been a huge evolution (growth) in the current years. The growth is particularly because of the availability or requirement of small size sensors, which senses the environment with the help of tiny size sensor nodes and which is used in the communication of sensed data. WSNs are usually contains huge number of huge sink nodes and a sensor nodes. The multipath routing technique is the important task in the WSN for reliable transfer of data simultaneously by reducing delay and congestion. The multipath routing protocols improves Quality of service (QoS) and load balancing in addition to the reliable communication in the network. This survey gives a brief introduction about the multipath routing and the classifications of the various geographic multipath routing protocols based on the routing information (data) update mechanism using local or global heuristics knowledge. A comparison between these protocols in terms of various routing parameters for path maintenance, path discovery, traffic distribution is described for each class of geographic multipath routing protocols.

Chronic diseases are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality around the world. Unfortunately, these conditions are often difficult to diagnose, especially during their early stages. Detecting chronic diseases early on is crucial in order to prevent or delay their progression. To this end, researchers have proposed an early warning model (EWM) based on electronic health records (EHRs).

The EWM utilizes a range of techniques to determine whether a patient is likely to develop a chronic disease based on the undiagnosed narrative text of their EHRs. To improve the accuracy of the model, a professional medical terminology library known as Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine-Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) is employed. The model also makes use of the semantic relationships in the SNOMED CT to expand the effects of related terms of renal cancer.

To test the efficacy of their EWM, the researchers used a dataset of 1,300 medical records and more than 1,400 progress notes in EHRs. Their proposed EWM achieved impressive results, with a precision of 90%, recall of 91%, and F-measure of 91%.

Early warning systems like this could play a key role in improving the chances of early detection and intervention for chronic diseases such as renal cancer. By identifying patients at risk of developing these conditions, healthcare professionals can take proactive steps to monitor and manage their health, ultimately leading to better health outcomes.

Nowadays, higher education institutions worldwide are shifting towards informatization. In China, the "Transformation and Overtaking" program and the "Double 10,000 Plan" have kickstarted this trend, with MOOCs playing a crucial role. This presents a plethora of opportunities and challenges for universities, including how to apply innovation diffusion theory to advanced teaching with MOOCs, balancing the application to the diffusion's characteristics to speed up the process and promote deep integration of information technology and education, and organizational innovation and reform for teaching informatization.

This paper draws from innovation diffusion theory and focuses on MOOCs' construction and application in higher education, particularly in Jinan University's context. Based on this case study, the paper proposes an integrated promotion mode to achieve scalable teaching information ecology, benefit, and teaching informatization. Key areas of focus include design and omni-directional management and support of MOOCs, construction, implementation, innovation diffusion, application of online assessment and SPOC on-line application modes, and quality control for one-stop practice training. These recommendations can facilitate the innovation and development of information technology in higher education institutions.

In this study, we propose an adaptive Fourier linear combiner (FLC) based on a modified least mean kurtosis (LMK) algorithm for canceling the sinusoidal noise signals from the desired signals. In the proposed framework, the weight coefficients of the FLC are adjusted by using the modified LMK algorithm instead of the conventional least mean square (LMS) algorithm. The fundamental reasons for using the proposed LMK algorithm in the FLC are that it provides a fast convergence rate, a lower steady-state error and a robust behavior against sinusoidal noise distributions. The performance of the proposed FLC algorithm is assessed on the noise canceling problem by comparing that of the conventional FLC based on the LMS algorithm. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FLC based the modified LMK algorithm outperforms its conventional LMS algorithm in terms of the convergence rate and the steady-state error.

Multipath is the dominant source of error in indoor positioning systems, since the reception of multipath can significantly distort the shape of the correlation function used for time-delay estimation. When a band-limited signal is used, the range resolution is often insufficient to decompose the overlapped received signals. This paper presents a multipath mitigation algorithm for ATSC DTV signal-based positioning systems. The algorithm combines sample interpolation with a multipath signal delay estimator based on an equalizer which periodically suppresses a specified number of the lowest-magnitude equalizer weights. The goal of the new equalizer is to more accurately predict the channel response. MATLAB simulations were carried out to demonstrate the proposed method and was confirmed with field-test data. The proposed approach can reduce the range estimation resolution by 60% compared to the Fourier limit.

A perspective is provided to compare the reliability requirements of Resistive Random Access Memory (RRAM) for digital memory application and neuromorphic computing application. Retention and endurance are considered as the two key metrics to evaluate the impact on neural network training. Statistical measurements and network simulation demonstrate that the retention and endurance degradation behaviors of analog RRAM are quite unique when implementing on a neuromorphic computing system. New evaluation method is therefore needed for reliability test.

Testing in the Cloud has been an area of active research, but there is a lack of evidence regarding the actual motivations, issues, and gains for adoption of automated cloud testing technology in real-world industrial contexts. In this paper, we present the findings from an empirical study that involved four quasi-experiments within various application domains, including e-commerce, 5G networking, WebRTC, and IoT.

The study was part of the ElasTest validation strategy that aimed to evaluate the impact of the ElasTest open-source platform for end-to-end testing of large distributed systems. The results of the study revealed significant benefits of using automated cloud testing technology in industrial contexts. These benefits included increased efficiency, faster testing cycles, improved software quality, and reduced costs.

Moreover, the study also highlighted various challenges, methods, and tools associated with cloud testing. The challenges included issues related to security, performance, and resource management, while the methods and tools included containerization, orchestration, and monitoring technologies.

In conclusion, the findings of this study provide valuable insights into the benefits, challenges, methods, and tools associated with the adoption of automated cloud testing technology in real-world industrial contexts. The study results also underscore the importance of continuing research in this area to ensure that industry can fully leverage the potential of cloud testing.

Error correction in quantum cryptography based on artificial neural networks is a new and promising solution. In this paper the security verification of this method is discussed and results of many simulations with different parameters are presented. The test scenarios assumed partially synchronized neural networks, typical for error rates in quantum cryptography. The results were also compared with scenarios based on the neural networks with random chosen weights to show the difficulty of passive attacks.

Code cloning is a frequently observed phenomenon in software development, but it can lead to the multiplication of bugs or even result in new ones if not handled properly. This research paper presents a method for creating a library of clone code cases that are based on bugs. The study focuses on the clone code of continuous multi-version software and involves four essential steps: clone detection, clone code evolution tracking, linking clone code with bugs, and creating and visualizing the clone code bug library. The resultant case base will offer scientific insights and practical value for reusing, reconstructing, and managing clone code. Additionally, it will provide clone maintenance recommendations that are relevant to various users based on their specific requirements.
